JOB DESCRIPTION 
 Title                            : STRIDES Technical Director 
 Report To                  : STRIDES Project Director 
 Location                     : Dhaka, Bangladesh 
 FHI 360 is a nonprofit human development organization dedicated to improving lives in lasting ways by advancing integrated, locally driven solutions. Our staff includes experts in health, education, nutrition, economic development, youth, research, technology, communication, and social marketing—creating a unique mix of capabilities to address today’s interrelated development challenges. FHI 360 serves more than 70 countries and all US states and territories. 
 FHI 360 has worked in Bangladesh for more than 45 years. Since 1975, we have taken a comprehensive approach to help transform the country’s health and development landscape. Leveraging a blend of global expertise and local insights, we have consistently strengthened community capacities, enhanced systems, and reinforced institutional frameworks for a sustainable impact. In partnership with the Government of Bangladesh, civil society, academia, and the private sector, FHI 360 Bangladesh delivers integrated programs across critical sectors. Our initiatives have spanned essential health services—including HIV and nutrition, tuberculosis, global health security, and economic participation.  
 This position is contingent upon funding from the Department of State (DOS). 
 Project Description: 
 A disease can spread from any remote village to any major city on all continents in as little as 36 hours. Increased international travel and trade, population growth and movement, greater urbanization, and insufficient attention to existing weak health systems are key drivers for the emergence of infectious diseases. The U.S. government’s (USG) Global Health Security (GHS) program provides life-saving assistance to prevent, detect, and respond to infectious disease threats which pose risks for public health outbreaks that could cost lives. As part of the USG’s GHS program, the STRengthening Infectious disease DEtection Systems (STRIDES) Activity advances cross-sectoral efforts to successfully identify, manage, and respond to infectious disease threats; detect and prevent further outbreaks; and instill confidence and trust in a country’s disease detection and surveillance structures and services. STRIDES aims to increase a country’s Joint External Evaluation (JEE) scores by supporting national governments to strengthen core capacities — including laboratory and surveillance systems strengthening and emergency response operations — thereby improving compliance with International Health Regulations (IHR) and overall global health security. 
 Position Summary: 
 The STRengthening Infectious disease DEtection Systems (STRIDES) Bangladesh Technical Director leads and directs technical focus areas across the Activity to enhance global health security in Bangladesh. They will align STRIDES technical frameworks, approaches, tools, and activities with relevant normative guidelines and technical standards in country.  This may include identifying specialized partnership needs and engaging qualified partners to ensure technical performance. STRIDES BangladeshTechnical Director works closely with technical leads, the Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) team and Program Management teams ensure adherence with the United States Government’s (USG) global health security priorities in country. They are accountable for the successful delivery of all technical aspects and reporting of the STRIDES activity in country from initiation through delivery and closeout in country, ensuring completion of technical deliverables on schedule and within budget and that meet or exceed quality standards..
 Accountabilities: 
 Serves as STRIDES technical lead and key point of contact for relevant topics.
 Provides technical direction to develop country-specific workplans and budgets, ensuring alignment with STRIDES objectives and USG priorities and with global technical standards.  
 Ensures high quality technical deliverables—including workplans, required and ad hoc reports, and success stories highlighting technical achievements—are developed, submitted and approved on schedule and within budget parameters.
 Provides direction to ensure technical activities to ensure technical activities are compliant with STRIDES contract, government regulations, relevant quality standards and FHI 360’s policies and procedures.
 Responds to client requests and questions on technical matters; ensures timely drafts and submissions of consent, approvals and/or waivers.
 Ensures technical activities are designed to support STRIDES monitoring and evaluation activities; collaborates with the MEL Advisor and Project Director to finalize and submit country-specific technical indicators and report against their progress in quarterly, annual, and other reports.
 Assesses subcontractors’ performance on technical activities and directs adjustments, as needed.
 Collaborates with the MEL Advisor, Project Director and Communications lead to promote STRIDES successes by collecting, writing, and distributing success stories, case studies, photos, and outreach at events.
 Represent STRIDES at global health security-focused events echnical working group meetings; collect and share information that could be valuable to the Activity.
 Supports performance management and professional development of direct reports, including ongoing feedback, coaching and career support.
 Performs other duties as assigned.
 Applied Knowledge & Skills: 
 Comprehensive knowledge of concepts, practices, and procedures with contract and project management and technical development.
 Excellent oral and written communication skills.
 Excellent and demonstrated organizational and problem-solving skills.
 Excellent and demonstrated project management and technical skills.
 Ability to influence, motivate, negotiate and work well with others.
 Ability to exercise judgment within generally defined practices and policies in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions.
 Comprehensive knowledge of concepts, practices and policies related to global health security.
 Proven ability to ensure that budgets, schedules, and performance requirements are met.
 Excellent and demonstrated leadership, organizational, and project management skills.
 Critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
 Excellent oral and written communication and analytical skills in English; additional language skills  a bonus.

 Works on problems of complex scope and require in depth evaluation of issues and assessment of intangible factors.
 Exercises judgment within broadly defined practices and policies to select methods and techniques for obtaining results.
 Decisions made generally affect overall success of functional, division or company operations.
 Problems encountered are complex, highly varied and require considerable judgment to obtain results.

 Provides direct supervision to technical staff in country

 Coordinates across STRIDES Management Team to set budgets, goals, and develops procedures and training for project.

 Master’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Public Health, Epidemiology, Microbiology, Infectious Disease, Laboratory Science, Health Systems Strengthening, or a related field from a recognized university.

FHI 360 is a global development   organization,   with a rigorous, evidence-based approach to human development. Our team of professionals includes experts in   education,   health, nutrition, economic development, civil society,   environment   and research. FHI 360   operates   from over 60 offices with more than 4 , 000 employees in the United States and around the world. Our commitment to partnerships at all levels and our multi-disciplinary approach allows us to have a lasting impact on the people,   communities   and countries we serve by improving the lives of millions.     
 We are currently seeking qualified candidates for the position of   Deputy   Chief of Party ( D COP)   for the upcoming   MCC Belize   Training and Transitioning to Work Activity   which seeks   to improve the efficiency, inclusivity and effectiveness of systems related to governance, financing and quality assurance of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system . This position will be based in   Belize   and   is contingent upon award.    
 Project Description   
 The Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) and the Government of Belize (GOB) have   signed   a $125 million , 5-year   Compact that   aims to address the binding constraints of low-quality education by increasing the number of post-primary graduates with the skills relevant to labor market demands.  Under the Compact, an Education Project will   invest in Belize’s secondary education and technical and vocational education training (TVET) sector.     
 Position Description   
 The   Deputy   Chief of Party (DCOP)   works in close coordination with the Chief of Party (COP)   and   is responsible for   managing the quality and timeliness of the project’s overall technical workstream s .   The D COP   will   lead the development of evidence-based approaches to improving TVET systems, including   national TVET governance reform,   implementation of the National TVET policy and strategy,   strengthening the National Training Agency, and   development of sector skills councils, work-based learning   systems   and   curriculum modernization . This position will contribute to the design, development, implementation,   monitoring   and evaluation of all ac tivities   that aim to improve   the quality, equity,   relevance   and efficiency of the TVET system . S / he will support ongoing quality assurance ,   supervise a technical team,   and   liaise with technical partners, relevant national stakeholders,   beneficiaries   and the donor.   The   D COP   will have   demonstrated   ability   to work in complex environments, across   different cultures , and manage diverse teams to deliver impact.   
 Job Summary/Responsibilities   
 Coordinates closely with the Chief of Party (COP) on all technical matters;   provides support to the leadership and management of the project, including budget formulation and oversight   
 Leads project interventions related   to the   technical design, implementation ,   an d quality assurance, ensuring that TVET interventions are evidence-based,   contextually-appropriate   and aligned with   Ministry of Education and   labor market demand.   
 Coordinates technical support to the   Government of Belize, the local MCA Belize entity and MCC     
 Guides the development of sector skills councils, accreditation systems, and partnerships that strengthen private sector engagement and improve coordination of apprenticeships   
 Oversees technical outputs (activities,   strategies   and deliverables) of all implementing partner   organizations through regular field visits   
 Develops and implements local partner technical capacity building activities   
 Supports the COP to oversee project monitoring and evaluation activities in collaboration with the MEL Advisor to build and implement a cohesive data collection,   aggregation   and reporting strategy with partners   
 Provides leadership to technical staff and   ensures clear roles and responsibilities;   maintains   clear lines of communication with project team members   
 Collaborates with in-country team and headquarter-based technical staff to ensure the project is implemented according to organization and industry best practices, program framework, and regulations   
 Required Qualifications     
 Master's  degree in in education policy, TVET, quality assurance, educational leadership, or   a related   discipline.     
 At least   12   years of experience working   in in the development or implementation of TVET quality assurance systems, accreditation frameworks, national vocational qualifications frameworks, or regulatory systems for training providers . 
 Experience designing or implementing accreditation and certification systems for training providers.    
 Knowledge of competency-based education and training frameworks and alignment with national or regional qualification systems.    
 Experience supporting institutional reforms within education or skills development systems. 
 8+ years of related work experience in increasingly senior roles , with three years in leadership positions; experience   working in   a non-governmental organization preferred. 
 Knowledge   of and experience   with   Belizean   education systems (including secondary, TVET and higher education)   and   Ministry of Education    
 Relevant managerial and technical experience working with programs that are of a similar scope and scale to this program.   
 Demonstrated ability to work in complex environments, across   different cultures , and manage diverse teams to deliver impact within agreed timelines   
 Proven ability to   manage productive relationships   with government stakeholders   and donors   
 Demonstrated knowledge of   MCC   and Government of Belize   rules, regulations, policies, and procedures as they relate to project and program compliance and reporting .   
 Experience in the education sector in   Belize   or the region .   
 Oral and written fluency   required   in   English .

FHI 360 is a global development organization, with a rigorous, evidence-based approach to human development. Our team of professionals includes experts in education, health, nutrition, economic development, civil society, environment and research. FHI 360 operates from over 60 offices with more than 4,000 employees in the United States and around the world. Our commitment to partnerships at all levels and our multi-disciplinary approach allows us to have a lasting impact on the people, communities and countries we serve by improving the lives of millions.    
 We are currently seeking qualified candidates for the position of  Team Lead/Chief of Party  to provide overall technical, strategic, operational, and stakeholder leadership for an anticipated MCC-funded education quality assurance activity in Belize. 
 This position will be based in Belize and is contingent upon FHI 360 receiving the award.    
 Project Description   
 The Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) and the Government of Belize (GOB) have signed a $125 million, 5-year Compact that aims to address the binding constraints of low-quality education and high electricity costs. The Quality Assurance activity is expected to support the Government of Belize to strengthen accountability for student learning through development and implementation of an educational quality assurance system, strengthening of the Belize Education Management Information System (BEMIS), and reform of teacher and school leadership policies and systems.  
 Position Description  
 The Team Lead will serve as the primary point of contact with MCC, MCA-Belize, the Ministry of Education, Youth, Sports and Culture (MoEYSC), and other key stakeholders. The Team Lead will oversee technical integration across all components of the activity and ensure delivery of high-quality, sustainable, and contextually appropriate reforms. 
 Job Summary/Responsibilities  
 Leadership and Project Management 
 Provide overall leadership, strategic direction, and management oversight for the activity.  
 Serve as principal liaison with MCC, MCA-Belize, MoEYSC, and key education stakeholders.  
 Ensure effective coordination and integration across all technical workstreams.  
 Lead annual work planning, implementation oversight, risk management, and adaptive management processes.  
 Ensure compliance with MCC requirements, reporting standards, and contractual obligations.  
 Technical Leadership 
 Guide implementation of integrated education quality assurance reforms, including:  
 Quality assurance frameworks  
 BEMIS strengthening and data systems integration  
 Teacher and school leader policy reform  
 School improvement planning  
 Performance management and accountability systems  
 Ensure coherence between quality assurance systems, teacher policy reforms, and national student assessment initiatives.  
 Promote evidence-based decision-making and institutional capacity strengthening.  
 Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination 
 Build and maintain strong working relationships with government counterparts, education institutions, school management authorities, donors, and implementing partners.  
 Facilitate stakeholder consultation and consensus-building processes.  
 Support coordination with parallel reform initiatives and donor-funded activities.  
 Team Supervision 
 Supervise senior technical personnel and oversee multidisciplinary teams and consultants.  
 Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture.  
 Support mentoring and professional development of project staff and counterparts.  
 Required Qualifications  
 Bachelors degree in Education Planning, Educational Measurement, Monitoring and Evaluation, Education Statistics, Data Analytics, Education Management Information Systems (EMIS), Public Policy, or   a related   field . Master's or higher preferred. 
 Minimum 12 years of progressively responsible experience, in education system reform,   education quality assurance, school   improvement   or education governance ( Including 8+ years of experience in designing or implementing national or subnational education quality assurance, accountability, or school evaluation systems). 
 Evidence shall include leadership of at least three (3) relevant assignments involving standards development, school supervision, performance monitoring, institutional strengthening, or accountability systems, including at least one (1) assignment that involved piloting or national/subnational rollout.   At least one (1) year experience working in Caribbean or small-state education systems is preferred. 
 Demonstrated experience in education quality assurance systems through   a minimum of three (3) completed assignments within the past ten (10) years   involving at least two of the following areas: school evaluation, school supervision, school improvement planning, education quality standards, performance monitoring, or quality assurance frameworks. Experience shall be   evidenced   through submitted reports, frameworks, methodologies, or similar deliverables produced by the proposed expert .  
 Demonstrated experience   facilitating   stakeholder engagement processes through   a minimum of three (3) completed assignments   that included consultation, validation, consensus-building, or policy development activities involving government agencies, education authorities, schools, development partners, or other relevant stakeholders.  ( Evidence shall include meeting reports, consultation reports, validation workshop reports, stakeholder engagement plans, or similar documented outputs) .
 Demonstrated ability to analyze complex education-sector issues and produce high-quality technical outputs through   a minimum of three (3) completed assignments   that resulted in the preparation of policy documents, strategic plans, quality assurance frameworks, implementation plans, evaluation reports, or similar technical documents that were formally accepted by the client.  ( Evidence shall include sample deliverables, client references, completion certificates, or documented acceptance of outputs.   Assignments should   demonstrate   the ability to integrate policy, operational, implementation, and data-related considerations into practical recommendations and reform strategies) .  
 Experience with MCC-funded programs strongly preferred.  
 Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary technical teams and coordinating with high-level government stakeholders.  
 Experience in the Caribbean and/or small island developing states preferred.  
 Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

offres.description:
JOB SUMMARY: 
 The Senior Director, Strategic Information/Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (SI/MEL), Health Programs is a strategic leader within FHI 360, responsible for the technical leadership and strategic direction of strategic information, monitoring, evaluation, analytics, data systems, and learning (SI/MEL) across the Health Programs (HP) portfolio within the Programs and Research Group (PRG). The Senior Director also provides scientific and technical leadership in epidemiology, surveillance, health informatics, and data use. This role provides technical and operational oversight to a division comprised of multiple project SI/MEL teams, fosters innovation, and ensures the delivery of high-quality, timely, and actionable data aligned with organizational objectives and funder requirements. The Senior Director establishes and continually refines SI/MEL frameworks, approaches, tools, and activities; identifies specialized partnership needs; and engages qualified partners to ensure technical performance. Working across FHI 360 Health Programs projects and country portfolios, the Senior Director strengthens the integration of surveillance, MEL, data management, analytics, and digital health systems, in close collaboration with project SI/MEL leadership teams to ensure coherence, technical alignment, and mutual learning across initiatives. The Senior Director leads one integrated SI/MEL team that serves all Health Programs projects, so that each country has a single SI/MEL point of contact across awards, with shared standards, harmonized indicators, and staffing and level of effort planned across the portfolio. The Senior Director collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to gather and share evidence, lessons learned, and best practices to drive continuous improvement and organizational impact. The Senior Director serves as a recognized technical leader and thought partner in strategic information, surveillance, epidemiology, and health informatics . They also contribute technical leadership to new business development and represent FHI 360 as a thought leader in strategic information, health informatics, and data-driven program improvement. Engagement with country and field teams is exercised primarily through project SI/MEL leadership; direct, hands-on support to field teams is expected on bilateral awards and is provided to global projects at the request of project leadership. Their decisions are guided by organizational strategy and have significant short- and long-term impacts on public health and development outcomes.

 Ensures project data systems meet funder reporting standards (e.g., DATIM, DHIS2, MER indicators) and support programmatic decision-making at all levels.
 Provides technical leadership in the design, implementation, and utilization of surveillance systems and public health evaluations.
 Leads efforts to strengthen the collection, analysis, interpretation, visualization, and use of health data across country portfolios.
 Guides methodological approaches for surveillance and program evaluation.
 Identifies opportunities to leverage routine health information systems, EMRs, surveillance platforms, and real-world data to improve program performance and public health outcomes.
 Serves as a senior resource on epidemiologic methods, disease surveillance, measurement approaches, and data quality across the portfolio.

Project Description 
Meeting Targets and Maintaining Epidemic Control (EpiC), a global project funded by the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), that provides strategic technical assistance and direct service delivery to achieve HIV epidemic control among all at-risk populations and people living with HIV (PLHIV); strengthen global health security (GHS), including outbreak response; expand tuberculosis detection and treatment (TB), improve maternal and child health (MCH), address malaria; and promote health systems strengthening (HSS) including supply chain management.
 In Ghana, EpiC will work to support the Ghana Ministry of Health (MOH), Ghana Health Service (GHS)-National AIDS/STI Control Programme (NACP) and Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC), Regional Health Directorates (RHDs) and  District Health Directorates (DHDs) to achieve the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets by 2030 in the three PEPFAR-supported regions through the focused implementation of innovative prevention, case finding, linkage to care and treatment, treatment continuity, and viral load suppression strategies.
 Job Description: 
 The Clinical Specialist, will support the effective delivery of integrated HIV clinical care and laboratory services across program implementation sites within the EpiC Ghana project. S/he will be in routine contact with NACP, RHDs, DHDs, health facilities, and implementing partners in the three PEFAR supported regions in the country, providing ongoing technical and quality assurance support for HIV clinical care and laboratory functions to enhance program outcomes and contribute to achieving HIV epidemic control. The Clinical Specialist will lead quality improvement initiatives and provide support for supply chain. The role will also strengthen clinical–laboratory coordination to improve viral load coverage, ensure timely sample processing and return of results, and promote the use of results for clinical monitoring and patient management.  The position requires close collaboration with the HIV Technical Advisor and other program staff within EpiC and the FHI 360 Ghana country office to ensure application of best practices and alignment with project strategies.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Supports the design, implementation and monitoring of clinical care and lab services related to HIV treatment, continuity of treatment, viral load and AHD activities for PLHIV, HIV prevention (including PrEP) for pregnant and breastfeeding women, PMTCT, EID, and case detection.
 Collaborates closely with the Ghana Health Service-NACP, RHDs, DHDs, health facilities/ART Centers, PEPFAR-supported nurse assistants, community organizations and EpiC community/facility treatment staff to ensure quality clinical care and lab services for PLHIV, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and HIV exposed infants.
 Collaborate with NACP to ensure that commodities such as ARVs, HTS test kits, PrEP commodities are available on a consistent basis at all clinical service provision facilities.  
 Is knowledgeable about the national protocols on HIV Clinical management and all the differentiated models of ARV delivery such as MMD, SDART, DSD, Early refills
 Expert inpatient-centered care strategies that prioritize a holistic approach to maximize chances of patient ART adherence and viral load suppression
 Ensures high quality standard operating procedures for clinical care contextualized to the Ghana environment.
 Assists in strengthening the implementation and monitoring of the project diagnostic components such as specimen collection for viral load, specimen referral, specimen transport, supply chain, equipment management, expansion of point-of-care diagnostic services, and , especially related to HIV testing, viral load monitoring, CD4 testing and TB/HIV diagnostics.
 Contributes technical and programmatic expertise in diagnostics, quality management systems relevant to the Ghana context.
 Assists in assuring that commodities such as ARVs, HTS test kits (rapid, self-testing), TB Prophylaxis drugs and TB diagnostics, and viral load reagents are available on a consistent basis at all clinical service provision facilities and labs.
 Participates in the development and facilitation of clinical and laboratory training within the EpiC Ghana project and contributes to reporting on the effectiveness of such training.
 Supports the development and implementation of EpiC Ghana project workplans and budgets related to clinical lab & supply chain activities.
 Supports in the design and development of corrective workplans to address performance issues identified in the sub-network of the PEPFAR supported regions.
 Contributes to the preparation of timely and accurate technical reports specific to EpiC Ghana clinical HIV activities.
 Contributes to the achievement of high-quality results in accordance with the targets identified in the work plan and Performance Monitoring and Evaluation Plan.
 Contributes to providing and reviewing weekly and monthly performance data
 Reviews key performance indicators pertaining to missed appointment and IIT patient tracking, ART patient retention, and VL coverage and suppression
 Contributes to program quality according to FHI 360 standards including quality assurance and quality improvement initiatives.
 Receives technical guidance and mentorship from senior staff, including the HIV Technical Advisor at the designated areas of activity implementation and other settings as appropriate for the EpiC Ghana project.
 Takes swift action to implement technical recommendations from the HIV Technical Advisor, the facilities, the health department, and other relevant entities.
 Assists in developing lessons learned from activities related to clinical and laboratory services and management for HIV care and treatment within EpiC Ghana and contribute to applying these lessons to improve both existing programs and the design of new programs.
 Contributes to writing success stories to demonstrate the impact of the project by identifying successes and key achievements pertaining to clinical care and services.
 Perform other duties as assigned.
 Qualifications: 
 Medical Doctor with specialization in family medicine, infectious diseases, internal medicine, or a related field.
 6+ years of relevant experience in technical and program management in HIV-care settings, including a minimum of 5 years’ experience  in supervision and oversight of program implementation with skills and competencies in providing technical mentoring and coaching
 5+ years of relevant experience in handling, interpretation and integration into the relevant electronic platforms (EMR, E-Sante, PLR) of different lab test results such as Viral load testing, PCR testing for EID, TB testing, IO diagnostics, self-testing, EMR of the HIV laboratory management.
 Experience in assisting with technical capacity strengthening and supporting sub-partners, especially those working with PLHIV.
 Previous experience working with USAID or PEPFAR supported programs.
 Ability to meet tight deadlines and deliver high volumes of work with minimal supervision.
 Excellent report writing, analytical, and communication skills, including oral presentation skills.
 Familiarity with Ghana public health sector, NGOs in Ghana is highly desirable.
 Cultural sensitivity and sound understanding of the needs of high risk populations and PLHIV.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications such as MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, and well-developed computer skills.
 Ability to travel within the departments of the PEPFAR supported regions, nationally, and internationally if needed.
 Fluency in English with strong written and oral communication skills

 The Senior Technical Advisor (STA), workforce optimization provides technical leadership and support for health supply chain workforce development.  This position is responsible for ensuring workforce development and capacity-building activities are planned, coordinated, and implemented effectively to strengthen the competencies of health supply chain professionals.

 The Advisor promotes the appropriate use of electronic technologies and innovative learning approaches to strengthen supply chain competencies.  The Senior Technical Advisor (STA), Workforce Optimization provides technical leadership and support for health supply chain workforce development. The role supports the development and implementation of workforce development strategies, capacity-building plans, and institutional strengthening initiatives in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, PO-RALG, MSD, and other relevant stakeholders. The position is responsible for ensuring well-coordinated and effective implementation of these strategies to strengthen the competencies and performance of health supply chain professionals.

Senior Technical Officer, Emergency Response Analyst (Technical Officer III)   
 Job Summary:   
 The Senior Technical Officer, Emergency Response Analyst occupies a critical role within the STrengthening Infectious disease DEtection Systems (STRIDES) Activity, including overseeing the execution of day-to-day data analytics and data visualization tasks for emergency and outbreak response activities, implementing policies and processes, and ensuring quality data collection, analysis, and reporting to ensure evidence-based decision-making. This position will provide home office analytics backstopping to a large-scale global project, working directly with country teams, technical teams in the home office, global partners and clients, to ensure that FHI 360 is fulfilling its mission as an evidence-driven, adaptive and effective actor on the global stage. The incumbent plays a crucial role in providing quality assurance for monitoring, evaluation and learning. Strong communication and teamwork skills are of absolute importance to succeed in this role, as is the ability to manage individual and team contributions across projects and time zones. This position offers vast opportunities for creative, passionate individuals who care about development, and who have demonstrated commitment and success in infusing learning and adaptive management into development programs.   
 Accountabilities:   
 Technical Requirements:  
 Provides project staff with overall technical direction and guidance to support planning, implementation of, and reporting against STRIDES Activity Emergency and Outbreak Response tasks.  
 Supports technical aspects of analytical systems for projects as well as staff and partner capacity building in data use for decision making.  
 Monitors and maintains project protocols, instruments, data sets, manuals, training materials and reports related to monitoring and evaluation of projects.  
 Works closely with the team to ensure data analysis and visualization implementation remains technically sound and adheres to company strategy and standard operating procedures (SOPs).  
 Develops dashboards, data analysis summaries, and other analytics products to support programmatic decision making and contribute to technical reports, briefs, and other technical documents.  
 Conducts analysis of monitoring data and epidemiological intelligence data to identify areas for improvement and propose appropriate technical strategy and guidelines.  
 Assists with the implementation of research studies by providing technical support and overall management to ensure coordination and field-level implementation.  
 Provides mentorship and team building at the task level.  
 Collaborates with the project team to interpret data sets and other assessment findings. 
 Develops and monitors MEL plans and budgets.   
 Participates in client / funder meetings and drafts report presentations.    
 Project Design Implementation:   Develops strategies and tools for the design and implementation of specific technical components of MEL systems.   
 Monitors analytics deliverables and reports to supervisors.   
 Leads analytics and data visualization activities and sub activities and assists with their implementation in close collaboration with country teams.   
 Identifies and raises issues to senior technical staff.   
 Functions as the technical lead with oversight of analytics and visualizations for technical deliverables.   
 Operations Management:   Ensures data analysis activities are on track with work plans, with technical expertise informing project implementation.   
 Oversees analytics specific timelines and MEL activity budgets. Assists in the development of donor reports and presentations.   
 Collects technical tracking data on Emergency Response activities; prepares reports.   
 Coordinates procurement need and technical specifications for procurements.    
 Project/Program Reporting:   Prepares reports and papers summarizing project results and analyzing data sets and technical assessment findings.   
 Establishes and maintains SOW and budget tracking systems for emergency response data analytics activities.   
 Drafts/prepares analytics technical reports . 
 Creates data analytics technical content (e.g., reports, presentations).    
 Quality Assurance:   Develops in-depth knowledge of quality standards through formalized system that documents processes, procedures, and responsibilities for achieving quality policies and objectives.   
 Coordinates and direct activities to meet client/funder and regulatory requirements. 
 Applied Knowledge & Skills:   
   In-depth knowledge of Emergency Response data analytics and visualization concepts, practices, and procedures with providing technical support for emergency response activities.   
 Development of scope of work and deliverables for partners, consultants, etc.   
 Deep knowledge of technical and quality standards for data analytics and epidemiological intelligence for emergency response.   
 Proficiency with database management software, business intelligence tools, and on-line search tools required.  
 Has sensitivity to cultural diversity and understanding of the political, contextual, and ethical issues in assigned areas.   
 Articulate, professional, and able to communicate in a clear, positive manner with clients and staff.   
 Must be able to read, write, and speak fluent English.   
 Ability to read, write, and speak fluent French is strongly preferred.   
 Excellent organizational and analytical skills.   
 Excellent and demonstrated project management skills.   
 Demonstrated proficiency with using Microsoft Office Suite required.   
 Ability to analyze and interpret data, identify errors, and prepare reports.   
 Ability to solve problems and implement corrective action as needed.   
 Creativity, problem solving, demonstrated ability to effectively collaborate with others and independent thought are a must.    
 Education:   
 Master’s Degree required in one of the following or related fields: epidemiology, data science, biostatistics, public health, or equivalent.    
 Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.   
 Experience:    
 At least 6 years of experience developing and implementing data analytics and visualization methodologies for global health programs, 7-8 preferred.    
 Prior work experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO), government agency, or private organization.   
 Experience working with diverse teams and applying research-to-practice principles to support program implementation.    
 Experience effectively communicating and utilizing research and technical content for practical application; direct experience with Knowledge Management and Communication a plus.   
 Prior work experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO) or in work-related academic, governmental, or industry setting, experience working internationally highly desirable.   Experience working with emergency response and infectious disease outbreaks strongly preferred.   
 Typical Physical Demands:   
 Typical office environment.   
 Ability to spend long hours looking at computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.   
 Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time.   
 Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.   
   Technology to be Used:   
 Personal Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.   
 Travel Requirements:   
 10% - 25%

Job Summary: 
 The Strengthening Infectious Disease Detection Systems (STRIDES) activity in Vietnam is seeking a Senior Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) Officer to support country-level implementation of STRIDES indicators by managing data collection, supporting country reporting, and contributing to learning and management of STRIDES implementation in country. The officer will support the development and operationalization of MEL tools and dashboards to enable evidence-based decision making. The officer will provide technical support and guidance to the STRIDES Vietnam team, ensuring MEL activities are implemented according to the Activity MEL Plan (AMELP) and organization standards. Working closely with STRIDES Vietnam and STRIDES US teams, the MEL officer will contribute to and help manage country capacity building for staff and country partners, support data quality assurance, and promote data use for program improvement.
 Accountabilities: 
 Technical Requirements: 
 Supports leading and managing country level implementation of MEL systems, tools, and procedures to collect, collate, analyze, and use data that demonstrates program progress and accountability.
 Tracks STRIDES Vietnam indicators at the country level and produces reports and projects to inform STRIDES teams and leadership
 Provides project staff with MEL related direction and guidance in line with STRIDES expected outcomes.
 Supports MEL aspects of STRIDES implementation, including staff and partner capacity building.
 Monitors and maintains project protocols, instruments, data sets, manuals, training materials and reports related to MEL
 Assists with the implementation technical activities by providing technical support, monitoring, and documenting processes.
 Provides mentorship and team building at the task level.
 Collaborates with STRIDES US MEL team to interpret data sets and other assessment findings.
 Provides technical support in the development and dissemination of tools, materials, reports, papers, and intervention for research projects.
 Provides technical input on MEL best practices to assist with STRIDES implementation in Vietnam
 Assists with implementing components of the technical portions of the STRIDES Vietnam work plan
 Develops and monitors MEL aspects of technical work plans and budgets.
 Participate in client / funder meetings and draft reports / presentations related to MEL work in country
 Project Design Implementation: 
 Implements components of the AMELP at the country level
 Contributes to the documentation of lessons learned and supports knowledge sharing in country and across STRIDES Vietnam
 Provides technical input on monitoring and evaluation portions of project workplans and reports
 Develops strategies and tools for the design and implementation of specific MEL components.
 Monitors MEL-related deliverables and reports to supervisors.
 Leads MEL-focused project activities and sub activities and assists with project implementation.
 May implement components of the technical portions of the STRIDES Vietnam workplan
 Identifies and raises issues to senior technical staff.
 Functions as the technical lead with oversight of project MEL administrative and finance compliance, MEL deliverables, and MEL team management,
 Operations Management (Finance, HR, etc.): 
 Ensures project MEL activities are on track with work plans, with technical expertise informing project implementation.
 Creates technical content (e.g., reports, presentations, manuscripts) related to MEL work in country
 Quality Assurance: 
 Supports data quality assurance activities, including validation, verification, and monitoring of country-level MEL data
 Develops in-depth knowledge of quality standards through formalized system that documents processes, procedures, and responsibilities for achieving quality policies and objectives.
 Coordinates and directs MEL activities to meet client and regulatory requirements.
 Applied Knowledge & Skills: 
 In-depth knowledge of MEL concepts, practices, and procedures for country level monitoring
 Broad knowledge of MEL quality standards
 Proficiency with database management software and data visualization tools such as Excel, Tableau, Power BI, etc.
 Has sensitivity to cultural diversity and understanding of the political, contextual, and ethical issues in assigned areas.
 Articulate, professional, and able to communicate in a clear, positive manner with clients and staff.
 Must be able to read, write, and speak fluent English.
 Excellent organizational and analytical skills.
 Excellent and demonstrated project management skills.
 Ability to influence and collaborate with others.
 Demonstrated proficiency with using Microsoft Office Suite required.
 Ability to analyze and interpret data, identify errors, and prepare reports.
 Ability to solve problems and implement corrective action as needed.
 Problem Solving & Impact: 
 Works on problems of moderate to complex scope that require review of various factors.
 Exercises good judgment with selecting methods and techniques to determine appropriate action.
 Decisions may cause delays and affect a work unit or area within a department.
 Identifies and raises issues to senior technical staff
 Networks with key internal and external personnel.
 Decision may cause delays or failure to achieve results that impact departmental goals.
 Supervision Given/Received: 
 Determines methods and procedures on new projects and assignments.
 Serves as team lead and may mentor other lower-level personnel.
 May supervisor junior level staff.
 Reports to the STRIDES Vietnam Project Director
 Education: ** ** 
 Master’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Data Science, Monitoring and Evaluation, Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, International Development, Human Development, or a Related Field.
 Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.
 Experience: ** ** 
 Typically requires 6+ years of relevant experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, including managing data collection, analysis, and reporting at the program or project level..
 Prior work experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO), government agency, or international organization preferred.
 Proficiency with data visualization tools and statistical software (e.g., Excel, Tableau, Power BI, SPSS, Stata, or similar) preferred.
 Experience supporting MEL capacity building, data quality assurance, and evidence-based decision-making is desirable.

 Typical office environment.
 Ability to spend long hours looking at computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.
 Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time.
 Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.

 Personal Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

 10% - 25%

Contribuye activamente al fortalecimiento de capacidades locales en M&E, asegurando que los datos reflejen con precisión el desempeño del proyecto y cumplan con los estándares del donante.
 El puesto requiere habilidades analíticas, conocimiento profundo de los indicadores de VIH, manejo de herramientas digitales de seguimiento, y capacidad para coordinar procesos de validación en campo. Aunque no está directamente vinculado a funciones financieras o de desarrollo de negocios, el Oficial de M&E colabora en la planificación técnica, el diseño de herramientas de monitoreo y la sistematización de resultados para informar decisiones estratégicas.
 Los técnicos (niveles I a III) prestan diversos servicios técnicos y administrativos de complejidad creciente para apoyar la ejecución de proyectos y la elaboración de propuestas. Se espera que quienes ocupen estos puestos demuestren un nivel de competencia cada vez mayor en el área técnica específica correspondiente.
 Responsabilidad y funciones: 
 Complejidad y resolución de problemas:
 Diseñar y actualizar herramientas de recolección de datos clínicos y comunitarios.
 Validar la calidad de los datos en bases clínicas, comunitarias e índices, asegurando coherencia entre registros físicos y digitales.
 Apoyar en la elaboración de informes técnicos, presentaciones y resúmenes de hallazgos.
 Monitorear indicadores clave y alertar sobre inconsistencias.
 Coordinar procesos de validación en campo, incluyendo revisión de expedientes, entrevistas técnicas y retroalimentación a socios.
 Documentar buenas prácticas, hallazgos y recomendaciones técnicas para mejorar la calidad del dato.
 Resolver problemas relacionados con la implementación técnica de proyectos y recomendar acciones correctivas según sea necesario.
 Colaborar en la resolución de problemas técnicos y guiar el análisis de datos.
 Proporcionar información técnica para la planificación del trabajo y supervisar el desarrollo de los planes de trabajo.
 Discreción e impacto: 
 Brindar apoyo en los aspectos técnicos de la implementación del proyecto, ofreciendo orientación y asegurando el cumplimiento de las prácticas establecidas.
 Las decisiones que se tomen pueden afectar a unidades de trabajo o áreas específicas dentro de un departamento.
 Proporcionar control y garantía de calidad para los informes del proyecto y la documentación técnica. 
 Colaboración e interacción:

 Brindar apoyo y coordinación en materia de investigación, capacitación, eventos y reuniones, con asistencia técnica y administrativa.

 Conocimiento del proceso de validación de calidad de datos (DQA) de indicadores de VIH.
 Conocimientos básicos de conceptos de investigación técnica, con capacidad para apoyar estudios de investigación técnica.

Contexte   
 FHI 360 est une organisation internationale de développement humain qui intervient notamment dans les domaines de la santé, de la nutrition et du renforcement des systèmes de santé.
 Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ses projets au Sénégal, FHI 360 assure l’acquisition de biens, d’équipements médicaux, de mobilier hospitalier et de services nécessaires à la réalisation des activités programmatiques, y compris l’équipement et la réhabilitation de structures sanitaires.
 Le/La Procurement Officer apporte un appui opérationnel à la planification, à l’exécution et au suivi des activités d’approvisionnement. Il/Elle est notamment chargé(e) d’identifier les fournisseurs, de solliciter et d’analyser les offres, de négocier les conditions d’achat et de coordonner les livraisons, tout en veillant au respect des politiques et procédures de FHI 360, des exigences contractuelles et des règles applicables des bailleurs de fonds.
 En collaboration avec les équipes techniques et programmatiques, il/elle veille à ce que les acquisitions répondent aux besoins du projet, aux spécifications techniques approuvées, aux contraintes budgétaires et aux calendriers de mise en œuvre.
 Une attention particulière sera accordée aux acquisitions d’équipements médicaux et de mobilier hospitalier, ainsi qu’à la coordination des achats avec les travaux de réhabilitation et la mise en service des structures sanitaires.
 Responsabilités principales 
 Gestion des achats et approvisionnements 
 Fournir un appui opérationnel aux activités d’approvisionnement de FHI 360 au Sénégal.
 Préparer et exécuter les procédures d’achat conformément aux politiques internes, aux seuils d’approbation et aux exigences applicables des bailleurs.
 Préparer les demandes de cotation (RFQ), les dossiers de consultation et les appels d’offres selon la procédure applicable.
 Solliciter des offres auprès de fournisseurs qualifiés et assurer une mise en concurrence équitable et transparente.
 Obtenir des devis et négocier les prix, les délais de livraison, les conditions contractuelles, les garanties et les services après-vente.
 Préparer les tableaux comparatifs des offres et les dossiers de justification de sélection des fournisseurs.
 Soumettre les dossiers aux niveaux d’approbation requis avant tout engagement contractuel ou émission de commande.
 Préparer les bons de commande et assurer leur transmission aux fournisseurs après approbation.
 Suivre les commandes et anticiper les risques de retard, de dépassement budgétaire ou de non-conformité.
 Acquisition d’équipements médicaux 
 Participer à l’acquisition d’équipements médicaux, de matériel de diagnostic, d’équipements de maternité, de laboratoire et de consultation, ainsi que de mobilier hospitalier.
 Collaborer avec les équipes médicales, biomédicales et programmatiques pour définir et valider les spécifications techniques.
 Vérifier la conformité des offres aux exigences techniques, fonctionnelles et contractuelles.
 Examiner les garanties, la disponibilité des pièces de rechange, les conditions de maintenance et les services après-vente proposés.
 Contribuer à l’évaluation des fournisseurs en tenant compte de leur expérience, de leur capacité de livraison et de la qualité des produits.
 Coordonner le suivi des livraisons, de l’installation et de la mise en service des équipements lorsque ces prestations sont prévues au marché.
 Veiller à la disponibilité des documents techniques, certificats, manuels et garanties requis.
 Participer à la réception des équipements et documenter toute réserve ou non-conformité constatée.
 Achats liés à la réhabilitation des structures sanitaires

TITRE DU POSTE: HIV Supply Chain Advisor / Chargé de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement VIH

 Introduction : 
  Family Health International (FHI 360) est une Organisation Non Gouvernementale (ONG) à but non lucratif, dédiée à l’amélioration de la vie de façon durable via des solutions intégrées. FHI 360, est présente dans plusieurs pays et dans tous les États et territoires des États-Unis et intervient dans les domaines de la santé, de l’éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, de l'économie et du développement, de la recherche et technologie, créant ainsi une combinaison unique de capacités pour relever les défis du développement.
 FHI 360 est une organisation de développement humain à but non lucratif dédiée à améliorer les vies de manière durable par l'avancement de solutions intégrées, conduites localement. Le personnel comprend des experts en santé, éducation, nutrition, environnement, développement économique, société civile ; en genre, jeunesse, recherche et technologie, créant ainsi un mix unique de capacités pour relever les défis du développement.
 Contexte : 
  À la suite de la décision du Département d'État américain de transférer les activités de chaîne d'approvisionnement VIH et Paludisme au Togo de GHSC-PSM vers FHI 360, le/la Chargé(e) de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement VIH pilotera l'appui technique quotidien au ministère de la Santé, à la CAMEG-Togo et au PNLS-HV-IST pour renforcer la gestion des produits VIH, conformément au cadre de travail AF-GHS de FHI 360.
 Résumé du poste 
 Le/la Chargé(e) de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement VIH fournit un appui technique et un mentorat direct aux acteurs nationaux et au niveau des sites afin d'assurer la disponibilité continue des produits VIH, appuie les processus de quantification et de prévision, et contribue à la feuille de route globale de transition depuis le partenaire sortant.
 Supervision: Sous la supervision du « Associate Director ,Technical » de FHI 360 Togo,
 Principales responsabilités : 
  Fournir un appui technique au ministère de la Santé et au PNLS-HV-IST en matière de quantification, de prévision et de planification des approvisionnements en produits VIH, y compris l'utilisation du Quantification Analytics Tool (QAT).
 •  Assurer l'élaboration et la soumission dans les délais du plan d'approvisionnement trimestriel VIH .
 •   Fournir un appui opérationnel à la distribution du dernier kilomètre des produits VIH achetés par le Gouvernement américain et stockés à la CAMEG, en coordination avec la CAMEG et les acteurs logistiques nationaux.
 •   Assurer un mentorat sur site auprès du personnel des formations sanitaires et laboratoires appuyés par le PEPFAR, afin de renforcer la gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement VIH au niveau des sites.
 •   Suivre les niveaux de stock des produits VIH (situation actuelle et prévisions) au niveau des sites et au niveau national, et signaler les risques de rupture ou de surstockage.
 •     Contribuer à la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route de transition élaborée dans le cadre de la mission du consultant Chaîne d'Approvisionnement de FHI 360, en particulier pour les actions relatives au VIH.
 •  Appuyer le renforcement des capacités de la CAMEG relatives aux produits VIH, afin de faciliter une transition ordonnée vers le Gouvernement du Togo.
 •  Contribuer aux données et aux éléments narratifs pour le rapportage au bailleur sur les indicateurs de la chaîne d'approvisionnement VIH.
 •   Coordonner étroitement avec le/la Chargé(e) de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement Paludisme et le/la Chargé(e) de la Gestion des Données, afin d'assurer une approche cohérente et intégrée.
 •    Renforcer la coordination avec les autres partenaires de la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Appuyer le ministère de la Santé et le Programme national de lutte contre le VIH (PNLP) dans la coordination des activités liées à la chaîne d’approvisionnement en produits contre le VIH avec les principaux partenaires nationaux et internationaux, notamment le Fonds mondial, et les autres parties prenantes concernées, afin de promouvoir une quantification harmonisée, une planification des achats, une distribution des produits et une utilisation efficace des ressources disponibles.
 Compétences et qualités requises   
 •  Diplôme en pharmacie, santé publique, logistique ou domaine connexe.
 •   Expérience avérée en gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement en santé publique, idéalement sur les produits VIH et les programmes financés par le PEPFAR/Département d’Etat US
 •  Bonne connaissance des outils de quantification et de prévision (QAT ou équivalent) et des acteurs nationaux de la chaîne d'approvisionnement au Togo (CAMEG, PNLS-HV-IST, DPML).
 •    Solides compétences en facilitation et en coordination, avec une expérience de mentorat auprès du personnel des formations sanitaires et des laboratoires.
 •      Maîtrise du français exigé ; bonne connaissance pratique de l'anglais pour le rapportage au bailleur.

TITRE DU POSTE : Senior Technical Officer, Supply Chain Data Management / Analyste Senior de la Gestion des Données de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement 
 TEAM/PROGRAMME: EpiC Togo 
 Lieu : Lomé, Togo, avec déplacements dans les régions appuyées
 Type de Contrat : National, CDD, Durée : Période du financement AF-GHS (octobre 2026 – septembre 2027), renouvelable. 
 Introduction : 
 Family Health International (FHI 360) est une Organisation Non Gouvernementale (ONG) à but non lucratif, dédiée à l’amélioration de la vie de façon durable via des solutions intégrées. FHI 360, est présente dans plusieurs pays et dans tous les États et territoires des États-Unis et intervient dans les domaines de la santé, de l’éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, de l'économie et du développement, de la recherche et technologie, créant ainsi une combinaison unique de capacités pour relever les défis du développement.
 FHI 360 est une organisation de développement humain à but non lucratif dédiée à améliorer les vies de manière durable par l'avancement de solutions intégrées, conduites localement. Le personnel comprend des experts en santé, éducation, nutrition, environnement, développement économique, société civile ; en genre, jeunesse, recherche et technologie, créant ainsi un mix unique de capacités pour relever les défis du développement.
 Contexte  : 
 Alors que FHI 360 reprend les activités de chaîne d'approvisionnement VIH et Paludisme au Togo, auparavant assurées par GHSC-PSM (Chemonics), la fiabilité des systèmes de données est centrale à la réussite de la transition. Le/la Chargé(e) de la Gestion des Données de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement pilotera le travail transversal de renforcement des systèmes d'information de gestion logistique (SIGL) et de visibilité des données, contribuera au renforcement du SIGL et à un portail unifié de données de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, et permettra aux Chargé(e)s de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement VIH et Paludisme de suivre la performance à partir de données fiables et à jour.
 Résumé du poste  :
 Le/la Chargé(e) de la Gestion des Données de la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement veille à ce que les données de la chaîne d'approvisionnement — niveaux de stock, distribution, quantification — soient exactes, visibles et utilisées pour la prise de décision à tous les niveaux, de la formation sanitaire jusqu'au niveau national. Ce poste intervient de manière transversale sur les composantes VIH et Paludisme et joue un rôle central dans la documentation et le transfert des systèmes et outils de données depuis le partenaire sortant.
 Supervision : Sous la supervision de l'Associate Director, Strategic Information (SI) de FHI 360 Togo 
 Principales responsabilités : 
 •         Renforcer les systèmes d'information de gestion logistique (SIGL), les flux de données et la visibilité des données sur les composantes VIH et Paludisme, au niveau des sites, régional et national.

 veille à la bonne gestion financière, administrative et logistique des activités et s'assure que l'ensemble des interventions du projet EDS dans sa province d'affectation respecte les politiques, procédures et normes de FHI 360, ainsi que les exigences des bailleurs de fonds.  
 Responsabilités   
 Assure la direction et la supervision de la mise en œuvre du projet, de son lancement à sa clôture.  
 Représente l’organisation et assure la coordination des interventions dans le domaine des EDS, notamment auprès des autorités gouvernementales, des piliers de la riposte à Ebola, des partenaires humanitaires, des leaders communautaires et des organisations de la société civile.  
 Veille à ce que l’ensemble des opérations, des activités, des dépenses et des procédures administratives soit conforme au plan de travail et au budget approuvé du projet.  
 Supervise les activités quotidiennes du projet en accordant une attention particulière à la gestion logistiques et financières et au fonctionnement administratif global du projet.  
 Soutient le renforcement des capacités du personnel en matière de coordination et de gestion de la mise en œuvre des activités, afin de garantir leur bonne exécution, leur qualité et le respect des exigences de redevabilité.  
 Encadre, conseille et supervise le personnel du projet, en veillant à une définition claire des plans de travail et des priorités du projet et en encourageant le travail d’équipe.  
 Élabore et présente les plans de travail, la documentation, les outils de formations, les présentations et les propositions budgétaires à la direction et au personnel.  
 Anticipe et identifie les difficultés susceptibles d’affecter la mise en œuvre du projet, propose des solutions adaptées et met en place des mesures correctives afin de garantir le respect des délais et du budget.  
 Apporte un soutien à l’équipe de terrain afin de garantir la qualité, l’efficacité et la conformité aux normes et politiques applicables au projet et à FHI 360.  
 Établit, développe et renforce les partenariats stratégiques clés pour favoriser la mise en œuvre efficace du projet.   
 En collaboration avec les chargés de la sécurité et les charges de l’EC, effectue une analyse continue du contexte opérationnel et sécuritaire. Définit et met en œuvre    
 des mesures d’adaptations et d'atténuation des risques et des incidents, et des mesures de protection du personnel, des partenaires et des biens du projet.  
 Connaissances et compétences   
 Maîtrise approfondie des principes et outils de gestion de projet, notamment en matière de planification budgétaire, d’élaboration de plans de travail et de suivi de la performance.  
 Capacité à analyser et à suivre l’exécution du budget, à assurer une supervision financière rigoureuse et à veiller au respect des exigences des bailleurs de fonds.  
 Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale, avec une capacité avérée à influencer, convaincre et négocier avec les principales parties prenantes.  
 Capacité à gérer simultanément des priorités concurrentes et à superviser plusieurs projets complexes dans des environnements exigeants.  
 Expérience confirmée en management et en supervision d’équipes, y compris dans des contextes opérationnels complexes.  
 Expérience avérée dans la supervision de la mise en œuvre de programmes d’urgence humanitaire ou de santé publique.  
 Bonne connaissance des Normes humanitaires fondamentales (CHS), des standards Sphère et des principes du Code de conduite du Mouvement international de la Croix-Rouge et du Croissant-Rouge et des ONG.  
 Expérience de collaboration avec des bailleurs de fonds institutionnels, notamment le gouvernement des États-Unis (USG).  
 Formation et experience   
 Licence ou équivalent international en développement international, sciences sociales, gestion d'entreprise, société civile, communication, développement économique, environnement, santé ou tout autre domaine connexe.  
 Un master ou tout autre diplôme de deuxième cycle est un atout.  
 Une certification en gestion de projet est un atout.  
 Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente en gestion de projet, avec une expérience confirmée dans la coordination et la supervision de projets complexes ainsi que dans le management d’équipes, et des résultats démontrés.  
 Expérience préalable au sein d’une organisation non gouvernementale (ONG), d’une agence gouvernementale ou d’une organisation privée.  
 Solide expérience en gestion budgétaire, suivi financier et rapports de projet.  
 Expérience antérieure dans la représentation d’une organisation non gouvernementale auprès des autorités locales, d’autres organisations partenaires et des mécanismes de coordination humanitaire.  
 Excellentes capacités de travail en équipe et aptitude à favoriser le dialogue et à rechercher des consensus avec des interlocuteurs de différents niveaux hiérarchiques et institutionnels.  
 Maîtrise du français tant à l’écrit qu’à l’oral ; la connaissance du swahili, du lingala et de l’anglais sont des atouts considérables.  
 Encadrement hiérarchique    
 Relève du Conseiller Technique Principal en Santé Globale (GHS Senior Technical Advisor).  
 Supervise une équipe de chargés EDS, et de chargés EC.  
 Technologie et outils utilisés   
 Ordinateur, Microsoft Office 365 (c'est-à-dire Word, Excel, PowerPoint, messagerie électronique), téléphone professionnel, téléphone portable et imprimante/photocopieuse.  
 Déplacements    
 Entre 25% et 50 % du temps de travail, dans la province de l’Ituri ou la province du Nord Kivu.  
 Critères Minima de Recrutement    
 FHI 360 offre une rémunération compétitive et est un employeur qui souscrit au principe de l'égalité

offres.titre: Coordonnateur(trice) des équipes de reponse rapide-- RTT/Surge Coordinator
offres.description:
Contexte    
 FHI 360 est une organisation à but non lucratif dédiée au développement humain qui s'engage à améliorer durablement les conditions de vie en proposant des solutions intégrées et adaptées au contexte local. Notre personnel comprend des experts dans les domaines de la santé, de l'éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, du développement économique, de la jeunesse, de la recherche, de la technologie, de la communication et du marketing social, créant ainsi un ensemble unique de compétences pour relever les défis interdépendants du développement actuel. FHI 360 intervient dans l’ensemble des États et territoires des États-Unis ainsi que dans plusieurs pays à travers le monde, dont la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) ou elle met en œuvre le programme Strengthening Infectious Disease Detection System (STRIDES), programme mondial financé par le Département d’État des États-Unis (DoS) visant à renforcer les capacités des pays à prévenir, détecter et répondre rapidement aux épidémies et aux menaces de maladies infectieuses.  
 Description du poste  
 Le/la Coordinateur(trice) des Equipes de Réponse Rapide (ERR – Rapid Response Team ou RRT en anglais) supervise la préparation, la mobilisation, l’appui au déploiement et le retrait des équipes multidisciplinaires de réponse rapide et du personnel de renfort mobilisés pour soutenir la riposte de STRIDES à l’épidémie Ebola. À ce titre, il/elle assure la gestion des viviers de personnel mobilisable, veille à leur bonne préparation, coordonne la composition des équipes et organise les procédures de déploiement. Il/elle s’assure également que le personnel, les kits d’intervention (Go-Kits), les fournitures et les moyens logistiques et opérationnels nécessaires sont disponibles et prêts à permettre un déploiement rapide et sécurisé.  
 En étroite collaboration avec les structures gouvernementales de gestion des incidents, les autorités provinciales et les responsables des zones de santé, les différents piliers techniques de STRIDES et les équipes opérationnelles de FHI 360, il/elle veille à la traduction des priorités d’intervention approuvées en capacités opérationnelles sur le terrain. Il/elle coordonne également les rotations du personnel, assure le suivi des déploiements et veille à la documentation des leçons apprises. Il/elle contribue ainsi au renforcement des mécanismes d’intervention existants et au transfert progressif des capacités opérationnelles aux structures gouvernementales partenaires.  
 Le/la Coordinateur(trice) veille à ce que les équipes et les ressources soient prêtes à être mobilisées et assure la coordination de leur déploiement. Il/elle intervient dans le cadre des mandats et des responsabilités définis, les décisions finales concernant le lancement des déploiements, les orientations techniques, l’engagement des dépenses et les autorisations de sécurité restant du ressort des responsables habilités.  
 Responsabilités  
 Préparation et gestion de la liste d’intervention d’urgence  
 Assure la mise à jour d’une base de données consolidée des membres des équipes de réponse rapide, des spécialistes d’appoint et des remplaçants. Veille à ce que les informations relatives à leurs compétences, formations, langues parlées, localisation, disponibilité, historique de déploiement et habilitations requises soient régulièrement actualisées, dans le respect des règles de confidentialité et de protection des données personnelles.  
 Définit les différents niveaux de disponibilité opérationnelle des membres des équipes de réponse rapide, des spécialistes d’appoint et des remplaçants et en assurer la vérification régulière. Met en adéquation les compétences et les ressources disponibles avec les besoins géographiques et les exigences de déploiements simultanés, identifie les éventuelles insuffisances en personnel et propose des mesures pour y remédier.  
 Définit, en concertation avec les responsables techniques, les compétences minimales requises pour chaque type de déploiement. Élabore et actualise le plan de préparation et de mobilisation des renforts couvrant l’ensemble du processus : activation, mise en attente, mobilisation, organisation des rotations, remplacement du personnel et fin de déploiement.  
 Coordonne les sessions d’orientation, les formations de remise à niveau, les exercices pratiques et les simulations afin de maintenir le niveau de préparation des équipes. Actualise les listes de contacts et les procédures d’escalade entre les différents services concernés, notamment les équipes d’intervention, les opérations, la sécurité et les services chargés de l’orientation.  
 Planification de l’activation et du déploiement  
 Définit et soumet à approbation les critères d’activation, d’escalade, de prolongation et de clôture des interventions, en prenant en compte la répartition géographique des besoins, des exigences liées aux enquêtes urgentes, des insuffisances des capacités locales et des demandes de déploiement dûment autorisées.  
 Examine et documente les demandes de déploiement en évaluant notamment leur degré d’urgence, leur localisation, la durée prévue de l’intervention et les dispositifs d’appui déjà assurés par les partenaires. En concertation avec les responsables techniques et les homologues gouvernementaux, définit les objectifs de chaque mission, les résultats attendus, les profils d’expertise nécessaires ainsi que les conditions et critères de fin d’intervention.  
 Planification des déploiements et soutien opérationnel  
 Recommande la taille et la composition des équipes en fonction des besoins opérationnels et des compétences requises, notamment en matière de surveillance, d’épidémiologie, de laboratoire, de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI) et de biosécurité (BSS), de coordination avec les équipes d’Engagement Communautaire (EC) régionales, de système d’information et de gestion des données (SIG), de logistique et d’autres domaines pertinents. Propose un(e) cheff(e) de mission et veille à la définition claire des rôles, des responsabilités, des modalités de supervision et des lignes hiérarchiques.  
 Prépare les termes de référence des missions, les plans de travail, les budgets, les itinéraires de déplacement, les évaluations des risques, les plans de communication et les autorisations nécessaires. Assure le suivi des demandes à chaque étape du processus de validation et de mobilisation, documente les éventuels retards et signale les contraintes aux responsables concernés.  
 Veille à ce que la sélection des membres des équipes tienne compte de la diversité des profils et des expériences culturelles, afin de favoriser la complémentarité des compétences, la collaboration, l’esprit d’équipe et le professionnalisme au sein des équipes d’intervention.  
 Mobilisation et préparation au déploiement  
 Coordonne la mobilisation des ressources humaines, financières, matérielles et logistiques nécessaires au déploiement, en collaboration avec les services concernés (ressources humaines, finances, approvisionnement, logistique, administration et sécurité). Veille à la confirmation des affectations, des déplacements, de l’hébergement, du transport, des moyens de communication, du financement et des modalités d’accueil des équipes sur le terrain.  
 Vérifie que les membres des équipes ont suivi les formations obligatoires et obtenu les habilitations requises en matière de santé et de sécurité au travail. S’assure que les listes de contrôle préalables au déploiement sont dûment renseignées et signale toute insuffisance susceptible de compromettre la préparation des équipes avant leur départ.  
 Organise les briefings préalables au déploiement afin de présenter aux équipes les objectifs et les modalités de la mission, les lignes hiérarchiques, le contexte local, les procédures de sécurité, les exigences en matière de protection et d’engagement communautaire, ainsi que les mécanismes de signalement des incidents.
