Job Summary 
 The Senior Health Informatics & Systems Integration Analyst provides technical leadership in the development, maintenance, integration, and enhancement of health information systems, databases, and analytical applications for global and country programs under the direction of an Associate Director. The position serves as a technical expert for assigned systems, including InfoLink, FHI 360's HIV DHIS2 database, and country-level DHIS2, DHIS2 Tracker, and electronic data collection platforms. The analyst leads the design and implementation of data integrations, automated pipelines, and analytical solutions; troubleshoots complex application and data exchange issues; manages system enhancements and production changes; and works with technical and program teams to translate requirements into reliable, maintainable solutions. The position also supports data analysis, visualization, reporting, technical assistance, and capacity strengthening. 
 Responsibilities/Duties 
 Complexity & Problem Solving:  
 Lead the design, development, and implementation of technical solutions involving health information systems, database management, data integration, and analytics. Evaluate complex problems, identify appropriate methods, and implement solutions aligned with project objectives and technical standards. 
 Manage and enhance InfoLink and assigned country databases, including indicators, data elements, datasets, organization units, validation rules, and reporting configurations. Lead configuration and implementation of DHIS2, DHIS2 Tracker, and electronic data collection tools such as REDCap, ODK, and KoboToolbox. 
 Design, develop, and maintain integrations between health information systems, databases, and reporting platforms using APIs, SQL, Python, and automated ETL/ELT processes. Develop data mappings, transformation rules, and synchronization workflows to support interoperability across program, national, and donor systems. 
 Develop and maintain automated data pipelines and analytical datasets, including extraction, validation, transformation, and reconciliation of data from multiple sources. Troubleshoot integration failures, data discrepancies, and system performance issues, implementing appropriate quality controls and error-handling procedures. 
 Lead development and improvement of Power BI dashboards, data models, and analytical products. Conduct advanced program and survey data analysis, automate recurring reporting processes, and develop reusable tools and methodologies to improve technical efficiency and data use. 
 Discretion & Impact: 
 Use judgment to organize routine work and choose suitable methods within established guidance. Recommend approaches to system architecture, interoperability, and reporting, coordinating major technical decisions and resource implications with senior leadership.
 Apply checks for completeness, consistency, and accuracy; test changes against approved requirements, document results and exceptions, and follow up with responsible teams.
 Follow FHI 360 and applicable Ministry of Health requirements for data access, confidentiality, security, and identifiable health information. Escalate access or policy decisions to authorized staff.
 Produce accurate and timely outputs that support donor reporting and program management. Recognize that errors and delays can affect project delivery and departmental goals.
 Collaboration & Interaction: 
 Work with country and HQ program staff, data system specialists, developers, vendors, ministries of health, and implementing partners. Coordinate assigned work with Associate Directors, Directors, and senior technical staff, communicating findings and requests clearly.
 Provide practical user support and assist with training and demonstrations on data capture, database use, analysis, and visualization; adapt explanations to different audiences and cultural contexts.
 Prepare and update user guides, job aids, standard operating procedures, technical briefs, and training materials. Document recurring questions, solutions, and implementation lessons.
 Contribute data and technical text to reports, presentations, proposals, and scopes of work under technical leadership’s direction. Review relevant guidance and literature and present assigned work in internal, partner, or professional meetings.
 Management & Supervision: 
 Reports to an Associate Director. May provide technical oversight and guidance to junior staff, consultants, and technical teams supporting assigned activities, without necessarily having direct supervisory responsibility.
 Lead planning and coordination of assigned technical workstreams, ensuring alignment with project work plans, timelines, budgets, and deliverables. Monitor implementation progress, manage competing priorities, and identify risks and resource needs.
 Mentor colleagues, support knowledge sharing and capacity development, and contribute to improvements in technical processes, tools, and approaches.
 Embraces other duties as assigned, contributing to the team's multifaceted and evolving responsibilities.
 Qualifications 
 Knowledge & Skills:  
 Advanced knowledge of health information systems, strategic information, data management, and monitoring and evaluation, with demonstrated ability to design and implement technical solutions for complex public health programs. 
 Strong technical expertise in DHIS2 configuration and administration, including metadata management, data exchange, indicators, and DHIS2 Tracker. Experience with electronic data collection platforms such as REDCap, ODK, or KoboToolbox. 
 Proficiency in data integration and database technologies, including SQL, REST APIs, ETL/ELT processes, data transformation, and automated workflows. Experience integrating data across multiple systems and troubleshooting data exchange and synchronization issues. 
 Advanced proficiency in Power BI, Excel, and analytical tools, with experience in data modeling, visualization, validation, and automated reporting. Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical documentation, and communication skills. 
 Demonstrated ability to independently manage technical assignments, coordinate multiple deliverables, and provide technical assistance to diverse stakeholders. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and fluent written and spoken English. 
 Minimum Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's degree or its international equivalent in health informatics, public health, epidemiology, information systems, computer science, data science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience sufficient to perform the key responsibilities. 
 Typically requires 8+ years of relevant experience in health information systems, data management, systems integration, analytics, or technical assistance, including demonstrated experience designing and implementing technical solutions and supporting complex projects. Experience in an NGO, government agency, or international development setting preferred. 
 Certifications:  
 No specific certification is required. 
 Preferred Qualifications : 
 Experience with HIV or other public health programs in resource-limited settings, including integration of national health information systems with donor or program reporting platforms. 
 Familiarity with Python, Azure, SQL, Tableau, or similar data processing and reporting tools.  
 Travel 
 10%-25% travel required.
 Typical Physical Demands 
 Typical office environment. Regularly uses a computer and keyboard and other standard office equipment for data management, analysis, documentation, and communication.  
 Technology 
 Computer or laptop; DHIS2 and DHIS2 Tracker; Power BI; Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft 365 applications, including SharePoint and Teams; REDCap, ODK, and KoboToolbox; approved database, analytical, and scripting tools; mobile technology and standard office equipment.

Job Summary:
 The Malaria Technical Officer will provide technical support to FHI 360 programs, including the Meeting Targets and Maintaining Epidemic Control (EpiC) project in Cambodia and other relevant initiatives, with a primary focus on malaria surveillance, malaria elimination, and Prevention of Re-establishment (POR) of malaria transmission in target provinces. Working under the guidance of the Malaria Regional Coordinator, the position will support Provincial Health Departments (PHDs), Operational Districts (ODs), health facilities, and subawardee to implement project activities in line with national guidelines and global standards. The Malaria Regional Technical Officer will support the implementation and monitoring of technical activities, conduct supportive supervision, help address implementation challenges, and recommend practical strategies to improve program quality and effectiveness.
 The Malaria Technical Officer will support the development of technical tools and materials and contribute to progress reports, technical updates, and presentations in collaboration with the Malaria Regional Coordinator and the project team. The position will also help document lessons learned and good practices that strengthen government ownership and the transition toward sustainable, government-led implementation. As needed, the Malaria Regional Technical Officer will assist with business development efforts, including opportunity identification, proposal development, and strategic partnerships. This position will be based at a sub-office of FHI 360 located in Battambang Provincial Health Department. 
 Accountabilities:
 Technical Requirements :
 Provides technical guidance and on-site support to PHDs, ODs, health facilities, and subawardee in line with national malaria guidelines and global standards to support high-quality implementation of surveillance, POR, and malaria elimination activities.
 Supports quality assurance and quality improvement of malaria activities in assigned provinces and operational districts.
 Supports the development, adaptation, and maintenance of project tools, checklists, data sets, training materials, and reports related to surveillance, POR, and malaria elimination.
 Drafts technical briefs, reports, and other materials to document results, best practices, policies, and procedures.
 Analyzes project implementation and data to identify gaps and proposes practical solutions and corrective actions to the Malaria Regional Coordinator.
 Provides on-the-job coaching and mentoring to provincial, district, and health facility staff during supportive supervision.
 Provides technical input to the provincial components of the work plan, within the given resources and financial constraints.
 Assists with implementing the technical components of the work plan, including implementation of the POR model toward the integration of malaria POR into the Commune/Sangkat Investment Program and the preparatory documentation for subnational verification for malaria-free certification.
 Participates in coordination meetings with government counterparts, partners, and donors, and drafts meeting notes, reports, and presentations.
 Project Design Implementation :
 Supports the Malaria Regional Coordinator in coordinating malaria activities across assigned provinces and operational districts.
 Supports PHDs, ODs, and subawardee to plan and implement project activities effectively and on schedule.
 Conducts regular monitoring and supportive supervision of malaria activities at provincial, district, health facility, and community levels.
 Leads assigned technical activities and sub-activities and assists with overall project implementation.
 Monitors and follows up on project deliverables and reports progress to the Malaria Regional Coordinator.
 Identifies implementation challenges and raises issues to the Malaria Regional Coordinator for timely resolution.
 Project/Program Reporting :
 Assists the Malaria Regional Coordinator in preparing progress reports, technical updates, and presentations summarizing provincial implementation, results, and data analysis.
 Documents supervision findings, agreed follow-up actions, lessons learned, and good practices.
 Reviews subawardee and health facility reports and data for completeness, accuracy, and timeliness, and flags issues to the Malaria Regional Coordinator.
 Contributes technical content to donor reports, presentations, and other technical products as required.
 Quality Assurance :
 Supports quality improvement of malaria surveillance, POR, and elimination activities through regular review of processes, procedures, and data.
 Supports compliance of field activities with national guidelines, donor requirements, and project quality standards.
 Follows up on the implementation of corrective actions agreed during supervision visits and coordination meetings.

 Ensures assigned activities are on track with approved work plans and timelines, with technical expertise informing implementation.
 Supports the Malaria Regional Coordinator and Project Manager in monitoring project timelines and budgets, including subawardee implementation.
 Tracks Statement of Work (SOW) deliverables and activity expenditures; provides updates to the Malaria Regional Coordinator.
 Assists in collecting financial and technical tracking data and prepares reports.
 Supports government counterparts to strengthen ownership and plan for the transition to sustainable, government-led implementation.
 Coordinates logistics and procurement for field activities, including liaison with suppliers, as needed.

 In-depth knowledge of concepts, practices, global guidelines and frameworks relevant to global health security (GHS) programming.

 Experience conducting supportive supervision, on-the-job mentoring, and follow-up of field activities at provincial, district, health facility, and community levels.

 Demonstrated project management and technical skills.
 Broad knowledge of quality standards and quality assurance practices.

 Has sensitivity to cultural diversity and understanding of the political, contextual, and ethical issues in assigned areas.
 Articulate, professional, and able to communicate in a clear, positive manner with clients and staff.
 Must be able to read, write, and speak fluent English and Khmer.
 Excellent organizational and analytical skills.
 Excellent and demonstrated project management skills.
 Ability to influence and collaborate with others.
 Demonstrated proficiency with using Microsoft Office Suite required.
 Ability to analyze and interpret data, identify errors, and prepare reports.
 Ability to solve problems and implement corrective action as needed.

offres.titre: Senior Technical Advisor, STRIDES Emergency Response
offres.description:
Job Summary
 The Senior Technical Advisor for Emergency Response serves as a subject matter expert who provides leadership in designing and guiding the technical direction for highly complex emergency responses across the STRIDES global portfolio. This position will serve as a senior scientific advisor during public health emergencies and provide technical and clinical guidance to internal staff and external partners including, US Government agencies, and other implementing partners. This role is responsible for ensuring the quality of existing projects globally, setting strategies, guiding the investment of resources, and overseeing technical aspects.  The Senior Technical Advisor is accountable for developing technical strategies, operational plans, and ensuring compliance with regulatory and budgetary requirements. Specifically, this position will lead global preparedness, surveillance, and outbreak response activities for viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHF) including Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), and other high consequence pathogens. The Senior Technical Advisor will serve as a VHF technical expert and provide expert clinical recommendations and guidance around infection prevention and control strategies prior to and during such public health emergencies. The role includes staff development, mentoring, and overall responsibility for large-scale technical initiatives.
Responsibilities/Duties
 Complexity & Problem Solving: 
 Develop and oversee the technical components of complex global health emergency responses within financial constraints.
 Coordinate technical teams deployed to support cross-functional response activities. 
 Monitor epidemiological trends and use data to guide operational decision-making.
 Review surveillance reports and provide recommendations for response adjustments based on updated epidemiological data. 
 Facilitate daily incident management meetings, situation reviews, and operational planning sessions.
 Ensure alignment of response activities with national and international Ebola response protocols and guidelines. 
 Guide the development of best practices and ensure technical implementation aligns with global gold standards for emergency response.
 Create mitigation plans to proactively identify risks or challenges to technical deliverables.
 Discretion & Impact: 
 Exercise significant judgment in decision-making that impacts project outcomes, financial budgets, and organizational goals.
 Ensure technical components meet funder contractual obligations and regulatory compliance for highly complex units.
 Provides project staff with overall technical direction and guidance in line with STRIDES’ expected outcomes.
 Monitors and maintains project protocols, instruments, data sets, manuals, training materials and reports related to technical area of expertise.
 Collaboration & Interaction: 
 Foster collaborative relationships with donors, government agencies, and NGOs to support project execution.
 Lead client and funder meetings, acting as the primary point of contact for technical activities.
 Provide technical input in business development meetings and client presentations.
 Maintain consistent technical exchange with field counterparts, implementing partners, and internal stakeholders.
 Management & Supervision: 
 Provide technical oversight of STRIDES BVD outbreak preparedness and response activities globally.
 Supervise and mentor technical staff, providing guidance to ensure high-quality project execution and professional development.
 Manage staff assignments and workload distribution to meet project timelines and deliverables.
 Provide guidance to deployed response teams, government counterparts and implementing partners
 Provide strategic leadership in the preparation of financial and technical reports for sponsors and partners.
 Embraces other duties as assigned, contributing to the team’s multifaceted and evolving responsibilities.
Qualifications
 Knowledge & Skills: 
 In-depth knowledge of technical aspects of emergency response management, including clinical, epidemiological, laboratory, and data systems. .
 Expertise in donor-funded projects and deep understanding of the emergency response environment, including political, legal, and financial influences.
 Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage complex, multi-departmental challenges.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience in publishing technical documents, peer-reviewed articles, and external communications.
 Fluency in English and French, with additional language skills preferred
Minimum Qualifications: 
 Master’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Public Health, Infectious Diseases, Microbiology, or a related field.
 Typically requires 8+ years of relevant experience in technical implementation, capacity building, and business development, with documented exp. providing technical assistance on large-scale projects.
 Experience in project management within an NGO, government agency, or private organization setting, with demonstrated success in developing and managing technical deliverables.
Preferred Qualifications: 
 Doctorate Degree in a related field preferred, preferably a Medical Degree with training in Infectious Diseases.
 Trained by the US CDC Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS)
 Significant international outbreak response/deployment experience
 Demonstrated technical expertise in the field with publication in peer reviewed journals.
 Project Management (PM) Certification.
Travel 
 Up to 25% travel required.

The Compensation Band for all national local employees aligns to the Compensation Structure based on the Country location of the job.
 The expected US Based hiring salary range for this role is listed below. Candidates FHI 360 pay ranges represent national averages that vary by geographic location. When determining an offer amount, FHI 360 factors in multiple considerations, including but not limited to: relevant years of experience and education possessed by the applicant, internal equity, business sector, and budget. For internal candidates, salary placement will also follow FHI 360’s current promotional increase guidelines.  Location                                  Dhaka, Bangladesh 
  FHI 360 is a nonprofit human development organization dedicated to improving lives in lasting ways by advancing integrated, locally driven solutions. Our staff includes experts in health, education, nutrition, economic development, youth, research, technology, communication, and social marketing—creating a unique mix of capabilities to address today’s interrelated development challenges. FHI 360 serves more than 50 countries and all US states and territories.
 FHI 360 has worked in Bangladesh for more than 50 years. Since 1975, we have taken a comprehensive approach to help transform the country’s health and development landscape. Leveraging a blend of global expertise and local insights, we have consistently strengthened community capacities, enhanced systems, and reinforced institutional frameworks for a sustainable impact. In partnership with the Government of Bangladesh, civil society, academia, and the private sector, FHI 360 Bangladesh delivers integrated programs across critical sectors. Our initiatives have spanned essential health services—including HIV and nutrition, tuberculosis, global health security (GHS), and economic participation.  
 Project Description: 
 The Meeting Targets and Maintaining Epidemic Control (EpiC) is a global project, funded by the U.S. Government. In Bangladesh, EpiC strengthens national preparedness and health security. Through risk communication, protective behaviors, cross-border transmission prevention, and facility readiness, the project supports the rapid containment of health threats while ensuring continuity of essential maternal, newborn, and child health and nutrition (MNCHN) services. Working closely with the Government of Bangladesh, the U.S. Government, and in-country GHS actors, EpiC Bangladesh builds resilient systems that protect populations in selected high-risk districts and sustain lifesaving services during emergencies.

 Position Description: 
 The Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) Specialist will support the implementation of RCCE activities under the EpiC project in Bangladesh. Reporting to the RCCE Manager, the Specialist will assist in designing, coordinating, and implementing community engagement and risk communication interventions that promote health awareness, strengthen community trust, and encourage positive health-seeking behaviors. The RCCE Specialist will work closely with government counterparts, local partners, frontline health workers, community leaders, and project teams to support the dissemination of timely, accurate, and appropriate health information. The position will contribute to strengthening community feedback mechanisms, monitoring rumors, supporting behavior change initiatives, and ensuring effective two-way communication with communities during routine programming and public health emergencies. The incumbent will support activities related to maternal and child health, nutrition, immunization, outbreak preparedness and response, health security, and One Health initiatives, with a focus on improving community participation and enhancing the effectiveness of communication interventions.

 Support implementation of behavior change and social mobilization initiatives that promote healthy practices and service utilization.
 2. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination

 Facilitate communication between field teams and project leadership to ensure timely implementation of activities.
 Support coordination and follow-up with relevant government RCCE focal persons and multisectoral RCCE coordination platforms, as assigned by the RCCE Manager.
 3. Community Feedback and Behavioral Insights 
 Support collection and analysis of community feedback, concerns, perceptions, and behavioral insights.
 Assist in identifying rumors and barriers to service uptake and recommend appropriate communication responses.

 Contribute to strengthening community feedback systems and ensuring findings are integrated into program planning and messaging.

 4. Capacity Strengthening

 Assist in developing training materials, job aids, and facilitation guides.
 Organize workshops, orientations, and learning sessions for district and community-level stakeholders.
 Promote community-centered and participatory approaches within project implementation.

 Maintain RCCE activity trackers, consolidate district updates, flag implementation gaps and follow up on agreed actions, and ensure timely reporting of achievements and challenges with Strategic Information team.
 Support collection, compilation, and analysis of program data related to communication and community engagement interventions.

 Contribute to development of success stories, case studies, presentations, and donor reports.
 Collaborate with Strategic Information, Monitoring & Evaluation, and Communications teams to track activity performance and results.

 Support RCCE activities during disease outbreaks, public health emergencies, and other crisis situations.

Job Summary   
 The Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer will support STRIDES activities in Banten Province to strengthen veterinary laboratory capacity for detecting zoonotic diseases with pandemic potential, particularly Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI).
 The officer will provide hands-on technical support to strengthen HPAI diagnostic capacity, particularly real-time PCR testing at UPTD PPV Banten. The role includes supporting laboratory testing readiness, quality management, biosafety and biosecurity, specimen management, and timely laboratory reporting. The officer will also support coordination and monitoring of HPAI laboratory testing for surveillance activities in priority districts, particularly Lebak and Tangerang.
 Working closely with the Senior Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer, STRIDES team, and government counterparts, the officer will support laboratory assessments, assist in addressing identified gaps, and monitor progress in implementing agreed improvements to improve the timeliness of HPAI detection, reporting, and outbreak response in line with the 7-1-7 target.
 This is a full-time, Banten-based position requiring regular on-site work at UPTD PPV Banten and close coordination with provincial and district government counterparts.
 Responsibilities/Duties   
 Technical Requirements:   
 Provide hands-on technical support to strengthen veterinary laboratory capacity for HPAI detection, particularly real-time PCR testing.
 Support laboratory testing readiness, including equipment functionality, reagent and consumable availability, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), and implementation of standard operating procedures (SOPs).
 Support laboratory assessments and assist laboratory personnel in addressing identified gaps through practical improvements, technical training, and mentoring.
 Monitor progress in implementing agreed recommendations and corrective actions and report challenges requiring further support.
 Support the implementation of laboratory quality management, biosafety, and biosecurity practices to improve diagnostic quality and laboratory safety.
 Work with laboratory personnel and STRIDES technical teams to identify additional needs and coordinate appropriate technical assistance.
 Specimen Management, Referral, and Laboratory Reporting:   
 Support coordination and monitoring of HPAI sample submission and laboratory testing from priority districts, particularly Lebak and Tangerang.
 Work with laboratory personnel and government counterparts to strengthen coordination of specimen collection, transportation, receipt, documentation, and referral procedures.
 Support timely laboratory testing, result reporting, and communication with relevant government counterparts.
 Assist with laboratory data management and reporting through relevant information systems, including IVLab and iSIKHNAS, as applicable.
 Identify challenges that may delay sample submission, laboratory testing, or result reporting, and support practical solutions to improve timely disease detection and response.
 Project Implementation and Coordination:   
 Work closely with provincial and district livestock services, veterinary laboratories, DIC Subang, and other relevant government partners.
 Support coordination between laboratory diagnostics, surveillance, and outbreak response activities, including efforts to improve performance against the 7-1-7 target.
 Assist in planning, implementing, and monitoring STRIDES laboratory strengthening activities in Banten Province.
 Participate in technical meetings, laboratory assessments, training, and field visits as required.
 Identify implementation challenges, communicate them to the Senior Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer, and support agreed follow-up actions.
 Monitoring, Documentation, and Reporting:   
 Monitor progress of laboratory strengthening activities against agreed work plans, recommendations, and deliverables.
 Maintain accurate records of technical activities, laboratory support, and follow-up actions.
 Prepare technical reports, presentations, meeting summaries, and implementation updates for STRIDES and relevant stakeholders.
 Support collection and analysis of laboratory performance data to inform program monitoring and decision-making.
 Problem Solving & Impact 
 Identifies technical and operational challenges affecting laboratory testing and reporting.
 Works with laboratory personnel and STRIDES technical teams to develop practical solutions.
 Exercises sound judgment and raises technical or implementation issues to the Senior Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer when needed.
 Contributes to improving laboratory readiness, diagnostic quality, and timely HPAI detection and reporting.
 Qualifications   
 Knowledge & Skills:   
 Good understanding of laboratory diagnostic practices, particularly molecular diagnostics and real-time PCR.
 Knowledge of laboratory QA/QC, SOP implementation, biosafety, biosecurity, and specimen management.
 Ability to identify laboratory capacity gaps and support practical improvements.
 Strong communication and interpersonal skills, particularly when working with government laboratory personnel and other stakeholders.
 Ability to coordinate activities, monitor progress, and follow up on agreed actions.
 Good organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
 Ability to work independently while maintaining close coordination with the STRIDES technical team.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and basic laboratory data management.
 Minimum Qualifications:   
 Bachelor's degree in Veterinary Medicine, Veterinary Laboratory Science, Microbiology, Medical Laboratory Technology, Biological Sciences, or a related field. A veterinary background is strongly preferred.
 A minimum of 4 years of relevant professional experience in laboratory diagnostics or laboratory systems strengthening, preferably in veterinary or infectious disease diagnostic laboratories. Academic internships, university laboratory assistant roles, and laboratory activities conducted as part of academic studies do not count toward the minimum experience requirement.
 Demonstrated hands-on experience in molecular diagnostics, particularly real-time PCR, including sample processing, quality control, and interpretation of test results.
 Knowledge of zoonotic diseases with epidemic and pandemic potential, particularly avian influenza, is highly desirable.
 Experience implementing laboratory QA/QC, SOPs, biosafety, and biosecurity practices.
 Experience supporting laboratory assessments, technical training, mentoring, or laboratory capacity strengthening is an advantage.
 Experience working with government laboratories, veterinary services, or public health programs is preferred.
 Familiarity with laboratory information systems and specimen referral networks is an advantage.
 Previous experience with donor-funded projects, particularly U.S. Government-funded programs, is desirable but not required.
 Strong organizational, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
 Good working proficiency in English and Bahasa Indonesia, including the ability to prepare technical reports and communicate effectively with project teams and government counterparts.
 Working Conditions and Travel Requirements:   
 This position is based in Banten Province. The successful candidate must reside in Banten Province or be willing to relocate.
 Regular on-site work at UPTD PPV Banten is required to support HPAI laboratory testing and capacity strengthening.
 The position requires a combination of office-based, laboratory-based, and field-based work.
 Ability to spend long hours looking at a computer screen and performing repetitive keyboard tasks.
 Ability to sit and stand for extended periods.
 Ability to lift or move up to 5 lbs.
 Approximately 10–25% local and regional travel may be required for laboratory assessments, coordination, and field activities.

Job Summary: 
 Regional Technical Officer, Tuberculosis (TB) provides technical expertise and support for implementing and scaling up comprehensive TB prevention, screening, diagnosis and treatment, within the EpiC Project in Tanzania. This role supports the integration of TB and HIV services across Police and Prison (PnP) health facilities and strengthens TB services within public health facilities to ensure early case detection, diagnosis, timely treatment initiation and completion. The role works closely with the Ministry of Health, the Police Medical Unit (PMU), the Prisons Health and Nutrition Unit (PHNU), the Prime Minister’s Office–Regional Administration and Local Government (PMO-RALG), Regional and Council Health Management Teams (RHMTs/CHMTs), facility teams, and implementing partners to strengthen the delivery of high-quality, equitable, and client-centered TB services, including TB/HIV collaborative activities in accordance with national guidelines and global recommendations.
 Accountabilities: 
 Technical Requirements:
 Provides technical support to regional technical teams, health facilities and community platforms in the planning, implementation, monitoring, and scale-up of TB interventions.
 Supports implementation of quality TB screening, active case finding, diagnosis, treatment, TB preventive treatment (TPT), TB/HIV collaborative services, DR-TB, and TB infection prevention and control (IPC) in line with national standards.
 Ensures TB service delivery is implemented in accordance with Tanzania MOH/NTLP guidelines and approved project standards.
 Support integration of TB services within HIV in public, PnP facilities, and community platforms to improve TB case identification, linkage, treatment initiation, adherence, and continuity of care.
 Conduct mentorship, coaching, supportive supervision, on-the-job training, and clinical case reviews to strengthen health worker capacity and improve the quality of TB services.

 Supports facilities to develop and implement site-level improvement plans and follow up on agreed actions to address identified TB service delivery gaps.
 Supports the implementation of TB/HIV collaborative activities, including TB screening among PLHIV, HIV testing among TB clients, linkage to ART, TPT provision, adherence, retention, and appropriate referral and follow-up.
 Supports identification, referral, treatment monitoring, and follow-up of clients with drug-resistant TB in collaboration with facility teams and relevant TB program structures.

offres.titre: Senior Regional Technical Officer (SRTO) – Laboratory Services - Iringa
offres.description:
Job Summary: 
 The Senior Regional Technical Officer (SRTO) – Laboratory Services provides technical leadership, mentorship and quality assurance support to strengthen HIV and Tuberculosis (TB) services under the America First Global Health Security (AFGHS) FHI 360 Project in Tanzania. The role supports implementation and scale up of quality diagnostic services, including HIV viral load (HVL), early infant diagnosis (EID), Human Papilloma Virus Deoxynucleic Acid (HPV DNA), HIV drug resistance (HIVDR), advanced HIV disease (AHD) diagnostics, and TB molecular testing, including point-of-care (POC) technologies, across Police and Prison (PnP) health facilities and supported public health facilities. The position also strengthens sample referral, laboratory information systems (LIS), and data use, quality management systems, and diagnostic supply chains to improve testing coverage, turnaround time, and result utilization for timely clinical decision-making.
 The SRTO works closely with the Regional and Council Health Management Teams (RHMTs/CHMTs), Ministry of Health (MOH), conventional laboratories, facility teams, and implementing partners to ensure delivery of high-quality, sustainable laboratory services in accordance with national guidelines and international quality standards, including ISO 15189:2022.
 Accountabilities 
 Technical Requirements:
 HIV Laboratory Services 
 Support the delivery of high quality HVL, EID, HIV testing, HPV DNA, HIVDR testing and other relevant laboratory services.
 Provide technical support on HVL, EID, and HPV testing laboratories to optimize instrument utilization, testing capacity, and workflow, and to prevent sample backlogs.
 Support the quality of HIV rapid testing, including adherence to the national HIV testing algorithm, rapid test continuous quality improvement (RTCQI), proficiency testing, and testing site and tester certification.
 Strengthen sample management for HVL and EID, including proper collection, handling, and processing of plasma and DBS samples, to reduce rejection rates.
 Strengthen implementation of AHD diagnostics, including CD4 testing (laboratory-based and point of care (POC such as VISITECT), TB LAM, cryptococcal antigen (CrAg), and promote timely use of results to guide clinical management in accordance with national guidelines
 Support timely referral and testing of HIVDR samples for clients with persistent high viral load, in line with national guidelines.
 Identify and address gaps affecting viral load coverage, turnaround time, sample rejection, and result utilization.
 Strengthen implementation and monitoring of the use of available POC technologies for multi-disease testing (VL, EID, HPV, TB, and other tests, in line with the MOH rollout plan.
 Strengthen the clinic–laboratory interface, including appropriate test requests, complete request, timely sample collection and referral, and prompt results sharing for clinician review, documentation, and action on HVL, EID, HPV, HIVDR, and AHD results.
 TB Laboratory Services 
 Provide technical assistance on the appropriate and optimal use of TB molecular diagnostic platforms, including GeneXpert and Truenat MTB and MTB-RIF Dx assays, line probe assays, and other approved technologies.
 Support implementation of the national TB diagnostic algorithm, including use of WHO-recommended molecular rapid diagnostic tests (mWRDs) as the initial diagnostic test for all people with presumptive TB in accordance with national guidelines.
 Support expanded use of alternative specimens and tests, including stool-based testing for children and urine TB LAM for people living with HIV.
 Strengthen drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) diagnosis, including timely referral of samples for Line Probe Assay (LPA), culture, and drug susceptibility testing (DST), and linkage of results to DR-TB treatment.
 Support laboratory components of TB screening and active case finding at PnP facilities, including sample collection, referral, and testing during screening campaigns.
 Monitor GeneXpert and Truenat performance, including utilization, module functionality, error and invalid rates, and turnaround time, and support integrated multi-disease testing on GeneXpert.
 Support functional implementation of GeneXpert and other molecular platforms, including servicing, preventive maintenance, annual calibration, and timely module replacement, in coordination with National TB and Leprosy Program (NTLP) and service providers.
 Strengthen TB laboratory quality assurance, including Internal Quality Control (IQC), External Quality Control /Proficiency Testing (EQA/PT) for molecular testing, and blinded rechecking for smear microscopy.
 Monitor TB cartridge and reagent stock levels and support forecasting to prevent stock-outs.
 Promote adherence to TB laboratory biosafety and infection prevention and control practices.
 Ensure Standard Operating Procedures ( SOPs) for TB laboratory tests and preventive maintenance are available and properly used.
 Laboratory Data Management and Performance Monitoring 
 Monitor laboratory performance against project indicators, targets and milestones and prepare quarterly  performance reports highlighting achievements, gaps and corrective actions to be reported to MoH, the donors and project leadership.
 Monitor key laboratory indicators, identify performance gaps, and support analysis and interpretation of laboratory data to inform program decisions.
 Track the performance of HIVDR, HPV DNA, POC, and TB LAM testing services
 Support the appropriate use of laboratory information systems (LIS) and reporting tools, and strengthen linkage between the CTC–Lab interface, e-SRS, LIS, LabXpert connectivity, and eTL (including GeneXpert connectivity) and HIV/TB program databases.
 Support implementation of standardized HIV and TB laboratory data collection and reporting tools (e.g. ESRS - Electronic Sample Referral System, LAT - Laboratory Analytical Tool, and Lab Xpert - A TB reporting tool on molecular tests) to ensure accurate documentation and timely use of results for clinical decision making.  
 Support data quality assessments and the resolution of data discrepancies.
 Sample Referral and Supply Chain 
 Strengthen the full testing cascade: sample collection, packaging, transport, testing, result return and client follow-up.
 Strengthen the sample referral coordination between regional stakeholders, including R/CHMTs, TPCs and facilities.
 Ensure optimal implementation of the sample referral system to improve access to, and utilization of molecular diagnostic services for HIV and TB.
 Support facilities to maintain appropriate sample collection, storage, packaging and transport practices.
 Monitor the availability of laboratory commodities, reagents, consumables, and supplies using existing systems like eLMIS, Lab reports on logistics data and also liaising with supply chain team within FHI 360 Tz.
 Work with government structures and partners to address stock-outs and diagnostic supply chain challenges.
 Quality Assurance 
 Support and monitor implementation of laboratory quality management systems in line with ISO 15189:2022.
 Conduct or support quarterly laboratory assessments of selected laboratories per region, continuous quality improvement (CQI) exercises and other quality improvement initiatives.
 Strengthen internal quality control (IQC), external quality assessment (EQA) and proficiency testing (PT), and corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
 Support facility enrollment and sustained participation in EQA/PT programs.
 Analyze EQA feedback include conducting root cause analysis and develop improvement plans to address major gaps in quality assurance.
 Capacity Building and Sustainability 
 Facilitate onsite and virtual training, orientation, mentorship, and supportive supervision for laboratory staff, including HIV and TB program laboratory professionals, and other healthcare providers.
 Build the capacity of regional, council, and facility teams

Position Title:            Technical Officer M&E/Accountability 
 Location:                    Maiduguri, Nigeria
 Supervisor:                Senior Technical Officer-MEL 
 Project Description: 
 FHI 360 UK-Nigeria is the wholly owned subsidiary of FHI 360 UK, who themselves are a wholly owned subsidiary of FHI 360, and combined form part of FHI 360’s family of companies. FHI 360 UK-Nigeria was incorporated in 2026 to carry on the business of programme implementation, project management and the provision of advisory, technical and support services in relation to humanitarian, development, public health, educational and social impact initiatives, including the execution and management of projects funded by governmental, multilateral, bilateral or private institutions. Contexte     
 FHI 360 est une organisation à but non lucratif dédiée au développement humain qui s'engage à améliorer durablement les conditions de vie en proposant des solutions intégrées et adaptées au contexte local. Notre personnel comprend des experts dans les domaines de la santé, de l'éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, du développement économique, de la jeunesse, de la recherche, de la technologie, de la communication et du marketing social, créant ainsi un ensemble unique de compétences pour relever les défis interdépendants du développement actuel. FHI360 intervient dans l’ensemble des États et territoires des États-Unis ainsi que dans plusieurs pays à travers le monde. Nous recherchons actuellement des candidats qualifiés pour le poste de Directeur(trice) Financier(ère) Adjoint(e) pour les projets de santé de FHI 360 en RDC.  
 Description du poste   
 Sous la supervision du Directeur Financier, le/la Directeur(trice) Financier(ère) Adjoint(e) assure la gestion et le suivi du contrôle budgétaire des projets tout en veillant au respect des procédures, règles et réglementations financières et comptables de FHI 360 et du Département d’Etat Américain. Il/elle garantit un soutien financier, administratif, logistique et sécuritaire robuste, indispensable à l'efficacité opérationnelle, à la conformité et au bon déroulement des opérations. Il/elle pilote l’élaboration du budget, les rapports financiers, le suivi des dépenses des projets et maintient les systèmes de classement financier. Il/elle supervise les activités de l’équipe financière, examine et valide les recommandations relatives à la planification et au contrôle financiers, et fournit à la direction exécutive les informations nécessaires à la prise de décision. Il/elle supervise les systèmes et processus comptables, garantit l’exactitude et la fiabilité des données comptables, assure le reporting et participe aux projets financiers spécifiques, dans le respect des normes et réglementations applicables. Il/elle assure le pilotage stratégique de l’équipe comptable, coordonne les activités avec les bureaux pays et le siège, et élabore les politiques et procédures visant à garantir l’efficacité des opérations et la conformité financière. Il/elle supervise la comptabilité du bureau national, y compris la clôture mensuelle des comptes, les rapprochements de comptes du bilan, la tenue du grand livre, ainsi que le rapprochement des avances de personnel sur terrain. Il/elle participe également au recrutement, encadre et évalue les membres de son équipe afin de garantir l’efficacité et le bon fonctionnement du service financier. Il/elle travaille en étroite collaboration avec le bureau pays, les bureaux régionaux et le siège de FHI 360 pour assurer la santé financière des projets.  
 Responsabilités principales    
 Gère les fonctions financières afin d’assurer une mise en œuvre fluide des projets, la conformité et l’efficacité.  
 Développe et améliore, en collaboration avec les équipes concernées, les outils de suivi et les tableaux de bord nécessaires à la planification financière et à la gestion des risques.  
 Dirige le processus annuel de planification budgétaire, les rapports financiers aux financeurs et supervise l’exécution du plan opérationnel des projets.  
 Dirige les prévisions de revenus et analyse régulièrement le pipeline financier afin d’anticiper les besoins et les risques.  
 Prépare les rapports financiers mensuels pour des analyses internes et externes, en comparant les budgets prévisionnels aux dépenses réelles, et formule des recommandations adaptées.  
 Est responsable de la performance et de l’atteinte des objectifs des questions financières, administratives et d’approvisionnement des projets.  
 Prépare et coordonne les rapports financiers destinés au bailleur, notamment les rapports mensuels, trimestriels et annuels, ainsi que tout autre rapports requis par le Département d’État américain (DOS).  
 Fournit à la direction des analyses et des conseils sur la gestion financière, les risques et les questions de conformité.  
 Établit et maintient des procédures comptables et des mécanismes de contrôle interne rigoureux et transparents pour les activités financières, opérationnelles et les sous-subventions.  
 Coordonne les audits internes et externes, prépare les documents et rapports requis et veille à la mise en œuvre des recommandations qui en découlent.  
 Supervise les systèmes et processus comptables, garantie le respect des normes financières et résout les problématiques comptables complexes.  
 Assure la clôture mensuelle à temps et la résolution de tous les problèmes comptables au bureau pays.   
 Veille à ce que le rapprochement systématique de tous les comptes du bilan soit fait chaque fin du mois pour le bureau pays, et que les comptes généraux et les sous-comptes soient correctement tenus.   
 S'assure que les pratiques comptables du bureau du pays sont adéquates, documentées et conformes aux exigences internes de FHI360 et répondent aux principes de la comptabilité.  
 Fait office de point de contact du bureau pays pour les demandes d'audit (audit annuel, audit OHADA, audits des projets des donateurs) et facilite la fourniture rapide des documents requis.  
 Veille à ce que les directives des systèmes internes (par ex., GFAS, DPA, Costpoint, processus du portail bancaire) soient respectées et harmonisées ; fournit des formations et soutient la prise en main du système de budgétisation TM1, le cas échéant  
 Coordonne les activités avec les équipes financières des différents bureaux, les auditeurs externes et la direction, tout en assurant le reporting et le conseil stratégique.  
 Assure le suivi financier et administratif des sous-bénéficiaires, notamment le contrôle des dépenses, l’examen des rapports financiers et la clôture des sous-subventions.  
 Supervise le suivi et la liquidation des avances accordées au personnel, aux partenaires et aux consultants.  
 Élabore et met en œuvre des mesures d’amélioration continue des processus financiers et des procédures opérationnelles.  
 Forme et accompagne le personnel dans l’application des politiques et procédures financières, des principes comptables et des bonnes pratiques de gestion des relations avec les clients et les partenaires.  
 Supervise le suivi et la liquidation des avances pour les ateliers, le personnel, les partenaires et les consultants.  
 Contribue à l’élaboration de plans de travail de qualité et de rapports d’activité et financiers, et réalise toute autre tâche pertinente confiée dans le cadre de ses fonctions.  
 Connaissances et compétences    
 Connaissance approfondie des concepts, pratiques et procédures liés à la comptabilité, aux contrôles financiers et aux systèmes d’information financière.   
 Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite.   
 Excellentes compétences démontrées en organisation et en présentation.   
 Excellentes compétences démontrées en gestion de projet.   
 Excellentes compétences en organisation, supervision, leadership et gestion.   
 Capacité à fournir un leadership et des conseils stratégiques à l’équipe, à échanger des informations et à collaborer avec des collègues et des pairs à l’intérieur et à l’extérieur de l’organisation.   
 Capacité à influencer, motiver, négocier et bien travailler avec les autres.   
 Excellente connaissance des lois et réglementations étatiques ayant une incidence sur l’analyse financière et les contrôles de gestion.   
 Expérience significative de Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), des rapports financiers automatisés, des pratiques comptables gouvernementales, Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) et des Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR).  
 Connaissance complète et expérience antérieure de Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) - des directives et des normes de rapportage.   
 Formation et expérience    
 Titulaire d’une Licence en comptabilité, gestion financière, commerce ou dans un domaine connexe, ou quali

Job Summary   
 The Associate Director, Research is responsible for managing and executing research projects or departmental services, overseeing the planning, development, and monitoring of communication research activities to ensure timely and efficient completion. This includes driving the development and execution of cross-functional plans and ensuring consistent practices throughout the project life cycle. The Associate Director of Research also manages budgets, provides subject matter expertise, mentors staff, and collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to meet research goals.  This posting is for a 50% level of effort position (half time employee). 
 Responsibilities/Duties   
 Complexity & Problem Solving:   
 Manage the planning and execution of complex communication research projects, resolving issues using innovative and creative approaches.  
 Develop and implement systems to ensure effective completion of project or departmental goals, addressing operational challenges as they arise.  
 Oversee research methodologies, ensuring alignment with strategic goals and compliance with industry standards.  
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot challenges and implement solutions to meet research and project objectives.  
 Discretion & Impact:   
 Exercise authority in budget management, resource allocation, and the development of research protocols.  
 Make strategic decisions that directly impact project success, timelines, and budget management.  
 Ensure project deliverables meet quality standards, influencing overall project outcomes and organizational goals.  
 Resolve issues and manage risks, ensuring adherence to regulatory requirements and organizational policies.  
 Collaboration & Interaction:   
 Foster strong collaborations with internal teams, including finance, project management, and external stakeholders to ensure smooth project execution.  
 Act as a key liaison with external partners, sponsors, and clients, ensuring alignment with project goals and timelines.  
 Provide clear direction to research teams and cross-functional partners, ensuring effective communication and collaboration throughout the project lifecycle.  
 Regularly engage with leadership to update on project status, key milestones, and any challenges.  
 Management & Supervision:   
 Supervise and mentor project and departmental staff, including research teams and administrative personnel, ensuring team alignment with project objectives.  
 Oversee performance management, offering regular feedback, coaching, and professional development opportunities to direct reports.  
 Develop operational plans, set goals, and provide strategic direction for project teams to achieve tactical and long-term objectives.  
 Manage departmental budgets, ensuring financial oversight and alignment with project goals.  
 Embraces other duties as assigned, contributing to the team’s multifaceted and evolving responsibilities.  
 Qualifications   
 Knowledge & Skills:   
 Comprehensive knowledge of research and evaluation design, including qualitative and quantitative methodologies.  
 Strong project management skills, with demonstrated experience in overseeing complex research initiatives.  
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present research findings to stakeholders clearly and concisely.  
 Ability to influence and collaborate with cross-functional teams and external partners to achieve project goals.  
 Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex issues related to research execution, budgets, and stakeholder expectations.  
 Minimum Qualifications:   
 Master’s Degree or its international equivalent in Knowledge/Information Services, Communications, Education, Environment, Health, Behavioral, Life/Social Sciences, International Development, Human Development, or a related field.  
 8+ years of experience in research and evaluation implementation, analysis, and project management.  
 Experience in a non-governmental organization (NGO), government agency, or private organization.  
 Preferred Qualifications:   
 Prior experience in managing large-scale research projects, with a focus on evaluation and analysis.  
 Strong knowledge of the regulatory requirements for research projects and prior experience managing research teams.  
 Travel 
 Less than 10% travel required based on project needs.
 Typical Physical Demands   
 Typical office environment. Constantly uses a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer. Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.   
 Technology   
 Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

PROJECT SUMMARY :
 The Strengthening Infectious Disease Detection Systems (STRIDES) Activity is a U.S. government-funded project that provides life-saving assistance to countries to prevent and mitigate outbreaks of emerging infectious diseases that threaten U.S. national security. Global health security safeguards lives and prevents devastating economic repercussions.
 The project aims to 1. strengthen detection capacity and systems at the national and sub-national levels for both human and animal laboratory networks and increase access to quality laboratory services for diseases of public health importance. 2. develop and enhance sustainable and surveillance systems, using event-based (EBS) and indicator-based (IBS) systems, to detect events of significance for public health and health security. 3. provide technical assistance to develop and strengthen host country capacity in data collection, analysis, and reporting for actionable disease prevention and response decision making. 4. provide targeted technical surveillance and detection assistance during an outbreak. Its geographic focus includes Upper East Region, Upper West Region, Bono East Region, and Volta Region
 JOB SUMMARY :
 The Driver is responsible for providing safe, reliable, and timely transportation services for Staff, Consortium Partners, Consultants, HQ staff on TDY in country, and authorized goods in support of the STRIDES project activities in Ghana. The role requires strict adherence to road safety regulations, organizational policies, and security procedures, while maintaining assigned vehicles in good working conditions. The Driver demonstrates a client-oriented approach, high sense of responsibility, courtesy, tact, and the ability to work with people of different national and cultural backgrounds.

 Safely transport staff, consultants, partners, and visitors to meetings, project sites, airports, and other official destinations.
 Support field missions and program activities by ensuring timely and dependable transport.
 Deliver documents, equipment, supplies, and other authorized items as required. 
 Plan routes in advance, taking into account traffic conditions, road safety, and security considerations.
 Vehicle Management 
 Conduct daily vehicle checks including fuel, oil, water, brakes, tires, and lights
 Ensure assigned vehicles are kept clean, roadworthy, and properly secured at all times
 Maintain accurate vehicle logbooks, fuel records, and mileage reports
 Arrange routine servicing and report mechanical faults promptly to the supervisor. 
 Ensure vehicle insurance, roadworthiness certificates, and other documentation are valid and available
 Safety, Security, and Compliance 
 Adhere strictly to Ghana Road Traffic Regulations and FHI 360’s transport/travel and safety policies
 Follow organizational security protocols, especially during field travel and emergency situations
 Ensure the safety of passengers and vehicle contents at all times. 
 Report accidents, incidents, or security concerns immediately in line with reporting procedures
 Administrative Support 
 Provide basic administrative or logistical support when not driving, as requested
 Assist with loading and unloading of goods and equipment
 Support office operations during peak periods or special events
 Knowledge and Skills: 
 Strong knowledge of Ghana’s road networks and traffic regulations.
 Ability to follow routine verbal and written instructions and communicate effectively
 Good understanding of vehicle maintenance and basic mechanical issues.
 Ability to remain calm under pressure and in challenging road or security conditions.
 Knowledge of Greater Accra and other regions in Ghana, and key information on geo-political history of Ghana.
 Proven experience driving in both urban and rural areas in Ghana.
 Knowledge of basic first aid
 Safeguarding and Code of Conduct 
 Commitment to the FHI 360’s values, code of conduct, and safeguarding policies
 Zero tolerance for harassment, exploitation, or abuse of any kind

 Basic Education Certificate

 Supervisor:                               Technical Officer, Health and Nutrition Services

 Basic Function: Providing nursing and midwifery care, treatment and follow-up of patients according to protocols applied in service and universal hygiene standards/precautions, in order to ensure the quality and continuity of care for the targeted population. Using your midwifery skill assist female patients in all stages of pregnancy, childbirth and post-delivery. He/she will also provide antenatal and postnatal advice and support to women and their families
 Duties and responsibilities: 
 Work as part of a multidisciplinary team to provide high-quality nursing and midwifery care to vulnerable populations.
 Ensure patients are appropriately received, admitted, and supported throughout their care, with particular attention to assisting those with limited autonomy in meeting their physical, personal hygiene, mobility, comfort, and psychosocial needs while preserving their dignity, safety, and well-being.
 Conduct patient triage in waiting areas, wards, and emergency situations; identify priority and acute cases, provide first aid when necessary, and refer patients to the appropriate clinician.
 Promote, implement, and adhere to universal precautions, infection prevention, and hygiene standards.
 Organize and provide nursing and midwifery care according to medical prescriptions and established clinical protocols and assist during consultations and medical procedures.
 Participate in patient and caregiver health education activities as required.
 Conduct patient admission, monitoring, and follow-up, including assessing clinical progress and identifying any deterioration or emergency conditions.
 Complete and maintain all required clinical and administrative documentation, including patient records, registers, statistics, and consumption tracking tools.
 Support, supervise, and build the capacity of Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs), volunteers, and other support staff within the assigned unit.
 Adhere to FHI 360 policies, professional codes of conduct, and ethical standards.
 Participate in outreach activities and community health programs as required.
 Participate in continuing professional development activities, including training, mentorship, and skills improvement initiatives.
 Develop and implement patient care plans in collaboration with the supervising physician and other members of the healthcare team.
 Provide direct nursing and midwifery services, including administration of medications, intravenous therapy, wound care, clinical observations, antenatal care, postnatal care, labor and delivery support, and other essential maternal, newborn, and general nursing services.
 Ensure proper cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization of reusable medical equipment and instruments.
 Maintain accurate records of patient care, medical supplies, consumables, and equipment utilized.
 Ensure the delivery of high-quality nursing and midwifery services across all project-supported sites.
 Collaborate with Technical and Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL/M&E) teams to collect and report required program data.
 Prepare and submit timely and accurate periodic reports.
 Ensure infection prevention and control (IPC) measures are consistently implemented and maintained.
 Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor.
 Knowledge, Skills & Attributes: 
 Ability and willingness to stay and rotate to any LGA within Borno state is required.
 Willingness and capacity to be flexible and accommodating when faced with difficult and frustrating working conditions like long-distance walking to distribution sites.
 A very good spoken and written local (Hausa, Kanuri, Fula, or any other) languages spoken in NE and fluent English languages.
 Good interpersonal and communication skills.
 Previous experience working in a clinical and maternity setting is an asset. 
 Ability to prepare weekly and monthly program reports.
 Be flexible and adaptable with regard to the implementation of the daily work 
 Qualifications and requirements: 
 ·       Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) in Nursing with a minimum of three (3) years of relevant clinical experience.
 ·       Registration as both a Registered Nurse (RN) and Registered Midwife (RM), with a valid practicing license, is mandatory . Candidates in this category should have a minimum of five (5) years of clinical practice experience.
 ·       Additional qualifications or certifications in Public Health or other closely related fields from a government-recognized institution will be an added advantage.
 ·       Familiarity with the Nigerian public health system and experience working with NGOs and CBOs is highly desirable.
 ·       Previous experience working in humanitarian or emergency response settings is highly desirable.
 ·       Previous relevant experience with FHI 360 and a satisfactory performance record will be an added advantage.

offres.titre: Assistant Technical Officer, Nursing and Midwifery (Banki)
offres.description:
Position Title:                           Assistant Technical Officer, Nursing and Midwifery (Banki)
 Location:                                 Banki LGA, Borno State
 Supervisor:                               Technical Officer, Health and Nutrition Services
 Project Description :
 FHI 360 UK-Nigeria is the wholly owned subsidiary of FHI 360 UK, who themselves are a wholly owned subsidiary of FHI 360, and combined form part of FHI 360’s family of companies. FHI 360 UK-Nigeria was incorporated in 2026 to carry on the business of programme implementation, project management and the provision of advisory, technical and support services in relation to humanitarian, development, public health, educational and social impact initiatives, including the execution and management of projects funded by governmental, multilateral, bilateral or private institutions. This is in addition to supporting the full range of FHI 360 services, particularly in global health security and economic resilience.
 Northeast Nigeria is currently facing a growing humanitarian crisis with a vast number of Internally Displaced Persons in need of emergency assistance. These IDPs are living among host communities, lacking access to livelihoods and resources, ultimately leading to unprecedented levels of malnutrition and food insecurity.
 FHI 360 UK and FHI 360 UK-Nigeria are now expanding activities to support FHI 360 in Borno state to respond to the IDP crisis through integrated WASH, Health, Nutrition and Protection interventions 
 Basic Function: Providing nursing and midwifery care, treatment and follow-up of patients according to protocols applied in service and universal hygiene standards/precautions, in order to ensure the quality and continuity of care for the targeted population. Using your midwifery skill assist female patients in all stages of pregnancy, childbirth and post-delivery. He/she will also provide antenatal and postnatal advice and support to women and their families
 Duties and responsibilities: 
 Work as part of a multidisciplinary team to provide high-quality nursing and midwifery care to vulnerable populations.
 Ensure patients are appropriately received, admitted, and supported throughout their care, with particular attention to assisting those with limited autonomy in meeting their physical, personal hygiene, mobility, comfort, and psychosocial needs while preserving their dignity, safety, and well-being.
 Conduct patient triage in waiting areas, wards, and emergency situations; identify priority and acute cases, provide first aid when necessary, and refer patients to the appropriate clinician.
 Promote, implement, and adhere to universal precautions, infection prevention, and hygiene standards.
 Organize and provide nursing and midwifery care according to medical prescriptions and established clinical protocols and assist during consultations and medical procedures.
 Participate in patient and caregiver health education activities as required.
 Conduct patient admission, monitoring, and follow-up, including assessing clinical progress and identifying any deterioration or emergency conditions.
 Complete and maintain all required clinical and administrative documentation, including patient records, registers, statistics, and consumption tracking tools.
 Support, supervise, and build the capacity of Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs), volunteers, and other support staff within the assigned unit.
 Adhere to FHI 360 policies, professional codes of conduct, and ethical standards.
 Participate in outreach activities and community health programs as required.
 Participate in continuing professional development activities, including training, mentorship, and skills improvement initiatives.
 Develop and implement patient care plans in collaboration with the supervising physician and other members of the healthcare team.
 Provide direct nursing and midwifery services, including administration of medications, intravenous therapy, wound care, clinical observations, antenatal care, postnatal care, labor and delivery support, and other essential maternal, newborn, and general nursing services.
 Ensure proper cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization of reusable medical equipment and instruments.
 Maintain accurate records of patient care, medical supplies, consumables, and equipment utilized.
 Ensure the delivery of high-quality nursing and midwifery services across all project-supported sites.
 Collaborate with Technical and Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL/M&E) teams to collect and report required program data.
 Prepare and submit timely and accurate periodic reports.
 Ensure infection prevention and control (IPC) measures are consistently implemented and maintained.
 Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor.
 Knowledge, Skills & Attributes: 
 Ability and willingness to stay and rotate to any LGA within Borno state is required.
 Willingness and capacity to be flexible and accommodating when faced with difficult and frustrating working conditions like long-distance walking to distribution sites.
 A very good spoken and written local (Hausa, Kanuri, Fula, or any other) languages spoken in NE and fluent English languages.
 Good interpersonal and communication skills.
 Previous experience working in a clinical and maternity setting is an asset. 
 Ability to prepare weekly and monthly program reports.
 Be flexible and adaptable with regard to the implementation of the daily work 
 Qualifications and requirements: 
 ·       Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) in Nursing with a minimum of three (3) years of relevant clinical experience.
 ·       Registration as both a Registered Nurse (RN) and Registered Midwife (RM), with a valid practicing license, is mandatory . Candidates in this category should have a minimum of five (5) years of clinical practice experience.
 ·       Additional qualifications or certifications in Public Health or other closely related fields from a government-recognized institution will be an added advantage.
 ·       Familiarity with the Nigerian public health system and experience working with NGOs and CBOs is highly desirable.
 ·       Previous experience working in humanitarian or emergency response settings is highly desirable.
 ·       Previous relevant experience with FHI 360 and a satisfactory performance record will be an added advantage.
 Safeguarding : 
 FHI 360 UK-Nigeria is committed to providing a safe environment for all employees, beneficiaries and anyone contracted by FHI 360 UK Nigeria. This Includes taking measures to protect vulnerable people from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) by either FHI 360 UK Nigeria employees or associated personnel. FHI 360 UK Nigeria abides by child safeguarding principles. FHI 360’s Safeguarding Policies apply and flow out to all FHI 360 UK Nigeria staff, board members, volunteers, and partner staff (subcontractors, consultants, vendors, and subrecipients), regardless of the funding mechanism or amount of contract, agreement, or purchase order.
 The expected hiring salary range for this role is indexed to USD 7,160 - 8,500 for annual gross salary (basic and allowances). When determining an offer amount, FHI 360 factors in multiple considerations, including but not limited to: relevant years of experience and education possessed by the applicant, internal equity, market pay, and budget.  For internal candidates, salary placement will also follow FHI 360’s current promotional increase guidelines

Job Summary: 
 Performs work in the operation of a vehicle to provide safe and reliable transportation for staff, visitors, and official materials in support of organizational activities. The role ensures the responsible stewardship of assigned vehicles and contributes to the effective delivery of office operations through adherence to organizational policies and road safety standards
 Accountabilities: 
 Transportation Services 
 Provides safe, timely, and professional transportation for staff, consultants, visitors, and authorized materials in support of organizational activities.
 Plans and coordinates travel routes and schedules to support efficient operations while ensuring compliance with road safety requirements and organizational policies.
 Vehicle Maintenance and Care 
 Ensures assigned vehicles are safe, secure, clean, and maintained in a roadworthy condition through routine inspections, preventive maintenance, and timely servicing or repairs.
 Monitors vehicle condition and promptly reports maintenance requirements to minimize operational disruptions and ensure vehicle readiness.
 Vehicle Records and Compliance 
 Maintains accurate vehicle records and ensures vehicle documentation, licenses, insurance, and related requirements remain current and compliant with organizational and regulatory standards.
 Safety and Incident Management 
 Promotes safe driving practices and contributes to the safety and security of passengers, vehicles, and organizational assets.
 Reports and supports the management of accidents, incidents, vehicle damage, and safety concerns in accordance with established procedures.
 Operational Support 
 Supports office operations through the timely delivery and collection of documents, packages, equipment, and other transportation-related logistical requirements.
 Provides logistical and transportation support for program and office activities as required.
 Performs other duties as assigned in support of program and organizational objectives.
 Problem Solving & Impact: 
 Identifies and resolves routine transportation and vehicle-related issues in accordance with established procedures and organizational guidelines. Exercises judgment in route planning, scheduling, vehicle inspections, and the timely reporting of maintenance or safety concerns. Refers non-routine problems, accidents, incidents, and complex operational issues to the supervisor or appropriate staff for resolution. Errors in judgment, non-compliance with safety requirements, or delays in reporting vehicle concerns may result in operational disruptions, increased costs, safety risks, or delays in implementation.
 Supervision Given/Received: 
 Works under the general supervision of the Administrative Assistant or designated supervisor, receiving guidance on routine assignments and direction on new or special assignments as required. Performs day-to-day transportation and vehicle-related responsibilities independently within established procedures, organizational policies, and safety guidelines. Refers non-routine issues, incidents, and exceptions to the supervisor for resolution. The role has no direct supervisory responsibilities and maintains regular contact with staff, consultants, visitors, service providers, and external stakeholders to obtain, provide, and coordinate information in support of organizational operations
 Education: ** 
 Secondary School Education/Vocational training in driving or a related field.
 Certification from a recognized driving training institution is an added advantage.
 Experience: ** 
 Minimum three (3) years of professional driving experience, preferably with an NGO, international organization, development partner, or similar environment.
 Valid driving license with a clean driving record required.
 Typical Physical Demands: 
 Ability to sit and drive for extended periods of time.
 Ability to maintain concentration and alertness during local and long-distance travel.
 Ability to enter and exit vehicles frequently and assist passengers as required.
 Ability to lift, carry, and move light loads, documents, packages, and equipment as part of transportation and logistical support activities.
 Ability to work outdoors and in varying field conditions as required
 Technology to be Used: 
 Mobile phones and other communication devices for coordination of transportation and operational activities.
 Microsoft Office applications and other organizational systems required for communication, recordkeeping, and reporting.
 GPS, navigation, and vehicle tracking systems, where applicable.
 Standard office equipment and related technology used in support of assigned responsibilities.
 Travel Requirements: 
 Frequent travel within the duty station and surrounding project areas as required.
 Periodic travel to support program and operational activities in other locations within Tanzania.
