Job Summary   
 The Project Director I leads the development and implementation of company projects, coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the delivery of new or existing projects within prescribed schedules and budget constraints. This role oversees the entire project lifecycle, from initiation through delivery, and ensures that all project activities comply with company policies and external regulations. The Senior Project Manager is responsible for leading project teams, evaluating personnel, and managing resources to achieve project goals. This role also ensures the creation of a safe and equitable work environment while promoting compliance with safeguarding systems. The Senior Project Manager works closely with internal and external stakeholders, including donors, and provides ongoing support for the performance and development of direct reports.  
 Responsibilities/Duties   
 Complexity & Problem Solving:   
 Manages complex projects involving cross-functional teams across different business units.  
 Develops innovative solutions to address project challenges, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives.  
 Exercises critical thinking and problem-solving to resolve resource, budget, and timeline constraints.  
 Discretion & Impact:   
 Makes strategic decisions impacting the success of large-scale projects.  
 Holds significant responsibility for project outcomes, with decisions influencing both management and division operations.  
 Ensures compliance with funding parameters, policies, and donor requirements.  
 Collaboration & Interaction:   
 Fosters partnerships with internal teams, donors, and external stakeholders to achieve project success.  
 Collaborates with cross-functional teams and provides clear communication on project progress and deliverables.  
 Engages with high-level stakeholders (e.g., UN agencies, donors, district governments) to build positive working relationships.  
 Management & Supervision:   
 Leads the project team, ensuring roles and responsibilities are clearly defined and aligned with project objectives.  
 Supervises, mentors, and develops direct reports, providing career support and performance feedback.  
 Oversees the induction of new staff, ensuring alignment with organizational values, standards, and policies.  
 Embraces other duties as assigned, contributing to the team’s multifaceted and evolving responsibilities.  
 Qualifications   
 Knowledge & Skills:   
 Strong project management skills, including the ability to plan, organize, and manage resources for successful project completion.  
 Comprehensive knowledge of project management principles, practices, and tools.  
 Expertise in managing multi-sector projects, including strategic planning, budget oversight, and compliance with international development and NGO regulations.  
 Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to influence and negotiate with diverse stakeholders.  
 Proficiency in risk management, financial analysis, and problem-solving.  
 Minimum Qualifications:   
 Bachelor’s Degree or its International Equivalent in Civil Society, Communication and Social Marketing, Economic Development, Education, the Environment, Gender, Health, Nutrition, Research, Technology, Youth, or related field.  
 Minimum of 10+ years of relevant experience in project management, including at least 5 years of line management experience.  
 Demonstrated experience in managing complex, multi-sector projects that are strategic and international in scope.  
 Proven track record in strategic planning, staff development, and capacity building.  
 Fluent in English, with the ability to communicate effectively in the host country language.  
 Preferred Qualifications:   
 Experience working in insecure environments and managing humanitarian or development programs.  
 Experience working in a non-governmental organization (NGO) or with international donors.  
 Familiarity with applicable rules, regulations, and policies in international development.  
 Travel   
 10% - 25% travel required.    
 Typical Physical Demands   
 Typical office environment. Constantly uses a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer. Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.   
 Technology   
 Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

The Technical Officer, Tuberculosis (TB TO) will serve as a technical staff supporting for FHI 360 Vietnam country program in TB and multi-drug-resistant TB (TB/MDR-TB) case finding, diagnosis and treatment supporting project implementation in project priority provinces. Key roles include strengthening TB case detection to support epidemic control in these areas, supporting efforts to link to diagnosis via rapid molecular testing or other diagnostic modalities, and link to confirmed cases to treatment for drug-susceptible TB (DS-TB) and drug-resistant TB (DR-TB), promoting the integration of TB care into primary healthcare services, and facilitating the transition to health insurance-covered TB services within the assigned locations.  
 Key Responsibilities: 
 ·         Provide technical management and support the project activities implementation including intensified/active TB case finding, treatment, and prevention at all levels including provincial, health facilities and commune level
 ·         Provide technical support and capacity building for local partners in Support to End TB project supported sites during the implementation of the project activities
 ·         Provides technical support to ensure the quality of services in these settings, including assistance to implement MOH/NTP guidelines and policies, new algorithms, standard operating procedures and apply quality improvement to continuously improve performance
 ·         Be focal point for the assigned technical areas under the project, manage the sub-contracts and oversee the implementation of the subcontract and project activities to meet the quality and timely manner
 ·         Supports the timely and accurate use of data to improve and ensure that the project meets its case finding targets in selected priority provinces
 ·         Provides technical inputs on technical areas and topics by reviewing current literature and their relevance to the project’s activities and for the National TB Program; provide recommendations to improve programming based on field experience, research, and best practices
 ·         Works closely with other project staff to ensure strong linkages between best practices of TB diagnosis, treatment, and prevention with the project programming in these same areas.
 Experience and abilities for the position: 
 ·         University degrees in medicine, public health or related fields.
 ·         Minimum three years of professional experience in providing TB services or technical support in Vietnam
 ·         Profound knowledge of the Vietnam health systems and related laws in health sector
 ·         Experience with U.S. government contractual requirements and experience in an international NGO working environment desirable
 ·         Ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with a variety of stakeholders including government, international and social entities
 ·         Strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize
 ·         Self-motivation and high sense of team spirit
 ·         Well-developed written and oral communication skills in both Vietnamese and English
 ·         Computer literate with strong skills in use of MS office package (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint…)
 ·         Ability to travel as necessary

 Location: Konduga, LGA Level, Borno State
 Supervisor: Field Coordinator
 Technical supervision by Senior Technical Officer –WASH
 Project Description: 
 FHI 360 UK-Nigeria is the wholly owned subsidiary of FHI 360 UK, who themselves are a wholly owned subsidiary of FHI 360, and combined form part of FHI 360’s family of companies. FHI 360 UK-Nigeria was incorporated in 2026 to carry on the business of programme implementation, project management and the provision of advisory, technical and support services in relation to humanitarian, development, public health, educational and social impact initiatives, including the execution and management of projects funded by governmental, multilateral, bilateral or private institutions. This is in addition to supporting the full range of FHI 360 services, particularly in global health security and economic resilience.
 Northeast Nigeria is currently facing a growing humanitarian crisis with a vast number of Internally Displaced Persons in need of emergency assistance. These IDPs are living among host communities, lacking access to livelihoods and resources, ultimately leading to unprecedented levels of malnutrition and food insecurity.
 FHI 360 UK and FHI 360 UK-Nigeria are now expanding activities to support FHI 360's work in Borno State to respond to the IDP crisis through integrated WASH, Health, Nutrition, and Protection interventions.
 Position Summary 
 The Assistant Technical Officer (ATO) - WASH plays an important role in supporting the delivery of water, sanitation, and hygiene activities at the field level. Working closely with communities, local authorities, contractors, and partner organizations, the ATO-WASH helps ensure that WASH facilities are properly constructed, maintained, and accessible to those who need them most. The position also supports water quality monitoring, hygiene promotion activities, community engagement, and routine project reporting.

 WASH Infrastructure and Technical Support
 Support the construction, rehabilitation, and maintenance of water and sanitation facilities.
 Monitor ongoing WASH works to ensure they meet required technical standards and project specifications.
 Conduct site visits, assessments, and routine inspections to identify needs and monitor progress.
 Work with contractors and community structures to ensure the proper use and upkeep of WASH facilities.
 Water Quality and Environmental Health
 Conduct regular water quality testing and monitoring activities.
 Support efforts to maintain safe and reliable water supplies in project locations.
 Promote good environmental sanitation practices, including proper waste management.
 Assist in implementing measures that reduce public health risks associated with poor sanitation and unsafe water.
 Community Engagement and Hygiene Promotion
 Support community-based hygiene promotion and awareness activities.
 Work with community volunteers, leaders, and WASH committees to encourage ownership of facilities.
 Assist communities in establishing cleaning and maintenance systems for shared sanitation facilities.
 Encourage safe hygiene practices that contribute to improved health outcomes.
 Coordination, Planning, and Reporting
 Participate in coordination meetings with government agencies, humanitarian partners, and community stakeholders.
 Maintain positive working relationships with local authorities and other partners involved in WASH programming.
 Contribute to the development of work plans and activity schedules.
 Prepare timely reports and maintain accurate records of project activities and achievements.
 Support monitoring and evaluation activities, including data collection and documentation.
 Other Duties
 Support the management and tracking of WASH supplies and materials.
 Carry out any other duties reasonably assigned by the Field Coordinator or STO-WASH in support of project objectives.
 Knowledge and Skills
 Understanding of WASH programming, particularly in humanitarian or emergency settings.
 Knowledge of water supply systems, sanitation facilities, and water quality monitoring.
 Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
 Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines.
 Strong problem-solving, organizational, and report-writing skills.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
 Fluency in English is required; knowledge of Hausa is an added advantage.

 Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Environmental Health, Public Health, or a related field.

offres.titre: OFFICIER DE SECURITE ET ACCES HUMANIATIRE
offres.description:
Contexte  
 FHI 360 est une organisation à but non lucratif dédiée au développement humain qui s'engage à améliorer durablement les conditions de vie en proposant des solutions intégrées et adaptées au contexte local. Notre personnel comprend des experts dans les domaines de la santé, de l'éducation, de la nutrition, de l'environnement, du développement économique, de la jeunesse, de la recherche, de la technologie, de la communication et du marketing social, créant ainsi un ensemble unique de compétences pour relever les défis interdépendants du développement actuel.
 Une épidémie de virus Ebola Bundibugyo a été déclarée en RDC le 15 mai 2026. En réponse, FHI 360 met en œuvre des activités d'urgence intégrées. Un soutien administratif, financier, administratif et sécuritaire robuste est essentiel pour assurer l'efficacité opérationnelle, la conformité et le fonctionnement de toutes les activités.
 Description du poste 
 Sous la supervision du Security Manager, le/l’Officier de sécurité et accès humanitaire fait partie de l’équipe chargée de la mise en œuvre et du suivi des politiques de sûreté et de sécurité de FHI 360 en RDC en appui aux projets EpiC et STRIDES. Il/elle soutient la mise en œuvre, la coordination et le suivi du programme de sûreté et de sécurité de FHI 360 à partir de la base de Beni. Il/elle contribue à l’élaboration, à la mise à jour et à l’application des procédures de sécurité conformément aux politiques de l’organisation, tout en veillant à la bonne coordination des exercices de simulation d’urgence, des protocoles de communication et des plans de contingence. Il/elle appuie également la gestion des incidents de sécurité, assure la coordination opérationnelle sur le terrain lors de situations d’urgence ou de crise et veille au respect des normes et procédures de sûreté et de sécurité établies par FHI 360. À ce titre, il/elle assure la tenue des registres et de la documentation liés à la sécurité, compile et analyse les données relatives aux incidents et aux pertes, et contribue au renforcement continu des pratiques de gestion de la sûreté et de la sécurité au sein de FHI 360.
 Responsabilités principales liées à l’accès humanitaire.           
 Évaluation des risques sécuritaires dans les zones de santé de l'Ituri touchées par l'épidémie. 
 Mener une négociation de l'accès humanitaire auprès des leaders communautaires, des autorités locales pour permettre aux équipes de riposte (vaccination, enterrements dignes et  sécurisés) d'opérer en toute sécurité.
 Assurer une supervision des mouvements des équipes de riposte sur le terrain à travers un suivi des déplacements en temps réel. (Online FHI360 staff movement system).
 Définir et mettre à jour des plans de contingence et d'évacuation d'urgence pour le staff de FHI360 au Nord-Kivu.
 La sécurisation des infrastructures de riposte lors des enterrements. 
 Assurer une bonne coordination avec les Centres de Traitement Ebola (CTE) et des centres d'Isolement.
 Mettre en place de mesures de contrôle d'accès strictes au bureau pour éviter les intrusions et sécuriser les intrants médicaux sensibles.
 Avec l’appui de la direction et du Security manager de gérer les incidents de sécurité, tels que les manifestations et les riots ou les attaques ciblées contre les activités de FHI360 lors des enterrements.
 Assurer une bonne sensibilisation et une bonne gestion des tensions communautaires. 
 S’assurer qu’une bonne sensibilisation et une bonne analyse de la perception de la riposte par la population locale est mise en place pour anticiper les rumeurs, les résistances communautaires et les risques de violence.
 Briefer les staffs national et international avant leur déploiement dans les zones à haut risque au Nord-Kivu.
 Promouvoir le respect strict du principe de neutralité et de l'approche Do No Harm (Ne pas nuire) auprès des équipes médicales de FHI360 pour minimiser les tensions avec les communautés.
 Coordination et Reporting 
 Rédiger les rapports de situation (SITREP) réguliers détaillant les incidents de sécurité, les tendances des menaces et les restrictions d'accès et faire des recommandations aux staffs.
 Participer activement aux réunions de coordination de la sécurité humanitaire (INSO, UNOCHA et des clusters de sécurité pour la riposte de la MVE).
 Partager les alertes sécuritaires en rapport avec la riposte afin de permettre à FHI360 d’adapter ses stratégies d'intervention médicale dans la province du Nord-Kivu.
 Responsabilités principales liées à la gestion de securité.   
 Appuie le Security Manager dans l’élaboration, la coordination, la mise en œuvre et le suivi du programme de sûreté et de sécurité de l’organisation.
 Développe et entretient un réseau de relations avec les professionnels de la sécurité, les prestataires de services de sécurité, les autorités compétentes et les autres parties prenantes afin de contribuer à la protection du personnel, des actifs et des informations de l’organisation.
 Réalise des évaluations des risques et des menaces, préparer des rapports d’analyse et formuler des recommandations de mesures d’atténuation adaptées.
 Participe aux évaluations sécuritaires des zones d’intervention des projets et documente les résultats conformément aux outils et modèles standards de FHI 360.
 Contribue à l’élaboration, à la mise à jour et à la mise en œuvre du Plan de Sécurité Pays, du Plan d’Évacuation ainsi que des politiques, procédures et protocoles de sécurité de l’organisation.
 Effectue des analyses régulières du contexte sécuritaire afin d’anticiper les risques susceptibles d’affecter les opérations.
 Conçoit et anime des formations et séances de sensibilisation sur la sûreté et la sécurité à l’intention du personnel.
 Établit et maintient, dans le respect des principes humanitaires, des relations constructives avec les autorités locales, les leaders communautaires et les autres acteurs pertinents afin de faciliter l’accès aux zones d’intervention.
 Collabore étroitement avec les différents départements de l’organisation, notamment les équipes Approvisionnement, Technologies numériques (DTT), Ressources Humaines (People and Culture), ainsi que Contrats et Subventions.
 Assure la veille sécuritaire permanente, collecte, analyse et recoupe les informations relatives aux menaces, et diffuse les alertes sécuritaires appropriées au personnel sous la supervision du Security Manager.
 Veille à la mise en œuvre de mesures d’atténuation adaptées aux risques identifiés, notamment les mesures de protection physique, les procédures de travail sécurisées, les restrictions de mouvement, les équipements de protection et les dispositifs de gardiennage lorsque requis.
 Supervise et coordonne les mouvements du personnel, les déplacements, les moyens de transport ainsi que les systèmes de suivi des effectifs dans les zones géographiques assignées.
 Assure le suivi des prestataires de sécurité contractés par les projets, veille au respect de leurs obligations contractuelles et sert de point focal pour les relations avec ces prestataires.
 Signale sans délai les incidents, violations ou préoccupations sécuritaires aux responsables concernés et recommande les mesures correctives appropriées.
 Veille à ce que tout nouveau membre du personnel, consultant, prestataire ou visiteur reçoive les briefings et orientations de sécurité requis.
 Réalise régulièrement des inspections et audits de sécurité des bureaux, résidences et autres installations afin de s’assurer du bon fonctionnement des dispositifs de sécurité (serrures, systèmes d’alarme, contrôles d’accès et autres équipements de protection).
 Veille à la disponibilité et au bon état de fonctionnement des équipements de lutte contre les incendies, maintient les plans d’évacuation d’urgence et organise périodiquement des exercices et formations en matière de sécurité incendie.
 S’assure que les procédures de contrôle des visiteurs et des véhicules sont adaptées au contexte sécuritaire et correctement appliquées.

TITLE:                          Senior Technical Officer, Health Information System
 REPORTS TO:             Technical Advisor
 LOCATION:                  Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
 FHI 360 is an international non-governmental organization that, in Vietnam, promotes the health and well-being of the Vietnamese people, particularly vulnerable and marginalized populations. It works with the Vietnam Ministry of Health and other national bodies, as well as provincial and commune-level health services to achieve project aims. FHI 360 is currently implementing programs to address challenges in HIV prevention, testing, and treatment , Tuberculosis (TB) case finding, health system strengthening, maternal and child health and nutrition, and global health security.
 The Meeting Targets and Maintaining Epidemic Control (EpiC) is a global project focused on HIV and global health security with funding from the United States Government. EpiC is seeking a qualified and motivated Vietnamese candidate to serve as a Senior Technical Officer, Health Information System (HIS) based in our office in Ho Chi Minh City.
 Main responsibilities: 
 The Senior Technical Officer will play a key role in strengthening health information systems (HIS) through the design, development, integration, and implementation of digital health solutions to support disease prevention and control and advance digital transformation in Vietnam. The position will support the effective operation, maintenance, and utilization of health information systems at facility, provincial, and national levels to enhance patient management, disease surveillance, program monitoring, and data-driven decision-making. The Senior Technical Officer will work closely with government counterparts, healthcare facilities, software vendors, and other technical partners to promote system interoperability, strengthen data quality and utilization, and improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and sustainability of health information systems.
 Specific responsibilities may include but are not limited to the following:
 Collaborate with government partners, software developers, and program teams to support the development, integration, and enhancement of national and provincial health information systems.
 Conduct assessments of existing information systems, business processes, data flows, and user needs to identify gaps and opportunities for system improvement. 
 Translate programmatic, operational, and reporting needs into business requirements, functional specifications, and data standards, and liaise with software developers to ensure effective implementation. 
 Work with government partners to design and deliver training for health facilities and provincial staff on system use, data quality assurance, and data-driven decision-making.
 Provide technical support and capacity building to GVN counterparts to strengthen their capacity in health information system management, data quality, and utilization.
 Assess proposed technical solutions and provide technical oversight throughout system development, integration, testing, deployment, and maintenance to ensure quality, interoperability, scalability, and sustainability.
 Monitor software vendors’ implementation progress and review technical deliverables to ensure alignment with agreed requirements and project objectives.
 Serve as the technical focal point for assigned HIS activities, fostering collaboration, coordination, and government ownership.
 Represent the project in technical working groups, coordination meetings, workshops, and field trips.
 Cultivate strong working relationships across FHI 360 programs and units, Government of Vietnam institutions, USG, and other key stakeholders, providing technical support as needed.
 Perform other relevant tasks assigned to advance project objectives and outcomes.
 Experience and abilities for the position: 
 Bachelor’s degree in HIS, public health, or related fields. Master’s degree preferred.
 Minimum five years of experience in information systems for disease prevention and control. 
 Knowledge and experience in program reporting requirements are an asset.
 Ability to work well with all project staff, implementing agencies, GVN counterparts, donor agencies
 Highly responsible, organized person that pays attention to details.
 Ability to work under pressure, meet deadlines, and achieve ambitious results. 
 Well-developed written and oral communication skills in both Vietnamese and English
 Ability to travel as necessary.

The Technical Advisor for Supply Chain Management supports the Supply Chain team's operations under the direct supervision of the Principal Technical Advisor for Procurement and Supply Chain Management (PTA PSM), with a focus on strengthening the procurement, storage, inventory management, distribution, and monitoring of priority health commodities. In addition, the position will support emergency preparedness and resilient supply chain arrangements, including contingency and strategic reserve planning for HIV/TB and other priority commodities, to maintain continuity of essential health services during supply disruptions and other emergencies. 
 The Technical Advisor will work closely with the Ministry of Health (MOH), the Center for Public Health (CPH) and its regional branches, regional Health Departments, the State Enterprise “Medical Procurement of Ukraine” (MPU), healthcare facilities, NGOs and other relevant stakeholders, providing technical assistance and coordination to strengthen sustainable and resilient supply chain systems in Ukraine.

 - Monitor commodity availability, identify supply chain gaps and risks, and provide recommendations to improve inventory management, distribution, and overall supply chain performance.
 - Provide technical assistance to national, regional, and sub-regional stakeholders on inventory management, forecasting, and supply chain risk management for HIV/TB medicines and supplies.
 - Support the development and delivery of capacity-building activities, including training materials and sessions for regional stakeholders on inventory management, forecasting, and risk management.
 - Provide technical support for the strengthening of storage and cold-chain capacity for priority health commodities at national, regional, and healthcare facility levels.
 - Support the planning, procurement, and deployment of essential storage and cold-chain equipment based on identified supply chain and infrastructure needs.
 - Support emergency preparedness, contingency planning, and stakeholder coordination to ensure uninterrupted access to HIV/TB and other priority commodities through effective continuity-of-supply mechanisms during emergencies and disruptions.

 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing heath challenges.  
 About the Project 
 There have been persistent efforts focused on improving primary healthcare (PHC) and overcoming the hurdles of low coverage and poor quality of health services through several Digital Health interventions. However, majority of these initiatives are designed with very specific clinical or administrative purposes and lack a comprehensive ecosystem approach resulting in multiple applications and digital portals in use for their health system. This cascades into poor accountability and performance, time and resource wastage, lack of continuum of care, and low coverage of health services, resulting in poor health outcomes. PATH is supporting the state of Maharashtra with digitization of primary level of care and health service delivery in select districts. The project intends to demonstrate end to end digitization in healthcare and develop a digital saturation model at district level, leveraging fit for purpose digital solutions/interventions through the use case of improving reproductive, maternal and child health service delivery indicators. The district saturation model will include coverage across rural & urban areas and service delivery across public and private sectors. The focus will be on digitizing healthcare facilities, community health initiatives/programs and deploying innovations for accelerating service delivery across continuum of care. The project aims to form a digitally competent health workforce, improve access to health and systems-level data for resource planning and management, enable creation of longitudinal health records for patients, and enable interoperability of digital systems across healthcare facilities. This will result in data-driven decision-making leading to improved access and service coverage, citizen empowerment, quality care, and enhanced healthcare provider accountability. These positive health outcomes, complemented by favorable policies, governance support, local leadership, and partnerships, will accelerate Universal Health Coverage (UHC).
 PATH is currently seeking for a Block coordinator – Digital PHC on Third Party Payroll (Randstad) for PATH’s Digital Primary Healthcare program in Maharashtra. PATH is looking for highly motivated, analytical professionals possessing a ‘will do attitude’ to work with the organization to support roll out of field activities and support program work in the district.  About the project 
 Pregnancy-associated anemia is a pressing global public health issue, especially prevalent in South Asia, where it plays a significant role in maternal mortality, contributing to nearly half of all maternal deaths. In India, the burden of maternal anemia is particularly severe, with more than half of pregnant women affected. Anemia during pregnancy not only increases the risk of maternal morbidity and mortality but also jeopardizes the health and survival of newborns.
 The Maternal Anemia Project, with a specific focus on the states of Meghalaya, is designed to tackle this critical issue by reducing the incidence of moderate and severe anemia among pregnant and lactating women (PLWs). The project involves a multi-faceted approach that works in close collaboration with state and district-level government authorities to ensure targeted, sustainable interventions. The successful reduction of maternal anemia through this project has the potential to significantly lower the rates of maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality. Healthier mothers are more likely to have safer pregnancies and healthier babies, thereby contributing to overall improvements in maternal and child health outcomes in the target regions.

offres.titre: Regional MNCH Co-ordinator (Consultant), Malaria and Neglected Tropical Diseases (MNTD) - REACH Malaria Madagascar
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing heath challenges.  
 * *Nous procédons actuellement au recrutement de quatre postes de consultants répartis dans les localités suivantes : Alaotra Mangoro, Anosy, Fitovinany ou Haute Matsiatra** 
 PATH est une organisation mondiale à but non lucratif engagée pour l’équité en santé. Depuis plus de 40 ans, elle crée des partenariats multisectoriels et mobilise son expertise en sciences, économie, technologie, plaidoyer et dans de nombreux autres domaines afin de développer et mettre à l’échelle des solutions innovantes face aux défis sanitaires mondiaux. Son programme Paludisme et Maladies tropicales négligées, leader dans la lutte contre les cas et les décès liés au paludisme, conçoit et améliore des outils et des approches, investit dans les programmes nationaux et produit des données pour appuyer les gouvernements dans leurs efforts d’élimination du paludisme.
 PATH recherche un(e) “Coordinateur(trice) Régional(e) MNCH” pour le projet mondial Reaching every at-risk community and household with malaria services (REACH Malaria), financé par le gouvernement des États-Unis (USG). REACH Malaria vise à fournir un appui à la mise en œuvre et une assistance stratégique aux pays afin d’accélérer les progrès dans la prestation complète des services de lutte contre le paludisme, tant au niveau des formations sanitaires que des communautés. Cela inclut la prise en charge des cas de paludisme, la prévention du paludisme pendant la grossesse (MiP), la chimioprévention du paludisme saisonnier (CPS), le renforcement des systèmes de santé, la collecte et l’utilisation des données pour améliorer la prestation des services, ainsi que d’autres interventions de prévention du paludisme. A Madagascar, le projet appuie également les interventions prioritaires du Ministère de la Santé Public en matière de santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et nutrition qui viennent compléter le paquet d’interventions sus citées.
 Veuillez noter que ce poste est un contrat de consultance et que le lieu d’affectation est à Madagascar. 
 Le/La Coordinateur(trice) Régional(e) MNCH assurera le rôle de chef d’équipe de REACH Malaria au niveau de la région d’affectation et apportera un soutien administratif, technique et logistique a son équipe et a la DRSP. Il/Elle sera responsable de la coordination, de l’orientation stratégique et de l’appui technique du projet pour la mise en œuvre des programmes de santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile, de nutrition et du paludisme, ainsi que de la santé communautaire au niveau régional. Il veillera à la qualité et à l’efficacité des interventions dans tous les districts ciblés, en favorisant l’engagement des parties prenantes. La fonction requiert une collaboration étroite avec la DRSP et le chef de région, en apportant un accompagnement technique aux responsables au niveau du BRF et des programmes concernés et des autorités régionales.  Il/Elle travaillera aussi avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre, les autres partenaires techniques et financiers, les prestataires de soins (publics et privés) et les équipes internes, afin d’assurer une exécution coordonnée et dans les délais impartis des activités.
 Responsabilités 
 Servir de liaison entre le bureau central de REACH Malaria et la DRSP/EMAR/EMAD.
 Assumer la responsabilité principale au niveau régional pour diriger l’exécution des stratégies du programme, en veillant à leur alignement avec le PTA, les calendriers et les livrables, couvrant les trois composantes : paludisme, SMNI et nutrition.
 Apporter un appui stratégique et technique à la région et aux districts (EMAD et équipe du projet) afin de garantir la mise en œuvre cohérente d’interventions SMNI à fort impact, en conformité avec les programmes nationaux ainsi que les directives et protocoles en vigueur.
 Planifier et superviser le déploiement des formations, ateliers et visites de mentorat, incluant l’élaboration des calendriers, la sélection des facilitateurs, le suivi post-formation et la supervision formative.
 Renforcer et maintenir des relations de travail solides avec les parties prenantes clés : DRSP, BRF, SDSP, agents de santé au niveau des CSB et/ou clinique, ainsi que les autres départements concernés.
 Représenter le projet REACH Malaria lors des différentes réunions aux niveaux régional et de district, ainsi que dans les groupes de travail techniques (GTT).
 Assurer des responsabilités techniques spécifiques liées à la SMNI, en collaboration avec les responsables régionaux paludisme et santé communautaire, nutrition et survie de l’enfant, MEL ; ainsi que les field officers de districts de REACH Malaria.
 Fournir une assistance technique sur site pour renforcer et institutionnaliser les processus d’amélioration de la qualité des soins dans les formations sanitaires et les sites communautaires.
 Collaborer avec le/la MEL régional et l’équipe Suivi et Évaluation de la DRSP pour analyser les données du programme, suivre les progrès et appuyer la production de rapports fiables et ponctuels et leurs envois au niveau central.
 Assurer une gestion efficace des aspects administratifs, des ressources humaines et financiers avec l’assistant.e A&F régional et en coordination avec l’équipe basée à Antananarivo.
 Documenter et capitaliser les enseignements tirés, les bonnes pratiques et les études de cas avec les EMAR/BRF et l’équipe technique régionale REACH Malaria.
 Exécuter toute autre tâche demandée par le superviseur ou assignée a REACH Malaria.
 Qualifications et expériences requises: 
 Médecin diplômé d’État, spécialiste en santé publique ou en santé communautaire, ou équivalent.
 Minimum de 5 années d’expérience dans un poste similaire.
 Une expérience avec les programmes financés par le gouvernement américain (USG) serait un atout.
 Solide expertise technique en SMNI, amélioration de la qualité des soins, gestion des données et/ou de la chaine d’approvisionnement ou autres domaines connexes de la santé publique et communautaire.
 Connaissance approfondie du système de santé malagasy.
  Connaissance opérationnelle et linguistique de la région d’affectation.
 Bonne compréhension des politiques nationales de santé, des directives, protocoles et programmes liés à la SMNI.
 Maîtrise de Microsoft Office et familiarité avec les outils de communication virtuelle.
 Compétences et aptitudes 
 Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite en Malagasy et français. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais constitue un atout.
 Solides aptitudes en engagement des parties prenantes, plaidoyer et négociation.
 Capacité à établir des partenariats efficaces avec les autorités locales, les partenaires de mise en œuvre et de développement.
 Capacité à travailler en équipe et à établir des relations de travail solides.
 Aptitude à gérer simultanément plusieurs responsabilités dans des environnements diversifiés et dynamiques.
 De préférence originaire de la région d’affectation.
 Disponibilité à effectuer des déplacements au sein des districts et de la région.

offres.titre: Public Health Specialist, ASPIRE, Health System Strengthening (HSS)
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing heath challenges.  
 About the project 
 ASPIRE is PATH’s flagship youth mental health initiative in Karnataka, focused on improving mental health outcomes among adolescents and young people aged 15–24 years. Implemented in Chikkaballapura district, ASPIRE strengthens mental health literacy, self-care, help-seeking, early identification, access to care, and continuity of mental health services through primary healthcare systems, schools, and community-based platforms, while leveraging digital tools and peer-led approaches.
 About the position 
 PATH is seeking a field-driven Public Health Specialist (internally titled Youth Engagement Officer) to lead block-level implementation of the ASPIRE project in assigned taluks of Chikkaballapura district and support project implementation in 2 additional blocks under the leadership of the District Program Manager. The role combines hands-on public health implementation with youth engagement and system coordination. The incumbent will spend ~60% of their time driving on-ground delivery across health facilities, schools, and community platforms, and ~40% supporting district-level data management, stakeholder coordination, and multi-departmental liaison in close collaboration with the District Project Manager.
 The position is suited for Kannada-speaking public health professionals who can work effectively at the intersection of community engagement and government systems, with strong field presence and the ability to collaborate with frontline providers and block- and district-level officials across Health, Education, and Women & Child Development departments.
 Responsibilities: 
 Block-level Implementation & Youth Engagement (Primary – ~60%) 
 Implement all ASPIRE project activities across health facilities, schools, and community platforms within the assigned taluk in collaboration with the primary healthcare providers.
 Coordination at the Primary Health Centre and Health Sub-centre levels with Medical Officers, CHOs and PHCOs in organizing youth outreach sessions, sessions for screening, counselling and reassessment in schools, colleges and other institutional and community platforms.
 Undertake follow-up of young people receiving services within ASPIRE
 Maintain timely, complete and accurate updates of all young people reached through the program using excel.
 Ensure quality of the outreach sessions for mental health awareness, screening, counselling, referral, follow-up, and youth engagement activities aligned with project protocols.
 Provide on-site support and supervision to Primary Health Care Providers including Community Health Officers (CHOs), Primary Health Care Officers (PHCO) and ASHAs and Peer Educators.
 Coordinate with Block Health Officers and Primary Health Centre- Medical Officers regularly for planning of ASPIRE activities and their review along with other health activities and report the outcomes to District Program Manager.
 Coordinate with RBSK teams in the block to implement youth outreach activities.
 Coordinate and undertake training sessions for Peer Educators, health staff, and other frontline stakeholders.
 Share regular field insights, challenges, and recommendations with the district and national project teams.
 Undertake additional responsibilities as assigned by Project Lead.
 District Support, Coordination & Data Systems (Secondary – ~25%) 
 Contribute to district-level coordination through ongoing liaison with relevant officials to enable smooth implementation.
 Ensure timely documentation of field activities and support collection, compilation, and updating of MS-Excel–based MIS trackers from health facilities and schools across the district.
 Share implementation insights, emerging challenges, and field learnings to inform district planning and review processes.
 Provide programmatic and administrative support for district-level reviews, reporting, and convergence efforts.
 Cross-cutting Responsibilities 
 Participate in service mapping and strengthening of youth mental health referral linkages.
 Support convergence across departments to improve youth access to mental health services.
 Undertake any additional responsibilities aligned with project priorities as assigned by the Project Lead.
 Required experience and qualifications: 
 Advanced degree in social work, rural development, community health, psychology, psychiatric social work, health sciences with 2-3 years’ experience and demonstrated skills in implementation of youth outreach and support interventions in community and primary care settings.
 Experience of working with local/block/district level government health department and other sectors related to youth development such as education.
 Technical knowledge and field experience of youth and health programs in Karnataka.
 Familiarity with Indian public health system at the local level - Ayushman Bharat – Ayushman Arogya Mandir, Mental Health Programs, and other initiatives related to adolescent health, youth empowerment, school health and wellness of Karnataka government.
 Skills / Abilities: 
 Proven ability to collaborate work effectively with diverse stakeholders including government officials, local institutions, and others at all levels.
 Ability to work in community settings and schools/ colleges.
 Ability to work independently and plan and execute program activities independently.
 Ability to establish collaborative relationships with stakeholders across different levels - health facilities, schools, colleges, and block level government officials.
 Advanced analytical, communication, presentation and report writing skills.
 Proficiency with MS Office applications, especially MS Word, MS Excel, and MS PowerPoint
 Fluency in Kannada, and English/ Hindi. 
 Location: 1 Taluk in Chikkaballapura district, Karnataka
 Payroll: 3rd Party Payroll (Randstad)

Our current portfolio in Indonesia includes work to support healthcare providers and communities in preventing and responding to communicable and non-communicable diseases, advance digital health innovation, and address global health security priorities. 
 PATH seeks a District Coordinator —based in Maros District of South Sulawesi Province—to support implementation of Phase 2 of the Primary Health Care (PHC) Transformation in Indonesia project, which will include the expansion of project activities to Maros District. The project aims to strengthen cadre skills to implement ILP (integrasi layanan primer/ILP), offer life-course-based PHC screening and referral services, including expanding community-based health screening; promote the use of digital tools to facilitate PHC service delivery and puskesmas -community linkages; and create an enabling and continuous learning environment to enhance cadre and puskesmas skills and further strengthen community PHC delivery.  
 The Maros District Coordinator will oversee and be responsible for timely and high-quality implementation of all project activities in Maros and will serve as the project focal point for district-level partners and stakeholders, including but not limited to the District Health Office (DHO) and Provincial Health Office (PHO). This position will report to the Project Coordinator. People from minority groups and individuals with disabilities and special needs are encouraged to apply. 
 Responsibilities:  
 Lead start-up of project activities in Maros District, under the direction of and in coordination with the Project Coordinator and relevant national-level project focal points, across technical program areas, monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL); finance and operations; and others.   
 Drive development of the district quarterly project workplan and quarterly activity budget, in alignment with the overall project workplan and under the leadership of the Project Coordinator. 
 Proactively oversee and coordinate the operationalization and monitoring of all district-level project activities, in alignment with the quarterly district workplan and in close coordination with the Project Coordinator, to ensure timely and high-quality implementation.  
 Provide day-to-day oversight of all district project staff in Maros, including ensuring staff are equipped with information and support needed for timely and high-quality completion of assigned tasks and support developing and/or reviewing terms of reference, scopes of work, and other technical documents. 
 Provides strategic oversight on activities planning, data utilization and coordination with national teams. 
 Monitor performance of district-level sub-partners and consultants (as relevant) to ensure timely completion of activities and submission of required deliverables. 
 Participate in district-level supportive supervision, mentoring, and monitoring visits to ensure puskesmas and household-level project activities are proceeding smoothly and with quality and to identify additional needs, challenges, or gaps to be addressed.  
 Work with the District MEL Officer to ensure that all required data from district-level puskesmas, sub-partners, and other entities are captured and submitted in a timely manner via required reporting processes and forms.  
 Maintain close engagement with the Provincial Health Office, DHO, and other related district-level government offices during project implementation. 
 Facilitate district-level reviews and planning workshops/meetings with project partners. 
 Participate in project-wide weekly update meetings and provide verbal progress updates against activities, milestones, and deliverables outlined in the project workplan. 
 Lead or coordinate the preparation and submission of written weekly progress updates with the Project Coordinator and other project team members. 
 Anticipate and communicate (in advance) any potential implementation challenges and delay to the Project Coordinator and management team and contribute to discussion on mitigation measures.    
 Contribute to the development of overall project work plan and budget.   
 Coordinate with project district-level staff to lead preparation of or contribute inputs to project technical documents, presentations, and reports (including to the donor).  
 Represent the project by attending regular district/provincial-level PHC-related meetings and sharing notes on key outcomes/next steps with the Project Coordinator and management team. 
 Actively participate in project results dissemination through meetings, conferences, webinars, roundtables, publications, as requested etc. 
 Perform other tasks as required.

 Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of five years of job-related experience in public health, health sciences, and medicine; at least two years of experience in a management role.

 General understanding of advocacy and budget planning processes of the Provincial Health Office, DHO, and other local government entities.  
 Experience working across various stakeholders in Indonesia (government, local partners and civil society, heath care facilities and workers).

 Excellent judgment, strategic thinking, and strong proactivity. 
 Strong oral and written proficiencies in Bahasa Indonesia; English language fluency required. 
 Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook).

 PATH recherche un(e) “Responsable technique régional(e) en nutrition” pour le projet mondial  Reaching every at-risk community and household with malaria services (REACH Malaria),  financé par le gouvernement des États-Unis (USG). REACH vise à fournir un appui à la mise en œuvre et une assistance technique aux pays afin d’accélérer les progrès dans la prestation complète des services de lutte contre le paludisme, tant au niveau des établissements de santé que des communautés. Cela inclut la prise en charge des cas de paludisme, la prévention du paludisme pendant la grossesse (MiP), la chimioprévention du paludisme saisonnier (CPS), le renforcement des systèmes de santé, la collecte et l’utilisation des données pour améliorer la prestation des services, ainsi que d’autres interventions de prévention du paludisme. A Madagascar, le projet appuie également les interventions prioritaires du Ministère de la Santé Publique en matière de santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et nutrition qui viennent compléter le paquet d’interventions sus citées aux niveau national, régional, district et communautaire. 
 Le/la responsable technique en nutrition sera placé(e) sous l’autorité administrative du/de la coordinateur(trice) MNCH régional(e) et sous la supervision technique du/de la conseiller(ère) technique en nutrition du projet REACH Malaria et sera chargé(e) de veiller à ce que les interventions nutritionnelles du projet soient appuyées par des contributions techniques de qualité, en s'appuyant sur les priorités stratégiques du Madagascar en matière de santé et de nutrition.
 Principales responsabilités 
 Assurer la coordination et la mise en œuvre des programmes au niveau de la région, du district, des communes, et CSB et de la communauté.
 Participer à l'élaboration et à la mise en œuvre du plan de travail et du budget.
 Assurer la mise en œuvre et le suivi des plans de travail, budgets et rapports.
 Coordonner l'assistance technique avec le/la responsable nutrition régional(e) de la DRSP pour la mise en œuvre de qualité et conformément aux directives nationales du programme.
 Assister le conseiller technique en nutrition dans la conception, la mise en œuvre, le suivi, le rapportage et l'évaluation des activités.
 Contribuer à l'élaboration de nouvelles approches de programmes liées aux services connexes.
 Collaborer avec les consultants de REACH et PATH pour l’organisation et la réalisation des formations, des supervisions formatives, des rapportages, ainsi que des soutiens au programme.
 Maintenir des collaborations et partenariats stratégiques au nom de REACH avec les équipes de management régional (EMAR) et de management de districts, les donateurs et autres partenaires.
 Soutenir la documentation et la diffusion des meilleures pratiques et des leçons apprises.
 Compétences et expérience requises 
 Diplôme de licence en nutrition ou équivalent avec des expériences pertinentes dans le domaine.
 Posséder de solides connaissances et compétences en matière de formation en nutrition, notamment dans les domaines de la politique nationale et la programmation en santé et nutrition.
 Au moins 5 ans d'expérience professionnelle à responsabilités croissantes, notamment dans les domaines de la programmation et la mise en oeuvre d’interventions en santé et nutrition.
 Expérience de travail avec le personnel du ministère de la santé publique, notamment dans les régions, districts et communes et bonne connaissance des systèmes et programmes de santé et nutrition.
 Expérience avérée en matière de mentorat et de supervision pour le renforcement des services de nutrition; formation aux approches d'amélioration de la qualité ; compétences en matière de pensée critique et de résolution de problèmes pour faciliter la mise en œuvre des programmes.
 Compétences informatiques, notamment une expérience pratique avérée de la suite MS (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
 Connaissances (fonctionnelles ou techniques) 
 Une compréhension de base des questions de nutrition et de santé, dans une perspective nationale, est nécessaire.
 Excellente compréhension des programmes du gouvernement américain.
 Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite, ainsi qu'en présentation en français.
 Connaissance professionnelle de l’anglais oral et écrit serait un plus.
 La connaissance de l'évaluation et du renforcement des capacités des organisations de la société civile/ONG/OBC constitue une valeur ajoutée.
 Posséder des connaissances, des compétences et une attitude à jour et pouvoir les transmettre aux autres.
 Les Candidats(es) locaux (les) seront privilégiés(es) à compétences égales.

 Résumé du poste  
 Le/la « MEL Officer » aura pour mission principale d’assurer la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du système de suivi-évaluation et apprentissage (MEL) du projet à travers la gestion des données, l’assurance qualité, l’analyse, l’apprentissage et l’utilisation des évidences pour améliorer la performance et soutenir la prise de décision. Le/la titulaire du poste devra collaborer avec les équipes techniques du projet tant du niveau national, régional que district, l’équipe MEL régionale, les partenaires de mise en œuvre, les équipes du Ministère de la santé publique, les partenaires techniques et financiers, les prestataires de soins (publics et privés) afin d’assurer une exécution coordonnée et dans les délais impartis des activités pour la disponibilité et l’utilisation de données fiables à tous les niveaux. 
 Responsabilités   
 Appuyer l’équipe dans le développement et la mise en œuvre des systèmes et outils appropriés pour mener les activités de suivi et évaluation 
 Administrer et utiliser DHIS2 pour la collecte, l’agrégation et l’analyse des données de routine, de surveillance et programmatiques. 
 Développer et maintenir des tableaux de bord Power BI pour le suivi des indicateurs de performance. 
 Assurer l’automatisation et la fiabilité des flux de données entre DHIS2 et les outils d’analyse. 
 Mettre en œuvre les évaluations de la qualité des données (DQA/RDQA) conformément aux standards du bailleur et du Ministère de la Santé Publique. 
 Suivre la complétude, la cohérence et la ponctualité des données. 
 Préparer les rapports périodiques à partir des données consolidées via les tableaux de bord et les outils MEL 
 Analyser les données pour identifier les tendances, écarts et opportunités d’amélioration. 
 Appuyer et faciliter les revues de données et de performance et documenter les leçons apprises. 
 Assurer le suivi des actions issues des recommandations des revues de données et des exercices d’apprentissage. 
 Contribuer à la capitalisation des expériences terrain et à leur intégration dans les rapports techniques et produits de connaissance. 
 Fournir un appui technique et des formations de proximité aux équipes et partenaires sur DHIS2, Power BI et les outils MEL. 
 Développer des guides, SOP et outils pour renforcer la qualité et l’utilisation des données. 
 Assurer l’encadrement des équipes MEL au niveau régional et effectuer les supervisions des activités sur le terrain 
 Travailler étroitement avec les équipes techniques du projet, l’équipe du MSanP et partenaires pour assurer l’alignement MEL–programme. 
 Contribuer à la coordination MEL avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et les autres parties prenantes et aux cadres de concertation pertinents.

 Une expérience en systèmes d’information sanitaire (SIS/HMIS), en renforcement des systèmes d’information sanitaire ou en évaluation de programmes est fortement souhaitée. 
 Expérience avérée dans la gestion ou l’utilisation de DHIS2 pour la collecte, la configuration et le rapportage des données. 
 Expérience pratique dans la conception, la maintenance et la publication de tableaux de bord Power BI. 
 Compétences et aptitudes  
 Solides compétences analytiques et capacité à résoudre des problèmes, avec un grand souci du détail. 
 Capacité à traduire des données complexes en analyses claires, narratives et visuelles. 
 Excellentes compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, notamment pour la formation et l’engagement des parties prenantes. 
 Maîtrise de Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams) et des outils de gestion (SQL, Kobo, …) et d’analyse des données (Stata, …). 
 Capacité à travailler en équipe et à établir des relations de travail solides. 
 Aptitude avérée à gérer simultanément plusieurs responsabilités dans des environnements diversifiés et dynamiques. 
 Sens aigu du professionnalisme, esprit d’initiative, intégrité, crédibilité et engagement envers la mission de PATH.

 French Translation below: 
 Applications are to be submitted in English. 
 PATH has unparalleled expertise and experience in developing new tools and strategies for malaria elimination and has the potential to become a recognized leader in accelerating efforts toward global malaria elimination and eradication. PATH’s Center for Malaria Control and Elimination (CMCE) collaborates with PATH staff and strategic partners to coordinate expertise and programs and to maximize our collective impact in support of malaria elimination.
 PATH is seeking a Provincial Administrative Assistant for the Global (REACH Malaria) project funded by the United States Government (USG): Reaching every at-risk community and household with malaria services . PATH aims to provide implementation support services and technical assistance to countries to accelerate progress in delivering comprehensive malaria services at health facility and community levels. This includes malaria case management, malaria prevention in pregnancy (MiP), health systems strengthening, data collection and use for service delivery, as well as other malaria prevention interventions.
 The Administrative Assistant will report to the Provincial Coordinator and will provide logistical and administrative support to facilitate the introduction and implementation of malaria support services, in coordination with the relevant ministries of health, PATH technical teams, and other implementing partners.
 Location: Burundi/Gitega, Muyinga, Makamba
 Division: Global Health Programs
 Responsibilities: 
 Work closely with partners at the provincial level to assist and provide technical support during planned or unplanned events and meetings.
 Collaborate with the finance team and the program team to support implementation of projects defined in the work plan.
 Support the program and finance teams to prepare documentation for financial transactions, ensuring compliance with PATH policies.
 Participate in activities during and after meetings: organizing online conferences and calls, taking notes, and following up on action items.
 Assist with planning and coordinating end-to-end logistics for workshops, meetings, and field exercises.
 Develop detailed budgets for activities; prepare financial reports for workshops, meetings, and field exercises.
 Initiate payment processes in BusinessWorld and follow up with the accounting team to ensure timely settlement of supplier invoices.
 Ensure that all financial transactions are correctly coded and charged to the appropriate project codes.
 Coordinate with project teams to ensure effective management of administrative tasks.
 Work closely with the procurement team to coordinate acquisition of project services and supplies.
 Arrange travel for team members and consultants; track travel schedules, including any changes, and follow up on related activities such as reimbursement requests.
 Support the development and implementation of project management systems to coordinate, track, analyze, and report progress across all project-related activities.
 Contribute to monitoring implementation of key project tasks and recommendations, with a particular focus on operational aspects.
 Contribute to program development, proposal writing, and budget preparation as needed.
 Provide support to the finance team to ensure accuracy of the project inventory.
 Serve as a focal point and backup for other program assistants.
 Perform any other relevant tasks assigned by the supervisor.
 Required skills and experience: 
 Bachelor’s degree in accounting, management, business administration, or a related field, with at least 3 years of experience.
 Ability to work on a multi-site project team with minimal supervision, including a demonstrated track record of proactively solving problems and meeting deadlines.
 Excellent attention to detail and results orientation, while able to adapt to shifting priorities.
 Strong interpersonal and organizational skills.
 Ability to organize and deliver events for large groups and international guests.
 Demonstrated excellent organizational, communication, and writing skills.
 Ability to manage time effectively and work independently.
 Experience working with international NGOs and donors is preferred.
 Fluency in English and French, both written and spoken, is required.
  Ability and willingness to travel.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Position: Assistant(e) Administratif(ve) provincial
 Localisation/emplacement: Burundi/Gitega, Muyinga, Makamba
 Division: Global Health Programs
 PATH est une organisation mondiale à but non lucratif dédiée à l’équité en matière de santé. Forte de plus de 40 ans d’expérience dans la création de partenariats multisectoriels et dotée d’une expertise en sciences, économie, technologie, plaidoyer et dans des dizaines d’autres disciplines, PATH conçoit et met à l’échelle des solutions innovantes aux défis sanitaires les plus pressants du monde. Le programme PATH's Malaria, Neglected Tropical Diseases program est un leader dans la lutte contre la morbidité et la mortalité liées au paludisme : il affine et développe des outils et approches, investit dans les programmes nationaux et construit des bases de données pour permettre aux gouvernements de poursuivre l’élimination du paludisme.
 PATH possède une expertise et une expérience inégalées dans le développement de nouveaux outils et stratégies pour l’élimination du paludisme et a le potentiel de devenir un leader reconnu dans l’accélération des efforts vers l’élimination et l’éradication mondiale du paludisme. Le Centre pour le Contrôle et l’Élimination du Paludisme (CMCE) de PATH collabore avec le personnel de PATH et des partenaires stratégiques afin de coordonner l’expertise et les programmes et de maximiser notre impact collectif en faveur de l’élimination du paludisme.
 PATH recherche un(e) Assistant(e) administratif provincial pour le projet Global (REACH Malaria) financé par le gouvernement des États-Unis (USG) : Reaching every at-risk community and household with malaria services . PATH vise à fournir des services de soutien à la mise en œuvre et une assistance technique aux pays afin d’accélérer les progrès dans la prestation complète de services de lutte contre le paludisme au niveau des établissements de santé et des communautés. Cela inclut la prise en charge des cas de paludisme, la prévention du paludisme pendant la grossesse (MiP), le renforcement des systèmes de santé, la collecte et l’utilisation des données pour la prestation de services, ainsi que d’autres interventions de prévention du paludisme.
 L’Assistant(e) administratif relèvera du Coordinateur Provincial et fournira un appui logistique et administratif pour faciliter l’introduction et la mise en œuvre des services de soutien contre le paludisme, en coordination avec les ministères de la santé concernés, les équipes techniques de PATH et les autres partenaires de mise en œuvre.
 Responsabilités : 
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec partenaires présents au niveau provincial pour assister et fournir un appui technique lors d’événements et réunions planifiés ou imprévus.
 Collaborer avec l’équipe financière et l’équipe programme pour soutenir la mise en œuvre des projets définis dans le plan de travail.
 Aider les équipes programme et finances à préparer la documentation des transactions financières en veillant au respect des politiques

offres.titre: District Monitoring, Evaluation, and Quality Improvement Officer (Maros District), Primary Health Care
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing heath challenges.  
 PATH has been working to support the advancement of health equity in Indonesia through technical partnerships since the 1980s. Our current portfolio in Indonesia includes work to support healthcare providers and communities in preventing and responding to communicable and non-communicable diseases, advance digital health innovation, and address global health security priorities. 
 PATH seeks a District Monitoring, Evaluation, and Quality Improvement (M&E and QI) Officer , based in Maros District of South Sulawesi Province, to support implementation of Phase 2 of the Primary Health Care (PHC) Transformation in Indonesia project, which will include the expansion of project activities to Maros District. The project aims to strengthen cadre skills to implement ILP (integrasi layanan primer/ILP), offer life-course-based PHC screening and referral services, including expanding community-based health screening; promote the use of digital tools to facilitate PHC service delivery and puskesmas -community linkages; and create an enabling and continuous learning environment to enhance cadre and puskesmas skills and further strengthen community PHC delivery. 
 The District M&E and QI Officer will lead day-to-day coordination of project activities related to monitoring, evaluation, and learning and quality improvement, ensuring timely collection of data and qualitative observations to inform project impact assessments and robust documentation of key learnings to inform scale up of effective project activities. They will report to the Project Coordinator. People from minority groups and individuals with disabilities and special needs are encouraged to apply. 
 Responsibilities:  
 Work closely with the National Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Specialist—with additional oversight from the Project Coordinator and Maros District Coordinator—to plan and execute all district-level project M&E and QI activities, ranging from data collection, management, and analysis of data and information from qualitative and quantitative sources. 
 Lead engagement with puskesmas , sub-partners, and other entities contributing to data collection and/or analysis to ensure that all required data are captured and submitted in a timely manner via required reporting processes and forms.  
 Drive the implementation of district-level continuous quality improvement (CQI) activities, including pause-and-reflect sessions, by producing agendas and materials for pause-and-reflect sessions and working with the District Coordinator to ensure district-level CQI activities are well-executed and findings captured for further discussion and follow-up to ensure improvements/adaptations are fed back into project activities.  
 Maintain strong working relationships with district stakeholders to incorporate government priorities in project plans, enable data access, establish feedback loops for key learnings, and to provide technical assistance on data use and triangulation. 
 Provide technical assistance to triangulate routine data and community data, including from digital tools ( Kader Kita ; performance dashboards) implemented at the community level, to inform CQI and cadre planning and management efforts (leveraging existing district-level processes). 
 Contribute to data entry, compilation, analysis, and visualizations for project assessments/evaluations and other technical write-ups and presentations, as requested.  
 Contribute to the design of project-level data dashboards and other relevant data visualization tools.  
 Contribute content for technical reports and presentations, including district-level updates on evaluation or assessment progress.   
 Access and synthesize data from routine district-level sources relevant to the project M&E and QI focus areas related to the health workforce, digital, financing, and gender considerations. 
 Perform other tasks as required.  
 Required Experiences and Skills:  
 Bachelor’s degree in public health, statistics, social studies, and/or related degrees, with 3-5 years of relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation and data management.  
 Demonstrated experience in the collection, management, analysis and interpreting of quantitative and/or qualitative data (mixed methods expertise preferred), including data use for continuous quality or project improvement initiatives.  
 Knowledge and experience in using digital tools for community-level data collection, monitoring and reporting.  
 Understanding of Indonesia's primary health care health system, including knowledge of the community health services (puskesmas, CHWs, and routine reporting). 
 Excellent organizational skills, with proven ability to successfully manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.  
 Proven capacity to work independently and collaboratively in a teamwork environment with solid interpersonal and verbal communication skills. 
 Excellent judgment and strong initiative. 
 Strong oral and written proficiencies in Bahasa Indonesia; English language fluency desired. 
 Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook), familiarity with basic data visualization is an added benefit. 
 Candidates currently living in Maros are strongly preferred.
