offres.titre: Regional MEL Officer – REACH Malaria pour Alaotra Mangoro et Haute Matsiatra, Madagascar
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.  
 * *Nous procédons actuellement au recrutement d'un poste de consultant pour les localités suivantes: Alaotra Mangoro et Haute Matsiatra** 
 PATH recherche un(e) “Regional MEL Officer” pour le projet mondial  Reaching every at risk community and household with malaria services (REACH Malaria),  financé par le gouvernement des États-Unis (USG). REACH vise à fournir un appui à la mise en œuvre et une assistance technique aux pays afin d’accélérer les progrès dans la prestation complète des services de lutte contre le paludisme, tant au niveau des établissements de santé que des communautés. Cela inclut la prise en charge des cas de paludisme, la prévention du paludisme pendant la grossesse (MiP), la chimioprévention du paludisme saisonnier (CPS), le renforcement des systèmes de santé, la collecte et l’utilisation des données pour améliorer la prestation des services, ainsi que d’autres interventions de prévention du paludisme. A Madagascar, le projet appuie également les interventions prioritaires du Ministère de la Santé Publique en matière de santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et nutrition qui viennent compléter le paquet d’interventions sus citées.   
 Résumé du poste  
 Le/la « Regional MEL Officer » aura pour mission principale d’assurer la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du système de suivi-évaluation et apprentissage (MEL) du projet au niveau régional et district en garantissant la qualité des données, l’analyse des performances et l’utilisation des résultats pour améliorer la mise en œuvre des activités du projet. Le/la titulaire du poste devra collaborer avec les équipes techniques du projet, les partenaires de mise en œuvre, les équipes du Ministère de la santé publique du niveau régional et district, les partenaires techniques et financiers, les prestataires de soins (publics et privés) afin d’assurer une exécution coordonnée et dans les délais impartis des activités.  
 Responsabilités   
 Assurer la collecte, la consolidation et la vérification des données de routine au niveau régional et district.  
 Appuyer l’utilisation correcte de DHIS2 et autres outils numériques par les districts et structures sanitaires.  
 Vérifier la cohérence des données saisies et signaler les anomalies au MEL Officer.  
 Contribuer à l’amélioration continue des outils de collecte et des processus de remontée d’information.  
 Suivre la complétude, la cohérence et la ponctualité des données régionales.  
 Organiser et appuyer les évaluations de la qualité des données (DQA/RDQA) au niveau des districts, formations sanitaires et communautaire.  
 Produire les rapports régionaux périodiques et les transmettre au niveau national dans les délais requis.  
 Appuyer la préparation des contributions régionales aux rapports pour les bailleur/partenaires.  
 Analyser les données régionales pour identifier les tendances, écarts de performance et goulots d’étranglement.  
 Appuyer l’organisation des revues de performance au niveau régional et district avec les équipes techniques et partenaires.  
 Documenter les leçons apprises et bonnes pratiques issues de la mise en œuvre au niveau régional.  
 Assurer le suivi des recommandations issues des revues de données.  
 Identifier les besoins en formation et appuyer les équipes régionales, districts et partenaires dans la collecte et la validation des données, l’utilisation de DHIS2, l’interprétation des indicateurs.  
 Fournir un appui technique de proximité pour résoudre les problèmes liés aux données.  
 Travailler étroitement avec les équipes techniques régionales, l’équipe du Ministère de la Santé au niveau régional et districts et les partenaires de mise en œuvre.  
 Participer aux réunions techniques régionales (comités techniques, coordination).  
 Assurer la liaison technique entre le niveau régional et le MEL Officer au niveau central.  
 Contribuer à la capitalisation des expériences régionales.  
 Effectuer les supervisions des activités sur le terrain  
 Appuyer le partage des connaissances et la capitalisation au sein du projet.  
 Exécuter toute autre tâche demandée par le superviseur.  
 Qualifications et expériences requises:  
 Diplôme d'études supérieures en santé publique, statistiques, ou sciences sociales ou équivalent dans un domaine pertinent   
 Minimum de 2 années d’expérience dans un poste similaire. Une expérience avec les programmes financés par le gouvernement américain (USG) serait un atout.  
 Expérience en collecte et gestion de données de routine.  
 Maîtrise pratique de DHIS2 (utilisation, extraction).  
 Compétences et aptitudes   
 Excellentes compétences relationnelles et capacité à travailler avec les équipes terrain.  
 Maîtrise de Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams) et des outils de gestion (SQL, Kobo, …) et d’analyse des données (Stata, …).  
 Aptitude avérée à gérer simultanément plusieurs responsabilités dans des environnements diversifiés et dynamiques.  
 Sens aigu du professionnalisme, esprit d’initiative, intégrité, crédibilité et engagement envers la mission de PATH.  
 Disponibilité à effectuer des déplacements au sein des districts et de la région.  
 Les Candidats(es) locaux(les) seront privilégiés(es) à compétences égales.

offres.titre: Ebola Response Consultant, Epidemic Preparedness and Response, Global Health Programs
offres.lieu: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Remote
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing heath challenges.  
 Location : Democratic Republic of the Congo, with deployment to Eastern DRC and other outbreak-affected areas as required
 Contract Type : Short-term consultant/ Consultant Roster
 Duration : Intermittent assignments and field deployments of up to six weeks at a time
 PATH seeks Ebola Response Consultants for the STRengthening Infectious disease DEtection Systems (STRIDES) Project. The global project will support and strengthen surveillance, detection and analytical capacity of infectious diseases across both human and animal health.
 Through this call, PATH intends to establish a roster of qualified national and international consultants who can be deployed on short notice to support Ebola response activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, particularly in Eastern DRC.
 Selected consultants will provide technical and operational assistance across one or more of the following areas:
 Public health surveillance and field epidemiology.
 Case detection, alert management, and outbreak investigation.
 Contact tracing and transmission chain analysis.
 Health information systems and outbreak data management.
 Data analysis, visualization, dashboards, and automated reporting.
 Geographic information systems, geolocation, and spatial epidemiology.
 Community-based and event-based surveillance.
 Points-of-entry and points-of-control surveillance.
 Cross-border surveillance and information sharing.
 Surveillance training, mentoring, and supportive supervision of response personnel.
 Consultants must meet or exceed the required qualifications listed below. They should be subject matter experts capable of providing practical, field-oriented technical assistance in complex and rapidly evolving outbreak environments, with limited supervision.
 Responsibilities include: 
 Depending on the consultant’s area of expertise and the requirements of each deployment, responsibilities may include one or more of the following technical areas:
 Surveillance and epidemiology 
 Support the day-to-day technical and operational implementation of Ebola surveillance and epidemiological response activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
 Support implementation of national, provincial, health-zone, health-facility, community, point-of-entry, and point-of-control surveillance activities.
 Strengthen systems for alert detection, notification, triage, verification, investigation, classification, referral, and closure.
 Support active case finding in health facilities and communities, including retrospective review of registers and investigation of unexplained illnesses or deaths.
 Support indicator-based, event-based, community-based, laboratory, mortality, and point-of-entry surveillance.
 Conduct epidemiological analyses to describe transmission by person, place, and time.
 Identify transmission hotspots, high-risk populations, surveillance gaps, and priority locations for intervention.
 Support investigation and reconstruction of transmission chains.
 Develop or adapt Ebola case definitions, standard operating procedures, investigation forms, line lists, alert logs, job aids, and reporting tools.
 Support daily and weekly surveillance coordination and epidemiological review meetings.
 Produce situation reports, epidemiological bulletins, presentations, risk assessments, dashboards, maps, and other decision-support products.
 Contact tracing and case investigation 
 Support rapid and comprehensive investigation of suspected, probable, and confirmed Ebola cases.
 Assist response teams in identifying exposure histories, places visited, potential sources of infection, and individuals who may have been exposed.
 Support timely listing, classification, registration, and risk categorization of contacts.
 Establish or strengthen procedures for daily contact follow-up, symptom monitoring, escalation, referral, and discharge.
 Strengthen systems for tracing contacts who are traveling, displaced, unavailable, lost to follow-up, or located across provincial or international borders.
 Support transmission chain analysis and visualization.
 Monitor contact tracing indicators, including listing completeness, daily follow-up coverage, timeliness, loss to follow-up, symptomatic contacts detected, and referrals completed.
 Reconcile case, contact, laboratory, vaccination, and case management data.
 Support implementation and use of Go.Data or other approved contact tracing platforms.
 Train and mentor case investigators, contact tracers, supervisors, community health workers, and surveillance personnel.
 Work with community engagement teams to address reluctance, stigma, misinformation, and community concerns affecting contact identification and follow-up.
 Health information systems and data management 
 Support the design, deployment, optimization, and management of Ebola surveillance and response data systems.
 Assess and strengthen data collection, reporting, storage, validation, analysis, visualization, and information-sharing processes.
 Support configuration and use of DHIS2 and other approved outbreak information systems.
 Develop and maintain case line lists, alert databases, contact tracing databases, laboratory datasets, case management modules, and related response datasets.
 Harmonize data definitions, unique identifiers, classifications, indicator calculations, and reporting periods across response pillars.
 Strengthen interoperability and data exchange among surveillance, laboratory, case management, contact tracing, vaccination, mortality surveillance, and points-of-entry systems.
 Establish data cleaning, deduplication, validation, reconciliation, backup, and quality assurance procedures.
 Conduct data quality assessments and support implementation of corrective actions.
 Develop automated dashboards, alerts, data visualizations, and routine reporting products.
 Support data governance, access controls, confidentiality, security, and information-sharing procedures.
 Troubleshoot hardware, connectivity, software, user-access, data-flow, and reporting challenges in field settings.
 GIS, geolocation, and spatial epidemiology 
 Support geolocation of cases, contacts, alerts, deaths, health facilities, laboratories, treatment centers, vaccination sites, burial locations, points of entry, points of control, and community surveillance structures.
 Develop and maintain geospatial databases, administrative boundary files, health-area maps, settlement datasets, transport routes, and other operational layers.
 Produce routine and ad hoc maps for surveillance, contact tracing, vaccination, laboratory referral, case management, logistics, and community engagement.
 Conduct hotspot, cluster, proximity, accessibility, catchment-area, and spatial risk analyses.
 Support mapping of transmission chains, population movement, displacement patterns, transport corridors, markets, border crossings, and other locations relevant to outbreak risk.
 Identify surveillance blind spots, underserved communities, high-risk border areas, and locations requiring active case finding.
 Support use of GPS-enabled and mobile data collection tools, including KoboToolbox, Survey123, Open Data Kit, or other approved platforms.
 Validate geographic coordinates and resolve inconsistencies in place names, facility locations, and administrative boundaries.
 Integrate geospatial data with epidemiological and surveillance datasets while protecting confidentiality.
 Train response teams in geolocation, mobile data collection, map interpretation, and use of geospatial products.
 Capacity strengthening and coordination 
 Train, coach

 PATH’s Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (CVIA) brings together our expertise across every stage of the long and complex process of vaccine research, development, and delivery to make lifesaving vaccines widely available to children and communities across the world. CVIA’s current portfolio encompasses more than two dozen vaccines either in development or already in use to protect against fifteen different diseases. Our focus is on vaccines to address the leading diseases that claim children’s lives worldwide: pneumonia, diarrheal disease, and malaria; as well as other global health priorities, such as polio and meningitis. We work in partnership with national health ministries, pharmaceutical manufacturers, donors, international financing and regulatory organizations, and many others. PATH has led numerous global partnerships, including the award-winning Meningitis Vaccine Project and the Malaria Vaccine Initiative, which helped develop the first malaria vaccine candidate recommended for pilot implementation.
 CVIA seeks a Global Head of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls, and Non-clinical Toxicology (Global Head of CMC) to help further our mission to ensure affordable and accessible vaccines for people living in low-income settings. The Global Head of CMC provides leadership and management, operational excellence, and technical expertise to all CMC & NT activities within the CVIA portfolio of vaccine candidates and projects through collaboration with CVIA Project Teams, CVIA Diseases and Functional Areas, and CVIA’s vaccine development partners. This role is also responsible for the assessment of new partnership opportunities with respect to process development, product analytics, manufacturing, and quality control, adherence to WHO Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) non-clinical safety assessment and toxicity studies of biological products. The CMC team is comprised of approximately 8 CMC experts and also draws on consultants for specialized competencies.

offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most. With 50 years of experience, a global team of experts, and trusted partnerships spanning 70+ countries, PATH turns breakthroughs into better health for millions every single year.
 Location : Philippines (selected provinces); field travel required
 Timeline:  ~130 working days.
 The Strengthening Infectious Disease Detection Systems (STRIDES) activity is a U.S. Department of State–funded global health security program implemented by FHI 360, with PATH as a core sub-contractor. STRIDES strengthens surveillance, detection, and analytical capacity across human and animal health. In the Philippines, STRIDES works in high-risk provinces across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao in support of the Department of Health (DOH), the Research Institute for Tropical Medicine (RITM), and subnational health authorities, who lead and own the systems being strengthened.
 PATH seeks an AMR Surveillance Assessment Consultant to conduct a rapid, evidence-based assessment of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance and reporting practices in selected provinces, and to translate the findings into prioritized, actionable recommendations. The consultancy is advisory and analytical: the consultant assesses and recommends; implementation of any resulting reforms rests with government counterparts and the wider STRIDES team. The consultant will:
 1. Conduct a rapid assessment of AMR surveillance and reporting practices in selected provinces, identifying gaps in data completeness, timeliness, and platform use.
 2. Based on the findings, develop prioritized recommendations for AMR data management, antibiogram development and training, and inter-facility data review to strengthen AMR surveillance and reporting.
 Responsibilities include :
 Conduct a desk review of national and subnational AMR surveillance policies, RITM-ARSP protocols, DOH-EB PIDSR reporting guidelines, and available AMR datasets and dashboards to orient field planning.
 Conduct structured Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) in STRIDES-supported provinces with Provincial/City Health Offices, public hospital laboratories, Regional Epidemiology and Surveillance Units (RESUs), and ARSP sentinel sites, assessing AMR data workflows from specimen collection through WHONET/LIS entry, RESU consolidation, and ARSRL/PIDSR reporting.
 Evaluate data completeness, reporting timeliness, cross-platform consistency, WHONET/LIS/PIDSR adoption, manual versus electronic reporting processes, and interoperability gaps between facility, RESU, and national levels.
 Conduct structured gap analysis across technical, reporting, and platform dimensions, with root cause analysis benchmarked against RITM-ARSP protocols, CLSI standards, and PIDSR reporting requirements.
 Present preliminary findings at a STRIDES-facilitated stakeholder validation session with DOH and RITM-ARSP counterparts; incorporate feedback into the final report.
 Submit five deliverables to STRIDES Philippines (PATH) for review and clearance:
 Inception Report and Data Collection Tools (Week 1);
 Fieldwork Summary (Week 3);
 Draft Assessment Report with findings, gap analysis, and recommendations (Week 5);
 Validation Presentation (Week 6);
 Final Assessment Report with executive summary, consolidated gap analysis, and prioritized recommendation matrix (Week 7).
 Report to the STRIDES Regional Surveillance Lead (PATH); provide weekly progress updates; and coordinate with DOH-EB, RITM-ARSP, and RESUs through introductions facilitated by STRIDES.
 Support country and partner technical staff to ensure assessment activities are on track and informed by technical expertise; review and contribute to project reporting and technical documentation as requested.
 Required qualifications and experience :
 Master's degree or international equivalent in public health, epidemiology, microbiology, medical technology, health informatics, or a related field.
 Minimum 5 years of applied experience in AMR surveillance, laboratory systems strengthening, or public health surveillance in low- or middle-income country settings.
 Demonstrated familiarity with WHONET or equivalent AMR data management and reporting platforms.
 Proven experience conducting health systems or laboratory assessments using mixed qualitative and quantitative methods.
 Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with experience working across government health agencies.
 Experience working on USG-funded global health security programmes or equivalent technical implementation.
 Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to produce clear, action-oriented reports with prioritized recommendations.
 Familiarity with the Philippine health system, DOH-EB, PIDSR architecture, and the ARSP/RITM-ARSRL sentinel network preferred.
 Prior experience in AMR governance, laboratory quality systems, or One Health surveillance collaborations preferred.
 Must have legal authorization to work in the Philippines, where the consultancy is based.
 Please include your proposed daily rate in your submitted application. This will be one of the fields in your application questionnaire.

 Applications will be evaluated on a rolling basis. The advertisement will be withdrawn once a candidate with the requisite skills is identified 
 Background 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With nearly 50 years of experience building multisector partnerships and expertise spanning science, economics, technology, advocacy, and many other disciplines, PATH develops and scales innovative solutions to some of the world's most pressing health challenges.
 Headquartered in Seattle, Washington, PATH works in more than 70 countries across a range of health areas, including health technologies, maternal and child health, reproductive health, vaccines and immunization, and emerging and epidemic diseases. For more information, please visit www.path.org .
 One area of PATH's longstanding focus is expanding access to voluntary family planning and reproductive health services. A key innovation in this space is subcutaneous DMPA (DMPA-SC), a lower-dose, easy-to-use injectable contraceptive that provides three months of pregnancy protection. DMPA-SC combines the drug and needle in the prefilled BD Uniject™ injection system, which was originally developed by PATH.
 Today, DMPA-SC is approved for use in more than 75 countries worldwide and for self-injection in more than 55 countries, including nations across sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, Latin America, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Europe. Building on its role in the product's development, PATH has worked for more than 15 years with ministries of health, global partners, manufacturers, and implementers to support DMPA-SC introduction and scale-up. Through this work, PATH has provided technical assistance to countries developing and implementing total market approaches that expand access while strengthening sustainable contraceptive markets.
 This experience serves as the foundation for PATH's work in Uganda. In collaboration with the Uganda Ministry of Health, PATH is leading the Uganda Private Sector Market Facilitation for Family Planning in Uganda project (2023–2027), which aims to expand access to contraceptive methods through commercial outlets. As the lead training partner supporting Phillips Pharmaceuticals Uganda's introduction of DMPA-SC in pharmacies, drug shops and private clinics. PATH is training pharmacy and drug shop operators in six of Uganda's largest cities and has reached more than 650 providers to date, with the potential to support more than 4,000 private health facilities nationwide.
 Key challenge 
 Despite significant progress in expanding access to family planning (FP) services in Uganda, the private sector remains an increasingly important source of contraceptive services, particularly through private clinics, pharmacies, and licensed drug shops. However, the availability, quality, and timely use of private-sector family planning service data remain a major challenge.
 Currently, Uganda’s national health information system, including the District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2), primarily relies on reporting mechanisms that are more established within the public sector. While efforts have been made to strengthen private-sector engagement and reporting, many private providers continue to face challenges in capturing, managing, and routinely reporting family planning service data in a standardized and efficient manner.
 As a result, critical information on FP service provision, contraceptive method uptake, client trends, and commodity needs from private-sector.
 It is therefore, against this background that PATH is seeking to hire a consultant to enhance, deploy, and support the Digital Family Planning Register/Application to create a secure, scalable, interoperable, and user-friendly digital platform that enables effective family planning data capture, reporting, and integration.
   Consultant's Scope of Work 
 The consultant will be responsible for enhancing, deploying, and supporting the Digital Family Planning Register/Application to make it a secure, scalable, and interoperable digital platform for private-sector family planning service providers. The key areas of work include:
 System Enhancement and Cross-Platform Development 
 Upgrade the application to operate seamlessly on Android, iOS, Windows, and modern web browsers through a responsive, cross-platform solution.
 Offline Functionality 
 Implement offline data entry, secure local storage, and synchronization capabilities to support units operating in low-connectivity environments.
 Centralized Deployment and Administration 
 Establish a centrally hosted system with secure user authentication, role-based access control, centralized administration, monitoring, backups, and audit trails.
 Facility Onboarding and Geographic Configuration 
 Configure the system to support onboarding and management of private clinics, pharmacies, licensed drug shops, and other accredited providers across all administrative levels, with the ability to add new facilities without system redevelopment.
 Form and Workflow Improvements 
 Modify the electronic family planning register by: Replacing individual age entry with HMIS 105-compliant age bands.
 Making the client name field optional.
 Reviewing and improving skip logic, validation rules, and overall data-entry workflows.
 Reporting and Notifications 
 Develop configurable reminder mechanisms for monthly reporting using in-app notifications, email, push notifications, and SMS (where applicable), including escalation workflows for overdue reports.
 Interoperability 
 Configure secure integration with DHIS2 through data mapping, validation, automated or approved data transmission, reconciliation, and prevention of duplicate submissions.
 Data Security and Compliance 
 Strengthen data security by implementing role-based access controls, encryption, audit logging, and secure authentication.
 Testing and Pilot Implementation 
 Conduct system testing, user acceptance testing, and pilot implementation in selected units, incorporating user feedback before wider rollout.
 Documentation, Training, and Knowledge Transfer 
 Prepare technical and user documentation, develop training materials, train system administrators and users, and provide knowledge transfer to ensure sustainable system management.
 Required expertise, qualifications, and competencies for the Consultant 
 This assignment will be best delivered by a consultant or a company with experience in software development and programming. Additionally, working with a team of experienced individuals with knowledge in Reproductive Child Health and Rights, Family planning, and contraceptive supply chain.
 ●     A minimum of master’s degree in the field of software development.
 ●     At least 8 years’ experience in health systems and developing digital/eHealth systems and    innovations.
 ●     Comprehensive knowledge of Uganda’s reproductive health and supply chain context.
 ●      Comprehensive knowledge of quality-of-care dimensions in sexual and reproductive health. 
 ●     Knowledge of functionality of digital platforms and ability to develop digital content.
 ●     Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality deliverables with aspect of System Integration. 
 ●     A good understanding of the current digital health transformation and health data platforms will be an added advantage.

 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.  
 About the Project 
 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) has launched the Metropolitan Disease Surveillance Strengthening component under the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM). This initiative, supported by the World Bank through the Transforming India’s Public Health Systems for Pandemic Preparedness Program (PHSPP), covers 20 cities across India. PATH has been selected as a key partner by the World Bank in establishing a Technical Support Unit (TSU) to provide expert guidance in the design and implementation of this initiative. The TSU will provide strategic direction and technical support for the initial two years of the program, leveraging global experience and best practices to strengthen metropolitan disease surveillance. The primary objective is to facilitate operationalization, address challenges, and promote innovations as global public goods.
 Position Overview 
 The Consultant – Planning and Finance Management will be instrumental in guiding the strategic implementation, monitoring, and enhancement of the metropolitan disease surveillance program. This role involves collaboration with national health authorities, stakeholders, and technical partners to ensure the program’s success and sustainability. The Consultant will lead initiatives aimed at improving planning, financial management, and sustainable financing for public health interventions across metropolitan cities.
 Duty Location: National Centre for Disease Control, Delhi
 Key Roles and Responsibilities 
 Strategic Planning and Budgeting: Assess cost norms from global metropolitan cities and provide recommendations for realistic planning and budgeting of activities for the metropolitan disease surveillance program.
 Funds Flow and Financial Systems: Evaluate the existing funds flow systems of the program, identifying areas to improve efficiency and transparency in financial management.
 Financial Reporting and Accountability: Analyze the accounting and financial reporting mechanisms to enhance timeliness, accuracy, and accountability in financial reporting.
 Sustainable Financing Solutions: Develop strategies for ensuring sustainable financing for metropolitan surveillance units post-PM-ABHIM, ensuring the long-term financial viability of the program.
 Capacity Building: Provide technical assistance and capacity-building support to finance and administrative teams within metropolitan surveillance units to enhance financial management practices.
 Monitoring and Evaluation: Develop and implement monitoring tools to track the financial performance of the program, ensuring alignment with planned budgets and timely disbursement of funds.
 Policy Recommendations: Collaborate with government counterparts to provide policy recommendations aimed at strengthening planning and finance management for metropolitan disease surveillance.
 Qualifications and Experience 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field. A Master’s degree or professional certification (e.g., CPA, CMA, CFA) is a plus.
 Experience: Minimum 10 years of experience in planning, financial management, or related roles within public health, international development, or government sectors.
 Essential Skills 
 Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills in English and Hindi, with the ability to convey complex technical information.
 Project Management: Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines effectively.
 Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), familiar with financial management software and digital tools for data analysis.
 Stakeholder Engagement: Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with government counterparts, donors, and development partners at national and state levels.
 Health Systems Knowledge: Comprehensive understanding of India’s health system, particularly in the context of disease surveillance and key national programs like NHM, Ayushman Bharat, PM-ABHIM, and others.
 Flexibility: Willingness to travel up to 30% of the time for program-related activities.
 The candidate must have legal authorization to work in India.

offres.titre: Senior Outbreak Response Coordination Lead, STRIDES
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.  
 PATH seeks a Senior Outbreak Response Coordination Lead for the STRengthening Infectious disease DEtection Systems (STRIDES) Project. The global project supports and strengthens surveillance, detection, response, and analytical capacity for infectious diseases across human and animal health systems.
 The Senior Outbreak Response Coordination Lead will be based in Bunia, Ituri Province, and will provide senior-level technical, operational, and coordination leadership for STRIDES-supported outbreak response activities in Eastern DRC, with an emphasis on Ebola Virus Disease and other epidemic- and pandemic-prone diseases. The position will support coordination across provincial and health-zone authorities, technical response pillars, implementing partners, donors, community-facing response teams, and national response structures.
 The position will serve as a key STRIDES field-based coordination focal point for the EVD outbreak response, helping ensure that project activities are technically sound, operationally feasible, aligned with Government of DRC priorities, and coordinated with the broader outbreak response architecture.
 The successful candidate should bring strong experience in disease surveillance,EVD outbreak response, and working with government health authorities at the national, provincial, health-zone, and health-area level in DRC. This may include the Ministry of Health (MOH), Centre des Opérations d'Urgences de Santé Publique (COUSP), Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP), Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB), Direction de Surveillance Epidémiologique (DSE), Programme National de l'Hygiène aux Frontières (PNHF), and Ituri’s Division Provinciale de la Santé (DPS). The candidate should also have direct experience working with the Bureau Central de la Zone de Santé (BCZ) and Médecin Chef de Zone (MCZ), as well as health-area and health-center management and surveillance teams, including IT/ITAs and RECOs. Prior experience coordinating with other relevant stakeholders and outbreak response partners in DRC, including Africa CDC, WHO, US government agencies, UN agencies, and international and national NGOs, will also be critical to this role.
 The Senior Outbreak Response Coordination Lead must meet or exceed the required qualifications listed below. The individual should be a senior outbreak response professional with strong technical understanding of Ebola and other viral hemorrhagic fever responses, demonstrated ability to coordinate complex field operations, and the judgment to operate effectively in high-pressure, rapidly evolving, and politically sensitive response environments.
 Responsibilities include: 
 Outbreak response coordination and leadership: 
 Provide senior-level field coordination and technical leadership for PATH activities under STRIDES-supported outbreak preparedness and response in the DRC.
  Serve as the primary Bunia-based coordination focal point for PATH under STRIDES outbreak response activities, ensuring effective communication between field teams, provincial authorities, health-zone teams, national counterparts, technical partners, and project leadership.
  Support alignment of STRIDES activities with Government of DRC-led response priorities, provincial response plans, incident management structures, and partner coordination mechanisms.
 Coordinate closely with national, provincial, health-zone, and health-area government structures, including MOH, COUSP, INSP, INRB, DSE, PNHF, Ituri DPS, BCZs, MCZs, health-area teams, health-center teams, IT/ITAs, Community Health care workers (Relais Communautaire or RECOs), and other frontline surveillance structures.
 Coordinate closely with WHO, Africa CDC, CDC, other US government agencies, UNICEF, IOM, MSF, other UN agencies, international and national NGOs, implementing partners, and local authorities involved in outbreak preparedness and response.
 Facilitate coordination across key response pillars, including surveillance, case management, contact investigation, points of entry, logistics, data management, operations, and other pillars as deemed necessary.
 Support preparation, implementation, and follow-up of coordination meetings, technical working groups, pillar meetings, partner meetings, and field review sessions.
 Identify coordination gaps, duplication, bottlenecks, and unmet technical or operational needs, and propose practical solutions.
 Support establishment of clear roles, responsibilities, referral pathways, information flows, escalation mechanisms, and follow-up systems across partners and response structures.
 Track agreed actions, timelines, responsible parties, and implementation progress across STRIDES-supported outbreak response activities.
 Support rapid prioritization of response activities based on epidemiological risk, operational feasibility, available resources, partner presence, access constraints, and community needs.
 Provide regular updates to STRIDES leadership on field implementation progress, coordination issues, risks, urgent needs, and recommended corrective actions.
 Technical support to Ebola and outbreak response implementation 
 Provide technical oversight and quality assurance for STRIDES-supported Ebola and outbreak response activities, particularly those related to surveillance, epidemiology, data systems, contact tracing, points of entry, points of control, and cross-border or interprovincial surveillance.
 Support strengthening of systems for alert detection, notification, verification, investigation, classification, referral, and reporting.
 Support active case finding, community-based surveillance, event-based surveillance, health facility surveillance, mortality surveillance, and laboratory-linked surveillance.
 Support implementation and quality improvement of contact tracing, case investigation, transmission chain analysis, and follow-up of high-risk contacts.
 Support the use of timely and high-quality surveillance and response data for decision-making at provincial, health-zone, health-area, health-facility, and national levels.
 Work with data and health information system teams to strengthen dashboards, line lists, situation reports, data review processes, and data quality improvement activities.
 Support geolocation and mapping of cases, contacts, alerts, points of entry, points of control, health facilities, response assets, population movement routes, and high-risk areas.
 Support interprovincial and cross-border surveillance coordination, including information sharing and follow-up of mobile cases, contacts, alerts, travelers, and population movements.
 Provide input into Ebola and outbreak response plans, operational guidance, standard operating procedures, training materials, supervision tools, partner workplans, and technical reports.
 Ensure technical activities are implemented in alignment with national guidance, International Health Regulations, Joint External Evaluation recommendations, Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response principles, One Health approaches, and relevant global outbreak response standards.
 Partner engagement and stakeholder management 
 Maintain regular engagement with national, provincial, health-zone, health-area, and health-facility government counterparts, technical partners, donors, and implementing organizations involved in outbreak preparedness and response.
 Build and maintain effective working relationships with DRC-based stakeholders, particularly those operating in Bunia, Ituri, and surrounding outbreak-affected or high-risk areas.
 Engage directly with MOH, COUSP, INSP

offres.titre: Open Call for Consultants – Health Policy Advocacy and Communications
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.  
 Open Call for Consultants – Health Policy Advocacy and Communications 
 Working across our portfolio PATH's Center for Advocacy & Policy turns evidence into policy adoption and sustainable financing. We  partner with governments, regional bodies, and multilateral institutions to strengthen the evidence, relationships, and policy processes that inform decisions on budgets, regulation, and health system priorities helping accelerate access to proven health innovations. As our portfolio grows across sub-Saharan Africa, donor capitals, and multilateral forums, we are building a roster of experienced consultants and specialist organizations to provide surge capacity for defined, time-bound assignments.
 Scopes of Work 
 Selected consultants will be engaged on a project-by-project basis and may support a range of activities, including: 
 Political economy literacy and analysis, stakeholder mapping, and influence strategy in specific countries or regional bodies 
 Advocacy campaign design and delivery — theory of change, power mapping, message and narrative strategy, moment planning, and coalition mobilization to secure specific policy or financing decisions 
 Development of advocacy tools including policy briefs, positioning papers, technical reports, and presentations 
 Health financing and public financial management analysis — budget cycle engagement, domestic resource mobilization, investment cases, and debt-and-fiscal-space framing 
 Rapid evidence synthesis — ability to surface relevant research quickly and distill it into decision-relevant form 
 Data visualization and storytelling — making complex data intuitive and politically compelling 
 Government relations. 
 Technical policy engagement with ministries of health, finance, and national regulatory authorities 
 Regional and continental advocacy support (African Union, Africa CDC, AUDA NEPAD, African Medicines Agency) and multilateral engagement (WHO governing bodies, Global Fund, Gavi, Unitaid) 
 Development of advocacy communications products — media strategy, op-ed and press material development, polling and public opinion research, and launch packages 
 Facilitation and convening — designing and running iterative collaborative processes with diverse actors (government officials, donors, civil society, researchers); managing group dynamics across power asymmetries 
 Event management - design and delivery for high-level global and regional moments and events 
 Advocacy and funding proposal development — articulating theory of change and translating advocacy strategy into competitive proposals for philanthropic, bilateral, and multilateral donors 
 Qualifications 
 We are seeking candidates who meet all of the following core requirements: 
 Core Requirements 
 Demonstrated experience in health policy, advocacy, or government engagement in low- and middle-income, and multilateral settings 
 Fluency in English 
 Strong client-facing communication and facilitation skills 
 Ability to work independently in dynamic, multicultural, and politically sensitive environments 
 Project management skills 
 Desirables 
 Degree in public policy, public health, economics, international development, or equivalent experience 
 Demonstrated experience designing and running advocacy or political campaigns that achieved a defined change in government policy, budget, or public commitment — including coalition-building, grassroots or grasstops mobilization, and narrative strategy 
 Systems thinking and problem mapping - ability to diagnose complex policy problems, map stakeholder incentives, and identify leverage points 
 Digital and earned-media campaign experience, including audience targeting and rapid-response communications 
 Professional proficiency in French or Portuguese 
 Direct experience advising ministries of health or finance, national regulatory authorities, or working within a legislature or regional body (e.g., AU, Africa CDC, AMA, RECs) 
 Specialist depth in one or more of: health financing/public financial management, regulatory systems policy, global health security, digital health and data systems, artificial intelligence in health, NCDs, climate and health; investment-case economics, media and strategic communications, polling and public opinion research.  
 Established relationships with key health policymakers  and networks  in one or more priority geographies (e.g., Nigeria, Ghana, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Mozambique, Malawi, Zambia, South Africa, Francophone West Africa, USA, UK) 
 Prior work with or knowledge of international donors and financing mechanisms 
 Application Process 
 Interested applicants should submit: 
 Combined application containing your CV (max 3 pages), or capability statement for organizations, and a short cover letter (max 1 page) summarizing relevant experience and naming principal area(s) of specialism from the list above 
 Daily rate in USD 
 We accept applications on a rolling basis and will prioritize candidates and organizations available for short-notice deployments or remote technical support. Due to the anticipated volume of applicants, we will not be able to contact individuals unless they are shortlisted. 
 Position Type: Short-term Consultant (Roster) 
 Location: Global, Remote - with priority for candidates based in or able to work across sub-Saharan Africa, and in donor and multilateral capitals 
 Languages Required: English required; French or Portuguese preferred 
 Start Date: Rolling / As needed 
 Application Deadline: October 23rd 2026

offres.titre: Senior Statistician, Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access
offres.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here 
 PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most. With 50 years of experience, a global team of experts, and trusted partnerships spanning 70+ countries, PATH turns breakthroughs into better health for millions every single year.
 PATH’s Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (CVIA) brings together our expertise across every stage of the long and complex process of vaccine research, development, and delivery to make lifesaving vaccines widely available to children and communities across the world. CVIA’s current portfolio encompasses more than two dozen vaccines either in development or already in use to protect against fifteen different diseases. Our focus is on vaccines to address the leading diseases that claim children’s lives worldwide: pneumonia, diarrheal disease, and malaria; as well as other global health priorities, such as polio and meningitis. We work in partnership with national health ministries, pharmaceutical manufacturers, donors, international financing and regulatory organizations, and many others. PATH has led numerous global partnerships, including the award-winning Meningitis Vaccine Project and the Malaria Vaccine Initiative, which helped develop the first malaria vaccine candidate recommended for pilot implementation.
 PATH is seeking a Senior Statistician who is an experienced clinical trial biostatistician to support the design, planning, execution, and analysis of Phase 1, 2, and 3 vaccine clinical trials, with an initial focus on oral polio vaccine studies. Within CVIA, the polio program supports the global polio eradication effort through a broad portfolio of clinical, epidemiological, and diagnostic work, including clinical development of novel oral polio vaccines (nOPVs), with projects spanning early-phase safety and immunogenicity studies through large Phase 3 international clinical trials. The Senior Statistician’s initial focus will be on the clinical development of nOPVs, including two Phase 3 trials currently in design stage, with opportunities to contribute to other CVIA vaccine development programs as needed.
 Reporting to the Director of Statistics and Data Management, under the leadership of the Global Head of Clinical, statisticians on the clinical team support CVIA programs by overseeing CROs; contributing to protocol design; developing statistical analysis plans; analyzing trial data; drafting and reviewing clinical study reports and manuscripts; and providing statistical consultation on the design and analysis of clinical trials and epidemiological studies.
 This role requires both hands-on statistical leadership and effective oversight of external partners, with responsibilities spanning protocol design, analysis planning, clinical study reporting, regulatory support, and scientific communication.
 Please apply by Tuesday, December 1, 2026 end of day for consideration. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
 Responsibilities: 
 Serve as a study statistician for Phase 1, 2, and 3 clinical trials of oral polio vaccines (OPVs, nOPVs), conducting, supporting, and overseeing all statistical activities across all phases of these studies.
 Lead or contribute to the statistical design of OPV/nOPV trials, including sample size and power calculations, randomization schedules, interim/futility analyses, and Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) support.
 Develop or review statistical analysis plans and analyze and interpret data from OPV trials (e.g., immunogenicity, shedding, and safety endpoints), providing input to study reports and manuscripts with emphasis on the statistical methods section.
 Provide statistical support to CVIA’s broader clinical development programs to ensure that scientifically valid conclusions are drawn concerning claims with respect to efficacy and safety of the products under development.
 Contribute to and/or review study protocols, Investigator’s Brochures (IBs), Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), and other study-related documents in order to ensure collection of required data and correctness of statistical representation of data and results.
 Serve as the primary point of contact for statistical issues between the study team and statistical CRO partner, providing technical oversight of statistical CRO activities, including review of analysis specifications, statistical outputs, data review deliverables, and timelines.
 Support scientific merit reviews (SMR) of CVIA protocols to ensure high standards of rigor and scientific validity.
 Give clear, well-organized in-house presentations of relevant statistical material when requested.
 Attend and represent PATH CVIA at key domestic and international scientific meetings.
 Keep abreast of new developments in the field by reading, attending seminars, and reviewing publications.
 Participate in the preparation and review of regulatory and prequalification submissions for clinical trials receiving PATH support (e.g., develop templates for Integrated Summary of Safety (ISS) and Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE) statistical tables, provide specs, conducts analysis or supervises production of ISS and ISE tables).
 Required skills and experience: 
 Master or Doctoral degree in biostatistics, statistics, or a related scientific discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. 
 Five or more years of experience supporting clinical research, preferably including experience presenting and discussing statistical results and study designs with external stakeholders and funders, such as the Gates Foundation.
 Advanced knowledge of biostatistics and clinical trial methodology.
 Experience supporting vaccine clinical trials strongly preferred; experience with polio or enteric vaccine studies a plus.
 Strong knowledge of statistical software programming with languages such as SAS and R.
 Ability to support US as well as international trials.
 Ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously and also have the flexibility of working both collaboratively and independently in a multidisciplinary project environment.
 Ability to multi-task and effectively prioritize work and projects.
 Ability to work as a member of multidisciplinary teams.
 Ability to clearly communicate basic statistical concepts to other scientists and nonscientists.
 Ability and willingness to travel up to 10–15%.
 Ability to communicate fully in English
 Must have legal authorization to work in PATH country location, such as US, UK, Switzerland, or Belgium. Fully remote candidates in PATH country locations will be considered.
 PATH is a diverse nonprofit organization that creates a culture of collaboration and partnership. Learn more about the impact you can make globally  here .
 We offer our employees a competitive salary and generous benefits. For candidates based in the U.S., the annual salary range for this position is $144,000-$180,000. The final salary is based on a variety of objective factors. PATH provides a comprehensive benefit package that includes 15 vacation, 11 holiday, 2 personal, and 12 sick days per year; medical and dental plans; life insurance; and disability and retirement benefits. For more details click here .
Remote & Hybrid Work
PATH operates within a hybrid workplace model unless otherwise noted. Hybrid employees must reside within commuting distance of one of our PATH offices. PATH’s US offices are located in Seattle, WA, and Washington, DC. This position is approved to be a remote employee from a US state where PATH is registered.
 Please apply by Tuesday, December 1, 2026 end of day for consideration. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

 3.     Promote the use of data and learning for adaptive management and decision-making. 
 About the position 
 PATH is seeking a Monitoring & Evaluation Officer to support monitoring, evaluation, learning, and data-use activities across health systems projects. Reporting to the Lead - Learning and Impact, the M&E Officer will support the design and implementation of M&E frameworks, data-collection systems, assessments, data-quality processes, analysis, visualization, reporting, and documentation of learning.  Responsibilities 
 ·        Support the Lead – Learning and Impact in developing and updating the project’s results framework, logframe, MEL plan, indicator reference sheets, data management plans, data dictionaries, and M&E standard operating procedures, with clear definitions, data sources, frequency, responsibilities, and quality standards. 
 ·        Help set baselines and targets for key project indicators and track progress against them on a regular basis. 
 ·        Design, test, and update data collection tools such as surveys, facility checklists, and interview guides, including digital forms on platforms such as KoBoToolbox or ODK. 
 ·        Train state and city teams, field staff, and partners on data collection tools, sampling, informed consent, and data quality. 
 ·        Coordinate routine monitoring and periodic assessments, including baseline, midline, and endline data collection across intervention geographies. 
 ·        Carry out regular data quality checks, including spot checks, back-checks, and data verification visits; document errors found and corrections made. 
 ·        Ensure project data is stored securely and handled in line with PATH’s data protection and research ethics standards; maintain structured, well-documented, and version-controlled datasets with appropriate metadata and access controls. 
 ·        Clean, analyse, triangulate, and interpret quantitative and qualitative data; disaggregate findings as appropriate, conduct trend and gap analyses, and maintain progress trackers and dashboards in Excel, Power BI, or similar tools to generate actionable insights for programme teams. 
 ·        Support government counterparts at state, district, and city level in analysing and using routine data from HMIS, AB-HWC, and other national portals for planning and review. 
 ·        Draft monthly, quarterly, and annual progress reports, donor reports, and data summaries, clearly separating observed data from estimates and stating data limitations. 
 ·        Support the design and management of internal assessments and external evaluations, including development of protocols, sampling approaches, analysis plans, terms of reference, review of tools, ethics-related documentation where applicable, and quality assurance during fieldwork. 
 ·        Coordinate with external data-collection, research, or evaluation agencies/consultants, as required, to ensure adherence to agreed methodology, data-quality standards, timelines, and deliverables. 
 ·        Help organise review meetings and learning sessions; support the project learning agenda, document lessons learned, case studies, and good practices, and track agreed actions so that monitoring and evaluation findings are used for course correction and programme improvement. 
 ·        Prepare technical reports, impactful presentations, and knowledge products for government, donor, and internal audiences. 
 ·        Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor from time to time for the smooth functioning of the program and to achieve program goals. 
 ·        Available to travel up to 30-40% of the time. 
 Required Experience and qualifications. 
 ·       Master’s degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Statistics, Population Studies, Health Informatics, Social Work, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. 
 ·       At least 3-5 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public health or development programmes. 
 ·       Hands-on experience in designing data collection tools, managing field data collection, implementing data-quality assurance processes, managing datasets, and analysing programme data. 
 ·       Working knowledge of at least one statistical package such as Stata, SPSS, or R, with a sound understanding of quantitative analysis; experience with qualitative data analysis is an added advantage. 
 ·       Demonstrated understanding of results-based monitoring, indicator design, target setting, sampling, data-quality assessment, and interpretation of routine health information systems. 
 ·       Experience with digital data collection platforms such as KoBoToolbox, ODK, or SurveyCTO. 
 ·       Experience with INGOs in the health sector and/ or Ministries of Health, government is preferable. 
 ·       Familiarity with Indian public health system, health data sources, and flagship initiatives such as NHM, NUHM, Ayushman Bharat Health & Wellness Centers, PM-ABHIM, XV-FC, and HMIS. 
 Skills/ Abilities 
 Self-starter and committed to performing their duties with a high degree of autonomy and independence in line with project goals and objectives.
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to data quality, accuracy, and research ethics.
 Ability to explain data and findings in simple language to non-technical audiences.
 Ability to translate monitoring, assessment, and evaluation findings into clear recommendations and follow-up actions for technical and programme teams.
 Strong written and oral communication and presentation skills in English and Hindi.
 Direct experience of working with government health functionaries, district level administrators and other development partners on data and reporting.
 Advanced Excel skills; experience with dashboards such as Power BI or Tableau and GIS mapping is desirable. Familiarity with database management or automated data workflows would be an added advantage.
 Demonstrated ability to effectively collaborate in a matrix organizational structure.
 Ability to handle a variety of assignments under pressure of deadlines.

 PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most. With 50 years of experience, a global team of experts, and trusted partnerships spanning 70+ countries, PATH turns breakthroughs into better health for millions every single year.

CVIA’s current portfolio encompasses more than two dozen vaccines either in development or already in use to protect against fifteen different diseases. Our focus is on vaccines to address the leading diseases that claim children’s lives worldwide: pneumonia, diarrheal disease, and malaria; as well as other global health priorities, such as polio and meningitis. We work in partnership with national health ministries, pharmaceutical manufacturers, donors, international financing and regulatory organizations, and many others. PATH has led numerous global partnerships, including the award-winning Meningitis Vaccine Project and the Malaria Vaccine Initiative, which helped develop the first malaria vaccine candidate recommended for pilot implementation.
 PATH is recruiting for a Global Head, Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (CVIA), hereafter referred to as Head of CVIA . The incumbent will be a strategic, thoughtful, and inspiring leader who will report to PATH’s Chief Scientific Officer (CSO), Product Development. The Head of CVIA will partner within and across PATH Divisions to enhance PATH’s commitment to accelerating health equity. The incumbent will have deep scientific and technical expertise in vaccine development needed to lead CVIA’s portfolio of product development and introduction and technical assistance (impact enabler) projects, which are focused on preventing and/or controlling infectious disease burden that disproportionately affect people in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). 
 The Head of CVIA is responsible for leading the development of strategy and high-level tactics, as well as the implementation of PATH’s vaccines and biologics research, development, and introduction activities, consistent with PATH’s mission, values, and policies, and CVIA’s goals and objectives. The Head of CVIA is an integral member of the PATH Product Development Leadership Team, in addition to leading the CVIA Leadership Team (CVIA LT). Given the ever-changing external public-private partnership environment, the Head of CVIA will serve as a change leader, strategy creator, proactive partner in developing comprehensive cross-disciplinary tactics, and an enabler of exceptional execution through both cross-disciplinary, matrixed product teams as well as teams more narrowly focused on technical assistance in one or more disciplines.

 Create an organizational environment of collaboration, quality improvement, equity, innovation, and creative problem solving.
 Identify opportunities to accelerate impact and/or lower development costs for new and/or improved existing vaccines.
 Collaborate with external partners to advance vaccine and biologic candidates from discovery through clinical development and introduction.
 Provide oversight for the portfolio of existing and emerging vaccines and biologics, with a focus on innovation across the product lifecycle to take to scale fit-for-purpose products in communities in low resource settings with the highest need.
 Lead strategic and tactical analyses of vaccine technologies and assess candidates against a set of selection criteria that align with CVIA’s strategic plan and portfolio goals and objectives.

 The Expand ELEVATE (Engaging Local Experts in Validating and Analyzing TB-data to End TB) is a CDC (Centers for Diseases Control and Prevention) supported, and PATH implemented project under the guidance of the CTD (Central Tuberculosis Division). The project aims to build sustainable data analytics capacity among health program staff and promote data-driven decision-making within TB and public health programs to support TB elimination activities at local level. The project has been in implementation since July 2021 across eleven states of India (Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Mizoram, Odisha, Rajasthan, Sikkim and West Bengal) and it set to expand to new geographies.
 Each intervention state is supported by a Public Health Data Analyst (PHDA) who provides technical assistance to NTEP (National Tuberculosis Elimination Program) teams in data analysis and its use for programmatic actions.  The project promotes the Data Champion approach, wherein the programme staff are equipped with required analytic skills to independently assess programme performance, identify gaps in the tuberculosis care cascade and facilitate evidence-based programme actions.

offres.titre: Specialist, Design, Optimization and Operations Management - GL D - Defined Duration until December 2029
offres.description:
Specialist, Design, Optimization and Operations Management - GL D - Defined Duration until December 2029 
The Specialist, Design, Optimization & Operations Management will serve as a strategic advisor, business architect, and operational governance lead responsible for designing, optimizing, and continuously improving investment policies, decision frameworks, governance processes across the investment lifecycle. The Specialist will drive investment effectiveness, efficiency, transparency, and accountability by ensuring that investment planning, prioritization, review, approval, oversight, and reporting processes are strategically aligned, operationally effective, and responsive to organizational needs. 
Working in close partnership with teams across SIED, Grant Management, Legal, Finance, Risk, Information Technology, governance bodies, and external partners, the Specialist will act as a key integrator of cross-functional perspectives, translating strategic priorities and policy requirements into practical operating models, governance mechanisms, workflows, tools, and guidance. The Specialist will also lead the transformation and operationalization of Technical Review Panel (TRP) and Grant Approvals Committee (GAC) processes, including governance frameworks, differentiated review modalities, workflows, tools, guidance, and performance management mechanisms. The role will also ensure timely, consistent, evidence-based, and high-quality investment decision-making through effective coordination of review processes, robust analytics, policy implementation, and continuous process improvement.
Under the supervision of the Lead, Investment Oversight, the Specialist, will serve as a critical bridge between strategy, policy, governance, operations, and technology, by coordinating complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives that strengthen allocation, portfolio optimization, investment oversight, and decision support. 
The position will provide strategic insights, advice, oversight, and operational leadership to strengthen portfolio optimization, resource prioritization, decision support, and organizational performance while embedding a culture of continuous process improvement and operational excellence across the investment lifecycle. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Design and optimization of investment policies, decision frameworks, and processes 
 Provide oversight for the updating of OPNs, procedures and due diligence screening guidelines in relation to investment review and approval (TRP/GAC), including key areas such as Portfolio Optimization, Program split, Allocation Utilization Period (AUP), and CCM eligibility differentiation.
 Coordinate the development, review, and updating of key materials including but not limited to the Modular Framework, Performance Framework and other investment guidance materials.
 Lead the operational preparation and customization of allocation letters and share with internal stakeholders to send to applicants.
 Management of investment processes 
 Oversee the timely completion of program split changes and report any changes to the program split.
 Lead and quality assure the preparation of the list of applicants and typology and oversee the tracking and publication of Eligibility and Transition Projections as well as preparing Application classification type.
 Lead activities related to Prioritized Above Allocation Request (PAAR) and oversee development and publication of the Global Fund’s Register of Unfunded Quality Demand. Provide analysis and technical support to enable portfolio optimization and investment decisions, as well as facilitate donor investment enquiries related to the Register.
 Support the Lead, Investment Oversight during the Portfolio Optimization process, ensuring effective implementation of the Strategy Committee Prioritization Framework through robust data analysis and rigorous review, including:
 Leading the planning, preparation and execution of end-to-end Portfolio Optimization investment processes annually. This includes harmonizing prioritized investments across business owners, ensuring robust documentation of data driven investment cases, internal review and validation of prioritized investments in line with portfolio optimization principles and criteria, investment meetings and other prioritization processes.
 Coordinating cross-functional inputs to prepare comprehensive materials for GAC investment decision making and award processes. This includes conducting data analysis, developing presentation slides and decision dashboards, as well as preparing briefings that support investment decision-making.
 TRP and GAC management and transformation    
 Together with the Lead, Investment Oversight, provide strategic leadership for TRP/GAC transformation and implementation, designing and operationalizing governance frameworks, differentiated review mechanisms, workflows, tools, and guidance that support efficient and effective decision-making. 
 Coordinate end-to-end delivery of TRP and GAC review cycles under the direction of the Lead, including workplans, calendars, agendas, member deployment, meeting and remote-review logistics, stakeholder inputs, outcome communications and follow-up actions.
 Operationalize approved differentiated TRP review modalities for funding requests and catalytic investments, maintain supporting workflows and tools, and recommend practical improvements based on implementation experience.
 Draft and maintain TRP operating procedures, manuals, practical guidance and governance documentation in line with approved policy direction and the TRP terms of reference.
 Administer TRP membership and governance processes, including recruitment, onboarding, leadership and working-group coordination, member records, conflict-of-interest controls and performance data.
 Prepare and quality-assure GAC briefings, analyses, presentations and decision records, ensuring that materials clearly set out evidence, risks, policy considerations, precedents and options for decision.
 Synthesize recurring issues, lessons and portfolio-wide implications arising from TRP and GAC reviews, and provide evidence-based options to the Lead, Investment Oversight for process, policy and investment decision-making.
 Coordinate agreed information flows between TRP and GAC, maintain authoritative records of decisions and dependencies, and monitor completion of actions by responsible teams.
 Draft TRP and GAC reports, funding recommendation documentation and responses to governance queries for review and clearance by the Lead and relevant governance leadership.
 Perform people management responsibilities and provide day-to-day technical guidance and quality assurance to Operations Officers on assigned TRP/GAC deliverables.
 Subject to change by the Executive Director at any time at their sole discretion. 
 Qualifications 
 Essential: 
 Advanced university degree in public health, international development, public policy, business or public administration, economics, finance, operations management, investment management, or a related field; or a relevant first university degree and at least 4 years of relevant post-first-degree work experience.
 Desirable: 
 Professional certification or demonstrable experience in project or program management, business process improvement, operations, transformation, change management, and advanced data analytics.
 Experience 
 Essential: 
 Substantial relevant experience in investment, grant or portfolio management; strategic planning; policy and process design; operations; or organizational transformation in a complex international or public-sector environment.
 Demonstrated experience designing, implementing and continuously improving governance frameworks, operational policies, procedures, review processes, controls and performance measures.
 Experience supporting senior-level investment review, prioritization or approval processes and producing high-quality analyses, decision materials
