If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 As the humanitarian crisis in Venezuela continues, the risk of hyperinflation and mobility restrictions severely limit access to basic goods and services. To date, around 8 million Venezuelans have left the country.  The IRC has responded to the crisis by supporting Venezuelans within Colombia, providing health, nutrition, WASH (water, sanitation, and hygiene), economic recovery, protection, and education services.  At the same time, escalating violence and armed conflict have generated serious protection risks in Colombia and Ecuador. This escalation of violence adds to the existing pressures in both countries, which host 2.8 million and 441,000 Venezuelan migrants, respectively. Across the region, escalating violence and conflict are now generating new waves of internal displacement or confinement, directly disrupting access to services, deteriorating health and protection systems, and widening gaps in the provision of care.  In this context, the IRC works, together with local organizations, to support communities affected by conflict in both Colombia and Ecuador in accessing basic goods and services, including education, health, and protection. 
 JOB PURPOSE 
 The Deputy Director of Programs (DDP) position is a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT) and is central to the successful implementation of IRC programs in Colombia. Under the direction of the Country Director (CD), the DDP is responsible for leading program strategy in alignment with local government policies and strategies; guiding sound project management following industry best practices; supporting business development efforts; and ensuring compliance with donor regulations.  The Deputy Director of Programs for Colombia will manage all programming in Colombia, as well as partner-led outreach programs in Ecuador, and will provide leadership to all program staff based in, or traveling to, these countries. 
 The responsibilities of this position are aligned with the IRC’s global strategy and reinforce program excellence, gender equality, and greater client voice and choice. This role requires an innovative and pragmatic individual, willing to take smart risks within contexts constrained by security considerations. The DDP must be able to adapt and adjust programming to new scenarios as the context evolves, in order to ensure both staff safety and effective program delivery.  The role must comply with IRC security protocols, designed to protect staff, partner organizations, and clients, and to foster a culture of safety among program staff. 
 The DDP will lead the development and execution of the Country Strategic Plan and will be responsible for overseeing technical coordinators and project leads based in Colombia. The position will report to the Country Director for Colombia, Venezuela, and Ecuador, and will coordinate closely with other senior staff based in Caracas or Bogotá; with Regional and Global Technical Advisors in health, protection, economic recovery and development, education, and MEAL; and with the IRC’s Emergency Unit.
 The DDP will be based in Colombia and will be required to travel up to 30% of the time.
 Languages: Fluency in both English & Spanish required. 
 SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Program Strategy, Design, and Business Development  
 Lead efforts for sustainable program growth, proactively identifying opportunities for new programming initiatives and prioritizing multi-year funding opportunities to support them.
 Implement the IRC’s business development strategy in Colombia, identifying donors and funding opportunities, and expanding and strengthening the IRC’s donor base.
 Coordinate with the regional team, technical advisors, Colombia staff, and partners to submit innovative, high-quality proposals; lead the drafting of technical proposals and budgets.
 Collaborate with Communications, MEAL, and Grants to implement the IRC’s positioning strategy, sharing the impact of the IRC’s work with clients in Colombia and Ecuador.
 Ensure, together with Technical Unit staff, that project design reflects the IRC’s program quality standards and industry best practices. 
 Provide guidance, strategies, and tools to ensure that programming decisions are based on the findings and analysis of needs assessments (primary and secondary data), on input from communities and clients, and on a thorough understanding of context, technical best practices, and operational feasibility.
 Formulate integrated program initiatives so that technical sectors complement one another and promote the incorporation of protection principles and gender-sensitive approaches.
   Program Management – Implementation, Monitoring, and Evaluation 
 Provide overall leadership and management of the IRC’s program portfolio in Colombia and Ecuador, ensuring strategically coherent program direction, well-managed growth, and compliance with IRC and donor regulations.
 Support the Country Director in designing, implementing, and updating the Strategic Action Plan (SAP) for Colombia, in order to guide decision-making and define our added value, based on updated context analyses and needs assessments. 
 Continuously seek ways to strengthen the capacities of program team members, both individually and collectively.
 Ensure that detailed, realistic, and feasible project implementation plans are developed, and adapted as needed to better respond to changing contextual needs, in collaboration with the program and operations teams.
 Coordinate with other Senior Management Team members on appropriate management, compliance, and performance standards, as well as effective systems for budget management, knowledge management, and risk management.
 Collaborate with the Security Coordinator to ensure that appropriate security protocols are developed for effective yet security-conscious program implementation. 
 Support program staff in collecting, documenting, and disseminating lessons learned and best practices, incorporating them into the design of new projects. 
 Together with program staff, develop effective, results-oriented MEAL plans that accurately reflect the impact of our work on the lives of our clients, including methodologies and tools to strengthen the quality of data collection, analysis, and reporting.
 Review M&E and accountability data with program staff to identify and address areas for operational improvement.  Ensure that feedback channels are responsive to client profiles and that client feedback is addressed and incorporated into adaptive management processes.
 Work through the IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS), a comprehensive set of compliance tools for establishing, managing, and closing partnerships and grants. 
 Serve as a liaison with partner organizations and support partnerships staff to ensure that all partners understand their role and responsibilities, and feel that they can share feedback with the IRC.

offres.titre: Team Leader, Syria Education Programme III (SEP III)
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Please note this is an evergreen position. We accept applications on an ongoing basis to build a talent pipeline for roles that open regularly. Because this posting may not reflect a current opening, we may not contact every applicant. If your background aligns with an open need, our team will reach out. We also encourage you to visit our careers page to explore other opportunities. 
 The IRC has worked in Syria since 2012 and is one of the largest providers of humanitarian and early recovery assistance in the country, delivering health, protection, economic recovery, water and sanitation, and education programming, including as a partner to the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO).
 SYRIA EDUCATION PROGRAMME III (SEP III) 
 Building on SEP I (2018–2022) and SEP II (2022–2027), which supported primary educatio in Idleb and Aleppo, FCDO plans to procure a new Technical Assistance (TA) contract, SEP III, to support the Syrian Ministry of Education (MoE) in implementing its nationally-led reform agenda, complementing the Ministry's wider reform programme, including support provided through the Global Partnership for Education (GPE). Since December 2024, the MoE has begun to reunify a fragmented education system, but progress has been constrained by limited institutional capacity, a lack of data, weak policy development processes and the absence of a clear long-term strategy for recovery. Unlike earlier phases, which focused primarily on service delivery in northwest Syria, SEP III will work directly with the MoE and local Education Directorates, generally at national level and directorate level, in partnership with Ministry officials, to help the Ministry translate its policy and process reforms into practice through technical advice, capacity building, coaching and support to implementation.
 SEP III has two components. The first, which is the subject of this contract, is politically informed TA to the MoE and Education Directorates to strengthen inclusive, effective and evidence-based policy making. The second is non-formal education (NFE) for returning refugees and internally displaced persons, which is outside the scope of this contract and will be delivered by a separate provider. The TA supplier will be required to work collaboratively with the NFE component.
 The exact scope of the TA work will be determined jointly with FCDO and the MoE through a demand-led, co-designed and flexible approach. No reform priorities are set in advance; they will be identified with the Ministry during inception. The work is expected to focus on strengthening the education system to improve foundational learning outcomes for primary-school-aged children across Syria, delivered through: 1) Services and Analysis to inform TA and policy decisions; 2) Foundational Learning thematic TA (for example teacher development, coaching and supervision, safeguarding, learning data generation and use, and inclusive education); and 3) Education Systems Strengthening TA (sector planning and prioritisation, policy development, financial management, and monitoring and accountability). Given the difficult fiscal choices likely to shape the sector over the coming years, the programme is also expected to support the Ministry's public finance and value-for-money decision-making. Illustrative technical priorities include: supporting policy reform and Ministry-led coordination, standard-setting, and system strengthening; supporting the roll-out of child safeguarding and Codes of Conduct; improving the quality and consistency of teaching through professional development and a national Teacher Competency Framework; and data-driven planning, including through education management information systems (EMIS/SIMIS).
 Given the fluid transition context, the programme will need to operate flexibly, respond quickly to changes, and seize windows of opportunity for reform as they arise. FCDO expects a politically informed, 'test, learn, adapt' approach rather than a fixed blueprint. Delivery must be aligned with government systems, avoiding parallel platforms and the substitution of government functions, and must be underpinned by gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) and conflict sensitivity. This requires strong political judgement, including a clear understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, an in-depth understanding of the Syrian education system and its institutional actors, and the ability to sustain trusted relationships with the Ministry, FCDO, and other sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), and the World Bank.
 The anticipated delivery model comprises i) a Core Delivery Team responsible for overall leadership, technical oversight, coordination, MEAL, governance and quality assurance, which should be predominantly Syrian and mostly based in Syria; and ii) a demand-led TA Pool of experts with education and governance backgrounds. The contract is expected to begin on 1 July 2027 with a six-month inception period, during which the supplier must mobilise rapidly, establish a presence in Damascus and operationalise its delivery systems. Details are indicative and will be confirmed in FCDO's Tender Notice.
 POSITION SUMMARY 
 The Team Leader holds overall accountability for the design, rapid mobilisation, and delivery of SEP III, including leading the Core Delivery Team and overseeing the TA Pool, ensuring the programme is implemented in accordance with the contract, FCDO requirements, IRC policies and principles, and internationally recognised quality of assistance standards. The Team Leader is the primary point of contact with FCDO and, working closely with the ESS Technical Director and senior Ministry counterparts, provides strategic direction to support the Ministry's implementation of its reform priorities.
 The Team Leader is responsible for the programme's overall management, including budget oversight and value for money, performance against contractual KPIs, and risk management (including fiduciary and reputational risk in a sensitive political environment), with the technical quality of the programme's workstreams assured by the ESS Technical Director. The postholder ensures the programme operates adaptively — using political analysis, evidence, monitoring data, and regular review points to prioritise, test, learn and adapt in response to a fast-moving political and institutional context — while maintaining the flexibility needed to respond to emerging windows of opportunity for reform.
 The Team Leader maintains strong working relationships with the implementing team, consortium/delivery partners (if applicable), the MoE and Education Directorates, FCDO, the provider of the NFE component, and other education sector stakeholders, and represents the programme and IRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups, and policy dialogues. The postholder also oversees programme staffing, procurement, and administrative functions, and ensures robust communications and knowledge management, both internally and with external stakeholders, to share progress, evid

 Job Overview 
 Under the direct supervision of the Child Protection Coordinator, the Evidence, Learning and Advocacy Manager - Child Protection will lead evidence generation, learning capture, technical documentation, external reporting support, advocacy and policy engagement, and strategic government engagement for IRC Ukraine's Child Protection department. The position will serve as a key support to the Child Protection Coordinator for national-level positioning, regular engagement with government counterparts, coordination mechanisms, donors, UN agencies, and other strategic stakeholders. 
 The position will translate programme data, assessments, partner and field learning, and operational experience into high-quality external reports, analysis, briefing materials, presentations, learning products, policy and advocacy outputs, and technical documentation. The role will maintain a strong understanding of Ukraine's child protection system, institutional architecture, policy and reform environment, and key government and coordination processes, and will help ensure that IRC's Child Protection evidence and programme experience are consistently reflected in external engagement and sector-level discussions.

 • Support and contribute to external reporting for donors, coordination bodies, government counterparts, and other external stakeholders by providing clear technical narrative, cross-location analysis, evidence of results, emerging needs, challenges, adaptations, and lessons learned, in coordination with Grants and MEAL.

 • Attend regular meetings with key government counterparts, national and sub-national authorities, technical working groups, and inter-agency coordination mechanisms when delegated by the CP Coordinator, ensuring consistent and professional IRC Child Protection representation.

If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 L'IRC a commencé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire provoquée par l'afflux de réfugiés du Darfour vers l'est du Tchad, avec une intervention dans le camp de réfugiés d'Oure Cassoni. L'assistance aux réfugiés soudanais s'est maintenant étendue à la gestion de dix camps à l'est et d'un camp à l'ouest, avec une assistance aux réfugiés et aux communautés locales en matière de santé, de nutrition et d'eau, d'hygiène et assainissement.
 En 2012, pour répondre à la sécheresse et à l'insécurité alimentaire, l'IRC a étendu sa couverture géographique dans la région du Guéra. L'IRC travaille actuellement dans trois districts sanitaires, Mongo, Mangalmé et Melfi, et fournit des services de prévention et de traitement de la malnutrition à la population locale.
 En mai 2016, l'IRC a ouvert un bureau dans la région du Lac pour répondre à la crise de Boko Haram L'IRC met en œuvre des projets d'assistance dans les domaines de la santé, de la nutrition ainsi que de la protection et de la réponse à la violence basée sur le genre.
 L'IRC Tchad s'engage dans son plan d'action stratégique 2025-2030 à continuer à fournir des services humanitaires essentiels en matière de santé, de nutrition et de protection / VBG, tout en améliorant le bien-être économique et en renforçant la résilience des bénéficiaires, en particulier des femmes et des filles. L'IRC Tchad continuera à travailler avec et à soutenir étroitement les acteurs étatiques / ministères de tutelle dans les domaines clés afin que les actions de l'IRC soient intégrées dans les politiques nationales pour assurer une meilleure appropriation des actions entreprises.
 APERCU DU POSTE 
 Le/La Coordinateur/trice Budget et Reporting assiste le Directeur Adjoint des Finances dans la gestion du département Budget et Reporting. Il/Elle apporte un soutien technique et opérationnel dans la planification budgétaire, le suivi financier, la production des rapports financiers et des bailleurs, ainsi que dans la supervision, la formation et la gestion du personnel. Il/Elle contribue également au renforcement des contrôles internes, à la gestion des partenariats et à la mise en œuvre des politiques et procédures financières afin d’assurer la conformité et l’atteinte des objectifs du programme pays. 
 PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES 
 Le/La Coordinateur/trice Budget et Reporting est responsable de l’orientation stratégique et de la supervision globale de la gestion budgétaire et du reporting financier du programme pays. Sous la supervision du Directeur Adjoint des Finances, il/elle assure la planification, le suivi et l’analyse des budgets, la supervision financière des partenariats, ainsi que le renforcement des capacités et l’accompagnement technique du personnel finance. Il/Elle contribue également à l’amélioration des processus financiers, à la qualité des rapports financiers et au respect des exigences des bailleurs de fonds et des politiques de l’IRC. 
 Budget: 
 Aider à la préparation et à la révision des propositions et des budgets des programmes et des subventions.
 Participer à la préparation et à la mise à jour du budget de fonctionnement du pays, y compris la préparation de directives budgétaires pour aider les responsables de programme à formuler les budgets.
 Conformément aux exigences des donateurs et à la politique de l'IRC, il élabore le budget des opérations sur le terrain et suit la méthodologie d'allocation des frais généraux aux budgets de subvention pour couvrir les besoins opérationnels des programmes.
 Travailler avec le personnel du programme pour préparer les budgets des subventions afin de soutenir les réalignements pour assurer une couverture adéquate des coûts de fonctionnement et des coûts directs et indirects de NY.
 Examen mensuel des résultats réels par rapport au budget afin de garantir l'utilisation maximale des montants budgétisés et de fournir des recommandations pour les réalignements, le cas échéant.
 Assurer la surveillance des dépenses de subventions actives par rapport au budget afin de s'assurer que les dépenses sont conformes aux objectifs et que les écarts/reclassements sont réduits au minimum.
 Préparer ou examiner les journaux d'ajustement pour corriger les erreurs de codage, les reclassifications, etc.
 Participer à l'ouverture/la clôture des subventions et aux réunions mensuelles de révision du BVA.
 Assurer le suivi et fournir un retour d'information au personnel des opérations et des programmes sur les points d'action des réunions BVA précédentes et proposer des journaux d'ajustement nécessaires pour tous les rapports BVA et financiers en conformité avec les règlements des donateurs.
 S'assurer que les prévisions sont mises à jour pour les subventions et préparer une analyse avec les chiffres réels pour montrer les écarts et les domaines d'amélioration.
 Rapports des Donateurs 
 Préparer et consolider les rapports financiers des subventions et les soumettre à l'examen du directeur adjoint des finances.
 Analyse du budget du partenariat par rapport aux résultats réels afin d'identifier les problèmes de comptabilité ou de conformité.
 Identification des problèmes de procédure ou de formation à résoudre pour améliorer la qualité des rapports de données. Informer régulièrement le directeur adjoint des finances des problèmes à résoudre concernant les rapports financiers des partenaires.
 Assurer la soumission en temps voulu des rapports financiers, y compris des actifs, et veiller à ce que toutes les échéances soient communiquées aux donateurs en temps voulu. Assurer une liaison proactive avec le responsable du projet ou le coordinateur budgétaire/donateur si les délais ne peuvent être respectés.
 Autres tâches 
 Contribuer au bon fonctionnement général du département financier en assumant toute autre tâche assignée par le superviseur.
 Contribuer à l'amélioration générale du système financier et comptable de l'IRC Tchad en faisant des recommandations au superviseur sur les domaines spécifiques qui pourraient être améliorés.
 Programmer et coordonner la réunion financière hebdomadaire, y compris les finances sur le terrain, et diffuser les minutes et les actions avec le personnel financier.
 Fournir un soutien aux défis et l'assistance nécessaire pour exécuter la tâche hebdomadaire du département des finances à partir des réunions.
 Coordonner la communication entre les subventions, les programmes et les sous-bénéficiaires de l'IRC.
 En collaboration avec l'unité subvention/le chef de projet, convoquer régulièrement des réunions de coordination des partenaires.
 Documenter et partager les comptes rendus des réunions de coordination des partenaires, assurer le suivi des points d'action convenus lors de la réunion de coordination avec les partenaires.
 Travailler et maintenir une communication régulière avec les coordinateurs sectoriels pour l'intégration du programme par la mise en œuvre de projets impliquant des partenaires.
 Contribuer au travail d'équipe et au jeu d'équipe.
 Remplacer le directeur adjoint des Finances, en cas de besoin.

 Job Overview/Summary: 
 The Finance Partnership Coordinator is a key position within the Finance Department, leading the financial oversight and management of the IRC Partnerships Department's sub-awardees, in very close coordination and cooperation with the IRC's internal Finance staff.
 The position is responsible for providing strategic oversight and quality assurance of the financial management of sub-awardees, and for supervising the Finance Partnership Manager in the day-to-day execution of this work. The Finance Partnership Coordinator leads capacity-building efforts for sub-awardees to strengthen their financial management and administrative capacity, in coordination with the partners, Partnerships Department staff, and IRC Finance staff. The Finance Partnership Coordinator oversees the review of sub-awardee budgets at the proposal stage, leads pre-award due diligence processes, and ensures that all financial matters related to sub-awardees' finances are properly documented to assure audit readiness at all times. The position acts as the senior focal point for financial and compliance aspects of the Partnerships Department for sub-awardees, including ensuring high-quality financial monitoring of sub-awardees, and provides technical guidance and escalation support to the Finance Partnership Manager.
 The Finance Partnership Coordinator also plays a key role in strengthening the financial capacity of partners by identifying capacity gaps, risks, opportunities for improvement, and areas requiring targeted support. The position leads the development and implementation of tailored financial improvement plans, working closely with partners to address identified challenges, mitigate financial and compliance risks, and prevent potential adverse impacts to IRC. Through proactive engagement, the position identifies practical solutions, promotes continuous improvement, and supports partners in strengthening their financial management systems, controls, and overall accountability. The Coordinator monitors progress against agreed improvement plans, escalates significant risks when appropriate, and ensures that capacity-building interventions contribute to stronger, more accountable, and resilient partnerships while safeguarding IRC's financial and operational interests.
 This position reports directly to the Deputy Director of Finance and directly supervises the Finance Partnership Manager.
 Specific Responsibilities: 
 Promote Effective Partnerships 
 Promote and oversee the application of the IRC's Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results system (PEERS), building a strong understanding of PEERS throughout the Ukraine Country Program, and ensuring that IRC's partnership principles, skills and approaches are applied by staff, including the Finance Partnership Manager, across programs and projects with partners.
 Oversee systematic partner feedback on IRC's management of the partnership relationship, including the documentation of, and response to, partner feedback.
 Program Delivery 
 Lead the Partner's Capacity Assessment (PCA) of potential partners as appropriate, and lead efforts to collaboratively analyze and manage material risks identified, as it relates to finance.
 Oversee and quality-assure the work of the Finance Partnership Manager in developing and finalizing budgets and budget amendments with partners, and, in the case of milestone-based partnership agreements, in determining the costing of milestones.
 Review and approve draft partnership agreement terms relating to advances, reporting and any special conditions relating to finance.
 For cost-reimbursable partnership agreements, agree with partners the specific documentation required to support each type of cost, adjusting standard requirements to the operating context and the partner.
 Participate in Partnership Project Opening, Review and Closure Meetings, including to review successes, challenges, and lessons learned with the partner, and capture effective finance practices for future partnerships.
 Oversee the timely provision of funding to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement to ensure program continuity, ensuring clear communication with the partner and efficient resolution where for whatever reason this is not possible.
 Provide oversight to ensure completeness, correctness, and accuracy of financial reports and cash requests submitted by partners.
 Review, and ensure the Finance Partnership Manager reviews, partner financial reports (and narrative reports for consistency) and supporting documents to ensure compliance with the partnership agreement, donor regulations and IRC policy, and provide feedback to the partner as appropriate.
 Oversee the monitoring of partner budgets and actual spending in collaboration with technical coordinators and the Finance Partnership Manager, identifying issues and working proactively and collaboratively with partners to resolve them.
 Lead timely and effective finance review and reflection (monitoring), identifying appropriate follow-up actions, and providing completed reports to the Deputy Director of Finance.
 Oversee the close-out of partnership agreements, including in relation to financial verification and asset confirmation.
 Lead the review of the performance of the partner, of the IRC, and of the partnership, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
 Program Support & Capacity Sharing 
 Lead the provision of finance and accounting training and mentoring support to partners, in accordance with partner project support plans, with a focus on supporting the partner to strengthen financial management systems and capacities that are responsive to the needs of the partner (rather than replicating IRC's systems and policies).
 Team Management 
 Directly supervise the Finance Partnership Manager, including day-to-day management, coaching, mentoring, and performance management, with the aim of strengthening technical capacity and providing professional development guidance.
 Other 
 Any other duties as assigned by the Deputy Director of Finance.
 Key Working Relationships: 
 Position Reports to: Deputy Director of Finance
 Position directly supervises: Finance Partnership Manager.
 Other Internal and/or external contacts: Programs Team, Finance team, Grants team, other Partnership focal points and external stakeholders and partners.

 The Protection Expert Capacity Strengthening & Systems Engagemen t (Women Protection and Empowerment) provides national-level technical expertise to strengthen GBV prevention and response systems and IRC’s engagement with national and local partners in Ukraine. The position works closely with relevant institutions and organizations to assess existing capacities, identify systemic and institutional gaps, and develop practical approaches to strengthen the quality, accessibility, and sustainability of GBV prevention and response.
 The role manages the technical engagement with a portfolio of WPE partners, leads capacity and needs assessments, develops tailored capacity strengthening and institutional development plans, and initiates relevant programme interventions to address identified priorities. The position contributes to strengthening linkages between humanitarian programming, local organizations, and national systems and supports the application of survivor-centred approaches, GBV standards, and sustainable models of service delivery.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 Maintain and regularly update mapping of women-led organizations (WLOs), women’s rights organizations (WROs), and other relevant Ukrainian organizations working on GBV prevention, response, and women’s protection and empowerment to identify opportunities for engagement, partnership, and collaboration.
 Work closely with the Partnerships Department to support partner identification and engagement, capacity assessment and development processes, partnership planning, and monitoring of organizational and technical capacity strengthening results.

If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 The Crisis Response, Recovery, and Development (CRRD) Department  
 The CRRD Department houses all the IRC’s Country Programs that implement our work, within a four-pillar department structure:
 Program Delivery, comprised of 5 Regions with more than 30 Country Programs. These are our implementing and management teams delivering our programs.
 Technical Excellence, comprised of 5 Technical Units supporting sector-specific and cross-cutting program quality, as well as program design and strategic leadership.
 Awards Management, leading our processes and implementation around business development, grants management, compliance, and donor engagement and awards management strategies.
 Emergencies, leading stand-alone emergency responses in crisis-affected areas, as well as supporting existing teams with surge support and resources if emergencies break out in their contexts.
 All four pillars of CRRD collaborate closely with Country Program staff on the frontlines of program delivery to provide high-quality programming with impactful results for the people we serve.
 JOB OVERVIEW 
 The Administrative and Department Manager for CRRD will be responsible for providing high quality, core administrative support to the Senior Vice President (SVP) of CRRD and for leading on the overall administrative work of the department. For the SVP they will be responsible for coordinating calendars, meetings and events; coordinating travel arrangements; coordinating media and external engagements; and tracking expenses. For the department, they will provide wider coordination of meetings and events; document management; internal communications support; AV and logistical support; org charts; email lists; and for supporting events or changes in the HQ office space. Working directly with the SVP and alongside the department’s senior leadership, they will be a trusted member of the central administrative team – sitting in on senior meetings and entrusted with sensitive information. The role demands tremendous discretion, and in return it offers an unusually close view of how a global, fast-moving humanitarian organization runs and how decisions get made at the most senior level. This role requires very strong organization, communication, and interpersonal skills.
 Growth, Access, and Opportunity 
 This role sits at the center of a global department and comes with unusual access: direct exposure to the SVP and senior leaders, a front-row seat in high-level meetings, and a network that reaches across the IRC’s work. There are multiple career paths this role can lead to, and the team will actively help you find and navigate the ones that fit your strengths and interests (specific next roles are earned not guaranteed). If you are someone who spots a problem, gets excited about solving it, and wants to grow, this is a place to do exactly that. A successful candidate will bring a can-do attitude and a collaborative team spirit, ready to support the diverse needs of a small and efficient executive team.
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Executive Leadership Support 
 Manage SVP calendar and communicate with meeting participants regarding internal and external meetings
 Support SVP speaking event and other travel coordination (logistics, travel documentation, partnering with others on speaking content, registrations, visas, etc.)
 Support media requests including last-minute schedule requests
 Organize, schedule, and support HQ meetings including room reservations, light AV support, and catering if applicable
 Prepare documents and other types of meeting materials, present slides and disseminate meeting materials
 Maintain and update shared calendars and trackers to document SMT and Executive Board travel and leave
 Submit credit card reconciliations and reimbursements on behalf of the SVP, as appropriate
 Support teams in obtaining signatures and approvals from the SVP
 Information / Document Management and Internal Communications   
 Work with Strategy & Performance team to maintain files and disseminate resources from pillar, departmental, and inter-departmental meetings
 Support pillar document formatting and meeting preparation
 Organize Box (online storage) folders and support collaboration and archival organization across CRRD
 Update organizational charts monthly, alongside departmental teams’ org charts as needed
 Oversee regular Distribution List updates and ensure accuracy of mailing lists  
 Update the Emergency Contact List Card in coordination with Safety & Security colleagues
 Support onboarding for new CRRD hires that include scheduling time with pillar leaders 
 Systems, Process Improvement, and Ownership Opportunities 
 Take ownership of discrete strategic planning and coordination tasks in partnership with the SVP’s office and the wider team, with scope that can grow to match your strengths and interests
 Identify and lead administrative process improvements that streamline how the department works
 Support the roll-out of new software, tools, and protocols – potentially from testing through to adoption
 Special Events and Special Projects 
 Support with annual Core Humanitarian Standards audits (uploading policies and documents, tracking relevant materials and emails)
 Arrange workshops and conferences with assistance from others (venue procurement, travel logistics arrangements and tracking, information dissemination with participants, hotel liaising and management)
 Plan and facilitate special occasions (e.g. birthdays, baby showers, retirements, welcome or farewell parties, etc.)
 Other duties as requested
 Position Reports to:  Senior Director, Strategy & Performance, CRRD
 JOB REQUIREMENTS 
 Bachelor’s degree, Associate’s degree, or equivalent, with 2–3 years of professional experience in an administrative role
 Excellent organizational skills, including the ability to juggle competing priorities and manage time for yourself and others
 Service-oriented and flexible, commitment to help and support in a fast-paced, fast-changing environment
 Sound judgment and discretion in handling confidential and sensitive information
 A proactive, ownership mindset: you anticipate needs, spot problems before they escalate, and are energized by the chance to make things work better
 Poise and confidence working directly with senior leaders and external stakeholders
 Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people, within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment
 Strong computer acumen including proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point and Outlook
 Ability to work independently, resourcefully, and to own initiative, with flexibility to changing priorities and an eagerness to learn
 French, Arabic, Spanish or other relevant language skills an advantage
 Optimism and good humor warmly welcomed
 Compensation: (Pay Rate: $68,000-$74,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget.  Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

offres.titre: Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Job Overview 
 The Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery is a senior global role responsible for making IRC's supply chains fit for scale across its most ambitious health and humanitarian programming commitments. The role is designed to translate strategic program targets into operational supply chain solutions that work at country level and ensuring country realities shape global supply chain strategy in return.
 The role has three integrated areas of responsibility. 
  It serves as a primary GSC lead and contributor to business development: identifying, designing, and positioning supply chain funding opportunities with institutional and non-traditional donors, and leading supply chain sections of competitive proposals. 
 It provides support across IRC's Impact at Scale (I@S) thematic supply chains, driving end-to-end performance from demand planning and forecasting through sourcing, pre-positioning, and last-mile delivery.
 It builds country and regional capacity to sustain health supply chain improvements over time, providing direct technical support, deploying to high-priority contexts, and harmonizing tools and SOPs across country programs in collaboration with Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs) and other relevant Global Supply Chain (GSC) units and IRC stakeholder departments.
 Reporting to the Director of Emergency and Health Supply Chain, the Deputy Director works in close collaboration with the Health Technical Unit, Global Procurement, Regional Supply Chain Directors, Country Programs, IT, Finance, and external partners including UNICEF, WHO, ECHO, and peer INGOs. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Leadership for Program Delivery 
 The Deputy Director plays an active role in GSC’s business development (BD) function. Supply chain is an increasingly fundable programming area, with institutional donors such as ECHO, SIDA, Gates and non-traditional donors explicitly framing requirements around operational efficiency, commodity management, and supply chain innovation.  Additionally, private and corporate donors have expressed specific interest in funding the optimization of health and emergency supply chains.
 Act as the primary GSC focal point within I@S agile working groups and cross-functional scaling teams, ensuring supply chain planning is embedded in program design from the outset and not treated as a downstream implementation task.
 Implement the strategic direction for cross-cutting supply chain enablers including pooled procurement, global pre-positioning frameworks, harmonized delivery models, and digital systems and oversee their development and rollout across priority country programs.
 Provide supply chain leadership and oversight for the addition of any new I@S Ready to Scale thematic areas, ensuring new commodities and delivery models are integrated into IRC's global supply chain architecture without creating fragmentation or duplication.
 Serve as GSC's coordinating focal point with the Research and Innovation Department, contributing to supply chain innovations including AI-enabled solutions.
 2. Business Development & Resource Mobilization 
 Is responsible for operationalizing the BD strategy, assembling inputs to create compelling bids, gap filling in the BD process as needed/relevant, and driving ultimate bid success through correct donor intel and positioning, strong bid submission, and effective cross-functional collaboration.
 Flag, track and route relevant funding opportunities to GSC Leadership and work closely with internal stakeholders to plan for staff needs and business development capacity requirements to successfully write and budget for winning bids based on the pipeline 
 Lead or co-lead the technical design of supply chain sections for proposals where GSC has a primary role, including narrative writing, logical framework development, and supply chain costing.
 Collaborating with program and business development leads to embedding supply chain considerations into program design, with specific attention paid to Impact at Scale initiatives
 Contribute to bid assessment, probability-of-winning analysis, and positioning strategy for supply chain funding opportunities with specific focus on I@S thematic areas 
 Develop and maintain GSC supply chain capability statements and value propositions relevant to I@S programming areas, for use in capture and proposal development.
 Participate in the BD review cycle for proposals with significant supply chain components, ensuring technical quality and alignment with IRC’s global supply chain strategy.
 Mobilize opportunities with non-traditional partners such as Airlink to improve program delivery and increase cost savings
 Take the lead with External relations and other fundraising teams to enable increased use of GIK goods and services, enabling program delivery whilst making IRC more cost effective.
 Build and maintain donor intelligence on supply chain funding streams
 Support pre-award activities including donor engagement, capture visits, and key personnel recruitment where relevant to I@S supply chain opportunities.
 Coordinate with Regional Supply Chain Directors and country programs to ensure country-level supply chain needs and evidence are reflected in proposals.
 Contribute to after-action reviews following award decisions to capture lessons and improve future supply chain BD submissions.
 Identify and evaluate opportunities for business development & partnerships with academic or research centers, with Research & Innovation colleagues as appropriate.
 3. Implementation of Strategic Initiatives Supporting Impact @ Scale 
 Strengthening global forecasting and demand planning systems for key health commodities.
 Collaborate with Global Procurement to define sourcing strategies, monitor supplier performance, and ensure security of supply.
 Lead global visibility efforts by consolidating country-level data on demand, pipeline status, consumption, and stock risks. Collaborate with GSC Systems and Data to digitalize as many aspects of this as possible in a timely manner.
 Work with country teams to improve quantification, storage, distribution planning, and last-mile delivery.
 Translate I@S targets into actionable supply chain plans with milestones, KPIs, and risk controls.
 Design and support the rollout of cross-country improvements (e.g., pooled procurement feasibility, centralized pre-positioning, LMIS integration, preferred vendor strategies, emergency surge mechanisms, harmonized delivery models).
 Support the implementation of the supply chain I@S bodies of work.
 Escalate and advise GSC Leadership on global priorities, risks, and mitigation strategies impacting success of I@S activity plans.
 4. Capacity Building, Country Support & Operational Strengthening 
 Provide specialized technical support to country supply chain and health teams.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 BACKGROUND 
 The Ministry of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared the country’s 17th Ebola outbreak on 15 May 2026, following the laboratory confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Ituri Province, Eastern DRC. Concurrently, Uganda also confirmed imported cases linked to the outbreak in DRC. On 17 May 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Unlike the Zaire strain involved in previous outbreaks in eastern DRC, the current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus, for which there is currently no licensed vaccine or specific treatment.
 The outbreak is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security context marked by chronic insecurity, armed group activity, repeated population displacement, and high levels of cross-border movement between DRC and neighboring countries, particularly Uganda and South Sudan. The provinces of Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu continue to face severe humanitarian needs, with large populations of internally displaced persons (IDPs), weakened health systems, and limited access to healthcare in several affected areas. Mining activities, informal trade routes, and population mobility further increase the risk of transmission.
 As of August 2026, the outbreak has expanded rapidly across multiple health zones in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. According to WHO and DRC authorities, more than 4,500 cases have been reported, and over 2,100 deaths confirmed. Several healthcare workers have also died following exposure during patient care, highlighting major IPC challenges. Contact tracing and surveillance efforts remain constrained by insecurity, population movements, and community resistance in some locations.
 The IRC has a dedicated Ebola response team in place, with a focus on maintaining safe continuity of essential health services and strengthening preparedness and infection prevention and control capacities in health facilities. IRC interventions include reinforcing IPC measures, establishing screening and isolation capacities, improving water supply and healthcare waste management systems, supporting safe referral pathways, ensuring continued access to lifesaving health services for women and children, and strengthening community engagement and risk communication activities. The IRC is also supporting frontline healthcare workers through training, supervision, and provision of essential supplies in affected and high-risk areas across eastern DRC.

The team's core responsibility is to rapidly and effectively design, develop, and manage the IRC's on-site humanitarian response to meet the immediate needs of the affected population, while also transferring responsibilities and knowledge to long-term staff to ensure continuity of IRC programming and operations.
 All ERT staff must be prepared to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification and should expect to spend up to 65% of their time in the field, in either an emergency or roving capacity.
 The ERT Protection Coordinator (Child Protection) will be responsible for starting up and leading integrated protection and/or child protection programming in acute emergency responses. This may include rapid assessment, program start-up, strategy development, proposal development, technical oversight, staff recruitment and management, budget management, grants compliance and local partner relations. When not deployed, the ERT Protection Coordinator will contribute to IRC's strategic objectives and technical workstreams for CP and violence prevention and response in emergencies. A successful candidate will demonstrate a track record of working independently in fast-paced environments and applying creative, flexible design to protection programming in acute emergency contexts.

 Context Evaluation 
 Following the onset of an emergency, identify areas with greatest impact, highest needs, and emerging safety protection risks for diverse populations (integrated protection, CP, WPE / GBV, PROL), including specific protection risks for young children, adolescents, and families, and care arrangements
 Conduct stakeholder analysis: continually review existing actor mapping with a view to identifying key actors and establishing partnerships with focused on the delivery of protection services
 Design and conduct multisector needs assessments
 Program design and management 
 Provide strategic direction, leadership and overall technical management of IRC’s protection response aligned to the response strategy and emergency safety outcomes, while ensuring high program quality and alignment with IRC’s standards and approaches
 Lead and directly contribute to the start-up, implementation and coordination of emergency protection programming, including (depending on the context): emergency case management; support to Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC), including Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) and alternative care; cash for protection; rapid group MHPSS interventions; emergency safety and wellbeing sessions; two-way, responsive information services; community-based protection and risk mitigation; group cash transfers for community-led protection actions; and safe, inclusive programming and protection mainstreaming.
 In collaboration with partners, develop a VPRIE strategy to respond to identified protection risks and needs, outlining a problem statement, response modalities, activity sequencing, and required resources
 In collaboration with response leadership and technical coordinators, input into the design of an overall emergency response strategy, including partnerships so that the IRC is working in ways that are complementary to and in support of partners and child protection actors
 Participate in cross-departmental collaboration and coordination with other sector colleagues to ensure that linkages between programs are made and programs gain from protection best practice
 Ensure – through program design and practice, team capacity and behavior – that clients, including young children, adolescents, and caregivers, participate in the design and implementation of IRC programs, and that their access to services and programs is meaningful and safe
 Develop and/or adapt technical tools and approaches, and deliver creative solutions to mitigate challenges in the operating context, to facilitate response start-up and day to day implementation 
 Support emergency protection staff to implement and monitor work plans ensuring that activities reflect the commitments IRC made to the donor and the community
 Oversee IRC’s relationship with partners, ensuring co-design, regular exchange, and project performance monitoring to achieve program objectives
 Design and implement appropriate monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems ensuring consistent reporting and analysis of results to improve program effectiveness and quality
 Provide a comprehensive handover to successor, including ensuring transfer of all related documentation, program data and staff performance information
 Grant and financial management 
 Manage emergency grant/program implementation including recruitment and training, work plan development, procurement and inventory planning, budget management, and M&E plans
 Develop high quality technical propos

offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 This position will be based in Kyiv, with occasional travel to other locations in Ukraine as necessary. This position is open for Ukrainian citizens. 
 JOB SUMMARY: 
 The Senior National Advocacy and Government Liaison Manager leads IRC Ukraine's national government-liaison work, and informs IRC Ukraine’s advocacy strategy, with a strong focus on political and policy analysis, stakeholder mapping, and institutional relationship-building. Working closely with, and under the strategic direction of, the IRC Ukraine Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator, this role owns the analytic and on-the-ground liaison work that underpins IRC Ukraine's national advocacy positioning. This person will identify, establish, and maintain effective communication channels with relevant Ukrainian national institutions, including ministries, agencies, and departments, as well as with other relevant stakeholders who may be allies in advocacy and liaising work, in areas relevant to IRC programming. They will conduct policy research, analysis, and stakeholder mapping to inform IRC's advocacy efforts. The person will also provide support and guidance to program teams and partners in terms of coherent engagement with the public institutions across all levels of governance.
 This position will be based in Kyiv, with occasional travel to other locations in Ukraine as necessary. 
 MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Reporting to the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator, the Senior National Advocacy and Government Liaison Manager will:
 Analysis and research 
 Track, monitor, and analyze national legislative and policy developments relevant to humanitarian and early recovery assistance in Ukraine, producing regular internal – and when relevant external - analysis notes and briefings.
 Conduct stakeholder and political economy analysis – mapping key government, donor, and civil society actors and their positions, interests, and influence – to inform IRC Ukraine's advocacy strategy and positioning.
 Provide research, analysis, and recommendations, drawing on primary and secondary data collection, to inform the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator, as well as program teams, in developing position papers, briefs, and campaign materials.
 Stay up to date on political developments in-country that may affect IRC's humanitarian and early recovery programming, and flag implications to the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator.
 Gather program and field evidence relevant to advocacy efforts and government engagement and bring it into IRC’s dialogue with institutions and advise on their inclusion into the advocacy work.
 Recommend how IRC Ukraine’s analysis, research, and studies are used for stakeholder engagement and advocacy, and develop and maintain an accessible repository of these products.
 Government and institutional liaison 
 Own IRC Ukraine’s relationships with relevant Ukrainian national and regional authorities, including ministries, agencies, and departments relevant to IRC programming: identify, establish, and maintain them, and keep the engagement plan current..
 Assess political, reputational, and operational risks of government engagement, apply IRC’s principles in all interactions with authorities, and escalate sensitive issues to the Coordinator.
 Coordinate and facilitate communication between IRC Ukraine and relevant authorities, ensuring timely and accurate dissemination of information as needed.
 Advise on and draft official communications to government authorities and bodies as required.
 Prepare and manage documentation for International Technical Assistance (ITA) project registration and re-registration in line with Cabinet of Ministers procedures, including official letters, Memorandums of Understanding, and associated annexes; coordinate internally on procurement plans, MoU review, and translation, and externally with donors and government authorities to secure approvals; monitor the progress of submitted applications.
 Lead IRC Ukraine’s engagement on the critical status of humanitarian organizations policy: follow policy developments, assess implications for IRC in consultation with the Ukraine NGO advocacy working group, legal advisors, and other stakeholders, and prepare the application for critical status.
 Deputize for the Coordinator on government-facing matters in their absence.
 Advocacy support and representation 
 Support the development and implementation of IRC Ukraine's policy and advocacy strategy, under the direction of the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator and in coordination with program colleagues and partner organizations.
 Support IRC representation in the Ukraine NGO advocacy working group, contributing IRC's analysis and positions to jointly agreed advocacy priorities and initiatives.
 Cultivate relationships with international and national civil society actors, and partner organizations to support coordinated advocacy efforts and information-sharing.
 Collaborate with partner organizations to help develop and disseminate positions that support IRC's Strategy Action Plan, the policy and advocacy strategy, and the interests of the communities IRC serves.
 Provide country-context input to the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator's engagement with regional and global communications colleagues, helping ensure public-facing messaging reflects the on-the-ground environment.
 Contribute to capacity-building for IRC Ukraine staff and partners, and provides guidance, on government engagement and liaison practice.
 Support the development of LinkedIn posts and other outreach content aimed at public institutions, in coordination with the Content and Social Media Officer and the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator.
 Supervisory Responsibilities:  None.
 Key Working Relationships 
 Internal: Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coordinator (close, regular coordination); Senior Management Team and program staff; regional and global communications, advocacy, and policy colleagues.
 External: NGO Forum, the Advocacy Working Group; government officials at national and regional levels; public and private donor agencies; international and national NGOs; UN agencies.
 JOB REQUIREMENTS 
 Education: Minimum: Bachelor’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Foreign Policy, Development Studies, Law, Public Relations or another related field. Master’s degree strongly preferred.
 Demonstrated Skills and COMPETENCIES: 
 Minimum 5 years of professional experience in advocacy, policy, or government-liaison work.
 Proven analytical and strategic thinking skills, with experience supporting advocacy and government-relations initiatives in a challenging environment.
 Strong research and analytical skills, including experience conducting stakeholder analysis, political economy analysis, or similar mapping exercises.
 Knowledge of research methods, including primary and secondary data collection, processing, and analysis.
 In-depth knowledge of Ukrainian government institutions and bodies at national and regional/oblast levels, and of relevant law and policy-making processes.
 Good understanding of Ukrainian government and author

 Leadership and Partnership 
 Manage all technical aspects of MEAL data and information management across Thailand programs; respond to program needs; foster high standards and practices for quality data, analysis, and reports; enable accountability to clients, partners, and donors through robust client feedback and response systems.
 Improve M&E/MEAL systems and approaches and foster learning

 A Minimum of 5 years of working experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning and information management systems functions, preferably in humanitarian or development contexts.
 Technical skills in setting up MEAL processes, logical frameworks, data analysis, and information management systems including database design and data visualization.
 Strong understanding of accountability and proven ability to build and manage client feedback systems.
 Proficiency with mobile data collection (CommCare, Kobo, ODK Collect), Microsoft Excel, and Power BI. Knowledge of Tableau, GIS, or statistical software (SPSS, Stata) are assets.
 Demonstrated ability to train and build capacity of staff and partners.
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills; able to prioritize and multi-task.

 Fluency in English (written and spoken) required; proficiency in Karen and/or Burmese strongly preferred.

 Background 
 Every donation processed, every campaign that lands, every supporter who stays engaged — that's the technology you'll help build and deliver.
 As IT Program Manager MarTech , you'll manage the digital platforms behind one of the world's leading humanitarian organizations, directly enabling the fundraising that funds life-saving programs for displaced communities across the globe. This is a high-impact, fast-paced role at the intersection of technology delivery, stakeholder engagement, and mission-driven purpose.
 You'll be a core member of our Project Management team, working across a modern MarTech ecosystem — including donation and e-commerce platforms (Fundraise Up, Springboard) , our website (Drupal) , Salesforce CRM , Databricks , email marketing (Pardot) , and SMS platforms (Mobile Commons, Mogli) . You'll own the delivery of enhancements, integrations, and new capability launches that keep the IRC's digital supporter experience best-in-class.
 Why Join Us? 
 Real-world impact — your work directly supports humanitarian programs serving millions of people in crisis.
 Breadth and ownership — lead a complex, multi-platform portfolio with genuine strategic influence from day one.
 Collaborative culture — work alongside Product Managers, Data Engineers, Business Analysts, and business stakeholders in a distributed, multicultural team that's deeply committed to its mission.
 Modern delivery — Agile/Scrum at the core, with room to shape how the team works.
 Remote-first flexibility — work from anywhere in the US as part of a truly global organization.
 What You'll Do 
 Drive end-to-end program delivery Own the full lifecycle of multiple concurrent MarTech initiatives — from scope definition and roadmap planning through to launch and post-delivery review. Develop and maintain detailed project plans, work breakdown structures, and product backlogs, ensuring delivery against time, budget, and quality targets.
 Lead program governance Establish and run the governance structure for programs assigned to you- reporting cadence, escalation paths, decision forums, and stage-gate reviews- in line with the IRC’s project management methodology. Report up to leadership on program performance, maintain program roadmap and support the portfolio PMO lead on yearly planning.
 Champion Agile ways of working Serve as Scrum Master for your project and product teams — coaching on Agile principles, facilitating sprint planning, standups, retrospectives, and reviews, and proactively removing blockers to keep delivery on track. Tailor the delivery approach (Agile or Hybrid) to each initiative and use PM tooling to maintain an integrated view of delivery across workstreams.
 Keep stakeholders informed and aligned Prepare clear, timely status reports covering scope, milestones, risks, and budget. Communicate confidently with audiences from engineers to senior executives, tailoring your message appropriately. Manage expectations and build trust across business and technology teams.
 Manage budgets and vendors Oversee budget tracking and vendor invoicing for your portfolio. Support cost estimation, validate expenditure, and contribute to the annual budget planning process to ensure initiatives are delivered within financial targets.
 Lead business analysis activities Work with the team to define and track functional and technical requirements, document current and future state processes, and coordinate testing activities. Partner closely with Business Analysts to ensure delivery is grounded in well-understood business needs.
 Manage risk, scope changes and quality Maintain consolidated view of risks, issues and mitigation plans across initiatives and assess ripple effects across initiatives. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 BACKGROUND: 
 Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours.
 Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.
 Active in public health, education in emergencies, cash and basic needs and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, ask ‘Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.
 CONTEXT: 
 The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared the country's 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026, following laboratory confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Ituri Province. On May 17, 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), and it has since become the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in DRC and the fastest-expanding on record. The outbreak is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security context marked by chronic insecurity, armed group activity, repeated population displacement, and high levels of cross-border movement, particularly with Uganda and South Sudan. 
 The IRC is supporting containment of the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. IRC's primary focus is to support existing primary health care (PHC) facilities to ensure safe continuity of services, strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC) practices and infrastructure, raise community awareness of behaviors that limit further spread, and reinforce the protective environment, including through MHPSS support. 
 JOB OVERVIEW: 
 The position of Program Lead, Ebola Response (PL) is a member of the Ebola Response Senior Management Team and is integral to the successful implementation of IRC's programs in the affected provinces. Working under the direction of the Ebola Response Director, the PL will be responsible for overall leadership in the design, implementation, and management of the Ebola Response’s programs to address clients’ needs and priorities. She/he will be responsible for providing strategic direction of programs, conceptualizing and promoting innovations, and continuing to deepen the impact of IRC’s programs on the ground. 
 The PL assists the Ebola Response Director in the integrated planning and implementation of activities crucial to the success of local programs. This includes internal and external coordination and stakeholder engagement, including with donors, government and non-government partners, and IRC technical and regional support teams; overseeing multi-sector project design and implementation; managing sector teams to propose, coordinate, and deliver quality programs aligned with strategic priorities and beneficiary needs; and managing strategic funding opportunity tracking, partnering and pre-positioning decisions. 
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:  
 Program Strategy, Design and Fundraising 
 Lead the operationalization of IRC's current Ebola Response strategy and actively engage in strategic planning processes to shape the response's longer-term direction.
 Perform regular analysis of the outbreak and ensure IRC's strategy and operational presence is responsive to those needs and highly mobile program models.
 Work closely with Coordinators and HQ-based Emergency Unit and Technical Unit staff to ensure that project design reflects IRC's program quality standards and adheres to industry best practices.
 Lead efforts to achieve sustainable program growth, proactively identifying opportunities for new programming initiatives and placing particular emphasis on securing multi-year funding to sustain them.
 Provide leadership and strategic support to program and grants teams as they develop competitive, evidence-based, and cost-effective funding applications.
 Provide guidance, strategies, and tools to ensure that program choices are grounded in the findings of needs assessments (drawing on both primary and secondary data), rigorous analysis, meaningful input from affected communities, a thorough understanding of context, technical best practices, and operational viability.
 Formulate integrated program initiatives that allow technical sectors to complement one another, while promoting the mainstreaming of protection principles and gender-responsive approaches throughout programming.
 Program Management — Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation 
 Provide overall leadership of IRC's Ebola Response program portfolio, ensuring strategic coherence, well-managed growth, and full compliance with IRC and donor regulations.
 Build the capacity of program team members, both individually and as a team.
 Work with Program Coordinators and the Operations team to develop and adapt detailed, realistic, and feasible implementation plans.
 Collaborate with the Senior Management Team to uphold management, compliance, and performance standards, and to maintain effective systems for budget, knowledge, and risk management.
 Support program staff in capturing, documenting, and disseminating lessons learned and best practices, feeding them into future project design.
 Work with program staff to develop robust monitoring and evaluation (M&E) plans, including methodologies and tools that strengthen data collection, analysis, and reporting quality.
 Review M&E and accountability data with program staff to identify and address gaps in operational performance.
 Champion IRC's "partner first" approach, building strategic, respectful, and empowering relationships with local organizations, and ensuring partners are actively engaged in decision-making, program design, and service delivery, positioning IRC as a partner of choice.
 Ensure partnership management is high-quality, accountable, and collaborative, including oversight of partner-led delivery, adaptive technical support, and consistent application of IRC's partnership framework and principles.
 Grants Management 
 Provide strategic leadership in developing and executing a comprehensive funding strategy: expanding and strengthening the donor base, driving excellence in grants management and compliance, strengthening program and grants information systems, and contributing to high-quality proposals and reporting.
 Oversee internal and external reporting in coordination with the Ebola Response Director across programs and finance, ensuring reports are well-written, timely, and meet donor, IRC, and partner requirements; conduct thorough review of all external reports compiled by

 Calidad Técnica y Desarrollo de Programas
 Apoyar la implementación de las actividades de Protección de la Niñez (CP) y Protección y Empoderamiento de la Mujer (WPE) en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia, garantizando el cumplimiento de los estándares institucionales y humanitarios.
 Brindar seguimiento técnico y programático a las actividades implementadas por el equipo y los socios locales, asegurando la calidad, pertinencia y oportunidad de las intervenciones.

 Realizar visitas periódicas de monitoreo a terreno para verificar la calidad de los servicios prestados y brindar acompañamiento técnico al personal y socios implementadores.
 Apoyar el fortalecimiento de capacidades de los socios y equipos de protección mediante acompañamiento técnico, orientación y seguimiento continuo.
 Garantizar la adecuada recopilación, revisión y reporte de información programática, contribuyendo a la elaboración de informes internos y externos.
 Participar activamente en reuniones de coordinación internas y externas, grupos de trabajo, clústeres y otros espacios de coordinación humanitaria relevantes.

 Velar por la integración de los principios de protección, enfoque de género, edad, diversidad, inclusión y rendición de cuentas hacia las poblaciones afectadas en todas las actividades del programa.
 Garantizar que las actividades se implementen de acuerdo con las políticas de salvaguarda, protección infantil, prevención de la explotación y el abuso sexual (PSEA) y los principios humanitarios.
 Elaborar hojas de tiempo (Time Sheest) y entregarlas en los plazos establecidos.
 Apoyar cualquier otra actividad relacionada con la implementación, monitoreo, coordinación y desarrollo de los programas de protección que sea requerida por la gerencia.
 Coordinación & Representación
 Coordinar con socios, proveedores de servicios y actores humanitarios para garantizar una respuesta de protección efectiva.
 Participar en reuniones de coordinación, grupos de trabajo y espacios humanitarios relevantes.
 Dar seguimiento a los mecanismos de referencia y articulación entre servicios de Protección de la Niñez y Protección y Empoderamiento de la Mujer.
 Mantener relaciones de trabajo efectivas con autoridades, organizaciones socias y líderes comunitarios.
 Informar oportunamente sobre avances, riesgos y desafíos programáticos a la gerencia y equipos técnicos.

 Monitoreo y Evaluación 
 Dar seguimiento a los indicadores, metas y resultados del programa, reportando oportunamente avances, desafíos y desviaciones.
 Garantizar la recopilación, revisión y carga oportuna de la información programática en las plataformas y herramientas de monitoreo establecidas.
