 Scope of Work:  
 The Extended Case Management (ECM) team provides case management services to up to 400 new clients each year at the IRC in Silver Spring. The team works directly with new refugees, asylees and other humanitarian immigrants resettling in the DC Metro area; utilizing a holistic 2Gen household approach for the families served, the team addresses both short-term and long-term barriers to support overall well-being in the US. This intern will report to one of the ECM caseworkers. 
 Responsibilities:   
 Conduct check-in calls and send messages to clients to determine the status of any unresolved service provision and provide guidance or assistance with the support of supervisor.  
 Submit and follow up with a variety of external referrals, including for English classes, health screenings, and housing assistance programs.  
 Assist clients with scheduling and teaching them how to navigate various organizations, such as public benefit offices or medical offices.  
 Assist clients with completing and following up on applications for public benefits, Medicaid, childcare vouchers, social security cards, and more.  
 Research and build community resources to fill any gaps in services.  
 Provide clients with public transportation orientations in the field if needed.  
 Regularly track service provision through electronic data entry and organize required client documentation.  
 Other duties as assigned by the ECM team. 
 Learning Objectives:   
 Intern will gain US resettlement agency experience.  
 Intern will acquire knowledge of internal programs and public benefits available to humanitarian immigrant families.  
 Intern will learn how to communicate with variety stakeholders population, including how to effectively utilize interpreters.  
 Intern will gain skills in building resources and coaching limited English proficiency clients.  
 Intern will learn tracking and reporting requirements for resettlement agencies and how capturing this data improves services. 
 Qualifications  
 Current undergraduate, graduate student or less than 12 months out of school. *  
 Minimum 24 hours per week, three-month commitment and three full working days per week; full-time 32-37.5 hours per week highly preferred.  
 Proficient digital literacy skills (e.g., MS Excel, Outlook, and Word) and the ability to learn new software and tasks.  
 Organized and attentive to detail.  
 Ability to work independently and multi-task.  
 Strong verbal and written communication skills.  
 Interest in working in a global environment  
 Knowledge of or interest in learning about public benefits and other community resources.  
 Ability to build out community resources is a plus.  
 Driver’s license and access to a reliable, insured vehicle is a plus.  
 Fluency in Dari, Pashto, Haitian Creole, Spanish, or Ukrainian is a plus.

 The Walk-In Services team is the first point of contact for the nearly 2,000 new walk-in clients who visit the IRC in Silver Spring each year.  BACKGROUND

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. 
 The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

 IRC Background: 
 The IRC in Northern California was established in 1975 in response to the needs of the growing refugee population. Over the past 40 years the IRC has resettled nearly 60,000 clients in Northern California. Originally focused on reception and placement, the IRC provides a range of services including economic empowerment, immigration, community gardening, and case management for victims of trafficking. IRC’s Economic Empowerment programming focuses on connecting individuals to employment opportunities in an effort to lead them down the path of self-sufficiency. This is accomplished through a combination of employment services, financial education and coaching, and access to public benefits and income support.
 Job Overview:
 The Youth Outreach Specialist leads community-based outreach, recruitment, and eligibility intake for the IRC's Out-of-School Youth (OSY) program in Alameda and Contra Costa counties. This position identifies and engages youth ages 16–24 who are not currently enrolled in school and who meet one or more OSY barrier criteria, such as being a school dropout, basic skills deficient, an offender, in foster care or aging out of foster care, homeless or a runaway, pregnant or parenting, an individual with a disability, or otherwise in need of additional assistance to complete an educational program or secure employment. Working closely with local schools, juvenile justice and foster care agencies, community-based organizations, and employers, the Youth Outreach Specialist builds a steady pipeline of eligible referrals as well as determines and documents WIOA eligibility.
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Conduct sustained, community-based outreach and recruitment to identify eligible out-of-school youth, including canvassing neighborhoods, alternative schools, GED/HSE programs, shelters, foster care and juvenile justice systems, and other settings where OSY are likely to be found in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.
 Build and maintain referral relationships with school districts and alternative education providers, the foster care and juvenile justice systems, homeless service providers and community-based organizations.
 Determine OSY eligibility, collect and verify required documentation (proof of age, residency, income, and barrier-to-employment documentation), and complete eligibility files in accordance with state and local workforce board policy.
 Enter and maintain accurate, timely participant data in the required state case management system and IRC program databases, including eligibility, required services and referral partner.
 Develop and distribute outreach and recruitment materials in accessible, culturally and linguistically appropriate formats for the local youth population.
 Conduct phone outreach, and in-person meetings with youth and families to explain program services, eligibility requirements, and the enrollment process.
 Track outreach activity, referral sources, and enrollment numbers against program recruitment targets and performance goals, and report progress to the Program Supervisor.
 Represent the IRC at community events, resource fairs, school functions, and partner meetings to promote the OSY program and maintain IRC's visibility as a youth service provider.
 Support compliance with state and workforce board regulations, child labor laws, and local workforce development board policies and monitoring requirements.
 Participate in Program team, funder and partner meetings as well as required WIOA/grant trainings.
 Other duties as assigned to support program outreach, eligibility, and enrollment goals.
 Key Working Relationships: 
 Position Reports to: Workforce Development Supervisor
 Internal Contacts: Economic Empowerment team, IRC Oakland team
 External Contacts: Local Workforce Development Board staff, school districts and alternative education programs, foster care and juvenile justice agencies, homeless service providers, and community-based organizations
 Job Requirements: 
 Bachelor's degree in social work, education, human services, or a related field preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience; experience with federally and state funded youth programs preferred.
 At least 1–2 years of experience in outreach, recruitment, case management, or youth-serving work; direct experience with WIOA, other workforce development programs, or out-of-school/disconnected youth strongly preferred.
 Knowledge of Out-of-School Youth eligibility criteria or ability to learn program regulations and local workforce board policy quickly.
 Demonstrated ability to build trust and rapport with youth facing barriers and with their families and caregivers as well as external partners.
 Strong attention to detail for eligibility documentation, case file compliance, and data entry into state and program case management systems.
 Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills; comfortable with public speaking and representing the IRC at community events.
 Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with a state workforce case management system (e.g. CalJOBS) a plus.
 Fluency in English required; proficiency in one or more languages spoken by the local client population strongly preferred (e.g. Spanish, Dari).
 Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel locally to conduct outreach, recruitment, and home visits.
 Ability to work some evenings and weekends to accommodate youth and family schedules as well as external events.

 Job Overview  :The IRC’s Refugee School Impact Program (RSIG) and Refugee Youth Mentoring Program (RYMP) support the integration and holistic wellbeing of school-aged students who hold a humanitarian immigration status. The programs work to reinforce a sense of belonging and security within schools and surrounding communities, build students’ confidence in their English and academic abilities, and help students develop graduation and career plans tailored to their unique interests and skills. Throughout the year, students take part in after-school programming, college and career discovery workshops, field trips, and our Summer Academy each designed to address the expressed needs of our clients. 
 An additional component of the internship is youth case management, which includes enrolling new clients in the youth program and completing individual service plans for each client. Interns work closely with Youth Team staff and clients to provide direct case management support and follow-up. 
 RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Build supportive, culturally responsive relationships with refugee and immigrant youth in the after-school program. Deliver engaging, differentiated small-group and one-on-one sessions that reflect the IRC’s Social Emotional Asset Development (SEAD) framework. Design and adapt culturally relevant instructional materials and activity guides for multilingual learners. Contribute to a shared team library of resources and instructional tools accessible to all program staff. Help administer and record attendance, pre- and post-assessments, and participant progress data. Co-facilitate or participate in volunteer and staff orientation and training, modeling effective facilitation and instructional techniques. Support continuous quality improvement by identifying programmatic gaps and opportunities and raising them to the Youth Supervisor and Coordinator. Maintain a safe, inclusive, and welcoming learning environment. 
 Tutor Track: 
 Academic & English Language Development  
 Provide academic tutoring and homework support across content areas. Deliver English Language Development (ELD) instruction and language practice aligned to Maryland WIDA standards. Design, adapt, and differentiate ELD lesson plans and supplementary materials for multilingual and English Language Learner (ELL) youth. Administer IRC’s pre- and post-ELD assessments and contribute to reviewing results to inform instruction.
   Mentor Track: 
 College & Career Readiness  
 Mentor youth in college exploration, post-secondary planning, and career awareness, connecting learning to real-world pathways. Design and adapt college- and career-readiness curriculum, units, and workshops (e.g., goal-setting and study skills, college options and the application process, financial aid and FAFSA awareness, resume building, interview practice, and workplace readiness). Support youth in identifying their interests, strengths, and goals, and in building the habits and confidence to pursue them. Integrate English language support as needed, while keeping college and career growth the primary focus. Help track mentee goals and progress and contribute to program data and reporting.

 Currently enrolled in, or holding, a bachelor’s or master’s degree. offres.titre: Strategy and Planning Senior Officer, Global Policy & Advocacy
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Background : The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. We deliver lasting impact by providing health care, helping children learn, and empowering individuals and communities to become self-reliant, always with a focus on the unique needs of women and girls. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, we now work in over 40 crisis-affected countries as well as communities throughout the U.S., Europe and Latin America.
 The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.
 Job Overview/Summary:  
 The Strategy and Planning Senior Officer will lead on key strategic planning and prioritization efforts for the Policy & Advocacy team. The Senior Officer will coordinate portions of organization-wide strategy and investment planning, collaborate with the Vice President of Policy & Advocacy on team prioritization processes, and manage a collaborative but streamlined process for strategy development. This person will maintain crucial processes and relationships and collaborate at all levels within and across the teams, and across the IRC.
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Facilitate priority-setting processes:  Translate organization-wide strategy and policy products into department strategies, market-specific advocacy priorities, and thematic policy areas of focus.
 Lead strategy development processes:  Work closely with Policy and Advocacy team members to support the development of specific, actionable policy and advocacy strategies, helping individual units develop strategies relevant to their priority issues and their geographic/political markets that include stakeholder mapping, activity planning, product development plans, and desired external change metrics as relevant. Lead Policy and Advocacy engagement in organization-wide annual planning processes, linking Policy and Advocacy planning to multi-year organizational strategies and Department-wide objectives.
 Develop and facilitate activities and processes across Policy and Advocacy teams:  Facilitate and maintain efficient ways of working within, across, and with the Policy and Advocacy teams as appropriate. Identify and elevate collaboration challenges and develop ways of working systems to address those issues.  Ensure ways of working are routinely updated to address feedback from team members and represent team in org-wide, multi-departmental process conversations. 
 Manage long-term projects : Own project management, strategic content development, and logistics for key team efforts such as the Annual Planning and Quarterly Pause processes, retreat planning, and others. 
 Facilitate cross-team collaboration and communication:  Create tools and processes for effectively sharing information and collaborating internally, communicating with IRC stakeholders routinely, and managing workflows in a streamlined and smooth manner. Facilitate regular, effective, and efficient communication between team members and from organizational leadership to the rest of the teams, cascading information from ER leadership, finance, and HR as necessary. Manage the internal website and routine reporting to senior leaders. Develop deep understanding of Policy and Advocacy priorities and strategies in order to communicate effectively about team objectives and outcomes with internal stakeholders through reporting processes, internal websites, email and other means as appropriate.
 Lead KPI development and progress tracking:  Working with the VP and members of the Policy and Advocacy team develop a set of high-level objectives for teams alongside a more detailed set of KPIs to enable reporting out to the organization on progress. Plan and facilitate quarterly internal progress reviews of individual strategies (and associated metrics) across Policy and Advocacy. Ensure KPIs and reporting metrics are logical, consistent, and regularly reported on by team members on a weekly basis.
 Teamwork:  Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Organize team retreats, staff meetings, team building activities and trainings. 
 Key Working Relationships:  
 Position Reports to:   Vice President of Policy & Advocacy with a Management in Partnership to the Director of Strategy & Planning
 Position directly supervises:   N/A

 Internal:  Global Policy and Advocacy team; Strategy & Planning Team; Business Operations; Marketing and Mobilization; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department; President’s Office; Finance; Information Technology; Human Resources
 External:  NGOs, think tanks, U.S. government agencies, Congress, multilateral institutions and other organizations as needed
 Job Requirements:  
 Education:  Bachelor’s degree in International Relations, Political Science or other related field
 Work Experience:  
 5-6 years work experience, experience in policy and advocacy preferred

 Excellent organizational and time management skills, including juggling competing priorities and tight deadlines and prioritizing tasks appropriately
 Experience designing and implementing strategic planning processes and progress metrics

 Familiarity with or experience in policy analysis or advocacy to high-level policymakers and thought leaders
 Strong project management skills, ideally within a cross-organizational team to deliver on projects/strategies 
 Solid English language writing and editing skills with a focus on details

 Job Overview: 
 IRC in Sacramento’s Financial Empowerment Center (FEC) department is expanding its service model to include housing stabilization services for low- to moderate-income households in the Sacramento region. Through the Stockton Boulevard Housing Stabilization Program, IRC in Sacramento will provide direct financial assistance, including rental arrears, utility support, and emergency funds, paired with financial coaching to help households avoid eviction, prepare for homeownership, and maintain long-term housing stability.
 The Senior Housing Stabilization Specialist will serve as the primary point of contact for housing stabilization services, responsible for conducting intake and eligibility determinations, navigating clients through housing resources and assistance programs, administering direct financial assistance, and coordinating closely with FEC financial coaches and external community partners. This is a senior specialist role that requires independent judgment, strong case management skills, and demonstrated experience in eviction prevention and housing stabilization programming.
 The Housing Stabilization Specialist reports directly to the Financial Empowerment Center Program Manager.
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Duties shall include, but are not limited to:
 Intake, Eligibility & Case Management 
 Conduct comprehensive housing-focused intake and eligibility assessments for applicants seeking rental, utility, deposit, and emergency financial assistance.
 Verify income eligibility, geographic residency (zip codes 95817, 95820, 95824, 95828 and citywide), and program-specific documentation requirements.
 Gather and review supporting documentation from clients, including proof of income, lease agreements, utility bills, eviction notices, and landlord contact information.
 Develop individualized housing stability plans in coordination with FEC financial coaches to address both immediate crises and longer-term financial barriers.
 Conduct follow-up with clients on an ongoing basis to ensure timely processing of assistance, monitor progress toward housing stability goals, and identify emerging needs.
 Enroll eligible households into HMIS (Homeless Management Information System) and accurately record all services to avoid duplication across programs.
 Direct Financial Assistance Administration 
 Administer direct financial assistance across three categories: rent/mortgage/utility arrears, emergency financial assistance for unexpected expenses, and one-time rent/deposit and moving assistance.
 Coordinate payment processing with landlords, utility providers, and vendors in compliance with program guidelines and funder requirements.
 Ensure all assistance is documented accurately and in accordance with City of Sacramento and IRC compliance standards.
 Track services and maintain up-to-date records in IRC’s case management systems.
 Housing Navigation & Stabilization 
 Navigate clients through Sacramento’s rental market and affordable housing landscape, including public housing programs, subsidized housing waitlists, and community resources.
 Coordinate with landlords, property managers, and legal aid partners to facilitate eviction prevention and housing retention.
 Connect clients to complementary services including FEC financial coaching, employment programs, and public benefits to promote long-term self-sufficiency.
 Partnerships, Outreach & Reporting 
 Collaborate with FEC financial coaches and the Program Manager to deliver integrated housing and financial empowerment services to enrolled households.
 Build and maintain relationships with community-based partners, including U-N-I Housing Foundation, CLTRE, Legal Services of Northern California, and other housing service providers.
 Participate in outreach activities and community events to recruit eligible households and raise awareness of available housing stabilization resources.
 Represent IRC Sacramento in coalitions, partner meetings, and community convenings related to housing stabilization and eviction prevention.
 Participate in ongoing professional development trainings, including HUD Housing Counselor Certification within 6 months of hire if not already certified.
 Perform other duties as assigned
 Position Reports to:  Financial Empowerment Center Program Manager
 Position directly supervises : Interns and volunteers 
 Indirect Reporting:  Site Director
 Other Internal and/or external contacts:  
 Internal:  IRC program staff, interns and volunteers 
 External:   Community partners and economic empowerment programs. 
 Job Requirements:  
 A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and/or three or more years of directly relevant experience in housing stabilization, eviction prevention, case management, or social services;
 Demonstrated experience conducting intakes and eligibility assessments for low- to moderate-income households;
 Experience administering direct financial or rental assistance programs, including documentation review and vendor/landlord coordination preferred;
 Familiarity with Sacramento County’s rental market, affordable housing resources, and eviction prevention programs;
 HUD Housing Counselor Certification preferred; candidates not yet certified must obtain certification within 6 months of hire;
 Essential Skills: 
 Strong case management and organizational skills, including the ability to manage a high-volume caseload with accuracy and attention to detail;
 Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and prioritize competing demands in a fast-paced environment;
 Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including experience navigating difficult conversations with clients in crisis and coordinating with landlords and legal partners;
 Bilingual preferred — English plus Spanish, Dari, Pashto, Arabic, or other languages spoken by immigrant and refugee populations in Sacramento;
 Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook; ability to learn and use client management databases (Salesforce; HMIS);
 Commitment to culturally responsive, trauma-informed service delivery;
 Available to work occasional evenings or weekends as program needs require.
 Working Environment:  
 This role has a hybrid work environment with a mix of virtual and in-office days. The current hybrid schedule may change. The schedule includes:
 Virtual Work:  Some days will be fully remote, allowing you to work from home.
 In-Office Work:  Certain days will require you to be present in our main office.
 Variable Office Locations:  Occasionally, you may need to work from a partner's office space.
 This position is expected to end on November 15, 2027.

 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. The IRC has been operating in Thailand since 1975 and currently provides assistance to displaced persons in Tak, Kanchanaburi, Ratchaburi, and Mae Hong Son provinces
 Established in 1975 to assist refugees from Vietnam, Loas and Cambodia, the IRC Thailand is one of the longest-running country programs. Operating from Mae Sot with a small representational office in Bangkok, the IRC is currently supporting the transition of residents of the Thai-Myanmar refugee camps to a life of self-reliance within Thailand. IRC also provides emergency assistance to people fleeing violence and unrest in Myanmar and supports the Royal Thai Government and local civil society to strengthen climate resilience in Thailand’s southern states.
 The IRC Protection and Empowerment Program work to protect and promote the rights of crisis-affected and displaced populations along the Thailand – Myanmar border by ensuring people are safe in their homes and communities, receiving timely and appropriate support after experiencing harm, and are empowered to make free and informed decisions about their lives and futures. The program supports displaced populations to build self-reliance and future planning capacity, including through employability and life-skill development. It adopts a multi-sectoral approach, coordinating legal, medical, and psychosocial services to provide comprehensive and integrated protection assistance. Gender equality, diversity, and inclusion are mainstreamed across all activities, and the program is committed to strengthening the use of data for evidence-based decision-making and advocacy to improve protection system and outcomes for displaced population in Thailand.
 Job Overview/Summary: 
 The Senior Protection Project Officer provides administrative and operational support to the implementation of Protection and Empowerment programming. The position is responsible for coordinating day-to-day project operations, liaising with internal and external stakeholders, supporting procurement and logistics processes, maintaining project documentation, and ensuring activities are implemented in accordance with IRC policies, donor requirements, and project workplans. The role serves as a key focal point between program and operations teams to facilitate timely and effective project delivery while supporting strong coordination, accountability, and compliance across program activities.
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Program Implementation 
 Support the Protection and Empowerment Program in planning, coordination and implementation of program activities, working closely with local stakeholders, community groups and program teams to ensure timely and quality delivery.
 Maintained organized and up-to-date project filing and documentation system, ensuring all supporting documents are accurately archived and readily available for internal and donor compliance requirements.
 Provide day-to-day administrative and operational support to the Protection and Empowerment Program, including preparing purchase requests, tracking approvals, and facilitating the procurement of program supplies and materials.
 Develop and regularly update the project procurement plan, track the lead time and deliverables of equipment and materials, manage financial advances, and travel arrangements for staff and program participants.
 Serve as the primary liaison between the Protection and Empowerment team and Operations departments to ensure am on all administrative matters related to the program.
 Organize and provide logistical and administrative support for trainings, workshops, meetings, community events, and other program activities, including venue arrangements, participant coordination, material preparation, and activity documentation.
 Monitor and track program and office supply expenditures, ensuring spending remains aligned with approved budgets and complies with IRC policies and donor regulations.
 Identify operational bottlenecks and proactively coordinate with relevant teams to address implementation challenges and maintain project timelines.
 Coordination and Representation 
 Coordinate and maintain effective working relationships with local authorities, community leaders, local organizations, civil society actors, and other relevant stakeholders to support program implementation and community engagement.
 Represent the Protection and Empowerment Program in coordination meetings, working groups, and stakeholder engagements as delegated by the supervisor.
 Key Working Relationships:

 Other Internal and/or external contacts:

 External : Local partner organization, local government authorities, community leaders and the CCSDPT’s member organizations.
 Job Requirements: 
 A diploma or university degree in logistics, business administration, accounting, or a relevant field.
 Minimum of five years in a development organization, administration, or related field.
 Proficient in documentation management and coordination with various stakeholders.
 Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
 Ability to prioritize tasks, work under pressure, and meet competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
 Responsive to urgent requests and willing to travel frequently to field locations.
 Problem-solving skills and an understanding of working in a multicultural environment.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and online communication platforms such as Zoom or Microsoft Teams.
 Excellent oral and written communication skills in Thai, good command of English, and/or proficiency in Karen/Burmese is beneficial.
 Working Environment : This position is based in the IRC office in Mae Sot, with extensive travel other work areas in Tak, Mae Hong Son, Ratchaburi and Kanchanaburi as required.

 The Partnership Procurement Officer carries out operational procurement reviews, monitoring and day-to-day supply chain support for assigned partners. The Officer checks documents and records, prepares findings and recommendations, delivers agreed support activities and follows up on outstanding actions. The role works independently within agreed procedures and priorities set by the Partnership Procurement Manager, referring significant findings, exceptions and complex matters to the Manager for review and direction.
 Reporting to the Partnership Procurement Manager within IRC Ukraine's centralized Procurement function, the Officer works closely with partner teams and IRC Partnership, Programs, Finance and Supply Chain colleagues. Partner procurement support and monitoring remain the role's primary responsibilities. The Officer may also support direct IRC procurement, subject to available capacity and assignments coordinated through the Partnership Procurement Manager.
 RESPONSIBILITIES

 Partner assessments and procurement controls

 Help partners prepare and update consolidated procurement plans, checking specifications, sourcing methods, sequencing and lead times against planned activities and delivery needs.
 Identify upcoming complex or high-risk procurements and flag the need for advance technical support and IRC review before key procurement decisions or commitments.
 Tender support and supplier due diligence

 Carry out assigned supplier due diligence, checking qualifications, capacity, licences and registration against supporting documents and available sources. Document identified risks and proposed mitigation measures for review.
 Follow up with partners on supplier performance and contract implementation issues, including delivery delays and quality or service concerns, and refer complex or unresolved matters to the Partnership Procurement Manager.

 Maintain monitoring and corrective-action trackers, follow up with partners on agreed deadlines and collect and check evidence of completion. Update progress records independently and submit supporting evidence to the Partnership Procurement Manager for confirmation before recording corrective actions as completed.

 Background 
Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. 
 The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable. 
 External Relations 
 The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions: Private fundraising, Mobilization & Marketing, Policy & Advocacy and Operations & Analytics. To enable IRC to deliver our Strategy100 commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance our ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally. 
 The Purpose of the Role

 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) began operations in Burundi in 1996, amid civil war and widespread instability. From the outset, the organization engaged in life-saving emergency interventions, providing immediate assistance to refugees and internally displaced persons. The sociopolitical and security crisis led to significant population movements.
 Today, Burundi hosts more than 130,000 refugees, primarily from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). At the same time, more than 250,000 Burundians have been forced to flee their country and currently live in exile, mainly in Tanzania, Rwanda, and the DRC. Within Burundi itself, an estimated 100,000 people have also been displaced, largely due to the effects of climate change, such as flooding.
 To address these challenges, the IRC has progressively expanded and adapted its programs to meet the growing needs of affected populations. The organization implements integrated interventions focused on emergency humanitarian response, while strengthening community resilience through protection, health, and economic wellbeing and education initiatives. The Burundi country program currently implements 9 projects with an annual operating budget of approximately USD 10 million.
 To support the management and growth of its multi-donor grants portfolio, IRC Burundi is seeking a Grants & Partnership Coordinator to ensure efficient and timely grants management, from proposal development through donor compliance and reporting.
 Job Overview:   
 The Grants & Partnership Coordinator is responsible for resource mobilization, proposal development, and coordinating the management of IRC Burundi's grants portfolio. S/he oversees all functions of the Grants & Partnerships unit. S/he works in close collaboration with the Programs department: the MEAL Coordinator, Technical Coordinators, Project Coordinators and Managers, the Senior Operations Coordinator, and the Deputy Director - Finance, and reports to the Deputy Director - Programs.
 Major responsibilities 
 Business and Proposal Development (30%) 
 In collaboration with the DDP and headquarters colleagues, proactively identify new funding opportunities by tracking and analyzing donor strategies and funding trends.
 Support effective internal communication and information management processes to ensure relevant stakeholders across the organization can access and use Business Development information, including maintaining an up-to-date opportunity matrix.
 Lead the tracking and analysis of the country program's opportunity pipeline.
 Work with the DDP, national technical coordinators, and regional colleagues to identify international partners and negotiate the IRC's role in proposal consortiums, ensuring a competitive positioning for IRC Burundi that adheres to partnership principles and the organization's strategic direction.
 Support country team staff in developing and maintaining key relationships with donors, partner organizations, and private sector actors, with a view to identifying opportunities, creating shared value, and forming strategic alliances.
 Support the DDP and technical leads in the development of new program designs.
 Prepare and facilitate Go/No Go meetings related to funding opportunities, as needed.
 Ensure that Go/No Go discussions and program design are consistent with the partnership ambition of the Country Strategic Action Plan (SAP) and IRC Burundi's programmatic approach, as well as IRC's Business Development guidance (Business Development Manual).
 Promote and coordinate partner engagement in program development efforts.
 Ensure strong and effective representation and budgeting of IRC's partnership strategy, approach, and management in proposals and reports submitted to donors.
 Oversee the development of all concept notes and proposals, either taking on or delegating the role of lead writer or editor. Develop effective process management tools for proposal development.
 Clearly define and communicate the roles, responsibilities, and timelines of each department. Facilitate effective inter-departmental coordination.
 Thoroughly review all proposal documents to ensure consistency between narratives, logical frameworks, and budgets.
 Serve as the focal point with headquarters during the review, editing, and submission of proposals.
 Ensure that all proposal deliverables are accurate, complete, high-quality, and submitted on time.
 Grants and Information Management (15%) 
 Coordinate the management of IRC Burundi's grants portfolio.
 Serve as the focal point for communications with headquarters on all grants and partnership administration functions.
 Review donor agreements and coordinate their review and signature with the relevant headquarters offices. Coordinate pre-award expenditure approvals, as applicable.
 Lead and/or support all project revisions, amendments, and budget realignments.
 Coordinate the monitoring and facilitation of Budget vs. Actuals (BvA) reviews to bring teams together and ensure sound financial management.
 Actively promote partners' full participation in program implementation through Project Cycle Meetings (PCM).
 Oversee the preparation, review, and monitoring of sub-grant agreements with partners, in coordination with the Finance and Supply Chain departments.
 Ensure proper grant closeout, including the production of final reports, budget reconciliation, and asset disposition, in line with donor and IRC rules.
 Maintain and circulate a regularly updated grants tracking table.
 Ensure that all departmental communication with IRC colleagues and donors is constructive, clear, and well organized.
 Maintain a well-organized and comprehensive information management and filing system for grants and sub-grants.
 Ensure that the IRC's internal Opportunity Tracking Information System (OTIS) is kept up to date and maintained throughout the grant lifecycle.
 Liaise with the Finance department to monitor spending by donor and promptly flag any risk of budget under- or over-expenditure.
 Build the capacity of IRC and partner staff in grants management by facilitating trainings and providing targeted support as needed.
 Partnership Management (15%) 
 Actively contribute to the relevant sections of the Partner Capacity Analysis (PCA) and to the development of resulting partner support plans.
 Coordinate the implementation of IRC Burundi's partnership strategy and partnership ambitions, in line with the PEERS (Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System) manual and the Strategic Action Plan.
 Support the Partnerships Manager in facilitating IRC Burundi's Partnership Working Group.
 Promote a partnership approach aligned with PEERS principles.
 Participate in due diligence processes and collaborative partnership risk management, as needed.
 Actively promote partners' full participation in program implementation through Project Cycle Meetings (PCM).
 Donor Compliance (15%) 
 Provide Programs and Operations teams with day-to-day technical guidance to ensure all grants are implemented in accordance with IRC and donor regulations.
 Coordinate with headquarters on specialized compliance issues, as needed.

 CONTEXTO 
 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas. 
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos. 
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Zulia, Falcón, Táchira, Apure, Distrito Capital y La Guaira trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales.

 Following the escalation of the war in Ukraine in 2022, The Health Cluster progressively adapted its coordination architecture from a nationwide approach to a more focused model covering 10 conflict-affected oblasts by 2026. To enhance operational relevance and proximity to affected populations, sub-national coordination capacities were strengthened across eastern, northern, and southern Ukraine, enabling closer engagement with frontline health actors, local health authorities, and affected communities. This approach is aligned with the broader humanitarian coordination structure led by OCHA through its operational hubs in Kharkiv, Dnipro, and Mykolaiv, including Area-Based Coordination (ABC) and Humanitarian Operations Coordination Group (HOCG) mechanisms. The decentralized coordination model supports a more predictable, accountable, and needs-based health response by ensuring that partner interventions are guided by operational realities, aligned with the Health Cluster strategy, and responsive to barriers affecting access to healthcare, particularly for vulnerable and displaced populations. Given the continued pressure on the health system and persistent humanitarian needs, sustained Cluster coordination remains critical to guiding the implementation, monitoring, and adaptation of health responses while ensuring that beneficiary feedback informs programming and decision-making.
 The engagement of a sub-national co-coordinator through IRC is aimed at improving ownership of the operational response by partners and local authorities and have a meaningful involvement in co-leading an effective humanitarian response which is adapted to the local context and implemented in strong collaboration with local communities and other stakeholders.
 This position will be based in Kharkiv, with occasional travel across Ukraine, as necessary. 
 This position is open to Ukrainian nationals only. 
 The monthly gross salary ranges from UAH 120,000 to UAH 130,000, before taxes. 
 JOB SUMMARY: 
 The Subnational Health Cluster Co-Coordinator will support the Health Cluster Coordinator in performing dedicated coordination, needs assessments, strategy adaptation, resource mobilization, and supporting the implementation and monitoring of the joint incident management system and advocacy function in the Health Cluster.
 MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Build and maintain meaningful and consistent relationships with all relevant stakeholders, including partners and health authorities. Provide interpretation and translation support as needed.
 Maintain regular contact with officials from the oblasts’ Department of Health (DOH), national and international NGOs, UN agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.
 Ensure that information management activities are implemented to enhance the effectiveness of the response across different domains.
 Guarantee effective reporting from and to the national cluster to maximize coordination and accountability.  Collate information and make inputsto inform information products and reports.
 Chair and facilitate the Kharkiv subnational cluster coordination meetings, holding them twice per month.
 Establish and manage regular meetings between the Kharkiv subnational cluster and the oblast departments of health as well as other health authorities (CDM, NHSU), conducting them monthly.
 Act as the representative of the health cluster in Kharkiv and provide updates during Kharkiv OCHA general coordination meetings, held once per month.
 Engage in with other clusters focused on Kharkiv oblast, contributing to the collective identification of critical issues that demand multi-sectoral responses. Submit reports on an ad hoc basis.
 Ensure the timely sharing of meeting minutes/updates with the Health Cluster Coordinator (in organized team meetings) and save them in the designated shared folder following each meeting.
 Regularly update the relevant sections of the bi-weekly update report (internal update, achievements, next steps) on a weekly basis, twice per month.
 Supervise the incorporation of cross-cutting issues into the health cluster's response and implementation plans, with consideration for local adaptation. This should be accomplished through regular partner briefings and follow-ups, conducted on a monthly basis.
 To initiate or take part in field monitoring visits to supervise partner projects as well as provide feedback for improvement to align with the Health Cluster strategy.
 To contribute to the Ukraine Country-Based Pool Fund process by informing on locations to be prioritized in the Kharkivska oblast as well as reviewing projects for Kharkivska for relevance based on identified needs.

 Job Overview:  The Senior Core Services Caseworker delivers trauma-informed support to refugee clients during their resettlement and post-resettlement periods, as well as to other eligible immigrant populations, including Cuban, Haitian, and Ukrainian clients. The Caseworker is responsible for promoting a positive resettlement experience and helping clients achieve self-sufficiency. This role involves close collaboration with clients, internal teams, and external partners to create individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients with a range of financial, medical, social, and vocational resources in alignment with program guidelines and client eligibility criteria.
 Major Responsibilities: 
The Senior Core Services Caseworker plays a critical role in ensuring that clients successfully transition to life in their new community and achieve self-sufficiency. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
 Client Intake, Assessment & Planning 
 Conduct comprehensive intake services to assess individual and family needs, including housing, health, education, employment, and social services.
 Develop tailored self-sufficiency plans in collaboration with clients, outlining specific goals, timelines, and action steps to achieve self-reliance.
 Identify immediate needs and prioritize services such as securing housing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing medical services.
 Pre- and Post-Arrival Coordination 
 Ensure clients receive essential services upon arrival, including temporary or permanent housing, access to nutritious food, healthcare, and transportation support.
 Coordinate with internal departments and external service providers to facilitate timely delivery of services and resources.
 Provide ongoing orientation to clients on accessing services in their new community, including healthcare systems, public benefits, financial literacy, and transportation.
 Direct Support, Advocacy & Case Management 
 Offer individualized support to clients, ensuring they receive appropriate referrals to community resources such as schools, legal services, and mental health providers.
 Advocate on behalf of clients to help them overcome barriers in accessing services and exercising their rights.
 Monitor and assess client progress regularly, addressing challenges and updating self-sufficiency plans as needed to ensure successful outcomes.
 Facilitate connection to employment services in coordination with the employment team to support clients in gaining job readiness skills and securing suitable employment.
 Assist clients in completing critical documents, including benefit renewals, address change notifications (AR-11 forms), and other legal documentation.
 Home Visits & Community Integration 
 Conduct home visits to assess living conditions, provide follow-up services, and ensure clients are safe and stable.
 Help clients build community connections by facilitating their engagement with local services, cultural events, and educational workshops.
 Financial Assistance & Budgeting 
 Plan, request, and track direct assistance funds, ensuring expenditures are aligned with program requirements and client needs.
 Assist clients with financial planning, helping them budget for rent, utilities, and other essential expenses.
 Manage Matching Grant Program client finances, ensuring compliance with program guidelines and accurate reporting of funds disbursed.
 Documentation & Reporting 
 Maintain detailed case files and documentation for each client interaction, ensuring accuracy and compliance with program standards.
 Enter data into client databases and assist with program tracking and reporting requirements.
 Prepare reports as required by internal leadership and external funders.
 Collaboration & Relationship Building 
 Collaborate with internal teams such as Employment, Health, and Youth Services to ensure seamless service delivery.
 Build and maintain relationships with external service providers, such as healthcare organizations, schools, and community groups, to expand the support network for clients.
 Participate in cross-departmental meetings and community coalitions to strengthen partnerships and identify additional resources for clients.
 Client Education & Workshops 
 Develop and facilitate educational workshops for clients on topics such as navigating healthcare, job readiness, budgeting, tenant rights, and U.S. culture.
 Encourage and support client participation in group activities that promote learning, self-advocacy, and social integration.
 Supervision & Volunteer Engagement 
 Train, supervise, and coordinate the activities of interns and volunteers, ensuring they understand program goals and the needs of clients.
 Provide ongoing feedback and support to volunteers to maximize their contribution to client success.
 Compliance, Ethical Standards & Safety 
 Ensure compliance with all organizational policies, program guidelines, and ethical standards in the delivery of services.
 Maintain confidentiality and uphold the highest professional standards in all client interactions.
 Participate in ongoing training and professional development to stay current on best practices and program regulations.
 Transportation & Logistics 
 Use a personal, insured vehicle or public transportation to transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
 Assist clients in learning how to use public transportation to access essential services independently.
 Other Responsibilities 
 Support special projects and initiatives that enhance client services and improve program outcomes.
 Perform other duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of clients and the organization.

 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El Oficial de Monitoreo, Evaluación, rendición de cuentas y Aprendizaje (MEAL), coordinará una amplia  gama de actividades de recolección de datos a nivel de campo (por ejm. encuestas, grupos focales, etc.), dirigidas a evaluar la experiencia de los beneficiarios y el progreso/ desempeño de las intervenciones de cada programa. El objetivo principal de este puesto es diseñar herramientas, recopilar y analizar la información para garantizar la calidad, comprender el impacto y mejorar la entrega de los programas, de acuerdo con las herramientas y procesos de seguimiento establecidos.  The DDP leads, oversees, and ensures the compliance of IRC’s program portfolio, while ensuring alignment with organizational and donor guidelines. The DDP ensures internal and external coordination to develop high-quality proposals and deliver effective, timely programs. The DDP collaborates with all departments and partners, reports to the Country Director (CD), and is a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT). We are looking for a dynamic leader with strong cross-departmental collaboration skills, able to drive strategic success and support an inclusive, motivated team, in particular by empowering women to exercise leadership.
 In coordination with the Country Director, the DDP establishes and maintains strong relationships with donors, as well as with DRC government entities and authorities.
 The DDP directly supervises the senior program coordinators/managers responsible for proposal development, program quality, and implementation.
 The incumbent is expected to spend at least 40% of their time supporting programs and teams in the provinces and in the field.
 MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES 
 1. Program Implementation 
 Oversee and ensure that programs are implemented to high quality standards and within the required timelines, including by supporting Program Coordinators and Technical Coordinators in the use of structured and realistic project management tools (including work plans, procurement plans, and spending plans), in coordination with the Operations teams.
 Closely monitor budgets, expenditures, and program progress to ensure that grants are implemented within budget and closed on time, ensuring consistent Project Cycle Management (PCM) routines and taking prompt, structured corrective action when needed.
 Ensure clear accountability, well-defined roles and responsibilities, and highly effective communication and coordination channels between teams within the Programs Department.
 Provide the CD with accurate, up-to-date advice on developments and opportunities in programming and project implementation, accompanied by recommendations for action.

 In coordination with the CD and other colleagues, update the country program and sector strategies annually, as part of the SAP process, so that they remain relevant and operationally effective in the face of changing contexts.
 Lead the development and rollout of strategic initiatives such as research and innovation, and ensure that cross-cutting issues (gender, climate change, and disaster risk reduction) are integrated into sector programming.
 3. Grants, Partnerships, and Business Development 
 Foster a partnership-driven, equality-based culture and working environment that reflects partnership principles and values and celebrates partnership successes (including risk sharing with partners and holding leadership accountable for a safeguarding culture in safe partnership).

 Provide overall direction and leadership to the IRC DRC Grants and Program Development teams by ensuring that a robust business development strategy, processes, and systems are in place, and that adequate funding is secured to deliver the intended results for clients.
 Oversee sound program design and proposal strategy for each new funding opportunity, including needs- and evidence-based program design, strong technical and operational engagement in design processes, and rigorous, competitive budgeting.

 Increase the impact of IRC programming by maintaining and strengthening the trust of donors, partners, and key collaborators, while proactively positioning IRC for new program development opportunities.
 4. Human Resources and Staff Development

Participate in recruitment and manage individual and collective performance, including development plans, performance standards, and evaluations, in line with organizational standards.

 Foster collaboration, accountability, and staff well-being through quality management practices, performance monitoring systems, and leadership suited to the dynamics of remote work.
 5. Liaison/Representation and Coordination 
 Maintain a solid understanding of IRC programs in order to represent the organization and its interests externally in a professional manner, including with donors and government authorities, to ensure the sustainability of programs across the portfolio.
 Encourage and support greater program cohesion through coordination initiatives and information sharing among key country program staff.
 Actively contribute to advocacy initiatives, platforms, and external coordination forums, providing data from IRC programs to strengthen the protection of beneficiaries’ rights
 Participate actively in the Senior Management Team and serve as acting CD when necessary.

 BACKGROUND 
 Over the past 90 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in some 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient.
 The IRC global network has its headquarters in New York and London. IRC Europe is part of this network with offices in the UK, Germany, Sweden, Belgium and Switzerland. In addition, the IRC has a partnership with Stichting Vluchteling in the Netherlands.
 The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.
 Read more about the IRC here: https://www.rescue.or.kr 
 EXTERNAL RELATIONS AND THE PRIVATE FUNDRAISING FUNCTION 
 The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions, including Private fundraising, in which this role falls under. To enable IRC to deliver its organizational commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance its ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.
 Within Private Fundraising sits the Mass Markets unit. This unit is currently made up of seven teams – US, UK, Germany, Sweden, Korea, Digital & Remote Markets and our Supporter Journey and Acquisition teams. Mass Market’s primary goal is to increase the number of sustainers we have globally, via targeted and cost effective acquisition and by building meaningful connections with our donors to ensure we can retain them. By increasing our sustainer numbers and capitalizing on cash giving moments we aim to grow unrestricted revenue for IRC and the people we serve.

The Finance & Compliance Manager leads consolidated project financial oversight and fiduciary assurance, ensuring that budgets, expenditure, financial reporting and compliance requirements are managed coherently across IRC and all participating organizations. The position coordinates and quality-assures project-level financial and compliance information, while participating organizations retain responsibility for their own internal controls and underlying records. 
 In addition to project-level oversight, the position carries direct partnership finance management responsibility for the sub-implementing partners engaged under this project, acting as the finance focal point across the full partnership finance cycle — from budget development and capacity assessment through to financial reporting, monitoring, capacity building and financial close-out — in coordination with IRC Finance, Grants and Partnerships functions. 
 The position will be based in the Mykolaiv / Kherson Field Office, Ukraine, with regular travel to project locations within Khersonska Oblast and to Kyiv as required for project coordination, partner monitoring and donor engagement.  Maintain a clear calendar of financial deliverables and escalate material gaps or delays promptly. 
 Compliance, assurance and audit readiness:

 Maintain proportionate project-level financial and compliance monitoring and assurance tools, drawing on participating organizations' systems and evidence wherever feasible. 
 Monitor material compliance findings, questioned costs, documentation gaps or control weaknesses and coordinate corrective-action tracking with the responsible functional owners. 
 Coordinate project financial and compliance readiness for UHF/OCHA monitoring, spot checks, audits and other assurance exercises. 
 Support complete, traceable and retrievable project-level financial documentation while participating organizations retain responsibility for their underlying records and audit trails. 
 Ukrainian statutory, fiscal and tax compliance: 
 Maintain current working knowledge of Ukrainian tax and fiscal legislation relevant to donor-funded humanitarian programmes, and ensure project financial arrangements reflect applicable statutory requirements.

 Job Overview:  The Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other US Office for Refugee Resettlement (ORR) eligible populations. The Caseworker, is expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 
 Determine client eligibility for case management programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client. 
 Develop individualized plans for each client enrolled in the SCM, OIRS, and Youth Health Programming.
 Assist clients in navigating social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments. 
 Record services and evaluate client progress during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed. 
 Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs. 
 Provide clients with extended orientation on a variety of topics such as developing social support networks, navigating transportation systems, and navigating physical healthcare systems with families. 
 Respond to client crises, with guidance from supervisor as needed. 
 Assist clients with requesting financial assistance when applicable and track the received financial assistance within case files.

 May train and guide the activities of volunteers and interns.
 Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion, and cohesion in IRC Missoula.
 Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies.
 Other duties as assigned.

 Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.

 Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
 Fluent in English required, both spoken and written; proficiency in Pashto, Dari, Arabic, Swahili, Spanish is preferred.

 Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 The IRC is seeking two (2) Program Development & Award Advisors.  These positions are open to candidates in the West and Central Africa Region (WACAR), or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply. 
 BACKGROUND 
 Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable. 
 Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) 
 The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.
 The Awards Management Unit (AMU) is one of four pillars within CRRD . The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources. 
 West and Central Africa Regional Overview 
 The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR) supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches. 
 WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration. 
 The regional team responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs. 
 WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria. 
 The Purpose of the Role 
 As part of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the PDAAs oversee a diverse portfolio of awards across the humanitarian, recovery, and development sectors. PDAAs liaise with country programs, HQ departments and donor contacts to ensure high-quality guidance and support to country offices throughout the award lifecycle.
 These roles will support country programs in the West and Central Africa region (WACAR) with donor compliance, award management, and producing high-quality donor deliverables. They will advise on IRC’s partnership system (PEERS), manage donor relationships including with HQ counterparts.
 In addition, these roles will support WACAR country programs in securing funding for their programmes, through supporting and leading pursuit of new funding opportunities, in line with IRC’s Business Development Strategy. Support includes all phases of the business development process, from opportunity identification to contract signature, including pre-positioning, partnerships building, proposal development, and due diligence phases.
 Successful candidates will have a strong track record of contributing to new humanitarian and development funding opportunities, deep knowledge of donor rules and regulations, and experience collaborating with local partner organizations.
 Scope and Authority 
 These roles have no line management responsibilities.
 Key Working Relationships 
 These positions will report jointly to the Senior Program and Awards Advisor (SPAA) and the Head of Business Development (HBD) for the WACAR region  and work closely with RPAS team members, country program grants and partnership teams, and across all teams within the Awards Management Unit, Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, Technical Excellence, and other key departments within IRC. PDAAs also serve as donor and partner points of contact as applicable per region.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
 Awards Management and Compliance 
 Manage a portfolio of awards for the WACAR region as assigned.
 Provide timely support on narrative reporting and post-award deliverables, guiding country offices on amendments, modifications, and submissions while collaborating with technical and financial staff.
 Provide support on budget realignments, changes in scope, NCEs, and other amendments for project elements not captured at proposal stage or emerging needs.
 Serve as first point of contact for country program-based awards staff to problem solve, guide and advise them on compliance post-award issues within the mentioned portfolio and to act as a connecting point between country program and other AMU teams to facilitate the timely flow of key information between them.
 Manage donor relationships by maintaining communication on contractual issues, updates on program implementation and following up on compliance queries and securing changes and approvals as needed.
 With support from the Program & Awards Officer (PAO), guide and coach country offices on partner management policies and PEER system compliance, and review and process sub-grants/partnership agreements. Coordinate with the Sub-awards and Partnerships (S&P) team as needed.
