The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 The IRC responds to people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives. Our work engages some of the most pressing issues in contemporary humanitarian action, including access, conflict sensitivity, coordination and impact.
 The IRC began its programs in Yemen in October 2012, establishing its presence in the south of the country in the Red Sea coastal city of Aden. Following the outbreak of war in March 2015 and the resulting humanitarian crisis, the IRC launched an emergency response in the southern governorates of Aden, Lahj, Abyan, Shabwah and Al Dhale, and later expanded. Yemen's operating environment requires a combination of direct implementation and partner-led approaches. The Grants Coordinator will support a diverse portfolio implemented across multiple geographic areas through both IRC teams and local partners, ensuring high-quality donor compliance, coordination, reporting, and award management.  Our programs cover health, WASH, nutrition, economic recovery and development, education, child protection, and women’s protection and empowerment.
 The IRC has worked in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, more than 2,200 staff work across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria and Yemen, supporting people affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.
 Scope of work 
 The Grants Coordinator manages a large, multi-donor grant portfolio for IRC Yemen and ensures the timely development, submission and reporting of funding proposals. The role covers all grants administration activities, including proposal development, donor compliance, contract management and internal and external reporting, while keeping systems and documentation current. The Grants Coordinator also leads process-improvement initiatives and provides training and mentoring to country program staff and partners to strengthen donor management and compliance.
 Job summary 
 The Grants Coordinator is a strategic role responsible for managing IRC Yemen’s grant portfolio, ensuring compliance with donor requirements, and leading the development of high-quality proposals and reports. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Programs (DDP), the Grants Coordinator supervises the grants team, coordinates inter-departmental efforts to secure and manage funding, and serves as the primary focal point for donor communications and risk mitigation. The role requires exceptional organizational skills, advanced writing ability, and the capacity to work effectively in a complex, conflict-affected environment.
 The Grants Coordinator works closely with all departments, including program, METAL, finance, supply chain, HR and partnerships, and liaises with the regional office in Amman and with IRC headquarters grants and technical units.
 Working relations 
 Reports to: Deputy Director of Programs (DDP)
 Directly supervises: Grants Manager, Grants Officer and Communications Senior Officer
 Key internal collaborators: Technical Program Coordinators, METAL staff, Field Coordinators, the Partnerships team, Finance and Supply Chain teams, the Awards Management Unit, and Regional and HQ Grants units
 External: Donor representatives, local partners, government counterparts, and clusters and working groups
 Main responsibilities 
 Proposal development and business development 
 Ensure that IRC’s proposal development system is understood and followed across management, program, finance and operations, resulting in timely, high-quality submissions.
 With the DDP and HQ colleagues, proactively identify new funding opportunities by monitoring donor strategies, policies and funding trends, and keep the opportunity pipeline up to date.
 Support the DDP and technical leads in new program design and in maintaining the Yemen business development strategy, in line with the country Strategic Action Plan (SAP).
 Prepare for and lead Go/No-Go meetings for funding opportunities as required.
 Oversee the development of all concept notes and proposals, acting as lead writer or editor, and develop efficient process-management tools for proposal development.
 Define and communicate clear roles, responsibilities and timelines for each department, and facilitate cross-departmental coordination.

 Interpret donor solicitations and donor-specific rules and regulations to ensure responsive and compliant proposal design.
 Act as focal point with HQ and external consultants during proposal review, editing and submission.

 Maintain a broad and deep understanding of IRC policies and of the terms and conditions across the grant portfolio and ensure that the Grants unit develops and maintains the procedures needed to apply them.
 Review donor agreements and coordinate their review and signature with the relevant HQ offices; coordinate approval of pre-award spending as required.
 Coordinate all project revisions, amendments, extensions and budget realignments, in consultation with the DDP.
 Ensure timely and productive facilitation of Project Cycle Management (PCM) meetings, including design, opening, implementation, closing and lessons-learned meetings; capture action points and follow up to completion.
 Maintain and regularly disseminate the grants tracker, including grant opening and closing dates, and share portfolio updates internally and with the Awards Management Unit.
 Work with the Finance team to review spending plans and financial health, and to ensure effective spending, amendments, and closeout.
 Ensure that the Opportunity Tracking Information System (OTIS) is updated and maintained throughout the award lifecycle.
 Ensure that the grants filing system is respected and that all donor contractual documents, reports and key correspondence are filed consistently in up-to-date shared libraries.
 Ensure that all communication with IRC colleagues and donors is constructive, clear and organized.

 Develop and update compliance cheat sheets for all grants.
 In coordination with the DDP and the Policy, Advocacy and Communications Coord

 TITLE: Interpreter Services Administrative Support Intern

 BACKGROUND : Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee is a leading, non-sectarian, non-profit organization providing emergency relief, protection, rehabilitation assistance, resettlement services, and advocacy for refugees and victims of oppression or violent conflict.  Domestically, our 28 offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.
 SCOPE OF WORK: The Administrative Support Intern is a key contributor to the Interpreter Services team. In addition, this program serves the global IRC network, including IRC headquarters, with interpretation and translation services.

 • Attend an intern orientation.
 • Work as a team member to monitor Fluency Internet Interpreter Scheduling System for interpreter requests and match them with available interpreters.
 • Support and correspond with interpreters to assign and reschedule appointments.
 • Provide customer support, including answering emails and phone calls, editing and rescheduling appointments in Fluency, and following up as needed.
 • Monitor occasional voicemail/phone calls and direct urgent calls to Interpreter Services staff for assistance if necessary.
 • Provide tech support for Fluency, Microsoft Office products, and other communication platforms for interpreters and customers.
 • Assist with evaluating and training new interpreter candidates, including administering language exams.
 • Record hours and submit completed timesheet for each month via the IRC’s online Volunteer Dashboard.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Nigeria, Chad, and Cameroon. 
 Ce poste est ouvert aux candidats résidant au Nigeria, au Tchad ou au Cameroun et disposant du droit légal de travailler dans leur pays de résidence. 
 Présentation du poste 
 Airbel est le laboratoire d'innovation de l'IRC. Nous travaillons aux côtés des personnes touchées par les conflits et les crises pour concevoir des services plus utiles, plus dignes et plus durables. Ce poste place un·e designer au cœur de ce travail en Afrique de l'Ouest et centrale, au plus près des communautés, du personnel de première ligne et des questions qui déterminent si un produit ou un service aide réellement quelqu'un.
 Vous serez nos yeux et nos mains sur le terrain. Vous mènerez la recherche design, échangerez avec les clients et les prestataires, observerez ce qu'ils font et pourquoi, et transformerez vos découvertes en prototypes que vous testerez et affinerez sur le terrain. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec la Responsable du design centré sur l'humain, qui vous appuiera sur la synthèse et le développement des concepts pendant que vous façonnez votre propre travail.
 Responsabilités principales 
 •    Mener la recherche design sur le terrain : entretiens, observation et temps passé avec les clients et le personnel de première ligne.
 •    Rester au contact d'une même zone géographique ou d'un même axe de travail assez longtemps pour repérer les tendances qui n'apparaissent qu'avec le temps.
 •    Donner du sens à ce que vous observez sur le terrain et repérer les étincelles d'innovation déjà présentes dans les solutions et les idées des gens eux-mêmes.
 •    Transformer la recherche en prototypes, les tester avec de vraies personnes et itérer au fil de vos apprentissages, plutôt que de suivre un script figé.
 •    Restituer ce que vous apprenez sous une forme utile à l'équipe : notes claires, visuels, parcours utilisateur, tout ce qui rend une observation parlante.
 •    Collaborer avec les équipes programmes pays, les responsables techniques et le personnel de première ligne avec soin et respect, en gagnant l'accès dont dépend une bonne recherche.
 •    Intervenir en Afrique de l'Ouest et centrale francophone, et dans d'autres contextes humanitaires selon les besoins, en vous adaptant rapidement à de nouveaux contextes et à de nouvelles équipes.
 Exigences du poste 
 Expérience professionnelle 
 Nous aimerions comprendre votre façon de penser et de travailler, notamment :
 •    Une expérience de recherche auprès des personnes, dans n'importe quel cadre : recherche design, ethnographie, recherche UX ou produit, recherche participative ou recherche-action, ou tout autre type de recherche qualitative. Ce qui compte, c'est que vous soyez allé·e au-delà d'un script pour comprendre pourquoi les gens agissent comme ils le font.
 •    Vous avez construit ou mis en place quelque chose (un service, un petit pilote, un outil, une application, voire une version papier sommaire d'une idée), vous l'avez testé avec les personnes concernées et vous l'avez fait évoluer en fonction de ce que vous avez appris. Nous appelons cela du « prototypage », mais vous n'avez pas besoin d'avoir employé ce mot.
 •    Un sens de l'observation des opportunités du quotidien : les solutions de contournement, les petits détails et ce que les gens ont déjà trouvé par eux-mêmes.
 •    Quelque chose qui montre votre façon de penser : un portfolio, une étude de cas, un compte rendu de recherche, des photos d'un prototype ou un projet que vous avez contribué à façonner. Ce n'est pas grave si ce n'est pas abouti, mais nous aimerions voir votre réflexion sous une forme ou une autre.
 Compétences démontrées 
 •    De solides compétences en recherche : vous savez concevoir et mener un travail de terrain, échanger avec tout le monde, respecter l'éthique auprès de personnes en situation de vulnérabilité, et lire une situation pour ce qu'elle révèle, avec soin dans votre manière de recueillir et de consigner ce que vous trouvez.
 •    De solides compétences en test de prototypes : vous construisez de façon sommaire, testez tôt et ajustez en cours de test plutôt que d'attendre une version finie.
 •    Une réelle curiosité pour ce qui pousse les gens à agir comme ils le font, et le discernement pour y déceler l'étincelle d'une idée.
 •    De l'aisance sur le terrain : vous pouvez passer deux semaines d'affilée sur un site et y faire du bon travail.
 •    Une capacité d'adaptation à des cultures, des langues et des plans qui changent, portée par l'humilité et le soin des personnes avec qui vous travaillez.
 Compétences linguistiques 
 Un français et un anglais fonctionnels, suffisants dans les deux langues pour mener des recherches et travailler avec des équipes ailleurs sur le continent. Les propositions et présentations peuvent être rédigées dans l'une ou l'autre langue, puis traduites.
 Expérience et compétences souhaitées 
 •    Un œil pour rendre les enseignements lisibles à travers des visuels, des cartes et des présentations simples.
 •    Une expérience dans des contextes humanitaires, de santé ou communautaires.
 Autorisation de travail 
 Les candidat·e·s doivent disposer du droit légal de travailler dans le pays où le poste est base.
 Environnement de travail 
 Ce poste est basé dans un bureau pays de l'IRC en RDC, au Nigéria ou au Tchad, avec une installation de bureau standard. Le travail implique des déplacements fréquents, jusqu'à 40 %, vers des sites situés dans divers contextes humanitaires, dans la région et à l'international. Une mission de recherche design ou de prototypage peut représenter deux semaines d'affilée dans des lieux reculés, à faibles ressources et parfois peu sûrs, avec un hébergement sommaire, une connectivité limitée et de longues journées. Si c'est justement le fait d'être au plus près du terrain qui vous attire, ce poste est fait pour vous.
 IRC et les employés de IRC doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes contenus dans le IRC WAY (normes de conduite professionnelle). Ce sont l'Intégrité, Egalite, le Service, et la Responsabilité. En conformité avec ces valeurs, IRC opère et fait respecter les politiques sur la protection des bénéficiaires contre l'exploitation et les abus, la protection de l'enfant, le harcèlement sur les lieux de travail, l'intégrité financière, et les représailles.
 Rémunération : (Taux de rémunération au Nigeria : 1 368 460 à 2 189 540 NGN par mois ; au Tchad : 15 864 à 20 616 USD par an ; au Cameroun : 895 050 à 1 158 300 XAF par mois). Ces fourchettes tiennent compte de divers facteurs, notamment le marché du travail, le type de poste, l'équité interne et le budget. Les offres exactes sont déterminées en fonction du lieu de travail, de l'expérience et des compétences de chaque candidat par rapport aux exigences définies pour le poste.

 Airbel is IRC's innovation lab. We work alongside people affected by conflict and crisis to design services that are more useful, more dignified, and more likely to last.  Lead the responsible evaluation and adoption of AI within the CRM ecosystem, including Agentforce and integrations with external AI models, identifying worthwhile use cases while meeting IRC’s data protection, security, ethical AI and governance requirements.
 Assess AppExchange and other third-party products and recommend what IRC should adopt, keep or retire.
 Architecture and technical leadership 
 Own the solution architecture of the platform: data model, automation, security model, integrations and managed packages, including NPSP, Account Engagement (Pardot), Outlook integration, Blackthorn and Apsona.
 Set design and build standards for declarative and programmatic development (Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, APIs), and review the work of the team and partners against them.

 Oversee integrations with donation platforms, finance systems, the data warehouse and reporting tools, so that data flows are reliable and well documented.
 Stay hands-on: prototype, configure and build when that is the fastest way to unblock the team or prove an approach.
 Team and partner leadership 
 Lead, coach and develop a team of Salesforce administrators, developers and a business analyst, including recruitment, performance management, career development and workload planning.
 Build a team culture of good engineering practice, clear documentation and service to the people who use the platform.

 Governance, security and operations

 Oversee incident, problem, change and release management, including readiness for Salesforce’s three annual releases and managed-package updates.
 Oversee user support, testing and defect resolution delivered by the team and partners.
 Make sure reports and dashboards give leaders accurate, trusted information.
 Stakeholders and business context 
 Build strong relationships with fundraising, finance, data and programme leaders, and understand how IRC raises, processes and stewards income in different countries.
 Explain technical options, risks and trade-offs in plain language so that senior, non-technical stakeholders can make good decisions.
 Key Working Relationships:  
 Position Reports to:  Senior Director, Marketing Technology 
 Position directly supervises:  Team of Salesforce Admins/Developers/Business Analyst 
 Other Internal and/or external contacts : 
 Internal :  Close collaboration with global and regional stakeholders across External Relations, Resettlement, Asylum and Integration, Information Technology, Communications, Finance, Data and Analytics and other teams that rely on the CRM platform. 
 External :  Technology suppliers, implementation partners, consultants, contractors and other service providers. 
 Job Qualifications:  
 Education:

 Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business systems or a related discipline or equivalent professional experience.

 Experience acting as a product or platform owner, including developing roadmaps, governing demand and prioritising investment.

 CONTEXTO. 
 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas.  
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos.  
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Miranda, La Guaira, Caracas, Zulia, Lara, Falcón, Táchira y Apure, trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales. 
 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El/La Auxiliar de Programas brindará apoyo transversal a la implementación de las actividades desarrolladas en el Estado Táchira. Será responsable de apoyar la movilización comunitaria, el levantamiento de información, la identificación de necesidades humanitarias, la coordinación con líderes comunitarios y actores locales, la organización de actividades en terreno incluyendo la logística de distribución de servicios, el registro de beneficiarios/as y el seguimiento de indicadores. Facilita la coordinación con comunidades, socios y autoridades locales en la región. Actuará como enlace entre las comunidades afectadas, socios implementadores, instituciones locales y el equipo de la organización, contribuyendo a garantizar una implementación eficiente, oportuna y segura de las actividades del programa.  CONTEXTO: 
 El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas cuyas vidas y medios de vida se ven afectados por conflictos y desastres a sobrevivir, recuperarse y obtener el control de su futuro. Fundado en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, el IRC trabaja hoy en más de 40 países y 22 ciudades de EE. UU.
 En El Salvador, el IRC apoya a población en situación de vulnerabilidad que es afectada por diferentes factores del contexto, a través de programas de protección, y asistencia humanitaria. El equipo de Cadena de Suministro de la oficina de San Salvador gestiona compras y logística para sostener la respuesta humanitaria en varios departamentos del país.
 Descripción general de la posición: 
 La pasantía en Cadena de Suministro ofrece una experiencia práctica e integral en la gestión de compras, logística y transporte, gestión de almacenes e inventarios, y datos para la toma de decisiones, dentro de una operación humanitaria real. El/la pasante formará parte del equipo de Cadena de Suministro de la Región CAMEX y reportará al Oficial de Cadena de Suministros y tendrá soporte técnico del área de cadena de suministros regional quienes lo acompañarán durante todo el proceso. A través de un plan de rotación individual, el/la pasante participará en las principales sub-áreas de la función (compras de emergencia y logística de distribución, entre otras), con responsabilidades crecientes y al menos un proyecto de mejora con entregable propio. Al finalizar, contará con una visión integral de cómo opera la cadena de suministro en una organización humanitaria internacional, además de un certificado de finalización y una carta de referencia.
 Responsabilidades mayores: 
 Aprendizaje y Desarrollo 
 Procesos y políticas de compras humanitarias, gestión de almacenes e inventarios, control de activos, y herramientas de seguimiento en Excel/Power BI.
 Inducción general al IRC y al equipo país, capacitación inicial en políticas de Cadena de Suministro y en las herramientas internas de gestión, y acompañamiento cercano de su supervisor/a durante las primeras semanas.
 Comprender el ciclo completo de la cadena de suministro humanitaria y ser capaz de apoyar de forma autónoma tareas de compras, logística, almacén y reporte de datos.
 Apoyo Operativo y Administrativo 
 Apoyar la elaboración de solicitudes, estudios de mercado en zonas operativas, base de datos de proveedores, crear un archivo innovador que permita la gestión documental de procesos de adquisición, y la coordinación logística de envíos y distribuciones.
 Uso de las herramientas internas del IRC para gestión de compras, control de inventarios y activos, y bases de datos en Excel para el seguimiento de indicadores del equipo
 Apoyo en la recepción, verificación y registro de mercancía en almacén, así como en conteos cíclicos, conciliaciones periódicas de inventario y seguimiento a fechas de vencimiento y condiciones de almacenamiento.
 Apoyo a Proyectos y Programas 
 Apoyo directo a proyectos de compras de emergencia y logística de distribución, en coordinación con los equipos de programa que dependen de un abastecimiento oportuno.
 Recopilación y análisis básico de información de proveedores, tiempos de entrega y costos, para apoyar la toma de decisiones del equipo.
 Apoyo en el registro y actualización de la base de proveedores, así como en el seguimiento a su desempeño (cumplimiento de tiempos de entrega, calidad y condiciones acordadas).
 Participación en reuniones de coordinación del equipo y, según el contexto de seguridad, en visitas a terreno u oficinas de campo.
 Coordinación y Trabajo en Equipo 
 Coordinación semanal con su supervisor/a para revisar avances, prioridades y aprendizajes, y contacto regular con otras áreas del programa (finanzas, programas, seguridad).
 Participación activa en las reuniones de equipo de Cadena de Suministro y comunicación oportuna de avances, dudas o dificultades.
 Otros 
 Otras tareas afines asignadas por su supervisor/a, acordes con el nivel y el propósito formativo de la pasantía.
 Relaciones clave de trabajo: 
 Reporta a: Oficial de Cadena de Suministros con soporte
 Requisitos del puesto: 
 Estudiante de últimos ciclos o egresado/a reciente (máximo 12-18 meses de graduación) de Ingeniería Industrial, Logística, Administración, Comercio Internacional o carreras afines.
 No se requiere experiencia laboral previa. Se valorará experiencia en proyectos académicos, prácticas o voluntariado relacionados con compras, logística o inventarios.
 Disposición para aprender, proactividad, responsabilidad, organización, atención al detalle, buena comunicación y trabajo en equipo.
 Manejo intermedio de Excel; deseable conocimiento básico de Power BI u otras herramientas de análisis de datos.
 Estar inscrito/a en una institución educativa o haber egresado en los últimos 12-18 meses; cumplir la edad mínima legal para pasantías según la normativa local.
 ESTÁNDARES: 
 Estándares de conducta profesional: los trabajadores de IRC deben adherirse a los valores y principios descritos en IRC Way - normas para la conducta profesional. Estos son integridad, servicio, responsabilidad e igualdad. De acuerdo con estos valores, el IRC opera y aplica políticas sobre la protección del beneficiario contra la explotación y el abuso, la salvaguardia del niño, el acoso en el lugar de trabajo, la integridad fiscal y anti-represalias.
 Igualdad de género: IRC se compromete a reducir la brecha de género en posiciones de liderazgo. Ofrecemos beneficios que proporcionan un entorno propicio para que las mujeres participen en nuestra fuerza de trabajo, incluido el permiso parental, los protocolos de seguridad sensibles al género y otros beneficios y subsidios de apoyo.
 Igualdad de oportunidades del Empleador: IRC es un empleador de igualdad de oportunidades. El IRC considera a todos los solicitantes sobre la base del mérito sin tener en cuenta la raza, sexo, color, origen nacional, religión, orientación sexual, edad, estado civil, estado de veterano, discapacidad o cualquier otra característica protegida por la ley aplicable.
 Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

 Extensive experience leading the development of large multi-sector funding proposals.

 In-depth knowledge of institutional donor compliance required. Knowledge of ECHO, SIDA, GFFO, BMZ and Gulf donor requirements a particular advantage.

 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas.
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos. 
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Zulia, Lara, Falcón,  Táchira y Apure, trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales.

 Diseñar, implementar y dar seguimiento a campañas comunicacionales internas y externas, desde la definición de objetivos, audiencias y mensajes clave hasta la medición de resultados.
 Redactar y difundir notas de prensa, comunicados, historias de impacto y otros contenidos escritos para medios de comunicación, redes sociales, sitio web y donantes.

 Apoyar la cobertura comunicacional de eventos, actividades públicas y visitas de donantes o aliados.

 Cualquier otra labor necesaria para el área.
 ENTREGABLES: 
 Piezas gráficas y materiales de visibilidad elaborados conforme a la línea gráfica vigente.
 Notas de prensa, historias de impacto y contenidos para redes sociales, sitio web y donantes.
 Guiones y material audiovisual (videos y registros fotográficos), con su archivo debidamente organizado.
 Informes periódicos de resultados de las campañas y de las actividades de comunicación.
 Requisitos del trabajo: 
 Título universitario en Comunicación Social, Periodismo, Comunicación Audiovisual, Publicidad o carreras afines.

 Experiencia en el manejo y la creación de líneas gráficas e identidad visual.
 Experiencia en el diseño e implementación de campañas comunicacionales.

 Adicionalmente, el 24 de junio de 2026 el país fue impactado por dos terremotos de magnitud 7.2 y 7.5, los cuales ocasionaron afectaciones significativas en viviendas, infraestructura pública, establecimientos de salud, sistemas de agua y medios de vida, especialmente en los estados La Guaira, Miranda y Distrito Capital, generando nuevas necesidades humanitarias y de recuperación temprana. Como consecuencia de estos eventos, fue declarado Estado de Emergencia nacional para coordinar la respuesta y recuperación de las zonas afectadas.
 En Venezuela, el IRC desarrolla intervenciones humanitarias a través de operaciones directas y mecanismos de colaboración con organizaciones locales. Actualmente fortalece acciones relacionadas con protección, salud, educación, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH), seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida, transferencias monetarias, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitarias.
 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El/La Oficial Senior de Recuperación Económica y Desarrollo será responsable de coordinar e implementar las actividades del portafolio ERD del IRC en Venezuela, asegurando la calidad técnica, operativa y el cumplimiento de los objetivos establecidos con los donantes. Este rol contribuirá a fortalecer, coordinar e implementar intervenciones de asistencia basada en mercados y transferencias monetarias, dirigidas a hogares afectados por la crisis humanitaria.

 CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND 
 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than twenty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.
 Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.
 With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.
 The IRC launched an emergency health response in Yemen in 2012. Since then, and despite continued instability and conflict, the IRC has extended its presence throughout the country, implementing a diverse, integrated program of health, nutrition, WASH, protection, and cash programs. These programs prioritize local partnerships with both public institutions and civil society, and span emergency response, humanitarian, and recovery modalities, while serving vulnerable Yemenis including IDPs and returnees, migrants and refugees, women, children, and youth.
 SCOPE OF WORK 
 The Country Director (CD) sets the strategic direction, leads all programs, emergency response, financial and operational matters, and oversees humanitarian access and the adherence to and application of security measures, as well as external relationships and partnerships in Yemen. As lead of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the CD ensures accountability of the SMT for the overall leadership and supervisory management of approximately 120 IRC staff and more than 400 incentive workers, programming, and operations, including program quality and accountability, stewardship of resources, staff safety and security, performance management, and external representation, for which the CD remains accountable.
 Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary, demonstrated leadership abilities who deploys strong communication and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong contextual analytical skills and an ability to translate the impact of geopolitical developments and rapidly changing humanitarian conditions into operational priorities and effective responses. They will build a network of partnerships, diversify program resources, and ensure organizational readiness to respond to emerging and escalating emergencies while maintaining continuity of critical humanitarian services. They will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design, and deliver responsive, high-quality humanitarian, emergency response, early recovery, and development programs; ensuring the efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance, and focused, timely reporting; and overseeing financial management and compliance systems.

offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 NOTE ABOUT COMPENSATION: 
 Internships at the IRC are unpaid. No financial compensation, including compensation for relocation, is available. Reimbursement is available for mileage when using a personal vehicle. Eligible interns will also receive a nominal per diem reimbursement aligned with current intern reimbursement policies. 
 BACKGROUND: 
 Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee is a leading, non-sectarian, non-profit organization providing emergency relief, protection, rehabilitation assistance, resettlement services, and advocacy for refugees and victims of oppression or violent conflict. Domestically, our 28 offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.
 SCOPE OF INTERN WORK: 
 The Occupational Therapy (OT) program focuses on life skills training as a supportive supplementary intervention that works alongside IRC UT’s various case management program. Under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist, the inter will support a wide range of areas for self-sufficiency and access to community resources for refugee and immigrant families. Through the program, the intern will work with individuals to build the skills and alternative approaches to everyday tasks, including managing personal finance (budgeting, paying bills, banking), navigating public transit, medication management, development safe routines in-home, and confidently accessing resources (scheduling appointments, etc.). Specialized support may also include job readiness and Pre-Driving training. Intern will report to: Yda Smith, PhD, OTR/L.
 MINIMUM COMMITMENT: 
 10 – 20 hours per week for 10-12 weeks
 START DATE: 
 January 12, 2027 (final start date to be confirmed)
 THE PROFESSION OF OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY: 
 The fundamental core of OT is to support clients’ abilities to participate in the everyday activities that they need and want to do. OTs have, at a minimum, a master’s degree, and OT Assistants have a community college or bachelor’s degree. Most often, they work in a healthcare environment with people of any age who are dealing with physical, cognitive, or mental health issues. OT education includes knowledge of many health conditions across the life span. Breaking down tasks into simpler and smaller components and therapeutic-use-of-self are skills practiced. In many settings, there are OT aides who do not have a degree in OT but who provide assistance to clients under the direction of the staff OT. The intern position at IRC is similar to the OT Aide position in other settings and provides an opportunity to learn about the OT profession. 
 RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Under the direction of the staff occupational therapist, work one-on-one with a variety of clients to provide life skills training activities in-home and around the community.
 Assist with group training approaches, including working with interpretation, preparing for groups, and managing group dynamics.
 Collaborate across teams to achieve client goals, includes engaging with caseworkers, community health workers, and other IRC teams. 
 Case note all activities completed to document progress toward goals and ensure interventions are providing positive support.
 Attend staff meetings as schedule allows. 
 Assist staff occupational therapist and OT students as assigned. 
 Support the IRC UT office with other duties as assigned.
 LEARNING OBJECTIVES: 
 Gain professional experience working in the public health sector.
 Gain experience teaching and communicating with clients to break new learning tasks into smaller pieces to support client success. 
 Gain experience teaching life skills in a community setting. 
 Gain knowledge about the profession of occupational therapy and other professions represented at the IRC. 
 Gain experience collaborating and communicating with a wide range of IRC professionals from different backgrounds and specialities. 
 Gain experience communicating with English Language Learners and use of an interpreter. 
 Gain public speaking experience through teaching classes to clients and reporting in staff meetings. 
 REQUIREMENTS: 
 Must be currently enrolled in a graduate/undergraduate program, or have graduated less than 6 months ago.
 Interest in working with diverse populations.
 Motivated, flexible, able to work independently.
 Strong communication skills and ability to work as part of a team.
 Proficient in Microsoft365 and data entry.
 Valid driver’s license and insurace, access to a personal vehicle, and willingness to drive clients.
 Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in English; fluency in additional language(s) preferred.
 Background in occupational therapy, health promotion, social work, or other related field preferred.
 Complete IRC background check & all related orientations/trainings.

 Sobre SignPost 
 Signpost es una iniciativa digital innovadora que proporciona a la comunidad humanitaria una plataforma para llegar a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo y comunidades afectadas por crisis en todo el mundo con información accesible. Comenzó en 2015 en Grecia y desde entonces se ha expandido para incluir instancias en todo el mundo, incluso en América Central y ahora en Colombia a través de la instancia InfoPa’lante.
 Cada canal de InfoPa’lante proporciona a los usuarios información actualizada y específica del contexto sobre necesidades vitales como derechos legales, transporte y servicios médicos, lo que permite a las personas tomar decisiones informadas en los momentos más críticos.
 Descripción del Cargo: 
 El/la moderador/a es nuestro personal digital "de primera línea", que utiliza las redes sociales para comunicarse directamente con nuestros usuarios todos los días, respondiendo a sus comentarios, mensajes y preguntas. Además, se encarga de sistematizar la información recibida, hacer remisiones, completar reportes, participar en actividades comunitarias de socialización de InfoPa’lante, estar en constante comunicación con los otros miembros del equipo, entre otras actividades. El trabajo será principalmente en línea, con reuniones presenciales de manera ad-hoc.
 Responsabilidades: 
 Responder a los mensajes y comentarios recibidos en los canales de redes sociales de InfoPa’lante con la ayuda de un equipo de expertos y pautas de moderación.
 Involucrar a los usuarios en una conversación en línea.
 Seguir el protocolo para escalar cualquier comunicación de casos vulnerables a especialistas en protección.
 Trazar estrategias sobre comentarios representativos y notables y escribir un análisis de las comunicaciones del día (incluidas las respuestas a publicaciones, tendencias en la conversación y lagunas de información).
 Compartir opiniones, comentarios, conciencia cultural, conocimiento contextual y aprendizaje con el equipo más amplio de manera continua.

 Analizar las brechas de información entre las poblaciones de refugiados para alimentar la futura creación de contenido.
 Realizar remisiones en casos de riesgos de protección
 Desarrollar reportes en torno a las actividades realizadas
 Mantenerse al día con toda la información nueva que se publica de manera continua y asista a entrenamientos regulares según sea necesario
 Otras actividades designadas relevantes al cargo

 Requerimientos esenciales

 Capacidad para trabajar de forma autónoma y en equipo.
 Respeto por las personas de todos los ámbitos de la vida.

 El compromiso de ir más allá en la búsqueda de brindar a las personas en crisis información precisa.

 Correcto uso de reglas gramaticales y ortográficas
   Requerimientos deseados 
 Experiencia administrando un Fan Page o Página de Facebook.
 Experiencia en atención al cliente

 Job Overview 
 We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.
 This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.
 The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.
 This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

 Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
 Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
 Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa. 
 Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained
 Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance 
 Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution

 Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
 Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders
 Personal Attributes 
 Spanish language proficiency
 Builds credibility quickly with leadership 
 Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it 
 Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences
 Working Environment :  
 This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

What did you do with it, and what happened? A cover letter is required for your application to be considered, and applications submitted without one cannot move forward. 
 Why we’re asking: This step helps us confirm that every applicant is a real person and keeps the selection process fair for all candidates. It is not part of your skills assessment, and it will take only a few minutes. 
 Job Background / Overview 
 The IRC is actively investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As the organization expands its use of AI platforms, including tools from Anthropic, OpenAI, and integrated data environments, the IT department is building dedicated technical capacity to keep these systems running reliably, securely, and effectively.
 The IRC is investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As that investment grows, so does the need for someone to own the technical layer underneath it: the systems, integrations, and infrastructure that make AI tools work at scale.
 The AI Platform Engineer is that person. This is a technical operations role, not a user-facing one. This role is responsible for keeping the IRC's enterprise AI environment running managing platform configurations and API access, building and maintaining integrations between AI tools and IRC systems, writing scripts and automations, and serving as the technical point of contact for data engineering and InfoSec. Day-to-day, this person is more likely to be reading logs, troubleshooting a broken pipeline, or pushing a configuration change than answering questions from end users.
 The role works in close coordination with the AI Platform Support Director, who owns vendor relationships, licensing, and adoption strategy. This role owns the technical execution underneath that, ensuring the systems are reliable, observable, and properly connected to the rest of the IRC's data and operational environment.

 Tracking uptime, error rates, token consumption, and integration reliability

 Develop lightweight scripts, connectors, and automations to support AI-assisted workflows across teams, primarily in Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript
 Troubleshoot integration failures, data flow issues, and API connectivity problems across the AI ecosystem
 Collaborate with the data engineering team on AI/KM pipeline work, including vector store ingestion, retrieval configuration, and source data connections
 Contribute to technical design discussions with engineering partners, translating operational requirements into implementable solutions
 Maintain technical documentation for all integrations, including architecture notes, runbooks, and dependency maps
 Monitoring, Resource Optimization & InfoSec Liaison (15%) 
 Track and report on AI resource utilization across platforms, identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve cost efficiency in coordination with the AI

 Contribute to sprint and project planning with accurate estimates on technical effort and dependencies

 AI & Cloud Platforms 
 Hands-on experience administering enterprise AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable tools), including API management, access controls, and environment configuration

 Experience working with Databricks or comparable data/ML platforms is a strong plus
 Integration & Development

 Experience building and maintaining REST API integrations, including authentication patterns, webhook handling, and error management

 Familiarity with version control (Git) and standard deployment practices for scripts and integrations
 Systems Administration & Monitoring

 Security & Compliance

 BACKGROUND: 
 Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.
 SCOPE OF WORK: 
 The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.
 RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
 Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
 Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs.
 Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
 Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
 Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
 Assist with housing set-ups for new arrivals as needed.
 Assist clients in completing initial medical appointments as needed.
 Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in ETO and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
 Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
 Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
 Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
 May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
 Other duties as assigned.

 Education: Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.
 Work Experience: 
 Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
 Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
 Demonstrated Skills & Competencies: 
 Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
 Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
 Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
 Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
 Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.

offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Contexto: 
 El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a algunas de las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo, ayudando a las personas afectadas por conflictos, desastres y desplazamiento a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundado en 1933 a petición de Albert Einstein, el IRC trabaja en más de 40 países brindando asistencia en salud, protección, educación, recuperación económica, medios de vida, agua, saneamiento e higiene y fortalecimiento comunitario.
 La situación humanitaria en Venezuela continúa generando importantes necesidades en materia de acceso a servicios básicos, protección, salud, seguridad alimentaria y recuperación económica.
 Adicionalmente, el 24 de junio de 2026 el país fue impactado por dos terremotos de magnitud 7.2 y 7.5, los cuales ocasionaron afectaciones significativas en viviendas, infraestructura pública, establecimientos de salud, sistemas de agua y medios de vida, especialmente en los estados La Guaira, Miranda y Distrito Capital, generando nuevas necesidades humanitarias y de recuperación temprana.
 Como consecuencia de estos eventos, fue declarado Estado de Emergencia nacional para coordinar la respuesta y recuperación de las zonas afectadas.
 En Venezuela, el IRC desarrolla intervenciones humanitarias a través de operaciones directas y mecanismos de colaboración con organizaciones locales. Actualmente fortalece acciones relacionadas con protección, salud, educación, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH), seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida, transferencias monetarias, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitarias.
 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El asistente de Recuperación Económica y Desarrollo apoyará la implementación efectiva de actividades y estrategias de recuperación económica, seguridad alimentaria y programas de transferencias monetarias en el marco del programa de Atención Humanitaria y Recuperación Temprana. Trabajará en estrecha colaboración con Oficiales y Oficial Senior del programa ERD del IRC, asegurando la correcta ejecución de las actividades según lo planificado. Reportará directamente al Oficial del programa.
 Responsabilidades principales: 
 Calidad Técnica y Desarrollo de Programas 
 Apoyar la implementación de las actividades del programa ERD, conforme a la estrategia, los SOPs y las normativas del IRC.
 Contribuir a la gestión del conocimiento mediante la recopilación y difusión de lecciones aprendidas y buenas prácticas. 
 Mantenerse actualizado en desarrollos relacionados con transferencias monetarias, asistencia basada en mercado y estándares humanitarios. 
 Apoyar la recolección y el análisis de datos de mercado: monitoreo periódico de precios, visitas a comercios y proveedores y seguimiento a la funcionalidad de los mercados.
 Apoyar la caracterización, focalización, registro, verificación y enrolamiento de participantes según los criterios definidos.
 Apoyar el manejo seguro de las bases de datos de participantes y de las entregas realizadas.
 Orientar a los participantes sobre la modalidad de asistencia, el uso de los mecanismos de entrega y los canales de retroalimentación.
 Contribuir a pruebas piloto, validación de herramientas y metodologías.
 Participar en las actividades de formación programadas.
 Planificación, Operación y Seguimiento 
 Apoyar la logística de actividades de caracterización y entrega de asistencia humanitaria, incluyendo planificación de recursos y organización de espacios. 
 Ejecutar los planes de trabajo y cronogramas en coordinación con el equipo, y programar y reportar las actividades realizadas.
 Apoyar el monitoreo post distribución y el seguimiento a participantes, diligenciar las listas de verificación y reportar los problemas al supervisor.
 Registrar las quejas y la retroalimentación de los participantes y referir los casos vulnerables a otros sectores del IRC (Salud, Protección, Educación) según las rutas definidas.
 Apoyar la elaboración de informes, la gestión del conocimiento y la preparación de información para los espacios de coordinación cuando se solicite.
 Cumplir las políticas institucionales y los principios humanitarios, incluyendo la protección contra la explotación y el abuso sexual y la salvaguarda, y reportar rápidamente cualquier inquietud o incidente de seguridad.
 Relaciones clave de trabajo: 
 Reporta a: Oficial Senior ERD
 Responsabilidades del SGSST
 Responsabilidades de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo

 Procurar el cuidado integral de su salud.
 Suministrar información clara, completa y veraz sobre su estado de salud.
 Cumplir las normas de seguridad e higiene propias de la empresa.
 Participar en la prevención de riesgos laborales mediante las actividades que se realicen en la empresa.
 Informar las condiciones de riesgo detectadas al jefe inmediato.
 Reportar inmediatamente todo accidente de trabajo o incidente.
 Requisitos del trabajo:
 Educación 
 Título universitario o técnico superior en Economía, Administración, Contaduría, Ciencias Sociales, Ingeniería Industrial o carreras afines, o experiencia equivalente demostrable.
 Experiencia laboral: 
 De 1 a 2 años de experiencia laboral en la implementación de proyectos humanitarios, de medios de vida y/o en la entrega de transferencias monetarias, vales o asistencia en especie, en contextos humanitarios y de recuperación temprana.
 Deseable: experiencia en levantamiento de datos de mercado y monitoreo de precios.
 Deseable: manejo de herramientas de recolección y gestión de datos (KoBo, CommCare u otras).

 Habilidades y competencias demostradas: 
 Manejo de Microsoft Office, en particular Excel intermedio para el manejo de bases de datos y listas de precios.
 Habilidades de comunicación efectiva.
 Excelentes competencias interpersonales y de trabajo en equipo.
 Capacidad sólida para organizar el trabajo, cumplir los plazos, coordinar múltiples tareas y mantener la atención al detalle.

 Entorno de trabajo cambiante.
 Sede en Caracas. La presencia y los movimientos de trabajo geográficos y el alcance del programa podrían cambiar a medida que el programa crezca.
 Viajes frecuentes a otros municipios o estados es posible.

 About Us 
 Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster.  ·       Support refinement of business development processes for Technical Excellence.
 ·       Attend key cross-unit and cross-departmental meetings regarding business development to maintain an in-depth understanding of IRC funding streams and business development priorities.
 ECHO Awards Management and Compliance (10%) 
 Awards Management: Act as IRC Germany’s post-award focal point for Technical Excellence and Global Supply Chain ECHO awards.
 ·       Provide ad-hoc compliance guidance to grants team on ECHO awards
 ·       Coordinate with grants team to ensure timely submissions of reports on APPEL.
 ·       Monitor ECHO portfolio through participation in project implementation meetings, ensuring progress against objectives and compliance with ECHO guidelines.
 ·       Manage donor relationship with ECHO across portfolio.
 Your Profile 
 Essential 
 ·       Experience preparing or submitting proposals to ECHO
 ·       5+ years of progressive work experience connected to business development and working in or closely with Technical teams
 ·       Highly collaborative and pro-active colleague with a talent for delivering results with cross-functional groups

 ·       Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a multi-cultural environment
 ·       University degree in Business Administration, Finance, International Development or a relevant field, or equivalent work experience

 Desired 
 ·       Experience working with IRC systems is a plus
 ·       Dedication to diversity, equity and inclusion, and a strong passion for our mission
 ·       Comfortable adapting to new challenges and dynamic priorities, while maintaining professional grace
 ·       Fluency in French, Spanish or Arabic language a plus
 We Offer 
 Meaningful work within a collaborative team
 A starting salary between 60,028 and 67,090 Euro gross per year as well as an annual salary increase
 Attractive employee benefits such as gym membership, company pension scheme, shopping vouchers, childcare subsidy, job bike leasing, subsidized Deutschlandticket (national public transport), and access to timely and confidential psychological support if needed
 30 days of annual leave and special leave days
 Flexible hybrid-work options (working hours, office/homebased)
 Training and professional development opportunities, including access to free language courses
 Assistance services for people with disabilities, if required.

 Experiencia demostrada en movilización comunitaria, implementación de jornadas educativas, actividades extramurales de salud y captación activa de beneficiaros, con enfoque en resultados y cumplimiento de metas.
 Conocimientos básicos en herramientas ofimáticas y manejo de bases de datos.

 The Content and Creative team, a part of M&M, consists of award-winning creative specialists and idea partners, developing powerful communications and experiences to engage audiences and ultimately to deliver on ER ambitions and objectives. Our mission is to be a leading provider of brand creative and storytelling products about the IRC’s clients, staff and programs.    
 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is seeking a skilled Graphic Designer to support our Impact at Scale work within the Creative Studio Design Team. This full-time role is focused on producing high-quality donor facing deliverables—primarily presentation decks, data visualizations, proposals and reports—that communicate the IRC’s humanitarian impact with clarity and precision. 
 The ideal candidate plays a pivotal role in securing support for the IRC’s most ambitious and impactful priorities. This individual brings the IRC’s Impact at Scale vision to life—translating complex program strategies into clear, compelling communications that motivate giving across Trusts & Foundations, High Net Worth Individuals (HNWI), Global New Business prospects, and Corporate partners. Working closely with the Strategy Unit, program teams, and External Relations colleagues, the Designer develops high quality proposals, reports, and pitch materials that show donors the meaningful impact their investment can make. 
 This designer thrives in a fast-paced creative environment, brings exceptional expertise and a sharp eye for typographic systems and layout hierarchy, and can translate complex data and narratives into polished, compelling visual documents. Must be experienced in the Adobe Creative Studio systems including InDesign, Photoshop and Illustrator. Figma and Figma Slides knowledge are a bonus but not required. 
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Reports & Long-Form Documents 
 Design and lay out high-quality impact reports, funding propositions, and donor collateral in Adobe InDesign
 Build and maintain paragraph and character styles, master pages, and grid systems to ensure typographic consistency and layout integrity
 Apply meticulous attention to type hierarchy, spacing, and detail across multi-page documents
 Produce print-ready and digital PDF outputs optimized for various distribution contexts
 Data Visualization & Infographics 
 Transform raw data and statistics into clear, meaningful charts, diagrams, and infographics
 Design visuals that communicate impact metrics at a glance for high-value donor audiences
 Work within established brand frameworks while bringing a strong visual sensibility to each piece
 Presentations & Decks 
 Design and produce executive-ready presentation decks (PowerPoint and/or Google Slides) aligned with IRC brand guidelines
 Develop scalable deck templates and systems that are easily reused and adapted across teams
 Collaborate with stakeholders to clarify goals, audience needs, and key messages; refine content structure for clarity, pacing, and emphasis
 Translate complex data, technical concepts, and program results into logical, digestible visual flows that guide understanding
 Collaboration & Brand Stewardship 
 Partner with the Creative Studio team and front-line fundraisers on bespoke HV donor projects
 Maintain strict brand consistency across all deliverables and seek approval through the Creative Studio as appropriate
 Manage multiple concurrent projects with tight turnarounds while maintaining exceptional quality and attention to detail
 Essential Qualifications: 
 4–5+ years of professional graphic design experience, with a strong portfolio demonstrating print and digital publication work
 Expert-level proficiency in Adobe InDesign, including master pages, paragraph/character styles, and grid-based layout systems
 High-level proficiency in Adobe Creative suite including Photoshop and Illustrator
 Strong command of Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop
 Demonstrated experience designing presentation decks in PowerPoint and/or Google Slides. Figma Slides knowledge is a preference but not required.
 Exceptional typographic skills and a meticulous eye for layout hierarchy, spacing, and detail
 Experience creating data visualizations and infographics that communicate complex information clearly
 Ability to work independently, manage deadlines, and adapt quickly in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment
 Passion for the IRC’s mission and commitment to humanitarian work
 Demonstrated Skills and Competencies: 
 Presentation Narrative & Content Strategy: ability to collaborate with stakeholders, identify key messages, and structure content for clarity and impact
 Typographic Excellence: deep understanding of type hierarchy, grid systems, and design consistency across long-form documents
 Data Visualization: skill in transforming quantitative information into intuitive visual formats for non-specialist audiences
 Attention to Detail: unwavering precision in design execution, file management, and brand application
 Communication: clear, concise communicator capable of working across teams and managing feedback constructively
 Time Management: proven ability to prioritize and deliver high-quality work across multiple concurrent projects
 Desired Qualifications: 
 Experience working in the nonprofit, humanitarian, or fundraising sector
 Familiarity with IRC’s brand guidelines and design system
 Experience with Figma or other UI/UX tools
 Working Environment: 
 This role may require working remotely full- or part-time (i.e., telecommuting). Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.
 Compensation: ( $73,000 - $85,000/annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget.  Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.
 Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation.
