offres.titre: Procurement Officer, Mass Marketing and External Relations (Fixed Term - 30th Sept 2027)
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Background 
 The Global Procurement Unit, within Global Supply Chain, leads sourcing strategy, category management and supplier management for IRC. Within this unit, the Senior Global Procurement Manager, Fundraising and Marketing Categories, leads category strategy and supplier portfolio management for fundraising, marketing and donor engagement services. The Procurement Officer supports delivery of these strategies through assigned procurement activities.
 The Procurement Officer sources services for External Relations' mass marketing and fundraising activities, including direct mail, digital and paid media, telemarketing, face-to-face and door-to-door fundraising, creative and production services, and donor data services. The role supports value for money, timely campaign delivery and compliance with applicable procurement requirements.
 Position Overview 
 The Procurement Officer manages assigned procurement activities for Mass Marketing and Fundraising within External Relations, maintaining complete sourcing records and coordinating supplier due diligence, approvals and contract administration.
 The officer independently handles routine sourcing activities within delegated authority and supports the Senior Global Procurement Manager on high-value, complex or high-risk procurements. The role works with External Relations, Finance, IT, Legal and risk specialists to progress requests and escalate issues requiring specialist advice or management decisions.
 This is an execution-focused individual contributor role and the day-to-day procurement focal point for assigned requests. The officer follows approved category strategies and procurement procedures. Category strategy, exception approvals and specialist risk acceptance remain with the responsible managers and authorized functions.
 The role reports to the Senior Global Procurement Manager, Fundraising and Marketing Categories, who sets priorities and provides guidance and oversight. The officer also maintains a strong working relationship with Mass Marketing teams and Regional Supply Chain Directors in relevant markets.
 Key Responsibilities 
 A. Procurement Planning and Market Research 
 Collect and maintain spend, supplier and market information to support procurement planning, updating it as requests and campaign plans change.
 Prepare and update procurement plans for assigned requests in line with IRC standard operating procedures and agreed priorities.
 Conduct market research and identify potential suppliers, pricing benchmarks and opportunities for consolidation for the manager's review.
 Provide sourcing data and supplier information to support the manager's development of fundraising and marketing category strategies.
 Maintain approved supplier lists and framework agreement records, and support supplier onboarding and use of existing agreements.
 Compile supporting documentation for justified waiver or single-source requests and route them for the required approvals; the officer does not approve exceptions.
 Coordinate scheduled performance reviews for assigned suppliers, gathering business-owner feedback and recording agreed follow-up actions.
 B. Sourcing Execution and Contract Administration 
 Manage assigned requests for information, quotations and proposals within delegated authority. Prepare tender documents, coordinate bidder communications and evaluation records, and submit award recommendations for approval. Support the manager on complex, high-value or high-risk tenders.
 Agree realistic sourcing timelines with requesters, taking account of campaign dates, contract expiries and required reviews, and escalate likely delays promptly.
 Compare supplier offers on a consistent basis, including total costs, agency fees, media markups, production charges and performance-based pricing where relevant, with technical input from External Relations.
 Identify and document opportunities for cost savings, improved service and procurement efficiency for discussion with the manager and business owners.
 Execute assigned sourcing activities in line with the approved category strategy and the manager's guidance.
 Help business teams prepare clear scopes of work, deliverables and evaluation criteria; business owners remain responsible for technical requirements and evaluation input.
 Negotiate pricing and commercial terms for assigned procurements within agreed parameters, escalating non-standard terms and material issues to the manager and Legal as appropriate.
 Prepare contract and statement-of-work drafts using approved templates, coordinate Legal review and authorized signature, and maintain executed agreements and amendment records.
 Coordinate inclusion of clauses approved by the relevant specialists for data protection, safeguarding, ethical fundraising and fraud prevention. Refer non-standard provisions to the responsible reviewers.
 Handle day-to-day procurement communications with assigned suppliers and coordinate with business owners on delivery and service issues.
 Support requesters with procurement intake forms and purchase requisitions, and create and track purchase orders in Integra as assigned and authorized, maintaining segregation of duties.
 Provide procurement documentation and follow up on payment-related queries through ServiceNow as needed; business owners and Finance retain responsibility for service acceptance and payment authorization.
 C. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation 
 Collect supplier information and coordinate required due diligence and screening with the responsible functions, including conflicts of interest, supplier conduct, data protection, sanctions and anti-terrorism checks, financial viability and applicable donor requirements.
 Track required clearances from Information Security, Data Protection, the Office of General Counsel, Risk and Compliance, and Finance before the applicable award or commitment stage. Escalate outstanding reviews; specialist assessment and risk acceptance remain with authorized functions.
 Ensure procurement files are complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements.
 Track and follow up on missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews.
 Record supplier performance issues, refer material concerns to the manager and business owner, and follow up on agreed corrective actions.
 D. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support 
 Provide procurement guidance on assigned requests and refer category strategy or supplier selection decisions beyond delegated authority to the manager.
 Coordinate procurement actions with requesters and relevant review teams, providing clear status updates and identifying blockers.
 Confirm that business owners have provided required specifications, evaluation input and service acceptance documentation at the relevant stages.
 Provide practical, responsive procurement support to External Relations teams.
 Follow up on outstanding actions to keep requests progressing within agreed timelines and required controls.
 Help stakeholders use approved procurement routes and flag unauthorized commitments or purchasing outside agreed procedures to the manager.

 This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.  
 This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised. 
 Job Overview:  The Senior Core Services Caseworker delivers trauma-informed support to refugee clients during their resettlement and post-resettlement periods, as well as to other eligible immigrant populations, including Cuban, Haitian, and Ukrainian clients. The Caseworker is responsible for promoting a positive resettlement experience and helping clients achieve self-sufficiency. This role involves close collaboration with clients, internal teams, and external partners to create individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients with a range of financial, medical, social, and vocational resources in alignment with program guidelines and client eligibility criteria.
 Major Responsibilities: 
The Senior Core Services Caseworker plays a critical role in ensuring that clients successfully transition to life in their new community and achieve self-sufficiency. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
 Client Intake, Assessment & Planning 
 Conduct comprehensive intake services to assess individual and family needs, including housing, health, education, employment, and social services.
 Develop tailored self-sufficiency plans in collaboration with clients, outlining specific goals, timelines, and action steps to achieve self-reliance.
 Identify immediate needs and prioritize services such as securing housing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing medical services.
 Pre- and Post-Arrival Coordination 
 Ensure clients receive essential services upon arrival, including temporary or permanent housing, access to nutritious food, healthcare, and transportation support.
 Coordinate with internal departments and external service providers to facilitate timely delivery of services and resources.
 Provide ongoing orientation to clients on accessing services in their new community, including healthcare systems, public benefits, financial literacy, and transportation.
 Direct Support, Advocacy & Case Management 
 Offer individualized support to clients, ensuring they receive appropriate referrals to community resources such as schools, legal services, and mental health providers.
 Advocate on behalf of clients to help them overcome barriers in accessing services and exercising their rights.
 Monitor and assess client progress regularly, addressing challenges and updating self-sufficiency plans as needed to ensure successful outcomes.
 Facilitate connection to employment services in coordination with the employment team to support clients in gaining job readiness skills and securing suitable employment.
 Assist clients in completing critical documents, including benefit renewals, address change notifications (AR-11 forms), and other legal documentation.
 Home Visits & Community Integration 
 Conduct home visits to assess living conditions, provide follow-up services, and ensure clients are safe and stable.
 Help clients build community connections by facilitating their engagement with local services, cultural events, and educational workshops.
 Financial Assistance & Budgeting 
 Plan, request, and track direct assistance funds, ensuring expenditures are aligned with program requirements and client needs.
 Assist clients with financial planning, helping them budget for rent, utilities, and other essential expenses.
 Manage Matching Grant Program client finances, ensuring compliance with program guidelines and accurate reporting of funds disbursed.
 Documentation & Reporting 
 Maintain detailed case files and documentation for each client interaction, ensuring accuracy and compliance with program standards.
 Enter data into client databases and assist with program tracking and reporting requirements.
 Prepare reports as required by internal leadership and external funders.
 Collaboration & Relationship Building 
 Collaborate with internal teams such as Employment, Health, and Youth Services to ensure seamless service delivery.
 Build and maintain relationships with external service providers, such as healthcare organizations, schools, and community groups, to expand the support network for clients.
 Participate in cross-departmental meetings and community coalitions to strengthen partnerships and identify additional resources for clients.
 Client Education & Workshops 
 Develop and facilitate educational workshops for clients on topics such as navigating healthcare, job readiness, budgeting, tenant rights, and U.S. culture.
 Encourage and support client participation in group activities that promote learning, self-advocacy, and social integration.
 Supervision & Volunteer Engagement 
 Train, supervise, and coordinate the activities of interns and volunteers, ensuring they understand program goals and the needs of clients.
 Provide ongoing feedback and support to volunteers to maximize their contribution to client success.
 Compliance, Ethical Standards & Safety 
 Ensure compliance with all organizational policies, program guidelines, and ethical standards in the delivery of services.
 Maintain confidentiality and uphold the highest professional standards in all client interactions.
 Participate in ongoing training and professional development to stay current on best practices and program regulations.
 Transportation & Logistics 
 Use a personal, insured vehicle or public transportation to transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
 Assist clients in learning how to use public transportation to access essential services independently.
 Other Responsibilities 
 Support special projects and initiatives that enhance client services and improve program outcomes.
 Perform other duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of clients and the organization.
 Job Requirements: 
 Preference:  Bilingual or multilingual candidates are strongly preferred. Proficiency in additional languages relevant to the client population is a plus.
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.
 Work Experience: 
 Required: Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in the human services field.
 Preferred: Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant communities.
 Demonstrated Skills & Competencies: 
 Relationship Building & Networking: Proven ability to build and maintain effective internal and external relationships through strong diplomacy, communication, and collaboration skills.
 Cross-Cultural Communication: Demonstrated success in working and communicating in a multicultural environment.
 Initiative & Problem-Solving: Self-motivated with excellent problem-solving abilities, capable of managing multiple tasks, setting priorities, and meeting deadlines efficiently.
 Detail-Oriented: Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
 Digital & Technical Skills: Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and skilled in using the internet and digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving.

offres.titre: Oficial en Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y AHS
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Contexto: 
 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas.  
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos.  
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Zulia, Lara, Falcón, Táchira y Apure, trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria,  Medios de Vida y ASH. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales. 
 Descripción general del trabajo:  
 El/la Oficial de Seguridad Alimentaria/Medios de Vida/Agua, Saneamiento e higiene (SA/MdV/ASH) es responsable de gestionar, supervisar e implementar la estrategia del programa en el estado de Táchira, en articulación con la Gerencia. Así mismo, será responsable de coordinar e implementar por medio de un enfoque integrado con el personal de finanzas, movilización comunitaria, programas, rendición de cuentas y suministros de CIR-VE; para asegurar la correcta ejecución de actividades frente al marco lógico, el cronograma de trabajo y el plan presupuestal. Se espera que el Oficial viaje frecuentemente a campo para supervisar que se cumpla con la línea técnica en las actividades del programa. Además, será responsable de la administración general y del funcionamiento de la implementación en Táchira. Finalmente, será responsable principal de representar al CIR-VE en territorio frente a otras organizaciones de la cooperación, aliados estratégicos, estructura de gobierno, comunidades y cualquier estructura de coordinación.
 Responsabilidades principales: 
 Supervisa y asegura la correcta gestión de las actividades en terreno, incluyendo la verificación de estándares en SA/MDV/ASH según las intervenciones, con conocimiento del plan de acciones, mapa de actores locales y generación de reportes que reflejen avances en las actividades de medios de vida y/o seguridad alimentaria.
 Armoniza la línea técnica de la organización con los procesos operativos, garantizando que las metodologías incluyan criterios en Seguridad Alimentaria/Medios de Vida/ Agua, saneamiento e higiene y que la ejecución del programa cumpla con estándares internacionales (MERS, Sphere, otras).
 Diseña un plan de acompañamiento operativo que integre acciones en SA/MDV/ASH en los planes de trabajo locales, alineado con metas y cronograma general de la subvención.
 Asegura y hace seguimiento a la ejecución del presupuesto, verificando que los recursos asignados para SA/MDV/ ASH, se utilicen de manera eficiente y conforme a los objetivos del proyecto.
 Revisa la información de las diferentes actividades en territorio, asegurando que los reportes incluyan indicadores de SA/MDV/ASH. Da seguimiento al contexto y reporta cambios relevantes, incluyendo riesgos que afecten los Seguridad Alimentaria/Medios de Vida, así como incidentes que puedan comprometer las operaciones del proyecto.
 Coordina la adherencia de la línea técnica dentro del equipo, asegurando la aplicación de estándares en SA/MDV/ASH y metodologías participativas para asegurar los aprendizajes y los objetivos del proyecto en la población beneficiaria.
 Coordina con los otros proyectos y áreas de la organización, asegurando la integración, complementariedad, sinergias que puedan asegurar una implementación que busque el mejor uso de los recursos y el mayor beneficio para los beneficiarios.
 Asegurar la implementación de la calidad programática en los proyectos implementados, verificando el cumplimiento de SOPs y herramientas que incluyan componentes en SA/MDV/ASH.
 Garantiza la coordinación interna de acciones, asegurando que las áreas técnicas y operativas integren SA/MDV/ASH en sus compromisos y acuerdos.
 Coordina la agenda en el marco de visitas de donantes, mostrando avances y resultados en materia de SA/MDV/ASH.
 Reconoce medios de comunicación y actores clave, identificando espacios para promover mensajes clave en SA/MDV/ASH que buscan fortalecer la participación comunitaria.
 Responsabilidades de SG- SST: 
 Todos los cargos de supervisión (con personal a cargo) deberán velar por adecuadas condiciones y medio ambiente de trabajo en su ámbito de actuación, departamento, área o programa, analizando los trabajos desarrollados e identificando riesgos potenciales y gestionarán lo necesario para minimizarlos o reducirlos, cumpliendo y cumpliendo los objetivos establecidos en seguridad y salud, vigilando la observancia de las buenas prácticas. De igual manera, deberán participar en la investigación de accidentes de trabajo ocurridos en su respectiva área, departamento o programa, participarán y promoverán la participación de sus supervisados en las actividades de prevención, y promoverán la participación del personal en comités de seguridad y salud, convivencia laboral, seguridad vial y brigadas de emergencia y rendirán cuentas a las autoridades competentes y partes interesadas, periódicamente y/o cuando les sea solicitado. El incumplimiento de las responsabilidades y funciones de seguridad y salud, serán tenidas en cuenta como falta grave, y serán causal de procesos y medidas disciplinarias y/o terminación del contrato de trabajo.
 Requisitos del trabajo: 
 Profesional en ingeniería, ciencias ambientales y naturales, ciencias sociales, gestión del desarrollo o áreas afines psicología, trabajo social o áreas afines.
 Experiencia mínima de 3 años en la gestión y ejecución de proyectos humanitarios, con un enfoque en Seguridad Alimentaria/Medios de Vida/agua, saneamiento e higiene y/o manejo logístico.
 Implementando estrategias y metodologías para medios de vida es deseable en entornos de emergencia; en agua, saneamiento e higiene en comunidad método de barreras múltiples, higiene, saneamiento y en establecimientos de salud asociado a control, integrados a prevención y control de infecciones -P

offres.titre: Oficial Senior de Proyectos - Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y ASH
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Contexto: 
 El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a algunas de las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo, ayudando a las personas afectadas por conflictos, desastres y desplazamiento a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundado en 1933 a petición de Albert Einstein, el IRC trabaja en más de 40 países brindando asistencia en salud, protección, educación, recuperación económica, medios de vida, agua, saneamiento e higiene y fortalecimiento comunitario.
 La situación humanitaria en Venezuela continúa generando importantes necesidades en materia de acceso a servicios básicos, protección, salud, seguridad alimentaria y recuperación económica.
 Adicionalmente, el 24 de junio de 2026 el país fue impactado por dos terremotos de magnitud 7.2 y 7.5, los cuales ocasionaron afectaciones significativas en viviendas, infraestructura pública, establecimientos de salud, sistemas de agua y medios de vida, especialmente en los estados La Guaira, Miranda y Distrito Capital, generando nuevas necesidades humanitarias y de recuperación temprana.
 Como consecuencia de estos eventos, fue declarado Estado de Emergencia nacional para coordinar la respuesta y recuperación de las zonas afectadas.
 En Venezuela, el IRC desarrolla intervenciones humanitarias a través de operaciones directas y mecanismos de colaboración con organizaciones locales. Actualmente fortalece acciones relacionadas con protección, salud, educación, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH), seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida, transferencias monetarias, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitarias. El IRC mantiene presencia programática en Caracas, Maracaibo y San Cristóbal, apoyando intervenciones en Distrito Capital, Miranda, La Guaira, Zulia y Táchira.
 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El Oficial Senior de Proyectos será responsable de coordinar, implementar y supervisar la ejecución de proyectos de asistencia humanitaria, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de resiliencia comunitaria en el estado Zulia, en las áreas de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y Transferencias Monetarias (CASH-PTM).
 Será responsable de asegurar la correcta gestión del ciclo de proyecto, el cumplimiento de estándares programáticos, presupuestarios y operativos, así como de facilitar la implementación de los lineamientos técnicos definidos y aprobados por la Gerencia del Programa y los asesores técnicos correspondientes.
 El cargo tendrá un papel clave en la implementación de actividades orientadas a mejorar el acceso de los hogares vulnerables a servicios esenciales, agua segura, medios de vida sostenibles, asistencia alimentaria y mecanismos de transferencias monetarias, contribuyendo a la recuperación y resiliencia de las comunidades afectadas por crisis humanitarias y desastres naturales.
 Además, el Oficial Senior supervisará las actividades diarias del personal de campo bajo su responsabilidad, incluidos oficiales, asistentes y auxiliares de proyecto, asegurando la adecuada ejecución de las actividades programáticas y el cumplimiento de los procedimientos operativos, estándares de calidad y lineamientos técnicos establecidos para los proyectos.
 Responsabilidades principales :
 Contribuir al desarrollo de la estrategia programática de WASH, Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y CASH-PTM con integración a otros sectores claves como salud y protección.
 Participar en evaluaciones multisectoriales, análisis de necesidades y elaboración de propuestas de proyectos.
 Promover mejoras técnicas e innovaciones que fortalezcan la calidad y alcance de las intervenciones.
 Garantizar la calidad técnica de los programas bajo su responsabilidad.
 Asegurar la aplicación de estándares humanitarios internacionales y lineamientos institucionales.
 Diseñar e implementar actividades que respondan a la teoría de cambio y marco lógico de los proyectos de relacionadas con WASH, recuperación económica, fortalecimiento de medios de vida, seguridad alimentaria, CASH-PTM y recuperación temprana.

offres.titre: Oficial Senior de Proyectos - Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y ASH
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Contexto:
 El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a algunas de las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo, ayudando a las personas afectadas por conflictos, desastres y desplazamiento a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundado en 1933 a petición de Albert Einstein, el IRC trabaja en más de 40 países brindando asistencia en salud, protección, educación, recuperación económica, medios de vida, agua, saneamiento e higiene y fortalecimiento comunitario.
 La situación humanitaria en Venezuela continúa generando importantes necesidades en materia de acceso a servicios básicos, protección, salud, seguridad alimentaria y recuperación económica.
 Adicionalmente, el 24 de junio de 2026 el país fue impactado por dos terremotos de magnitud 7.2 y 7.5, los cuales ocasionaron afectaciones significativas en viviendas, infraestructura pública, establecimientos de salud, sistemas de agua y medios de vida, especialmente en los estados La Guaira, Miranda y Distrito Capital, generando nuevas necesidades humanitarias y de recuperación temprana.
 Como consecuencia de estos eventos, fue declarado Estado de Emergencia nacional para coordinar la respuesta y recuperación de las zonas afectadas.
 En Venezuela, el IRC desarrolla intervenciones humanitarias a través de operaciones directas y mecanismos de colaboración con organizaciones locales. Actualmente fortalece acciones relacionadas con protección, salud, educación, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH), seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida, transferencias monetarias, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitarias. El IRC mantiene presencia programática en Caracas, Maracaibo y San Cristóbal, apoyando intervenciones en Distrito Capital, Miranda, La Guaira, Zulia y Táchira.
 Descripción general del trabajo:
 El Oficial Senior de Proyectos será responsable de coordinar, implementar y supervisar la ejecución de proyectos de asistencia humanitaria, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de resiliencia comunitaria en el estado Táchira, en las áreas de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y Transferencias Monetarias (CASH-PTM).
 Será responsable de asegurar la correcta gestión del ciclo de proyecto, el cumplimiento de estándares programáticos, presupuestarios y operativos, así como de facilitar la implementación de los lineamientos técnicos definidos y aprobados por la Gerencia del Programa y los asesores técnicos correspondientes.
 El cargo tendrá un papel clave en la implementación de actividades orientadas a mejorar el acceso de los hogares vulnerables a servicios esenciales, agua segura, medios de vida sostenibles, asistencia alimentaria y mecanismos de transferencias monetarias, contribuyendo a la recuperación y resiliencia de las comunidades afectadas por crisis humanitarias y desastres naturales.
 Además, el Oficial Senior supervisará las actividades diarias del personal de campo bajo su responsabilidad, incluidos oficiales, asistentes y auxiliares de proyecto, asegurando la adecuada ejecución de las actividades programáticas y el cumplimiento de los procedimientos operativos, estándares de calidad y lineamientos técnicos establecidos para los proyectos.

offres.titre: Oficial en Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 CONTEXTO IRC: 
 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas.  
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos.  
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Zulia, Lara, Falcón, Táchira y Apure, trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales.
 Descripción general del trabajo:  
 El/la Oficial de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene ASH, es responsable de gestionar, supervisar e implementar la estrategia del programa en el Estado Zulia o cualquier otro territorio del país, en articulación con la Gerencia. Así mismo, será responsable de coordinar e implementar por medio de un enfoque integrado con el personal de finanzas, movilización comunitaria, programas, rendición de cuentas y suministros de CIR-VE; para asegurar la correcta ejecución de actividades frente al marco lógico, el cronograma de trabajo y el plan presupuestal. Se espera que el Oficial viaje frecuentemente a campo para supervisar que se cumpla con la línea técnica en las actividades del programa. Además, será responsable de la administración general y del funcionamiento de la implementación. Finalmente, será responsable principal de representar al CIR-VE en territorio frente a otras organizaciones de la cooperación, aliados estratégicos, estructura de gobierno, comunidades y cualquier estructura de coordinación.  
   Responsabilidades principales: 
 Acompañar y brindar apoyo al plan de trabajo diseñado por el Gerente de Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y ASH y/o el Oficial Senior de Proyectos.
 Liderar y acompañar la implementación de actividades formativas en metodologías seleccionadas del CIR-VE dirigidas a las comunidades focalizadas.
 Acompañar y brindar apoyo a los procesos y estrategias de prevención desarrolladas en Comunidades por el Gerente de Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y ASH y/o el Oficial Senior de Proyectos.
 Liderar y acompañar y apoyar en los procesos de diagnósticos participativos comunitarios en las zonas de intervención identificadas.
 Apoyar y garantizar el cumplimiento de los procesos internos de compra y adquisiciones propios del programa; realizar planes de compra, creación de solicitudes de compra y demás elementos propios del proceso institucional, esto bajo el liderazgo del Gerente e Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de vida y ASH y/o el Oficial Senior de Proyectos.
 Reconocer medios de comunicación, espacios de participación y en general e identificar los actores claves en los territorios de intervención para el desarrollo de las actividades mandatarias de la organización.
 Apoyar al Gerente de Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida y ASH y/o Oficial Senior de Proyectos en los procesos de identificación de necesidades de las comunidades focalizadas.
 Desarrollar acciones de sensibilización en las Comunidades sobre los Programas e intervenciones del CIR-VE.
 •    Acompañar en los procesos de seguimiento, monitoreo y evaluación (Intercambios de Experiencia y Comunidades de Aprendizaje) de los impactos y cambios en las comunidades para identificar impacto de las intervenciones del CIR-VE
 •    Gestionar necesidades adicionales y/o complementarias de los clientes identificando oferta de servicios existentes y posibles organizaciones a brindar respuesta (mapeo de servicios).
 •    Apoyar la implementación de la Estrategia de Movilización Comunitaria del CIR-VE en terreno, asegurando la documentación asociada, la socialización de los avances, y brindando sugerencias para los desafíos que emerjan.
 Entregar reportes semanales de las actividades realizadas.
 Contribuir al desarrollo de la dirección estratégica del programa de agua saneamiento e higiene
 Coordinar con personal de las áreas de CIR-VE (ASH, Salud, Protección, MEAL) a nivel de campo.
 Contribuir a la construcción de la planificación del programa salvaguardando el cumplimiento y alcance de metas, el uso eficiente de los recursos y el cumplimiento de los procedimientos institucionales.
 Brindar insumos y recomendaciones extraídos de su experiencia en campo y la interacción con los clientes para hacer mejoras programáticas.
 Responsabilidades de SG- SST: Para cargos de supervisión (con personal a cargo) 
 Todos los cargos de supervisión (es decir, con personal a cargo) deberán velar por adecuadas condiciones y medio ambiente de trabajo en su ámbito de actuación, departamento, área o programa, analizando los trabajos que se desarrollan e identificando posibles riesgos potenciales y gestionarán lo necesario para proceder a minimizarlos o reducirlos, cumpliendo y haciendo cumplir los objetivos establecidos en seguridad y salud, vigilando la observancia de las buenas prácticas. De igual manera, deberán participar en la investigación de accidentes de trabajo ocurridos en su respectiva área, departamento o programa, participarán y promoverán la participación de sus supervisados en las actividades de prevención, y rendirán cuentas a las autoridades competentes y partes interesadas, periódicamente y/o cuando les sea solicitado. El incumplimiento de las responsabilidades y funciones de seguridad y salud, serán tenidas en cuenta como falta grave, y serán causal de procesos y medidas disciplinarias y/o terminación del contrato de trabajo. 
 Requisitos del trabajo: 
 Profesional en ingeniería, ciencias ambientales y naturales, ciencias sociales, gestión del desarrollo o áreas afines psicología, trabajo social o áreas afines.
 Experiencia mínima de 3 años en la gestión y ejecución de proyectos humanitarios, con un enfoque en ASH y/o manejo logístico.

offres.titre: Asistente de Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Contexto: 
 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas.  
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos.  
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Zulia, Lara, Falcón, Táchira y Apure, trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria,  Medios de Vida y ASH. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales. 
 Descripción general del trabajo:  
 El/la Asistente SA/MDV será responsable de apoyar la implementación diaria de las actividades programáticas de Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida en el Estado Zulia y dentro de las áreas geográficas asignadas.
 La posición apoyará la organización, ejecución y seguimiento de actividades comunitarias, registro de participantes, distribución de materiales, levantamiento de información, monitoreo de actividades y acompañamiento a las poblaciones participantes, garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos y estándares de calidad establecidos por la organización.
 Bajo la supervisión directa del Oficial SA/MDV, el/la Asistente contribuirá al cumplimiento de las metas programáticas mediante la ejecución efectiva de actividades en terreno y el fortalecimiento de la relación con comunidades, líderes comunitarios y actores locales.
 Responsabilidades principales: 
 Apoyar la ejecución de actividades de Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida en las comunidades asignadas.
 Participar en procesos de focalización, identificación y registro de participantes.
 Brindar apoyo logístico y operativo durante la implementación de actividades programáticas.
 Apoyar jornadas informativas, sesiones educativas, capacitaciones y actividades comunitarias.
 Realizar visitas de seguimiento a participantes y comunidades beneficiarias.
 Verificar el cumplimiento de los criterios de participación establecidos para cada actividad.
 Apoyar procesos de entrega de asistencia y distribución de materiales cuando corresponda.
 Apoyar la organización de actividades relacionadas con medios de vida y recuperación económica.
 Realizar seguimiento básico a participantes de programas productivos o de generación de ingresos.
 Apoyar actividades de capacitación y fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitarias.
 Recopilar información relevante sobre necesidades y avances de los participantes
 Apoyar las actividades de promoción de higiene en comunidades e instituciones.
 Participar en actividades de sensibilización sobre prácticas seguras de higiene y saneamiento.
 Apoyar procesos de distribución de insumos de higiene cuando sean requeridos.
 Realizar seguimiento a actividades comunitarias relacionadas con agua, saneamiento e higiene.
 Contribuir a la identificación y reporte de necesidades observadas durante las visitas de campo
 Completar formularios, registros y herramientas de seguimiento utilizadas por el programa.
 Recopilar información de campo de manera oportuna y precisa.
 Mantener actualizados los registros de participantes y actividades.
 Presentar reportes periódicos al Oficial SAMDV
 Reportar incidentes, desafíos y necesidades identificadas durante la implementación de actividades.
 Mantener relaciones respetuosas y efectivas con comunidades y participantes.
 Apoyar la organización de reuniones comunitarias y actividades participativas.
 Promover la participación equitativa de mujeres, hombres, adolescentes y otros grupos vulnerables.
 Difundir información sobre servicios y actividades disponibles.
 Apoyar los mecanismos de retroalimentación y rendición de cuentas hacia las comunidades.

 Todos los cargos de supervisión (con personal a cargo) deberán velar por adecuadas condiciones y medio ambiente de trabajo en su ámbito de actuación, departamento, área o programa, analizando los trabajos desarrollados e identificando riesgos potenciales y gestionarán lo necesario para minimizarlos o reducirlos, cumpliendo y cumpliendo los objetivos establecidos en seguridad y salud, vigilando la observancia de las buenas prácticas. De igual manera, deberán participar en la investigación de accidentes de trabajo ocurridos en su respectiva área, departamento o programa, participarán y promoverán la participación de sus supervisados en las actividades de prevención, y promoverán la participación del personal en comités de seguridad y salud, convivencia laboral, seguridad vial y brigadas de emergencia y rendirán cuentas a las autoridades competentes y partes interesadas, periódicamente y/o cuando les sea solicitado. El incumplimiento de las responsabilidades y funciones de seguridad y salud, serán tenidas en cuenta como falta grave, y serán causal de procesos y medidas disciplinarias y/o terminación del contrato de trabajo.

 Profesional o Técnico Superior Universitario (TSU) en ingeniería, ciencias ambientales y naturales, ciencias sociales, gestión del desarrollo o áreas afines psicología, trabajo social, nutrición o áreas afines.

 Experiencia en trabajo directo con comunidades.
 Deseable experiencia en Seguridad Alimentaria, Medios de Vida.

offres.titre: Managing Attorney, Detention and Deportation Defense Initiative (DDDI)
offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 IRC BACKGROUND: 
 The IRC’s Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) department creates opportunities for refugees and other vulnerable migrants to survive and thrive in the US. RAI serves nearly 50,000 individuals each year in the US through a portfolio of programs aimed at achieving outcomes in five impact areas: Health, Safety, Economic Wellbeing, Education, and Power.
 IRC seeks a Managing Attorney to lead its role as the statewide coordinating entity for NJ’s Detention and Deportation Defense Initiative. DDDI promotes due process, family unity, and access to justice by providing legal representation to low-income New Jersey residents. The DDDI Coordination Entity is responsible for statewide referral coordination, provider communication, technical assistance, programmatic reporting, quality assurance, and other statewide coordination activities.
 JOB OVERVIEW:  
 The Managing Attorney will coordinate IRC’s implementation of the DDDI project in New Jersey, in partnership with the NJ Office of New Americans (ONA) by establishing and managing a centralized public facing detention and deportation legal services referral hotline and intake system; administering referral protocols and coordinating referrals among participating legal services providers; maintaining reporting database, tools, forms, templates and guidance for providers; collecting, analyzing and reporting aggregate programmatic and performance data; monitoring provider performance; and identifying gaps, needs and opportunities to strengthen the statewide detention and deportation defense network.
 The Managing Attorney will bring not only legal expertise and a passion for this area of work, but also a strategic mindset and vision for enhancing access to legal assistance for immigrants in New Jersey through the DDDI network. The position will work in close collaboration with a network of legal services partners across the state and will coordinate regular legal trainings for the DDDI network provided by IRC’s Legal Services Technical Unit (TU). 
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:  
 Oversee a team of legal intake specialists who will gather referral information from individuals in detention or at risk of detention in New Jersey and ensure swift and effective referrals to the DDDI network of legal services providers. 
 Develop and monitor intake procedures, standard operating procedures, reporting to ONA, and coordination and collaboration with participating DDDI providers.  
 Create and maintain a communication strategy to develop and maintain strong relationships with participating DDDI provider agencies, as well as other nonprofit legal providers, community-based organizations, and the private bar.
 Ensure program data is collected consistently, managed appropriately and reported timely to ONA.
 Actively co-facilitate and support contract management, including developing/implementing monitoring & evaluation plans. 
 Work with IRC’s IT and data teams to ensure the centralized intake and referral system is adapted to the DDDI network needs; ensure timely updates and adaptations to meet data collection and reporting needs. 
 Establish, maintain and periodically refresh intake, referral, data collection, and reporting protocols and policies. 
 Coordinate with IRC’s Legal Services Technical Unit to provide monthly trainings and technical assistance on removal defense, immigration detention, and related topics to DDDI participating legal services providers. 
 Employ adaptive management techniques to provide regular individual supervision and support; mentor staff, set clear performance expectations and goals, give regular performance feedback, help prioritize workloads, help troubleshoot challenges, and maintain appropriate professional development plans
 Collaborate with other IRC program areas as appropriate to ensure client-centered service. 
 Serve on NY/NJ Management Team and work effectively across programs to further IRC’s mission. Contribute to and support office-wide Strategic Action Plan.
 Serve as a strong advocate for humanitarian immigrants. 
 KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:  
 Position Reports to:  NJ Deputy Director; Position liaises closely with HQ Legal Services Technical Unit.
 Position Directly Supervises:  4 intake specialists, 1 program assistant and interns.
 JOB REQUIREMENTS:  
 Law degree (JD or LLM) from an ABA-accredited U.S. institution and member in good standing of any state bar;
 5 years’ experience or more providing direct representation in immigration court, including experience representing people in immigration detention;
 At least 2 years of program management experience and/or experience coordinating services across a network of organizations;
 Strong understanding of the New Jersey legal services ecosystem and legal needs of New Jersey community members at risk of detention.
 Experience with relevant legal matters including bond proceedings, removal proceedings, appeals, motions to reopen, habeas corpus petitions, and other separate forms of immigration relief or related litigation. 
 Strong legal supervision skills and superb legal judgment; 
 Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills;
 Bilingual in one or more languages preferred (eg, Spanish, French, Arabic);
 Deep commitment to working with humanitarian immigrants;
 Trauma-informed and sensitive listening and communication skills;
 Desire to join a team working to protect due process and immigrant rights; and
 Must have ability to travel frequently in and around the service area to engage with community partners.
 Compensation: (Pay Rate: $95,000-$109,446/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget.  Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements. 
 Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.
 The IRC in South Sudan
 The IRC has worked in South Sudan since 1989, through the decades of conflict that preceded independence in July 2011 and in the years since. The IRC South Sudan program is registered as an international NGO. It is led by a country office in Juba and delivers services through field offices in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Lakes, Unity and Central Equatoria states.
 Through emergency and longer-term programming, the IRC supports people affected by conflict and displacement in areas including health (such as primary health care and community case management of childhood illness), nutrition, environmental health, women’s protection and empowerment, protection, and economic recovery and livelihoods.
 The Malualkon field office
 This position is based in Malualkon, in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State. The field office delivers services close to the communities the IRC serves, including through nutrition centers that the Finance Assistant visits to pay staff. The office works in close coordination with the Juba country office, which receives its cash records, supporting documents and bank information and which provides oversight of field finance.
 Why field finance matters
 Every service the IRC delivers depends on funds being handled responsibly. Donors, government authorities and the people we serve trust the IRC to account for every payment and receipt. In a field setting, where cash is used for many transactions, accurate records, clear authorization and complete documentation protect that trust. They also support the IRC’s commitment to fiscal integrity, which is one of the policies every IRC worker must follow.
 Main purpose of this job
 Under the supervision of the Finance Officer (FO), the Finance Assistant handles all cash payments and records transactions in the cash book daily.
 In practice, the Finance Assistant is the first line of control over cash in the Malualkon field office. The role ensures that every payment and receipt is authorized at the right level, supported by complete documents, recorded promptly in the correct currency, and traceable from the cash book to its supporting document and on to the Juba office. The Finance Assistant also keeps the field office’s banking, filing and statutory payment obligations on schedule.
 How this role contributes
 Safeguards funds: strong cash controls reduce the risk of loss, error and misuse of IRC and donor resources.
 Enables program delivery: staff and field activities, including those at nutrition centers, are paid accurately and on time.
 Supports compliance: payments follow the IRC delineation of authority, and documents are stamped, filed and archived in line with IRC and donor requirements.
 Keeps records audit-ready: well-organized, sequential and scanned records allow the FO, the Juba finance team, donors and auditors to verify transactions quickly.
 Supports the Juba office: timely, complete cash records and supporting documents allow the country office to close its books and report to donors on schedule.
 Scope of the role
 The Finance Assistant works under the direct supervision of the FO and works closely with the Field Coordinator (FC). The role has no decision-making authority. Any exception, such as a missing approval, a cash difference or a request outside approved limits, is referred to the FO.
 Key responsibilities
 Each responsibility below is followed by a short explanation of what it involves in day-to-day work.
 Cash and bank payment processing
 Maintain both the SSP and USD cash books within the set limits and take responsibility for any cash differences that arise.
 Keep a separate cash book for each currency and record every receipt and payment daily. Keep the cash balance within the limit set for the office. Because the Finance Assistant is accountable for any difference between the cash book and the cash on hand, compare the two regularly and raise any difference with the FO promptly.
 Ensure that all cash payments are properly supported and duly authorized, in line with the IRC delineation schedule, before disbursement.
 Before releasing any cash, check that the payment has the required supporting documents and the required approvals. The delineation schedule sets out who may approve which type and amount of expenditure. Do not release a payment if documents or approvals are incomplete.
 Ensure that authorizations on payment requests are within the approved limits in the delineation chart. 
 Check the approver’s name and signature against the delineation chart for the amount requested. Return any request that has been approved by someone who does not hold the authority for that amount and inform the FO.
 Prepare the cash spreadsheets for uploading, ready for review by the FO before they are uploaded to the SUN system. 
 Compile the cash book entries into the cash spreadsheets used for uploading to SUN, the IRC accounting system. Check amounts, currency and coding so the FO can review the spreadsheets without having to correct basic errors. Nothing is uploaded until the FO reviews it.
 Perform cash counts every Friday with the FO and the Field Coordinator (FC), and ensure that all cash count sheets are signed, filed and shared with the Juba main office. 
 Count the physical cash every week with the FO and the FC and compare the result with the cash book balance. All three parties sign the count sheet. File the signed original and send a copy to the Juba main office so the count is independently verified.
 Maintain the receipt book and ensure that authorized receipts are issued when money is received. 
 Keep the receipt book secure and use it in sequence. Issue an official receipt whenever money is received, so there is proof of every receipt, and no money is received without being recorded.
 Ensure that all cash received is duly receipted and coded and promptly banked or recorded in the cash book. 
 Give a receipt for all cash received, assign the correct accounting code, and either bank the money or record it in the cash book without delay. Prompt banking limits the amount of cash held in the office and reduces risk.
 Each month, stamp original documents “PAID” or “RECEIVED BY IRC” (or with the relevant donor stamp) before sending them to Juba. 
 Before the monthly document package goes to Juba, stamp the original documents so they cannot be used to support a second payment. Use the donor-specific stamp where the donor requires it.
 Maintain the bank information file for both SSP and USD accounts. 
 Keep one organized, up-to-date file for each account, including, for example, account details and correspondence with the bank, so that information is easy to find for reviews and audits.
 Act as the bank agent for the field office.

 1. Job Overview 
 The Health Supply Chain Specialist will provide integrated operational and technical leadership to strengthen supply chain performance across four critical health program areas, including but not limited to: Nutrition (with a focus on Ready-to-Use Food, or RUF), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH, covering Family Planning commodities and Postpartum Hemorrhage prevention and treatment supplies), Primary Healthcare (PHC, covering essential medicines and primary-level clinical supplies), and Infection and Disease Prevention and Control (IDPC). Focus will be on IRCs Impact at Scale ‘’go-big’’ designated country programs.
 This is a project management and integration role embedded in Global Supply Chain (GSC), with a Management in Partnership (MIP) reporting line to Deputy Director, Health Unit (HU).  Working in close collaboration with Country Programs, Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs), Global Procurement, Nutrition, SRH and IDPC Technical Leads, and external partners (including UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO, other UN agencies and NGOs, and vendors), the Specialist will cover demand planning, forecasting, procurement coordination, and delivery across all four commodity areas, including essential medicines and IDPC commodities used in IRC health facilities and outbreak response. The role will also act as a key connector between field realities and global supply strategies — ensuring operational challenges are converted into actionable learning, system improvements, and scalable solutions.

 Develop and maintain a consolidated global demand plan covering RUF (Nutrition), IDPC and key SRH commodities (FP and PPH) for Go-big countries.

 Implement forecasts and supply chain plans for FY27 and FY28 for all Go-Big countries in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH.
 Regularly analyze and report on demand, stock, pipeline, and spend data at global and country levels, incorporating stockout data and mitigation actions.

 In alignment with country scale plans, support short-, medium-, and long-term improvement activities anchored to each country's operational profile and risk level .

 2.3 RUF SOP Implementation and Fraud Risk Management

 Track RUF SOP adoption, compliance gaps, and corrective actions to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including travel to at least one country program.
 2.4 IDPC-Specific Supply Chain Strengthening

 Represent IRC in relevant external supply chain and humanitarian coordination platforms, including the Global Health Cluster and IDPC technical working groups.
 Act as the global focal point for CIK deliveries in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH.
 2.7 Reporting, Data, and Knowledge Management 
 Document best practices and lessons learned to inform future improvements across all commodity areas.
 Produce a data-driven summary report linking supply levels to FY27 and FY28 I@S targets for Nutrition, IDPC and SRH Go-Big countries.
 Maintain an evidence repository (data, reports, learnings) for handover to Nutrition, SRH, IDPC and GSC teams.
 Lead the integration of Impact at Scale (I@S) priorities and core indicators into the Global Pharma Indicator (GPI) Dashboard, in collaboration with relevant I@S Leads, the Health Unit/Pharma Specialist, and Global Supply Chain teams. Ensure the dashboard tracks key pharmaceutical and nutrition supply chain performance indicators aligned with I@S objectives, enabling progress monitoring, gap identification, and evidence-based decision-making.

 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El IRC busca un auxiliar de salud que se encargue de brindar soporte a la ejecución del programa de salud en Ipiales, Samaniego y Cumbitara.
 Responsabilidades: 
 Administrar y mantener actualizadas las agendas de los médicos, enfermeras y otros profesionales de salud, garantizando un flujo adecuado de clientes.
 Organizar los consultorios y espacios de atención clínica, asegurando condiciones adecuadas de limpieza, disponibilidad de insumos y privacidad.
 Implementar la estrategia de focalización de población priorizada, captando activamente clientes para todos los servicios de salud: SSR, salud mental, ITS, planificación familiar, controles prenatales, IVE, entre otros.
 Asignar citas médicas, hacer seguimiento a inasistencias y reorganizar agendas cuando sea necesario.
 Realizar remisiones internas y externas, asegurando el diligenciamiento correcto de formatos, la trazabilidad y la continuidad del tratamiento.

 Elaborar los ítems de Forecasts (PIF) de medicamentos e insumos médicos en coordinación con farmacia y el oficial senior de salud.
 Apoyar auditorías de cuentas médicas, organizando y entregando los soportes requeridos por las áreas de calidad, finanzas y MEAL.
 Coordinar la logística de actividades clínicas y comunitarias, incluyendo espacios, materiales, recursos y transporte.
 Establecer comunicación oportuna y efectiva con las áreas de finanzas y operaciones para la ejecución del programa de salud.
 Atender a los clientes del programa de salud con enfoque humanitario, garantizando orientación, trato digno y seguimiento a sus necesidades.
 Apoyar las líneas de atención, canalizando inquietudes, gestionando solicitudes y fortaleciendo el vínculo con la comunidad.
 Apoyar técnicamente los procesos del programa de salud, especialmente el trámite y la organización física y digital del archivo del programa.
 Diligenciar de manera oportuna y precisa las bases de datos y herramientas delegadas por el equipo de MEAL, asegurando el control, seguimiento y trazabilidad de las actividades del proyecto, conforme a los indicadores establecidos.

 Apoyar las acciones relacionadas con la atención de Infecciones de Transmisión Sexual (ITS), incluyendo la identificación y captación de personas con necesidades de atención, el apoyo en la toma de pruebas rápidas autorizadas (cuando aplique), el registro oportuno de la información y la remisión inmediata al personal clínico para la interpretación, consejería y manejo, de acuerdo con los protocolos institucionales.
 Cumplir con las demás funciones que le sean asignadas por su supervisión inmediata, de acuerdo con las necesidades del programa.

 Las funciones del cargo se desarrollarán principalmente bajo modalidad extramural, en el marco de las actividades programadas en terreno.

offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Please note this is an evergreen position. We accept applications on an ongoing basis to build a talent pipeline for roles that open regularly. Because this posting may not reflect a current opening, we may not contact every applicant. If your background aligns with an open need, our team will reach out. We also encourage you to visit our careers page to explore other opportunities. 
 BACKGROUND: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. At work in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities to provide humanitarian aid to those in need. The IRC in Atlanta office was established in 1979 and has resettled over 30,000 refugees from more than 65 countries into the Greater Atlanta area. Serving over 5,000 individuals annually, we provide integration support including casework, education, healthcare navigation, and school enrollment services.
 SCOPE OF ADULT EDUCATION INTERN WORK: The IRC’s Adult Education Intern assists refugee and immigrant adults in ESL classes to develop the language skills critical for success. The classes aim to build vocabulary and communication skills, convey skills necessary for the American workforce, and impart information about integral life skills and systems so that clients can be successful and productive members of their communities, that they can be civically engaged, and so that they can pursue career pathways of their choice. Please note that all internship positions are unpaid. 
 These classes meet regularly three days per week, Tuesday through Thursday, for 3-hour class sessions, with both in-person and online class options, and offer instruction to adult students at varying levels of English proficiencies, from Basic to Advanced. Year-round classes operate with rolling enrollment and new students are oriented and placed into classes and levels weekly. Classes are multi-level meaning multiple levels will be represented within a single class and interns and other class assistants allow for multiple breakout groups to separate students by their proficiency level. Instruction is focused on developing literacy, comprehension, and confidence to apply towards real world situations including dealing with housing issues, shopping, the K-12 public school system, public transportation, employment, healthcare, and other daily life skills.
 Adult Education interns work under class lead instructors and other IRC Adult Education staff to effectively engage with prospective and current immigrant and refugee clients. This can include a variety of ongoing activities such as:
 Recruitment and Outreach: providing information about programming, schedule, and expectations around education services.
 Intake and Orientation: working with clients individually to complete enrollment documents, to discuss goals, and schedule a formal proficiency level assessment
 Classroom Support: assisting lead instructors with classroom management activities, following developed curriculum and leading instruction with groups of English language learners.
 Classroom Support is expected to be a primary activity for nearly all Adult Education interns. 
 Retention and Follow-up: conferencing with, surveying, and connecting with current and former participants, assessing goals and identifying appropriate referrals
 Adult Education interns in Spring 2027 will work with both virtual classes and with in-person classes, working with students joining classes through online platforms and with students attending at the IRC in Atlanta’s main office.
 RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 ·       Teaching groups of students in multi-level classes following curriculum developed by lead instructor.
 ·       Assist instructor in developing and implementing multi-level comprehension and literacy activities.
 ·       Supporting outside-of-class functions of the Adult Education program in recruitment and outreach, intake and orientation, classroom support, and retention and follow-up activities.
 ·       Support program activities by researching new curriculum content and preparing educational materials as requested by instructor.
 ·       Submit intern hours on volunteer dashboard.
 ·       Other duties as assigned.
 QUALIFICATIONS : 
 Interns must have
 ·       Strong communication skills: communication between instructors and fellow class assistants before, during, and after classes, and communication with adult Education language learners during classes.
 ·       Availability for at least 9 hours of class time per week .
 ·       An interest in or experience with teaching in generally and teaching ESL specifically.
 ·       An interest in working closely with a diverse population of adults.
 ·       Comfortability in working in a cross-cultural environment, in-person, online, and over the phone, with adult learners, sometimes with little or no English proficiency.
 ·       Comfortability in working with a variable number of students (individually and in groups).
 ·       Ability to work in a collaborative environment and in co-teaching.
 ·       Comfortability in adapting learning activities with limited notice.
 ·       Fluent in spoken and written English. Bi-lingual abilities are not necessary but can be a plus.
 REQUIREMENTS: 
 Must submit intern hours on volunteer portal.
 Must pass a background check.
 Commitment of 9 hours per week for a minimum of 3 consecutive months.
 Must be at least 18 years old.

 About the programme 
 The IRC is to implement the Nourish and Grow: Cash for Nutrition and Youth Livelihoods in Palabek Refugee Settlement in Lamwo District, northern Uganda project. The project will address the challenges of widespread food insecurity and malnutrition in Palabek among the refugees especially among the children young women, young mothers and youth with disabilities.
 The project responds to these challenges through two linked outcomes. First, it will support nutrition and food security for pregnant and breastfeeding women, who will receive four months of cash for nutrition, nutrition education, and screening and referral through existing health facilities. Their households will also be supported to establish kitchen gardens, start income-generating activities and join savings associations. Second, it will strengthen youth livelihoods for young people aged 15-24, at least half of them young women, who will receive one-off start-up capital and training in entrepreneurship and financial literacy, and will join Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs).
 Job Overview 
 The Nutrition and Livelihoods Officer is the lead technical and day-to-day manager on the ground for cash assistance project in Palabek Refugee Settlement. S/he will turn the plan into on-time, accountable delivery by managing the work plan, budget and procurement, tracking progress, flagging risks early, and holding monthly reviews with the finance manager. S/he will supervise and coach volunteers, prepare monthly updates and donor reports, and keep project files audit-ready. Working with participants, community leaders, the Office of the Prime Minister, WFP, health facilities and IRC’s finance, supply chain and MEAL teams, s/he will verify pregnant and breastfeeding women for safe, traceable cash payments, deliver nutrition education, set up kitchen gardens, and coordinate screening and referral of malnourished children and at-risk women. You will also enroll young people aged 15-24, at least half of them young women, and support them to start or expand income-generating activities, run VSLAs and build financial literacy, adapting activities so young mothers and youth with disabilities can take part fully.
 S/he will work with the MEAL team on baselines, endlines and routine data collection, run post-distribution and post-training monitoring, manage community feedback channels, and document lessons for IRC and the donor. Throughout, you will apply IRC’s Way of Work, safeguarding and PSEA policies and the Client Responsiveness approach, reduce risks of fraud, diversion and exclusion through transparent targeting and spot checks, ensure documentation meets IRC and donor requirements, and refer any protection or safeguarding concerns through the right channels.

 Prepare monthly progress updates and donor narrative reports and contribute to the final report. 
 Keep project files complete and audit-ready, including participant lists, payment records and distribution reports.

 Work with community leaders, the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) settlement team, the World Food Programme (WFP) and partners to identify and verify 400 pregnant and breastfeeding women. Prioritize food-insecure households not receiving WFP assistance. 
 Ensure cash payments are accurate, timely, safe and traceable, working with IRC finance and the cash specialist. 
 Plan and deliver nutrition education on dietary diversity, maternal, infant and young child feeding, hygiene and using cash for food. 
 Lead the set-up of kitchen gardens: select households, distribute seeds and tools, run demonstrations and follow up on results. 
 Coordinate screening and referral of acutely malnourished children and at-risk women through existing health facilities, and track whether referrals are completed.

 EXTERNAL RELATIONS AND THE PRIVATE FUNDRAISING FUNCTION 
 The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions, including Private fundraising, under which this role falls. To enable IRC to deliver its organizational commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance its ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.
 Within Private Fundraising sits the Mass Markets unit. This unit is currently made up of seven teams – US, UK, Germany, Sweden, Digital & Remote Markets and our Supporter Journey and Acquisition teams. Mass Market’s primary goal is to increase the number of sustainers we have globally, via targeted and cost effective acquisition and by building meaningful connections with our donors to ensure we can retain them. By increasing our sustainer numbers and capitalizing on cash giving moments we will grow unrestricted revenue for IRC and the people we serve.
