 BACKGROUND 
 Venezuela continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis. Inside the country, millions of people have limited access to food, health care, safe water and other essential services, and needs are most acute among people on the move and returnees, Indigenous communities, women and girls at risk of gender-based violence, and children at risk of acute malnutrition. In 2026, an earthquake affecting La Guaira, Miranda and Caracas added new humanitarian needs. At the same time, more than 7 million refugees and migrants have left Venezuela, making this one of the largest external displacement crises in the world, with Colombia hosting the largest number of them.
 In Colombia, the escalation of the internal armed conflict has deepened humanitarian needs. Disputes between non-state armed groups over territorial control are driving forced displacement, confinement, movement restrictions, the recruitment of children and adolescents, and gender-based violence, particularly in border and Pacific regions such as Norte de Santander and Nariño. The crisis in Catatumbo alone, which began in January 2025, has displaced more than 100,000 people. Mixed migration flows continue in several directions, including Venezuelans in transit and pendular movements across the border, as well as reverse flows of people returning south from Central and North America and returns to Venezuela, which add complexity to the response.
 The IRC is addressing these needs through an integrated, population-based response in Colombia and Venezuela, covering health (including sexual and reproductive health and mental health), protection and women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, multipurpose cash and economic recovery, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and education. The IRC employs a mixed modality, providing lifesaving services directly and with local partners, and in Venezuela a significant share of funds is channeled through local organizations. Activities are financed by a diverse portfolio of donors, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, OCHA-managed pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Latin America and the Caribbean), the Disasters Emergency Committee, UN agencies and private foundations, among others.

 IRC Chad strategy 
 The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 in response to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of Darfur refugees into eastern Chad, starting with the Ouré Cassoni refugee camp. Today, the IRC supports Sudanese refugees and host communities in 14 camps and host villages in the east, and since April 2023 has expanded its response to assist refugees fleeing the conflict in Sudan. Services in the east include health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), economic recovery and development, women’s empowerment and protection. The IRC also works in Guéra province to address malnutrition and in the Lac region to respond to the Boko Haram crisis, with projects in health, nutrition, protection and response to gender-based violence. Across the country, IRC Chad combines humanitarian, nexus and development responses to help the most affected populations exercise their rights with dignity and access quality basic social services that meet their needs.
 IRC Chad’s strategy focuses on three outcome areas: health (nutrition, child health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and climate-resilient WASH), safety (high-impact targeted individual assistance) and economic wellbeing (food security, basic needs, early recovery and resilience). It is underpinned by commitments to gender equality, diversity and inclusion, cash and voucher assistance, and investment in partnerships with relevant ministries and local partners.
 SCOPE OF WORK 
 The Country Director will provide the strategic vision and leadership for the country program with the primary focus on ensuring IRC Chad’s programs meet the expressed needs of the beneficiaries we serve.  S/he is responsible for ensuring the delivery of quality programs, maintaining/expanding donor and government relations, engaging strategic local organizations, fundraising and budget management, security and operations management, and developing a motivated and professional team. 
 Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary leadership abilities who deploys strong communications and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will enjoy developing networks to build partnerships and diversify program resources. Given the operating environment, the Country Director is expected to be attentive to risk management. S/he will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design and deliver responsive, high-quality programs; ensuring efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance and focused, timely reporting; and oversight of financial management and compliance systems.
 Reporting to the Regional Vice President, this position receives support from regional and headquarters staff in the areas of program quality, new business development, safety and security management, finance, operations management, and external affairs. The Country Director is additionally expected to actively participate in defining the IRC’s public advocacy positions.
 SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Leadership and Representation 
 Provide exemplary leadership by fostering a strong team spirit, open communication, and an inclusive and empowering work environment.
 Develop and maintain strategic relationships with: Chad Government authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private); UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups. 
 Position IRC as a key partner for major international donors and seize opportunities to promote IRC’s work.
 Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
 Initiate and sustain strong, mutually beneficial, and authentic partnerships with Chadian organizations.
 Seek out and pursue opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Chad, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.
 Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Development 
 Ensure that the country program’s strategic vision and direction are aligned with the IRC’s strategy to serve populations through responsive, high-quality, and accountable programming, and secure the necessary resources for its implementation.
 Ensure the country program’s alignment with the IRC strategy and the implementation of the strategic action plan.
 Ensure program quality through rigorous design, M&E, and accountability processes, and investments in staff development and partner capacity sharing. 
 Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
 Ensure country program alignment with and involvement in meeting regional objectives.
 Identify opportunities to expand programming and ensure continuous contextual monitoring.
 Oversee the development and submission of competitive, high-quality proposals; lead partnerships with local civil society organizations in line with PEERS standards, lead negotiations with donors; and build relationships with Chad Ministries. 
 Safety Security and Access Management 
 Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
 Oversee the management of all security issues, including appropriate response to emergency situations as they arise.
 Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including trainings and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
 Keep security, evacuation and contingency plans up to date and accessible to country program staff.
 Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety & Security Director on safety security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.
 Staff Performance Management and Development 
 Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
 Provide constructive feedback and counsel on appropriate career paths and professional development for IRC staff.
 Oversee the management, coaching and development of all staff to build a cadre of skilled, committed and motivated personnel.
 Pursue nationalization of senior management positions. 
 Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
 Undertake regular reviews of labor laws, and salary markets in Chad for the purpose of enhancing the competitiveness of the IRC’

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Titre :  Assistant Protection de l’Enfant 
   Département : Protection 
 Grade : 9A 
 Nombre Place : 1 
 Statut Poste : Local 
 Superviseur Direct : Senior Officer Protection de l’Enfant 
 Superviseur Technique : Manager Protection 
 Localisation : Ndele 
 CONTEXT E 
 L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale. Elle a été fondée en 1933, à l’initiative du célèbre physicien Albert Einstein. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC est l’un des leaders mondiaux en matière de secours, de réhabilitation, de protection, de développement post-conflit, de réinsertion et de plaidoyer pour les personnes affectées par les crises. La mission de l’IRC est d’aider les personnes dont les vies et les moyens de subsistance sont détruits par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, se relever et prendre en main leur avenir. 
 IRC est actif en République centrafricaine depuis fin 2006 et dispose d’un bureau principal à Bangui, d’une base à Bocaranga, d’un bureau projet à Ndele, IRC intervient dans plusieurs secteurs. 
 Le programme de gouvernance et renforcement des systèmes à travers le projet « Appui à la société civile en République Centrafricaine » financé par l’Union européenne, est mis en œuvre par IRC en consortium avec les partenaires EEDD, OJLD et OFCA. IRC et ses partenaires ont pour mission de renforcer les OSC centrafricaines en tant qu'acteurs indépendants de bonne gouvernance et de développement au niveau national et contribuer au renforcement d’un espace inclusif, participatif, autonome, indépendant et démocratique promouvant un dialogue ouvert entre les OSC dans les préfectures de Nana-Gribizi, Bangui, Ombela Mpoko, l’Ouham, Lobaye, Nana Mambere, Mambere-Kadei, Sanga Mbaeré, Ouaka ; dont les communes respectives sont Kaga-Bandoro, Bangui et Bimbo Boali, Bossangoa, Mbaïki, Bouar, Berberati, Nola, Bambari, pour une période de trois ans. 
 Le Programme PAF (Protection et autonomisation de la femme) contribue à créer des cadres tant à l’échelle locale que national, de concertation, dialogue, impliquant les femmes et les filles, où leurs voix sont appliquées, où les décisions prises sont centrées sur la satisfaction des leurs besoins primaires, de leurs intérêts stratégiques et où leur protection fait partie intégrante des priorités gouvernementales. Il s’agit ici de renforcer les stratégies de développement du leadership des femmes et des filles, de promouvoir la prévention, la réponse et l’atténuation des risques des VBG/EAS à travers les approches innovantes. Le Programme PAF IRC soutient le mécanisme de la coordination VBG en RCA en collaboration avec UNFPA et les autres acteurs du domaine de responsabilité (AoR VBG). Le programme travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère du Genre et soutient la stratégie Nationale sur la protection et autonomisation de femmes et filles. Dans le cadre de la Protection et Etat de droit ( PRoL), le Programme assure à ce que les personnes sont en mesure d’accéder à la justice et d’exercer leurs droits, Les femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons ont les informations et le soutien nécessaires pour demander justice et y accéder de manière indépendante. Des services de protection de qualité, y compris la gestion de cas/ soutien psychosocial, le monitoring de protection, le renforcement des capacités des acteurs, la documentation civile ainsi que le renforcement du système juridique et des espaces communautaires sûrs et accessibles pour femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons. 
 Le programme Relèvement et Développement Economique (ERD) travaille à faire en sorte que les besoins fondamentaux de survie des personnes que nous servons soient satisfaits et qu’elles disposent d’une combinaison d’actifs et de revenus pour prospérer. Le programme s’assure que les personnes répondent à leurs besoins fondamentaux et protègent leurs moyens de subsistance en cas d’urgence, qu’elles développent leurs moyens de subsistance et se remettent des chocs et afin que les personnes deviennent autonomes et jouissent d’une stabilité économique à long terme. 
 Le programme protection de l’enfant et développement des jeunes (CYPD) répond aux violations de la protection des enfants à travers les approches centrées sur l’enfant, le renforcement de la famille et de la communauté ainsi que le renforcement du système de protection de l’enfance. Le programme renforce les familles et les communautés pour aider à prévenir les violations de la protection de l'enfance et à y répondre lorsqu'elles se produisent à travers des approches " préventives", que " préventives et réactives » adaptées au genre et aux âges. 
 Le programme santé, nutrition et wash organise l’offre des soins curatifs, préventifs et promotionnels avec un focus sur la santé des groupes vulnérables comme le couple mère-enfant, des adolescents et jeunes en appuyant les formations sanitaires existantes, des cliniques mobiles, les sites de soins communautaires ou toute autre structure communautaire pouvant améliorer l’accès et/ ou la qualité des soins de santé, de nutrition ou de l’hygiène individuelle et collective. 
 Le programme Education , donne aux enfants les plus vulnérables un accès au primaire, transition vers le premier cycle et le secondaire.  Tout particulièrement les filles et les enfants affectés par des crises, notamment les déplacés, pour une amélioration de vie dans les zones ciblées par le projet à travers la formation des enseignants, distribution des différentes kits scolaires pédagogiques, récréatifs et dignité, mise en place des groupes Kundukwa et les différents suivis pédagogiques par les Conseillers pédagogiques. 
 IRC en République centrafricaine met actuellement en œuvre son plan stratégique " Stratégie 100", à travers lequel nous visons à fournir le meilleur impact possible pour les garçons, filles, femmes et hommes les plus vulnérables touchés par les crises humanitaires. Dans tout ce que nous faisons, nous nous efforçons de respecter les valeurs fondamentales d’IRC que sont l'intégrité, la responsabilité, le service et l'égalité. 
 Généralités du poste : 
 L’Assistant(e) Protection de l’Enfant joue un rôle clé dans la mise en œuvre des activités de protection de l’enfance. Il/elle est le lien direct entre les enfants vulnérables, leurs familles et les services disponibles. Sa mission est de garantir que chaque enfant identifié bénéficie d’une prise en charge complète, respectueuse et conforme aux standards internationaux de protection. 
 Elle/Il sera sous la supervision directe de l’officier Protection de l’enfance et sera basé (e) dans son lieu d’affectation. Elle/il travaillera en étroite collaboration à l’interne avec les supports de IRC (Logistique, Finance, Administration et les Ressources Humaines) et à l’externe avec les autres acteurs œuvrant dans le domaine de la protection de l’enfant les volontaires, les membres RECOPE et des Clubs des jeunes. Il accompagne le partenaire dans la mise en œuvre des activités du projet. 
 Principales responsabilités : 
 1. Gestion de cas 
 Identifier les enfants victimes ou à risque d’abus, exploitation, négligence ou violence. 
 Documenter chaque cas avec rigueur (fiches, bases de données, rapports).

If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Background/IRC Summary:  
 The IRC has worked in Sudan for decades, delivering life-saving and recovery programmes in health, nutrition, protection, women's protection and empowerment, education, and economic recovery. Today we deliver as a single country programme, providing vital assistance to communities across the country.
 Sudan is experiencing one of the world's largest and most severe humanitarian crises. More than 12 million people have been displaced across all 18 states, around 30 million people need humanitarian assistance, and some 25 million face acute food insecurity — including hundreds of thousands of children with severe acute malnutrition. Most health facilities are no longer fully functional and humanitarian access remains constrained. The IRC has scaled up its response to meet these growing needs.
 We know that we serve communities better when our own teams reflect the diversity of the people we work alongside, and when every colleague is able to do their best work and be themselves at work.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Organizational Background 
 The IRC’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads the organization’s global emergency preparedness and response activities. Its mission is to meet immediate survival needs and reduce the suffering of affected populations during the acute phase of an emergency.
 Response Background 
 The Ministry of Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo officially declared the country’s 17th Ebola virus disease outbreak on 15 May 2026, after confirming cases caused by the Bundibugyo virus species (BDBV) in Ituri Province. The outbreak was initially detected in and around the Mongbwalu, Rwampara and Bunia health zones.
 On 17 May 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) assessed the outbreak as a public health emergency of international concern, owing to the risk of regional spread and the challenging operational context. The IRC is preparing its support to contain the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. The response rests on three complementary pillars: infection prevention and control and WASH (IPC/WASH); risk communication and community engagement (RCCE); and integrated protection, including safeguarding, PSEA, MHPSS, GBV referral mechanisms and protection risk mitigation.
 Scope of the Position 
 The Senior Grant Manager will contribute to overall grants management at IRC DRC. The position reports to the Emergency Programme Lead and is based in Bunia, with occasional trips to field sites as needed. The Senior Grant Manager will work collaboratively with all members of the DRC Country Program, Grants and Partnerships Unit, the Technical Coordinators, the Operations and Finance teams. The IRC DRC portfolio consists mostly of grants from the EU, US DoS, OCHA, Irish Aid and private foundations.
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Proposal and business development: 
 Support the Emergency Program Lead to proactively identify new funding opportunities by monitoring donor strategies, polices and funding trends
 Prepare for and lead Go/No-Go meetings for funding opportunities
 Lead coordination of concept note and proposal development and amendments (including design meetings) working with program staff and ensuring proper review at the HQ level, gathering input from technical coordinators, technical advisors, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) staff, and the Regional Unit.
 Lead and coordinate budget development for newly assigned proposals and amendments, working with program staff, other members of the Grants and Partnerships Unit, the Finance Department and Regional Program and Business Development Units.
 Ensure proper review of new budgets and realignment/modification budgets at both HQ and DRC levels, incorporating all feedback and ensuring that budgets are accurate.
 Coordinate and develop budget narratives, edit proposals, and ensure proper proposal and grant management procedures are followed through clear roles, responsibilities and timelines for each department
 Act as the focal point for in-country donors during the proposal development process, as needed.
 Liaise with IRC New York, UK and Germany grant units in order to ensure proposals meet internal standards, apply IRC’s Outcomes Evidence Framework (OEF), are in line with IRC DRC’s Strategic Action Plan (SAP) and are donor compliant.
 2. Reporting 
 Ensure that reports to donors are submitted on time; that reports are coherent and accurate (quarterly, interim or final reports); and that the internal reporting tracker and OTIS reporting information is up to date.
 Lead Project Cycle Meetings, as well as monthly/regular grants management meetings (BVA meetings) which include representation from each unit (finance, programs, logistics) and ensure proper follow up of issues raised.
 Monitor and support the use of project cycle management tools such as Project Dashboard, Budget vs. Actual (BVA) for the proper monitoring and the successful implementation of programs and early warning in case of obstacles or challenges.
 3. Donor Compliance 
 Work closely with the Response Program Lead and the EmU Finance and Grant Team to support research on donor compliance issues for new opportunities or existing grants, as needed, within the assigned portfolio of IRC DRC.

 Ensure that grants are implemented in compliance with IRC and relevant donor regulations.
 Raise compliance issues early with program staff, the Emergency Program Lead and senior management, and flag any projected inability to meet contractual obligations.
 Maintain and update grant files related to all donor contractual documents, reports and key correspondence are filed consistently in up-to-date shared libraries.
 4. Communication and Information Management 
 Communicate with donors and attend donor meetings in order to share IRC’s accomplishments as well as to stay up to date on the latest donor developments and requirements.
 Distribute to IRC staff all documentation (grant proposals, reports, budget, etc.) related to their specific programs.
 Keep an updated inventory of all communications related to programs/donors and ensure communication and visibility requirements are met.
 5. Management and Capacity Building 
 Provide orientation to Program team members. Topics may include donor compliance rules and regulations, BVA, OTIS, project design, proposal development, budget development, and Grant Opening and Grant Closing meetings.
 6. Administrative/Other 
 Ensure OTIS data is up to date for all assigned new proposals. Secure all OTIS approvals for the assigned new proposals prior to submission to the donor.
 Keep an accurate Grants Filing system on the Shared Drive (Box), OTIS and hardcopy folder.

 Education: BA degree required; master’s degree in accounting, economics, international affairs, social sciences or a STEM field (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) strongly preferred.
 Experience: At least 4 years of experience in program management, grants management and/or proposal/business development and design.

 Excellent interpersonal, cultural and diplomatic skills.

 Strong capacity to mentor and build the capacity of staff.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 CONTEXTO: 
 El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas cuyas vidas y medios de vida se ven afectados por conflictos y desastres para sobrevivir, recuperarse y obtener el control de su futuro. Fundado en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, el IRC trabaja con personas obligadas a huir de la guerra, los conflictos y los desastres y las comunidades anfitrionas que los apoyan, así como con aquellos que permanecen dentro de sus hogares y comunidades. En el trabajo de hoy en más de 40 países y 22 ciudades de EE. UU., Restauramos la seguridad, la dignidad y la esperanza a millones de personas desarraigadas y que luchan por sobrevivir. El IRC lidera el camino del daño al hogar.
 El IRC trabajó en El Salvador entre 1984 y 1992 durante la guerra civil, y se fue con la firma de los acuerdos de paz. En respuesta a la violencia y los peligros en curso en El Salvador, el IRC regresó en 2017 para ayudar a satisfacer las necesidades agudas de comunidades vulnerables como mujeres, niñas, adolescentes, la comunidad LGTBI, las personas desplazadas por la violencia y las personas que regresan al país después deportación. Este programa utiliza enfoques innovadores para ofrecer programación humanitaria, principalmente a través de un enfoque de asociación con organizaciones locales de la sociedad civil, así como con el Gobierno de El Salvador.
 ALCANCE DEL TRABAJO: 
 El/La Gerente/a de proyecto se encargará de asegurar la implementación, seguimiento y monitoreo  oportuno del proyecto ACNUR-IRC, apoyando y guiando al equipo para  el  fortalecimiento  de  capacidades  a  instituciones gubernamentales y organizaciones no gubernamentales nacionales e internacionales dentro del mismo, Por  igual,  estará  encargado/a  de  la  creación  de  alianzas  interinstitucionales  por  medio  de  la participación  en  espacios  estratégicos  de  coordinación, centrándose  inicialmente  en  los municipios priorizados y otros socios estratégicos a nivel nacional,. Basándose en su análisis de la implementación de las actividades a nivel de la comunidad, el gerente apoyará a un mejor desarrollo de intervenciones programáticas seguras y de alta calidad, tomando como base los objetivos propuestos en el proyecto.
 Objetivos del cargo: 
 Ser el punto focal dentro del IRC para el proyecto con el donante, organizaciones claves dentro de este y otro actor relevante que contribuya a la correcta implementación del mismo.
 Participar junto con el Coordinador de Operaciones en la negociación de términos y condiciones con los proveedores seleccionados y coordinar la entrega oportuna de productos y servicios contratados.
 Planear, coordinar, ejecutar y controlar las diferentes tareas operativas y/o administrativas del proyecto hasta la terminación del mismo, asegurando el cumplimiento de fechas de entrega, calidad de los resultados y compromisos adquiridos.
 Anticipar, identificar y evaluar posibles riesgos que puedan afectar el desenvolvimiento del proyecto, y proponer estrategias de mitigación a fin de que se cumplan los objetivos establecidos.
 Asegurar la participación de todas las áreas técnicas y administrativas relacionadas, según el proyecto para la correcta puesta en marcha de acciones.
 Administrar los recursos asignados al proyecto (presupuesto, equipo, recurso humano, etc.), maximizando el uso de estos.
 Establecer mecanismos para el control y balance líneas presupuestarias.
 Apoyar en el desarrollo de documentación aplicable a los procesos requeridos por el donante y el cumplimiento de los tiempos para estos.
 Asistir periódicamente con otros puntos clave dentro del proyecto a las reuniones de seguimiento con el donante para garantizar la correcta implementación de las acciones propuestas.
 Monitorear y evaluar junto al Oficial de M&E los informes requeridos dentro del proyecto, incluyendo el informe final.
 Supervisión y Desarrollo del Personal 
 Brindar acompañamiento y supervisión constante al equipo implementador del proyecto, a fin de asegurar la calidad de las intervenciones por parte de estos.
 Apoyar al equipo implementador en las distintas áreas, la identificación de puntos focales municipales para coordinación de actividades dentro del proyecto.
 Apoya al equipo implementador a través de visitas frecuentes para procurar los recursos a lo largo de la implementación.
 Estar alerta activamente de cualquier problema de seguridad para equipo implementador o beneficiarios. Junto con el Coordinador de Seguridad de IRC recomendar estrategias de mitigación.
 Mantener relaciones abiertas y profesionales con los actores locales y los miembros del equipo IRC, promoviendo un fuerte espíritu de equipo.
 Asegurarla finalización oportuna y la presentación de informes de horas laboradas mensuales y revisiones anuales del desempeño del trabajo.
 Planificación e Implementación 
 Apoyar la implementación del proyecto y garantizar el cumplimiento de los planes de trabajo y los planes de monitoreo, así como la evaluación por parte de los socios implementadores.
 Contribuir a las actividades de desarrollo de nuevas propuestas para el proyecto, recomendando la mejor manera de continuar la implementación de la programación basada en contextos locales.
 Monitoreo de Subvenciones y Reportes 
 Asegurar el monitoreo de los indicadores y las modificaciones según sea necesario.
 Monitorear y consolidar la información recopilada de las distintas intervenciones.
 Coordinar con el equipo correspondiente el Reporte mensual de beneficiarios atendidos por los socios implementadores.   
 Gestión de Socios

 BACKGROUND:  The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.
 The IRC responds to people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives. Our work gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, conflict sensitivity, coordination, and impact. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) have been working in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, the IRC has more than 2,200 staff working across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, and Yemen to support those affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.
 The IRC Yemen began its programs in October 2012. Since establishing its presence in the South of Yemen, in the Red Sea Coastal city of Aden, following the war which broke out in Yemen in March of 2015 and the humanitarian disaster. IRC launched an emergency response program to support conflict-affected and displaced communities, with programmes in Health, Nutrition, Protection (including Women’s Protection and Empowerment and Child Protection), emergency preparedness and response Mechanisms and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). IRC Yemen currently implements the FCDO-funded RISE Consortium (a health and protection programme) in southern Yemen together with national partner organisations
 Background and Objectives of YHC 
 Yemen continues to face one of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, driven by years of conflict, economic disruption and the degradation of public services. Only 54% of health facilities are currently functioning, and just 18% of those offer at least 75% service availability. Maternal mortality stands at 183 per 100,000 live births and under-five mortality at 61.9 per 1,000. Food security and basic needs are the top priority for 80% of households; 96% of households are food insecure, and 47% report insufficient water to meet their daily needs. Intimate partner and household-based gender-based violence predominates, while services are constrained by a severe shortage of female caseworkers and fragmented referral pathways. The Yemen Humanitarian Capacity programme is an anticipated FCDO-funded, three-year programme expected to succeed the current RISE programme. YHC is designed to deliver lifesaving, integrated health, nutrition, and protection services across Yemen.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 The IRC began planning to reopen an oPt country program in mid-2022 and launched an emergency response in Gaza in October 2023. The organization is currently supporting a network of local partners in both Gaza and the West Bank to sustain critical health, protection, food security, cash, education, and early childhood development interventions. The IRC is also deploying emergency medical teams to provide surge clinical capacity in hospitals and other health facilities.
 The IRC is working to scale its emergency response while building a longer-term oPt country program in parallel. This effort is being jointly managed by the Emergencies and Humanitarian Action Unit (EHAU) and the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, with a view to eventually transition the country program fully under the MENA region.  
 SCOPE OF WORK: 
 The Health Assistant will provide practical, administrative, and field support for assigned health activities in the West Bank. Working under the direction of the Senior Health Officer, the health assistant will assist in organizing trainings, meetings and field activities; maintain accurate activity records; collect supporting documents; and follow up agreed actions. The position is an activity-support role.
 REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS AND COORDINATION: 
 Internal 
 Senior Health Officer 
 Health Coordinator 
 Supply Chain Team 
 MEAL Team 
 Finance and Operations Teams 
 External 
 Health Facilities 
 Ministry of Health Representatives 
 Community Organizations 
 Implementing Partners 
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Support implementation of approved health project activities in accordance with project workplans, technical guidance, and instructions provided by the Senior Health Officer.
 Assist in conducting field visits, site assessments, readiness checks, and activation exercises using approved monitoring tools and checklists.
 Assist in organizing and facilitating health training, simulations, drills, orientations, and other capacity-building activities.
 Maintain accurate records of training and project activities, including attendance sheets, pre/post assessments, evaluations, and supporting documentation.
 Support routine monitoring of project activities and document implementation progress, challenges, lessons learned, and follow-up actions.
 Assist in tracking procurement requests, deliveries, inventory status, and the distribution of project equipment and supplies.
 Draft activity summaries, site visit reports, meeting notes, and implementation updates for review by the Senior Health Officer.
 Ensure project files, records, and supporting documentation are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with IRC procedures and donor requirements.
 Carry out other project implementation and field-support duties assigned by the Senior Health Officer that are consistent with the scope of the position
 Job Requirements: 
 Education: 
 Bachelor's degree in public health, nursing, health sciences or another relevant field. A health or public-health background is preferred
 Work Experience 
 At least one to two years of relevant experience in health programming, programme assistance, field implementation, community work or a similar role.
 Previous experience with an NGO, humanitarian organization or development project is strongly preferred.
 Experience supporting activities with health facilities, government bodies, local authorities or community organizations is an advantage.
 Technical Skills 
 Ability to maintain accurate activity records, trackers and supporting documentation.
 Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
 Strong written and spoken Arabic and good working proficiency in English, including the ability to prepare basic reports and communicate professionally via email.
 Professional Competencies: 
 Strong organization, follow-up and attention to detail.
 Clear and respectful communication with health workers, authorities, trainers and community participants.
 Ability to complete assigned field tasks reliably, keep the supervisor informed and seek guidance when decisions are required.
 Commitment to teamwork, inclusion, confidentiality and humanitarian principles

 ABOUT THE PROGRAMME 
 JOB OVERVIEW/SUMMARY: 
 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Uganda is recruiting a full-time Pilot Manager to run a pilot that helps 200 refugees and host community members in Kampala earn income as mobile money and bank agents on the Opareta platform. The role is funded by Airbel Ventures and runs from December 2026 through the final report in September 2027.
 Uganda's 2006 Refugees Act gives refugees the right to live and work in towns and cities, but formal jobs and credit remain hard to reach. This pilot tests whether working as a mobile money and bank agent can give people a more stable income, and whether those agents widen access to financial services in their communities:
 Partner: Opareta, a financial technology company that recruits, trains, finances and manages agent networks for telecoms and banks. Opareta provides digital onboarding that accepts refugee ID cards, field and call-centre support, and float rebalancing. 
 Clients: 200 agents in total, about 100 existing Re:BUiLD clients who run micro-enterprises and about 100 clients not previously served by Re:BUiLD. The target mix is 60% refugees and 40% host community members, 60% women and 40% men, with a strong emphasis on youth.
 Reach: 200 direct clients and about 500 indirect members, including community members and agents' household members.
 Research: The pilot is evaluated with the Airbel research team against three hypotheses on income, viability and safe capital, and financial inclusion.
 Purpose of the role 
 The Pilot Manager is accountable for delivering the pilot on time, on budget and to the standard needed to produce credible evidence. You will coordinate IRC Uganda ERD, Opareta, Airbel Ventures and the Airbel research team, make sure the right clients are referred and onboarded, and keep clients safe and well supported as they start their agent businesses. By September 2027 you will deliver a final report with recommendations on whether and how to scale the model.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIE S: 
 Pilot planning and delivery 
 Turn the approved pilot proposal into a detailed workplan, with milestones and risks, and keep it current.
 Run monthly check-ins with Opareta, Airbel Ventures and Airbel Research, and flag and resolve issues quickly.
 Keep the pilot on track against the timeline: onboarding of the first cohort by mid-December 2026, about 200 agents by the end of February 2027, midline and endline surveys, and the final report in September 2027.
 Client referral and onboarding 
 Design and run the referral process with ERD and Re:BUiLD colleagues, using agreed eligibility criteria.
 Identify and refer about 200 clients between December 2026 and January 2027.
 Track each client from referral through know-your-agent (KYA) checks to becoming active and resolve blockages with Opareta.
 Brief clients honestly on what agent work involves, including likely earnings, working capital needs and risks to enable them to make informed choices.
 Partner management 
 Act as IRC's day-to-day lead for Opareta, including the subaward agreement, deliverables, reporting and payments.
 Follow up on Opareta's agent data reports and discuss patterns with the partner, including agents who stall or drop out.
 Raise performance concerns early and agree corrective actions with Opareta and Airbel Ventures.
 Monitoring, evaluation and learning 
 Work with the Airbel researcher to put the research plan into practice, including the baseline, midline and endline surveys, interviews and client feedback.
 Track the pilot metrics: monthly commission income, speed of progression, income stability, retention, referral-to-active conversion, cost per active agent, customer activation and range of products used.
 Make sure data is collected, stored and shared ethically, with informed consent and in line with IRC data protection standards.
 Facilitate learning sessions with ERD, Re:BUiLD and country leadership, and use the findings to adjust the pilot while it runs.
 Finance, loans and risk 
 Manage the pilot budget with Uganda and Airbel finance teams, including monthly budget-versus-actual reviews and forecasts.
 Maintain a risk register covering credit risk, fraud, agent stockouts, connectivity and smartphone access, and agree mitigation with partners.
 Support the ERD team with partner compliance and with audit or verification requests.
 Safeguarding and client protection 
 Make sure clients can raise concerns safely through a feedback and reporting channel, and that any safeguarding or protection incident is reported and handled under IRC policy.
 Monitor for fraud, coercive debt collection and other harm to agents, and act quickly when it appears.
 Include a gender and inclusion lens in referral, support and learning, and work to remove barriers faced by women, youth and people with disabilities.
 Reporting, communication and scale-up 
 Prepare monthly progress updates and a final pilot report with clear findings and recommendations.
 Document what it takes for the model to work, including working capital, time and support, and contribute to the longevity and scalability brief.
 Provide inputs for donor conversations on scaling.
 Represent IRC with clients, community leaders and external partners with respect and professionalism.
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPER IENCE: 
 Bachelor's degree in business, economics, development studies, social sciences, project management or a related field. Relevant experience can substitute for formal education.
 At least 5 years of progressive experience managing livelihoods, economic recovery, financial inclusion or market-based programs, ideally with displaced or low-income populations.
 Proven experience managing a pilot, innovation or private-sector partnership project, including workplans, budgets and deliverables.
 Experience managing partner or vendor relationships and agreements, including monitoring performance and resolving problems.
 Strong skills in monitoring, evaluation and learning, including working with researchers, survey data and indicator tracking.
 Understanding of safeguarding, client protection and do-no-harm principles.
 Excellent written and spoken English, with strong writing and presentation skills.
 Ability to travel regularly within Kampala.
 Preferred qualifications 
 Master's degree in a relevant field.
 Experience working with refugees, asylum seekers or host communities in urban settings.
 Experience with fintech, telecom or banking partners, agent banking or digital onboarding and KYC processes.
 Familiarity with village savings and loan associations (VSLAs), cash-based programming or youth and women's economic empowerment.
 Experience with impact evaluation, randomized or quasi-experimental research, or learning agendas with an academic or research partner.
 Knowledge of Ugandan refugee policy, including the 2006 Refugees Act, and the financial regulatory environment, including agent banking regulations.
 Key competencies and professional standards 
 Delivery focus: Plans realistically, tracks progress closely and deliver to deadlines in a fast-moving pilot.
 Partnership and influence: Builds trust and gets results across IRC teams, a private-

 Job Overview:  
 Humanitarian needs are rising while funding falls. We believe AI, used well, can help close that gap. So we are transforming how the IRC works. We are giving staff across the organization AI tools and training. We are reshaping core work like supply chain and finance. And we are reinventing how we reach people in crisis, from detecting health threats earlier to putting an AI coach in the hands of teachers and parents.
 We are hiring a Manager, AI Transformation Portfolio to join the small central team that keeps this work coordinated, visible, and on track. You will track progress across a portfolio of about 40 projects, spot risks early, and make sure senior leaders have what they need to decide. You will coordinate internal communications on the transformation. And you will work directly with the IRC’s AI Executive Lead, its Chief Information Officer, and members of the Executive Board, the IRC’s senior-most leaders.
 This is a 12-month role with a clear mission: help the IRC move its AI priorities from pilot to scale. We are building the structure as we go. You will bring order to ambiguity, hold owners to their commitments, and build practices that departments can run on their own as the work matures. This is not a technical role, but you will use Claude and other AI tools every day to do it well. 
 What Success Looks Like in 12 Months:  
 This role will support each of AI Transformation Strategy’s 12 month Key Performance Indicators:
 A meaningful number of priority projects have moved from pilot to scale, with lessons captured and reused across the IRC. à You will help spot and share reusable insights and building blocks across projects. 
 The Executive Board has a clear, current picture of AI spend, use cases deployed, and impact, without a heavy reporting burden on project teams. à You will refine and maintain the high efficiency, AI-enabled system that enables this visibility.  
 Enterprise-wide risks have been identified and managed early. à You will spot and escalate key risks. 
 Departments are advancing their own AI priorities with minimal duplication. à You will help automate and simplify the tracking system so that, as directed by the Director, it can extend to projects outside the starting priority set without adding staff time for project teams. 
 Additionally, you will help build broader organizational awareness for the IRC’s transformation agenda down to the impacts and learnings of specific projects.

 El/la gerente MEAL, que reporta a la Deputy Director of Programs, lidera el sistema de monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas, aprendizaje y gestión de datos de IRC en Colombia, asegurando procesos sólidos desde la recolección hasta la visualización y uso de la información. Organiza el trabajo del equipo mediante una planificación anticipada de la carga y de los hitos de cada proyecto y tomando en cuenta las necesidades del portafolio completo.  Dar forma e implementar sistemas y enfoques MEAL que cumplan con las normas y prácticas del IRC (incluido el MEAL Handbook), que satisfagan las necesidades de los proyectos y programas, que permitan la rendición de cuentas a los clientes, socios y donantes, y que fomenten el aprendizaje del programa.
 Reforzar la integración de prioridades intersectoriales en MEAL, incluyendo género, protección, salvaguarda, reducción del riesgo de desastres, Diversidad-Igualdad- Inclusión y No Hacer Daño.
 2.Supervisión de equipo, organización del trabajo y administración unidad MEAL. 
 Supervisar y orientar al personal que depende directamente de él/ella, o que desempeñe funciones asociadas a MEAL. Incluye la comunicación de expectativas claras, el establecimiento de objetivos de rendimiento y el suministro de información periódica y oportuna sobre el rendimiento.
 Organizar el trabajo del equipo MEAL a nivel nacional y en las distintas oficinas y territorios, definiendo roles, responsabilidades, líneas de reporte y mecanismos de coordinación claros, y distribuyendo la carga de trabajo de manera equilibrada entre sectores, proyectos y ubicaciones.
 Elaborar y mantener un plan de trabajo anual y un calendario consolidado del área MEAL con planificación anticipada (como mínimo trimestral) de los hitos de los proyectos: líneas de base, recolección de datos, reportes a donantes, evaluaciones, cierres y nuevas propuestas, anticipando los picos de carga y asignando los recursos con antelación.
 Revisar periódicamente la capacidad del equipo frente a la cartera de proyectos y a los escenarios de financiamiento (nuevos proyectos, cierres, reducción de fondos), y proponer con antelación a la Deputy Director of Programs opciones de priorización, redistribución de funciones y continuidad de las operaciones. Coordinar con equipo MEAL de Venezuela para anticipar necesidades y prioridades en común.
 Establecer mecanismos de continuidad (matriz de roles con titular y suplente, documentación de procesos, bases de datos y herramientas, protocolos de traspaso) que reduzcan la dependencia de una sola persona y limiten la pérdida de conocimiento ante rotación, vacantes, reestructuración o reducción del equipo.
 Entrenar, capacitar y orientar al personal con el cual trabaja con el objetivo de fortalecer su capacidad técnica y su dominio del MEAL Handbook, intercambiar conocimientos dentro del equipo y proporcionar orientación para el desarrollo profesional.
 Diseñar e implementar un plan de fortalecimiento de capacidades técnicas del equipo MEAL, basado en un diagnóstico de competencias, para que cada integrante domine los componentes del MEAL Handbook del IRC (diseño y planificación, monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y retroalimentación, aprendizaje y gestión de datos) y pueda cubrir, de manera complementaria, funciones de otros roles y sectores.
 Promover la polivalencia y la transferencia de conocimientos mediante rotación de tareas, acompañamiento entre pares (duplas o mentoría), sesiones internas de capacitación, ejercicios prácticos y guías o listas de verificación de los procesos clave, y hacer seguimiento a los avances de cada persona en su plan de desarrollo.
 Asistir a reuniones de equipo y coordinación para facilitar la colaboración entre los sectores de IRC para garantizar una estrategia integral de monitoreo, evaluación y aprendizaje en todos los programas de IRC.
 Hacer seguimiento a las líneas presupuestales del área de MEAL y garantizar el uso correcto de los recursos.
 Coordinar con los equipos globales y regionales de MEAL para brindar asistencia técnica y asegurar la coherencia con estándares y procedimientos institucionales. Mantener una relación de trabajo estrecha y regular con el/la Asesor/a Técnico/a Regional de MEAL: realizar reuniones periódicas de seguimiento, compartir con antelación la planificación y las necesidades de apoyo técnico del equipo, solicitar revisión técnica y acompañamiento en diseño, evaluaciones y herramientas, y alinear las prioridades y el plan de fortalecimiento de capacidades del equipo con sus orientaciones y con el MEAL Handbook. Contar con apoyo de el/la asesor/a para cumplir con todas las tareas y responsabilidades.
 3. Diseño y Planificación:

 Participar en la planificación estratégica y diseño de programas.
 Planificar de manera anticipada, junto con los equipos de programas y Grants, las necesidades MEAL de cada proyecto (recursos humanos, presupuesto, herramientas, cronograma de recolección, análisis y reporte), anticipando cierres, renovaciones y escenarios de reducción y ampliación de financiamiento.
 Garantizar el desarrollo de herramientas de monitoreo y evaluación (en conjunto con equipos de programas y el/la asesor/a técnico/a de MEAL, y revisar técnicamente las herramientas para garantizar un seguimiento de calidad de los productos y resultados del proyecto, incluidas las herramientas para evaluar el impacto de las actividades y la satisfacción de los beneficiarios, de acuerdo con los principios rectores de seguridad, confidencialidad, respeto y no discriminación.
 Participar de la formulación de las propuestas y nuevos proyectos que se le asignen a nivel de consolidación de los indicadores y metas de los programas y diseñar el presupuesto asignado para el área de MEAL dentro de cada proyecto.
 Participar en el diseño e implementación de evaluaciones de necesidades.

He or she will be based in N’Djamena and will make frequent visits to field sites.
 The role of Protection Specialist will also involve building technical capacity in the areas of humanitarian coordination, strategy and the development of funding proposals. In their role as co-lead of the protection cluster, this person will work closely with the cluster lead, UNHCR, at national and local levels, as well as with cluster members, international actors and local organisations. 
 The Protection Specialist will be supported remotely by technical protection advisers to ensure that their approach is relevant and aligned with IRC’s global commitments and positioning on protection, particularly child protection, the protection and empowerment of women, and protection and access to justice.
 Main responsibilities

 Working closely with UNHCR and Chadian authorities in supporting the Protection Cluster lead in Chad with coordination, advocacy, information management, and capacity-building for cluster members to ensure an effective and integrated humanitarian response.
 Co-chair meetings and follow up on actions arising from regular sectoral coordination meetings of the Protection Cluster.
 Support the implementation and review of the Cluster’s transition strategy, action plans and the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP).

 Develop response and needs analyses to further help identify gaps in the response relative to identified needs.
 In collaboration with the Cluster’s Information Management Officer, support the Cluster’s data collection efforts, in particular by assisting Chadian partners in submitting accurate and consistent data; in turn, provide an analysis to the Cluster and other inter-agency bodies.
 Support other Clusters and their members in initiatives to mainstream protection, and promote the analysis and integration of protection risks into their strategies and associated responses.
 Lead and facilitate capacity-building sessions on protection for key stakeholders, in line with the Cluster’s agreed priorities.
 Support the Cluster’s representation in inter-agency forums; furthermore, support the mainstreaming of protection through inter-agency engagement and direct support to protection and non-protection actors.
 Work with protection and non-protection partners to promote understanding of and respect for humanitarian and protection principles and standards in accordance with international legal frameworks.

 SCOPE OF WORK: 
 The Youth Program Intern supports refugee children, youth, and young adults, along with their families, in achieving a successful transition to school, community life, and long-term educational and career pathways. The intern assists school-aged youth with academic and social-emotional adjustment while supporting young adults, up to age 24, in exploring career development, workforce readiness, and higher education opportunities. This role also contributes to program intake, planning, coordination, and service delivery for IRC Wichita youth programs. During the academic year, the Youth Program Intern works closely with the Youth Program Supervisor to support students' educational success and overall well-being. Responsibilities include assisting with communication between families and schools, collaborating with teachers and school staff, supporting student engagement, and helping develop and facilitate parent education workshops. For young adults, the intern provides administrative and programmatic support for career exploration, employment readiness, and postsecondary education initiatives. This is an unpaid internship position requiring a minimum commitment of 10 hours per week.
 RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 • Support the planning and implementation of educational outings, enrichment activities, workshops, an special events for refugee youth and young adult participants.
 • Assist with communication and relationship-building between students, families, schools, teachers, and community partners to support participant success.
 • Coordinate transportation logistics for students attending program activities, workshops, field trips, and educational events in collaboration with youth program staff.
 • Perform administrative and clerical duties, including data entry, filing, scheduling, document collection, and maintaining program records.
 • Collaborate with program staff to assess the educational, social-emotional, and career development needs of participants and adapt support strategies as needed.
 • Conduct outreach and recruitment activities within eligible communities to increase participation in youth and young adult programming.
 • Maintain regular contact with families and participants through phone calls, text messages, WhatsApp, and other approved communication methods to provide updates, share resources, and collect required documentation.
 • Support outreach and engagement efforts with adult youth and parents of school-aged participants who may be experiencing challenges with program participation or goal attainment.
 • Maintain accurate, timely, and comprehensive case notes and participant records in accordance with IRC policies and funding requirements.
 • Assist with the development and facilitation of parent engagement workshops, youth activities, career development initiatives, and higher education support services.
 • Participate in staff training, professional development opportunities, team meetings, and program planning sessions.
 • Uphold participant confidentiality and demonstrate cultural sensitivity when working with refugee and immigrant individuals and families.
 • Perform other duties and special projects assigned by the Youth Program Supervisor.
 LEARNING OUTCOMES: 
 • Experience working with refugee and immigrant populations.
 • Knowledge of youth development, educational support, and community based programming.
 • Skills in cross-cultural communication and family engagement.
 • Experience in program coordination, outreach, and event planning.
 • Exposure career development and higher education support services.
 • Professional experience in a nonprofit and humanitarian service environment.
 REQUIREMENTS: 
 • High school diploma required
 • Must be a current undergraduate or graduate student, or less than 12 months past graduation, preferably in the fields of Education, Social Work, or related.
 • Access to personal vehicle/reliable transportation.
 • Candidates must be a U.S. citizen or must have active and compliant visas and work authorization status in the United States.
 • Ability to handle sensitive client information confidentially.
 • Strong intercultural communication skills, including demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds and across language barriers.
 • Ability to work independently and as a part of a team

 CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND 
 The IRC has been present in Nigeria since 2012 when the organization responded to flooding in Kogi state. In February 2014 the IRC moved into Adamawa State in NE Nigeria to provide humanitarian interventions through a multi-sectoral, integrated approach for conflict affected populations. IRC Nigeria now operates a country office in Abuja and field offices in Mubi and Yola of Adamawa State, Maiduguri and Monguno of Borno state and Damaturu of Yobe State. Currently, IRC Nigeria implements programs primary health care, nutrition, environmental health, women’s protection and empowerment, protection, child protection, education, food security & livelihoods.
 Project Context 
 The OCHA/Nigeria Humanitarian Fund project is a multi-sectoral consortium response led by IRC in partnership with Life Helpers Initiative and ZOA. The project addresses urgent and protracted needs of internally displaced people, host communities and returnees across targeted locations in Northeast and Northwest Nigeria. It integrates Health, Nutrition and WASH interventions, with Protection and Cash mainstream across the response. The project seeks to improve access to coordinated, life-saving services, strengthen links with existing systems and community structures, and promote safe, dignified and accountable assistance.
 Job Overview/Summary 
 The Senior Project Integration Manager, based in Maiduguri, will lead the day-to-day coordination and quality assurance of integrated programming across all OCHA/NHF project locations in Northeast and Northwest Nigeria, including activities delivered directly by IRC and through implementing partners. Reporting to the Project Team Lead, the post-holder will work horizontally with all sector/outcome managers and field teams to ensure that Health, Nutrition and WASH interventions are planned and delivered as a coherent package, with Protection and Cash Assistance mainstreamed systematically throughout the project cycle.
 The role will strengthen integration and coordination amongst IRC and partner activities. The Senior Project Integration Manager ensures that plans, targeting, referrals, service delivery, community engagement, monitoring, partner implementation and reporting connect across sectors and locations. The post-holder will identify and resolve gaps, duplication and missed opportunities between sectors; promote consistent implementation across IRC and partner teams; and ensure that integrated activities comply with NHF/OCHA requirements, approved proposals, budgets, technical standards and IRC policies.

 CONTEXTE 
 L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale. Elle a été fondée en 1933, à l’initiative du célèbre physicien Albert Einstein. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC est l’un des leaders mondiaux en matière de secours, de réhabilitation, de protection, de développement post-conflit, de réinsertion et de plaidoyer pour les personnes affectées par les crises. La mission de l’IRC est d’aider les personnes dont les vies et les moyens de subsistance sont détruits par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, se relever et prendre en main leur avenir. 
 IRC est actif en République centrafricaine depuis fin 2006 et dispose d’un bureau principal à Bangui, d’une base à Bocaranga, d’un bureau projet à Ndele, IRC intervient dans plusieurs secteurs. 
 Le programme de gouvernance et renforcement des systèmes à travers le projet « Appui à la société civile en République Centrafricaine » financé par l’Union européenne, est mis en œuvre par IRC en consortium avec les partenaires EEDD, OJLD et OFCA. IRC et ses partenaires ont pour mission de renforcer les OSC centrafricaines en tant qu'acteurs indépendants de bonne gouvernance et de développement au niveau national et contribuer au renforcement d’un espace inclusif, participatif, autonome, indépendant et démocratique promouvant un dialogue ouvert entre les OSC dans les préfectures de Nana-Gribizi, Bangui, Ombela Mpoko, l’Ouham, Lobaye, Nana Mambere, Mambere-Kadei, Sanga Mbaeré, Ouaka ; dont les communes respectives sont Kaga-Bandoro, Bangui et Bimbo Boali, Bossangoa, Mbaïki, Bouar, Berberati, Nola, Bambari, pour une période de trois ans. 
 Le Programme PAF (Protection et autonomisation de la femme) contribue à créer des cadres tant à l’échelle locale que national, de concertation, dialogue, impliquant les femmes et les filles, où leurs voix sont appliquées, où les décisions prises sont centrées sur la satisfaction des leurs besoins primaires, de leurs intérêts stratégiques et où leur protection fait partie intégrante des priorités gouvernementales. Il s’agit ici de renforcer les stratégies de développement du leadership des femmes et des filles, de promouvoir la prévention, la réponse et l’atténuation des risques des VBG/EAS à travers les approches innovantes. Le Programme PAF IRC soutient le mécanisme de la coordination VBG en RCA en collaboration avec UNFPA et les autres acteurs du domaine de responsabilité (AoR VBG). Le programme travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère du Genre et soutient la stratégie Nationale sur la protection et autonomisation de femmes et filles. Dans le cadre de la Protection et Etat de droit ( PRoL), le Programme assure à ce que les personnes sont en mesure d’accéder à la justice et d’exercer leurs droits, Les femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons ont les informations et le soutien nécessaires pour demander justice et y accéder de manière indépendante. Des services de protection de qualité, y compris la gestion de cas/ soutien psychosocial, le monitoring de protection, le renforcement des capacités des acteurs, la documentation civile ainsi que le renforcement du système juridique et des espaces communautaires sûrs et accessibles pour femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons. 
 Le programme Relèvement et Développement Economique (ERD) travaille à faire en sorte que les besoins fondamentaux de survie des personnes que nous servons soient satisfaits et qu’elles disposent d’une combinaison d’actifs et de revenus pour prospérer. Le programme s’assure que les personnes répondent à leurs besoins fondamentaux et protègent leurs moyens de subsistance en cas d’urgence, qu’elles développent leurs moyens de subsistance et se remettent des chocs et afin que les personnes deviennent autonomes et jouissent d’une stabilité économique à long terme. 
 Le programme protection de l’enfant et développement des jeunes (CYPD) répond aux violations de la protection des enfants à travers les approches centrées sur l’enfant, le renforcement de la famille et de la communauté ainsi que le renforcement du système de protection de l’enfance. Le programme renforce les familles et les communautés pour aider à prévenir les violations de la protection de l'enfance et à y répondre lorsqu'elles se produisent à travers des approches " préventives", que " préventives et réactives » adaptées au genre et aux âges. 
 Le programme santé, nutrition et wash organise l’offre des soins curatifs, préventifs et promotionnels avec un focus sur la santé des groupes vulnérables comme le couple mère-enfant, des adolescents et jeunes en appuyant les formations sanitaires existantes, des cliniques mobiles, les sites de soins communautaires ou toute autre structure communautaire pouvant améliorer l’accès et/ ou la qualité des soins de santé, de nutrition ou de l’hygiène individuelle et collective. 
 Le programme Education, donne aux enfants les plus vulnérables un accès au primaire, transition vers le premier cycle et le secondaire.  Tout particulièrement les filles et les enfants affectés par des crises, notamment les déplacés, pour une amélioration de vie dans les zones ciblées par le projet à travers la formation des enseignants, distribution des différentes kits scolaires pédagogiques, récréatifs et dignité, mise en place des groupes Kundukwa et les différents suivis pédagogiques par les Conseillers pédagogiques. 
 IRC en République centrafricaine met actuellement en œuvre son plan stratégique " Stratégie 100", à travers lequel nous visons à fournir le meilleur impact possible pour les garçons, filles, femmes et hommes les plus vulnérables touchés par les crises humanitaires. Dans tout ce que nous faisons, nous nous efforçons de respecter les valeurs fondamentales d’IRC que sont l'intégrité, la responsabilité, le service et l'égalité.

 L’Assistante psychosociale joue un rôle clé dans la mise en œuvre des activités de prévention et de réponse aux VBG. Elle est responsable de la mise en œuvre des activités de gestion de cas de VBG et d’appui psychosociale aux survivantes de VBG et personnes à risque. Elle répondra aux besoins des survivantes de VBG identifiées lors des évaluations et par les mécanismes communautaires. 
 L’Assistante Psychosociale jouera un rôle clé dans la gestion des cas et l’accompagnement psychosocial des bénéficiaires. Sa mission est de garantir que chaque survivante de VBG accède aux services appropriés complets, respectueuse et conforme aux standards internationaux de protection. 
 Elle travaillera en étroite collaboration à l’interne avec les supports de IRC (Logistique, Finance, Administration et les Ressources Humaines) et a l’externe avec les autres acteurs œuvrant dans le domaine de la protection, les OC, les relais communautaires.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 Fondé en 1933, International Rescue Committee (IRC) a pour mission d'aider les personnes dont la vie et les moyens de subsistance ont été brisés par des conflits et des catastrophes à survivre, se rétablir et reprendre leur avenir en main. Depuis 1996, IRC-RDC répond aux besoins humanitaires et de développement des populations congolaises et réfugiées en RDC, tout en s’efforçant de promouvoir leurs droits et de renforcer leur santé, leur sécurité, leur bien-être économique, leur éducation et leur pouvoir décisionnel. Actuellement, IRC intervient dans les domaines de la santé (y compris sexuelle et reproductive), de la nutrition, de l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement (WASH), de la protection de l’enfance et des femmes, de la bonne gouvernance et de la gestion des conflits, et enfin, du redressement économique et du développement.
 Le ministère de la Santé de la RDC a déclaré une épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) en mai 2026, à la suite de la confirmation de cas dus au virus Bundibugyo dans la province de l’Ituri. Alors que les besoins de riposte et de préparation s’étendent au Nord-Kivu, IRC renforce son appui aux formations sanitaires et aux autorités sanitaires à Beni et Butembo, en mettant l’accent sur la réduction du risque de transmission au sein des formations sanitaires et le maintien d’un accès sûr aux services de santé essentiels.
 DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE 
 Sous la supervision technique du HASM, l'Officier(e) Accès Humanitaire, Sécurité & Sûreté (HASO) assure la gestion proactive des risques de sécurité, de sûreté et d'accès humanitaire afin de permettre la continuité et la qualité des opérations IRC à Beni et dans le Grand Nord-Kivu.
 Le/la HASO fournit des analyses et conseils opérationnels à la direction et aux équipes, facilite l'accès humanitaire, renforce l'acceptation de l'IRC et veille à l'application des standards et procédures de sécurité.
 Le poste contribue également à la préparation des équipes, à la coordination sécuritaire inter-agences et à la gestion efficace des incidents et situations critiques.
 RESPONSABILITES CLES 
 Accès humanitaire et engagement des parties prenantes (30%) 
 Développer et maintenir un réseau opérationnel avec les communautés, autorités, acteurs humanitaires, agences des Nations Unies et autres parties prenantes influençant l'accès.
 Appuyer les négociations et stratégies d'accès, en coordination avec le HASM et dans le respect des principes humanitaires.
 Renforcer l'acceptation communautaire de la présence et des activités de l'IRC.
 Conseiller les équipes sur les stratégies d'accès aux zones à risque ou à accès contraint.
 Intégrer le principe de Do No Harm dans les recommandations d'accès et de réduction des risques.
 Analyse du contexte et information sécuritaire (25 %) 
 Assurer une veille sécuritaire continue et trianguler les informations provenant de sources fiables, formelles et informelles.
 Produire et diffuser les rapports de situation sécuritaire (DSR) conformément aux standards IRC.
 Identifier les tendances, menaces et évolutions susceptibles d'affecter les opérations.
 Consulter régulièrement le personnel afin d'identifier les risques opérationnels et les vulnérabilités spécifiques.
 Fournir des recommandations pratiques et adaptées au contexte.
 Escalader immédiatement tout incident ou évolution majeure au HASM et à la hiérarchie concernée.
 Documentation et conformité (10 %) 
 Veiller au respect des IRC Global Safety & Security Standards et des protocoles PCI/EVD.
 Maintenir à jour les évaluations et outils de gestion des risques (SRA, matrices de risques).
 Assurer la qualité et l'utilisation des briefings sécuritaires pré-arrivée et à l'arrivée.
 Contribuer à la mise à jour du SMP, des SOP et des Plans de Contingence de Beni et du Grand Nord-Kivu.
 Formation et briefing (10 %) 
 Assurer les briefings de sécurité et EVD aux nouveaux employés, visiteurs et personnels en mission.
 Organiser les briefings pré-départ pour les mouvements terrain.
 Intégrer les dimensions de genre, diversité et vulnérabilités dans les formations et recommandations.
 Contribuer à la conception et à l'animation des formations Field READI et autres sessions de sensibilisation à la sécurité et aux protocoles PCI/EPI.
 Sécurité physique des sites (10 %) 
 Réaliser des évaluations régulières des bureaux, résidences et autres installations IRC conformément aux SMS.
 Identifier les vulnérabilités et suivre la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives.
 Veiller à la disponibilité et au bon fonctionnement des équipements de sécurité et stocks d'urgence.
 S'assurer que les plans d'évacuation, d'hibernation et autres mesures d'urgence sont à jour, affichés et connus du personnel.
 Gestion des incidents (10 %) 
 Assurer une gestion structurée des incidents conformément aux procédures IRC,
 Recevoir et traiter les signalements avec professionnalisme, confidentialité et sensibilité.
 Contribuer aux analyses post-incident et au suivi des recommandations visant à prévenir leur récurrence.
 Autres responsabilités (5 %) 
 Assurer toute autre responsabilité pertinente confiée par le superviseur technique ou administratif dans le cadre des priorités opérationnelles et de la réponse d'urgence.
 PROFIL REQUIS 
 Formation et expérience 
 Diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+3 minimum en sécurité, sciences sociales, droit, relations internationales, gestion des risques ou domaine pertinent, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
 Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans un environnement humanitaire ou de crise complexe, idéalement dans la gestion de la sécurité, de l'accès humanitaire ou des opérations terrain.
 Expérience dans un contexte d'insécurité active et/ou de réponse d'urgence souhaitée.
 Une connaissance du contexte sécuritaire et opérationnel du Grand Nord-Kivu constitue un atout majeur.
 Compétences techniques 
 Bonne maîtrise des outils de gestion des risques et de sécurité humanitaire : SRA, SMP, SOP, Plans de Contingence, etc.
 Capacité démontrée à analyser rapidement un contexte complexe et à produire des recommandations claires et opérationnelles.
 Bonne compréhension des mécanismes de coordination humanitaire et sécuritaire, notamment UNDSS, INSO et OCHA .
 Maîtrise des outils Microsoft Office et des plateformes pertinentes.
 Compétences comportementales 
 Intégrité, rigueur, discrétion et sens élevé de la confidentialité.
 Excellentes capacités de communication, de négociation et de gestion des relations avec des interlocuteurs divers.
 Capacité à travailler efficacement sous pression dans un environnement volatile et imprévisible.

 Excellentes capacités d'analyse, de rédaction et de synthèse.
 Langues

 Anglais : niveau professionnel – atout.

 Le ministère de la Santé de la République démocratique du Congo a officiellement déclaré la 17e épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola du pays le 15 mai 2026, après la confirmation de cas causés par l'espèce virale Bundibugyo (BDBV) dans la province de l'Ituri.  Le 17 mai 2026, l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) a évalué l'épidémie comme une urgence de santé publique de portée internationale, en raison du risque de propagation régionale et du contexte opérationnel difficile. L'IRC prépare son appui à l'endiguement de l'épidémie en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu. La réponse repose sur trois piliers complémentaires : la prévention et le contrôle des infections et le WASH (IPC/WASH), la communication sur les risques et l'engagement communautaire (RCCE), ainsi que la protection intégrée, notamment la sauvegarde, la PSEA, le MHPSS, les mécanismes de référencement VBG et l'atténuation des risques de protection.
