 Sous la supervision directe du/de la Responsable MEAL de la réponse Ebola, l'Officier/ère MEAL assure la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du système MEAL pour les interventions IPC/WASH, RCCE, redevabilité et protection intégrée dans la zone de Beni. Il/elle développe et tient à jour les bases de données des activités, digitalise les outils de collecte dans CommCare, conduit les évaluations IPC, assure le suivi des feedbacks et des rumeurs, contrôle la qualité des données et produit les analyses nécessaires au pilotage et à l'adaptation de la réponse.

 Mettre en œuvre le dispositif MEAL des interventions IPC/WASH, RCCE,protection  de redevabilité et de protection intégrée conformément au cadre logique, au plan MEAL et aux standards de qualité de la réponse Ebola.
 Développer et maintenir une base de données consolidée couvrant les formations sanitaires et sites communautaires soutenus, les formations, supervisions, distributions, travaux IPC/WASH, activités RCCE, interventions de protection et MHPSS, feedbacks, plaintes, rumeurs, référencements et actions de suivi.
 Digitaliser dans CommCare les outils de suivi des activités, formations, distributions, supervisions, consultations communautaires, feedbacks, rumeurs et autres interventions pertinentes, en intégrant des règles de validation, des identifiants uniques et des contrôles visant à réduire les erreurs et les doublons.
 Assurer l'utilisation du Toolkit IPC v2 standard de l'IRC pour les évaluations des formations sanitaires, ainsi que la qualité, la synchronisation et l'exploitation des données générées.
 Mettre à jour l'Indicator Tracking Table (ITT), le reach tracker, les listes maîtresses des sites et partenaires ainsi que les tableaux de bord, en garantissant l'exactitude des cibles, réalisations, localisations, périodes et désagrégations.
 Comparer régulièrement les activités planifiées aux réalisations, identifier les écarts de mise en œuvre et signaler rapidement les actions nécessitant une décision ou un suivi.
 Évaluations et suivi des interventions IPC/WASH
 Planifier et conduire les évaluations IPC dans les formations sanitaires, en coordination avec les équipes Santé/WASH et les autorités sanitaires, en utilisant le Toolkit IPC v2 de l'IRC et, selon le contexte, les outils IPC du ministère de la Santé.
 Garantir la collecte de données fiables sur les principaux domaines IPC : dépistage, triage et isolement; hygiène, nettoyage, désinfection et EPI; eau; assainissement et gestion des déchets de soins; et gouvernance IPC.
 Analyser les scores, les écarts aux standards et les tendances afin d'identifier les risques critiques, les priorités d'intervention et les besoins d'appui au niveau des formations sanitaires.
 Contribuer, avec les équipes Santé et WASH, à l'élaboration et au suivi de plans de rétablissement et d'amélioration fondés sur les résultats des évaluations.
 Assurer le suivi des formations, supervisions, distributions d'intrants et d'EPI, installations de triage et d'isolement, infrastructures WASH, comités d'hygiène et activités IPC communautaires.
 Veiller à ce que les résultats des évaluations et du suivi orientent la planification opérationnelle, la priorisation des interventions, l'allocation des ressources et l'adaptation de la réponse.

 L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale. Elle a été fondée en 1933, à l’initiative du célèbre physicien Albert Einstein. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC est l’un des leaders mondiaux en matière de secours, de réhabilitation, de protection, de développement post-conflit, de réinsertion et de plaidoyer pour les personnes affectées par les crises. La mission de l’IRC est d’aider les personnes dont les vies et les moyens de subsistance sont détruits par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, se relever et prendre en main leur avenir. 
 IRC est actif en République centrafricaine depuis fin 2006 et dispose d’un bureau principal à Bangui, d’une base à Bocaranga, d’un bureau projet à Ndele, IRC intervient dans plusieurs secteurs. 
 Le programme de gouvernance et renforcement des systèmes à travers le projet « Appui à la société civile en République Centrafricaine » financé par l’Union européenne, est mis en œuvre par IRC en consortium avec les partenaires EEDD, OJLD et OFCA. IRC et ses partenaires ont pour mission de renforcer les OSC centrafricaines en tant qu'acteurs indépendants de bonne gouvernance et de développement au niveau national et contribuer au renforcement d’un espace inclusif, participatif, autonome, indépendant et démocratique promouvant un dialogue ouvert entre les OSC dans les préfectures de Nana-Gribizi, Bangui, Ombela Mpoko, l’Ouham, Lobaye, Nana Mambere, Mambere-Kadei, Sanga Mbaeré, Ouaka ; dont les communes respectives sont Kaga-Bandoro, Bangui et Bimbo Boali, Bossangoa, Mbaïki, Bouar, Berberati, Nola, Bambari, pour une période de trois ans. 
 Le Programme PAF (Protection et autonomisation de la femme) contribue à créer des cadres tant à l’échelle locale que national, de concertation, dialogue, impliquant les femmes et les filles, où leurs voix sont appliquées, où les décisions prises sont centrées sur la satisfaction des leurs besoins primaires, de leurs intérêts stratégiques et où leur protection fait partie intégrante des priorités gouvernementales. Il s’agit ici de renforcer les stratégies de développement du leadership des femmes et des filles, de promouvoir la prévention, la réponse et l’atténuation des risques des VBG/EAS à travers les approches innovantes. Le Programme PAF IRC soutient le mécanisme de la coordination VBG en RCA en collaboration avec UNFPA et les autres acteurs du domaine de responsabilité (AoR VBG). Le programme travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère du Genre et soutient la stratégie Nationale sur la protection et autonomisation de femmes et filles. Dans le cadre de la Protection et Etat de droit ( PRoL), le Programme assure à ce que les personnes sont en mesure d’accéder à la justice et d’exercer leurs droits, Les femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons ont les informations et le soutien nécessaires pour demander justice et y accéder de manière indépendante. Des services de protection de qualité, y compris la gestion de cas/ soutien psychosocial, le monitoring de protection, le renforcement des capacités des acteurs, la documentation civile ainsi que le renforcement du système juridique et des espaces communautaires sûrs et accessibles pour femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons. 
 Le programme Relèvement et Développement Economique (ERD) travaille à faire en sorte que les besoins fondamentaux de survie des personnes que nous servons soient satisfaits et qu’elles disposent d’une combinaison d’actifs et de revenus pour prospérer. Le programme s’assure que les personnes répondent à leurs besoins fondamentaux et protègent leurs moyens de subsistance en cas d’urgence, qu’elles développent leurs moyens de subsistance et se remettent des chocs et afin que les personnes deviennent autonomes et jouissent d’une stabilité économique à long terme. 
 Le programme protection de l’enfant et développement des jeunes (CYPD) répond aux violations de la protection des enfants à travers les approches centrées sur l’enfant, le renforcement de la famille et de la communauté ainsi que le renforcement du système de protection de l’enfance. Le programme renforce les familles et les communautés pour aider à prévenir les violations de la protection de l'enfance et à y répondre lorsqu'elles se produisent à travers des approches " préventives", que " préventives et réactives » adaptées au genre et aux âges. 
 Le programme santé, nutrition et wash organise l’offre des soins curatifs, préventifs et promotionnels avec un focus sur la santé des groupes vulnérables comme le couple mère-enfant, des adolescents et jeunes en appuyant les formations sanitaires existantes, des cliniques mobiles, les sites de soins communautaires ou toute autre structure communautaire pouvant améliorer l’accès et/ ou la qualité des soins de santé, de nutrition ou de l’hygiène individuelle et collective. 
 Le programme Education , donne aux enfants les plus vulnérables un accès au primaire, transition vers le premier cycle et le secondaire.  Tout particulièrement les filles et les enfants affectés par des crises, notamment les déplacés, pour une amélioration de vie dans les zones ciblées par le projet à travers la formation des enseignants, distribution des différentes kits scolaires pédagogiques, récréatifs et dignité, mise en place des groupes Kundukwa et les différents suivis pédagogiques par les Conseillers pédagogiques. 
 IRC en République centrafricaine met actuellement en œuvre son plan stratégique " Stratégie 100", à travers lequel nous visons à fournir le meilleur impact possible pour les garçons, filles, femmes et hommes les plus vulnérables touchés par les crises humanitaires. Dans tout ce que nous faisons, nous nous efforçons de respecter les valeurs fondamentales d’IRC que sont l'intégrité, la responsabilité, le service et l'égalité. 
 Aperçu du poste : 
  L’Officière Protection est responsable de la mise en œuvre directe des activités de protection et d’appui psychosocial auprès des survivantes de VBG et des femmes/filles vulnérables dans la zone d’intervention. Elle assure la gestion des cas, la supervision des assistantes psychosociales internes, la mobilisation communautaire, ainsi que la coordination avec les autres secteurs du projet (santé, nutrition, WASH). Elle gère également la base de données GBVIMS et les rapports liés au volet psychosocial.
  Dans ce contexte d’intervention directe, l’Officière Psychosociale est l’actrice principale de la réponse, garantissant la qualité, la pertinence et la cohérence des services offerts, sans dépendre de partenaires externes.
 Principales responsabilités : 
 1. Gestion de cas VBG 
 Accueil et accompagnement direct : recevoir les survivantes dans un cadre confidentiel, instaurer un climat de confiance et offrir un soutien immédiat.
 Évaluation approfondie : analyser les besoins médicaux, psychosociaux, juridiques et sécuritaires de chaque survivante pour élaborer un plan individualisé.
 Suivi continu : assurer un accompagne

 SCOPE OF ADULT EDUCATION INTERN WORK: The IRC’s Adult Education Intern assists refugee and immigrant adults in Workplace Literacy (WPL) classes to develop the language skills critical for success. The classes work with the students’ employer and aim to build vocabulary and communication skills, convey skills necessary for the American workforce, and impart information about skills needed in their specific workplace so that clients can be successful and productive members of their team, and so that they can pursue career pathways of their choice. Interns and other class assistants will facilitate breakout groups to separate students by their proficiency level. Instruction is focused on developing literacy, comprehension, and confidence to apply towards real world situations including dealing with frustrated customers, peers at work, receiving feedback, and working towards a promotion. The schedule adjusts to the schedules of the students and classes are offered late afternoons, evenings, or weekends.
 Adult Education interns work under class lead instructors and other IRC Adult Education staff to effectively engage with prospective and current immigrant clients. Activities may include:
 Classroom Support: assisting lead instructors with classroom management activities, following developed curriculum and leading instruction with groups of English language learners. Classroom Support is expected to be a primary activity for nearly all Adult Education interns.

 Retention and Follow-up: conferencing with, surveying, and connecting with current and former participants, assessing goals and identifying appropriate referrals.

 ·       Other duties as assigned.

 Interns must have
 ·       Strong communication skills: communication between instructors and fellow class assistants before, during, and after classes, and communication with adult Education language learners during classes.
 ·       Availability for at least 4 hours of class time and at least 4 hours of prep time per week.

 ·       An interest in working closely with a diverse population of adults.
 ·       Comfortability in working in a cross-cultural environment, in-person, online, and over the phone, with adult learners, sometimes with little or no English proficiency.
 ·       Comfortability in working with a variable number of students (individually and in groups).
 ·       Ability to work in a collaborative environment and in co-teaching.
 ·       Comfortability in adapting learning activities with limited notice.
 ·       Fluent in spoken and written English. Bi-lingual abilities are not necessary but can be a plus.

 Commitment of 8 hours per week for a minimum of 3 consecutive months.

 Descripción general del trabajo:   
 El Asistente de administración reporta al Oficial de Operaciones y brindara apoyo y soporte a las solicitudes de las diferentes direcciones que maneja a misión de País (Country Director, Deputy Director Programs Deputy Director Operations), y la redacción y comunicación de dirección, son su responsabilidad, garantizando el cumplimiento de los estándares de IRC para cada proceso.
 El cargo es clave para fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta del IRC, asegurando que todas las solicitudes administrativas del área, gestión de eventos, y salidas oficiales cumplan con los estándares de calidad, regulaciones de donantes y políticas internas de la organización. Asimismo, el asistente contribuye a la implementación efectiva de intervenciones multisectoriales que incluyen seguridad alimentaria (MPCA y asistencia alimentaria), atención primaria en salud, salud reproductiva y obstétrica (SSR), salud mental y apoyo psicosocial (SMAPS), prevención de violencia de género (VBG) y educación en emergencias, garantizando que estas lleguen a las poblaciones más vulnerables con enfoque de protección, equidad de género y derechos humanos.

Además, el asistente contribuye a la planificación territorial, adaptando las operaciones a contextos de difícil acceso y población en desplazamiento, mediante presencia fija o despliegue móvil, para maximizar cobertura, continuidad de los servicios y efectividad de la respuesta.
 Finalmente, el asistente debe ser un agente activo en la gestión de riesgos y seguridad, cumpliendo con protocolos de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SST), estándares de protección y políticas de prevención de explotación y abuso sexual (PEAS), garantizando un entorno seguro tanto para el personal del IRC como para las comunidades beneficiarias.

 IRC BACKGROUND: 
 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC is at work today in more than 40 countries and in 26 U.S. cities. The IRC’s Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) department creates opportunities for refugees and other vulnerable migrants to survive and thrive in the US. RAI serves nearly 50,000 individuals each year in the US through a diverse portfolio of programs aimed at achieving outcomes in five impact areas: Health, Safety, Economic Wellbeing, Education, and Power. 
 In 2016, IRC re-opened its doors in Missoula and has since supported nearly 1,000 individuals building a new life in Montana. Over nine years, the IRC in Montana has served refugees and immigrants from Syria, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Iraq, Yemen, Burma, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Haiti, Venezuela, Central America, and Mexico.
 JOB OVERVIEW: 
 IRC seeks a Staff Attorney to join the Montana Legal team to represent refugees and other individuals with petitions before US Citizenship & Immigration Services (USCIS). The Staff Attorney will also conduct community-based Know Your Rights workshops. The position will be part of the IRC Immigration Legal Services Network led by IRC’s Immigration Technical Unit (TU) at IRC’s headquarters, which supports IRC’s 24 legal service programs across the US. The role will collaborate closely with the IRC team in Missoula, Montana, but the position may be based in another high-needs service area outside of Missoula. The position will require some travel within Montana.
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:  
 Direct Legal Representation and Program Management 
 Conduct intakes and consultations with IRC clients and community members, and provide direct legal representation to individuals before USCIS, DOS, and possibly other governmental agencies. 
 Coordinate closely within IRC’s multidisciplinary teams to identify needs and facilitate referrals to services offered in-house and through partnerships with external providers.
 Ensure client and program data is collected consistently, managed appropriately, and reported accurately in accordance with program reporting requirements set by IRC. 
 Position may supervise legal assistants and/or interns.
 Maintain up-to-date knowledge and expertise of changing immigration policies through independent research and analysis, regular trainings, and peer-to-peer consultation.
 Participate in community-based coalitions related to immigrant rights. 
 Serve as a strong advocate for humanitarian immigrants.
 Community Partnerships and Workshops 
 Create and maintain a viable outreach strategy to cultivate and maintain strong relationships with community-based organizations, local immigration attorneys, and nonprofit legal providers.
 Collaborate with other IRC departments and partners to offer community-based workshops or information sessions when demand exceeds capacity to provide direct legal representation. This may include pro se workshops to complete requests under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) among others. 
 JOB REQUIREMENTS:  
 Law degree (JD or LLM) from an ABA-accredited U.S. institution and membership in good standing with any state bar;
 Ideally at least 1-3 years of experience providing direct representation in immigration court and/or before USCIS to asylum applicants and other immigrants seeking humanitarian relief; law school graduates with clinical legal experience may be considered; 
 Excellent legal research, writing, analytical, and organizational skills;
 Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both orally in a courtroom setting and in writing; 
 Bilingual in one or more commonly spoken languages among IRC Montana’s client population preferred (eg, Spanish, Arabic, Swahili, Dari, Pashto);
 Deep commitment to immigrant rights and working with humanitarian immigrants;
 Trauma-informed and sensitive listening and communication skills; respect for diverse perspectives;
 Evidence of capacity to be a strong team member in a highly collaborative and fast-paced multidisciplinary environment; 
 Must have ability to travel in and around the service area to engage with clients and community partners and attend USCIS interviews.
 Working Environment :    
 Standard office environment with occasional participation in community outreach and legal assistance events.  
 Depending on location, remote work from within the state of Montana may be a possibility.
 May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

 CONTEXTO 
 Nuestra organización responde a las peores emergencias humanitarias del mundo y ayuda a las personas afectadas por crisis humanitarias, incluida la crisis climática, a sobrevivir, recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundada en 1933 a pedido de Albert Einstein, la organización trabaja en más de 50 países para generar un impacto duradero al brindar atención médica, ayudar a los niños a aprender y empoderar a las personas y comunidades para que sean autosuficientes, siempre buscando abordar las desigualdades que enfrentan las mujeres y las niñas.
 La crisis humanitaria en Venezuela continúa intensificándose. Los venezolanos enfrentan una hiperinflación, que los pone fuera del alcance de los bienes y servicios básicos, incluida la atención médica y la alimentación. La escasez de suministros médicos hace que sea difícil diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades transmisibles y las necesidades de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre otros servicios. La falta de alimentos ha provocado hambre y desnutrición. Entre 2015 y 2018, más de tres millones de venezolanos se fueron a buscar bienes y servicios principalmente en países vecinos. 
 Nuestra Organización brinda servicios de respuesta en emergencia en los estados Zulia, Lara, Falcón, Táchira y Apure, trabajando en colaboración con organizaciones de la sociedad civil venezolana, proporcionamos servicios esenciales a personas vulnerables, incluyendo Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición, prevención y respuesta a la Violencia de Género (VBG), prevención y respuesta en protección infantil, Educación en Emergencias, Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida. Este enfoque estratégico nos permite brindar atención vital a las personas necesitadas en Venezuela, alineándonos con el compromiso de fortalecer la localización y empoderar a los actores nacionales.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 ORGANIZATIONAL BACKGROUND 
 The IRC began planning to reopen an occupied Palestinian territories (oPt) country program in mid-2022 and launched an emergency response in Gaza in October 2023. The organization is currently supporting a network of local partners in both Gaza and the West Bank to sustain critical health, protection, food security, cash, education, and early childhood development interventions. The IRC is also deploying emergency medical teams to provide surge clinical capacity in hospitals and other health facilities.
 The IRC is working to scale its emergency response while building a longer-term oPt country program in parallel. 
 SCOPE OF WORK 
 The Deputy Director for Programs (DDP) provides strategic l eadership, decision-making and coordination for program development and delivery, overseeing the effective implementation and technical quality of IRC’s programs in oPt. The DDP ensures that programs are evidence-based and needs-driven, monitored closely, and funded appropriately. T he position reports to the Country Director (CD) and is a member of the Senior Management Team. The DDP directly supervises grants, partnerships, MEAL, and all technical coordinators, currently inclusive of health, protection, education and WASH, with potential to expand into additional technical areas. 
 This position has close working relationships with the MENA Deputy Regional Director and other members of the regional support teams.
 RESPONSIBILTIES 
 Strategic Leadership 
 Provide overall leadership and management of IRC Palestine programs, maintaining and enforcing strategic program direction and growth.
 Oversee the implementation of the country program Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and ensure it remains relevant and evidence-based.Drive IRC’s efforts towards a ‘partner first’ program approach and foster a network of local Palestinian partners, empowering those entities to lead key decision making and service delivery, and positioning IRC as a partner of choice.] Build strategic partnerships with local actors, fostering collaboration on strategy, program design and development, and capacity sharing.
 Serve as a leader in building a culture of effective and respectful partnerships. Promote attitudes and values conducive to building and sustaining collaborative partnerships across the country program.
 Participate actively in country program management, coordination, and strategy meetings with other members of the senior management team.
 Program Quality 
 Ensure programming is aligned with the emergency response plan, SAP priorities, and IRC’s Outcomes and Evidence Framework (OEF), including program planning and project design.
 Liaise with regional technical advisors and ensure technical coordinators apply relevant guidance and best practices in new program design and implementation.
 Ensure high-quality and adaptive technical program support and guidance to partners.
 Support the development of measurement tools to assess program impact and involvement of client groups in program design. Ensure the alignment of the IRC oPt programs with the MEAL Handbook and the use of established stringent monitoring and evaluation systems.
 Champion an organizational culture where data and client input are routinely used for decision making and program adaptation. Promote systems which ensure that evidence is used to inform proposal design and theories of change.
 Identify and pursue opportunities to improve client feedback mechanisms to ensure responsive programming.
 Program Delivery 
 Maintain a sound understanding of IRC oPt’s programs and activity plans. Ensure continued oversight of both partner and direct delivery.
 Support and supervise implementation of strong Project Management Cycle processes and tools in accordance with standard IRC tools.  
 Ensure program teams develop, implement, and regularly update detailed workplans, procurement plans, spending plans and staffing plans. 
 Actively contribute to and/or chair project implementation meetings as required to review progress of programs, including but not limited, to progress indicators, workplans and spending. When required, lead the development of corrective measures to ensure projects finish on time and on target, ensure timely follow up on any agreed actions.
 Ensure the office consistently promotes and effectively uses IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) and that partnership decision-making and action is driven by IRC’s partnership principles.
 Business Development and Grants Management 
 Work with colleagues in the country program, region and HQ to identify funding opportunities and develop competitive, responsive proposals that are strategically aligned and donor compliant.
 Provide strategic direction for new program design in close coordination with the grants and technical coordinators.
 Ensure that strategic partnership considerations are incorporated in program design, including in Go / No-Go funding discussions.
 Ensure the proactive engagement of partners in program development and project design efforts.
 Review and assure the quality of concept notes and proposals.
 In collaboration with the Grants Coordinator, ensure program compliance with donor regulations, local government regulations and IRC internal control procedures.
 Representation and Coordination 
 Maintain a strong working relationship with donors. Lead external representation with donors as required.
 Actively, systematically, and regularly ensure ongoing communication with various partners in country.
 Ensure that IRC oPt’s program interventions are planned and coordinated within the broader humanitarian effort. 
 Ensure IRC is represented at sector coordination groups, including the clusters.
 Staff Performance Management and Development 
 Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, and establishing a supportive environment while emphasizing accountability.
 Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
 Develop cohesive teams through regular department meetings, individual meetings, and the promotion of a collaborative working environment. 
 Coordinate performance management within the department and ensure a culture of high performance through staff engagement and accountability.
 Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices.
 Work with P&C colleagues to identify and implement recruitment and retention strategies.
 Model and encourage active practice of the principles of the “IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct” throughout the Palestine country program.
 REQUIREMENTS  
 Excellent professional track record with at least 8 years of experience in conflict and humanitarian environments with significant program leadership responsibilities. 
 Successful experience delivering programs in a complex and volatile security environment strongly preferred. 
 Proven ability to think strategically, prioritize and meet deadlines in a challenging emergency setting.

 IRC (International Rescue Committee) Germany is seeking a 
 Program Development & Award Advisor (d/f/m), Latin America 
 ***in Berlin, or remote (within Germany) | as soon as possible 
 ***in part-time (20 hours/week), increase to full-time in the future might be possible (contingent upon funding) | initially for 2 years 
 About Us 
 Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. In 2016, IRC Germany was founded and engages in global humanitarian work as well as throughout Germany in the areas of education, economic wellbeing, and safety, legal protection, and empowerment.
 IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) runs humanitarian relief, recovery, and development programs focused on safety, health, education, economic well-being, and people’s power to influence decisions, with particular attention to women and girls. Its Awards Management Unit (AMU) secures and manages government donor funding, bridging donors and country programs while ensuring compliance and managing risk.
 In Latin America and the Caribbean, the IRC responds to crises in Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico, Central America, and Haiti, supporting displaced and host communities through local partners and direct implementation. The Program Development and Award Advisor (PDAA) provides pre- and post-award support to country offices, ensures donor and IRC compliance, leads donor deliverables, and manages donor relationships.
 Major Responsibilities 
 Strategic Business Development: support country offices in advancing strategic business development planning efforts, donor engagement, intelligence gathering, positioning and capture. Prepare for and participate in donor meetings, engagement calls, and strategic discussions as needed.
 Proposal development: provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals, leading proposal development and coordination as needed. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements and policies.
 Award portfolio management: manage a portfolio of awards and act as the first point of contact for country award staff on compliance issues. Review agreements and lead negotiation of award terms and conditions with donor counterparts.
 Partnerships: guide country offices in managing local and international partners in line with IRC’s PEERs system, and review and process sub-grant agreements.
 Monitoring: monitor projects to ensure progress against objectives and compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, participation in routine meetings and other regular calls.
 Reporting: provide timely support on narrative reporting, amendments, and modifications. Ensure timely submission of high-quality donor deliverables.
 Donor liaison: manage donor relationships on contractual issues, compliance queries and approvals, and represent IRC externally at events and meetings.
 Capacity building: mentor Grants and Partnerships staff, develop and deliver training, and support recruitment and onboarding of new team members.
 Other duties: contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities, work with communications teams on donor communication products, and maintain checklists and work processes and systems.
 Your Profile 
 Significant work experience in award management or business development with EU donors, particularly ECHO, and other public donors. Experience with and a strong understanding of institutional donors’ compliance requirements.
 Two years of international field experience highly desirable, familiarity with countries in the region preferred.
 Experience writing, reviewing and editing funding proposals and other donor deliverables and excellent attention to detail.
 Excellent written and oral communication skills, including experience in speaking on relevant issues with internal and external audiences.
 English and Spanish language skills at C1-level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CERF) . Additional knowledge of French and/or German highly desirable.
 Excellent interpersonal & communication skills: ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.
 Good financial management and budgeting skills
 Ability to analyze and synthesize information, work collaboratively as part of a diverse team, handle complex tasks, and work independently
 Solid organizational and creative problem-solving skills: ability to be flexible and work well under pressure in a fast-paced multi-tasking team environment
 Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)
 Ability and willingness to travel internationally (up to 15 %)
 We Offer 
 Meaningful work within a collaborative team
 A starting salary between 32.000 and 33.500 Euro gross per year (for part-time, 20 hours/week) as well as an annual salary increase
 Attractive employee benefits such as gym membership, company pension scheme, shopping vouchers, childcare subsidy, job bike leasing, subsidized Deutschlandticket (national public transport), and access to timely and confidential psychological support if needed
 30 days of annual leave and special leave days
 Flexible hybrid-work options (working hours, office/homebased)
 Training and professional development opportunities, including access to free language courses
 Assistance services for people with disabilities, if required.
 We look forward to receiving your application (including CV and – if available – three references) via our application portal – even if you do not meet all the listed requirements.
 For questions, please contact Friederike Haarbrücker ( HR.Deutschland@rescue.org ).
 As an organization committed to an empowering work environment, equal opportunities, and against any form of discrimination, we welcome applications from people regardless of their origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disabilities, age, or other characteristics protected by applicable law. We particularly encourage people with personal or family experience of flight and migration to apply. 
 With equal qualifications, we give preference to applications from people with severe disabilities. If you have any questions about accessible applications or inclusion, please feel free to contact our Inclusion Officer, Christine Mader ( christine.mader@rescue.org ).
 To ensure equal opportunities, we kindly ask you to refrain from including photos in your application documents. 
 There is no specific application deadline for this job posting. The position needs to be filled as soon as possible and will remain posted until filled.

offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 JOB OVERVIEW 
 The Senior Humanitarian Access, Safety & Security Manager (SHASSM) supports safe, effective and efficient access to and by people in need of humanitarian assistance. The role reports to the Senior HASS Coordinator and supports field locations in implementing programs aligned with the IRC’s risk appetite and strong commitment to the safety and security of our staff. The Snr HASSM ensures access and security risks are identified on time, mitigations are implemented, and staff are appropriately briefed on the security risk environment, relevant SOPs and Contingency Plans. The role will have a strong focus on providing capacity building to the Humanitarian Access, Safety & Security teams in each Field location. The Snr HASSM will also cover gaps in the HASS team in field locations and deputize for the Senior HASS Coordinator when requested. 
 External: 
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Humanitarian Access Management 
 Identify barriers to access and support the HASS and program teams in developing mitigation strategies. 
 Provide technical support to program teams in assessing the suitability of establishing operations in new locations 
 Develop relationships with local authorities as needed and other power brokers within IRC’s implementation areas. 
 Promote and support the integration of humanitarian access approaches into program design and implementation. 
 Constantly monitor available sources to collect, compile and report information to the Senior HASS Coordinator including incidents and trends pertinent to humanitarian access in areas of operations 
 Support key field management teams to develop and implement community engagement strategies that promote acceptance and access. 
 Support the Senior HASS Coordinator to ensure that IRC’s visibility strategy and profile support principled humanitarian access. 
 Safety and Security Risk Management 
 Provide technical support to the field offices and program teams on all policies, procedures, guidelines and planning for staff safety, and program continuity in Ukraine. 
 Contribute to the development of and updating of Security Risk Assessments (SRA) for field sites. 
 Contribute to the development and updating of Field Security Management Plans (SMP), including all associated contingency plans and SOPs. 
 Monitor the rollout and implementation of SOPs and contingency plans at a field level ensuring compliance. 
 Ensure effective security risk management plans for cross-border access to field sites, principally through border crossings to/from Moldova. 
 Ensure contingency plans for hibernation, relocation, and evacuation are known to ield staff and exercise regularly. 
 Ensure that all program locations and routes are routinely assessed by the HASS team to identify access and security risks in a timely manner. 
 Ensure all field locations meet requirements for safety and security supplies and equipment including hibernation kits, first aid kits and emergency communications. 
 Ensure the emergency warden systems in field locations are fit-for-purpose and tested regularly. 
 As requested by field teams, conduct risk assessments in new geographic locations identified for program implementation. 
 Deploy alongside program teams to high-risk areas and establish deployment protocols commensurate to the risk assessed. 
 Conduct field visits to all IRC field offices and cover HASS teams gaps when requested. 
 Deputize the Senior Humanitarian Access, Safety & Security Coordinator as requested. 
 Demonstrated experience operating at a senior / strategic level with the ability to deputize for and cover the most senior in-country security role 
 Capacity Building 
 Liaise with the HASSM to jointly draft the annual capacity building plan based on the key risks faced by frontline staff. 
 Support the delivery of training to field staff; deliver trainings as needed and relevant. 
 Support the Senior HASS Coordinator to identify the capacity-building needs of the HASS team based on the needed capacities and skills to ensure safe, secure and principled humanitarian access. 
 Provide on-the-job capacity building for the HASS team through mentoring, coaching, and guidance. 
 Support the HASS team to strengthen and expand the capacity of field teams to prepare and respond in a timely manner to emerging emergencies 
 Support the HASS team to deliver staff awareness and training sessions. 
 Support the Senior HASS Coordinator to develop and deliver training on Critical Incident Management. 
 In coordination with the Senior HASS Coordinator, develop a plan to promote national talent within the team to assume more responsibility. 
 Context Monitoring and Reporting 
 Monitor open sources and available information to identify changes in the context of heightened tensions. 
 Support the Senior HASS Coordinator in ensuring field teams are appropriately advised of the risk environment, and preparedness actions are implemented. 
 Support the HASS team to compile regular context updates to monitor issues that could impact program delivery. 
 Work closely with the HASS team to ensure all incidents and accidents are reported on IRC’s online system within 48 hours of the incident occurring.  
 Support the Senior HASS Coordinator in scenario planning exercises. 
 REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS 
 Reports to: Senior Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Coordinator 
 Supervises: None. 
 Key Internal Relationships: HASS Manager, HASS Officers and Assistants, Field Coordinators 
 Key External Relationships: Local partners, INGOs operating in field locations, Security and Access Working Groups, local authorities and stakeholders relevant to program delivery 
 REQUIREMENTS 
 Job Requirements 
 Work Experience: 
 A University degree in a subject relevant to humanitarian action or security such as International Relations or Political Science. 
 Minimum of 5 years humanitarian safety, security and access management experience with an INGO, including demonstrated capability in planning, organizing and executing security operations in the field.  
 Demonstrated security leadership skills including operating independently with limited oversight. This role is a senior-level experienced and independent contributor. 
 Demonstrated experience managing safety, security and humanitarian access across multiple high-risk or conflict-affected country contexts is required Strong understanding of the humanitarian principles required. 
 Demonstrated experience negotiating and expanding humanitarian access in active conflict / frontline environments Knowledge of communications technology including satellite communications. 
 Strong experience as a trainer. 
 Ability to provide dynamic verbal and written briefings on short notice. 
 Able to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively to internal and external stakeholders. 
 Exceptional organizational and coordination skills 
 Excellent relationship-building, interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively represent IRC at forums and with external stakeholders 
 Experience working successfully with local stakeholders such as local and international NGOs and government with sensitivity and diplomacy. 
 Knowledge of GIS and Google Earth

A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions.  Program Brief 
  The humanitarian situation in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt), has resulted in unprecedented needs among children and families. Repeated cycles of conflict, displacement, destruction of infrastructure, and limited access to essential services have significantly impacted children's wellbeing, development, learning, and protection. Young children and caregivers face heightened psychosocial stress and barriers to accessing quality early childhood development and education services.
 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) delivers integrated humanitarian programming across the occupied Palestinian territory, including education, early childhood development, protection, women's protection and empowerment, economic recovery and development, and emergency response programming. IRC works closely with local partners and communities to ensure children and families have access to high-quality, safe, and inclusive services that support their wellbeing and resilience.
 Position Overview 
  Under the supervision of the ECD Manager, the ECD Officer will support the implementation and monitoring of ECD programming across the Gaza Strip. The position will work closely with teachers, facilitators, implementing partners, and community-based actors to support activity implementation, field monitoring, data collection and verification, reporting, and routine technical support.
  The ECD Officer will support trainings and capacity-strengthening activities, contribute to the use and contextualization of approved ECD tools and resources, and support procurement and activity planning processes, including the preparation and follow-up of Purchase Requests (PRs). The role will document project achievements, lessons learned, and implementation challenges, and provide regular updates to the ECD Manager. The ECD Officer will also collaborate closely with IRC program and operational teams, participate in coordination meetings as requested, and support effective implementation and service delivery across the Gaza Strip. 
Major Responsibilities
 1. Program Implementation & Monitoring 
 Support the implementation and monitoring of ECD activities across the Gaza Strip in line with approved workplans, targets, and technical guidance.
 Conduct regular field visits to monitor activities, verify progress, identify challenges, and provide implementation support as needed.
 Track implementation progress against workplans and targets, and escalate challenges, risks, and delays to the supervisor.
 Support the implementation of ECD activities in emergency and crisis-affected settings, and flag adaptation needs based on field realities.
 Raise and follow up on Purchase Requests (PRs) in Integra in accordance with approved procurement plans, and track the delivery and use of program materials and services.
 Support MEAL processes, including data collection, data verification, routine data quality checks, monthly ITT updates, and maintaining accurate activity records and supporting documentation.
 Support client feedback and accountability mechanisms and share findings with the supervisor.
 Document project achievements, lessons learned, success stories, and implementation updates.
 Ensure adherence to safeguarding, protection, and inclusion standards across all activities.
 2. Technical Support & Capacity Strengthening 
 Provide routine technical support and on-the-job coaching to facilitators, teachers, community workers, and partner staff using approved tools and guidance.
 Support the delivery of trainings, coaching sessions, and other capacity-strengthening activities.
 Support the use and contextualization of approved ECD tools, learning materials, and training resources.
 Promote the integration of nurturing care, play-based learning, caregiver wellbeing, and psychosocial support approaches within ECD activities.
 Collaborate with Education, Child Protection, WPE, Health, Nutrition, WASH, ERD, and MEAL teams to support integrated service delivery and referrals.
 Identify implementation challenges, capacity gaps, and emerging needs, and communicate them to the supervisor.
 3. Coordination & Partner Engagement 
 Maintain regular communication with implementing partners and follow up on activity implementation and agreed action points.
 Support partner monitoring visits and document implementation challenges, achievements, and capacity needs.
 Coordinate with IRC program and operational teams, including MEAL, Supply Chain, Finance, HR, HAS, and Field Management, to support effective implementation.
 Support information sharing and follow-up with government entities, local organizations, and other stakeholders as requested by the supervisor.
 Participate in coordination meetings, technical working groups, and field visits as requested by the supervisor.
 4. Reporting, Documentation & Compliance 
 Prepare and submit timely field visit reports, activity updates, indicator tracking information, success stories, and other routine program documentation.
 Contribute data, documentation, and implementation updates for donor reports, assessments, presentations, and program briefs.
 Provide regular updates on implementation progress and highlight risks, challenges, and follow-up actions to the supervisor.
 Ensure adherence to IRC Safety and Security SOPs and promptly report concerns or incidents.
 Uphold IRC values, safeguarding standards, and professional conduct.
 Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor to support program implementation and development.
 Requirements 
 Bachelor's degree in Education, Early Childhood Development, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
 Minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in ECD, Education, or child-focused programming with an NGO or INGO.
 Experience working in humanitarian, emergency, or development contexts in Palestine is preferred.
 Knowledge of early childhood development, play-based learning, school readiness, literacy, and numeracy approaches.
 Experience supporting training, coaching, and capacity-strengthening activities for teachers, facilitators, or partner staff.
 Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with diverse stakeholders.
 Ability to work effectively under pressure and adapt to evolving operational contexts.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
 Good written and spoken English skills.
 Ability and willingness to travel across the Gaza Strip, as access and security conditions permit.

 The Senior Partnerships Finance Manager is a key position for the Partnerships Finance Unit which provides support to IRC programs implemented inside Lebanon. The position is primarily responsible for providing oversight and day-to-day financial management of the IRC Partnerships Unit sub-awardees, in very close coordination and collaboration with the IRC’s internal Finance & Program staff. The position will be responsible for capacity building for sub-awardees in Lebanon to build their financial management, in coordination with the partners, Partnerships Department staff, and IRC Finance staff. The Senior Partnerships Finance Manager will work in close collaboration with staff in the Program teams, the Grants and Finance teams. This position will provide support to the Partnerships Department to review sub-awardee budgets at the proposal stage, participate in pre-award vetting processes, document all financial matters related to sub-awardees’ finances to assure audit readiness, and lead sub-awardee finances documents/reports including budget review, financial report review, providing guidance and training related to finance to sub-awardees in order to strengthen their capacity. The Senior Partnerships Finance Manager acts as the focal point for financial and compliance aspects of Partnerships Unit for sub-awardees, including ensuring high-quality financial monitoring of sub-awardees. This position reports directly to the Deputy Director of Finance. 
 Specific Responsibilities: 
 Management, Coordination, and Oversight: 
 Lead and oversee the Partnership Finance function, ensuring effective financial management, compliance, and risk mitigation across all partner-managed awards. 
 Participate in partner proposal review and modification processes, with a focus on sub-awardee budgets, in coordination with the Partnerships Department at the Country Program (CP). 
 Participate in case management meetings with program, finance, supply chain, and other relevant staff to address partner-related financial and operational issues and ensure coordinated responses. 
 Ensure proactive communication with sub-awardees regarding financial reporting requirements and timelines and communicate delays or issues to relevant team members and the Deputy Director of Finance (DDF). 
 Submit regular summaries of reported expenditures and partner spending plans to the DDF, outlining key issues and follow-up actions. 
 Provide technical guidance and mentoring to finance and partnerships staff involved in sub-grant management, strengthening internal capacity and ensuring consistent application of policies and procedures. 
 Maintain oversight of all partner-related financial and compliance trackers (reconciliation of partner’s accounts), to ensure they are regularly updated and reconciled, and prepare consolidated monthly partner finance reports for the DDF. 
 Financial Management and Reporting 
 Supervise the verification of partners’ financial reports and supporting documents, ensuring expenses are reasonable, allowable, and allocable to the approved budget and compliant with donor regulations. 
 Communicate review findings to partners, ensure timely follow-up, and document resolutions. Reviews should be conducted based on partner risk level, using sampling or full documentation review as required. 
 Review and validate partners’ spending plans against reported expenditure, following up with sub-awardees as needed. 
 Ensure sub-awardee financial reports are reviewed, approved, and signed by the appropriate IRC authority. 
 Prepare fully coded Journal Vouchers, upload the relevant vouchers and financial reports into the INTEGRA ERP system for review and approval by DDF. 
 Respond to financial queries from IRC Headquarters related to submitted partner financial reports. 
 Oversee reconciliation of sub-grantee advances on a monthly basis and report overdue or unliquidated advances to the DDF. 
 E nsure all sub-grant financial tracking tools are accurate, up-to-date, and maintained on a monthly basis. 
 Sub-Grants Payments and Disbursement Management: 
 Oversee and review the preparation of payments requests for sub-awardees, including advances and reimbursements. 
 Track the status of payment releases, track disbursements, and communicate payment status to sub-awardees in a timely manner. 
 Confirm receipt of funds with sub-awardees and follow up as needed.

offres.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 CONTEXTO IRC:
 El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a algunas de las crisis humanitarias más complejas del mundo, brindando asistencia vital y apoyo para que las personas afectadas por conflictos, desastres y desplazamientos forzados puedan recuperarse y reconstruir sus vidas. Fundado en 1933 a solicitud de Albert Einstein, el IRC trabaja actualmente en más de 40 países y 22 ciudades de Estados Unidos, promoviendo la seguridad, la dignidad y la resiliencia de millones de personas en situación de vulnerabilidad.
 En Venezuela, el IRC desarrolla programas de salud, nutrición, agua, saneamiento e higiene (ASH), protección, educación y recuperación económica para responder a las necesidades de las poblaciones más afectadas por la crisis humanitaria. Esta respuesta cobró especial relevancia tras los terremotos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026 en la región central del país, los cuales provocaron importantes pérdidas humanas, afectaciones a la infraestructura crítica y una significativa presión sobre el sistema de salud. En consecuencia, el IRC fortaleció su respuesta humanitaria para atender las necesidades urgentes de las comunidades afectadas, complementando sus programas regulares con acciones de emergencia y recuperación temprana.
 Como parte de este esfuerzo, y en coordinación con la Organización Panamericana de la Salud/Organización Mundial de la Salud (OPS/OMS) y las autoridades nacionales, el IRC acompaña a una organización socia en el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades institucionales, técnicas y operativas para avanzar hacia el reconocimiento como Equipo Médico de Emergencia (EMT) Tipo 1 Móvil, de acuerdo con los estándares establecidos en el Libro Azul de la OMS/OPS y el marco nacional de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias.
 Descripción general del trabajo: 
 El/la Gerente EMT será responsable de liderar el acompañamiento técnico y estratégico a las organizaciones socias que implementan proyectos de salud del IRC, garantizando la calidad programática de las intervenciones, el cumplimiento de los estándares técnicos y regulatorios, el fortalecimiento institucional y la ejecución efectiva de los servicios de salud. Esta posición desempeñará un rol clave en asegurar que las actividades implementadas por los socios se desarrollen de acuerdo con los estándares del IRC, los requisitos de los donantes, la normativa nacional vigente y los principios humanitarios, promoviendo una respuesta de salud oportuna, de calidad y centrada en las necesidades de la población afectada.
 Adicionalmente, el/la Gerente EMT liderará el acompañamiento técnico al socio implementador en su proceso de fortalecimiento y preparación para el reconocimiento como Equipo Médico de Emergencia (EMT) Tipo 1 Móvil, conforme a los estándares establecidos por la OMS/OPS. Esto incluirá la realización de procesos de autoevaluación institucional, el desarrollo y fortalecimiento de Procedimientos Operativos Estándar (POE) clínicos, administrativos y logísticos, la consolidación de estructuras y mecanismos de despliegue, así como el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de preparación, respuesta y recuperación ante emergencias y desastres. Para ello, mantendrá una estrecha articulación con la OPS/OMS, la CICOM, el Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS), Protección Civil y demás actores relevantes del sistema nacional de respuesta.
 Objetivos: 
 Acompañar técnicamente al socio en su ruta hacia el reconocimiento como EMT Tipo 1 Móvil, con base en el Libro Azul de la OMS/OPS (autoevaluación, POE y estructura institucional).
 Fortalecer las capacidades de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias y desastres del socio y de su red local.
 Coordinar con la OPS/OMS, la CICOM, el MPPS, Protección Civil y otros actores de respuesta (incluidas brigadas de emergencia) para alinear el proceso con el marco nacional.
 Apoyar a la coordinación de Salud con el portafolio de proyectos.
 Gestionar los proyectos, cumplimiento y presupuesto.
 Realizar informes de análisis de datos de los proyectos.
 RESPONSABILIDADES PRINCIPALES
 Preparación y respuesta a emergencias / Equipos Médicos de Emergencia (EMT) 
 Fortalecer las capacidades de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias del socio implementador.
 Acompañar al socio en su ruta hacia el reconocimiento como Equipo Médico de Emergencia (EMT).
 Articular el proceso con las instancias nacionales y los actores de respuesta.
 Acompañar al socio en su fortalecimiento frente a los estándares de la OMS/OPS para EMT (autoevaluación, POE y estructura interna de despliegue).
 Participar en el análisis de riesgos y capacidades y en los planes de contingencia y alerta temprana.
 Facilitar capacitaciones y simulacros, y aportar criterios técnicos al plan de compras.
 Coordinar con la OPS/OMS, la CICOM, el MPPS, Protección Civil y las brigadas, y documentar avances y lecciones aprendidas.
 Gestión de Programa y Liderazgo técnico
 Liderar la gestión integral del ciclo de proyectos bajo su responsabilidad, incluyendo diseño, planificación, implementación, monitoreo, adaptación y cierre.
 Garantizar la calidad técnica, pertinencia y efectividad de las intervenciones de salud implementadas por los socios del IRC.
 Asegurar el cumplimiento de metas, indicadores, cronogramas, acuerdos de subvención y compromisos con donantes.
 Identificar riesgos programáticos y operativos, proponiendo oportunamente medidas de mitigación y acciones correctivas.
 Promover la integración de las intervenciones de salud con otros sectores programáticos del IRC y con las prioridades del sistema nacional de salud.
 Asegurar la disponibilidad y uso de información programática para la toma de decisiones y la mejora continua de los proyectos.

 Liderar la implementación de sistemas de gestión de calidad y mejora continua para los programas de salud y fortalecimiento EMT.
 Garantizar el cumplimiento de la normativa nacional, estándares institucionales, lineamientos sectoriales y requisitos de los donantes.
 Supervisar auditorías, evaluaciones, visitas regulatorias y planes de mejora asociados a los proyectos bajo su responsabilidad.
 Velar por la calidad, integridad, confidencialidad y protección de la información clínica y programática.
 Gestión de equipos
 Proporcionar liderazgo técnico y programático al equipo bajo su supervisión, promoviendo una cultura de colaboración, aprendizaje y rendición de cuentas.
 Establecer objetivos claros, monitorear el desempeño del personal y brindar retroalimentación continua.
 Fortalecer las capacidades técnicas y de gestión del equipo mediante procesos de mentoría, acompañamiento y capacitación.
 Asegurar una adecuada planificación del trabajo y asignación de recursos para el logro de los objetivos programáticos.
 Monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y aprendizaje
 Supervisar, manejar, socializar y monitorear los indicadores de salud junto con el equipo de salud y otros miembros del personal de la organización, incluidos los indicadores de fortalecimiento institucional y de preparación como EMT.

 Job Overview: 
 The Admin & Logistics Officer is responsible for providing effective and efficient administrative, logistical, and operational support to the organization's office and project activities. This role ensures that all administrative and logistical procedures are implemented in accordance with IRC policies, donor requirements, and local regulations.
 Under the technical supervision of the Admin and Logistics Manager and the hierarchical supervision of the Field Coordinator, he/she will be responsible for the following:

 Provide general administrative support to the office and program staff.
 Manage office supplies and stationery, ensuring stock levels are maintained and replenished.

 Organize and coordinate meetings, workshops, and events, including venue booking, material preparation, and travel arrangements for participants.
 Liaise with external partners, vendors, and local authorities as needed for administrative matters.
 Ensure timely payment of utility bills and other office-related expenses.

 Ensure proper management of office keys, access control, furniture, fittings and other facility-related resources.
 Monitor the performance of contracted facility service providers and ensure services are delivered in accordance with agreed standards.
 2. Logistics ( Assets, Inventory, fleet management)

 Manage all travel arrangements for staff and visitors, including flight bookings, hotel reservations, and visa applications.
 Manage the day-to-day operations of the organization's fleet, ensuring vehicles are available, safe, roadworthy and appropriately utilized.
 Develop and maintain vehicle maintenance schedules, service histories, inspection records and vehicle documentation.
 Manage the organization's inventory and warehouse, ensuring proper storage and documentation of all incoming and outgoing goods.

 Ensure all organizational assets are properly recorded, tagged, labelled and assigned to responsible custodians.
 Maintain property documentation, including ownership documents, leases, rental agreements, security deposits and related records.
 Monitor lease expiration dates, rental obligations, property-related taxes and registration requirements.
 Coordinate office and property handovers, closures and landlord negotiations in collaboration with relevant departments.
 Monitor fuel consumption, mileage, vehicle utilization, fuel card transactions and associated operational costs.

 Supervise drivers, monitor their performance and ensure compliance with vehicle management procedures, safety standards and movement authorization requirements.

 Coordinate asset allocation, transfers between offices, staff handovers and returns of assets from departing personnel.
 Ensure proper documentation and authorization of asset disposal, write-offs, donations and auction processes.
 Ensure asset records are reconciled with the organization's ERP system and financial records.
 Ensure all incoming and outgoing stock transactions are accurately and promptly recorded in the organization's ERP system.

 Assist in budget monitoring for administrative and logistical activities.
 Coordinate with program, supply chain, finance, security and other relevant departments to ensure effective operational support.
 Tax declarations, compliance and timely adherence to tax requirements for all lease contracts and internal / external financial commitments of the organization.

 4. Safety and Security 
 Act as a security focal point, ensuring all staff are aware of and adhere to security protocols and measures.
 Support the implementation of health and safety policies to ensure a safe working environment.
 Report any security concerns or incidents to the relevant supervisor.

 Proficiency in using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and other relevant software or ERP systems
 Excellent organizational, planning, and problem-solving skills.

 Titre : Manager Protection

 Grade : 7B

 CONTEXTE 
 L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale. Elle a été fondée en 1933, à l’initiative du célèbre physicien Albert Einstein. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC est l’un des leaders mondiaux en matière de secours, de réhabilitation, de protection, de développement post-conflit, de réinsertion et de plaidoyer pour les personnes affectées par les crises. La mission de l’IRC est d’aider les personnes dont les vies et les moyens de subsistance sont détruits par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, se relever et prendre en main leur avenir. 
 IRC est actif en République centrafricaine depuis fin 2006 et dispose d’un bureau principal à Bangui, d’une base à Bocaranga, d’un bureau projet à Ndele, IRC intervient dans plusieurs secteurs. 
 Le programme de gouvernance et renforcement des systèmes à travers le projet « Appui à la société civile en République Centrafricaine » financé par l’Union européenne, est mis en œuvre par IRC en consortium avec les partenaires EEDD, OJLD et OFCA. IRC et ses partenaires ont pour mission de renforcer les OSC centrafricaines en tant qu'acteurs indépendants de bonne gouvernance et de développement au niveau national et contribuer au renforcement d’un espace inclusif, participatif, autonome, indépendant et démocratique promouvant un dialogue ouvert entre les OSC dans les préfectures de Nana-Gribizi, Bangui, Ombela Mpoko, l’Ouham, Lobaye, Nana Mambere, Mambere-Kadei, Sanga Mbaeré, Ouaka ; dont les communes respectives sont Kaga-Bandoro, Bangui et Bimbo Boali, Bossangoa, Mbaïki, Bouar, Berberati, Nola, Bambari, pour une période de trois ans. 
 Le Programme PAF (Protection et autonomisation de la femme) contribue à créer des cadres tant à l’échelle locale que national, de concertation, dialogue, impliquant les femmes et les filles, où leurs voix sont appliquées, où les décisions prises sont centrées sur la satisfaction des leurs besoins primaires, de leurs intérêts stratégiques et où leur protection fait partie intégrante des priorités gouvernementales. Il s’agit ici de renforcer les stratégies de développement du leadership des femmes et des filles, de promouvoir la prévention, la réponse et l’atténuation des risques des VBG/EAS à travers les approches innovantes. Le Programme PAF IRC soutient le mécanisme de la coordination VBG en RCA en collaboration avec UNFPA et les autres acteurs du domaine de responsabilité (AoR VBG). Le programme travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère du Genre et soutient la stratégie Nationale sur la protection et autonomisation de femmes et filles. Dans le cadre de la Protection et Etat de droit ( PRoL), le Programme assure à ce que les personnes sont en mesure d’accéder à la justice et d’exercer leurs droits, Les femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons ont les informations et le soutien nécessaires pour demander justice et y accéder de manière indépendante. Des services de protection de qualité, y compris la gestion de cas/ soutien psychosocial, le monitoring de protection, le renforcement des capacités des acteurs, la documentation civile ainsi que le renforcement du système juridique et des espaces communautaires sûrs et accessibles pour femmes, les hommes, les filles et les garçons. 
 Le programme Relèvement et Développement Economique (ERD) travaille à faire en sorte que les besoins fondamentaux de survie des personnes que nous servons soient satisfaits et qu’elles disposent d’une combinaison d’actifs et de revenus pour prospérer. Le programme s’assure que les personnes répondent à leurs besoins fondamentaux et protègent leurs moyens de subsistance en cas d’urgence, qu’elles développent leurs moyens de subsistance et se remettent des chocs et afin que les personnes deviennent autonomes et jouissent d’une stabilité économique à long terme. 
 Le programme protection de l’enfant et développement des jeunes (CYPD) répond aux violations de la protection des enfants à travers les approches centrées sur l’enfant, le renforcement de la famille et de la communauté ainsi que le renforcement du système de protection de l’enfance. Le programme renforce les familles et les communautés pour aider à prévenir les violations de la protection de l'enfance et à y répondre lorsqu'elles se produisent à travers des approches " préventives", que " préventives et réactives » adaptées au genre et aux âges. 
 Le programme santé, nutrition et wash organise l’offre des soins curatifs, préventifs et promotionnels avec un focus sur la santé des groupes vulnérables comme le couple mère-enfant, des adolescents et jeunes en appuyant les formations sanitaires existantes, des cliniques mobiles, les sites de soins communautaires ou toute autre structure communautaire pouvant améliorer l’accès et/ ou la qualité des soins de santé, de nutrition ou de l’hygiène individuelle et collective. 
 Le programme Education , donne aux enfants les plus vulnérables un accès au primaire, transition vers le premier cycle et le secondaire.  Tout particulièrement les filles et les enfants affectés par des crises, notamment les déplacés, pour une amélioration de vie dans les zones ciblées par le projet à travers la formation des enseignants, distribution des différentes kits scolaires pédagogiques, récréatifs et dignité, mise en place des groupes Kundukwa et les différents suivis pédagogiques par les Conseillers pédagogiques. 
 IRC en République centrafricaine met actuellement en œuvre son plan stratégique " Stratégie 100", à travers lequel nous visons à fournir le meilleur impact possible pour les garçons, filles, femmes et hommes les plus vulnérables touchés par les crises humanitaires. Dans tout ce que nous faisons, nous nous efforçons de respecter les valeurs fondamentales d’IRC que sont l'intégrité, la responsabilité, le service et l'égalité.

Il sera basé(e) à Bocaranga et travaillera sous la supervision de la Senior Manager Protection. Elle/il supervise les Officiers Protection de l’enfance(klinsky) et Psychosocial(e) (Echo), directement et les Assistants Protection, indirectement.  IRC’s AI Transformation Priorities set three aims: deploying new tools, reshaping workflows so that teams redesign how work gets done, and reinventing models so that services reach more people faster, at greater scale and at lower cost. The AI Policy is the responsible-use foundation under all three. The AI Learning Strategy is how IRC builds the skills, habits and shared practice behind those aims. This role contributes mainly to the second aim: helping Crisis Response, Recovery & Deliver (CRRD) teams redesign how work gets done. The CRRD Department implements our work, with staff on the frontlines of program delivery to provide high-quality programming with impactful results for the people we serve.
 Job Overview: 
 We are hiring an AI Adoption Lead to help embed AI in the day-to-day work of CRRD teams. A primary part of this role is understanding how work actually gets done, deciding which tasks AI should perform and which should stay with people (with accountability always remaining human), and reconstructing workflows accordingly. You will work alongside teams as a standing resource, diagnosing workflows, co-designing AI-enabled solutions, and building the local capacity teams need to sustain adoption on their own.
 The role has two connected parts. First, you will be an AI adoption partner for CRRD, supporting multiple teams at once rather than embedding with one team at a time: providing hands-on guidance, building reusable tools and templates, and cultivating superusers who become self-sustaining champions within their own teams. Second, you will play a key role in delivering the IRC’s AI Learning Strategy. That means partnering with Global Learning & Development (L&D), AI Learning and Change Management working groups, and CRRD colleagues to build experiential learning opportunities like workflow design workshops and master classes. 
 This is a limited-term role through September 2027. At the conclusion, success means that CRRD teams will work differently, not because of any single tool, but because redesigned workflows are in routine use, managers model their own AI use, and local champions sustain the practice without central support. 
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Capacity Building & Adoption in CRRD 
 Provide hands-on coaching, training, and feedback loops that build staff comfort and competence with AI tools.
 Facilitate Workflow Design Sprints (short, structured working sessions in which a team maps a real workflow and builds an AI-enabled version of it) with CRRD teams, helping them develop sophisticated, multi-step prompting workflows.
 Monitor adoption and usage patterns across CRRD, adjusting approach to ensure sustained uptake rather than one-off experiments.
 Work with L&D on ways to showcase what teams with AI users have created, show what they gained, and sustain AI-enabled practices after direct engagement ends.
 Workflow Diagnosis & AI Solution Design 
 Work alongside teams to map and diagnose existing workflows, identifying high-value opportunities for AI-enabled improvement and deciding which tasks AI should perform and which should stay with people.
 Build and scale reusable AI-enabled solutions (e.g., prompt & skill libraries, tools, and workflow templates) that can be deployed across teams.
 Ensure solutions are practical, sustainable, and designed for handoff, not dependent on ongoing central support.
 Delivering the AI Learning Strategy  
 In partnership with other AI Adoption Leads and Global Learning & Development, build, adapt and run learning for CRRD staff, including self-paced learning and live learning such as master classes.
 Run peer learning events that show people in the same role what AI has done for colleagues like them: Open Hours, live demos, learning segments in existing department or location meetings. 
 Help teams apply the repository standard for shared workflows, so that what teams build is verified, curated and published in a form other teams can reuse.
 Contribute to CRRD AI adoption metrics in partnership with CRRD and AI program leadership. Track and report to leadership quarterly. 
 Quality Assurance & Responsible AI Use 
 Make responsible use a practice, not a policy read once: help staff learn what must not be entered into AI tools, how to check the output, and how to own it, with particular care for beneficiary and other sensitive program data, safeguarding, and data protection.
 Contribute to organizational thinking about responsible AI use, ensuring practices reflect both ambition and rigor.
 Help teams apply “what good looks like” for AI-enabled solutions in CRRD (quality checks, human review expectations, evaluation approaches, and documentation), and make sure solutions meet that bar before broad rollout.
 Work with [IRC’s AI governance team] so that CRRD practice stays consistent with the AI Policy and the approval process for new AI tools and uses.
 AI Systems, Intake & Scalable Infrastructure 
 Maintain the playbooks, prompt libraries, and workflow templates (in partnership with programs staff) that allow AI-enabled practices to scale, sharing them with the other two AI Adoption Leads and Global L&D so that what is built for one area is reused in others.
 Document lessons learned, edge cases, and best practices in accessible formats that enable self-service adoption.
 Continuously update resources as AI capabilities evolve, staying current with frontier AI developments and proactively identifying new opportunities, ensuring the toolkit reflects what is currently possible.
 Feed insights, best practices, and emerging AI capabilities from your work into the AI Learning Working Group and IRC’s broader AI Transformation efforts.

 4–7 years of relevant professional experience (e.g., process improvement, product management, solutions engineering, operations, learning and development, or change management), with increasing recent focus on applying AI tools to personal and/or team workflows.
 fluent in AI platforms, particularly Claude (IRC’s primary platform for this work; hands-on experience with other frontier AI platforms is also valued), and stays current as capabilities evolve. comfort executing sophisticated, multi-step prompting against real operational data / context and using AI to generate and iterate on functional tools (e.g., dashboards, automations, lightweight applications).

 The ServiceNow Developer will support the administration, configuration, maintenance, documentation, reporting, testing, and end-user support of the IRC’s ServiceNow platform.
