 Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, and analytics to support operational performance, trend analysis, compliance, and decision-making. 
 Produce and maintain technical documentation, configuration documentation, user guides, admin guides, training materials, and Knowledge Base articles related to ServiceNow functionality and platform support. 
 Support agile delivery by helping prioritize, estimate, update, and complete assigned stories, tasks, incidents, and requests while communicating progress, risks, and blockers to the Senior System Administrator and relevant stakeholders. 
 Develop training materials and conduct ServiceNow training sessions for users, administrators, and stakeholders as needed, including at least once per quarter .

 Contexte / Présentation de l’IRC 
 International Rescue Committee (IRC) est une organisation humanitaire apolitique, à but non lucratif et non religieuse qui vient en aide aux réfugiés du monde entier. L'IRC met en œuvre des programmes visant à promouvoir des solutions durables pour les personnes déplacées, les réfugiés et les communautés d'accueil par le biais de projets de santé publique, d'assainissement, d'abris, de réhabilitation et d'éducation. IRC sert les réfugiés depuis 1933 et est présent dans 40 pays d'Europe, d'Afrique et d'Asie, ainsi que par le biais d'un programme de soutien à la réinstallation aux États-Unis. IRC est une organisation engagée en faveur de la liberté, de la dignité humaine et de l'autonomie. Cet engagement se traduit par une aide à la réinstallation bien planifiée, une aide d'urgence mondiale, la réhabilitation et la défense des réfugiés.
 IRC a commencé ses opérations au Cameroun en 2016 pour répondre aux préoccupations croissantes des personnes affectées par les violences liées à Boko Haram, dans l'Extrême-Nord du pays. L'assistance aux populations déplacées s'étend à tout l'Extrême-Nord, notamment au Diamaré, au Mayo Sava, au Mayo Tsanaga et au Logone & Chari par le biais du bureau de terrain à Maroua. IRC met en œuvre des programmes pour augmenter l'accès à l'eau et améliorer les pratiques d'hygiène dans les communautés vulnérables déplacées et d'accueil, des programmes de cash transfert pour permettre aux familles économiquement défavorisées de répondre aux besoins de base et d'améliorer la sécurité alimentaire. Cela comprend à la fois des services d'éducation et de protection de l'enfance pour répondre aux besoins et aux priorités des enfants en matière d'apprentissage et de sécurité. IRC propose également des programmes de protection pour lutter contre la violence sexiste à l'égard des femmes et des filles et pour soutenir les victimes de violations des droits de l'homme.
 À la suite de la crise croissante dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest du Cameroun, IRC a étendu ses opérations dans la région du Sud-Ouest en 2018 et dans le Nord-Ouest en 2019. IRC fournit une aide humanitaire vitale aux populations déplacées à l'intérieur du pays, avec des bases de terrain à Buea et Bamenda.

 Sous la supervision directe du Coordinateur Éducation, le/la Education Manager sera responsable de la mise en œuvre effective, du suivi et du rapportage des projets d’éducation au Cameroun, en veillant au respect des exigences des bailleurs, des standards techniques et des politiques organisationnelles.
 Le/la Education Manager garantira la qualité et la redevabilité des interventions, en favorisant un environnement de travail collaboratif et constructif qui encourage l’apprentissage, l’innovation et la résolution de problèmes. Il/Elle développera et mettra à jour l’ensemble des outils de gestion de projet (plan de dépenses, plan de passation des marchés, plan de mise en œuvre détaillé – DIP, plan de suivi-évaluation/redevabilité, registre des risques, etc.), tout en assurant une étroite collaboration avec les coordinateurs techniques (Éducation et Protection de l’Enfance).
 Il/Elle représentera l’IRC dans les instances de coordination pertinentes et veillera à l’alignement des activités sur les politiques du Ministère de l’Éducation de Base du Cameroun (MINEDUB).
 Conformément à la Stratégie100 de l’IRC, le/la Education Manager veillera à promouvoir une approche intégrée des programmes, en travaillant en étroite collaboration avec les coordinateurs nationaux des autres secteurs (Relance Économique et Développement – ERD, Santé Environnementale/EHA-WASH, Protection et Autonomisation des Femmes – WPE, Protection et État de Droit – PRoL).

 Animer les réunions hebdomadaires de coordination avec l’équipe projet et les partenaires.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
 The IRC and its consortium partners have been selected by British High Commission (BHC) Kampala for the Refugee Support, Empowerment and Transformation (ReSET) Programme, pillar 1. ReSET programme aims to make Uganda’s refugee response more sustainable and locally owned, while protecting refugees’ rights, delivering lifesaving aid, and supporting self-reliance and resilience.
 The IRC leads Pillar 1 (Lifesaving Assistance) through a local consortium of Refugee-Led Organisations Network (RELON), Transcultural Psychosocial Organisation (TPO) Uganda and Uganda Network on Law, Ethics and HIV/AIDS (UGANET). Pillar 1 meets core needs, such as food security and protection, for the most vulnerable refugees (typically new arrivals) and host communities facing acute shocks. It applies a cash-first principle, primarily multipurpose cash linked to protection and referral systems.
 ReSET will improve the ability of the most vulnerable refugees and host communities to meet core needs, withstand shocks, and avoid negative coping strategies, along with better community cohesion, more resilient local economies, and a more efficient, effective, and sustainable refugee response. The programme is built on vulnerability-based targeting, a “no wrong door” approach, closed-loop referrals, community-informed accountability, and the progressive transfer of leadership to government, national organizations and refugee-led organizations (RLOs). Stabilized households will be voluntarily connected to ReSET Pillar 2 and other self-reliance opportunities, with a route back to humanitarian assistance if vulnerability re-emerges.
 The programme covers 10 refugee settlements across 4 regions (West Nile, Mid-Western, Northern, South-Western), in close coordination with OPM, UN agencies, INGOs, national NGOs and district local governments.

 SCOPE OF WORK: 
 The Cash and Medical Assistance Benefits Specialist will provide comprehensive services and conduct activities related to Cash and Medical Assistance (CMA) programs that are funded by the Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR). The CMA Benefits Specialist will implement Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), Refugee Medical Screening (RMS), and/or Refugee Medical Assistance (RMA) programs as outlined in federal regulations, by KSOR, and the Medical Replacement Designee (MRD), as applicable. The CMA Benefits Specialist will represent the IRC and collaborate and coordinate closely with the donor, other implementing agencies, local stakeholders and service providers.
 Responsibilities: 
 Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:                                                              
 Provide comprehensive and required services to IRC clients enrolling or enrolled in Refugee Cash Assistance, Refugee Medical Services, and/or Refuge Health Screening services;
 Review applications for accuracy and make eligibility determinations, ensuring non-duplication of services.
 Prepare all enrollment documents and conduct enrollment meetings, ensuring clients understand their rights and responsibilities;
 Conduct monthly redetermination meetings to track and plan participation in employment services for the purpose of determining continued eligibility.
 Prepare the enrollment package including Enrollment Letter and Insurance Card and any other items designated by the Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR) or the Medical Replacement Designee (insurer) and conduct enrollment meetings to provide enrollment documents and ensure RMA recipients know their rights and responsibilities.

 Prepare and disseminate case closure documentation according to policies.
 Maintain meticulous documentation and ensure that all deliverables are submitted to KSOR on time and in compliance with the policies and procedures.
 Attend all KSOR-scheduled meetings to coordinate with key stakeholders, Quarterly Forums, training events and collaboration meetings.
 Actively engage with donors and other stakeholders to develop policy and processes, identify ways to improve programs and provide feedback.
 Communicate resettlement trends, including spikes in scheduled arrivals, to donors and medical providers on a regular basis.
 Remain current on topics and the context in which CMA benefits are processed, accessed and used, including the Code of Federal Regulations that relate to each of the benefits available through the Kansas CMA Benefits Program.

 JOB DESCRIPTION 
 Position:    Livelihood Project Assistance 
 Report to: Livelihood Officer 
 Department: Economic Recovery & Development 
 Location: Chinakson woreda of Eastern Oromia 
 Grade: 9A 
 Background: 
 The International Rescue Committee, one of the world’s largest humanitarian international NGOs, provides relief, rehabilitation, and development support to vulnerable people and communities in over 30 countries. We began work in Ethiopia in 2000 in response to severe drought in Ethiopia’s Somali region and are currently providing assistance to Ethiopians and refugees in six regions in Ethiopia, implementing emergency and development programs in health, water and sanitation, economic recovery and development (ERD), women’s protection and empowerment, education, child protection, and multi-sectoral emergency response. 
 The IRC has a focus on narrowing the gender gap in humanitarian aid and ensuring that we contribute to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in both our programs and operations by working to establish a context where our clients (including those from minority groups) enjoy the same rights and opportunities as well as an equal access to services. The IRC also has a strong commitment to creating an equitable and inclusive culture, where safeguarding is upheld in our workplace and programs. We are determined to protect our clients and staff from safeguarding violations through prevention and, where misconduct is alleged, to address it without fear or favor.
 Job Overview/Summary:
 IRC is planning to implement Irish Aid funded BRIDGE Project-to Building Resilience, Inclusion, and Durable Growth for Empowerment of Women, Youth, and Other Shock-Affected Communities in East Hararghe (Chinaksen and Gursum) and Gambella (Itang and Lare) woreda, Ethiopia. The primary Goal of the project is to Improve food security and resilience of vulnerable population against shocks and stress (Resilient Livelihoods and Food Security) in the intervention areas.
 The Livelihood Project Assistance is based in Chinakson town with frequent travel to the field project Kebele. The incumbent reports to the Livelihood Officer on day-to-day project management and implementation. He/She will provide implementation support, technical and project support to target beneficiaries in the whole project cycle implementation. The post holder will support and strengthen the planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the project in Chinakson woreda. He will collaborate closely with other project staff within IRC and among partner agencies, government, private sector, and community groups. She/he will give support to the program to ensure technically sound and complementary programming. The officers will ensure successful support for livelihoods programming which includes implement comprehensive interventions that include climate-smart agriculture, disaster risk reduction (DRR), natural resource management (NRM), livelihood diversification, market system strengthening, and peacebuilding activities, Provision of capacity building support for Livestock treatment and supply of improved crop seeds and other related activities.
 Key Responsibilities and Activities
 • Facilitate community mobilization, awareness creation, and beneficiary sensitization meetings at kebele and village levels.
 • Support beneficiary targeting, registration, verification, and selection processes according to project criteria.
 • Assist in organizing and conducting community assessments, baseline surveys, and data collection exercises.
 • Support the establishment and strengthening of community groups, including VSLA groups, producer groups, youth groups, and women's groups.
 • Coordinate and facilitate community trainings, demonstrations, field days, and experience-sharing events.
 • Provide regular follow-up and technical support to project beneficiaries to ensure effective implementation of project activities.
 • Monitor the progress of beneficiary activities and document success stories, challenges, and lessons learned.
 • Collect, verify, and submit accurate field data, beneficiary records, attendance sheets, and activity reports.
 • Support distribution of project inputs, materials, and productive assets while ensuring transparency and accountability.
 • Maintain close collaboration with community leaders, local government offices, extension workers, and other stakeholders.
 • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project interventions and provide timely feedback to the Project Officer/Manager.
 • Assist in organizing community meetings, workshops, review sessions, and stakeholder consultations.
 • Promote gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, and protection principles during project implementation.
 • Support establishment and strengthening of community-based monitoring, feedback, and accountability mechanisms.
 • Participate in household visits and coaching sessions to encourage adoption of improved livelihood and resilience practices.
 • Facilitate referral and linkage of beneficiaries to government services, financial institutions, cooperatives, and market actors.
 • Identify implementation challenges and communicate them promptly to supervisors with proposed solutions.
 • Ensure proper documentation and filing of project records at community level.
 • Support monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) activities, including surveys and beneficiary feedback collection.
 • Assist in emergency response, rapid assessments, and humanitarian activities when required.
 • Prepare weekly and monthly field activity reports and submit them to the Project Officer/Project Manager.
 • Jointly with the community development agents and the rest of project team actively engage in establishment of Community lead Participatory Learning and Action (PLA) groups and proper implementation of series of PLA session, community action plan and community bylaw development and their implementation to mitigate the climate, livelihood and protection problems and promote behavior changes . 
 Community Coordination Responsibilities
 • Serve as the primary focal person between the project and target communities.
 • Represent the project in community forums and local coordination meetings.
 • Strengthen community ownership and participation in project interventions.
 • Promote conflict-sensitive, culturally appropriate, and inclusive approaches during implementation.
 • Support sustainability plans for community structures and project-supported initiatives.
 Safeguarding Responsibilities: -
 • Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion and cohesion in IRC [team/office]
 • Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies
 Job Requirements: 
 Educational Requirements:
 • Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Agricultural Economics, General Agriculture, and/or related agricultural field of study or certification.
 • 2 years of relevant work experience for Diploma holders 
 • 0 years of relevant work experience for Degree holders 
 • NGO experience is a plus. 
 Preferred experience

The International Rescue Committee (IRC), in partnership with World Vision (WV), Reach A Hand Uganda (RAHU), Humanity & Inclusion (HI), and Open Capital Advisors (OCA), has secured a four-year grant from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN) to implement the PROTECT SRHR project whose major goal is to improve Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) and the social wellbeing of over one million adolescents, young people, and women of reproductive age in six districts of West Nile, Uganda including
 Koboko, Maracha, Terego, Nebbi, Packwach, and Yumbe. The project aims to achieve 04 long-term and 02 intermediate outcomes: Long-term Outcomes:
Reduced preventable maternal deathsReduced teenage pregnanciesReduced sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) and child marriageReduced new HIV infections among adolescents, especially girls Intermediate Outcomes:
Increased access to and utilization of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and SGBV services by women, adolescents, and young people (10-24), including marginalized groups
Improved retention and completion rates of girls and boys in primary and secondary schoolBackground to the SASA Together Baseline Assessment.
 The PROTECT SRHR project employs a comprehensive, community-driven approach to overcoming barriers to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), with a particular emphasis on transforming harmful gender norms and preventing gender-based violence (GBV).To achieve this, the project integrates a variety of complementary methodologies, i.e. SASA! Together for community mobilization against GBV; Girl Shine to empower adolescent girls and their caregivers through life skills and protection-focused mentorship; Engaging Men through Accountable Practices (EMAP) to promote positive masculinities and male allyship in gender equality; and inclusive SRHR programming to ensure the meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and marginalized groups.SASA! Together is a transformative community mobilization approach designed to address the power imbalances that drive violence against women and girls. By empowering adolescents, particularly girls, young people, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups, SASA! Together strengthens their ability to claim their rights and access essential SRHR and GBV services. The methodology is structured around a phased process—Start, Awareness, Support, and Action—that stimulates critical thinking, fosters community dialogue, and activates local leadership to challenge and change harmful gender norms. Through this process, SASA! Together encourages collective action to promote gender equality, safe relationships, and the sustainable prevention of GBV. By engaging community activists, leaders, service providers, and institutions, it enhances the capacity of entire communities to respond to and prevent GBV, fostering long-lasting social change.To ensure the successful implementation of SASA! Together, a baseline assessment will be conducted across the six project districts—Yumbe, Koboko, Terego, Maracha, Nebbi, and Pakwach. The assessment will explore existing knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, and practices related to power dynamics, gender equality, and GBV within the target communities. The findings will provide critical insights for customizing SASA! Together activities and establishing a baseline for tracking progress throughout the project. Moreover, the results will guide the development of targeted interventions, community engagement strategies, and cross-sectoral coordination to strengthen GBV prevention and response efforts.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
Background: 
 Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee (www.rescue.org) is a world leader in relief, rehabilitation and post-conflict development services for those uprooted or affected by violent conflict and oppression. The IRC is currently working in over 40 countries around the world, addressing both the immediate and lifesaving needs of conflict affected people in emergencies and the reconstruction needs of post-conflict societies. The IRC began programming in northern Uganda in 1998 in response to mass displacement and devastation wrought by rebel group, the Lord’s Resistance Army. In 2002, the IRC expanded to the remote, conflict-affected region of Karamoja and in 2011, began working with refugees in Kampala. Monitoring the influx of South Sudanese refugees at the end of 2015, the IRC began scaling up its response to refugees arriving in the West Nile region. By promoting durable solutions that deliver on the interdependent aims of saving lives, strengthening institutions, and supporting social cohesion, the IRC in Uganda is laying the building blocks for long-term stability and development –bringing people from harm to home. The IRC currently works in 9 districts in Uganda, including Kitgum, Lamwo, Kyegegwa, Moroto, Amudat, Yumbe, Arua, Kiryandongo, Kasese and Kampala. The IRC is currently implementing its health and nutrition program in West Nile and Acholi focusing on providing primary health care services to refugees in their settlements. Background :
Le Système des Nations Unies (SNU) en Tunisie a élaboré sa Stratégie des Opérations (BOS) pour renforcer la collaboration entre les agences onusiennes présentes dans le pays et assurer une gestion efficiente et transparente des ressources. Pour soutenir la mise en œuvre de cette stratégie, le SNU s’appuie sur son agence opérationnelle, le Bureau des Nations Unies pour les services d’appui aux projets (UNOPS), qui recrute le personnel chargé d’assurer la sécurité des locaux situés à Tunis et à Zarzis.
L’UNOPS, bras opérationnel des Nations Unies, fournit des services spécialisés en gestion de projet, passation de marchés et infrastructures, contribuant ainsi à l’efficacité et à la durabilité des projets de ses partenaires
Mission du personnel de sécurité. Le personnel de sécurité est responsable de la protection des personnes, des biens et des installations
techniques sur les sites des agences du Système des Nations Unies (sièges, ou centres). Sa mission s’inscrit dans une logique de prévention, de vigilance et d’intervention, contribuant directement à la sûreté des opérations et à la sérénité du personnel.

Mission du personnel de sécurité 
Le personnel de sécurité est responsable de la protection des personnes, des biens et des installations 
techniques sur les sites des agences du Système des Nations Unies (sièges, ou centres). Sa mission 
s’inscrit dans une logique de prévention, de vigilance et d’intervention, contribuant directement à la 
sûreté des opérations et à la sérénité du personnel.
Responsabilités principales :
✓ Assurer la surveillance continue des sites et des équipements sensibles.
✓ Garantir la protection physique des personnes présentes sur les lieux.
✓ Intervenir rapidement en cas d’incident ou d’urgence, en appliquant les consignes de sécurité
(SOP) et en contactant les services compétents.
✓ Informer le/la chef·fe d’équipe de tout incident ou accident survenu.
✓ Préparer et organiser son poste de travail en veillant au respect des règles de santé, sécurité
et environnement (SSE).
✓ Appliquer rigoureusement les instructions techniques transmises par la direction.
✓ Respecter la planification des rondes de surveillance et les horaires établis.
✓ Adopter un comportement professionnel et une communication appropriée sur les sites.
✓ Faire fonctionner et surveiller les systèmes et équipements de sécurité selon les besoins (CCTV,
alarmes, contrôle d’accès,x-ray)
✓ Contrôler l’accès, vérifier l’identité et inspecter les sacs/objets ainsi que les véhicules entrant sur le site.

✓ Capacité à travailler en horaires décalé, y compris les nuits, les jours fériés et les weekends.
✓ Assumer toutes autres taches, en respectant les procédures des agences UN.
Autorité opérationnelle :
Le personnel de sécurité dispose d’une autorité décisionnelle limitée à son périmètre de responsabilité, lui permettant de prendre des décisions immédiates et appropriées dans le cadre de ses fonctions, notamment en situation d’urgence ou de risque identifié.

Bangladesh is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or the 1967 Protocol and the Government does not recognise the Rohingya as refugees, referring to them as “Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals.” The country is generously hosting around one million Rohingya refugees across 33 camps including around 50,000 refugee arrivals who have fled the fighting that erupted in Myanmar in late 2023. The presence of large numbers of refugees – who now represent two-thirds of the local population – has had important impacts on local communities, service delivery, the economy and the environment. The Government sees the continued presence of Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh as a threat to regional stability and considers return to Myanmar, as soon as possible, as the only viable solution. This policy approach impacts on the humanitarian operation, with the Government discouraging medium or longer-term approaches, including the development of permanent infrastructure, providing formal education or livelihoods opportunities for the refugees and the use of cash to deliver assistance
The Associate Protection Officer - Data Protection Focal Point reports to the Assistant Representative- Protection, the Data Protection Focal Point designated by the Representative (the Data Controller) to assist in carrying out her responsibilities under responsibilities under the Policy on the Protection of Personal Data of Persons of Concern to UNHCR (2015) and the General Policy on Personal Data Protection and Privacy (GDPP, 2022), in the Representation in Bangladesh. The position is based in Cox’s Bazar Sub-Office and supports the Field Office on Bhasan Char Island, where the incumbent may be required to undertake missions. The incumbent provides functional expertise and oversight on data protection and offers guidance, standards, and advice – to functional units, as well as to partner organisations in Cox’s Bazar Sub-office and Bhasan Char Field Office – on the processing of personal data of the displaced population and other data subjects under the GDPP, which includes questions regarding the collection, storage, access to, sharing and use of personal data of persons of concern. S/he also provides advice to UNHCR staff on data protection issues and represents the Organization to external partners and other
stakeholders on data protection policy and practice.
The Associate Protection Officer – Data Protection is relied upon by the Office to provide quality, timely and effective data protection guidance, taking into consideration the rights of data subjects and the well-being of populations of concern, as well as UNHCR's operational needs. This includes ensuring that UNHCR staff have the necessary guidance and procedures, based on global policies and guidance, to be both proactive and responsive to data protection issues in ways that ensure the effective functioning of UNHCR's mandate and operations in Cox’s Bazar, including maintaining the trust of persons of concern. The incumbent will formulate and provide advice related to data protection to external partners, as well as respond to queries, including concerning requests for the sharing of personal data and developing data-sharing agreements and
arrangements where appropriate. To achieve this, the incumbent will need to build and maintain effective partnerships with external partners, functional units and field offices in Bangladesh and
relevant colleagues in Headquarters, and the Regional Bureau of Asia and Pacific.
Scope of Duties:
• Draft data sharing agreements or data sharing requests for key partners, including UN Agencies (WFP, IOM, UNICEF), UNHCR-funded partners and partners implementing complementary pathways for education and higher education programs (i.e. University of Geneva, University of Canada (ISOW))
• Train UNHCR-funded partners and partners of the Rohingya Coordination Platform (RCP) on data protection principles and practices
• Update the UNHCR global “One Trust” platform on data protection by guiding UNHCR-funded partners on the process and use it as a capacity-building opportunity
• Assist the Assistant Representative for Protection in preparing the Data Protection and Identity Assessment (DPIA) Addendum on the improved data processing with the Government of Bangladesh and track implementation of the mitigation measures countering the risk identified in the DPIA in “One Trust” platform.
• Collaborate with Supply team in data sharing agreements with suppliers and contractors
• Act as Alternate Data Protection Focal Point for the operation in Bangladesh in support of the Assistant Representative for Protection, Data Protection Focal Point
• Assist the operation with Personal data handover for change / termination of partnerships.
• Updating Data Processing inventory : to reflect changes.
• Drafting of rights procedures, standard responses to objectives etc
• Contribute to the drafting of the volunteer guidance that will be updated in the course of 2026 and reflect in Addendum to DPIA with possible information broadcast to participating agencies ( 86 in number).
• Possibility of revising data sharing arrangements -in light of UNHCR’s coordination role and the DIMA strategy that aims at having the joint Government of Bangladesh–UNHCR registration becoming the foundation on which the response can connect its data, deliver assistance more fairly and efficiently, and measure its impact, , including UNHCR’s collaboration with WFP on the Targeting and Prioritization Exercise (TPE), the necessity to triangulate data with other partners, propose innovative approaches and contribute to the establishment of a deduplication system.
• As part of UNHCR’s commitment to contribute to the consolidation of the Complaint and Feedback Mechanisms (CFM) in the Rohingya Refugee Response, provide technical advice on data protection and sharing matters related to interoperability and referrals of CFM between agencies and organisations.
• Conducting DPIAs/ risk assessments as and when required.
• Drafting DSAs/ MOUs/ other Data sharing arrangements as per thematic areas or needs, including in collaboration with Supply Section for suppliers and contractors. 
• Regularly report to Supervisor and as part of the quarterly UNHCR external report on Protection & Solutions on key activities, achievements and challenges
• Perform other related duties as required

• 3-5 years of working experience in Registration and Identity Management and/or Data Protection. Prior experience in working on data protection 
• Strong knowledge and understanding of registration and identity management and experience in collaborating with partners 
• Experience and knowledge of UNHCR’s policies and procedures on data protection and familiar with data protection tools, including “One Trust”
• Previous experience in a similar position in the UN and/or humanitarian work.
• Previous experience in similar operational settings, including large and protracted refugee response where the coordination is led by UNHCR in close collaboration with the hosting Government
• Strong drafting skills, proven experience in writing data sharing arrangements, Data Protection and Identity Assessment (DPIA) and and related documents.

Bangladesh is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol, and the Government does not recognize the Rohingya as refugees, referring to them as “Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals.” The country hosts [FIGURE TBC] registered stateless Rohingya refugees across 34 camps in Ukhia, Teknaf and Bhasan Char, including [FIGURE TBC] refugees who fled the renewed fighting in Myanmar from late 2023 onwards. The population is administratively segmented into three de-facto status tiers and across numerous administrative boundaries, each with its own Camp-in-Charge (CiC) authorization and certification requirements. 
Registration in Bangladesh is a joint Government of Bangladesh – UNHCR continuous procedure and is the foundational identity registry of the response: it is the only reliable record of Rohingya identity and the basis on which eligibility for assistance, protection and services across the response is determined. Errors in registration therefore directly affect refugees’ access to assistance, protection and services. Given the statelessness of the population — whose refugee claim rests on the systematic eradication of their citizenship, legal status and recorded identity — maintaining the integrity, accuracy and credibility of this registration requires specialized knowledge of stateless registration. 
The operating environment has changed substantially and continues to evolve, expanding the responsibilities carried by the registration function. Key drivers include the implementation of the Refugee Coordination Model and UNHCR’s formalized accountability within it; the roll-out of WFP’s Targeting and Prioritization Exercise (TPE), which relies on and places new strain on registration data and processes; the shift towards an Integrated Analytics-Driven Population Strategy (IAPS) that absorbs verification into routine, data-driven operations; the improved joint data processing with Government counterparts and associated KYC use cases; and a major effort to simplify, harmonize and make data-driven the registration procedures and SOPs across seven registration sites. 
These changes require a new registration structure across all sites. During its set-up and implementation, the new structure needs dedicated capacity building, coaching and oversight of the registration team, so that harmonized procedures are embedded consistently, integrity is maintained and team skills are developed across sites. The position provides this support throughout the transition and the convergence of new operational demands. 
Reporting to the Registration and Identity Management Officer within DIMA, the incumbent will support the management, oversight and harmonization of the joint GoB–UNHCR registration procedures, decision-making and related activities across all registration sites in Ukhia, Teknaf and Bhasan Char. The position covers all sites and requires regular travel across them, including to Bhasan Char. The incumbent will contribute to developing and implementing the operation’s registration strategy in line with overall protection objectives and the joint role with the Government, and will support the transition to simplified, harmonized and data-driven registration.
Specifically, the incumbent will: 
Support the registration team across the sites with all relevant activities — including capacity building, on the job training, SOP harmonization, data-driven processing and oversight — while roving regularly across registration sites. 
Participate in and accelerate activities aimed at simplifying access to registration, integrating processes, and delivering registration services in a refugee-centred manner. 
Maintain effective site-level working relationships with Camp-in-Charge (CiC) officials in the context of the joint continuous registration procedure, in support of the Registration and Identity Management Officer. Engagement with the RRRC and other Government counterparts remains with the Registration and Identity Management Officer and the DIMA Coordinator. 
Support proGres data quality and the wider use of PRIMES tools (including RApp, GDT, BIMS, PRIMES Forms) and the implementation of new tools such as kiosks and the digital gateway. 
Support the integrity team as a deputy focal point on registration-related integrity and fraud-mitigation matters. 
Support, in all sites, the shift towards a data-driven whole-camp approach, including documentation renewal and the absorption of a population verification into routine, data-driven operations, under the broader DIMA Strategy. 
Support the digitization of civil documentation and vital events at registration sites. 
Work closely with the DIMA Operational Data Management team on data quality and the roll-out of kiosks and the Digital Gateway, with the Information Management team, and with protection units and partners as relevant.
In line with the DIMA registration structure, the position carries a dedicated roving role across all sites, comprising: 
Process flow implementation and harmonization; 
SOPs harmonization and implementation; 
Capacity building and on-the-job training; 
Integrity and fraud mitigation. 
***Desired Candidate Profile***
Given the complexity and sensitivity of this operation, the desired candidate profile places particular weight on directly relevant operational and technical experience. To be successful in this role the candidate should have: 
3–5 years of professional experience in Registration and Identity Management in refugee contexts, with demonstrated experience in stateless registration and in camp settings. 
Direct experience in large, protracted and complex refugee responses where registration is a joint procedure with the hosting Government — experience in comparable operational settings, and familiarity with the specific complexities of the Bangladesh / Cox’s Bazar Rohingya operation, is a strong asset given the steep contextual learning curve and the sensitivity of the stateless caseload. 
Strong knowledge and understanding of registration and identity management, including experience coordinating partner work and refugee volunteers on registration procedures, and advanced knowledge of UNHCR’s registration policies and of the PRIMES ecosystem (proGres, BIMS, RApp, GDT, PRIMES Forms). 
Proven experience in work with Government counterparts in the context of joint registration procedures. 
Strong drafting skills, with proven experience in drafting, articulating and/or simplifying standard operating procedures and guidance and ensuring their consistent application. 
Demonstrated experience in capacity building, coaching and on-the-job training of large, multi-contract registration teams 
Experience with population Verification exercises 
Experience with registration integrity and fraud-mitigation measures. 
Experience in Hardship duty stations

 Terms of Reference 
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was established on 14 December 1950 by the United Nations General Assembly and is mandated to lead and coordinate international action to protect refugees and pursue durable solutions to refugee situations worldwide. Its primary purpose is to safeguard the rights and well-being of refugees and ensure access to asylum and international protection. UNHCR supports voluntary repatriation, local integration, and resettlement to third countries, and holds a specific mandate to prevent and reduce statelessness and protect stateless persons. Over more than six decades, UNHCR has assisted tens of millions of people affected by forced displacement, working in partnership with governments, UN agencies, non-governmental organisations, and other stakeholders across diverse operational contexts.
In the Asia and Pacific region, UNHCR operates within a complex landscape of emergency and protracted displacement, hosting over 17.6 million forcibly displaced and stateless persons. The majority reside in urban or peri-urban settings, often in countries where national asylum systems remain limited or underdeveloped. While the principle of non-refoulement is generally recognised, refugees and asylum-seekers continue to face risks related to arrest, detention, restricted access to territory, and deportation. The region also hosts more than half of the world’s known stateless population, including Rohingya and other long-standing groups, with uneven progress on legal identity, nationality reform, and inclusion in national systems. Limited access to livelihoods, education, and essential services continues to undermine self-reliance and heighten protection risks, particularly for women and girls.
Within this broader regional and global mandate, the Solutions Strategy for Afghan Refugees (SSAR) provides a dedicated regional framework for cooperation and responsibility-sharing in support of Afghan refugee responses. Endorsed by Afghanistan, Iran, and Pakistan and supported by the international community, the SSAR seeks to strengthen protection, enhance solutions opportunities, and promote more predictable and sustained support to host countries. It serves as the primary regional mechanism linking national, regional, and international efforts related to Afghan refugees, with a focus on coherence, alignment, and shared responsibility.
The SSAR Support Platform complements the strategy by providing a structured forum for international engagement, coordination, and resource mobilisation in support of SSAR objectives. It brings together affected states, donor governments, UN agencies, international financial institutions, and other partners to facilitate dialogue, monitor progress, and encourage coordinated support. Through the Support Platform, stakeholders work collectively to sustain attention on Afghan refugee situations, strengthen coordination across actors, and support approaches that reinforce protection and solutions over time within an increasingly constrained operating environment.

Information and data management staff are responsible for coordinating, planning and delivering on data and information activities for all UNHCR operational contexts, responses and populations of concern, including providing coordination and leadership in partnerships on data with all stakeholders - including forcibly displaced and stateless persons. They serve the entirety of UNHCR staff and activities, including protection, programme, operations, external relations and executive management for evidence-informed planning, advocacy, and coordination. They are key in ensuring multi-stakeholder, multi-sector, and multi-country activities are provided with robust and meaningful data and information to support planning, funding and advocacy efforts. Operational Context:
UNHCR has maintained a presence in Bosnia and Herzegovina since 1992. The UNHCR Representation for Central and South-East Europe covers nine operations, including Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH). In BiH, UNHCR works with national authorities, civil society, UN agencies and other partners to strengthen a sustainable and protection-sensitive asylum and solutions system and to promote effective access to rights for refugees, asylum-seekers, stateless persons and other persons under UNHCR's mandate.
BiH has established an asylum legal framework broadly aligned with international standards and the EU acquis and has made important progress in developing its national asylum system. The current context offers opportunities to consolidate these achievements, including by further strengthening access to asylum procedures, the quality and efficiency of refugee status determination, access to free legal aid, and the effective enjoyment of rights by persons granted international protection, while advancing sustainable approaches to refugee inclusion and integration. BiH’s multi-level institutional structure also creates an important space for strategic legal engagement, advocacy and coordination with authorities at different levels of government.
UNHCR's engagement in BiH focuses on strengthening national ownership and sustainable protection systems, including through institutional capacity development, strengthened public free legal aid, refugee inclusion and integration, and the prevention and reduction of statelessness. This work is also closely linked to BiH's EU accession process and continued alignment of national legislation and practice with international protection standards and the EU acquis.
Against this background, the Legal Associate will be part of the Protection team and will support legal and policy analysis, monitoring of legislative and jurisprudential developments, preparation of legal comments and advocacy materials, organization of capacity building/advocacy events, monitor and follow-up on individual cases involving legal or protection issues. 
Particular attention will be given to asylum procedures and procedural safeguards, access to justice and free legal aid, access to rights and integration of persons granted international protection, civil registration, nationality and statelessness. The incumbent will liaise with relevant authorities, legal aid institutions, civil society organizations and other partners and contribute to capacity-development activities aimed at strengthening sustainable, nationally owned protection systems.
The position requires strong legal research, analytical and drafting skills, sound knowledge of the legal and institutional framework in BiH, and the ability to work effectively with a wide range of national and international stakeholders.

 Standard Job Description 
 Head of Global Communications and Spokesperson 
 Organizational Setting and Work Relationships 
 The incumbent serves as a senior communications adviser and spokesperson to the High Commissioner of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Reporting directly to the High Commissioner, the incumbent is responsible for shaping and articulating UNHCR's institutional voice, protecting and strengthening its global reputation, and advancing the organization's strategic objectives through effective public engagement and communications leadership.
 The incumbent leads UNHCR's Global Communications Service and ensures that messaging, advocacy, media engagement and public positioning support the organization's protection mandate, operational priorities and strategic direction. The role requires close engagement with senior leadership across the organization, governments, the United Nations system, media organizations, civil society, private sector partners and other influential stakeholders.
 While serving as adviser and spokesperson to the High Commissioner, the incumbent works in close partnership with the Division of External Relations to ensure that communications function as a strategic enabler of UNHCR's advocacy, influence, engagement and resource mobilization objectives. The incumbent promotes coherence across all external-facing functions and ensures that institutional messaging reinforces UNHCR's strategic priorities.
 As a member of the senior leadership team, the incumbent provides strategic advice on communications, public positioning, stakeholder perceptions and reputational risk, particularly in complex political, humanitarian and media environments.
 All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR’s core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity.
 Duties 
 Strategic Adviser and Spokesperson to the High Commissioner 
 -        Serve as senior adviser to the High Commissioner on strategic communications, public positioning, stakeholder perceptions, reputational risk and communications aspects of policy, operational and political developments affecting the organization.
 -        Act as the official spokesperson of the High Commissioner and, when required, of UNHCR, representing the organization before international media, governments, partners and public audiences.
 -        Develop and implement strategies that strengthen the visibility, credibility and influence of the High Commissioner and reinforce UNHCR's leadership on refugee protection, forced displacement and statelessness.
 -        Ensure consistency between the High Commissioner's public positioning, UNHCR's operational priorities and the external communications of headquarters, regional bureaux and country operations.
 -        Provide communications leadership during emergencies, crises and politically sensitive situations, ensuring coherent institutional positioning, effective stakeholder engagement and sound reputational risk management.
 Institutional Positioning, Reputation and Public Engagement 
 -      Shape UNHCR's public narrative and strategic positioning on major humanitarian, political and protection issues affecting forcibly displaced and stateless populations.
 -      Foster a continuous exchange between operational realities, regional perspectives and institutional positioning, ensuring that insights from the field inform UNHCR's global communications strategy while strengthening the communications effectiveness of Representatives and senior leaders across the organization.
 -      Provide strategic oversight  of UNHCR's global reputation by monitoring external perceptions, identifying emerging risks and opportunities, advising senior leadership on engagement strategies, and ensuring that communications insights from across the organization inform leadership decision-making.
 -      Develop and drive proactive media and public engagement strategies that position UNHCR at the center of global conversations on displacement, refugee protection and humanitarian action.
 -      Identify opportunities to influence public debate, strengthen political and public support for UNHCR's mandate, and build enduring relationships with international media organizations, journalists, digital influencers and opinion leaders.
 Communications Capability and Organizational Leadership 
 -        Advise and support Representatives, Bureau Directors and senior managers across the organization on strategic communications, public engagement and reputation management.

 -        Serve as a senior communications partner to the Division of External Relations, ensuring that UNHCR's communications strategies support the organization's advocacy, engagement, partnerships, resource mobilization and external influence objectives.

The Shelter Associate will support the Shelter/NFI/CCCM function in Sittwe. Under the supervision of the Assistant CCCM Coordination Officer (or relevant supervisor), the incumbent will contribute to the planning, coordination, implementation and monitoring of safe, dignified and needs-based Shelter and CCCM interventions for displaced population in Rakhine, including populations living in recent and protracted camp and displacement settings where access and movement restrictions, congestion, recurrent seasonal hazards and protection risks significantly affect response options.
A good understanding of the displacement and operational context in Rakhine State is highly desirable. Previous experience working in Rakhine State, particularly in Sittwe and in IDP camp settings, would be a strong advantage, given the importance of contextual knowledge, engagement with communities and local stakeholders, and the identification of technically appropriate and feasible solutions. Demonstrated practical experience in humanitarian shelter construction, rehabilitation or infrastructure works, including the preparation or review of BoQs, technical drawings and specifications, site measurements, quantity verification and construction quality control, is essential.
The incumbent will contribute to shelter and site needs assessments, technical prioritization, response planning and implementation monitoring. S/he will support shelter construction, maintenance, upgrading and rehabilitation activities and contribute to risk-reduction measures addressing structural safety, fire, flooding, drainage, ventilation, privacy and overcrowding. Particular attention should be given to practical solutions that improve safety, dignity and habitability while responding to the constraints of protracted displacement settings.
The incumbent will undertake regular field monitoring and technical supervision, including site inspections, measurements, verification of completed works and materials, and quality control. S/he will contribute to the preparation and review of technical drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), technical specifications, cost estimates and work plans, and will support partners and contractors to ensure that works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with agreed technical standards, including relevant Sphere standards and humanitarian shelter guidance.
Furthermore, the incumbent will undertake regular field missions to displacement sites and other operational locations, including joint missions with colleagues, partners, donors and other stakeholders. S/he should be able to clearly communicate shelter, NFI and CCCM needs, technical approaches, implementation challenges, protection considerations and response priorities to both technical and non-technical audiences, including during field visits. The incumbent will also contribute to briefings, presentations and other communication products for donors, partners and visiting missions, translating technical and field-level findings into clear and practical messages.
The incumbent will support coordination with partners, relevant authorities, service providers and communities to promote coherent implementation, identify gaps and avoid duplication. S/he will work closely with Protection, WASH, Health, Education and other relevant sectors to support integrated approaches, including safe access, site-level risk reduction and appropriate referral of identified protection and service gaps. The incumbent will also contribute to partner capacity development through practical technical guidance, field-level coaching and support to strengthen implementation and reporting quality.
Community engagement and accountability to affected people (AAP) will be integral to the role. The incumbent will support inclusive consultations, community participation, complaint and feedback mechanisms and transparent communication on assistance, prioritization and implementation. S/he will ensure that Shelter/NFI and CCCM interventions appropriately consider age, gender and diversity (AGD), protection risks, accessibility and the specific needs of persons with heightened vulnerabilities, while applying protection mainstreaming and PSEA principles.
The incumbent will contribute to data collection, analysis and reporting, including consolidation of assessment and monitoring findings, maintenance of intervention and gap-tracking information, identification of trends and operational constraints, and preparation of practical recommendations to inform programme and coordination decisions.
The incumbent should demonstrate strong analytical, technical, drafting and reporting skills and the ability to translate field observations into practical recommendations and follow-up actions. S/he should be able to work independently, manage competing priorities, undertake regular field visits and collaborate effectively with colleagues, partners, communities and other stakeholders in a complex and evolving operating environment.

The incumbent assists the supervisor in ensuring that shelter & infrastructure responses within the AoR evolve according to the changing nature of the situation, progressively working towards more durable solutions and drawing from sustainable local building practices and materials. S/he provides technical assistance in general infrastructure planning, design and construction monitoring.

General Background : 
Although Bangladesh is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or the 1967 Protocol and the Government does not recognize the Rohingya as refugees, referring to them as “Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals”, the country is generously hosting some 1.2 million Rohingya refugees across 33 camps. This includes over 141,000 new arrivals who fled renewed violence and persecution in Myanmar’s Rakhine State and have entered the camps since 2024 despite the border being officially closure. The presence of large numbers of refugees – who now represent two-thirds of the local population in Cox’s Bazar – has had important impacts on local communities, service delivery, the economy and the environment. The Government considers return to Myanmar, as soon as possible, as the only viable solution. This policy approach impacts on the humanitarian operation, with the Government discouraging medium or longer-term approaches, including the development of permanent infrastructure, providing formal education or livelihoods opportunities for the refugees and the use of cash to deliver assistance.
With the escalation of the conflict in Northern Rakhine State since November 2023, the operation in Bangladesh has experienced the spill overs in the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar. On the one hand, UNHCR and partners have been recording a significant increase in security incidents in the camps, including homicides and abductions. UNHCR has also seen an emerging trend of organised groups recruiting refugees to engage them in the armed conflict in Myanmar. The compromised civilian and humanitarian character of asylum in the camps has heightened risks for refugees, refugee volunteers (the backbone of the humanitarian response) and humanitarian workers. On the other hand, the operation has been recording new arrivals in the camps despite the Government’s closed-door policy at the border with Myanmar. New arrivals are extremely vulnerable, many have suffered injuries as they were fleeing. The government has authorized their assistance but without registration. 
The Associate Protection Officer is part of the Legal Protection Unit (LPU) responsible for a broad portfolio of protection activities, including protection case management and response to complex and urgent protection cases; legal aid and access to justice, including legal counselling, assistance with filing complaints before police and courts, legal representation, and interventions to secure release from detention; camp and border protection monitoring; and protection coordination. Protection and border monitoring and analysis undertaken by the unit inform UNHCR's advocacy, including through weekly camp security monitoring updates and monthly border monitoring reports.
The unit maintains extensive engagement with law enforcement authorities and the judiciary, including through capacity development and support to the Government in upholding the civilian and humanitarian character of asylum and the camps and addressing the broader security situation in the camps. It also co-chairs the Anti-Trafficking Working Group with IOM. 
The work of the LPU is a critical pillar of UNHCR Bangladesh’s protection strategy and advocacy, and close coordination with the Registration, Community-Based Protection, Durable Solutions and Field Units is required.
The complexity and fast-moving nature of the operation require an incumbent who is highly adaptable and solutions-oriented, able to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgement and deliver effectively under pressure.
In addition, the incumbent stays in close contact with government camp administration officials under the Office of the Refugee Repatriation and Relief Commissioner (RRRC). S/he also works closely with the Protection sector of Rohingya Coordination Platform (RCP). The incumbent will have supervisory responsibilities. 
CANDIDATE PROFILE:
Essential:
- Demonstrated experience on protection and border monitoring in sensitive contexts (access to asylum, refoulement, cross-border and onward movement), and protection advocacy; 
- Demonstrated experience on anti-trafficking and coordination in interagency context; 
- Demonstrated experience on civilian and humanitarian character of asylum and camps;
- Demonstrated experience establishing excellent relationships with a variety of law enforcements authorities and the judiciary.
Desirable:
- A Master’s degree in international refugee law or equivalent;
- Excellent political awareness, ability to work independently and with minimal supervision, and demonstrated capacity to analyze complex and fast-changing operational contexts, including data;
- Demonstrated experience protection teams and partner relationships;
- Familiarity with and exposure to route-based approach; 
- Experience in the region and of the Rohingya Situation  
 Standard Job Description 
 Associate Protection Officer
Organizational Setting and Work Relationships
The Associate Protection Officer reports to the Protection Officer or the Senior Protection Officer. Depending on the size and structure of the Office, the incumbent may have supervisory responsibility for protection staff, including community-based protection registration, resettlement and education. S/he provides functional protection guidance to information management and programme staff on all protection/legal matters and accountabilities. These include: statelessness (in line with the campaign to End Statelessness by 2024), Global Compact on Refugees (GCR) commitments, age, gender, diversity (AGD) and accountability to affected populations (AAP) through community-based protection, Child protection, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention and response, gender equality, disability inclusion, youth empowerment, psycho-social support and PSEA, registration, asylum/refugee status determination, resettlement, local integration, voluntary repatriation, human rights standards integration, national legislation, judicial engagement, predictable and decisive engagement in situations of internal displacement and engagement in wider mixed movement and climate change/disaster-related displacement responses. S/he supervises protection standards, operational procedures and practices in protection delivery in line with international standards.
The Associate Protection Officer is expected to coordinate quality, timely and effective protection responses to the needs of forcibly displaced and stateless persons , ensuring that operational responses in all sectors mainstream protection methodologies and integrate protection safeguards. The incumbent contributes to the design of a comprehensive protection strategy and represents the organization externally on protection doctrine and policy as guided by the supervisor. S/he also ensures that forcibly displaced and stateless persons are meaningfully engaged in the decisions that affect them and support programme design and adaptations that are influenced by the concerns, priorities and capacities of forcibly displaced and stateless persons . To achieve this, the incumbent will need to build and maintain effective interfaces with communities of concern, authorities, protection and assistance partners as well as a broader network of stakeholders who can contribute to enhancing protection.

The Donor Relations Officer is part of a team tasked to maintain proactive dialogue with donor governments as well as with the regional and local donors aiming at building relationships, raise awareness and mobilize political and financial support for UNHCR's work and priorities.
The incumbent's primary role is pursuing opportunities for donor engagement, strengthening partnerships, sustaining support and fundraising opportunities. Due to the specific nature of these responsibilities, Donor Relations Officer posts are based only in Geneva Headquarters, major donor capitals or Regional Bureaux. S/he with also provide support to counterparts in Field Operations, especially to offices dealing with emergency situations.
The incumbent reports to a senior staff in the function of Donor Relations and/or External Engagement; the reporting relationships may vary and depends on the size and organizational structure of the office/operation. The incumbent may supervise professional and/or general service staff.
All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR's core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity.
Duties
- Maintain close dialogue with and provide information to donor governments on UNHCR operations and financial requirements including responding to donor governments’ requests for information on ad hoc basis.
 - Negotiate contributions, striving for timeliness, predictability and maximum flexibility.
 - Keep abreast of UNHCR’s operations worldwide with a specific focus on emergency situations to be able to serve donor’s information needs on all aspects of UNHCR’s work.
 - Identify and access new donors and funding sources as per Public Partnerships and Financing Service (PPFS) strategy.
 - Draft internal and external correspondence, including briefing notes for senior management to support them in negotiation and follow up of contributions with donors.
 - Assist in reviewing actions and strategies for assigned donors with a specific focus on monitoring and analysing; develop and maintain donor profiles and plans. Monitor recording and tracking of contributions and take necessary actions to satisfy donor requirements.
 Additional duties for position in Headquarters
 - Prepare submissions - in collaboration with respective Bureau, Divisions and UNHCR Offices - for specific funding from donors or provide other information donor may require in determining their financial/political support to UNHCR.
 - Serve as a liaison between UNHCR and Permanent Missions and arrange meetings for donors, and where applicable, organize annual bilateral consultations with selected donor government and provide follow-up to the conclusions of these meetings.
 Additional duties for positions in major donor capitals
 - Develop and cultivate network of counterparts and influencers, including in relevant ministries, parliament and local government.
 - Based on knowledge of local context, assist in developing country engagement strategy to raise locally available funds, in close collaboration with PPFS.

 Terms of Reference 
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was established on 14 December 1950 by the United Nations General Assembly and is mandated to lead and coordinate international action to protect refugees and pursue durable solutions to refugee situations worldwide. Its primary purpose is to safeguard the rights and well-being of refugees and ensure access to asylum and international protection. UNHCR supports voluntary repatriation, local integration, and resettlement to third countries, and holds a specific mandate to prevent and reduce statelessness and protect stateless persons. Over more than six decades, UNHCR has assisted tens of millions of people affected by forced displacement, working in partnership with governments, UN agencies, non-governmental organisations, and other stakeholders across diverse operational contexts.
In the Asia and Pacific region, UNHCR operates within a complex landscape of emergency and protracted displacement, hosting over 15.7 million forcibly displaced and stateless persons. The majority reside in urban or peri-urban settings, often in countries where national asylum systems remain limited or underdeveloped. While the principle of non-refoulement is generally recognised, refugees and asylum-seekers continue to face risks related to arrest, detention, restricted access to territory, and deportation. The region also hosts more than half of the world’s known stateless population, including Rohingya and other long-standing groups, with uneven progress on legal identity, nationality reform, and inclusion in national systems. Limited access to livelihoods, education, and essential services continues to undermine self-reliance and heighten protection risks, particularly for women and girls.
UNHCR is implementing a regional project funded by the European Union through the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (EU-INTPA). The project supports Afghan refugees in Iran, Pakistan and Central Asia, as well as returnees and internally displaced persons in Afghanistan. In addition, UNHCR implements other key regional donor-funded projects involving multiple country operations. These projects require close coordination with operations, headquarters and donor counterparts, as well as consistent planning, implementation monitoring, reporting and follow-up to ensure alignment with regional priorities and donor requirements.
The position will be based in Kabul and integrated within the UNHCR Afghanistan External Relations team, while primarily supporting regional priorities and providing support to Afghanistan-specific priorities as required. The incumbent will report to the Senior External Relations Officer, Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific, while working in coordination with the Senior External Relations Officer, UNHCR Afghanistan. 
Purpose and Scope of Assignment 
The incumbent will be responsible for the overall coordination of the regional EU-funded project and other key regional projects, including:
 Project Coordination & Monitoring
- Develop the project proposals and ensure alignment with donor requirements.
- Coordinate and prepare narrative and financial reports.
- Monitor implementation progress across multiple countries.
 Stakeholder Engagement
- Serve as the principal liaison between UNHCR and EU-INTPA teams in Brussels and field locations. 
- Maintain close collaboration with UNHCR offices in Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, and Central Asia, as well as RBAP, UNHCR Brussels and UNHCR HQ and other relevant actors involved as part of the coordination of the EU-INTPA and other regional projects.
- Engage with government partners and other stakeholders involved in the projects.
 Technical Support
- Provide guidance to UNHCR offices throughout the implementation period.
- Work closely with protection, programme, external relations, and information management units.
 Travel
- Travel to project locations (Iran, Pakistan, Central Asia) and within Afghanistan as required.
- Any other tasks relevant to the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific and the Afghanistan Operation.
3. Monitoring and Progress Controls
• Timely submission of project proposals and donor reports (narrative and financial).
• Regular coordination meetings held with UNHCR offices and EU-INTPA counterparts in Kabul and Brussels.
• Implementation progress tracked and documented.
• Compliance with EU-INTPA contractual and reporting requirements.
• Identification and mitigation of risks affecting project delivery.
4. Qualifications and Experience
Undergraduate degree with 6 years relevant experience, or Graduate degree with 5 years relevant experience in Political Science, Social Sciences, International Relations, or related fields.
 Work Experience 
• Experience in humanitarian operations in a field environment.
• Strong knowledge of UNHCR operations at HQ and field level.
• Proven experience in fundraising and programme management.
• Experience engaging with EU-INTPA and other EU institutions.
• Strategic analysis of EU regional and country strategies.
Core Competencies:
• Accountability: Taking ownership of responsibilities and delivering on commitments. Ensuring transparency and integrity in all actions.
• Communication: Conveying information clearly and effectively, both in writing and verbally, and adapting communication style to different audiences.
• Organizational Awareness: Understanding UNHCR’s mandate, structure, and priorities, and aligning work accordingly.
• Teamwork & Collaboration: Working effectively with colleagues across different locations and cultures, fostering a positive and cooperative environment.
• Client & Result Orientation: Focusing on delivering quality outcomes for beneficiaries and meeting donor expectations.
Managerial Competencies
• Empowering and Building Trust: Creating an environment where team members feel trusted and supported to perform their roles.
• Judgement and Decision Making: Making sound decisions based on analysis, experience, and available information, even under pressure.
Cross-Functional Competencies
• Analytical Thinking: Breaking down complex issues, identifying patterns, and proposing solutions.
• Innovation and Creativity: Developing new approaches to overcome challenges and improve processes.
• Political Awareness: Understanding the political and socio-economic context and its impact on humanitarian operations.

Organizational Setting and Work Relationships
The Shelter Associate provides support in carrying out comprehensive sectoral needs assessments in liaison with other relevant sectors such as protection, programme, community services, public health, WASH, administration and supply. To ensure the most effective response, both quantitative and qualitative data should be gathered on the profile/needs and living conditions of both the displaced population and host community. The incumbent will assist in the day to-day operations of all construction and general infrastructure projects within the Area of Responsibility (AoR) to ensure that works proceed as designed and comply with established standards and procedures for the full project cycle.
Close and regular contact is maintained with technical and non-technical staff of shelter sector members, national and international NGOs and Government Authorities. The Shelter Associate normally reports to a more senior shelter colleague.
The incumbent assists the supervisor in ensuring that shelter & infrastructure responses within the AoR evolve according to the changing nature of the situation, progressively working towards more durable solutions and drawing from sustainable local building practices and materials. S/he provides technical assistance in general infrastructure planning, design and construction monitoring.
Within an urban context, it is essential that shelter responses take into consideration urban planning strategies, including an analysis of residential areas, housing affordability and availability. In addition, regardless of the context, shelter assistance should at all times minimize the risk of harm, eviction, exploitation and abuse, overcrowded living conditions, limited access to services and unhygienic conditions. Special attention must be given to the environment and low carbon approaches, attention to material selection through sustainable means to ensure a green approach to shelter delivery.

 Assistant Government Liaison Officer
Organizational Setting and Work Relationships
The Assistant Government Liaison Officer is usually located in country operations. S/he plays a crucial support role in ensuring UNHCR's approach to the Government is consistent, strategic and coherent. UNHCR assists the Government on coordination, response delivery and protection issues. Typically, this involves joint coordination arrangements, partnership with various government departments in service delivery, and regular dialogue at all levels on refugee protection issues. The main aim is to assist senior management to ensure that UNHCR can fulfil its role to support the Government to lead the refugee response ensuring the protection of refugees and - in line with the GCR - promote the inclusion of refugees into national systems by coordinating with other actors - including development actors at the early stages of a refugee response and in mixed situations supporting the Government to prevent, respond to and resolve internal displacement while complementing and reinforcing national response efforts. This should be done in line with UNHCR's Mandate, the Global Compact for Refugees, the IDP policy, and agreed inter-agency commitments. More specifically, s/he advises the senior management on issues and processes concerning the relationship with the Government and related positioning, coordination, advocacy, information, resource allocation, fundraising, reporting, and communication with other UN agencies, NGOs, civil society actors, private sector, media and other relevant actors through strong engagement in humanitarian inter-agency processes, but also with a focus on development processes as they impact on UNHCR. The overall goal of the position is to support the effectiveness of UNHCR's leadership roles and responses to situations affecting people of concern to UNHCR (refugees, asylum-seekers, IDPs, stateless persons, returnees, host communities) through an open and transparent partnership approach with the Government.
The Assistant Government Liaison Officer ensures that support is provided for strategic planning, assessment, monitoring and analysis concerning the relationship with the Government. The Assistant Government Liaison Officer will support all planning and reporting activities. The incumbent will support the supervisor in maintaining a constant dialogue with the Government on the overall protection context. A key tool in this regard will be the facilitation and support of periodic meetings with the Government, as well as to support the broadening of mutual information through meeting reports, situation updates and newsletters.
