Operational Context 
Indonesia hosts a long-staying refugee and asylum-seeker population, with continued maritime arrivals and a key protection role along the South-East Asia (SEA) route. The population, of some 12,000 asylum seekers and refugees are dispersed in various locations throughout the country. While Indonesia is not party to the 1951 Refugee Convention or 1967 Protocol, the Constitution, Human Rights Law and a 2016 Presidential Regulations acknowledges the right to seek asylum. The country has yet to develop asylum legislation, and the government remain greatly reliant on the support of international organizations. Recognized refugees lack legal status in Indonesia which serves as a barrier to access to essential national services, including health insurance, work, education, etc. 
Indonesia hosts the ASEAN Secretariat and the Bali Process, two crucial platforms to advance domestic and regional refugee protection. These forums have also fostered a community of supporters, advocates and practitioners – ranging from member states (many of whom are accredited or positioned representation to ASEAN), parliamentarians, think tanks, academia and civil society which UNHCR can/should strategically leverage.
In addition to mandate delivery, emergency preparedness for boat arrivals and critical protection interventions for vulnerable refugees - following the High Commissioner’s 50by35 vision - UNHCR Indonesia is working towards incremental inclusion, systems building, and community-based protection, including climate sensitive initiatives. UNHCR is concurrently seeking to strengthen partnerships with ASEAN, bolster UNHCR’s role in the Bali Process and enhance relations with academia, think tanks and private sector. The operating context is dynamic, requiring UNHCR to be astute in navigating around developments impacting the refugee protection environment - including misinformation, disinformation and hate speech – while seizing opportunities to advance solutions.
In contributing the the above-mentioned objectives, the External Relations Associate will be supervised by the Representative, working closely with the Senior Protection Officer and Heads of Units. Advice and operational support may also be received from other senior staff and support units at the Country Office/

 Senior Protection Assistant
Organizational Setting and Work Relationships
The Senior Protection Assistant normally reports to a more senior Protection colleague. The incumbent monitors protection standards, operational procedures and practices in protection delivery in line with international standards and provides functional protection support to information management and programme staff.
The Senior Protection Assistant provides quality, timely and effective protection support to persons of concern (PoC) and identifies opportunities to mainstream protection methodologies and safeguards in operational responses. S/he contributes to designing a comprehensive protection strategy and may liaise externally with local authorities and partners on protection issues as guided by the supervisor.
The Senior Protection Assistant also ensures that PoC are involved in making decisions that affect them, whether in accessing their rights or in identifying appropriate solutions to their problems. To achieve this, the incumbent will need to build and maintain effective interfaces with communities of concern, local authorities and protection and assistance partners.
All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR's core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity.
Duties
- Consistently apply International and National Law and applicable UN/UNHCR and IASC policy, standards and codes of conduct.
- Provide counselling on protection issues to PoC; liaise with competent authorities to ensure the issuance of personal and other relevant documentation.
- Support activities in protection related AGD based programming with implementing and operational partners.
- Conduct preliminary information gathering and interviews in support of eligibility, status determination, durable solutions and social needs assessment.

- Contribute to a country-level child protection plan as part of the protection strategy.
- Contribute to a country-level education plan for PoC as part of the protection strategy.
- Monitor Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all protection/solutions activities.

 Terms of Reference 
1. General Background 
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is mandated to lead and coordinate international action to protect and assist refugees and other persons of concern (POC). 
Private Sector Partnerships Service (PSP) sits within UNHCR's Division of External Relations (DER) and is responsible for mobilizing resources from the private sector for refugees. UNHCR has developed a Private Sector Fundraising Strategy focusing on both Individual Giving and Private Sector Partnerships, identifying priority fundraising markets and regions.
Individual Giving (IG) is targeted at the public to secure the support of individuals through regular, unrestricted donations, cash appeals and legacies. The aim is to generate both monthly and one-time donations from individuals using various channels and methods including direct mail, face-to-face fundraising, telemarketing, digital fundraising, DRTV and emergency fundraising, with focus on strong donor loyalty and lifetime value. 
The purpose is to maximize the donor base from the individual giving (IG) for UNHCR, those with the ability to provide donations of between $1 to $10.000 (depending on local market conditions, as well as scope of responsibility) per year to UNHCR. 
Functionally guided by the Associate PSP IG Officer in the Donor Care and Development Team, this position will focus on developing relevant, engaging and personalized communications to key groups of UNHCR donors to increase loyalty and grow income.
All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR’s core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity.     
2. Purpose and Scope of Assignment 
• Handle inbound and outbound communications with donors, using all available platforms (including but not limited to direct mailers, events, emails, telemarketing and WhatsApp).
• Making daily follow-ups on donor inquiries and ensuring that relevant data are updated in the PSP database.
• Support and assist the implementation of best practices including standardized phone manners and customized scripts when answering/handling donor’s inquiry via phone calls and or emails and distribute to vendor(s) and responsible for any follow up and quality assurance of the telemarketing programme. 
• Support and assist the implementation of upgrade, conversion, reactivation, and other types of expansion activities aimed at maximizing long-term net income while meeting the required return on income (ROI) targets. 
• Assist Donor development and retention to execute retention and donor journey strategy to achieve annual budget and KPI. 
• Assist and support the implementation of donor save programme ; test, implement, and monitor donor movement on daily basis and provide analysis for trend and figures of donor save programme.
• Collaborate with individual giving and major donor manages to identify and cultivate the middle-donor segment within the individual-giving donors with personalized communication (online and offline) and plan on their migration through a proper pipeline programme to systematically further upgrade those with potential to the major donor programme.
• Monitor, track and analyze middle-donor giving trends, with regular reporting and recommendations to the management team. 
• Work closely with line manager towards achieving the annual target income plan.
• Perform other duties as required.
3. Monitoring and Progress Controls 
• Improved performance of the call centres. 
• Successful test with results that can be used for rolling out activities. 
• Smooth transition of database migration and successful roll out of new CRM system.
• Timely execution of donor projects, ensuring communications planned reach selected segments on time and as defined in the annual plan.
• Key performing indicators and metrics defined for the donor segment campaigns are measured, analyzed and reported timely and accurately to PSP Malaysia stakeholders.

• Minimum 2 years of experience for high school diploma or minimum 1 year of experience for Bachelor degree or higher with relevant job experience preferably in a similar position in an international NGO or the UN preferable.

• Strong interpersonal skills and excellent in building client/customer relationships. 
• Ability to analyze performance reports is an advantage. 
• Proven experience in fundraising and/or telemarketing is an added advantage.

• Proficient in written and spoken English and Bahasa Malaysia. Other additional languages will be an added advantage.

• Competent in translating online and offline communication materials.
• Proven ability to deal with multiple tasks in a courteous and service-oriented manner under demanding working condition. 
• Telemarketing experience would be a strong asset. 
• Good analytical skills, familiar with Excel, able to interpret and act on performance reports.

• Demonstrated knowledge in the NGO sector and private sector fundraising. 
• Ability to work independently and deliver under tight deadlines. 
• Good presentation skills and proficient in MS Office.
• Ability to interface effectively and professionally with key UNHCR stakeholders.

 Standard Job Description 
 Associate Human Resources Officer 
Organizational Setting and Work Relationships
The Associate Human Resources Officer supports the UNHCR's People Strategy and contributes to the implementation of the 2018 independent Human Resources review, which resulted in the establishment of HR strategic priorities and the reconfiguration and transformation of the Division of People Management (DPM) from a largely transactional model into a strategic business partner for field operations and senior management. Having the right people in the right place at the right time is at the core of enabling UNHCR to protect and respond to forcibly displaced and stateless persons. By attracting, retaining and developing a talented, diverse and agile workforce while nurturing a culture of excellence, respect and wellbeing for all, UNHCR's Human Resources acts as a strategic partner to the organization, enabling a people-centric culture.
The Associate Human Resources Officer provides support and assistance in the areas of operational support, workforce planning, assignments and talent acquisition, organizational cultural changes, HR policy implementation and duty of care. The incumbent maintains employee confidence and protects the organization and its workforce by keeping human resources information confidential.
The Associate Human Resources Officer is usually supervised by the HR Officer or Senior HR Officer or Head of Office in a Country Operation, or the most senior HR staff in a Regional Bureau. She/he usually supervises HR General Service staff.
The incumbent maintains a direct working relationship with a number of units within the Division of People Management (DPM). The incumbent also works closely with the Senior HR Partner, the Senior Medical Officer and the Senior Staff counsellor for his/her region.
All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR's core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity.
Duties
Workforce Operational Support:
- Assist in implementation of HR initiatives that support organizational culture change such as good people management practices, and promoting gender, inclusion and diversity.
- Implement HR operational activities to ensure timely provision of HR solutions, prioritizing according to the needs and risks.
- Contribute to the development of a HR customer service-oriented culture that values proactivity, continuous improvement, innovation and high performance.
- Provide support, guidance and trainings to HR staff.
Assignments and Talent Acquisition:
- Coordinate the process of recruitment, assignment and reassignment of locally-recruited staff and affiliate workforce, also assisting with set up and running of (Regional) Assignments Committee where relevant.
- Assist in organizing outreach campaigns to attract diverse applicants. Ensure proper consideration is given to all applicants without distinction on the grounds of race, color, sex, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation and gender identity.
- Analyse, track and report on recruitment and assignments trends for management, including efforts to reach gender parity.
- Take a proactive approach to risk management in the areas of recruitment, ensuring the issues are identified, addressed and reported and, where appropriate, escalated.
Advice to managers and staff, and contribution to an inclusive work environment:

2. Additional activities and needs

philanthropic investors is highly desirable

         Le poste contribue à améliorer l'efficacité et la transparence des opérations du bureau terrain de Kankan.

        Soutenir l'efficacité de la prestation quotidienne de services spécialisés, axés sur la satisfaction des autres collaborateurs et d'un bon rapport qualité-prix, dans le cadre du portefeuille de services de gestion et assurer le rôle de point focal des activités des Finances, des ressources humaines et de gestion des actifs (GEMS).

 Effectuer des tâches et des activités au sein du portefeuille des services de gestion afin de soutenir une prestation de services efficace et de haute qualité. Rassembler des données et préparer des analyses de base pour contribuer à la création de rapports en vue d'une gestion efficace des ressources. Traiter les actions de routine liées aux achats, aux finances (vérification des factures, gestion de la petite caisse, Suivi et exécution budgétaires,…), aux ressources humaines ( congés, appuyer el onboarding et toutes les activités y afférentes….) et à d'autres domaines pertinents, en contribuant à l'enregistrement efficace et opportun des données dans les systèmes de l'organisation. Gérer et conserver les dossiers physiques et numériques conformément aux procédures établies afin de garantir un accès rapide et aisé aux données, le cas échéant. Être le premier point de contact pour les questions internes, en fournissant des réponses rapides et précises afin de faciliter la résolution efficace et effective des problèmes quotidiens. Prendre part et suggérer des améliorations aux procédures et pratiques afin de soutenir l'amélioration continue des services fournis. Utiliser les outils numériques et les applications technologiques pour améliorer les pratiques de travail et le service aux collaborateurs. Fournir un soutien administratif pour la préparation d'initiatives inter-agences dans le cadre de la réforme des Nations Unies afin de réaliser des économies et d'améliorer la qualité des services. Assurer la liaison avec d'autres fonctions et des contractants tiers pour permettre une prestation de services efficace. Surveiller et analyser les dépenses mensuelles afin de soutenir la prise de décision basée sur des données fiables. Vérifier et traiter les demandes de paiement, avances et factures fournisseurs conformément aux règles financières et aux procédures d’approvisionnement du PAM. Extraire, vérifier et analyser les données issues des systèmes (ex : WINGS) et signaler toute anomalie ou incohérence. Gérer les actifs du bureau via le système GEMS, incluant, l'enregistrement, le suivi, les inventaires périodiques, le contrôle de l’utilisation des équipements et immobilisations. Effectuer des tâches de préparation et de réponse aux situations d'urgence en suivant les orientations données par le superviseur.

 JOB TITLE :Mobile Engineer Specialist - Android
 DIVISION: Private Partnerships (PSP) ShareTheMeal Org. Unit 50015246

 CONTRACT TYPE : Short-Term, Regular Consultant
 DURATION :11 months
 WORK SCHEDULE :Full time, Monday to Friday
 LINE MANAGER/SUPERVISOR : Lead Mobile Engineer ShareTheMeal
 ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT 
The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP is the world’s largest humanitarian organization, saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity for people recovering from conflict, disasters, and the impact of climate change. Around 20,000 people work for the organization, most of them in remote areas, directly serving the hungry poor.
To reach a world with zero hunger, WFP is investing in and growing private sector fundraising and partnerships. Serving as a broker between WFP and the private sector, WFP’s Private Partnerships and Fundraising Division (PSP) strives to mobilize funding, technical assistance, innovative solutions and visibility and awareness to help WFP fulfil its mission, while offering companies and the wider public the opportunity to contribute to a world with zero hunger.
ShareTheMeal is WFP’s fundraising and awareness-raising app. Free to download, the award-winning app is a pioneering way for people to join our efforts in creating a world with zero hunger. ShareTheMeal was launched in 2015 as the first pilot of WFP’s Innovation Accelerator, which among other things supports start-ups and innovators in developing their ideas for zero hunger.
ShareTheMeal currently has more than 1.9 million users worldwide, who have shared more than 290 million meals (US$ 200 million). WFP is pursuing an ambitious growth strategy for individual giving, and ShareTheMeal is a key driver for this strategy going forward. The team, located in Berlin and remotely, is focused on increasing the funds raised to help get to zero hunger by further developing the app to include new and innovative features, increasing the engagement of existing users and growing the user base through marketing and communication initiatives. As the user base has grown, there is a significant opportunity to increase funds raised from existing users and deliver an exceptional experience to build a long-term relationship with each supporter.
PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT
As the senior Android developer for ShareTheMeal's mobile engineering team, support and execute the mobile technology strategy, to enable the organization to scale from 1.9M to 10M+ users while maintaining exceptional user experience and operational efficiency impacting an annual revenue of $30 million USD.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES / RESPONSIBILITIES 
The Consultant, reporting to Head of Engineering - ShareTheMeal, is expected to:
 1. Technical Leadership and Architecture: 
a. Architect and implement secure, scalable Android solutions using modern Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Coroutines
b. Own the Android application architecture, ensuring performance, maintainability, and alignment with platform best practices
c. Lead code reviews and establish coding standards across the Android codebase
d. Drive and document technical decisions for team alignment and future maintainability
 2. Quality and Operations: 
a. Establish comprehensive testing strategies using JUnit and Maestro; maintain high test coverage
b. Own CI/CD pipelines, ensuring reliable and efficient release processes
c. Monitor production health via Sentry; lead incident response and root cause analysis
 3. Team Development: 
a. Mentor junior engineers through code reviews, pair programming, and technical guidance
b. Lead technical initiatives from conception through delivery
c. Champion engineering best practices that improve team velocity and code quality
 4. Strategy and Collaboration: 
a. Shape the Mobile Tech Strategy and roadmap alongside engineering leadership
b. Partner with Product to translate requirements into robust technical solutions
c. Identify and drive innovation opportunities that improve system quality and delivery speed
 DELIVERABLES AT THE END OF THE CONTRACT 
- Deliver Product features and Tech Initiatives across Android platforms.
- Documentation and handover to Lead Mobile Engineer for ShareTheMeal.
 QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED 
 Education 
▪ University degree in computer science or related field.
 Work history 
▪ At least, 4 years of experience in developing and designing Android native apps designed to serve thousands or more active users.
 Hard skills 
▪ Proficiency in Kotlin and modern Android development patterns, having an understanding of iOS (Swift) is a plus.
▪ Strong knowledge of Android SDK, Jetpack Compose, Coroutines, and other frameworks.
▪ Experience with Android architecture patterns (MVVM, MVP, Clean Architecture).
▪ Experience with Google Play submission process.
▪ Knowledge of Unit Testing, UI Testing (Maestro), and Test-Driven Development.
▪ Understanding of mobile app performance optimization techniques.
▪ Experience with mobile CI/CD pipelines and deployment processes.
▪ Familiarity with mobile analytics, crash reporting, and monitoring tools.
▪ Embracing principles of clean code, test-driven development, and clean architecture.
▪ Experience with agile development processes and cross-functional team collaboration.
 Soft skills 
▪ Strong analytical abilities, both quantitative and qualitative.
▪ Ability to make technical decisions that balance platform-specific needs with cross-platform efficiency.
▪ Excellent problem-solving skills with ability to debug complex mobile issues.
▪ Ability to interact with managers and stakeholders with maturity and tact.
▪ Mature judgment with strong interpersonal skills.
▪ Collaborative spirit able to work effectively across diverse teams and cultures.
▪ Self-motivated

 BACKGROUND OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 After nearly three decades of political and economic instability, Somalia is on a positive trajectory with significant progress made since the re-establishment of the Federal Government in 2012. However, the country continues to struggle with recurrent food and nutrition crises, widespread insecurity, political instability, underdeveloped infrastructure, and natural hazards such as drought and floods. In February 2015 WFP re-opened the Somalia Country Office in Mogadishu for the first time in 20 years. WFP has presence across Somalia with three operational Area Offices (Mogadishu, Garowe, and Hargeisa) and eight deep field location offices.
 PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 WFP Somalia’s greatest strength is its dedicated women and men working tirelessly to reduce hunger, often under difficult conditions where security threats and risks to personal safety are considerable. The Staff Counsellor will provide efficient and effective psychological counselling to staff requiring support related to workplace difficulties or personal issues. A large emphasis is placed on extensive engagement with staff and promotion of staff well-being.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority)

 Conduct regular missions to Area and Field offices to support staff and managers.
 Actively engage with management and staff to establish relationships based on trust and respect. This includes working cross-functionally and supporting team leaders as required.
 Contribute to staff readiness for deployment to Somalia through briefings, counselling sessions and other activities to ensure proactive support is extended to staff.
 Deliver workshops, trainings, and information sessions on a wide range of topics (e.g., stress management, team building, problem-solving, conflict resolution, etc.) both in-person and remotely, to ensure that staff regularly receive relevant information, and are aware of where to find resources, information or assistance.

 Complete administrative duties such as maintaining statistics on activities and completing reporting requirements as directed by Staff Wellness Division.

 Experience providing counselling, psychosocial support or staff wellness services within the Somali context is required, including a strong understanding of local cultural norms, languages, community dynamics, and the realities faced by national staff working in challenging and security-sensitive environments.
 Additional training or certification in related fields, such as stress management, critical incident stress management, trauma-informed care, psychological first aid, cross-cultural communication, conflict resolution, mediation, staff wellbeing, and support in hardship or security-sensitive duty stations, will be an advantage.

 Conflict resolution and mediation skills.

Duration: 11 months The Consultant will play a critical role in leading the KOICA- funded project in Timor-Leste, developing and implementing strategies to enhance nutrition outcomes, promote sustainable food systems, and improve the National School Feeding initiatives in Timor‑Leste. The incumbent will work closely with government counterparts and key stakeholders to design and roll out effective interventions that improve programme quality and impact at the individual, community, and institutional levels.
 The Consultant will provide technical support to ensure that school feeding strategies under KOICA project are evidence‑based, culturally appropriate, and effectively integrated into broader food security, emergency programmes, and nutrition programmes, including Home‑Grown School Feeding (HGSF).
 The role involves capacity building of stakeholders, monitoring and evaluating school feeding interventions, and ensuring that community‑level advocacy efforts support national policies on nutrition‑sensitive school feeding, food system transformation including linkage of the schools with local farmers.
 Additionally, the Home-Grown School Feeding Officer will ensure that KOICA project interventions are tailored to address gender and disability inclusion, particularly focusing on improving dietary diversity, quality school feeding practices.

This includes overseeing programme aspects such as infrastructure enhancement, fortified rice, food safety, and analysis of monitoring and reporting activities.
 Support reporting and partnerships to effectively manage information and ensure that standard procedures and templates are followed. This will drive quality, consistency, and standardization of information management and performance reporting in relation to the school meals project, in line with the Programme Document, agreements, and WFP guidance.
 Coordinate activities with WFP units, government ministries, project partners, and the donor (KOICA) to meet donor expectations, particularly in terms of outcome reporting related to the school meals programme.
 Establish and oversee mechanisms such as inter‑agency meetings, workshops, and activity coordination to strengthen collaboration with internal and external stakeholders for successful programme implementation.
 Prepare and disseminate reports and knowledge products that contribute to an evidence base informing decision‑making by WFP and stakeholders, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.
 Support food quality and safety by coordinating with relevant WFP teams to develop procedures for preventing and mitigating potential risks in relation to the school feeding programme.
  Harmonize key messages by coordinating with internal and external teams to align outputs from formative research with updated Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) activities.

 The Building Resilience and Reducing Rural Poverty Project (BRRRP) is an initiative by the Government of Lao PDR, particularly the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE), in collaboration with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), aimed at addressing food insecurity, rural poverty, and reduce vulnerabilities exacerbated by climate change. It aims to improve the health, resilience, and socioeconomic profile of poor households, particularly women, through a combination of adaptive and shock-responsive social protection measures.
 The project targets districts in four provinces: Khammouan, Louangphabang, Savannahkhet, and Xaiyabuly, which are characterized by high poverty rates, malnutrition, and climate risks. It combines nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfers (CCT) with an innovative poverty graduation program, aimed to support the most vulnerable populations, particularly poor pregnant women and mothers of young children.
 Key components of the project include: 
 Output 1: Coverage of shock-responsive and nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfer program expanded.
 Output 2: Gender-responsive and climate-resilient poverty graduation program piloted.
 Output 3: Social protection delivery systems and CCT implementation enhanced.
 Output 4: Institutional capacity for gender-smart and climate-responsive monitoring and evaluation strengthened.
 Under Output 2 WFP will provide technical support to MAE in the design, implementation, and evaluation of the climate-resilient and gender-responsive poverty graduation program specifically for rural women. The pilot will benefit at least 4,500 rural women as beneficiaries of conditional cash transfer, across four districts in four provinces.  Recognizing the multidimensional nature of poverty and climate vulnerability, the program will offer a holistic set of sequenced, climate-smart, and time-bound interventions tailored for poor women, combining targeted cash transfers with: (i) livelihood grants to pursue climate-resilient and sustainable livelihoods, (ii) technical skills training, (iii) support for financial inclusion, and (iv) social empowerment through psychosocial support, including dedicated coaching and life skills training to promote social inclusion and positive behavior change.
 The pilot graduation program under Output 2 consists of activities across five poverty graduation pillars (social protection, livelihoods promotion, financial inclusion, social empowerment, coaching & mentorship), in a strategic sequence within 24 months to empower poor women with skills, knowledge, tools, access to resources, livelihoods, and self-confidence to build long-term resilience, particularly to climate shocks. The pilot combines support for immediate needs (with conditional cash transfer) with longer-term investments in training and income generation to build long-term resilience.
 The position of Poverty Graduation Technical Specialist (national position) is based at the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment and will be required to periodically report and collaborate with WFP on the progress of implementation.

 Background
 The Building Resilience and Reducing Rural Poverty Project (BRRRP) is an initiative by the Government of Lao PDR, particularly the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE), in collaboration with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), aimed at addressing food insecurity, rural poverty, and reduce vulnerabilities exacerbated by climate change. It aims to improve the health, resilience, and socioeconomic profile of poor households, particularly women, through a combination of adaptive and shock-responsive social protection measures.
 The project targets districts in four provinces: Khammouan, Louangphabang, Savannahkhet, and Xaiyabuly, which are characterized by high poverty rates, malnutrition, and climate risks. It combines nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfers (CCT) with an innovative poverty graduation program, aimed to support the most vulnerable populations, particularly poor pregnant women and mothers of young children.
 Key components of the project include: 
 Output 1: Coverage of shock-responsive and nutrition-sensitive conditional cash transfer program expanded.
 Output 2: Gender-responsive and climate-resilient poverty graduation program piloted.
 Output 3: Social protection delivery systems and CCT implementation enhanced.
 Output 4: Institutional capacity for gender-smart and climate-responsive monitoring and evaluation strengthened.
 Under Output 2 WFP will provide technical support to MAE in the design, implementation, and evaluation of the climate-resilient and gender-responsive poverty graduation program specifically for rural women. The pilot will benefit at least 4,500 rural women as beneficiaries of conditional cash transfer, across four districts in four provinces.  Recognizing the multidimensional nature of poverty and climate vulnerability, the program will offer a holistic set of sequenced, climate-smart, and time-bound interventions tailored for poor women, combining targeted cash transfers with: (i) livelihood grants to pursue climate-resilient and sustainable livelihoods, (ii) technical skills training, (iii) support for financial inclusion, and (iv) social empowerment through psychosocial support, including dedicated coaching and life skills training to promote social inclusion and positive behavior change.
 The pilot graduation program under Output 2 consists of activities across five poverty graduation pillars (social protection, livelihoods promotion, financial inclusion, social empowerment, coaching & mentorship), in a strategic sequence within 24 months to empower poor women with skills, knowledge, tools, access to resources, livelihoods, and self-confidence to build long-term resilience, particularly to climate shocks. The pilot combines support for immediate needs (with conditional cash transfer) with longer-term investments in training and income generation to build long-term resilience.
 The position of Livelihood and Technical Training Specialist (national position) is based at the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRD-PR) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE) and will be required to periodically report and collaborate with WFP on the progress of implementation.

 Job Title: Programme Policy Officer (Adaptive Social Protection Expert)   
 Grade: SC9      
 Type of contract:  Service Contract

 This Vacancy Announcement is for Pakistan Nationals Only.  
 Note: This vacancy announcement will also be used to build a roster of prequalified applicants for future opportunities within same job profile at the current or lower level in Pakistan. 
 TERMS & CONDITIONS 
 WFP offers a competitive benefits package including salary, social security contribution, medical insurance, annual leave, parental leave, among other benefits.
 Important: All educational documents must be verified/attested by the Higher Education Commission (HEC). Appointment will be subject to submission of HEC-verified degrees.
 JOB PURPOSE 
 Towards the over-arching goal of Zero Hunger, the World Food Programme in Pakistan is working to support federal and provincial governments in strengthening social protection systems to be more effective and efficient in reaching the most vulnerable people, especially in times of crisis. In an effort to support the Government of Punjab to expand the scope of their existing social protection system, to adapt to changing needs in times of crisis, WFP is looking to hire an Adaptive Social Protection Expert to work with the government.
 With funding support from the Global Shield Financing Facility, WFP will collaborate closely with provincial
 stakeholders in Punjab to embed disaster risk management within the social protection system at the policy, programme-design and programme-implementation levels. To do so, the expert will be seconded to the Punjab Social Protection Authority (PSPA) in Lahore, Punjab, with regular reporting to the Head of Lahore Provincial Office and under the overall guidance of the Programme Policy Officer for Social Protection and the Head of Cash-based Transfers and Social Protection in the WFP Country Office in Islamabad.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (not all-inclusive, nor exhaustive):
 The key responsibilities of the adaptive social protection expert are listed below:
 1 . Provide technical and operational support to laying the foundations for an adaptive social protection system at the provincial level in Punjab 
The incumbent will provide operational and technical support to the PSPA in:
• Advancing adaptive social protection policy and institutional frameworks.
• Developing and adopting adaptive social protection protocols for key climate and disaster hazards.
• Integration of disaster risk and vulnerability data into PSPA systems to enable shock-responsive programme design and targeting.
• Establishing procedures and mechanisms for transferring emergency cash assistance
• Reviewing the 2025 flood response from a social protection perspective to understand how social protection can be leveraged for future climate shocks.
• Analyzing institutional roles relevant to ASP implementation and support coordination across provincial stakeholders.
 2. Actively participate in WFP’s assessment to identify opportunities and challenges for linking social protection and disaster risk financing, with a focus on Punjab 
The staff will support WFP in conducting a comprehensive assessment to identify opportunities and challenges for linking social protection with disaster risk financing. The exercise, covering federal and provincial levels with emphasis on Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, will examine feasibility, readiness, operational gaps, and bottlenecks. Findings will inform policy, governance, financing, and programme design, providing actionable recommendations to integrate disaster risk financing into social protection systems. The assessment will be undertaken through consultations and validations with government stakeholders and implemented by an external firm.
 3. Support PSPA and WFP’s undertaking an assessment to analyze opportunities for the use of a parametric insurance scheme, linked to the social protection system 
The expert will support WFP in conducting an assessment to explore opportunities for introducing a parametric insurance scheme and linking it to the social protection system in Punjab, in collaboration with PSPA and a third-party partner. The study will analyze feasibility, operational requirements, and cost implications of establishing swift, pre-arranged payouts triggered by floods and droughts. The assessment will be conducted at both federal and Punjab levels, providing evidence-based recommendations to integrate disaster risk financing into social protection delivery.
 DELIVERABLES: 
• Comprehensive review of previous Government emergency responses.
 • Review of existing provincial social protection programmes, identifying clear entry points for integrating adaptive approaches.
 • Targeted technical assistance sessions delivered to PSPA, strengthening policy, institutional arrangements, and programme design capacities.
 • Adaptive social protection protocols for priority hazards.
 • Vulnerability indicators for key hazards identified and proposed for integration into provincial targeting criteria.
 • Emergency cash delivery procedures and mechanisms designed for integration into the provincial social protection system.
 • Key contributions provided to the assessment on linkages between social protection and disaster risk reductions, including through participation in meetings, consultations and validations.
 • Key contributions provided to the assessment on the feasibility of a parametric insurance scheme linked to social protection, including through participation in meetings, consultations and validations.
 • Any other duty as required.
 All the deliverables shall be endorsed by the Punjab Social Protection Authority and WFP.

 Job Title: Programme Policy Officer – Inclusive Insurance Consultant
 Type of contract: CST-1
 Unit/Division: Climate and Resilience
 Duty Station: Nairobi, Kenya
 Duration: 11 months
 Background and purpose of the assignment 
 Climate change multiplies existing threats to food security, hunger and malnutrition. It will make natural disasters more frequent and intense, land and water scarce and difficult to access, and increases in agricultural productivity even harder to achieve. It will disproportionally impact the most vulnerable people, the majority of whom live in fragile areas prone to climate hazards, ultimately putting hundreds of millions of people at risk. It is estimated that by 2050, the risk of hunger could increase by 20 percent, and child malnutrition is anticipated to be 20 percent higher than it would have been without a climate change scenario.
 WFP approaches the challenge of climate change from the point of view of its impact on hunger and malnutrition. Specifically, on disaster risk financing (DRF), WFP takes a climate & resilience lens, based on the recently approved strategic plan (2026-2029) and focuses on developing risk financing instruments to provide timely resources to respond to climate events (SO1) and develop inclusive risk financing, through insurance, saving and credit to improve financial resilience and reduce humanitarian needs (SO2). In addition, the DRF team strengthen national systems, particular around adaptive social protection, and rural market development.  In the recently approved strategic plan, disaster risk financing is recognized as an innovative finance component, highlighting its role in supporting WFP's evolution of its financing and delivery model. In 2025, WFP implemented disaster risk financing activities in 37 countries, providing pre-arranged finance to 5 million people to a limit of US$ 348 million. 
 The position is part of Global HQ / Climate & Resilience Service, reporting to the DRF Regional Advisor in Easten and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO). The role provides technical guidance and support to a range of activities, from household-level micro and meso insurance programmes to macro insurance schemes both for WFP and governments. This position will focus mostly on supporting WFP’s Country Offices (COs) in the ESARO region on their Inclusive Risk Financing (IRF) programming. The consultant will work closely with the other climate & resilience teams (SAMS, Youth in Work in priority) and in programme (Social Protection, School Feeding) to ensure strong programmatic alignment and strategic vision at global, regional and national level, through WFP Country Strategic Plans.
 The position will also play a key role in further development, integration with other programmes, partners and units, and build stronger visibility on the work, internally and externally.

 BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DIVISION 
 Support to smallholder farmers and agricultural markets (SAMS) is a critical element to end hunger and achieve food security and reduce humanitarian needs. In the past years, WFP increasingly consolidated its support to smallholder farmers under the Smallholder Agricultural Market Support (SAMS) framework.
 The SAMS team, within the Climate and Resilience Service (PRGR), provides strategic and technical support and guidance to Country Offices (COs) and Regional Offices (ROs) to design and implement programmes that facilitate smallholder farmers' access to markets, contributing to the development of resilient agri-food value chains.
 Under the direct supervision of the SAMS Programme Policy Officer, the incumbent will provide technical support on knowledge and data management in coordination with staff from the Climate and Resilience service (PRGR) team, ROs and COs. The incumbent will support the SAMS team in capturing, creating, managing and sharing the knowledge, data and stories created around SAMS programmatic area.
 GENERAL INFORMATION 
 Type of assignment: Internship 
 Number of available positions: 1 
 Country of assignment: Italy 
 City of assignment: Rome 
 Hiring Unit: Climate and Resilience Service 
 Supervisor: SAMS Programme Policy Officer 
 Working arrangement: In person 
 Duration of assignment: 6 months 
 Expected Starting Date: January 2027 
 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Programme Guidance: Support the maintenance and dissemination of the SAMS programme guidance manual and accompanying tools, hosted in the WFP Programme Guidance Manual (PGM) platform.
 Capacity strengthening: Support the organization of webinars and training sessions to train country and regional staff on the revised SAMS guidance and tools.
 Knowledge Management and Corporate Reporting: Support the team in mapping SAMS interventions in the field, through review of 2025 Annual Country Reports and consolidation of information in a global matrix, to support analysis and country briefs.
 Support the 2026 Annual Country Reports exercise, by contributing to ad-hoc technical review to requesting countries.
 Support Eastern and Southern Africa Region SAMS portfolio review, based on past achievements and 2026 plans.
 Support the regular management of SAMS and PHL-related contents on WFP’s knowledge management platforms (e.g. WFPgo, PGM, GoDocs, Viva Engage Community, SAMS KM platform).
 Communication products: Support the update and/or development of communication and advocacy products (factsheets, infotech, briefs, reports, country success stories etc.).
 Liaising with WFP offices and partners: Support team members in setting up regular and occasional meetings and/or webinars with ROs, COs and other partners and in developing presentations and/or writing note for the records for such events, regularly updating the contact details for CO and RB focal points.
 STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 
 Be currently enrolled in an undergraduate programme in the field of international affairs, development studies, agricultural economics, environmental studies or other related fields, from a recognized university and have completed at least two years of the programme; OR
 Be currently enrolled in a graduate programme in the field of international affairs, development studies, agricultural economics, environmental studies or other related fields; OR
 Be a recent graduate from an undergraduate or graduate programme in the field of international affairs, development studies, agricultural economics, environmental studies or other related fields (within six months prior to the application to the internship programme);
 Classes attendance in the last 12 months of enrolment in a recognized university.
 Excellent written and spoken English is required (proficiency/level C). Working knowledge of another official UN language (French, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, Russian plus Portuguese) is an asset.
 TRAINING COMPONENTS 
 Throughout their assignment WFP interns have access to an industry leading learning platform, weLearn.  Depending on opportunities and availability of funds, he/she may participate in WFP workshops or seminars, as appropriate.
 LEARNING ELEMENTS 
 At the end of the assignment, the Intern should:
 Have a good understanding of WFP’s smallholder agricultural market support programmes, contributing to the development of agricultural value chains in multiple countries all over the world.
 Have a general understanding of what resilience building means within WFP and what are the key priorities for the humanitarian and development sector to address recurrent crisis.
 Have a broad understanding of the work of an action-oriented UN organization such as WFP, its key corporate processes and main longer term development
 Have experienced working as part of a multi-cultural team including field-based colleagues.
 Be acquainted to the challenges and opportunities of interacting and working with multiple country offices and regional offices.  
 INTERNSHIP TERMS AND CONDITIONS 
 Interns receive a monthly stipend from WFP up to the maximum amount of US$1,000 per month depending on the duty station of assignment.
 WFP is not responsible for living expenses, arrangements for accommodation, VISA requests and related costs.
 WFP will reimburse travel ticket for candidates who are nationals of developing countries and are pursuing their studies in their home country.
 WFP will recognize candidates’ educational credentials from recognised institutions that have been certified by competent international or national authorities such as the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) or Ministries of Education.
 Sons, daughters, brothers, or sisters of current WFP employees are not eligible to apply.

 THE ROLE 
 To support effective delivery of Cash Based Transfer (CBT) finance, budget and administration support services to facilitate transparent and efficient utilization of financial resources. 
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (not all-inclusive, nor exhaustive):
 Under the overall supervision of the Head of Finance and the direct supervision of the Finance Officer, the Finance Assistant will perform the following duties and responsibilities, including but not limited to:
 Provide procedural and technical support to staff in the finance area to ensure compliance with WFP financial policies, rules, and regulations.
 Support the development and implementation of financial policies and procedures and assist in setting up and implementing proper accounting systems and internal controls.
 Coordinate with other teams to ensure that financial services are performed efficiently and in line with the needs of the wider team.
 Monitor monthly expenditure forecasts and provide expenditure reports in order to facilitate informed decision-making.
 Monitor account balances and process financial transactions accurately and promptly to avoid overdrafts.
 Monitor and analyze general ledger accounts to identify issues and take corrective actions.
 Compile information from various sources to prepare reports relating to budgets, accounting, finance and statistics, including Key Risk Indicators (KRI) monthly.
 Functional Responsibilities: 
 Act as the finance focal point for Cash-Based Transfers (CBT) activities.
 Process CBT disbursement on time to ensure that beneficiaries get their monthly entitlement with no delay.
 Liaise with CBT focal points in Area/Field Offices and Hubs to ensure timely replenishment of CBT bank accounts in line with operational requirements.
 Familiarize with corporate and country-specific guidelines and procedures and ensure that services have been rendered and properly authorized before processing payments.
 Perform relevant functions and roles within the beneficiary database system (SCOPE) including verification of SCOPE payment lists and generation of PIN codes upon receiving requests from client unit, and within the corporate enterprise system (WINGS) related to cash-based operations.
 Verify vendor claims, advances and other receivables and observe appropriate procurement procedures, to ensure that suppliers are paid in a timely manner and in compliance with WFP finance rules and regulations.
 Monitor and record all expenses in line with the approved budget in order to ensure that correct expenditure costs are charged and payments to external suppliers, cash grants and other supplier invoices are processed in a timely manner.
 Retrieve, format and validate information obtained from various financial information systems and bring any discrepancy or inaccuracy to the attention of the supervisor and follow corrective actions.
 Monitor the distribution reconciliation process and ensure records are kept updated.
 Perform manual uploads for CBT bank accounts and clear general ledger items.
 Ensure that open items are identified and cleared promptly by the respective Area/Field Offices and Hubs.
 Maintain the web-based register for all invoices and payment transfers and record paperwork, to ensure that all documents are maintained and filed in compliance with WFP standards and guidelines.
 Perform any other duties as requested by the supervisor.
 QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE: 
 Education: Completion of secondary school education. A post-secondary certificate in the related functional area is desirable.
 Experience: At least five years of relevant work experience.
 Language: Fluency (level C) in both oral and written communication in English and Arabic.
 DESIRED EXPERIENCES FOR ENTRY INTO THE ROLE :
 Has experience collecting and monitoring financial data on projects and programmes, assessing financial health and status, and reporting findings to senior leaders.

Support the collation and dissemination of political and humanitarian analysis pertaining to WFP current or future responses and donor policies, trends and preferences to ensure country specific input to WFP’s operational reporting.
 4. Support the collation, analysis and communication of the ‘Essential Elements of Information’, pertaining to the operational environment and available human, financial and physical assets in order to facilitate access to timely and accurate information used at country and corporate level.
 5. Support the preparation of Annual Corporate Report (ACR) for the Annual Reporting Exercise, as ACR coordinator alternate, in collaboration with the country office programme, monitoring & evaluation, logistics and resource management, and other relevant functions by coordinating to ensure coherence and quality of performance information.
 6. Collaborate with counterparts internally to ensure consistency in humanitarian information and to complement WFP analysis and information.
 7. Support the enhancement of the capacity of WFP staff and partners to effectively manage operational information and performance reporting, for example through scheduling the delivery of the OIM & PR training on core competencies.
 8. Support CO in emergencies by preparing, organising and providing secretarial support to Operational Task Forces (OTFs).
 9.Support the initiatives for developing improved, streamlined, and harmonized OIM & PR including drafting of OIM & PR related normative guidance, as required.
 10. Support the assurance of defined quality standards in all processes and products.
 11. Support the Partnerships section for donor report editing and operational information sharing.
 12. Other as required.

 Education: Advanced University degree in Political Science, Economics, Statistics, Information Management or Journalism, Business Management, Social Sciences or other relevant field, or First University degree with additional years of related work experience and/or training/courses.
 Experience: Typically one year or more of postgraduate professional experience in a relevant field of work, with a background and interest in international humanitarian development.
 Knowledge & Skills: 
 • General knowledge of information management best practices, techniques and processes with some understanding of the basic theoretical background.
 • Strong written and oral communication skills, including substantive analysis and report writing skills, both in French and English.
 • Knowledge of, or the ability to quickly assimilate, WFP specific processes and systems, can be an advantage.
 Language: Fluency (level C) in French and English languages. Knowledge of other official UN language: Arabic, Chinese, Russian, Spanish, and/or Portuguese is an asset.

Only Mauritanian nationals are eligible to apply for this position.

 Type of Contract: Fixed-Term
 Grade: NOD

 Duty Station: Manila, Philippines

 This position is open to Filipino nationals only. 
 ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT: 
 The Head of Enabling Services will report directly to the Representative and Country Director and will provide strategic leadership and oversight of the Country Office’s enabling services functions.
 JOB PURPOSE: 
 To manage all the enabling services, which may include Management Services, Human Resources (HR), Budget & Programming, Finance, and TEC of the Philippines Country Office and manage the common back-office service provision to the recipient UN Agencies.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES: 
 Under the direct supervision of the Country Director of the Philippines Country Office, the incumbent will provide strategic leadership and oversight of the enabling services units, ensuring the effective, integrated, and client-oriented delivery of services to the CO, including all SOs and field presence structures.
 Oversee the effective management of CO financial, human, and technological resources, identifying risks and opportunities, with a strong focus on organizational effectiveness, operational enablement, workforce capability, results, innovation, efficiency, and cost- consciousness.
 Direct supervision of the enabling services units, Finance, Management Services Division (MSD), HR, and TEC, building an inclusive and respectful workplace culture and high performing team . Ensure close collaboration and alignment with the procurement unit.
 Establish and drive continuous improvement of processes and procedures in the areas of enabling services, ensuring compliance with the WFP governance frameworks, internal controls, and delegation of authority, for the effective and consistent provision of quality services to staff and stakeholders.
 Act as the CO audit and risk management focal point and ensure that a risk register is established and monitored, follow up on audit recommendations and implementation. Chair and manage quarterly risk management committee meetings.
 Monitor and oversee accurate and timely reporting that enables informed, data-based decision making, and consistency of information presented to stakeholders.
 Conduct regular field visits to monitor conditions and assess needs, requirements, risks, and opportunities, ensuring timely identification and resolution of issues.
 Establish and implement agreements and arrangements for common back-office services provided by WFP with UN agencies in the Philippines and ensure quality service delivery as the client manager for all recipient agencies irrespective of the service provided.
 Represent WFP and identify opportunities to increase support to the OMT.
 Support the Country Director and Deputy Country Director with office management/deputize when absent.
 Perform other related duties and responsibilities as required.
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE : 
 Education: Advanced University degree in Business/Public Administration, Social Science or other relevant field relating to office management and administration, or First University degree with additional years of related work experience and/or training courses
 Experience: At least eight (8) years of relevant progressively responsible, postgraduate experience in resource management, including Finance, Budget Management, Administration and Human Resources. 
 Knowledge & Skills: 
 Strategic thinking and business acumen.
 Ability to act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and influence decision-making.
 Excellence in people management, with demonstrated experience in building an inclusive and respectful workplace culture, and building high performing teams.
 Ability to challenge and guide the technical leads in the team, understand cross-functional dependencies, identify risks and opportunities across the enabling services portfolio, and make integrated resource allocation decisions.
 Demonstrated thorough and deep understanding of organizational governance frameworks, internal controls, and delegation of authority, with the ability to operate effectively and consistently within them.
 Operational excellence, demonstrating results-based management, process improvement and simplification, data-driven decision making, and digital enablement.
 Demonstrated ability to provide practical and innovative solutions, achieve the goals amidst resource constraints, and apply a client-oriented approach to problem solving.
 Demonstrated ability to build and maintain trusted partnerships across functions, organizational levels, and external stakeholders, enabling effective collaboration and service delivery.
 Experience in emergency contexts, particularly in scaling up in response to sudden onset emergencies.
 Strong understanding of WFP’s management frameworks and emergency procedures (desired requirement).
 Language: Fluency (level C) in English language and the duty station’s language, if different.

 Remuneration based on the applicable UN salary scale , with details communicated at the offer stage;
 Medical coverage for the staff member and eligible dependents;
 Pension benefits , subject to applicable eligibility requirements; and
 Leave benefits and other applicable allowances and entitlements in accordance with the conditions of service.

 JOB TITLE: Monitoring Assistant
 TYPE OF CONRTACT: Service Contract Level 5, SC5
 UNIT/DIVISION: RBJ/RAM Unit
 DUTY STATION (City, Country): Dodoma, Tanzania
 DURATION: 12 months
 PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:    
 Job holders typically report to a Monitoring Associate; the reporting lines may change depending on the location and size of the office. At this level, work is carried out under minimum supervision. Job holders are expected to produce organized and accurate technical work and reports. They may provide guidance on standard practices to other staff and counterparts in their area of work.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:  
 In consultation with the Head of Field Office and Monitoring Associate, support the preparation and implementation of monthly monitoring plans for assigned catchment areas and contribute to the regular updating of Risk-Based Monitoring Framework (RBMF) parameters in accordance with Country Office guidance.
 Monitor WFP programme activities and cooperating partner performance to ensure compliance with minimum monitoring requirements and support timely implementation. Coordinate and conduct process, output, and outcome monitoring activities, including distribution monitoring, post-distribution monitoring, surveys, observations, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and other qualitative and quantitative data collection exercises.
 Collaborate with cooperating partners, government institutions, NGOs, CSOs, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders to facilitate monitoring activities, collect programme information, and support evidence-based decision-making.
 Conduct routine data quality assurance and verification during monitoring missions to ensure that data reported by cooperating partners is accurate, complete, consistent, and supported by verifiable source documents. Identify data quality issues, provide on-site guidance for corrective actions, and escalate significant discrepancies for follow-up in line with WFP data quality standards.
 Ensure that findings and issues identified during monitoring visits are properly documented and promptly recorded in the Process Monitoring Issues Escalation System (SugarCRM). Support issue resolution processes, track corrective actions, and provide regular updates on implementation status to relevant stakeholders.
 Compile, analyze, and summarize monitoring data and findings to produce monitoring reports, support programme reviews, contribute to field office reporting requirements, and provide timely updates to monitoring tracking systems and corporate reporting platforms, including COMET.
 Maintain accurate records of monitoring activities and site coverage within assigned areas, ensuring that all activity sites are monitored according to approved plans and reporting requirements.
 Provide training and technical support to cooperating partners on WFP monitoring tools, methodologies, and reporting requirements. Support the organization and implementation of technical support, evaluation, and monitoring missions led by the Country Office or other stakeholders.
 Promote adherence to WFP monitoring policies, standard operating procedures (SOPs), Corporate Results Framework (CRF) requirements, data protection and privacy standards, and ethical principles throughout all monitoring activities.
 Work closely with the Complaints and Feedback Mechanism (CFM) team to support the communication of actions taken in response to monitoring and feedback findings, contributing to accountability and transparency with beneficiaries.
 Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor.
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE: 
 Education: 
 Completion of secondary school education is required. A post-secondary certificate in the related functional area is desirable. Having a bachelor’s degree in agriculture, agricultural economics, agribusiness, rural development, nutrition, food security, statistics, natural resources management of other related fields is an advantage.
 Experience: 
 Has a minimum of 4 years of relevant monitoring and/or operational experience, including coordinating project implementation and monitoring activities, developing monitoring data collection questionnaires and digitizing them, collecting monitoring data, conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses, and reporting findings to management, partners and other stakeholders. 
 Has worked with technical teams (i.e., agriculture, nutrition, food security analysis, etc.).
 Has contributed to implementation of programmes in support of food assistance, resilience building, livelihoods support, and small-holder farmer support.
 Has experience in dealing with horticultural crops.
 Has experience in applying sustainable farming systems and environmental conservation practices in agriculture.
 Knowledge & Skills: 
 Data analytical knowledge and skills on Programme output and outcome data monitoring.
 General knowledge of monitoring systems, processes, tools, and standards.
 Compilation, analysis, and presentation of data using statistical and presentation software such as Excel, SPSS, Tableau and PowerPoint.
 Experience in direct implementation or field monitoring of community or village-based projects.
 Demonstrate to have problem solving skills.
 Language: 
 Fluency in both oral and written communication in English and Swahili languages.

 JOB TITLE: Programme Policy Officer - Head of Programme
 TYPE OF CONTRACT: International Consultant
 LEVEL: Level I
 UNIT: Programme
 NUMBER OF POSITIONS ADVERTISED: Two (2)
 DUTY STATIONS: One (1) position based in Beni, DRC, one (1) position based in Kalemie, DRC
 DURATION: 11-months
 BACKGROUND: 
 The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues to face one of the world's most severe and complex food and nutrition crises. Protracted conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks, climate shocks, weak infrastructure and constrained humanitarian access continue to erode livelihoods and increase acute needs, particularly in eastern provinces.
 WFP DRC delivers life-saving food and nutrition assistance through in-kind food, cash and e-vouchers, while supporting school-based programmes, resilience and livelihoods, local food systems, emergency preparedness, anticipatory action and national capacity strengthening. Resource constraints require disciplined prioritization, strong programme assurance and close coordination across programme, supply chain, finance, security, monitoring, protection and partnerships.
 WFP is transitioning from the 2021-2026 Country Strategic Plan to the 2027-2030 CSP. The new CSP places crisis response first while advancing an integrated humanitarian solutions approach that links emergency assistance, where context and resources permit, with early recovery, resilience, nutrition-sensitive food systems, school-based programmes, social protection and nationally owned systems.
 ORGANIZATIONAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT: 
 The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world's largest humanitarian organization fighting hunger and supporting communities to improve nutrition, strengthen resilience and create sustainable pathways towards food security.
 In the DRC, WFP maintains a large operational footprint and works with communities, government authorities, United Nations entities, cooperating partners, civil society and the private sector. Delivery is supported by assessments and vulnerability analysis, digital beneficiary management, monitoring, community feedback mechanisms, supply chain services, the Logistics Cluster and the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service.
 Kalemie Field Office 
 Kalemie Field Office covers a broad and diverse operational area in Tanganyika Province, including Kalemie and field locations supported through the Nyunzu presence. The context combines food insecurity, malnutrition, displacement, localized insecurity, weak infrastructure and recurrent climate-related shocks, including flooding and rising Lake Tanganyika water levels. Access and supply routes are often difficult, requiring close operational planning and coordination. The portfolio includes unconditional food assistance through in-kind and cash-based transfers, nutrition prevention and treatment, school meals, resilience and livelihood activities, disaster preparedness and anticipatory action. The office also works with provincial authorities, cooperating partners and communities to strengthen preparedness, local systems and links between emergency response, early recovery and longer-term resilience.
 The Programme Policy Officer - Head of Programme will lead the Kalemie programme team and translate Country Office strategy into practical field plans across Tanganyika. The role will ensure integrated, timely and accountable delivery, with particular attention to programme quality, cash and in-kind operations, nutrition, school-based programmes, resilience, anticipatory action, partner management and operational assurance.
 Beni Field Office 
 Beni Field Office operates in the Grand Nord of North Kivu, an area affected by recurrent armed violence, displacement, public health emergencies and major access constraints. Operations require rapid adaptation to changing security conditions, strong emergency preparedness and close coordination with health, protection, logistics and security actors. The office manages food and nutrition assistance, including emergency distributions, cash-based transfers and support linked to disease outbreaks, while maintaining community engagement, accountability and conflict-sensitive delivery.
 The programme environment includes Beni, Butembo, Oicha, Lubero and surrounding hard-to-reach areas. Volatile access, population movements, market and financial-service constraints, partner capacity and pipeline risks require robust field-level leadership, evidence-based prioritization, strong operational controls and timely escalation to the Country Office.
 WFP DRC OPERATIONS AND CSP 2027-2030 PRIORITIES: 
 Protect life-saving food and nutrition assistance for severely food-insecure and nutritionally vulnerable people.
 Strengthen emergency preparedness, early warning, anticipatory action, rapid response and early recovery capacity.
 Connect emergency assistance with nutrition, resilience, livelihoods, local food systems and school-based programmes where context and resources allow.• Apply transparent, evidence-based prioritization, appropriate transfer modalities and adaptive programme management.
 Strengthen protection, accountability to affected people, gender equality, disability inclusion, localization, risk management and internal controls.
 Build effective partnerships with authorities, communities, United Nations entities, cooperating partners and donors.
 JOB PURPOSE: 
 Under the direct supervision of the Head of Field Office, the Programme Policy Officer - Head of Programme will lead the Programme team and manage the Field Office programme portfolio. The incumbent will translate WFP DRC strategy and the 2027-2030 CSP into coherent field plans; ensure timely, safe, accountable and cost-effective delivery; strengthen integrated humanitarian solutions; and maintain strong relationships with communities, government counterparts, United Nations entities

 ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT: 
 The position is based in Budapest, Hungary, and reports to the Head of Global Payments Solution (CFOFG). 
 The Global Payments Solution (GPS) is WFP's global payment shared service operating model established to centralize payment execution, standardize end-to-end payment processes, strengthen governance and controls, and leverage technology-enabled service delivery across WFP. Following completion of the design, build and rollout phases, GPS has entered a defined stabilization and optimization phase focused on consolidating the transformation achieved, completing deferred implementation activities, strengthening governance frameworks, advancing technology enablement and preparing the organization for its future steady state operating model.
 JOB PURPOSE: 
Reporting to the Head of Global Payments Solution, the incumbent provides temporary operational coordination and technical oversight of GPS payment activities during the stabilization and transition period, while driving the completion of defined transformation workstreams. The assignment combines business continuity responsibilities with delivery of the strategic initiatives required to institutionalize centralized payment operations across WFP. 
 The position combines payment operations, transformation, governance, systems integration, performance management, change management and knowledge transfer in a single time-bound assignment. While individual elements of these responsibilities may exist in other finance and shared service functions, their integrated application within WFP's centralized, high volume payment operating model is not fully reflected in existing Job Profiles and cannot reasonably be met through the existing rotational workforce. The assignment has defined outcomes and supports transition to the future steady-state GPS structure.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority):
 Strategic Transformation and Operating Model Stabilization: 
 Coordinate completion of the defined stabilization and consolidation activities for the Global Payments Solution operating model, ensuring realization of expected business benefits and alignment with WFP's shared service strategy. 
 Drive completion of the agreed transition activities towards centralized payment execution across WFP, including onboarding of deferred activities and integration of remaining payment processes within the approved assignment scope. 
 Coordinate implementation of priority GPS improvement initiatives, including agreed system enhancements across ITS, ServiceNow, SAP FI-AP and SAP BCM, together with strengthened governance, control and risk-management practices. 
 Implement the agreed GPS KPI, service-level and performance-monitoring framework and use process analysis to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, user experience, operational controls and risk management. 
 Coordinate change management, communication and adoption activities across Headquarters and Country Offices to support embedding of the GPS operating model within the approved rollout scope. 
 Develop and execute documented knowledge-transfer and capacity-building plans to support handover to the future steady-state organizational structure.
 Develop and execute knowledge-transfer and capacity-building plans to support transition towards the future steady-state organizational structure. 
 Technology and Process Enhancement
 Coordinate implementation of the agreed system enhancements across ITS, ServiceNow, SAP FI-AP and SAP BCM, ensuring alignment between business requirements, operational objectives and technology capabilities.
 Analyse exception trends, workflow bottlenecks and process-performance indicators to identify improvement opportunities and support data-driven decision-making. 
 Support redesign and optimization of payment workflows, controls and operating procedures to enhance scalability, standardization and control effectiveness. 
 Operational Coordination and Technical Oversight: 
 Provide operational coordination and technical oversight of centralized payment activities, ensuring continuity, control and timeliness of payment execution during the transformation and stabilization period. 
 Act as the escalation point for complex payment, compliance and system-related matters requiring cross-functional resolution. 
 Monitor compliance of payment operations with WFP Financial Regulations, IPSAS requirements and internal control standards while transformation activities are implemented. 
 Expected Assignment Outcomes The time-bound assignment is expected to deliver: 
 Completion of the GPS stabilization activities approved for the assignment period. 
 Integration of the payment processes approved for further centralization. 
 Implementation and documentation of the agreed governance and control mechanisms. 
 Deployment of the ITS, ServiceNow, SAP FI-AP and SAP BCM enhancements approved for implementation. 
 Implementation of the agreed GPS KPI, service-level and performance-reporting framework.
 Implementation of standardized payment procedures for the Country Offices included in the agreed rollout scope. • Completion of documented knowledge transfer and handover to the future steady-state GPS structure. These deliverables have an anticipated completion state and are distinct from the ongoing operational activities of the payment service, supporting the proposed project-bound LFT modality.

 Education: Advanced University degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field. A first level university degree with additional years of related work experience.

 At least five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in finance, accounting, payments, or financial operations. 
 Proven experience in coordinating or overseeing c

 The overall objective of this consultancy assignment is to support the GCF proposal development process through in country coordination and facilitation, ensuring effective engagement with national and local authorities, alignment with national policy frameworks, coordination of co financing commitments, and efficient organization of field missions.  Contribute towards the development of a wide variety of projects, plans and processes, ensuring alignment with wider programme policies and guidance.

 Other as required.

 Key proposal annexes inputs, contributing to the documents as relevant.

 Regular progress updates to WFP.
