The Early Warning Expert position will be based within the Supply Chain Unit’s Emergency Preparedness and Response Unit of the WFP Malawi Country Office and Seconded to the SADC Humanitarian and Emergency Operations Centre (SHOC) in Nacala, Mozambique. 
The position will report to the delegated authority of the Director, SHOC. 
To strengthen regional multi-hazard early warning, anticipatory action, and disaster risk management capacities by working closely with Government institutions, humanitarian partners, and regional organizations to enhance preparedness, improve risk analysis, and support evidence-based decision-making for disaster preparedness and response. Under the delegated authority of the Executive Director, the Early Warning Expert shall perform the following functions:
 1. Coordination and Partnerships 
 Support the WFP Project Manager in planning, coordinating and monitoring project activities in collaboration with SHOC
 Maintain regular liaison with Project technical partners to ensure alignment of national and regional activities.
 Support the planning and facilitation of technical coordination meetings, trainings and joint missions among project stakeholders and partners
 Support the establishment and coordination of regional early warning and Information Management working groups and technical task teams.
 Promote knowledge sharing and visibility of project outcomes across SADC and partner institutions.
 2. Hazard Monitoring & Early Warning Analysis 
 Lead real-time monitoring and analysis of regional multi-hazards through the SHOC Multi-Hazard Situation Room, ensuring timely identiﬁcation of triggers and thresholds that inform Anticipatory Action protocols across the SADC region.
 Generate actionable early warning briefs, advisories and risk intelligence updates for SADC Member States, incorporating co-production approaches and regional contextualization to ensure that advisories directly feed into pre-agreed anticipatory actions.
 Deliver anticipatory analysis and forward-looking risk assessments—including scenario building and probability-based risk proﬁling—to support evidence-driven preparedness planning and enable early actions before hazards materialize.
 Enhance and maintain multi-hazard monitoring dashboards and analytical tools in collaboration with SHOC’s Information Management and GIS teams, ensuring they integrate risk indicators, triggers, and decision-support layers used for activating anticipatory action mechanisms. 
 3. Technical and Operational Support 
 Support implementation of AI-enabled Early Warning Systems, geospatial analysis tools and risk modelling.
 Assist in the setup and operation of the Geospatial Information Management Service Desk, ensuring technical requests are tracked and addressed.
 Support SHOC and partners in integrating Early Warning geospatial data into decision-making, reporting, preparedness and emergency operations.
 Support the SADC Emergency Response Team (ERT) with early warning information before and during deployments
 4. Data Integration and Analytics 
 Collaborate with SHOC Information Management/GIS teams to develop integrated early warning datasets/information (Hazard, vulnerability, exposure and coping capacity).
 Continuously support the development and update of triggers for Anticipatory Action and monitor them for Early Action
 Support the establishment and update of the regional disaster loss database and monitoring tools Facilitate the co-production and interoperability between SHOC Early Warning products and systems and regional products platforms.
 5. Capacity Development and Communication 
 Assist in the development of training materials, guidance notes, and knowledge products for capacity building and dissemination.
 Support organization of training sessions and workshops for SHOC and NDMA staff on early warning, geospatial tools, and disaster preparedness.
 Liaise with SHOC and WFP’s communications teams for documentation of key milestones, success stories, and media materials.
 7. Monitoring, Reporting and Documentation 
 Compile monthly progress updates, quarterly reports, and ﬁnal project reports as per SHOC, WFP and donor requirements.
 Monitor performance indicators and document lessons learned, success stories, and best practices. Maintain an up-to-date project results matrix and ensure quality and accuracy of technical deliverables.
 QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: 
 Education: 
 Advanced University degree in Meteorology, Climate Science, Disaster Risk Management, Environmental Science, Natural Resources Management, or another relevant discipline.
 Experience 
 At least five years of progressively responsible professional experience in early warning systems, disaster risk reduction, climate services, humanitarian preparedness, emergency management or related fields.
 Demonstrated experience in multi-hazard risk assessment, anticipatory action, climate and weather analysis, GIS and information management.
 Experience working with Government institutions, UN agencies or humanitarian organizations.
 Knowledge of disaster risk management frameworks and emergency preparedness.
 Experience developing technical reports, dashboards and analytical products.
 Strong coordination, facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office, GIS applications and data analysis software.
 Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and multicultural environments.
 Languages : 
 Fluency (Level C) in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills, is required for effective coordination with internal and external stakeholders, reporting, and operational support activities.

 JOB TITLE: Junior Consultant – Global Planning and Prioritization TYPE OF CONTRACT: Jr. CST-II Regular Consultancy 
 DIVISION/UNIT: Programme Cycle, Quality and Budgeting Service – Global Budget Planning and Prioritization Unit (PQB-G)
 DURATION: 11 months
 DUTY STATION: Rome, Italy
 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:
 The Programme Cycle, Quality & Budgeting Service serves as a centralized support structure that integrates programme cycle management, CSP quality assurance, and global programme budget 
 management. Within the Service, the Budget Planning & Prioritisation Unit (PQBG) focuses on strengthening WFP’s strategic resource management by enabling high-quality, evidence-informed decisions through budget planning, prioritization, advance financing, corporate reporting and analysis, in support of field operations.
 The assignment will support the Advance Financing and Prioritization Team within PQBG by providing dedicated analytical, reporting and knowledge management expertise.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
 Under the supervision of the designated PQB-G manager, the consultant will perform the following. 
 functions:
 • Compile and analyse operational, budget and resource data to support planning, prioritization and resource allocation.
 • Monitor advance financing and multilateral resources, including utilization, repayments, 
 allocations and balances.
 • Maintain dashboards, trackers and analytical products, ensuring information is accurate and up to date.
 • Support the preparation of corporate planning and reporting products, including the Annual Performance Report and Management Plan.
 • Prepare analysis, presentations, briefing materials and other inputs for management review and meetings.
 • Maintain process documentation and knowledge resources, and support improvements to analytical, automated and AI-enabled tools and processes.
 Deliverables at the end of the consultancy:
 • Key corporate operational planning and reporting outputs, including the Annual Performance Report and Management Plan, are coordinated and prepared to a high standard, ensuring coherence, quality and alignment across the organization.
 • Advance Financing requests are managed, allocated and monitored in a timely and transparent manner, supported by accurate analysis, clear documentation and strong governance.
 • The Multilateral Budget Committee receives timely, accurate and well-coordinated analytical support to inform the prioritization and allocation of flexible resources.
 • Operational planning and reporting processes are strengthened through streamlined workflows, improved tools, audit support and policy analysis, while the unit is effectively represented in relevant meetings, committees and working groups from a budget and programming perspective. 
 Key competencies:
 • Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to integrate operational, budget and performance information from multiple sources.
 • Proficiency in data analytics, business intelligence and visualization tools; experience with process automation, artificial intelligence applications or predictive analytics is desirable.
 • Good drafting and presentation skills in English.
 • Strong knowledge management, drafting and presentation skills.
 • Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently and deliver high-quality outputs within tight deadlines.
 • Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues from different technical, national and cultural backgrounds.
 QUALIFICATIONS:
 Education and Experience:
 • Advanced university degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics or other relevant field, or first level university degree with additional relevant work experience.
 • One year of relevant working experience in the subject matter, which can include areas such as contributing to the development of budgets; production of planning/budgetary reports or other analytical reports to support management decision making; supply chain and resource management.
 • Experience in WFP, the United Nations or the humanitarian and development sector is an advantage.
 Language:
 • Strong written and spoken English skills.
 • Knowledge of another UN official language is an advantage.

 POSITION TITLE: Regular Giving Specialist
 ORG UNIT : Private Sector Partnerships (PSP) Org.Unit 50015246
 DUTY STATION: Remote (administrative DS is Rome, HQ)
 CONTRACT TYPE: Short-Term, Regular Consultant 
 DURATION: 11 months
 LINE MANAGER/SUPERVISOR: Mass Fundraising Lead
 ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT 
 The Private Partnerships Division (PSP) is responsible for mobilizing resources from the private sector to support the World Food Programme’s (WFP’s) global mission. WFP is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives and changing lives, delivering food assistance in emergencies and working with communities to improve nutrition and build resilience. Every day, over 5,000 WFP-chartered trucks are on the road, supported by around 80 aircraft and 20 ships delivering food and assistance to those in need.
 Despite our efforts, the needs remain immense and growing, driven by a deadly combination of conflict, climate shocks, economic instability, and forced displacement. As of 2025, over 345 million people face acute food insecurity across 79 countries. To meet these needs and build a more sustainable, predictable, and flexible funding stream, we began investing in growing our Individual Giving (IG) programme in 2019 and, this year marks the start of the second phase of the strategy (2026-2030).
 WFP’s second phase of the private sector strategy sets out an ambitious plan to further scale income from individuals, enabling us to reach more people with life-saving assistance. Our approach is digital-first, leveraging global reach and cost-effective tools to engage supporters worldwide. In addition to digital channels we are now expanding into Face-to-Face (F2F) and Direct Response Television (DRTV) fundraising to diversify acquisition and deepen engagement.
 This centralized, global strategy positions WFP to leapfrog traditional models and build a robust IG programme that delivers long-term impact.
 INDIVIDUAL FUNDRAISING 
 WFP’s Individual Giving programme launched in 2019 and has grown into a USD +50 million annual operation, raising over USD 150 million in its first five years. The programme is built around a digital-first strategy, led by a centralized global team that recruits supporters primarily through digital channels.
 We deliver a multi-lingual, multi-channel supporter experience, designed to offer a best-in-class donor journey. Donors are recruited in English, French, German, Spanish, and Arabic with additional capabilities in Korean and Chinese. Supporter engagement is delivered through email, WhatsApp, telephone and Meta.
 Regular Giving has been identified as a critical growth driver within the current strategy. Income from the programme is projected to increase from USD 25 million in 2026 to almost USD 60 million by 2030. WFP's Regular Giving programme currently operates across six core languages and is delivered through multiple channels including email, telemarketing, WhatsApp and Meta.
 PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT 
 The purpose of the assignment is to manage the entirety of WFP’s IG Regular Giving Programme. This includes supporting the development and delivery of the RG strategy, delivering RG comms, monitoring programme performance to ensure key benchmarks are met and exceeded, and providing strategic guidance on opportunities to increase the value of the RG file. Efforts will focus on improving RG retention rates and increasing the SG to RG conversion rate, through best-in-class donor communications. The role will also be responsible for monitoring Regular Giving performance across the wider IG programme, tracking the acquisition of new pledges regardless of source, assessing the overall health of the programme, and highlighting relevant insights and trends to stakeholders. It will be important to identify and raise new ideas, drawing inspiration from both within and outside the sector.
 You will have experience working at the international level, ideally within a UN agency, as part of the IG team delivering campaigns in multiple territories. You will have experience managing Regular Giving activities through digital and direct response channels, with a proven track record of building, maintaining and nurturing ongoing regular supporters. The role requires strong analytical skills, with the ability to identify, investigate and resolve performance issues.
 Until recently, this role sat within a standalone Regular Giving workstream. In Q4 2026, Regular Giving and Single Giving workstreams were brought together to form the new Mass Fundraising workstream. The Regular Giving Specialist will play a key role in supporting this integration, working closely with the Mass Fundraising Lead on planning and delivery, and helping to evolve the programme from a channel-led approach to a donor-centric, omnichannel model.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 1. Planning and strategy 
 Lead the Regular Giving retention programme, including annual planning, budgeting and objective setting.
 Develop an annual calendar of activities that demonstrates how the Regular Giving programme will deliver value and growth, outlining key activities, channels and timings.
 Support the development and implementation of the Regular Giving strategy in collaboration with the Mass Fundraising Lead.
 Make recommendations to Acquisition colleagues on where to recruit regular givers, considering volume, retention, CPA, payment method and lifetime value. Ensure recruitment activity prioritises supporters with the greatest long-term fundraising potential.
 2. Programme Delivery 
 Expand Regular Giving activities in line with the RG strategy to maximize return, with an initial focus on launching Telemarketing in Australia and Germany markets.

 JOB TITLE: Risk Financing & Insurance Analyst
 TYPE OF CONTRACT: CST-I
 UNIT/DIVISION: Disaster Climate and Resilience Service (PRGR), Programme, Policy and Guidance Division (PRG)
 DUTY STATION (City, Country): Rome, Italy
 DURATION: 11 months
 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:
 Climate impacts are increasing in frequency and intensity, driving humanitarian needs and amplifying food insecurity risks across WFP's areas of operation. WFP's Climate and Resilience Service (PRGR), located within the Programme, Policy and Guidance Division (PPG), supports governments and communities to better understand, manage and finance climate risks. Within this, the macro- and micro / meso-level disaster risk financing (DRF) portfolio is rapidly expanding, with innovative instruments - from macro insurance to catastrophe bonds and layered risk financing - becoming central to WFP's support for national preparedness and response systems.
 DRF has a clearly defined role across all three strategic objectives of WFP's new strategic plan: emergency preparedness and response, resilience strengthening, and systems strengthening through pre-arranged finance. WFP's macro insurance portfolio currently covers 25+ countries, protects over 3 million people, and provides more than USD 108 million in financial coverage across Africa, the Caribbean, the Pacific, and fragile states. Instruments span ARC Replica policies, government top-up arrangements through CCRIF, PCRIC, and SEADRIF, direct commercial insurance programmes (including bespoke products for fragile and conflict-affected states), catastrophe layers, and the development of insurance-linked securities.
 Under the overall guidance of the Macro Level Climate Risk Financing Programmes Lead, and under the direct supervision of the Senior Technical Advisor - DRF, the Risk Financing & Insurance Analyst will provide analytical and technical support across the DRF portfolio. The Consultant will contribute to index performance assessment, risk transfer parameter analysis, product design support, seasonal monitoring, and knowledge management, enabling the senior technical team to deliver high-quality DRF instruments and advisory services to Country Offices and government partners.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
 1.Technical Analysis - Risk Indices and Product Performance - Assess the performance of parametric indices (including WRSI, NDVI, rainfall and TC wind models) used across WFP's Macro and Inclusive Risk Finance insurance portfolio, evaluating their suitability relative to intended impact levels.
 2.Conduct back-testing and historical analysis of index triggers against known shock events to i- dentify basis risk and inform Risk Transfer Parameters selection for new or renewed policies.
 3.Support the Senior Technical Advisor in reviewing risk transfer parameters (attachment point, exhaustion point, coverage limit, rate on line) for country-level DRF products, preparing clear summaries for technical review and sign-off.
 4.Contribute to the development and quality assurance of customisation reports and technical notes required for policy placement and sign-off processes.
 5.Seasonal Monitoring and Early Warning - Carry out regular seasonal monitoring of key hazard indices across the DRF portfolio (drought, tropical cyclone, excess rainfall), flagging emerging trigger conditions to Country Offices and the senior technical team in a timely manner.
 6.Compile and maintain seasonal monitoring trackers, consolidating data from ARC, CCRIF, PCRIC, SEADRIF, commercial insurers, and other sources into accessible formats for internal and external audiences.
 7.Support the preparation of early warning bulletins and situation reports during active monitoring periods.
 8.Support to Country Offices and Capacity Building - Provide technical support to Country Office and Regional Advisor focal points on DRF product design, index methodology, and risk transfer parameters, responding to queries and preparing briefing materials.
 9.Assist in the preparation of training materials, guidance notes, and presentations for Country Office staff, government counterparts, and workshop participants on parametric insurance and DRF concepts.
 10.Support the documentation of lessons learned and evidence generation from payout events and operational plan implementation.
 11.Research, Evidence, and Knowledge Management - Undertake research on emerging DRF instruments, index methodologies, and market developments, including catastrophe bond structuring, ILS, and blended finance approaches.
 12.Support the preparation of technical briefing notes, policy papers, and donor reports on WFP's DRF portfolio and results.
 13.Maintain and update internal knowledge management systems, including product databases, RTP trackers, and portfolio documentation.
 14.Contribute to the risk financing framework study by supporting data collection, analysis, and review of service provider outputs.
 15.Market and Partner Support - Assist the Senior Technical Advisor in preparing materials for engagement with risk pools (ARC, CCRIF, PCRIC, SEADRIF), commercial insurers and brokers for direct insurance programmes, and other market partners.
 16.Support the coordination of Technical Working Group (TWG) processes, including meeting preparation, note-taking, and follow-up on action points.
 17.Contribute to WFP's engagement in relevant DRF fora and events by preparing background materials and supporting presentations.
 DELIVERABLES AT THE END OF THE CONTRACT:
 •Index performance assessments and back-testing analyses for a minimum of three country DRF programmes, with recommendations on basis risk and RTP selection.
 •Seasonal monitoring reports produced throughout the contract period, covering active hazard seasons across the portfolio.
 •Technical briefing notes and customisation report inputs for at least two policy

 BACKGROUND:

As Somalia continues to face recurrent climate shocks, food insecurity, displacement, disease outbreaks, and persistent malnutrition, WFP is committed to strengthening both nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions across its programme portfolio.
 The Nutrition Officer will support the design, implementation, monitoring, reporting, coordination, and operational management of WFP Somalia’s nutrition programmes. The role will provide technical leadership for nutrition integration across Food Systems, Livelihoods and Social Protection programming while simultaneously leading nutrition information management, reporting, monitoring systems, and specialized nutritious food (SNF) pipeline management.
 The incumbent will be based in Mogadishu and work closely with Area Offices, government counterparts, cooperating partners, UN agencies, Regional Bureau Nairobi, and HQ to strengthen programme quality, effectiveness, accountability, evidence generation, and operational efficiency.
 The position supports WFP's efforts to strengthen national Nutrition goals and contributes to broader education, nutrition, social protection, and human capital development objectives.
 PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 The position will strengthen Programme quality through technical support, nutrition information management, evidence generation, and specialized nutritious food (SNF) pipeline oversight.  BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 Technology and connectivity are rapidly reaching some of the most vulnerable people and places affected by crisis, but they are also increasingly expanding to the services responding to those same crises. As one of the main humanitarian actors, WFP has the opportunity and the obligation to leverage data and technology to better know and serve those in need by digitally transforming the way it works.
 Reporting to the Project Manager lead, the Project Manager is expected to oversee relevant TEC stakeholders and external implementing partners aiming for IT solutions which achieve the highest quality in terms of technical usability, user acceptability, and domain suitability. The incumbent will be responsible for leading teams to deliver projects that span across one or more business units and to manage resources, schedules, financials and adhere to deadlines throughout the whole project management cycle. This also includes the management of issues, risks, and project change requests to ensure successful and on-time project delivery.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 1) Lead and coordinate a portfolio of complex initiatives/projects encompassing one or multiple business lines, including the following duties:

 Liaise with Business Engagement Managers to better understand project requirements, needs, change requests, and the interdependencies between technology, operations, and business objectives.
 2) Lead the project management activities, ensuring that all documentation is in place and available for all stakeholders, and prepare for the roll-out.
 Ensure the gathering and validation of requirements follows a Human-Centered Design (HCD) approach, along with time and cost estimates related to scope implementation.
 Help define the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) with a focus on value delivery
 Design and implement the project governance structure.
 Design and implement a communication plan.
 Establish a work plan for staffing, and, in coordination with the IT Solution Owner, establish a Product Team.​
 Implement a change management plan.
 Ensure that the project delivery includes not only the main working IT deliverables but also all the mechanisms and processes for product maintenance, evolution, and full roll-out once the product Minimum Viable Product (MVP) has been delivered.
 3) Manage the project work-plan, risks, and issues, including:
 Monitor, track, and report the project’s progress against the project baselines. Identify key success factors and potential issues and risks that threaten performance and could affect outcomes, timeline, and budget, deciding how best to implement corrective actions.
 Identify, track, and manage divisional risks through corporate documents such as the risk register and developing a corresponding response plan.
 Discuss and support the resolution of issues and questions raised by the technical and functional teams of the project.

 TÍTULO DEL PUESTO: Asociado(a) de Programas - Nutrición 
 TIPO DE CONTRATO: SC L6
 UNIDAD/ DIVISIÓN: Programas
 ESTACIÓN DE SERVICIO: Ciudad de Guatemala, Guatemala
 DURACIÓN: 12 meses
 CONTEXTO ORGANIZATIVO 
 Guatemala enfrenta desafíos persistentes de malnutrición y desigualdad, asociados, entre otros factores, a la limitada diversidad y calidad de las dietas, las brechas en el acceso a servicios y protección social y la exposición recurrente a choques climáticos y emergencias. Este contexto requiere respuestas integrales que fortalezcan las capacidades y los sistemas nacionales y mejoren la situación nutricional de las poblaciones en mayor situación de vulnerabilidad. 
 En el marco de su nuevo Plan Estratégico de País (CSP), el Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) trabaja con el Gobierno de Guatemala y otros socios para contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, fortalecer los sistemas nacionales y promover soluciones sostenibles y resilientes. La nutrición constituye un componente transversal de esta programación, mediante intervenciones de nutrición específica y sensibles a la nutrición, cambio social y de comportamiento (SBC), generación y uso de evidencia y fortalecimiento de capacidades. 
 La posición de Asociado/a de Programas para Nutrición, forma parte del equipo de Programas y contribuye a la integración de la nutrición en los Objetivos Estratégicos 1 y 2 (SO1 y SO2) del CSP, incluyendo las intervenciones de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias, sistemas alimentarios, protección social y alimentación escolar.
 En este marco, la posición brinda apoyo técnico y programático para la implementación y seguimiento de las intervenciones de nutrición y contribuye a la coordinación con instituciones de Gobierno, Sistema de Naciones Unidas, socios y mecanismos de coordinación técnica y humanitaria, participando, según corresponda, en espacios técnicos y consultivos en representación del PMA.
 FINALIDAD DEL PUESTO 
 Bajo la supervisión general de la Jefatura de Programas y directa de la Oficial de Nutrición y Sistemas Alimentarios, la persona Asociada contribuirá a fortalecer la calidad y efectiva implementación de las intervenciones de nutrición de la Oficina de País, incluyendo enfoques de nutrición específica, sensible a la nutrición y cambio social y de comportamiento, y su integración en la preparación y respuesta ante emergencias, los sistemas alimentarios, la protección social y la alimentación escolar, en el marco de los Objetivos Estratégicos 1 y 2 del CSP.
 RESPONSABILIDADES (no se incluyen todas, dentro de la autoridad delegada): 
 La persona deberá: 
 1.     Proporcionar apoyo técnico y asistencia en la elaboración e implementación de diversos procesos y actividades dentro de su esfera específica de actividad, respaldando la armonización con las políticas y directrices más generales en materia de programas. 
 2.     Proporcionar apoyo especializado para la gestión de proyectos a programas específicos para garantizar que las diversas actividades se lleven a cabo teniendo en cuenta las metas establecidas y aplicando las políticas y procedimientos del PMA. 
 3.     Dentro de la esfera específica de responsabilidad, elaborar una serie de informes y análisis de datos (p. ej., sobre las necesidades de asistencia alimentaria, la utilización de recursos, la marcha de los programas o las realizaciones) y poner de relieve las tendencias y aspectos problemáticos, velando por que los resultados cuantificables se adhieran a las normas institucionales y superen el control de calidad. 
 4.     Realizar (o asegurarse de que se realice) una labor minuciosa y oportuna de registro de datos en el marco de la esfera técnica de actividad de que se trate (p. ej., programas de asistencia o análisis de la seguridad alimentaria y la vulnerabilidad), garantizando la coherencia de la información que se presenta a los interesados. 
 5.     Mantener el contacto con sus homólogos internos para sostener la colaboración, la implementación y el seguimiento eficaces de las actividades de los proyectos en curso. 
 6.     Coordinarse y comunicar con los asociados, los organismos, las ONG y las instituciones públicas a nivel local para realizar análisis minuciosos de la situación de seguridad alimentaria y garantizar la entrega eficiente de asistencia alimentaria. 
 7.     Prestar apoyo al fortalecimiento de la capacidad del personal del PMA, los asociados cooperantes y el Gobierno nacional en la esfera técnica específica de que se trate. 
 8.     Servir de punto de contacto para la resolución de toda una serie de consultas y problemas operacionales en el marco de una determinada esfera técnica de responsabilidad. 
 9.     Supervisar y/o revisar el trabajo de otros funcionarios de apoyo, proporcionando asesoramiento y orientación prácticos, para contribuir a alcanzar los objetivos de conformidad con las normas y los plazos convenidos 
 OTROS REQUISITOS DEL PUESTO 
 10.  Actuar como referente técnico en nutrición, brindando orientación y asistencia técnica a las unidades y equipos de campo para integrar adecuadamente los objetivos y criterios de nutrición en las intervenciones de sistemas alimentarios, protección social, alimentación escolar y otros programas relevantes. 
 11.  Brindar asistencia técnica para la implementación de la Estrategia de Cambio Social y de Comportamiento (SBC), incluyendo la revisión y adaptación de enfoques, contenidos, materiales y actividades relacionadas con nutrición, dietas saludables y prácticas de alimentación. 
 12.  Apoyar la integración de la nutrición en la preparación y respuesta ante emergencias, incluyendo acción anticipatoria, evaluación de necesidades, priorización de grupos nutricionalmente vulnerables, prevención de la malnutrición, respuesta alimentaria y nutricional, recuperación temprana y protección social reactiva ante emergencias. 
 13.  Brindar asis

 TÍTULO DEL PUESTO: Asociado(a) de Programas - Sistemas Alimentarios y Cadenas de Valor 
 TIPO DE CONTRATO: SC L7
 UNIDAD/ DIVISIÓN: Programas
 ESTACIÓN DE SERVICIO: Guatemala, Guatemala
 DURACIÓN: 12 meses
 CONTEXTO ORGANIZATIVO 
 Guatemala es un país de ingresos medios-altos con indicadores macroeconómicos estables y crecimiento económico sostenido. Sin embargo, persisten importantes desafíos relacionados con la pobreza, la desigualdad, la inseguridad alimentaria, la malnutrición y la limitada resiliencia de los medios de vida, especialmente entre las poblaciones rurales, indígenas y las mujeres. Asimismo, la alta exposición a fenómenos climáticos extremos y otros choques recurrentes continúa afectando la capacidad de los hogares y de los sistemas productivos para garantizar un acceso sostenible a alimentos nutritivos y saludables.
 En este contexto, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA), en trabajo conjunto con el Gobierno, la sociedad civil, comunidades, academia y el sector privado, entre otros, impulsa sistemas alimentarios más sostenibles, resilientes e inclusivos. Mediante el Plan Estratégico de País (CSP) 2026–2030, promueve soluciones integradas que fortalecen las capacidades de los actores clave, mejoran el acceso a dietas saludables y mercados y fortalecen las acciones para la preparación, anticipación y respuesta ante emergencias en el país.
 El Resultado Estratégico 2 (SO2) se enfoca en fortalecer los sistemas alimentarios mediante intervenciones orientadas al desarrollo de cadenas de valor inclusivas, el acceso a mercados públicos y privados, el fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales y comunitarias, así como la promoción de prácticas sostenibles, resilientes y sensibles a la nutrición. Este enfoque busca generar cambios sostenibles que contribuyan a mejorar los medios de vida, la seguridad alimentaria y el acceso equitativo a dietas saludables.
 Se espera que la persona que se desempeñe en este puesto apoye el diseño, implementación, seguimiento y fortalecimiento técnico de intervenciones y programas relacionados con el SO2 del nuevo CSP (2026-2030), en particular: sistemas alimentarios sostenibles, agricultura familiar, cadenas de valor inclusivas y resilientes, contribuyendo al logro de los resultados programáticos del Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) mediante la articulación con instituciones gubernamentales, organizaciones de productores, comunidades y socios implementadores.
 FINALIDAD DEL PUESTO 
 Bajo la supervisión general del oficial responsable de Cadenas de Valor, la persona Asociada de Programas será responsable de apoyar la planificación, implementación, seguimiento y coordinación técnica de las intervenciones de sistemas alimentarios y cadenas de valor, con énfasis en el fortalecimiento organizativo, productivo, empresarial y comercial de organizaciones de pequeños productores. Asimismo, contribuirá a su vinculación con mercados públicos, institucionales y privados, incluido el Programa de Alimentación Escolar, e impulsará la incorporación de resiliencia climática, sostenibilidad e inclusión en las intervenciones, en coordinación con instituciones gubernamentales, municipalidades, sector privado, socios cooperantes y otros actores territoriales. 
 RESPONSABILIDADES (no se incluyen todas, dentro de la autoridad delegada): 
 1.     Aportar conocimientos especializados y contribuir a la elaboración de actividades de proyectos, planes y procesos dentro de la esfera técnica de actividad de que se trate, garantizando la alineación con las políticas y las directrices más generales en materia de programas.  
 2.     Coordinar con eficiencia y proporcionar apoyo especializado en la gestión de proyectos a una serie de determinados programas para garantizar que las diversas actividades se lleven a cabo teniendo en cuenta las metas establecidas y aplicando las políticas y procedimientos del PMA.   
 3.     Dentro de la esfera específica de responsabilidad, preparar una serie de informes complejos y análisis sustanciales de datos (por ejemplo, sobre las necesidades de asistencia alimentaria, la utilización de recursos, la marcha de los programas o las realizaciones) y hacer recomendaciones a sus supervisores, velando por que los resultados cuantificables se ajusten a las normas y los controles de calidad institucionales. 
 4.     Dirigir y garantizar una labor minuciosa y oportuna de registro de datos dentro de la esfera técnica de actividad de que se trate (como los programas de asistencia o el análisis de la seguridad alimentaria y la vulnerabilidad), garantizando la coherencia de la información que se presenta a los interesados.  
 5.     Coordinarse y mantener el contacto con sus homólogos internos acerca de una variedad de asuntos complejos para posibilitar una colaboración, ejecución y seguimiento efectivos de las actividades de los proyectos en curso. 
 6.     Promover las relaciones y sostener el establecimiento de alianzas con los asociados, los organismos, las ONG y las instituciones públicas locales para realizar análisis minuciosos de la situación de seguridad alimentaria y garantizar la entrega eficiente de asistencia alimentaria.

 Organizational context
 The Executive Board Secretariat provides governance services to the Executive Board and its Bureau and facilitates interaction between the Board and WFP management.  Job purpose
 The Multilingual Web Content & Analytics and Translation Technology Professional will manage multilingual documents and website content, coordinate data reporting and analytics, and act as the Service Owner for the XTM translation management platform. The consultant will ensure that content, metadata, reporting information and linguistic assets are accurate, accessible and maintained through effective digital workflows. The role requires a unique combination of information and content management, translation technology, service management, data analysis, requirements management, vendor coordination and change-management skills.
 Accountabilities
 Document, Content, Data Reporting and Analytics
 ·    Coordinate the classification, quality control, publication, updating and archiving of multilingual documents and website content in the Content and Document Management platforms, applying approved taxonomy and metadata standards.
 ·    Analyse publication requests; maintain agenda items, document relationships and language versions; provide editorial guidance, training and support to content owners.
 ·    Monitor website content, usage and service data; coordinate reporting requirements, indicator definitions, data collection and validation, recurring reports and dashboards.
 ·    Identify improvements to information architecture, search, accessibility, publishing and reporting workflows, including opportunities for appropriate automation.
 ·    Maintain procedures, data definitions, guidance and training materials, and coordinate functional testing and user support.

 ·    Strong analytical, organizational, writing, communication, client-service, and problem-solving skills.

 Fluency (level C) in English. Intermediate knowledge (level B) of a second official UN language is required.

 ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT 
 This selection process will be used to fill the Investigation Officer positions in both the Investigations team and the Intake team.
 The Intake and Case Development Team receives and assesses complaints and referrals, conducts preliminary reviews, and prioritises matters to determine the most appropriate way forward, including investigation, closure or referral to another appropriate office or entity.

 Provide assistance to investigations, when possible and appropriate. 
 Accountabilities for positions in the investigations team  
 Efficiently plan and conduct office and field-based investigations into allegations of misconduct and wrongdoing, in accordance with applicable OIGI and WFP frameworks.  Fact-finding activities include engaging with investigative participants, collecting relevant records information and documentation, conducting interviews, and undertaking field missions.  
 Prepare clear, concise, and well-reasoned written outputs pertaining to assigned matters. Based on comprehensive evidence analysis and presentation, draw sound factual conclusions and formulate recommendations for corrective measures and/or referrals, in line with OIGI’s mandate. 
 Common accountabilities for positions in the intake and investigations teams  
 Effectively manage assigned workload within established timeframes and priorities, adjusting investigative strategies as necessary, and regularly consulting with supervisors and relevant OIGI colleagues, keeping them informed of progress.   
 Effectively engage with Global HQ, country or other offices, local officials, governments, and external organizations for support, to collect information, and/or otherwise facilitate fact-finding activities.

 Excellent analytical skills.
 Experience working as part of a multi-cultural team.

 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 Türkiye is exposed to frequent natural shocks, notably major earthquakes, floods, and wildfires. The February 2023 earthquakes, affecting 14 million people, were a reminder of the potential destructive impact of disasters in the country. Türkiye also faces humanitarian spillovers from the geopolitical instability in its immediate neighbourhood.
 In light of this risk environment, the World Food Programme (WFP) has placed Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) at the heart of its current Country Strategic Plan (2026-2028) for Türkiye. Preparedness is crucial for achieving faster, more effective, and more cost-efficient emergency responses. A key pillar of preparedness is logistics, enabling an ability to rapidly store, mobilise, and distribute assistance at scale.
 Beyond ensuring its own readiness for future emergencies, WFP Türkiye is supporting the Government of Türkiye and other national actors with logistics emergency preparedness. In 2027, the Country Office will launch and implement the Türkiye Readiness for Emergency Logistics project; an 18-month capacity strengthening project with the Ministry of Family and Social Services (MoFSS) to enhance its emergency warehousing, inventory management and distribution systems. MoFSS is the lead institution for in-kind warehousing and distribution under the Türkiye Disaster Response Plan (TAMP).
 With the launch planned for January 2027, the project will be implemented in six phases:
 Inception and Capacity Needs Assessment;
 Development of a joint Capacity Strengthening Plan;
 Strengthening of systems and operational capacity;
 Piloting in selected provinces or facilities;
 Simulation and validation;
 Institutionalisation. 
 The focus on logistics reflects WFP Türkiye’s longer-term direction. Türkiye is becoming an increasingly important logistics hub for WFP’s global operations, supported by a dedicated logistics team in Mersin. Strengthening national logistics preparedness complements this growing footprint, building the partnerships and capacities on which the transition will rest.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Under the supervision of the CO EPR Advisor, the Project Manager will lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of the Türkiye Readiness for Emergency Logistics project, in close collaboration with the LTC Emergency Preparedness team. The Project Manager will act as WFP’s project lead and main counterpart to MoFSS on the project, and will provide day-to-day guidance to the WFP Logistics Preparedness Officer on project activities. The Project Manager will also work closely with WFP’s logistics team in Mersin, ensuring that the project draws on WFP’s operational expertise in Türkiye and builds on existing national systems.
 The Project Manager will report to the Türkiye CO EPR Advisor, with a dotted technical reporting line to the LTC Field Based Preparedness Programme Lead to ensure alignment with the LTC strategy and methodology. Working days will be agreed with the EPR Advisor in line with the project workplan.
 Project management and coordination: 
 Lead the overall planning and implementation of the project, including creating and updating the workplan, milestones, critical path, timeline and budget, applying LTC methodology and respecting WFP rules and procedures.
 Act as WFP’s main counterpart to MoFSS on the project, representing WFP in meetings with senior officials and ensuring that activities respond to MoFSS priorities.
 Coordinate the inputs of LTC specialists, including the planning of their missions and in-country programmes.
 Provide day-to-day guidance to the Logistics Preparedness Officer on project activities.
 Lead regular focal point meetings and periodic consultations with MoFSS, ensuring that milestones, decisions and agreed actions are documented and followed up.
 Identify and manage project risks, escalating issues to the CO EPR Advisor and LTC FBPP Lead as needed.
 Technical leadership across the project phases: 
 Working in close collaboration with the LTC, the Project Manager is accountable to:
 Assure the effective use of the LTC FBPP Methodology and application of the respective tools.
 Lead the inception phase, including the inception workshop and agreement with MoFSS on priorities, roadmap and implementation arrangements and draft the Project Plan.
 Lead the Capacity Needs Assessment, including consultations with MoFSS departments, review of policies, procedures and systems, visits to MoFSS facilities, and the drafting of the assessment report and recommendations.
 Lead the development of the joint Project Plan for Capacity Strengthening with MoFSS, setting out priority actions, responsibilities, milestones and timelines
 Oversee all capacity strengthening activities in areas such as warehousing and inventory management (including warehouse management systems), distribution planning, surge capacity and coordination, sustainability, customs, digitalization, and the development or adaptation of SOPs, tools and training materials.
 Contribute to technical trainings, workshops and on-the-job coaching for MoFSS personnel.
 Lead the design, monitoring and documentation of pilot activities in selected provinces or facilities.

 Support MoFSS efforts to strengthen coordination among national actors involved in humanitarian logistics, including operationalising the TAMP In-Kind Warehousing and Distribution Group.

 PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 The WAE Content Collector will provide rapid, high-quality photography and/or videography for fundraising and communications needs in Gaza, Palestine. They will be engaged for campaign-specific requests and priority content assignments.

 ABOUT LOGISTICS OFFICER P3 – GLOBAL COMMODITY TRACKING INFORMATION ANALYTICS AT WFP 
The position is located in the Supply Chain and Delivery Division (SCD) at Headquarters (Rome), within the Global Commodity Tracking and Fund Management Unit.
 The unit provides global oversight and technical support for commodity tracking, FTC processes, and digital supply chain solutions across more than 80 Country Offices. It ensures system adoption, operational consistency, and alignment through structured knowledge management, communication, and capacity development initiatives.
 THE ROLE 
 The Logistics Officer (P3) is responsible for global coordination, governance, and delivery of Commodity knowledge management and capacity development frameworks supporting commodity tracking, FTC processes, and digital supply chain systems.
 The role ensures that corporate knowledge, training materials, and communication products are standardized, accessible, and effectively deployed, enabling consistent system adoption, knowledge retention, and operational performance across all regions.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority):
Commodity and FTC Data Analytics and Business Intelligence 
 Collect, consolidate, and analyses commodity management data from corporate systems and digital platforms.
 Develop analytical models to monitor commodity movements, stock balances, losses, diversions, near-expiry risks, and operational performance.
 Produce regular analytical reports, executive dashboards, and management briefings.
 Support data-driven decision-making through trend analysis and forecasting.
 Dashboard and Reporting Development 
 Design and maintain Power BI, DOTS, and other business intelligence dashboards.
 Develop automated reporting solutions to reduce manual reporting efforts.
 Create KPI monitoring tools aligned with corporate Supply Chain performance indicators.
 Support Regional Office and Country Offices in interpreting performance data and dashboards.
 Commodity Assurance and Compliance Analytics 
 Monitor compliance with commodity management guidelines and assurance requirements.
 Develop analytical tools to support commodity assurance reviews and remote monitoring activities.
 Identify anomalies, risks, and control weaknesses through data analytics.
 Support audit reviews and management assurance reporting through evidence-based analysis.
 Data Quality and Governance 
 Conduct data validation exercises across corporate systems.
 Develop data quality monitoring frameworks and exception reports.
 Support master data management initiatives and standard operating procedures.
 Promote data governance standards and reporting consistency globally.
 Digital Solution Support 
 Support Track & Trace, CP Stock Management Solution, SCOPE In-Kind, Digital Stack Cards, and other digital transformation initiatives.
 Define business requirements for analytics and reporting functionalities.
 Collaborate with TEC and business stakeholders on system enhancements.
 Test and validate analytical outputs from newly developed solutions.
 Performance Monitoring and Oversight 
 Develop global monitoring frameworks for commodity tracking activities.
 Support implementation of remote monitoring and oversight initiatives.
 Monitor corrective actions arising from audits, reviews, and assurance activities.
 Produce risk-based analytical assessments for management review.
 Knowledge Management and Capacity Building 
 Develop user guides, training materials, and reporting manuals.
 Conduct webinars and training sessions for HQ, Regional Bureau, and Country Office staff.
 Promote a data-driven culture through continuous learning and knowledge sharing.
 Provide technical support and coaching on analytical tools and reporting methodologies.
 QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE 
 Education: 
 Advanced University degree in Transport Economics, Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Supply Chain, Knowledge Management, Business Management or other related field, or First University degree with additional years of related work experience and/or training/courses.
 Certificate in Logistics Management or Supply Chain Design from a recognized institution is required.
 Experience: 
 Minimum of five years of postgraduate (or equivalent per Education requirements) professional experience in Supply Chain, Logistics, preferably on inventory and supply chain budget management area or other related areas.

 Experience in Supply chain operation, commodity information management, training, or capacity development in operational environments

 Experience conducting training sessions and facilitating workshops
 Experience supporting global or multi-country operations

2 December 2026-23:59-GMT+01:00 Central European Time (Rome) ABOUT THE SCHOOL MEALS ACCELERATOR 
 School Meals Accelerator ( the Accelerator ) is the fifth and newest initiative under  the School Meals Coalition,  operating as an independent initiative while being hosted by the World Food Programme (WFP). It is designed to support governments to scale and strengthen their national school meal programmes and turn their ambitions into real impact. Acting as a network catalyst and convenor, the Accelerator mobilizes resources and expertise from the right partners to deliver strategic technical assistance where it matters most.   
 The Accelerator’s mission: unlock the full potential of national school meal programs by improving design, scaling investment, and fostering collaboration across education, health, and food systems. It embraces a systems-thinking approach, adapts to country priorities, and thrives in deep collaboration among global, regional, and local actors. The Accelerator’s ambition: to help low- and lower-middle-income countries reach an additional 100 million children by 2030, making school meals a cornerstone of human capital development and a global standard of care.  
 The Accelerator operates in conditions of high complexity. Because it operates as a network facilitator rather than a traditional organization, its work spans multiple countries, organisations and institutional logics, and seeks to support system-level change rather than the delivery of predefined solutions.  
For this reason, the Accelerator has adopted a systemic leadership approach, which accepts that pathways to change are non-linear, and progress depends on learning, adaptation and collaboration across boundaries. Working in this way places ongoing demands on those involved and requires leaders who are able to work productively with uncertainty, difference and incomplete authority while maintaining accountability for results. Joining the Accelerator team therefore means being part of a first-of-its-kind development enterprise: a systems-focused effort to drive lasting, country-led change that requires a willingness to learn, adapt and be shaped by the work as it evolves.

 ➡️ Duration: 12 months  (renewable)
 🇺🇦 The position is only open to Ukrainian nationals or residents of Ukraine, with a legal work permit. 
 What will you do in this position?   
 You will provide specialized procurement support to ensure timely, efficient, compliant, and value-for-money acquisition of goods and services in support of WFP Ukraine operations. The incumbent contributes to procurement planning, sourcing, tendering, contract management, reporting, and compliance while ensuring adherence to WFP procurement rules, regulations, and procedures.
 Why work with WFP Ukraine?  
 The war in Ukraine has had drastic consequences, both for people inside the country and for those around the world who depend on its food supplies. The war has caused immense suffering for civilians, displaced families, and disrupted supply chains and food production. It has caused one of the fastest forced population movements since the Second World War. Close to 6 million Ukrainians are still living as refugees across Europe, and almost 3.6 million are internally displaced. Many have lost their homes and livelihoods. As food production and supply lines are disrupted by fighting, many families in the east and south of Ukraine do not have reliable access to nutritious food.
 WFP uses a combination of food and cash assistance to support communities affected by the war. This includes working with local partners to distribute food boxes in areas near the frontline and providing cash transfers in locations where people have access to banks and markets to buy food. Since March 2022, WFP has distributed food and cash assistance equivalent to 3.7 billion meals to people displaced and affected by the war.

 ✅ Competitive salaries per job level
 ✅ Pension contribution added to net salary
 ✅ Medical insurance with the possibility to enroll eligible dependents

 CONTEXTO ORGANIZATIVO 
 Guatemala es un país de ingresos medios-altos con indicadores macroeconómicos estables y crecimiento económico sostenido. Sin embargo, persisten importantes desafíos relacionados con la pobreza, la desigualdad, la inseguridad alimentaria, la malnutrición y la limitada resiliencia de los medios de vida, especialmente entre las poblaciones rurales, indígenas y las mujeres. Asimismo, la alta exposición a fenómenos climáticos extremos y otros choques recurrentes continúa afectando la capacidad de los hogares y de los sistemas productivos para garantizar un acceso sostenible a alimentos nutritivos y saludables. 
 En este contexto, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA), en trabajo conjunto con el Gobierno, la sociedad civil, comunidades, academia y el sector privado, entre otros, impulsa sistemas alimentarios más sostenibles, resilientes e inclusivos. Mediante el Plan Estratégico de País (CSP) 2026–2030, promueve soluciones integradas que fortalecen las capacidades de los actores clave, mejoran el acceso a dietas saludables y mercados y fortalecen las acciones para la preparación, anticipación y respuesta ante emergencias en el país. 
 FINALIDAD DEL PUESTO 
 Bajo la supervisión correspondiente del jefe de Programas, la persona Asociada Senior será responsable de coordinar y dar seguimiento a las operaciones del PMA en el área asignada, asegurando la articulación de las intervenciones programáticas, socios, instituciones y actores territoriales. La posición tendrá un énfasis particular en la gestión territorial, los sistemas alimentarios, las cadenas de valor, el desarrollo de negocios y el relacionamiento con el sector privado local, promoviendo oportunidades de mercado y alianzas que contribuyan al fortalecimiento de los medios de vida y las economías locales. Asimismo, coordinará territorialmente actividades vinculadas a las operaciones de preparación, respuesta ante emergencias, acciones anticipatorias y recuperación temprana, fomento de la nutrición y seguridad alimentaria y nutricional y otras iniciativas que se implementen en el área, de acuerdo con los lineamientos técnicos y operativos del PMA. 
 RESPONSABILIDADES (no se incluyen todas, dentro de la autoridad delegada): 
 Contribuir a la elaboración de un número limitado de proyectos, planes y procesos, garantizando su alineación con las políticas y directrices generales del programa. 
 Proporcionar apoyo en la gestión de proyectos para programas y proyectos específicos y definidos, de pequeña a mediana escala y de naturaleza relativamente sencilla, garantizando un enfoque coordinado con programas más amplios y el cumplimiento de las normas y procedimientos del PMA. 
 Dar seguimiento a los sistemas de recopilación de datos y monitoreo, asegurando el cumplimiento de rigurosos estándares de calidad. 
 Investigar y analizar cuestiones relacionadas con políticas y operaciones, con el fin de apoyar a colegas de mayor nivel en el desarrollo de políticas, programas y actividades. 
 Contribuir a la preparación de informes precisos y oportunos sobre programas y actividades, que permitan una toma de decisiones informada y garanticen la coherencia de la información presentada a las partes interesadas. 
 Mantener coordinación con las contrapartes internas para garantizar una colaboración eficaz y dar seguimiento a los proyectos en curso. 
 Apoyar la identificación, desarrollo y gestión de posibles alianzas, promoviendo el trabajo colaborativo que contribuya a mejorar los paquetes de asistencia alimentaria. 
 Apoyar el fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal del PMA, socios y Gobierno nacional para prepararse y responder a las necesidades de asistencia alimentaria, por ejemplo, mediante apoyo en la gestión de proyectos relacionados con iniciativas de aprendizaje. 
 Proporcionar orientación al personal de apoyo, actuando como punto de referencia y brindando asistencia en análisis y consultas. 
 Realizar otras funciones que sean requeridas. 
 OTROS REQUERIMIENTOS ESPECÍFICOS 
 Liderar la coordinación territorial de las intervenciones del PMA, promoviendo la articulación entre programas, equipos, socios, instituciones públicas, sector privado, y otros actores relevantes, e identificando riesgos, oportunidades y necesidades de ajuste para contribuir al logro oportuno de los resultados previstos. 
 Liderar territorialmente las intervenciones de sistemas alimentarios, cadenas de valor e acceso a mercados (públicos y privados), integrando el fortalecimiento organizativo, productivo y empresarial, la resiliencia, nutrición, infraestructura, servicios financieros y empresariales, logística y acceso a mercados, y promoviendo modelos con potencial de réplica y escalamiento. 
 Promover el fortalecimiento y la inclusión económica de organizaciones productivas, facilitando su vinculación sostenible con cadenas de valor, oportunidades de negocio y mercados públicos, institucionales y privados, así como con compradores, servicios financieros, empresariales, tecnológicos, logísticos y de calidad.

Identificar oportunidades de colaboración e inversión y representar al PMA, dentro de la autoridad delegada, en espacios técnicos y de coordinación territorial.

 Job Title: Programme Policy Officer - School Meals
 Contract Type : International Consultant
 Level : Level II
 Duration : 11-months
 Duty Station : Kinshasa, DRC
 ORGANISATIONAL CONTEXT 
 The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world’s largest humanitarian organisation, saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build pathways to peace, stability and prosperity. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, WFP supports government efforts to address food insecurity and malnutrition while strengthening national systems for education, social protection, resilience and food systems.
 School meals contribute to school enrolment, attendance, retention, learning, nutrition and protection. They also provide a platform for supporting smallholder farmers and local economies. In line with the Government’s commitments under the School Meals Coalition, WFP provides policy advice, technical assistance, operational support, evidence generation, capacity strengthening and resource mobilisation to advance a sustainable, nationally owned school meals programme.
 JOB PURPOSE 
 To lead the strategic development, technical oversight and operational management of WFP’s school meals portfolio in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while supporting the Government to design, finance, implement and monitor sustainable and nationally owned school meals programmes. The position is based in Kinshasa, DRC and reports to the Head of Resilience.
 The position will connect field operations, and the Country Office; strengthen collaboration with government and partners; and ensure that school meals contribute to education, nutrition, social protection, resilience, gender equality and food systems transformation.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES 
 Strategic leadership and policy suppor t
 Serve as the Country Office technical lead and principal focal point for school meals.
 Provide strategic and technical advice to management, field teams, government counterparts and cooperating partners.
 Review relevant strategies, policy documents, evaluations and evidence on school meals in the DRC and the region.
 Identify priority areas for WFP support and help operationalise the National School Feeding Strategy and School Meals Coalition commitments.
 Ensure alignment with the WFP Country Strategic Plan, WFP policies and relevant national education, nutrition, agriculture and social protection frameworks.
 Programme design and operational managemen t
 Lead programme design, planning, implementation, monitoring and periodic review, including targeting, beneficiary planning, food and non-food requirements, budgets, delivery arrangements and risk management.
 Design and operationalise Home-Grown School Feeding (HGSF) models linking school meal demand with smallholder production, aggregation and local procurement, ensuring reliable supplies of safe, nutritious and diversified food.
 Ensure interventions are evidence-based, conflict-sensitive, gender-responsive, nutrition-sensitive, inclusive and adapted to local contexts.
 Provide technical guidance to Field and Area Offices and cooperating partners, monitor performance against plans and budgets, and initiate corrective actions where required. 
 Undertake field missions to assess programme quality, support implementation and engage schools, communities and government authorities.
 Government capacity strengthenin g
 Assess national and subnational capacities and develop a practical capacity-strengthening plan.
 Provide technical assistance on policy, planning, costing, budgeting, local procurement, food safety, canteen management, monitoring, community participation and accountability.
 Support the development of national standards, operational guidance, tools and training materials.
 Promote a realistic transition pathway towards increased government ownership, implementation and domestic financing.
 Programme integration 
 Integrate school meals with nutrition, resilience, social protection, food systems, climate adaptation, gender, protection and disability inclusion.
 Promote Home-Grown School Feeding (HGSF) models that connect schools with smallholder farmers, producer organisations, local processors and markets.
 Collaborate with technical units and government counterparts to promote safe, nutritious, diversified, culturally appropriate and locally sourced meals.
 Strengthen links with national social protection systems and ensure the needs of girls, displaced children, children with disabilities and other vulnerable groups are addressed.
 Coordination and partnerships 
 Maintain effective coordination among WFP Field and Area Offices, the Country Office, Regional Bureau and Headquarters.
 Coordinate with Programme, Nutrition, Research, Assessment and Monitoring, Supply Chain, Procurement, Partnerships, Budget and Programming, Finance, Communications, Gender, Protection and Inclusion, and Technology teams.
 Maintain strategic dialogue with the Ministry responsible for education and other relevant institutions, and clarify the role expected of WFP.
 Reinforce collaboration with UNICEF, FAO, the World Bank, INPTA, United Nations agencies, donors, civil society, producer organisations, research institutions and the private sector.
 Support a government-led coordination mechanism and promote harmonised standards, tools, indicators and reporting arrangements.

 ABOUT PROGRAMME AND POLICY AT WFP 
 Pakistan faces a significant burden of maternal and child malnutrition. Stunting, wasting, anaemia and micronutrient deficiencies remain widespread, and are compounded by poverty, food insecurity, limited uptake of health services, inadequate maternal and young child feeding practices, and recurrent climate and economic shocks. The first 1,000 days, from conception to a child's second birthday, are therefore a critical window for preventing irreversible growth and development deficits.
 In 2020, the Government of Pakistan, through the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), launched the Benazir Nashonuma Programme (BNP) with support from the World Food Programme (WFP), UNICEF and WHO. BNP is Pakistan's flagship nutrition-sensitive social protection programme and combines conditional cash transfers with specialised nutritious foods, maternal and child health services, social and behaviour change support, growth monitoring, immunisation promotion, and prevention and management of acute malnutrition for pregnant and breastfeeding women and children under two.
 Since its launch, BNP has evolved from a pilot into a national delivery platform. By June 2026, the programme operated through more than 560 Facilitation Centres and had enrolled over 4.7 million pregnant women and children under two. Independent endline evidence confirms that the integrated BNP model can deliver measurable impact at scale, including substantial reductions in stunting, improved birth outcomes, and increased full immunisation coverage. These results support continuation of the combined cash, nutrition, health and counselling package, while programme learning highlights the need for earlier enrolment in pregnancy, stronger compliance and follow-up, improved coordination with provincial health systems, enhanced data interoperability, and sustained quality and accountability across the Facilitation Centre network.
 The third phase of BNP, started in July 2026 for three years, is designed to consolidate these gains and expand services, including to the whole of Pakistan. The new phase places greater emphasis on data-driven and digitised service delivery, Facilitation Centre optimisation, supply-chain efficiency and traceability, coordinated beneficiary identification and case management, stronger national and provincial coordination, integration with health and social protection systems, climate-responsive operations, value for money, and a phased transition toward stronger government ownership and long-term sustainability.
 As the programme evolves towards the next phase of implementation and scale, there is a need for dedicated project management leadership to strengthen governance, strategic oversight, performance management, risk management, stakeholder coordination, and delivery assurance across all BNP workstreams.

 The position is based in Islamabad and reports to Deputy Country Director.

 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:
 El Programa Mundial de Alimentos (WFP por sus siglas en inglés) es la organización humanitaria más grande del mundo, enfocada en salvar vidas durante emergencias y construir medios de vida sostenibles para las poblaciones más vulnerables. En Ecuador, WFP trabaja con el Gobierno Nacional, organismos internacionales, donantes, sector privado y organizaciones de la sociedad civil para fortalecer la seguridad alimentaria, la resiliencia climática, la protección social y la integración socioeconómica de poblaciones vulnerables.
 En el actual contexto de transición y reconfiguración de las prioridades gubernamentales, resulta fundamental que WFP fortalezca su capacidad de análisis político y relacionamiento institucional con las nuevas autoridades del Gobierno del Ecuador. Considerando que el Estado y sus Ministerios son los principales aliados para el cumplimiento de los objetivos de WFP en el país, es indispensable contar con una asesoría especializada que permita comprender oportunamente las dinámicas de toma de decisiones, las prioridades de las nuevas autoridades y los espacios de influencia relevantes para el posicionamiento de la agenda institucional.
 Esta posición permitirá identificar oportunidades de articulación con actores clave del Ejecutivo y otras instancias gubernamentales, facilitando un acercamiento más efectivo y alineado con las prioridades nacionales. Esto contribuirá a fortalecer el diálogo estratégico con el Gobierno, promoviendo una mejor comprensión del valor agregado de WFP y favoreciendo la construcción de relaciones de confianza que respalden la implementación de programas y proyectos orientados a la seguridad alimentaria, la nutrición y la resiliencia de las poblaciones más vulnerables.
 Asimismo, resulta especialmente relevante contar con este acompañamiento especializado para participar de manera estratégica en los espacios de consulta y diálogo relacionados con la formulación del nuevo Plan Estratégico de País (CSP). Una lectura adecuada del entorno político e institucional permitirá a WFP posicionar de forma efectiva sus prioridades programáticas, identificar puntos de convergencia con las políticas públicas nacionales y asegurar una participación más influyente en los procesos de planificación y coordinación con las entidades gubernamentales competentes.
 Finalmente, esta posición contribuirá a generar estrategias de relacionamiento de alto nivel que faciliten el impulso de nuevas iniciativas y proyectos conjuntos con el Gobierno. Un conocimiento actualizado de las estructuras institucionales, de los liderazgos emergentes y de las prioridades de la nueva administración permitirá anticipar oportunidades de colaboración, fortalecer mecanismos de coordinación interinstitucional y consolidar a WFP como un socio estratégico para el logro de los objetivos nacionales de desarrollo y atención a las poblaciones en situación de mayor vulnerabilidad.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
 1.Monitorear y analizar de manera permanente el entorno político, institucional y normativo del Ecuador, identificando tendencias, oportunidades y riesgos que puedan impactar la implementación de la estrategia y programas de WFP.
 2.Brindar asesoría estratégica a la Representación de WFP sobre las prioridades, agendas y dinámicas de relacionamiento con las nuevas autoridades del Gobierno Nacional, ministerios, secretarías y otras entidades públicas.
 3 Mapear y mantener actualizado el análisis de actores clave del sector público, identificando tomadores de decisión, liderazgos emergentes y espacios de influencia relevantes para el posicionamiento institucional de WFP.
 4.Diseñar e implementar estrategias de relacionamiento institucional de alto nivel que fortalezcan la colaboración y articulación entre WFP y las entidades gubernamentales prioritarias.
 5.Facilitar el diálogo estratégico y la coordinación con ministerios, autoridades nacionales y gobiernos subnacionales, promoviendo el alineamiento de las iniciativas de WFP con las prioridades del Gobierno del Ecuador.
 6.Asesorar la participación de WFP en espacios de consulta, concertación y diálogo interinstitucional, contribuyendo al posicionamiento de las prioridades programáticas de la organización en la formulación del nuevo Plan Estratégico de País (CSP).
 7.Liderar procesos de consulta y articulación con actores clave para la formulación del Country Strategic Plan (CSP).
 8.Impulsar alianzas estratégicas que permitan formular un plan de movilización de recursos para apoyar la implementación del CSP.
 9.Preparar análisis de coyuntura, informes ejecutivos, notas estratégicas y recomendaciones para la alta dirección, apoyando la toma de decisiones y la planificación institucional.
 10.Identificar oportunidades para el desarrollo de proyectos, alianzas e iniciativas conjuntas con entidades gubernamentales, promoviendo la movilización de apoyo político e institucional para los objetivos de WFP.
 11.Apoyar la gestión de reuniones y acercamientos de alto nivel con autoridades gubernamentales, elaborando mensajes clave, líneas argumentales, documentos de posición y materiales de apoyo para la Representación.
 12.Contribuir al fortalecimiento de la visibilidad y posicionamiento estratégico de WFP ante el Gobierno, promoviendo una comprensión clara del valor agregado de la organización en materia de seguridad alimentaria, nutrición, protección social, resiliencia climática e integración socioeconómica.

 To provide technical expertise and support the implementation and continuous improvement of Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) processes, systems, and tools that strengthen supplier performance, compliance, data management, and procurement outcomes.

Organize and manage the Vendor Management Committee (VMC), including preparation of agenda items, supporting documentation, recommendations, and follow-up actions.  2. Systems Management and Data Administration: Manage and maintain supplier management systems, databases, and platforms to support supplier lifecycle management processes. Oversee supplier data quality and integrity through data validation, cleansing, categorization, and continuous improvement activities. Develop and enhance supplier management tools, dashboards, workflows, and reporting mechanisms to support operational effectiveness and data-driven decision-making.
 3. Supplier Intelligence and Market Analysis: Conduct supplier mapping, market research, and supplier intelligence activities to identify opportunities for supplier expansion, diversification, and improved supplier engagement. Analyze supplier trends and market developments and provide recommendations to strengthen supplier management practices and support procurement objectives.
 4. Supplier Performance, Risk and Excellence Management: Monitor supplier performance and prepare supplier evaluation reports in collaboration with procurement and supply chain teams. Maintain supplier performance monitoring tools and support performance improvement initiatives. Maintain a log of supplier-related risks and monitor identified risks to support mitigation measures and minimize operational and financial impact. Participate in reconciliatory exercises and resolution processes related to supplier performance issues.
 5. Compliance, Due Diligence and Governance: Support supplier due diligence, supplier qualification, and supplier governance processes in accordance with organizational policies and procedures. Act as focal point for supplier sanction-related matters, including reviewing UNGM supplier sanctions information, assessing implications, coordinating communications, and monitoring required actions. Ensure supplier records, documentation, and management processes support compliance, transparency, audit readiness, and effective governance.
 6. Reporting and Stakeholder Engagement: Develop and maintain supplier management reports, dashboards, statistics, and analytical summaries. Provide technical advice and supplier management information to procurement staff, business units, and other stakeholders. Work closely with procurement, programme, logistics, finance, and other relevant stakeholders to support supplier onboarding, performance monitoring, supplier management initiatives, and continuous improvement activities.
 7. Capacity Building and Process Improvement: Develop supplier onboarding guidelines, procedures, user manuals, and training materials. Deliver training and awareness sessions on supplier management processes, systems, and tools to relevant stakeholders. Support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of SRM processes, systems, modules, tools, and platforms across the Organization.
 8. Supplier Communication and Collaboration: Manage supplier communications through established supplier management channels, ensuring timely, accurate, and consistent responses to supplier inquiries and appropriate escalation of issues when required. Conduct ad hoc research and support the preparation of analyses, reports, and documents to facilitate supplier engagement and informed decision-making.
 9. Other Duties and Responsibilities: Act as focal point for WINGS-related matters within the assigned area of responsibility. Perform other related duties as required and assigned by the supervisor in support of SRM, procurement, and organizational objectives.

 You will ensure receipt/dispatch and verification of commodities in warehouse, mitigate losses, and ensure implementation of the best storage management practices and compliance with WFP warehouse guidelines and standards.

 Implement appropriate measures to safeguard food and non-food commodities, to ensure quality control using standard preventive measures in line with WFP established procedures.
 Monitor condition of the warehouse and commodities and take appropriate actions, to support efficient warehouse space-planning and well-organized commodity storage following WFP warehouse standards. 
 Provide supervision, guidance and on-the-job training to warehouse staff supporting their development and high performance. 
 Perform other related tasks.

 Experience using logistics databases to monitor ongoing shipments, pipeline information, insurance claims, and food stock.  
 Experience analysing data (on commodities, funds, etc.) and drafting reports. 
 Experience in measuring service providers’ performance against set KPIs.  
 Experience in assisting the preparation of contract documentation.  
 Experience in providing technical business support in corporate systems.

 Data Analytics

 Good excel and Microsoft system knowledge.
