 The London Office plays a key role in fostering strategic partnerships and engaging UK stakeholders, including government, parliament, media, private sector, academia, civil society and the public. 
 What we do:
 •              Public and Private Sector Partnerships: We engage with the UK Government, particularly the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, as well as corporate partners and foundations. 
 •              External Relations: We engage with a range of institutions, including international NGOs, humanitarian think-tanks and parliament.

 •              Provide support in managing relationships with UK-based partners. 
 •              Support with research and information-gathering in response to UK donor queries. 
 •              Assist in preparing documents, including correspondence, funding materials and statistics, for the Partnerships Officer and the Director of WFP’s London Office. 
 •              Assist in the organization of meetings, events, senior-level visits to the UK and field trips with UK partners. 
 •              Provide UK-specific information in preparation for Executive Board and other meetings. 
 •              Follow closely political developments in the UK, assess their impact on WFP, and alert the team accordingly. 
 •              Assist in monitoring and conducting analysis of significant development and humanitarian policy themes in the UK that are relevant to the strategic partnership with WFP (e.g. nutrition, climate change, school feeding etc.) 
 •              Assist in exploring opportunities under the UK’s International Climate Finance portfolio and during the UK’s G20 Presidency in 2027. 
 •              Participate in all aspects of team activities, including weekly and strategic meetings. 
 •              Perform other duties as required. 
 In addition, the Partnerships Intern may also be required to: 
 •              Monitor parliamentary debates, parliamentary questions tabled and wider political developments relevant to WFP priorities.
 •              Support the drafting of briefing materials, stakeholder engagement notes and parliamentary outreach activities as required.
 •              Attend relevant parliamentary, NGO, think tank and sector events to strengthen stakeholder engagement and identify advocacy opportunities.

 Be currently enrolled in a graduate programme (Master’s degree); OR

 Have attended classes in the last 12 months of enrolment in a recognized university.
 Academic background in: Political Science, International Development, Development Economics or another relevant field;
 Excellent written and spoken English is required (proficiency/level C). Working knowledge of another official UN language (French, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, Russian plus Portuguese) is an asset;

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills;

 Team spirit, good organizations and interpersonal skills, able to work independently, and eager to learn about humanitarian assistance and development cooperation;  
 Knowledge of UK politics, foreign and development policy would be an advantage.

With the support of a comprehensive induction package, the Intern will rapidly become a productive member of the team.

 At the end of the assignment, the Intern should have a greater understanding of WFP’s work and its role within the wider humanitarian system.

Approximately 5.5 million people remain internally displaced. Since December 2024, more than 1.6 million Syrians have returned from abroad, many to communities where homes and infrastructure have been destroyed, livelihood opportunities remain limited and access to basic services is severely constrained. Sustained support is essential to help returning families meet their immediate needs, rebuild their livelihoods and reintegrate into their communities.

WFP’s interventions prioritize emergency relief and resilience-building efforts focused on the most severely food insecure populations. Additionally, WFP is a key actor in the country’s social protection sector also plays a vital role in strengthening Syria’s social safety-net systems.

 Support in the periodic monitoring of the response against the FSC response plans, strategy and logframe.
 Develop and maintain a database of FSC partners’ activities. Ensure accurate data processing, including data cleaning and a beneficiary counting system, and ensure that data are collected and presented consistently with FSC objectives.
 Proactively engage with FSC partners to support accurate and timely reporting, monitoring and information management processes, as required.
 Analyse and process collected data, and produce information products, including dashboards, maps, situation reports, bulletins, newsletters, presentations for partner meetings and donor briefings. Disseminate these products through appropriate communication channels.
 Ensure compliance with information-sharing protocols and data responsibility standards in the collection, analysis, storage, and dissemination of information (e.g. ICCG’s ISP).
 Maintain and regularly update the FSC funding tracking system to ensure up-to-date and reliable information on funding for food security activities (complementing FTS data where needed).
 Conduct secondary data review and compile an inventory of available assessments and relevant information sources. As appropriate, provide GSU and Cluster Leads, and FSC partners where applicable a list of available information/data with respective sources on a regular basis (e.g. common Cluster / Sector data sets, including population data disaggregated by age and sex, assessments and other surveys such as EFSA /CFSAM/SMART, IPC);
 Create and maintain Contact directories and mailing lists;
 Maintain and regularly update the FSC country webpage on the global Food Security Cluster website and the FSC Humanitarian Response webpages with all relevant material.
 Conduct capacity building for FSC partners on Information Management (e.g. on monitoring / reporting formats, project submission, ActivityInfo and excel use);
 Assist in organizing FSC meetings and working groups (if applicable);
 Together with the FSC Coordinator, support global Food Security Cluster (gFSC) initiatives, including Cluster Coordination Performance Monitoring (CCPM), the global cluster annual overview and global dashboards.
 Liaise with OCHA and IM Focal Points in other clusters, and attend IM Working Group meetings or other relevant WG meetings – share information as appropriate;
 Any other IM related FSC tasks, as required.

 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 Türkiye is exposed to frequent natural shocks, notably major earthquakes, floods, and wildfires. The February 2023 earthquakes, affecting 14 million people, were a reminder of the potential destructive impact of disasters in the country. Türkiye also faces humanitarian spillovers from the geopolitical instability in its immediate neighbourhood.
 In light of this risk environment, the World Food Programme (WFP) has placed Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) at the heart of its current Country Strategic Plan (2026-2028) for Türkiye. Preparedness is crucial for achieving faster, more effective, and more cost-efficient emergency responses. A key pillar of preparedness is logistics, enabling an ability to rapidly store, mobilise, and distribute assistance at scale.
 Beyond ensuring its own readiness for future emergencies, WFP Türkiye is supporting the Government of Türkiye and other national actors with logistics emergency preparedness. In 2027, the Country Office will launch and implement two mutually reinforcing projects in logistics preparedness with national counterparts, in close collaboration with the WFP-led Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC).
 Workstream: Logistics Response Training (LRT)
 Partner: Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency (AFAD)
 Scope: A multi-day operational simulation delivered jointly with AFAD, in which 20–25 participants from national and regional organisations are placed in a simulated emergency and work through realistic logistics constraints and bottlenecks. Planned for April 2027.
 Workstream: Türkiye Readiness for Emergency Logistics
 Partner: Ministry of Family and Social Services (MoFSS)
 Scope: An 18-month capacity strengthening project to enhance MoFSS’s emergency warehousing, inventory management and distribution systems. MoFSS is the lead institution for in-kind warehousing and distribution under the Türkiye Disaster Response Plan (TAMP). Launch planned for January 2027.
 The focus on logistics also reflects WFP Türkiye’s longer-term direction. Türkiye is becoming an increasingly important logistics hub for WFP’s global operations, supported by a dedicated logistics team in Mersin. Looking beyond the current CSP, the Country Office is planning to transition towards a Türkiye Strategic Food Hub from 2028. Strengthening national logistics preparedness complements this growing footprint, building the partnerships and capacities on which the transition will rest.
 ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Under the supervision of the EPR Advisor, the Logistics Preparedness Officer will support the planning, coordination, implementation, and reporting of the Country Office’s logistics preparedness workstreams. For the LRT, the Officer will act as the Country Office’s operational focal point, working closely with the LTC Community Development and Capacity Building team. For the MoFSS project, the Officer will provide support to the WFP project lead and LTC specialists from the Emergency Preparedness team. Across both, the Officer will work closely with WFP’s logistics team in Mersin to ensure that activities are delivered in an integrated manner, build on existing national systems and contribute to sustainable, nationally owned capacity.
 The Logistics Preparedness Officer will report to the Türkiye CO EPR Advisor. The Officer may have dotted technical reporting lines to the LTC for the two projects, to ensure regular information sharing and alignment with LTC strategy.
 In addition to the Türkiye CO workstreams, the Officer may be called upon by the LTC Community Development and Capacity Building team to support with the delivery of simulations and trainings in other countries. The scope and frequency of this support will be agreed between Türkiye CO and the LTC in a manner that ensures value for both and without compromising delivery of CO priorities.

 Acting as the Country Office’s operational focal point for the LRT, the Officer will:
 Work with the LTC and AFAD on the planning and delivery of the exercise, including maintaining the workplan, timeline, and budget tracker in line with WFP rules and procedures.
 Follow up on the outcomes of the LTC scoping visit, support any further preparatory missions and trainings for AFAD staff, and support the adaptation of the LRT scenario and materials.
 Coordinate site arrangements with AFAD, including accommodation, meeting space, outdoor setting, access to logistics assets, and safety, security and medical cover, and support the procurement of related services.
 Support the participant call for applications and selection process with AFAD and LTC, manage communications with selected participants, and support the identification of facilitators.
 Provide on-site logistical and administrative support throughout the exercise, acting as the day-to-day liaison between the facilitation team and AFAD.
 Support the post-exercise evaluation and exercise report, track agreed follow-up actions with AFAD, and capture lessons relevant to the simulation phase of the MoFSS project.
 Support communications and visibility around the exercise, in coordination with AFAD.

 CONTEXT ORGANIZATIONNEL 
 Ce poste est rattaché au Bureau pays (CO) du Tchad et rent compte à un responsable des Finances.
 Dans un Bureau pays, le/la titulaire du poste travaille au sein d’une équipe chargée des finances et fournit un appui financier général. 
 Selon la taille et les besoins du bureau ou de l’unité, le poste peut couvrir l’ensemble des aspects liés aux finances, au budget et à l’administration, ou mettre davantage l’accent sur les finances ou sur certains de ces domaines.
 À ce niveau, le/la titulaire du poste travaille généralement sous la supervision d’un membre du personnel plus expérimenté, qui lui fournit des orientations ainsi qu’un retour régulier sur le travail accompli.
 Il/elle contribue à la collecte, à la mise à jour, à l’analyse et à l’établissement de rapports sur les informations financières, afin d’optimiser l’efficacité des services financiers.
 OBJECTIF DU POSTE 
 Contribuer à la gestion responsable des ressources du PAM, notamment à travers le suivi des budgets, l’établissement de prévisions, la production de rapports sur les données clés, ainsi que la fourniture de services administratifs de base et d’un appui en matière de ressources humaines.
 Ces activités visent à assurer une gestion efficace des fonds et à garantir que l’assistance apportée aux bénéficiaires soit mise en œuvre de la manière la plus efficiente et efficace possible.
 PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS  
 A. Planification et gestion budgétaires - CSP, Prestation des services logistiques et Prestation des services à la demande. 
 1. Contribuer à l’élaboration et à la mise en œuvre des politiques et procédures relatives aux activités budgétaires et de programmation, au moyen d’un suivi étroit, afin d’assurer leur conformité avec les stratégies du PAM et celles du domaine fonctionnel.
 2. Contribuer à la compilation, à la préparation et à la révision des différents plans budgétaires, conformément aux procédures budgétaires et de programmation.
 3. Assurer le suivi des systèmes institutionnels du PAM en veillant à ce que toutes les pièces justificatives budgétaires soient exactes, correctement préparées et conformes aux recommandations, afin de permettre leur enregistrement exact dans les systèmes internes, et assurer le suivi des mesures liées à l’approbation des budgets.
 4. Participer aux activités de clôture des plans stratégiques de pays (CSP) et des plans fondés sur les ressources (RBP), et collaborer avec les unités dépensières pour repérer et clôturer les engagements en cours dans les délais requis, tout en signalant au supérieur hiérarchique tout problème potentiel.
 B. Gestion des fonds, gestion de la performance et rapports 
 5. Vérifier l’exactitude et suivre la programmation et l’utilisation des fonds dans les délais requis, en fonction des priorités opérationnelles, des propositions de financement et des conditions des donateurs, en formulant en temps voulu des recommandations et d’éventuelles mesures correctives permettant l’établissement de rapports en collaboration avec les unités dépensières.
 6. Effectuer et documenter les sous-allocations de fonds conformément aux procédures et directives en vigueur, afin de mettre les fonds à la disposition des unités dépensières pour leur engagement en temps voulu.

 UNIDAD: Programas

 CONTEXTO ORGANIZACIONAL: 
 La prevención de la explotación y el abuso sexuales (PEAS) por parte de trabajadores humanitarios y del desarrollo constituye un principio fundamental de las Naciones Unidas. La explotación y el abuso sexuales (EAS) por parte de estos actores contradicen directamente los principios y las políticas de la ONU y representan una falla en la protección por parte de la comunidad humanitaria y de desarrollo. La EAS causa daños a las personas que la comunidad humanitaria tiene la obligación de proteger y, asimismo, pone en riesgo la reputación de todas las entidades de las Naciones Unidas (ONU).
 La compleja situación en Colombia, derivada de la reconfiguración de los grupos armados no estatales en los territorios y de los flujos migratorios mixtos resultantes de la crisis de Venezuela, ha incrementado significativamente el número de actores humanitarios que trabajan con poblaciones de interés, contribuyendo, en consecuencia, a un mayor riesgo de explotación y abuso sexuales. Asimismo, un hallazgo recurrente de evaluaciones recientes indica la presencia generalizada de situaciones de explotación sexual, como el sexo transaccional y otros mecanismos negativos de afrontamiento, especialmente en las zonas fronterizas. Debido a la emergencia humanitaria, varios actores carecen de experiencia humanitaria previa consolidada y podrían no contar con políticas y procedimientos internos establecidos para la prevención y respuesta frente a la EAS.
 El Equipo de País de las Naciones Unidas (UNCT) en Colombia estableció el Task Force para la Prevención de la Explotación y el Abuso Sexuales (PEAS) en junio de 2018, con el objetivo principal de coordinar iniciativas interagenciales dirigidas a fortalecer la sensibilización y las capacidades de las Naciones Unidas, sus socios y diferentes organizaciones no gubernamentales, promoviendo una cultura de prevención y respuesta efectiva frente a la EAS. La PEAS constituye un tema transversal dentro de las estructuras del Equipo de País de las Naciones Unidas (UNCT), el Equipo Humanitario de País (HCT), el Fondo Multidonante de las Naciones Unidas para el Sostenimiento de la Paz (MPTF) y el Grupo Interagencial sobre Flujos Migratorios Mixtos (GIFMM).
 En este contexto, la reciente asignación de recursos desde del Fondo Humanitario Regional a Colombia representa una oportunidad para implementar las políticas y los planes interagenciales de PEAS. El fortalecimiento de la coordinación en el ámbito del taskforce de PSEA, la Red PEAS, incluida la reactivación de una función específica de coordinación facilitada por el Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) en apoyo a la Oficina de la Coordinadora Residente de la ONU (OCR), permitirá garantizar que los recursos sean aprovechados estratégicamente para fortalecer la rendición de cuentas, armonizar los esfuerzos entre los actores humanitarios y sostener una cultura de prevención y respuesta frente a la EAS. Esta inversión reafirma la importancia del compromiso institucional con la protección y salvaguarda de las poblaciones afectadas y con la consolidación de una acción colectiva frente a la explotación y el abuso sexuales.
 RESPONSABILIDADES PRINCIPALES (lista indicativa y no exhaustiva): 
 1. Coordinación interagencial, gobernanza y seguimiento 
 ·       Apoyar al liderazgo en el desarrollo e implementación de los Términos de Referencia (TDR) del Task Force de PEAS/PSEA y su plan de acción, con base en las prioridades identificadas.
 ·       Apoyar al liderazgo del Task Force de PEAS/PSEA en el fortalecimiento y promoción de la Red de PEAS/PSEA como mecanismo de coordinación técnica en esta materia, integrada por entidades de las Naciones Unidas, organizaciones internacionales, nacionales y locales, así como por la misión de las Naciones Unidas que opera en Colombia.
 ·       Participar y proporcionar insumos técnicos en espacios y reuniones globales para promover la PEAS/PSEA y asegurar una interacción permanente con instancias globales como OSCSEA, IASC, OVRA y DCO, entre otras.
 ·       Promover y formular recomendaciones para la implementación de medidas de prevención de la explotación y el abuso sexuales (EAS), mitigación de riesgos y respuesta, en los procesos de planificación y en el desarrollo de políticas y proyectos de los grupos interagenciales, incluidos los Grupos Interagenciales sobre Flujos Migratorios Mixtos (GIFMM) y los Equipos Locales de Coordinación (ELC).
 ·       Proporcionar insumos técnicos para el desarrollo de documentos estratégicos interagenciales, con el fin de incorporar actividades de PEAS/PSEA en proyectos y programas, así como contribuir a facilitar el acceso a recursos de financiación destinados a las acciones en esta materia.
 ·       Coordinar procesos de capacitación dirigidos a puntos focales y personal directivo, y proporcionar orientación técnica de acuerdo con las barreras, desafíos y avances identificados.
 ·       Apoyar la actualización, socialización y apropiación del SOP Interagencial y las rutas de remisión, en articulación con AAP/CFM, Protección, VBG y Protección de la Niñez.
 ·       Acompañar las herramientas interagenciales de análisis de riesgos y el seguimiento de medidas de mitigación en programas, proyectos y respuestas de emergencia.
 ·       Apoyar la evaluación y el fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales, consolidando información sobre diagnósticos, planes de mejora, réplicas y asistencia técnica.
 ·       Contribuir al análisis prospectivo y de sostenibilidad de los mecanismos interagenciales de reporte mediante evidencia agregada, consultas técnicas y formulación de escenarios.
 ·       Promover la integración de PEAS

 CONTEXTO ORGANIZACIONAL: 
 El Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) de las Naciones Unidas es el mayor organismo humanitario de lucha contra el hambre del mundo. En Colombia, el apoyo que PMA brinda al gobierno nacional responden a los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenibles (ODS) 2 y 17 haciendo uso de herramientas innovadoras tales como transferencias en dinero y compra local de alimentos a través de asociaciones de agricultores. Las actividades del PMA en Colombia se concentran en las poblaciones más vulnerables, que incluye víctimas de la violencia, comunidades marginadas y grupos étnicos. El objetivo es reconstruir y fortalecer sus fuentes de subsistencia, asegurando que tengan adecuado acceso en todo momento a dietas nutritivas y diversas e incrementando su capacidad para recuperarse y adaptarse a los cambios climáticos. Esto se hace de manera progresiva a través del desarrollo de las capacidades de autoridades locales para implementar programas responsables que contribuyan a reducir la inseguridad alimentaria y la malnutrición.
 La orientación estratégica y las actividades propuestas en la Estrategia de País responden a los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible (ODS) 2 y 17 ya los retos que actualmente enfrentan las poblaciones más vulnerables y los gobiernos locales en Colombia. La Estrategia de País contribuye a la construcción de paz, la reintegración y el mejoramiento de las medias de vida de las personas más vulnerables.
 En este contexto, el departamento de La Guajira, el Municipio de Maicao y el Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) han consolidado durante los últimos siete años una alianza de cooperación orientada a garantizar la implementación efectiva del Programa de Alimentación Escolar (PAE), asegurando la calidad, sostenibilidad y continuidad del servicio para miles de estudiantes. Este acompañamiento permitirá fortalecer la eficiencia operativa del programa y garantizar su adecuada puesta en marcha desde el inicio del calendario escolar.
 Bajo la supervisión del Asociado Senior de Programas y la orientación técnica de la Unidad de Nutrición de la Oficina Central, el Asistente Senior de Programas – Nutrición deberá liderar y brindar acompañamiento técnico especializado en los componentes de alimentación y nutrición, para la implementación del Programa de Alimentación Escolar (PAE) y demás proyectos desarrollados por la Oficina de Área de Riohacha.

 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 As Syria navigates a new chapter marked by historic opportunities and enduring challenges, the scale of humanitarian needs remains overwhelming. Today, more than 70 percent of Syria’s population continues to depend on some form of humanitarian assistance. Over half of the population is grappling with food insecurity, with nearly 3 million people facing severe food insecurity.  CONTEXTE NATIONAL/ CONTEXTE ORGANISATIONNEL : 
 Au Mali, le PAM fournit une assistance à plus d’un million de personnes en situation d’insécurité alimentaire, touchées par les conséquences des conflits et des catastrophes naturelles. Les activités d’intervention vont de l’assistance alimentaire d’urgence à l’alimentation scolaire, en passant par la prévention et le traitement de la malnutrition, le renforcement des actifs et les activités de soutien aux moyens de subsistance, ainsi que par des actions visant à renforcer les capacités des institutions.
 Le PAM fournit une assistance alimentaire d'urgence aux Maliens vulnérables, aux personnes déplacées et aux réfugiés. Cette assistance alimentaire d'urgence s'accompagne de mesures de prévention de la malnutrition et, si nécessaire, de traitements contre celle-ci. Le PAM apporte également une assistance à la prévention sociale en réponse aux crises et s'efforce de renforcer les capacités du gouvernement dans le domaine de la protection sociale.
 Les chocs climatiques récurrents, notamment les sécheresses et les inondations, aggravent cette situation déjà fragile et compromettent la sécurité alimentaire, les moyens de subsistance et les acquis en matière de développement à long terme. Le renforcement des capacités nationales à anticiper, à se préparer et à faire face à ces risques constitue une priorité essentielle pour le bureau de pays du PAM au Mali et ses homologues gouvernementaux.
 Le PAM au Mali met en œuvre l’« action anticipatoire » (AA) en tant que composante centrale de son programme de gestion des risques climatiques. Ce programme vise à aider le gouvernement à renforcer les systèmes d’alerte précoce, à traduire les prévisions en actions précoces et à établir des liens avec des financements préétablis afin de permettre des réponses opportunes et fondées sur la connaissance des risques.
 En étroite collaboration avec les institutions gouvernementales nationales et locales, ainsi qu’avec des partenaires humanitaires, de développement et scientifiques, le PAM soutient la mise en œuvre et l’intégration de l’AA dans les politiques, plans et systèmes nationaux. Cela inclut le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination, le développement des capacités techniques et la garantie que les informations d’alerte précoce déclenchent effectivement des actions anticipatives à grande échelle.
 Le PAM met en œuvre ses programmes en coordination avec les services techniques gouvernementaux et les ONG internationales et nationales. Ces partenaires ne sont pas seulement des partenaires d'exécution, mais aussi des partenaires stratégiques essentiels pour le PAM. La gestion de ces partenaires comprend non seulement la passation de marchés, les paiements et les contrôles ponctuels, mais aussi le renforcement des capacités.
 CONTEXTE ET OBJECTIF DE LA POSITON : 
 Le staff rendra compte directement au/à la responsable des politiques de programme chargé(e) des interventions de l’action anticipatoire et aussi va supporter les opérations de la prévention et traitement de la malnutrition.
 Le PAM cherche à recruter un expert en action anticipative (AA) possédant des compétences spécialisées en matière d’informations sur les risques climatiques et une expérience des systèmes d’alerte précoce, de l’AA et de la préparation aux catastrophes, pour soutenir les projets d’AA du PAM au Mali. Cet expert apportera son soutien aux activités du PAM liées à l’AA tout en fournissant un appui technique et opérationnel aux entités gouvernementales et en assurant la liaison avec les agences partenaires et les institutions scientifiques afin de renforcer la conception, la mise en œuvre et l’intensification de l’action anticipatoire dans le pays.
 Le personnel apportera également un soutien direct à l'équipe chargée de la nutrition, en mettant particulièrement l'accent sur la planification de la distribution, la gestion des fonds et la mise en œuvre. Cette personne contribuera également à la mise en œuvre de la stratégie nutritionnelle dans le cadre du nouveau plan stratégique national 2027-2031 et veillera à l'intégration de la nutrition dans l'ensemble des activités. Il s'agira également de veiller à ce que la nutrition soit intégrée dans le cadre de l'assistance à l'action anticipatoire.
 PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES: 
 Sous la supervision du responsable des opérations d’urgence, le chargé de mission chargé des politiques du programme d’action anticipative aura pour mission :
 Gestion des interventions d’action anticipatoire :
 De soutenir la mise en œuvre des activités d’action anticipatoire du PAM ;
 D’accompagner l’élaboration des plans nationaux d’action anticipatoire;
 D’accompagner l’élaboration de feuilles de route visant à intégrer l’action anticipatoire dans les cadres nationaux et infranationaux (politiques, plans, stratégies) ;
 Fournir des conseils techniques et opérationnels pour l’intégration de l’action anticipatoire au sein des programmes du PAM (par exemple, financement/assurance contre les risques climatiques, protection sociale, programmes de résilience) ainsi qu’au sein des structures gouvernementales chargées de la réduction des risques de catastrophe ;
 Avec le soutien de prestataires de services techniques, renforcer les capacités des homologues gouvernementaux, en particulier Mali Météo, le DNH et la DGPC, y compris le groupe de travail technique national sur l’adaptation aux aléas, qui siège au sein de la plateforme nationale de gestion des risques de catastrophe, afin de concevoir, mettre en œuvre et évaluer les systèmes d’adaptation aux aléas et d’alerte précoce ;
 Assurer la coordination avec les parties prenantes concernées par la gestion des risques de catastrophe et l’adaptation au changement climatique, notamment, mais sans s’y limiter, la FAO, le PNUD, le ministère de l’Agriculture, l’AGRHYMET, la Croix-Rouge et d’autres acteurs et projets liés à l’ada

 JOB TITLE: Programme & Policy Officer, CBT, IDM and Data Management
 TYPE OF CONTRACT: Regular Consultant Level 2 (CST II)

 DUTY STATION (City, Country): Bangui, Central African Republic
 DURATION: 11 months
 ABOUT WFP 
 The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world's largest humanitarian organization, saving lives in emergencies and changing lives through sustainable solutions. WFP increasingly leverages Cash-Based Transfers (CBT), digital beneficiary management systems, and data-driven approaches to deliver assistance efficiently, accountably and at scale.
 WFP is seeking a dynamic and results-oriented consultant to lead and strengthen Cash-Based Transfer operations, Identity Management (IDM), beneficiary data governance, and digital programme solutions. The selected candidate will contribute to enhancing operational excellence, accountability, government engagement, and beneficiary-centred service delivery.
 BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT: 
 The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world’s largest humanitarian organization. It saves lives in emergencies and uses food and cash assistance to change lives and empowers people to meet their essential needs. WFP supports countries in achieving Sustainable Development Goal 2 by responding to immediate food and nutrition needs while helping to establish systems and structures that address the root causes of hunger and strengthen development pathways for the most vulnerable. In fragile contexts, WFP programs also consider conflict dynamics and seek to contribute to peacebuilding outcomes where possible.
 The Central African Republic (CAR), a least-developed country, continues to be affected by prolonged conflict, socio-political instability, weak institutions, governance challenges and climate-related shocks. These factors have disrupted access to basic services, increased inequalities and left a significant proportion of the population in need of humanitarian assistance. Women, girls, young people, displaced populations and other marginalized groups remain particularly exposed to food insecurity, poverty and protection risks.
 To address these challenges, crisis response remains a priority under the CAR Country Strategic Plan (CSP 2023-2027). WFP supports the Government of CAR and the humanitarian community in providing food and essential assistance to vulnerable populations through general food distributions, nutrition interventions, school-based programs, resilience activities, Cash-Based Transfers (CBT), in-kind food assistance and capacity strengthening. WFP is committed to integrating protection, accountability, gender equality and community participation throughout the design and implementation of its programs.
 Cash assistance enables people to prioritize their own essential needs, including food, health care, rent and education. To ensure that cash programs are safe, effective and accountable, WFP must apply strong program design, assurance, risk management, identity management, transfer delivery, market analysis and reconciliation processes. This includes strengthening the Cash Assurance Framework, maintaining appropriate controls, monitoring operational and financial risks, and ensuring that assistance reaches the right people at the right time.
 At the same time, WFP CAR is expanding the digitalization of beneficiary management, transfer delivery and engagement systems to improve program efficiency, accountability and effectiveness. The Country Office is strengthening data management across its operations and with cooperating partners during implementation of the CSP. This requires reliable processes for beneficiary registration, verification, deduplication, data cleaning, data protection, analysis, visualization, reporting and maintenance in SCOPE and other corporate systems.
 Against this background, WFP CAR requires a Programme & Policy Officer, CBT, IDM and Data Management, to combine program oversight for cash operations with technical leadership in beneficiary data management and analysis.  Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programme, the incumbent will support the design, implementation and monitoring of CBT and in-kind operations; coordinate Identity Management (IDM) and SCOPE processes; oversee transfer delivery mechanisms, payment instruments and reconciliation; implement assurance and risk mitigation measures; and develop dashboards and the production of high-quality analyses and evidence to support operational and strategic decision-making.
 The incumbent will work closely with Programme, TEC, Finance, Supply Chain, Monitoring and Evaluation, field offices, cooperating partners and government counterparts. The position will also strengthen staff and partner capacities, promote compliance with WFP policies on privacy and personal data protection, identify operational anomalies, and support continuous improvement and innovation in cash, in-kind and digitally enabled assistance.
 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority): 
 Key Accountabilities 
 1. Cash Programme Planning and Implementation 
 Lead the design, implementation, scale-up and continuous improvement of Cash-Based Transfer (CBT) programmes in accordance with WFP corporate policies, Country Strategic Plan priorities and operational requirements.
 Contribute to the formulation and implementation of the Country Strategic Plan (CSP), ensuring effective integration of cash assistance modalities.
 Ensure CBT interventions are people-centred, gender-responsive, market-sensitive and aligned with beneficiary needs.
 Support emergency preparedness and response planning, including the integration of cash contingency measures and digital delivery mechanisms.
 Provide strategic advice to management on transfer modalities, delivery mechanisms

offres.titre: Global Roster - Child Protection Technical Advisor
offres.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.
 Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Please submit your Cover Letter and CV in English. 
 Please note: Our Global Technical Expertise Roster connects skilled professionals with opportunities to support humanitarian responses and long-term development programmes. Through the roster, we mobilise technical expertise to help protect lives, strengthen communities and contribute to sustainable recovery and development. 
 By applying to join the roster, you are expressing an interest in being considered for future positions, deployments or consultancy opportunities linked to humanitarian responses, development programmes and donor-funded initiatives. 
 Joining the roster does not constitute an offer of employment or guarantee an immediate opportunity. It means that your technical expertise may be considered, and you may be contacted when a suitable opportunity becomes available. 
 As this is not recruitment for a current vacancy, the review and selection process may take longer, particularly where there is no immediate opportunity linked to the roster advertisement.
 Here's where you come in: 
 The Child Protection Technical Advisor – Surge Roster provides short-term (1-29 days) child protection and Ending Violence against Children (EVAC) technical assistance, advisory support, capacity strengthening, and surge capacity for Field and Regional Offices operating in stable development contexts. 
 As a member of the Child Protection Surge Roster, you may be asked to provide technical support in person or virtually. Services provided can include, but is not limited to the following listed below under “Key Responsibilities:” 
 (Note: The requesting office will provide a detailed Terms of Reference outlining the specific technical support needed with objectives and main deliverables clearly stated). 
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 1. EVAC Strategy Design   
 Provide technical support to assess child protection/VAC risks, drivers of violence against children, and strengths and gaps within child protection systems, programmes, and services. Services may include:   
 Conducting child protection/VAC assessments, situation analyses, and landscape reviews.    
 Facilitating root cause analyses and identifying priority drivers of violence against children.    
 Mapping child protection systems, stakeholders, and service delivery mechanisms.    
 Undertaking baseline studies, capacity assessments, and contextual analyses.   
 Analyzing  programme data and evidence to inform programme design and improvement.    
 End Results 
 Improved EVAC strategies, programmes, and investments that are informed by high-quality evidence, contextual analysis, and a clear understanding of child protection system strengths, gaps, and priorities.
 2. Multi-Sectoral EVAC Programme Design and Adaptation  
 Provide technical expertise to support design, adaptation, and strengthening of EVAC programmes and interventions that address VAC. Services may include: 
 Developing or refining EVAC theories of change, technical approaches, and programme and indicator frameworks.  
 Designing EVAC projects, programmes, indicators and implementation plans.  
 Adapting evidence-based models and tools to local contexts.  
 Supporting integration of child protection across sectors and programmes.  
 Incorporating sustainability, systems strengthening, and community ownership approaches into programme design.  
 End Results 
 Improved EVAC programmes and investments that are evidence-based, contextually relevant, and integrated across sectors.
 3. EVAC Programme Quality Assurance   
 Provide technical guidance to support EVAC programme quality, implementation effectiveness, and continuous improvement. Services may include: 
 Reviewing programme implementation and technical quality.  
 Supporting adaptation and implementation of evidence-based PROTECT interventions.  
 Developing quality assurance plans, tools, and improvement measures.  
 Identifying opportunities to strengthen programme performance and impact. 
 End Results 
 Improved EVAC programme quality, effectiveness, and impact through the consistent application of evidence-based approaches, strengthened implementation practices, and continuous improvement processes that enhance outcomes for children and communities.
 4. EVAC Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Evidence  
 Provide technical support for monitoring, evaluation, research, and evidence-generation activities that strengthen EVAC programme effectiveness and accountability. Services may include: 
 Designing monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks and systems.  
 Developing or adapting assessment and data collection tools.  
 Conducting baseline, midline, endline, and evaluation studies.  
 Analyzing quantitative and qualitative data and generating evidence-based recommendations.  
 Supporting operational research, learning studies, and evidence-building initiatives.  
 End Result 
 Stronger evidence-based EVAC programming through enhanced monitoring, evaluation, research, and learning
 5. EVAC Capacity Building  
 Provide training, coaching, mentoring, and technical accompaniment to strengthen the capacity of child protection staff. Services may include: 
 Designing and facilitating EVAC technical learning events and training programmes.  
 Delivering refresher training on PROTECT (or any sub-component of PROTECT).  
 Providing coaching, mentoring, and technical accompaniment.  
 Supporting competency assessments and workforce development planning.  
 End Result 
 Stronger EVAC capacity and workforce developed 
 6. EVAC Advocacy, Positioning, and Influencing  
 Provide technical expertise to support policy, systems, and practice changes that strengthen the protection and well-being of children. Services may include: 
 Supporting evidence-informed EVAC advocacy and influencing strategies.  
 Developing technical recommendations and EVAC policy messaging.  
 Represent World Vision office at external EVAC-related events, conferences, decision-making forums. 
 End Results 
 Stronger policies, systems, and investments to prevent and respond to violence against children through evidence-informed advocacy, strategic engagement, and increased visibility of EVAC priorities among key decision-makers and stakeholders.
 7. Resource Development and Proposal Support  
 Provide technical expertise to support EVAC resource mobilization and investment opportunities in child protection. Services may include: 
 Contributing technical input to grant proposals, concept notes, and donor submissions.  
 Supporting EVAC programme design workshops, including theory of change and problem analysis processes.  
 Drafting or reviewing technical narratives and programme frameworks.  
 Supporting consortium development and proposal collaboration processes.   
 End Result 
 Increased investment in EVAC programming through stronger proposals, programme designs, and technical documentation.
 8. Technical Documentation, Learning and Knowledge Products  
 Provide technical support to document, synthesize, and disseminate evidence, learning, and promising practices from EVAC programming 
 Developing case studies, success stories, technical briefs, and learning products.  
 Preparing technical reports, evidence summaries, and research publications.  
 Documenting promising practices, innovations, and lessons learned.  
 Reviewing technical documents and knowledge products for quality and technical rigor.  
 End Result 
 Stronger organizational learning and evidence-informed decision-making through high-quality documentation, knowledge products, and the sharing of lessons learned

 Here's where you come in: 
 As a Safeguarding Advisor in a Response, you will provide in-depth safeguarding expertise and support to Response Management and key Functions, to ensure safeguarding is embedded in the culture and operations of a Response from the beginning and appropriately through every phase. They actively support Management to identify and mitigate safeguarding risk while equipping staff to become safeguarding champions for their teams.  They provide technical safeguarding guidance and capacity building to the Response on all aspects of safeguarding compliance, safer programming and safeguarding culture building in alignment with WV’s Child and Adult Safeguarding Policy. offres.description:
With over 70 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.
 Come join our 34,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
 Key Responsibilities: 
 The Management Quality Deputy Director will be responsible for overall financial, budgeting,  supply chain, and operational functions for a large-scale program aimed at strengthening the national HIV care and treatment program in Sierra Leone. This role ensures the program operates efficiently, complies with donor and organizational policies, and achieves its objectives through effective resource management and coordination. The project budget is estimated to be $12M per year over 5 years. Recruitment is contingent upon successful award of the project. Selection of the final applicant is subject to CDC approval. The project is anticipated to begin in October 2025.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 The Management Quality Deputy Director (MQ/DD) will be responsible for compliance oversight of the project and any related sub-agreements. S/he interprets USG and other donor regulations for the project’s management staff. The MQ/DD also assists with trainings on compliance, performs internal control assessments, conducts financial reviews and follow-up of recommendations, and identifies training needs, and develops country-specific curriculum to address the needs. S/he sources, supervises and mentors project Finance and Compliance staff. S/he develops and implements strategies to prevent or reduce compliance-related liabilities in project. The position reports directly to the Project Director and has relationships with the Operations Unit at World Vision Sierra Leone. S/he is part of the project program team and functions as an important member of the Project Senior Management Team.  Keep Christ central in individual and corporate life. Actively participate in and contribute to the spiritual disciplines of the organization (Christian conduct, devotions, chapel, prayer, worship); incorporate WV Core Values into decisions within scope of role.
 Grants and Contract Management
 Serve as principle point of contact on grant management and compliance issues with the treatment facilities, CRS/Zambia Finance, and Regional Finance and Compliance staff. Work with World Vision/Sierra Leone Finance, Regional Finance and Compliance Staff, and country coordinating teams to develop and coordinate grant management capacity building trainings at supported sites. Attend meetings/trainings related to grant reporting and compliance organized by World Vision. Disseminate strategies and training/learning materials by Regional Finance and Compliance staff. Improve field staff capacity to comply with regulations. Develop and deliver training curricula on compliance issues as required. Support the HSS and Sustainability coordinator in ensuring that supported NACP learned from World Vision experience in supporting District Health Management Teams (DHMTs) and health facilities to sustain the achieved gain. Support the Project Director with project close out. Oversee the preparation, review, and submission of financial and performance reports to donors. Monitor sub-grantee performance, ensuring alignment with program goals and adherence to contractual requirements. Develop and maintain systems for tracking grant activities, deliverables, and budgets.
 Supply Chain Management
 Oversee supply chain operations, including procurement, warehousing, and distribution of medical supplies and equipment. Ensure timely delivery of resources to project sites while maintaining cost-effectiveness and quality assurance. Collaborate with technical and program teams to forecast supply chain needs based on program activities. Monitor supply chain performance, address bottlenecks, and optimize processes.
 Financial Oversight
 Manage program budgets, ensuring alignment with donor requirements and organizational policies. Monitor expenditures and provide financial projections to ensure cost control and effective resource allocation. Support the Finance Manager in preparing audit-ready financial reports. Ensure risk management practices are in place, including compliance with anti-fraud policies. Train NACP and DHMTs and project staffs on budgeting. Provide technical support to NACP and DHMTs to finalize annual budgets of their supported Health Facilities. Ensure the integrity of project financial reporting and the effective control of financial assets. Regularly monitor and assess project’s ability to accurately record and post all financial transactions. Provide analysis and recommendations to the Project Team. Develop and deliver training curricula on finance issues as required.
 Operations and Administration
 Provide leadership in operational planning, ensuring alignment with program goals. Oversee administrative functions, including HR, IT, and logistics, to support program implementation. Manage relationships with vendors, contractors, and service providers to ensure high-quality services. Identify and mitigate operational risks, ensuring business continuity and efficiency.
 Capacity Building and Team Management
 Provide training and mentorship to staff and partners on grants management, financial oversight, and compliance. Supervise a team of operations, finance, and supply chain staff, fostering a collaborative and high-performing work environment. Build the capacity of local organizations to manage program resources effectively.
 Stakeholder Coordination
 Work closely with the Project Director to ensure seamless coordination between programmatic and operational functions. Represent the program in meetings with donors, government agencies, and partners as needed. Facilitate communication and collaboration between technical teams and operational units.
 Internal Control Assessments
 Participate in project’s Internal Control and Monitoring assessments as required. As required visit the NACP, DHMTs and the health facilities. Prepare Visit’s Reports on internal controls, procurement, human resource management, asset management, and budget utilization. Prepare working papers to document work carried out during site visits. Ensure that files are organized, legible, and logically developed to document the management, accounting and logistics systems, the assessment of those systems, the tests developed and conducted to evaluate those systems, and the tests of reporting accuracy. Give opinion on adequacy of internal controls, compliance with applicable laws and regulations, compliance with World Vision/USG policies and procedures.
 Qualifications:
 Advanced degree in business administration, finance, supply chain management, or a related field.
 Minimum of 8-10 years of experience in program management roles, including grants and supply chain management in donor-funded programs.
 Proven expertise in financial management, with experience in managing budgets over $5 million.
 Familiarity with CDC, PEPFAR, or USAID regulations and reporting requirements.
 Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage multidisciplinary teams.
 Demonstrated ability to build capacity within local organizations.
 Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
 Proficiency in financial management software and supply chain tools.
 Key Competencies:
 Strong organizational and project management skills.
 Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
 Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
 Commitment to compliance, accountability, and transparency.
 Cultural sensitivity and ability to work effectively in a diverse environment.
 Additional Requirements:
 Willingness to travel to project sites as needed.
 Fluency in English required; proficiency in local languages is an asset.

 Job Purpose 
 The Accounting Manager is responsible for overseeing and managing the accounting operations in an emergency response, ensuring financial compliance, accuracy, and efficiency in all financial processes. This role includes cash management, accounts payable oversight, financial reconciliations, and audit preparations. The position ensures that financial operations align with both World Vision International (WVI) financial policies and globally accepted accounting standards. The Accounting Manager plays a critical role in supporting financial decision-making, internal controls, and risk management in a high-pressure, fast-paced emergency setting.
 Key Responsibilities 
 A. Financial Management, Oversight and Internal Controls. 
 A.1 Cash Management, Accounting and Reporting 
 1.       Lead and oversee the comprehensive functionality and operations of Cash Management, Accounting, and Reporting for the Response, ensuring compliance with governmental regulatory requirements. 
 2.       Ensure accurate and timely submission of monthly financial reports to the Field Financial Reporting database. 
 3.       Oversee the analysis of balance sheet accounts and reconciliation processes. 
 4.       Facilitate seamless coordination with GC Shared Services (R2R and P2P) regarding accounting and reporting. 
 5.       Foster a customer-oriented approach in all interactions, ensuring timely and efficient responses to queries and concerns. 
 6.       Liaise with the Grants finance team, ensuring alignment in all accounting processes. 
 A.2 Internal Controls 
 1.       Monitor internal control systems to safeguard financial assets of the organization and ensure accurate financial statements. 
 2.       Periodically review and assess the effectiveness of internal controls, recommending improvements and modifications where necessary. 
 3.       Collaborate with internal and external auditors to ensure effective audits and address any identified deficiencies. 
 B. Team Leadership, Development, and Interdepartmental Collaboration 
 1. Provide strategic directions to the finance officers, leading day-to-day operations of the Accounting Team.
 2. Cultivate professional growth within the team, emphasizing performance reviews, skill development, mentoring, and succession planning.
 3. Champion interdepartmental collaboration, ensuring the Accounting Team works cohesively with other departments to achieve organizational objectives. 4. Engage in professional networking with the Regional/GC finance community, promoting knowledge exchange and best practices.
 C. Local Partnering: 
 1. Oversee the process of fund transfers to local partners, ensuring adherence to organizational and donor-specific guidelines.
 2. Implement robust financial controls for funds transferred to local partners, conduct regular financial audits and reviews and oversee all donor audits performed on local partners’ books.
 3. Work with local partners on capacity-building initiatives, focusing on financial management, record maintenance, and reporting.
 4. Foster consistent communication with local partners on financial expectations and reporting requirements.
 5. Address financial discrepancies with local partners, guiding them towards compliance.
 6. Coordinate inter-departmentally to ensure partnering processes align with broader organizational and donor requirements.
 C. Risk management 
 1. Lead(finance) in institutional/global/government audit preparation to provide required information, ensure follow up actions and implementation of audit recommendations related to finance, addressing common audit findings and disallowed costs.
 2. Assist Finance director in managing financial risk and implement anti-corruption strategies
 KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND EXPERIENCE 
 Require d Education, training, license, registration, and/or Certification 
 Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance or Business Administration, or a related field
 A full commitment to World Vision’s core values and mission statement.
 Full adherence to World Vision Child Protection, Code of Conduct and Conflict of Interest policies.
 Full Adherence to security protocols
 Required Professional Experience 
 Minimum 5 years’ experience in finance position with medium business/medium NGO/government agency 
 Minimum 5 years’ experience in finance and accounting management position 
 Experience in major donor regulations (US, UK, Canada Governments, ADH, BHA, UN agencies) is a must. 
 Practical knowledge of financial systems, internal financial controls & procedures and staff management skills. 
 Preferred Experience, Knowledge and/or other Qualifications 
 Advanced Degrees: MBA, MSc in Finance/Accounting/Auditing.
 Certifications : ACCA, CIMA, CPA, or équivalent Professional qualification.
 NGO/Humanitarian Experience: Prior experience in emergency response or crisis settings.
 System Proficiency: Knowledge of financial management software and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.
 Re quired travel and/or work environment accommodations 
 Ability to travel to/within domestically and internationally as required
 Work hours are often in excess of 12 hours per day during difficult periods of the response

 Occasional requirement to move within operational field locations with basic living conditions.
 May require standing or sitting for extended periods while performing accounting reviews and reconciliations.

 JOB PURPOSE: 
As a Cloud FinOps Analyst, you will serve as the strategic nexus between Finance, IT, and engineering teams, driving financial accountability and cost efficiency across our global cloud footprint. You will leverage data-driven insights and governance frameworks to optimize cloud investments, enable transparent chargeback models, and support mission-critical programs with scalable, cost-effective solutions.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Cost Analytics & Reporting 
 Aggregate, normalize, and analyze multi-cloud consumption data (AWS, Azure, GCP) to identify trends, anomalies, and cost-saving opportunities.
 Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and executive-level reports on cloud spend, forecast accuracy, and cost allocation.
 Budgeting, Forecasting & Governance 
 Partner with Finance and business unit leaders to establish rolling cloud budgets, consumption forecasts, and variance analyses.
 Implement and enforce FinOps governance policies, tagging standards, and budget guardrails to ensure adherence to organizational financial controls.​
 Chargeback/Showback Implementation 
 Design, deploy, and continuously refine chargeback and showback mechanisms that allocate cloud costs to product lines and projects, driving ownership and accountability.
 Educate stakeholders on FinOps principles, fostering a culture of cost transparency and shared responsibility.
 Cost Optimization Initiatives 
 Collaborate with architecture and engineering teams to execute rightsizing, Reserved Instance/Savings Plan procurement, spot-instance strategies, and automated shutdown schedules.
 Lead continuous improvement sprints—within Agile delivery cycles—to implement infrastructure-as-code (IaC) cost-management controls and automation.
 Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory 
 Act as the subject-matter expert to advise senior leadership on cloud financial implications of new services, migration patterns, and emerging technologies.
 Facilitate FinOps training workshops and working sessions to embed best practices across global technical teams.
 KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related discipline.
 3+ years of experience in cloud financial management, cost optimization, or FinOps within a large-scale, multi-cloud environment.
 Proficiency with cloud cost tools (e.g., AWS Cost Explorer, Azure Cost Management, GCP Billing), FinOps platforms (e.g., CloudHealth, Apptio), and BI/reporting solutions (Power BI, Tableau).
 Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and P&L reconciliation.
 Demonstrated ability to translate complex financial data into actionable insights and executive summaries.
 Technical Collaboration: Hands-on familiarity with IaC (Terraform, ARM templates), scripting (Python, PowerShell), and CI/CD pipelines to embed cost controls within DevOps workflows.
 Analytical Rigor: Expert problem-solving skills for diagnosing cost anomalies, optimizing utilization, and reconciling billing discrepancies.
 Value-Driven Mindset: Passion for maximizing cloud ROI and aligning technology spend with organizational impact metrics.
 Customer-Centric Orientation: Skilled at partnering with distributed teams to balance cost reduction with uninterrupted service delivery and program outcomes.
 Communication & Influence: Exceptional stakeholder management, able to facilitate cross-functional alignment and foster a culture of continuous cost optimization.
 Certifications (Desirable): FinOps Certified Practitioner (FinOps Foundation), Certified Cloud Practitioner (AWS/Azure/GCP), or equivalent.
 Applicant Types Accepted: 
Local Applicants Only

 Job Description: 
 World Vision Vanuatu (WV) is a Christian humanitarian organisation dedicated to working with children, families and communities to overcome poverty and injustice.  Since 1981, we have been working to transform communities through program delivery in education, health care, water, sanitation & hygiene, agriculture and sustainable livelihoods.  In line with the Vanuatu Government’s National Sustainable Development Plan (2016-2030) , World Vision – in partnership with communities - deliver programs that are relevant, cost-efficient, effective and make a lasting difference.  Community development is a key focus of World Vision Vanuatu, with 80% of our staff based in the communities where we work.
 The purpose of this position is to contribute to the achievement of high-quality technical program outcomes. This role will:
 Manage program quality functions including design and evaluation for World Vision Vanuatu to ensure a credible evidence base for informed programming decision making, delivery of quality programs and a high standard of reporting to our donors/stakeholders.
 Work effectively, efficiently, and in cooperation with the Portfolio Quality team ensuring quality implementation, cohesive team work and good information flow.
 Liaison with donors, support offices and WV regional offices on program quality functions.
 This position will ensure that all projects and programs achieve the greatest impact on the well-being of children.  This will also help WVV and its partners in Vanuatu to achieve their objectives so that WVV is seen as a partner of choice.  The PQ Manager is a member of the Senior Management Team, and will work closely with the Impact and Evidence Manager on any implementation risks.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
 Employee Contract Type:

 Job Description: 
 Note: Joining our Talent Pipeline position means you can be part of our candidate pipeline, ready to contribute when new opportunities arise. By applying, you express your interest in being considered for future roles linked to donor-funded initiatives. Please note that joining the pool does not represent an immediate employment opportunity; instead, it ensures we can reach out to you when suitable positions become available.  
 Here’s where you come in: 
 Job Purpose 
 The Chief of Party (COP) / Project Director serves as the senior-most leadership position for large-scale, donor-funded development and humanitarian programmes. The COP provides overarching strategic direction, technical guidance, financial stewardship, and stakeholder engagement across multi-sector, multi-cultural programme contexts. This pipeline role draws on the full breadth of the GAM Competency Framework, requiring mastery of the grant cycle, donor relationship management, compelling proposal oversight, grant process management, post-award compliance, and effective use of tools and systems.
 Major Responsibilities 
 1) Provides overall strategic direction for programme design, implementation, and learning, ensuring goals, milestones, and priorities are clearly defined and communicated. Leads the development, adaptation, and execution of programme strategies that respond to evolving operational, political, and contextual realities. Ensures alignment with World Vision’s mission, national strategies, partnership priorities, and donor expectations while fostering evidence-based decision-making, innovation, and adaptive management. (30%)
 End Results: 
 A clearly articulated and contextually relevant strategic approach that enables programme success and stakeholder alignment.
 2) Oversees day-to-day programme implementation to ensure activities meet targets, follow approved work plans, and comply with technical standards and donor regulations. Strengthens operational systems, including procurement, logistics, reporting, safeguarding, and risk management. Ensures effective coordination with internal units – Finance, Supply Chain, MEAL, HR, and Security – to maintain operational excellence.  20%
 End Results: 
 Programmes are implemented effectively, on time, and in full compliance, with reduced operational risks and strengthened systems.
 3) Leads financial planning and forecasting processes, including budget development, expenditure monitoring, and variance analysis. Ensures full compliance with donor rules, organisational policies, and audit standards while proactively addressing financial risks. Oversees management of sub-grants and partner agreements, ensuring partners meet financial and contractual obligations. Ensures all financial reporting is timely, accurate, and aligned with donor and organisational expectations.  20%
 End Results 
 Budgets are well managed, financial compliance is upheld, audit risks are minimised, and donors receive transparent, reliable reporting.
 4) Supervises senior national and international staff, establishing clear expectations, roles, responsibilities, and communication lines. Cultivates a cohesive, high-performing team environment grounded in accountability, trust, and continuous learning. Strengthens talent pipelines through coaching, mentoring, and structured capacity-building initiatives. Supports partner capacity strengthening in technical, operational, and compliance areas.10%
 End Results 
 A capable, motivated, and well-supported team equipped to deliver high-quality outcomes and sustain programme impact.
 5) Serves as the primary liaison with donors, government counterparts, UN agencies, implementing partners, community leaders, and other critical stakeholders. Represents World Vision at coordination forums, donor meetings, high-level engagements, and sectoral working groups. Leads external engagement strategies to elevate programme influence, strengthen relationships, and enhance visibility. 10%
 End Results 
 Strong external partnerships, improved donor and government relationships, and enhanced organisational positioning.
 6) Ensures development and implementation of strong MEAL systems that support data quality, evidence generation, learning loops, and adaptive programme management. Oversees production of high-quality performance reports, evaluations, and learning products aligned with donor timelines and requirements. Leverages technology platforms and knowledge management systems to improve programme oversight. 10%
 End Results 
 Programmes benefit from timely, reliable evidence that informs course corrections and satisfies donor reporting expectations.
 KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE 
 Required Professional Experience 
 Demonstrated success as a Chief of Party, Project Director, or equivalent, with proven ability to lead strategy, implementation, budgeting, supervision, and adaptive management in challenging contexts.
 10+ years of senior leadership experience managing large, complex, donor-funded international development or humanitarian programmes, including full project cycles and multi-partner coordination.
 Strong team and partnership leadership, including the ability to motivate multicultural teams, collaborate across institutions, and build shared vision with government, donors, local organisations, and private-sector partners.
 Excellent communication, representation, and relationship-building skills, effective at engaging high-level stakeholders as well as community partners and beneficiaries.
 Comprehensive management expertise across financial oversight, HR, procurement, compliance, operations, and risk mitigation.
 Required Education 
 University degree in humanitarian, development, international relations, public administration, or relevant field. Master’s degree preferred.
 Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications 
 Fluency in oral and written English. Additional languages (French, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic) are an asset.
 Familiarity with major bilateral and multilateral donor regulations (USG, FCDO, EU, Global Fund, BMZ, GAC).
 Experience with World Vision or similar faith-based international NGO operating environments.
 Demonstrated competence in Go/No-Go decision-making, donor landscape analysis, and evidence-based programme design aligned with GAM Competency 1 (Mastering the GAM Cycle).
 Travel and Work Environment 
 Ability to travel within the country/region as required. Willingness to serve in fragile, conflict-affected, or remote contexts.

By applying, you express your interest in being considered for future roles linked to donor-funded initiatives. Please note that joining the pool does not represent an immediate employment opportunity; instead, it ensures we can reach out to you when suitable positions become available.  
 Here’s where you come in: 
 Job Purpose 
 The Grant Acquisition Manager leads the end-to-end pursuit of institutional funding opportunities, from donor landscape analysis and opportunity identification through proposal development, submission, and award negotiation. The role serves as the primary driver of World Vision’s competitive positioning by building donor intelligence, coordinating cross-functional bid teams, and ensuring proposals are compelling, compliant, and aligned with organisational strategy. Grounded in the GAM Competency Framework, this position requires autonomous-level proficiency across mastering the GAM cycle, donor relationship management, and creating compelling proposals.
 Major Responsibilities 
 1) Conducts continuous donor landscape analysis to identify, track, and assess funding opportunities across bilateral, multilateral, and private-sector donors. Leads Go/No-Go analysis for each opportunity, applying data-driven decision-making frameworks. Maintains a pipeline tracker of upcoming and active opportunities, ensuring strategic alignment with national office and regional priorities. Applies World Vision’s Christian identity as a lens for opportunity filtering. (GAM Competency 1: Mastering the GAM Cycle) 30% 
 End Results 
 A robust, data-driven pipeline of strategically aligned funding opportunities with clear Go/No-Go rationale for each pursuit. 
 2) Leads proposal development from concept through submission, coordinating technical writers, sector specialists, finance teams, and partner organisations. Develops evidence-based theories of change, logical frameworks, and programme narratives that address donor evaluation criteria. Creates budgets that reflect programmatic priorities while ensuring good stewardship. Implements quality review processes at key milestones. (GAM Competency 3: Creating Compelling Proposals) 25% 
 End Results 
 High-quality, donor-compliant proposals that are competitive, evidence-based, and reflect World Vision’s value proposition. 
 3) Builds and maintains strategic relationships with institutional donors, government agencies, UN bodies, and peer organisations. Conducts stakeholder mapping to identify decision-makers and influencers within donor structures. Organises pre-positioning engagements such as technical learning exchanges, concept note presentations, and donor briefings. Transforms transactional donor relationships into collaborative partnerships. (GAM Competency 2: Building Relationships with Donors and Partners) 20%
 End Results 
 Strong, trust-based donor relationships that position World Vision favourably for competitive and sole-source opportunities. 
 4) Establishes and manages structured proposal development workflows using agile methodologies adapted for grant development. Coordinates cross-functional bid teams, facilitates kick-off meetings, manages timelines, and conducts retrospective reviews. Implements standardised document management and version control for all proposal assets. (GAM Competency 4: Managing Grant Processes) 10%
 End Results 
 Efficient, well-coordinated proposal development processes that reduce cycle times and improve proposal quality. 
 5) Supports award negotiation and transition to implementation teams. Contributes to start-up planning and ensures that proposal commitments are accurately reflected in implementation plans. Maintains lessons-learned documentation from each pursuit to strengthen future submissions. (GAM Competency 5: Post-Award Support) 10%
 End Results 
 Smooth transitions from acquisition to implementation, with institutional knowledge captured and applied to future pursuits.
 6) Utilises grant acquisition databases, CRM platforms, proposal templates, and competitive intelligence tools to streamline pursuit processes. Maintains knowledge management repositories for institutional memory. Champions adoption of AI-assisted tools and emerging technologies. (GAM Competency 6: Utilising Tools and Systems) 5% 
 End Results 
 Improved efficiency, consistency, and institutional memory across all grant acquisition activities. 
 KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE 
 Required Professional Experience 
 Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in grant acquisition, proposal development, or business development within the international development or humanitarian sector.
 Demonstrated track record of winning competitive grants from major institutional donors (USG, FCDO, EU, Global Fund, BMZ, SIDA, GAC, or similar).
 Experience leading cross-functional proposal teams and managing complex, multi-partner bids with budgets exceeding USD 5 million.
 Strong analytical skills for donor landscape mapping, competitive intelligence, and Go/No-Go decision-making.
 Proven ability to develop evidence-based theories of change, logical frameworks, and programme narratives.
 Required Education 
 University degree in international development, public administration, business, social sciences, or related field. Master’s degree preferred. 
 Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications 
 Fluency in oral and written English. Proficiency in French, Spanish, or Portuguese is a strong advantage.
 Experience with Shipley or similar structured bid management methodologies.
 Familiarity with World Vision’s programme models, theory of change approaches, and partnership frameworks.
 Experience building capacity of national office teams in grant acquisition processes and competencies.
 Travel and Work Environment 
 Willingness to travel up to 30% for donor meetings, proposal support to field offices, and capture planning.

 Note: Joining our Talent Pipeline position means you can be part of our candidate pipeline, ready to contribute when new opportunities arise.
