 Here’s where you come in: 
 Job Purpose 
 The Commercial Contract Manager leads the acquisition, negotiation, and compliance management of commercial contracts, fee-for-service agreements, and non-traditional funding instruments on behalf of World Vision. As institutional donors increasingly shift towards commercial contracting mechanisms, this role ensures World Vision can compete effectively, negotiate favourable terms, and manage contract performance to protect organisational interests while delivering programme impact. Grounded in the GAM Competency Framework, the position requires advanced proficiency in post-award support, grant process management, and donor relationship building, with the commercial contracting lens applied across all six competency areas.
 Major Responsibilities 
 1) Leads commercial contract negotiations with donors, prime contractors, and partner organisations, ensuring that terms and conditions protect World Vision’s interests while enabling programme delivery. Reviews and negotiates risk allocation, liability clauses, intellectual property provisions, termination terms, and dispute resolution mechanisms. Develops replicable negotiation templates and frameworks for use across offices. (GAM Competency 5: Post-Award Support) 25%
 End Results 
 Favourable contract terms that protect World Vision’s interests, reduce implementation risk, and create replicable templates for future negotiations. 
 2) Manages the full lifecycle of commercial contracts from pre-award compliance review through contract execution, modification, and close-out. Ensures adherence to donor-specific terms and conditions, organisational policies, and regulatory requirements. Monitors contract deliverables, milestones, and payment schedules. Leads contract modification and amendment processes as programme needs evolve. (GAM Competency 4: Managing Grant Processes)25% 
 End Results 
 Contracts are managed efficiently with full compliance, timely deliverables, and proactive risk mitigation throughout the contract lifecycle. 
 3) Scans the commercial contracting landscape to identify emerging opportunities from bilateral donors, multilateral agencies, and private-sector entities that utilise fee-for-service, cost-reimbursable, or fixed-price contract mechanisms. Conducts competitive analysis and advises on bid/no-bid decisions for commercial opportunities. Maintains intelligence on evolving donor procurement policies and contracting trends. (GAM Competency 1: Mastering the GAM Cycle) 20%
 End Results 
 A clear understanding of commercial contracting opportunities and risks, with data-driven pursuit recommendations. 
 4) Develops and reviews cost proposals, pricing strategies, and commercial terms for competitive bids. Ensures budgets are compliant with applicable cost principles (FAR, OMB, EU regulations) and reflect realistic cost recovery. Works with finance teams to structure indirect cost rates, fee structures, and profit margins in line with organisational and donor policies. (GAM Competency 3: 
 Creating Compelling Proposals) 15% 
 End Results 
 Competitive, compliant cost proposals that maximise cost recovery while meeting donor evaluation criteria. 
 5) Builds relationships with commercial contracting officers, procurement specialists, and compliance teams within donor agencies and prime contractor organisations. Represents World Vision in pre-solicitation conferences, industry days, and contractor forums. Develops teaming arrangements and subcontracting strategies with partner organisations. (GAM Competency 2: Building Relationships with Donors and Partners)10%
 End Results 
 Strong working relationships with contracting officers and prime contractors that enhance World Vision’s competitive positioning.
 6) Implements contract management systems, tracking tools, and compliance dashboards to monitor performance across the commercial contract portfolio. Maintains a contracts database with key terms, expiration dates, and modification histories. Champions digital tools for contract analytics and risk assessment. (GAM Competency 6: Utilising Tools and Systems) 5%
 End Results 
 Real-time visibility into contract performance, compliance status, and risk exposure across the portfolio. 
 KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE 
 Required Professional Experience 
 Minimum 7 years of experience in commercial contract management, procurement, or contract administration within international development, humanitarian, or government contracting environments.
 Demonstrated experience negotiating contracts with major institutional donors (USG, FCDO, EU, World Bank, UN agencies) or prime contractors.
 Strong knowledge of applicable cost principles and procurement regulations (FAR, AIDAR, OMB Uniform Guidance, EU Financial Regulation).
 Experience managing fixed-price, cost-reimbursable, time-and-materials, and indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract types.
 Proven ability to structure teaming arrangements, subcontracts, and consortium agreements.
 Required Education 
 University degree in law, business administration, public administration, finance, or related field. Master’s degree or professional certification (e.g., CPCM, CFCM, CCCM) preferred. 
 Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications 
 Fluency in oral and written English. Proficiency in French or Spanish is an advantage.
 Experience with contract management software and compliance tracking platforms.
 Familiarity with World Vision or similar faith-based international NGO operating environments.
 Understanding of the shift from grants to contracts in major donor funding portfolios and implications for NGO operations.
 Travel and Work Environment 
 Willingness to travel up to 25% for contract negotiations, compliance reviews, and donor engagement.

 Key Responsibilities: 
 The IT Event Management Engineer is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously improving global event detection and alerting systems that ensure proactive identification and resolution of IT issues before they impact users or services. This position operates at the intersection of engineering, automation, and service management , driving reliability, consistency, and operational excellence across hybrid cloud and on-prem environments.
 The role is foundational to achieving a proactive, data-driven IT operations model —helping transition the organization from reactive firefighting to predictive service assurance.
 Core Competencies 
 Technical Proficiency: Understanding of ITOM systems, monitoring frameworks, APIs, and integrations.
 Process Orientation: Ability to document, standardize, and institutionalize best practices through templates and guides.
 Collaboration: Works effectively across infrastructure, application, and service management domains.
 Analytical Thinking: Strong data interpretation skills to identify event trends and patterns.
 Innovation: Drives automation, simplification, and modernization of event workflows.
 Customer Focus: Designs alerting systems that directly enhance reliability, transparency, and user satisfaction.
 Qualifications & Experience 
 Education & Certifications
 Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
 ITIL Foundation (minimum); ITIL Intermediate or ITIL 4 Managing Professional is an advantage
 Relevant certifications in cloud platforms (Azure, AWS) or monitoring tools are desirable
 Experience
 At least 10–12+ years of total professional experience, with at least 5+ years of hands-on experience in IT Operations, Monitoring, and Event Management in enterprise environments.
 Proven experience working with enterprise monitoring and event management tools (e.g., OpsBridge, Azure Monitor, AWS CloudWatch, Site24x7)
 Experience integrating monitoring tools with ITSM platforms for automated incident management
 Hands-on experience in automation and scripting (e.g., PowerShell, Python, Ansible)
 Exposure to hybrid environments (cloud + on-prem infrastructure)
 Technical & Functional Skills
 Strong understanding of ITOM and monitoring frameworks, including event correlation, alert tuning, and noise reduction
 Experience designing or operating event-driven systems for proactive detection and service assurance
 Knowledge of APIs and system integrations
 Experience with dashboards, analytics, and reporting tools (e.g., Power BI, Kibana)
 Familiarity with ITSM processes (Incident, Problem, Change Management)
 Core Responsibilities 
 1. Event Detection, Ingestion & Correlation 
 •  Design and maintain event ingestion pipelines from multiple monitoring sources (e.g., Azure Monitor, AWS CloudWatch, network devices, applications, SaaS systems).
 •  Develop correlation logic and rules to identify related alerts and minimize redundant or noisy notifications.
 •   Maintain event taxonomies and classification standards to ensure consistent event tagging, severity, and categorization across systems.
 2. Automation, Orchestration & Remediation 
 •  Build and maintain automation scripts and workflows to automatically detect and remediate known issues (e.g., restarting services, clearing caches, resizing disks).
 •  Integrate event management systems with ITSM platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, SMAX) to auto-create and route incidents with contextual data.
 •  Participate in AIOps initiatives—leveraging predictive analytics and machine learning models to forecast incidents and anomalies.
 3. Standardization, Templates & Documentation 
 •  Develop standard operating procedures (SOPs) , runbooks , and knowledge articles for consistent event triage and escalation processes.
 •  Create event configuration templates (e.g., for threshold settings, escalation rules, integration blueprints) to ensure monitoring practices are repeatable and scalable .
 •  Maintain a Monitoring and Event Management Playbook outlining governance, workflows, and automation frameworks.
 •  Document integration patterns, naming conventions, and API schema mappings to enable faster onboarding of new systems.
 •   Ensure all documentation is version-controlled, accessible via Confluence or SharePoint, and updated as systems evolve.
 4. Operational Effectiveness & Continuous Improvement 
 •  Conduct routine health checks on event management systems to ensure optimal performance, data accuracy, and integration stability.
 •  Analyze event and incident data trends to identify gaps, redundancies, or opportunities for improvement.
 •  Partner with Service Desk, Cloud, and Network teams to optimize event thresholds, escalation rules, and notification logic.
 •  Drive continuous improvement initiatives—reducing false positives and increasing actionable alerts through tuning and refinement.
 5. Governance & Quality Assurance 
 •  Enforce standardized event handling procedures across global and regional IT teams.
 •  Support governance reviews and audits to demonstrate compliance with ITIL Event Management and ITOM standards.
 •  Ensure event management aligns with organizational KPIs such as system uptime, MTTD, MTTR, and service reliability targets.
 •   Support the development of a Monitoring Maturity Framework to assess and elevate event management capabilities globally.
 6. Collaboration & Knowledge Transfer 
 •  Partner with technical teams to integrate new services and platforms into the event management ecosystem.
 •  Conduct knowledge transfer sessions, workshops, and training for regional IT and operations staff to embed best practices.
 •   Participate in Agile ceremonies and cross-functional collaboration to align event management efforts with larger transformation initiatives.
 •   Act as a subject matter expert (SME) for monitoring and observability in project design and operational readiness reviews.
 7. Tool Evaluation & Innovation 
 •  Evaluate emerging monitoring and observability tools to identify opportunities for consolidation or modernization.
 •  Support proof-of-concept activities, benchmark tool performance, and provide recommendations for technology roadmaps.
 •   Contribute to architectural discussions regarding hybrid monitoring strategies, especially in multi-cloud contexts.

 Job Purpose: 
 The Director, Innovation and Continuous Analytics & Assurance drives transformation in audit practices through innovation and data-driven methodologies. Reporting to the Chief Audit Executive, the role leads the integration of continuous analytics to enhance risk visibility and assurance delivery.
 This position coordinates and coaches a team of Regional Specialists in Continuous Analytics & Assurance and ensures strategic alignment with GAA work streams as well as with global and regional function leaders to deploy solutions effectively. Operating with high ethical standards and minimal supervision, this role advances assurance through timely, technology-enabled insights.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Drive Innovation 
 Lead the design, development, and implementation of innovative methodologies, tools, and technologies that advance analytics and assurance practices.
 Champion the use of automation, AI, and data science to enable continuous monitoring, risk detection, and real-time assurance.
 Strategically collaborate with GAA work streams and global function leaders to pilot and scale cutting-edge solutions across the enterprise.
 Foster a culture of innovation by mentoring the Regional Specialists team and identifying opportunities for process improvement and future-focused assurance models.
 Monitor emerging trends in internal audit, risk analytics, and digital assurance to ensure the function remains at the forefront of industry practices.
 Promote and Ensure High Team Performance

 Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing across regions to promote consistency, innovation, and continuous improvement.

 Job Description: 
 To lead the compliance, safeguarding and integrity assurance functions of the WVPNG TB/HIV Global fund portfolio. This role ensures that the grant, its sub-recipients, and Provincial Health Authority (PHA) partners operate in line with the Global Fund and World Vision requirements, with emphasis on PSEAH, fraud and corruption prevention, asset accountability and audit readiness. The Manager also leverages this portfolio expertise to develop standardized compliance resources and provide expert technical support.
 MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Compliance Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement 
 Donors and stakeholders are confident in WVPNG’s compliance, safeguarding and integrity management of the grant, and all compliance reporting is timely and accurate.
 Prepare regular compliance reports for grant management and the Support Office, covering safeguarding, fraud, asset and audit status.
 Represent WVPNG on compliance and safeguarding matters in meetings with the Global Fund, LFA, government partners and sub-recipients.
 Ensure timely and accurate reporting of compliance status and incidents to all relevant stakeholders.
 Author, develop, and standardize key compliance resources for the grant, including manuals, checklists and training modules.
 Sub-recipient & PHA Compliance Oversight 
 Sub-recipients and PHA partners have the capacity and systems to be compliant, and compliance risks arising from decentralized implementation are identified and addressed early.
 Lead compliance oversight of the entire sub-recipient and PHA partner lifecycle, from due diligence to close-out.
 Develop and implement a risk-based compliance monitoring plan covering all implementing provinces, prioritizing higher-risk and decentralized sites, and conduct regular field compliance visits and spot checks.
 Work with provincial supervisors and focal points to ensure monitoring findings are acted on, and corrective action plans are completed.
 Review sub-recipient agreements, amendments and partner MOUs to ensure compliance, safeguarding and anti-fraud provisions are included before signature.
 Design and direct the grant’s compliance, safeguarding and anti-fraud capacity-building strategy for sub-recipients, PHA-hosted staff and grant staff, ensuring training is targeted and effective.
 Compliance Leadership, Internal Controls & Audit 
 A robust, proactive, and efficient compliance system is established, and the grant is always audit-ready, minimizing risk and ensuring adherence to all Global Fund, World Vision and legal standards.
 Design, implement, and lead the grant’s overall internal control framework to prevent and detect fraud, corruption and mismanagement, maintaining independence from the finance function.
 Serve as the primary focal point for Global Fund, LFA and OIG compliance inquiries, and for external and internal audits and reviews of the grant, coordinating evidence collection and timely, complete responses.
 Oversee the comprehensive risk management process, ensuring the risk register (including safeguarding, fraud and asset risks) is current, and mitigation plans are effective.
 Track implementation of audit recommendations, spot check findings and management actions through to closure.
 Advise Senior Leadership (DCOP, COP) on all compliance, safeguarding and integrity matters, providing solutions-oriented recommendations.
 Manage and mentor any compliance staff or focal points assigned to the grant, setting performance goals and fostering professional development.
 Fraud and Corruption Prevention & Asset Accountability 
 Grant funds, assets and health products are protected against fraud, corruption, theft and misuse, and all grant-funded assets are accounted for.
 Lead fraud and corruption risk assessments across the grant, with particular attention to decentralized implementation through PHAs and provinces and ensure mitigation measures are applied.
 Promote and monitor adherence to the Global Fund Code of Conduct for Recipients and World Vision anti-fraud, anti-bribery and conflict of interest policies, including annual conflict of interest declarations.
 Ensure suspected fraud, corruption or misuse of grant resources is reported promptly through World Vision’s whistleblowing and incident reporting channels and escalated to the Global Fund as required under the grant agreement.
 Support investigations led by authorized World Vision or Global Fund investigators as requested, without conducting independent investigations outside approved protocols.
 Establish and maintain a tracking system for grant-funded assets, including vehicles and equipment provided to PHAs and implementing partners, and conduct periodic physical verification of asset use, custody, maintenance and disposal.
 In coordination with the supply chain team, conduct periodic compliance checks on the storage, security and accountability of Global Fund health products held in area medical stores and health facilities.
 Safeguarding and PSEAH Assurance 
 Staff, partners and communities reached by the grant are protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH) and other harm, and all safeguarding concerns are reported, referred and managed in line with Global Fund and World Vision requirements.
 Lead the implementation and monitoring of child and adult safeguarding and PSEAH requirements across all Global Fund implementing provinces, sites, sub-recipients and PHA-hosted staff.
 Act as the grant’s compliance and safeguarding focal point, including on the Global Fund portal, working in close coordination with the National Office Operations and Safeguarding team.
 Ensure safeguarding and PSEAH clauses, codes of conduct and minimum standards are included in all sub-recipient agreements and partner MOUs and verify their application through spot checks and field monitoring.
 Ensure safeguarding incidents and allegations (including child protection and sexual harassment cases) are documented and referred promptly through World Vision’s established reporting and investigation channels, and that Global Fund notification obligations are met.
 Ensure reported cases are handled confidentially and, in a survivor-centered manner, and track follow-up actions to closure with the Safeguarding team.
 Ensure all grant staff, PHA-hosted staff and sub-recipient personnel complete mandatory safeguarding and PSEAH training and sign the applicable codes of conduct and maintain up-to-date records.
 Monitor that community feedback and complaints mechanisms at grant sites are functional, accessible and provide safe channels for reporting misconduct.
 EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE 
 Minimum 3-5 years’ experience in grant compliance, safeguarding, risk management, finance, or audit in an international development or humanitarian context.
 At least 3 years in a management or leadership position.
 Demonstrated expert knowledge of Global Fund rules and regulations.
 Proven experience in developing training materials, manuals, and policies.
 Experience overseeing compliance of complex sub-recipient or government partner portfolios.
 Demonstrated practical experience in safeguarding and PSEAH, including incident reporting, referral and survivor-centred case management.
 Demonstrated experience in fraud and corruption risk management, internal controls, and asset verification.
 Bachelor’s degree in Law, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Health, Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.

offres.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

 Key Responsibilities: 
 % of time 
 Activity
 End Results 
 10%
 Réaliser les visites à domicile pour identifier les femmes enceintes, allaitantes et les enfants de moins de cinq ans dans les communautés ciblées.
 Nombre de ménages visités selon le plan de travail.
 Nombre de femmes enceintes et d’enfants identifiés et enregistrés.
 15%
 Effectuer le dépistage communautaire de la malnutrition aiguë chez les enfants de 6 à 59 mois à l’aide du MUAC et de la recherche des œdèmes nutritionnels.

 Assurer le référencement rapide des enfants souffrant de malnutrition ainsi que des femmes enceintes à risque vers les structures de santé appropriées.

 Former et accompagner les mères leaders, groupes de soutien et relais communautaires sur les bonnes pratiques de santé, nutrition et hygiène.

 -        Conduire des séances de sensibilisation communautaire sur l’allaitement maternel exclusif, l’alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant (ANJE), l’hygiène et la prévention des maladies.

 Taux de participation communautaire.

 Promouvoir les pratiques familiales essentielles liées à la santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile.
 Adoption accrue des bonnes pratiques de santé familiale.

 Participer aux campagnes de vaccination, de supplémentation en vitamine A, de déparasitage et autres activités de santé publique organisées dans les zones d’intervention.

 Identifier et signaler rapidement les cas de maladies prioritaires, d’épidémies ou de situations d’urgence sanitaire au superviseur et aux autorités compétentes.
 Cas suspects rapportés à temps.

 Collecter, compiler et transmettre les données de santé et nutrition à travers les outils communautaires et plateformes approuvées.
 Rapports soumis dans les délais.
  Qualité et exactitude des données améliorées.

 Appuyer les mécanismes de redevabilité communautaire, la gestion des plaintes et le partage des résultats du projet (« Sa te chanje gras a nou »).
 Nombre de feedbacks/plaintes reçus et traités.
 Respect des politiques de sauvegarde et de protection.

 Zéro incident non signalé.

 GHANA COUNTRY CONTEXT 
 World Vision is a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. In1979, it expanded its operations to Ghana, a country situated in West Africa, and registered under the name, World Vision Ghana. Ghana has a diverse multiethnic population of over 31 million people, with a majority of the population being of Christian faith. The country also performs relatively well in metrics of healthcare, economic growth, and human development. World Vision Ghana’s head office is based in the capital city, Accra with two additional regional field offices, one based in Accra and the other in Tamale an area in the Northern part of Ghana. The portfolio of programs serves over 40,000 registered children within the various communities; the office operates in 18 Area Programmes and Grant project in 14 out of the 16 regions in Ghana. This is governed by a Board of Directors, whilst its operations are managed by a Senior Leadership team. The office has a staff strength of  about 250 employees who are currently supporting the organisation to implement its FY26-30 Operations Strategy aimed at empowering 2.5 million most vulnerable children directly and indirectly with Health and Nutrition, Education and skills development, Water Sanitation and Hygiene as well as food security and livelihood interventions

 The National Director (ND) will strategically lead, develop and direct the implementation of World Vision Ghana Strategy, in alignment with the Government of Ghana priorities and Our Promise.  In performing this role, the ND will be an effective leader locally, an effective member of the broader WVI Partnership, and will model the organization’s principles of Twin Citizenship to ensure high ministry quality and overall organizational effectiveness. The ND as a leader will contribute to partnership life and unity, by acting as both a local and global representative of the organization.  The ND will ensure the country's operations and operating models maintain the Partnership's focus on Child Well Being outcomes and aspirations as they apply in the Ghanaian specific country context, maximizing the impact in the field while maintaining efficiency as wise stewards of entrusted resources.

The ND will also ensure the office collaborates effectively with the WV Ghana Board, other partnership offices and divisions to achieve local and organizational goals.

 JOB PURPOSE : 
 The Enterprise Data & AI Integration Architect defines and evolves the organization's target-state data, integration, analytics, and AI architecture. The role connects business strategy to executable technology choices across data platforms, integration, information architecture, governance, analytics, machine learning, generative AI, and knowledge systems. The role operates across all architecture domains: Business, Data, Application, and Technology (BDAT), with particular depth in Data Domain. Strategic enough to shape investment and governance, and hands-on enough to validate designs, prototype critical patterns, lead complex global solution design and guide delivery teams.
 Acting as a trusted advisor and design authority, the architect establishes reusable standards and guardrails; leads current-state, target-state, and transition planning; assures major solution designs; and enables teams to deliver secure, interoperable, cost-effective, and AI-ready capabilities.
 The architect provides technical leadership and coordination across a defined portfolio, programme, or architectural domain, segment or global platforms, ensuring consistency, quality, and alignment of solution architectures within their scope, translating enterprise direction into practical guidance for delivery teams. This role bridges enterprise architecture intent and solution execution.
 Within the data specialization, the role provides architectural leadership for enterprise data design, data management, and data governance, ensuring solutions align with data standards, regulatory requirements, and approved enterprise architecture direction. This specialization focuses on embedding sound data architecture practices across initiatives while supporting consistent, scalable, and sustainable technology outcomes.
 Role mandate:
 Create a coherent enterprise data and AI architecture blueprint, with a pragmatic multi-year roadmap from current state to target state, to achieve and document NorthStar Architecture vision.
 Modernize the data landscape so governed, high-quality data can support operational use cases, analytics, machine learning, generative AI, and agentic workflows.
 Reduce fragmentation, duplicated platforms, tech debt, inconsistent definitions, uncontrolled data movement, and architecture debt in partnership with data governance.
 Embed security, privacy, resilience, regulatory compliance, responsible AI, observability, and cost management into architecture by design.

 Key Responsibilities: 
 Nutrition Research Intern 
 Remote within the US 
 World Vision Internships provide a three-month opportunity for exceptional students and recent graduates ready to explore a career in the international relief and development sector. We are committed to providing interns with a meaningful learning experience where they can learn, grow, and connect with other emerging professionals passionate about our mission.
 Internship Opportunity 
 Good health and nutrition empower children. We support over 184,000 Community Health Workers in 46 countries, providing timely counselling on healthy behaviours and building bridges to improved health and nutrition services. Our integrated approach enables caregivers, service providers, and over 300,000 faith leaders to protect, advocate for, and improve the health and nutrition of children where we work.
 Join our team to promote positive child development and well-being, prevent child death, reduce illness, and improve nutrition.
 What You’ll Do 
 Desk and Systematic Review: 
 Information Gathering: Identify information sources and develop search strategies using PubMed, Google Scholar, and websites of international organizations for food-based approaches (FBA) and related topics in malnutrition prevention.
 Material Review: Retrieve and systematically review gathered materials, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data from peer-reviewed journals using software such as SPSS and Excel.
 Synthesis and Documentation: Synthesize findings, assess source credibility, and document the review process comprehensively.
 Reporting: Communicate results effectively in a detailed report, including evidence, gaps, recommendations, and available tools.
 Conclusion and Recommendations: Conclude and provide actionable recommendations based on reviewed findings.
 Quantitative Data Analysis for PDH Program: 
 Data Cleaning: Clean quantitative data under the supervision of the Principal Investigator for the Positive Deviance/Hearth (PDH) program.
 Data Analysis Tools Utilization: Analyze data using SPSS and MS Excel to extract insights and identify trends.
 Findings Reporting: Report findings and trends derived from the data analysis process.
 Why Join Us 
 Exposure to Expert Guidance: Liaise with the Principal Investigator (PI)/Senior Technical Advisor (STA) for Nutrition to assist in desk and literature review on food-based approaches (FBA), infant and young child feeding counselling (IYCF), and behavior change approaches for malnutrition prevention.
 Active Participation in Project Teams: Participate in weekly calls/meetings with the STA for Nutrition and the FBA project team, gaining insights into ongoing research and project developments.
 Specialized Knowledge Acquisition: Increase knowledge in FBA, IYCF, and systematic review methodologies through practical involvement and learning sessions.
 Practical Application of Research Skills: Write a comprehensive report summarizing the systematic/desk review findings on FBA resources and publications. Analyze existing evidence, identify gaps, challenges, and formulate recommendations.
 Expand Your Horizons: Explore the international relief sector, unleash your leadership skills, and strengthen your Christian faith with Weekly Professional Development Sessions.
 Transform Lives: Take on challenging and meaningful work assignments while developing your technical skills and gaining valuable hands-on experience.
 Join an Inspiring Community: Form connections with a diverse nationwide intern cohort and colleagues who, inspired by their Christian faith, support children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places.
 What You’ll Bring: 
 Systematic and Desk Review Expertise: Experienced in conducting systematic and desk reviews of resources and tools in nutrition-related topics, proficient in literature search and data extraction.
 Quantitative Data Handling: Skilled in quantitative data analysis using SPSS or other statistical software, as well as MS Excel for synthesizing data across studies.
 Global Health and Nutrition Knowledge: Possess knowledge of global health and nutrition issues, including cultural sensitivity when collaborating with international staff, organizations, and academic partners.
 Effective Communication and Organization: Able to organize complex ideas into coherent written narratives. Demonstrates strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and effective time management abilities for independent and remote work environments.
 Responsibility and Enthusiasm: Responsible, responsive, and enthusiastic about using your God-given talents to positively impact the world.
 Commitment to our Mission: Demonstrated commitment to and alignment with the goals, mission, and vision of World Vision, embodying its values in all aspects of your work.

 Details 
 Location: Remote within the US . You must be physically located in one of the following states where WVI is registered as an employer: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia (Washington D.C.), Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Maryland, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and Washington.
 Appropriate Fields of Study/Majors: Master's in Public Health, Global Health, Nutritional Science, or related fields.
 Internship Cohort Dates : 25 January – 23 April 2027. 
 Stipend: This internship is unpaid, but all US-based interns receive a monthly stipend of $800.
 Hours: Full-time and part-time opportunities are available (20-40 hours/week)
 Eligibility 
 All candidates must meet the following requirements:
 At least 18 years of age.
 Must be legally authorized to work in the United States (e.g., U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or F-1 student visa holder with valid work authorization) and possess a valid U.S. Social Security Number.
 Able to commit to at least 20 hours per week for the entire internship period: 25 January – 23 April 2027. 
 Current student or recent graduate from a graduate programme (within 2 years).
 Adhere to World Vision International’s Christian Statement of Faith.
 Willingness to use own electronic devices for internship purposes and a disposition to let WVI install endpoint security software on those devices.

 Job Description: 
 World Vision International – Lao PDR (WVIL) is a partner of the UNICEF Child Nutrition Fund (CNF) initiative and in partnership with UNICEF and the Ministry of Health (MOH), aims to strengthen maternal and child nutrition services and reduce child waste in 15 districts of Savannakhet province. WVIL will work closely with Provincial and District Health Office, Health Center, Village Health Volunteer (VHVs) and communities to strengthen the prevention, early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition, improve maternal and child nutrition services including Multiple Micronutrient Supplementation (MMS), enhance preventive nutrition services, promote positive nutrition behaviors, and pilot innovative food-based solutions for complementary feeding and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) management.
 The Project is 33 months in duration and will focus on achieving the following expected outcomes and outputs:
 -         Strengthened quality and coverage of Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM/CMAM) services through improved community screening, referral, treatment, follow-up and supportive supervision systems.
 -         Improved access to and utilization of maternal nutrition services, including maternal nutrition counselling, weight gain monitoring, IFA and MMS for pregnant and lactating women.
 -         Improved access to and utilization of integrated preventive nutrition services, including maternal nutrition, Growth Monitoring and Promotion (GMP), Vitamin A supplementation, deworming, breastfeeding support and MIYCN counselling for pregnant women, caregivers and children under five.
 -         Strengthened capacity of health workers, Village Health Volunteers and local authorities through training, coaching, mentoring and supportive supervision on nutrition service delivery and acute malnutrition management.
 -         Improved caregiver knowledge and practices on infant and young child feeding, dietary diversity, complementary feeding and care-seeking behaviors through Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) interventions
 -         Increased adoption of innovative food-based solutions, complementary feeding approaches and locally available nutritious foods for prevention and treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM).
 -         Strengthened coordination, monitoring, evidence generation and learning system to support sustainable nutrition programming and improved nutrition outcomes in target communities.

 Overview 
 VisionFund Rwanda   is a Christian owner-operated mission-driven microfinance network working with caregivers in hard to reach, impoverished locations so they can create secure futures for their children. Inspired by Christian values, we are dedicated to working with the most vulnerable families and communities regardless of religion, race, ethnicity gender, to create lasting change in their lives.
 VisionFund serves low-income clients living in vulnerable and rural communities by offering financial and livelihood solutions, delivered through our Network, World Vision and partners; empowering families to create income and jobs; and unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive. The products and services offered fall into five broad categories: microloans, savings programmes, microinsurance, training and education. Benefits include sustainable livelihoods, increased economic well-being, improved community well-being, decreased dependence on outside aid and restoration of hope and dignity. Together with World Vision, we are focused on ending extreme poverty by 2030.
 The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide strategic, financial, operational, and transformational leadership to VisionFund Rwanda (VFR), driving sustainable growth, institutional resilience, and increased impact among vulnerable families and communities. The CEO will lead the transformation of VFR into a high-performing, commercially driven, customer-centric, and sustainable deposit-taking microfinance institution. A key priority will be shifting the organization from a traditional NGO mindset to a performance-oriented culture that balances strong financial results with social impact and Christian values.
 The role is accountable for achieving sustainable portfolio growth, deposit mobilization, profitability, and operational excellence. The CEO will strengthen VFR's funding structure by growing low-cost customer deposits, diversifying funding sources, reducing the cost of capital, and building strategic partnerships with donors, investors, and financial institutions.

 Please note: Our Global Technical Expertise Roster connects skilled professionals with opportunities to support humanitarian responses and long-term development programmes. Through the roster, we mobilise technical expertise to help protect lives, strengthen communities and contribute to sustainable recovery and development. 
 By applying to join the roster, you are expressing an interest in being considered for future positions, deployments or consultancy opportunities linked to humanitarian responses, development programmes and donor-funded initiatives. 
 Joining the roster does not constitute an offer of employment or guarantee an immediate opportunity. It means that your technical expertise may be considered, and you may be contacted when a suitable opportunity becomes available. 
 As this is not recruitment for a current vacancy, the review and selection process may take longer, particularly where there is no immediate opportunity linked to the roster advertisement.
 Here's where you come in: 
 World Vision International maintains a roster of qualified specialists to provide flexible, on-demand technical assistance for nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive programming across development, fragile and humanitarian settings. Specialists support World Vision offices, governments and partners to assess nutrition needs, design and strengthen high-quality programmes, respond to emergencies, and generate actionable evidence. Assignments are matched to each consultant’s demonstrated technical expertise and specific terms of reference.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Global nutrition programming and systems strengthening
 Provide assignment-specific technical advice for programme design, implementation, costing, monitoring, evaluation and adaptation.
 Support maternal, infant, young child, adolescent and women’s nutrition, micronutrient interventions, food systems and fortification, social behaviour change programming, food-based approaches, and nutrition-sensitive programming for prevention and treatment of undernutrition.
 Strengthen integration of nutrition within health systems, agriculture, food systems, social protection and other multisectoral platforms.
 Contribute to nutrition policy, governance, financing, investment cases, advocacy and resource mobilization; prepare technical inputs to proposals, budgets and donor reports.
 Develop technical guidance, training materials, operational tools and knowledge products; mentor World Vision staff, government counterparts and community partners.
 Emergency nutrition preparedness and response
 Support rapid nutrition assessments and evidence-based response strategies for disasters, conflict, displacement and disease outbreaks.
 Design, adapt and provide technical oversight for community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), including outpatient and inpatient care, and targeted or blanket supplementary feeding as appropriate.
 Provide technical guidance on infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E), breastfeeding protection, micronutrient interventions and links to food assistance.
 Strengthen emergency nutrition surveillance, monitoring, situation reporting and coordination in line with Sphere standards and applicable humanitarian guidance.
 Represent World Vision in government, nutrition cluster/sector and inter-agency coordination mechanisms; support response proposals, logframes, budgets and after-action reviews.
 Nutrition assessment, analysis and evidence
 Design, conduct or supervise population-based nutrition assessments, including SMART, coverage and IYCF surveys, as relevant to the assignment.
 Conduct or support qualitative and causal assessments, including KAP studies, Barrier Analysis, Link NCA and Cost of Diet analyses.
 Develop protocols, sampling frames and data-collection tools; train and supervise enumerators and manage field survey quality assurance.
 Oversee data cleaning and analysis of anthropometric indices, prevalence estimates and confidence intervals; interpret routine data from HMIS/DHIS2 and other surveillance systems.
 Produce clear assessment reports and actionable recommendations; communicate findings to programmes, governments, donors and coordination partners.
 Cross-cutting accountabilities
 Integrate gender equality, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), disability inclusion, child protection and safeguarding considerations throughout assignments.
 Manage agreed deliverables, budgets, timelines and field logistics, and provide timely progress updates.
 Ensure technical work aligns with relevant national protocols, international standards and World Vision policies.
 Areas of Technical Expertise for Roster Matching 
 Applicants may identify one or more areas of demonstrated specialization:
 Multisectoral nutrition, health and food systems strengthening; nutrition-sensitive agriculture and social protection
 Maternal, infant and young child nutrition; adolescent and women’s nutrition; micronutrients and fortification; food-based approaches; nutrition social behaviour change programming; Positive Deviance/Hearth (PDH)
 Nutrition policy, governance, financing, investment cases, implementation research and programme evaluation
 Emergency nutrition, CMAM, IYCF-E, supplementary feeding, humanitarian coordination and surge response
 Nutrition surveys, SMART/coverage/IYCF assessments, qualitative and causal analysis, and Cost of Diet
 Nutrition information systems, HMIS/DHIS2, surveillance, data quality and statistical analysis
 Gender equality and social inclusion; private-sector engagement and capacity strengthening
 Required Qualifications and Experience 
 Advanced university degree in nutrition, public health, epidemiology, statistics, food science, development studies or a related field; a bachelor’s degree with substantial additional relevant experience may be considered for appropriate assignments.
 Typically at least 5 years of progressive experience in nutrition or nutrition-sensitive programming for global technical assistance assignments; emergency nutrition and assessment-focused assignments may consider candidates with at least 5 years of directly relevant experience.
 Demonstrated technical depth and successful deliverables in at least one roster specialty, such as programme designs, assessment reports, evaluations, publications or guidance materials.
 Relevant experience in low- and middle-income countries, working with governments, international NGOs, multilateral organizations, local partners and/or donors.
 Strong analytical, technical writing, communication, cross-cultural collaboration and project management skills.
 For emergency deployments: demonstrated humanitarian experience, familiarity with Sphere and applicable IYCF-E guidance, and ability to work in rapidly changing or hardship settings.
 For survey assignments: relevant training and experience in population-based survey design, implementation, quality assurance and analysis.
 Professional proficiency in English, French, Spanish, Portuguese and/or Arabic as required by the assignment.
 Additional Requirements for only Specialized SMART Survey Assignments 
 For the dedicated SMART survey roster track, applicants must document at least five validated SMART surveys and five SMART consultancy assignments, with reports available for review; SMART training certification with distinction; and recommendation letters from at least two organizations where they managed SMART surveys.  Job Description: 
 The Project Engineer oversees the overall aspect of an assigned project, including planning. Budgeting, procurement, monitoring, and final evaluation. He/she will directly coordinate with the supervisor, project heads, and local government unit ensuring any renovations and constructions are of quality in accordance to the standard building code. He/she will also conduct a regular on site monitoring within the project areas.
 This is a fixed-term post for two years based in Tacloban City.
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Plan, Design and Budget 
 Coordinate with the project team to plan, design and allocate the budget the construction and renovation works based on the project implementation plan and the given budget.
 Lead the whole process related to the construction, renovation and even repair under the supervisor or project head like project director, project manager in collaboration with the field team.
 Ensure that all documentary requirements are completed.
 Regular and Final Evaluation Site Visits and Monitoring 
 Regular site visits to monitor and ensure the contract is implementing all the activities based on the agreement and plan. 
 Provide the technical support to the field team by all means to ensure that all works are properly completed.
 Make final evaluation with the engineer from partner LGU and support the issuance of certificate from LGU.
 Support Procurement Process  
 Produce the essential document such as work plan or other important internal documents to initiate the procurement process.
 Provide the technical support to the procurement team and procurement committee with integrity to find the best contractor for the given construction activities.
 Stakeholder Coordination 
 Closely coordinate with LGU and field team to fully fill the need of the community and LGU (from the design to the final completion).
 Respond to communication inquiries and concerns from the local partners.
 Direct and supervise the ongoing construction as described in the work plan.
 Support Regular Payment Processing 
 Make a internal document to confirm that each phase was completed based on the plan to facilitate the payment process.
 Make a regular monitoring report (or site visit report) to the supervisor or project (program) head based on the agreement.
 Organizational Contribution 
 Perform other related duties as instructed by project heads.

 Bachelor's Degree in Construction or Related Engineering Fields.
 Licensed Engineer (PRC license with a practice focus on construction execution).
 At least three years of job experience in construction project sites and related fields.

 Deeply familiar with the environment, geography, and local conditions of Eastern, Central, and Western Visayas.
 Willingness to travel frequently within Eastern Visayas and to Western/Central Visayas based on project site needs.
 High level of integrity, strong work ethics, and excellent communication skills.
 Related training or certifications (preferred, e.g., COSH/BOSH safety training, Project Management professional certifications).

 Key Responsibilities: 
 Position:           Community Development Facilitator 
 Location:          Sambour ADP, Kratie Province 
 Salary:               Negotiation 
 Closing Date:   30-November - 2026 
 POSITION DESCRIPTION: 
 To facilitate and implement the Technical Programmes using the WVIC development programme approach to enhance community participation, ownership and sustainability of projects for the wellbeing of children, families and communities.
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES 
 I. Promote Local Ownership & Effective Partnership: 
 Identify and assess the potential partner such as (CBO, Private sector, CSO) and work together to improve the CWB.
 Facilitate the local partner to develop a shared project for CWB (short/long term as agreed with partners)
 Support local level partners to identify needs and their underlying causes; and recognizing local assets and resources which could support them in meeting these needs, mobilize these in programme implementation
 Assess capacity gaps of partner and provide capacity Building, ongoing coaching, mentoring to partner.
 Work with local partners, implement the joint/ shared plan, and Initiate reflection, learning actions, which contribute to promote community ownership and local partnering.
 undefined
 II. Technical Project Implementation 
 Support the area team to make appropriate AP planning that reflect community identified priorities for child well-being in the area.
 Implement the technical project log-frame within the agreed design and budget.
 Work with AP Manager & TPO to identify and mitigate risks/issues to ensure quality implementation of technical project models.
 Lead reflection and learning of technical project models implementation for ongoing feedback and improvement with key project partners and stakeholders.

offres.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.
Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
 Employee Contract Type: 
Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term) 
 Job Description: 
 Contexte : 
 World Vision République démocratique du Congo (WVDRC) intervient dans 13 des 26 provinces de la RDC. Fondée dans les années 1980 en tant qu'organisation d'aide d'urgence, WVDRC est devenue l'une des plus importantes ONG internationales du pays, œuvrant pour le développement transformateur, l'aide humanitaire et le plaidoyer en faveur du bien-être des enfants et de leurs familles. Malgré ses abondantes ressources naturelles, des décennies d'exploitation et de mauvaise gouvernance en RDC ont engendré des conflits violents et prolongés pour le pouvoir politique et les ressources. De ce fait, 73,5 % des quelque 112,8 millions de Congolais vivent dans l'extrême pauvreté avec moins de 2,15 dollars par jour.
 En 2026, l'effectif total de World Vision RDC était d'environ 500 personnes. Ses principaux domaines d'intervention sont l'éducation, la protection de l'enfance, l'eau, l'assainissement et l'hygiène (WASH), la résilience et les moyens de subsistance, la santé et la nutrition, ainsi que l'aide d'urgence. Des programmes de développement à long terme et d'urgence sont mis en œuvre dans les 13 provinces où WV est présente, réparties en 3 grandes régions ou zones : Est, Ouest et Sud. Parmi les principaux donateurs figurent le Département d'État, les agences des Nations Unies (PAM, UNICEF, UNOCHA), le FCDO, l'UE, l'Alliance néerlandaise de secours, le Rotary, le DFAT (ANCP), l'ADH, ENABEL, le PNUD (projet du Fonds mondial), ECW.
 World Vision recrute Un(E) (01) Child Well-being Tracking Officer, basé(e) à Kinshasa / Ngandu. 
 Description du poste : 
 Soutenir la maximisation de la contribution au bien-être des enfants en mettant en place
 des mécanismes et des normes de gestion des connaissances, en analysant et en améliorant les processus opérationnels de programmation, en soutenant la contextualisation et la mise en œuvre de nouvelles initiatives et en promouvant
 l'apprentissage et l’innovation.
 Principales responsabilités : 
 I. Gestion des systèmes Horizon et stockage des données 
 S'assure qu’Horizon est mis à jour pour tous les ADP et que les informations sont partagées pour la prise de décision.
 Suit régulièrement les mises à jour du système / de l'application et met à niveau le système en conséquence.
 Prend en charge l'équipe AP pour créer un profil, entrer / entrer, télécharger DIP, etc. dans l'application Horizon.
 II. Gestion du système de parrainage et de ses performances 
 Surveille la sécurité et la gestion des risques en ce qui concerne les systèmes d'information et de parrainage des enfants.
 Saisie des données / informations sur le parrainage d'enfants et des communications SO par le biais de la saisie manuelle, de la numérisation des formulaires, de la modification, de la vérification, de la validation et du chargement des informations sur les enfants dans Horizon
 Génère tous les rapports du système tels que la gestion des SSUI, les formulaires de correspondance des enfants, le rapport de correspondance détaillé et l'exportation des formulaires de validation pour les programmes régionaux.
 Effectue des mises à niveau des systèmes et assure l'exécution des points d'accès sur les versions actuelles.
 Traite toute la correspondance dans Horizon SSUI, le cas échéant.
 Maintient la sécurité des données de parrainage, des ressources des systèmes et des adresses des sponsors.
 Entre les données de surveillance des enfants à l'aide d'Horizon.
 Assure la mise en œuvre de tous les systèmes de parrainage et des auditeurs de support logiciel en fournissant des informations d’audit lors des audits du programme régional.
 III. Identifier / saisir et diffuser les connaissances 
 Travaille avec le facilitateur de la CWB pour saisir / documenter les leçons, les meilleures pratiques et les innovations et s'assurer qu'elles sont partagées dans les rapports annuels, semestriels, de la CWB et toute autre communication pertinente aux parties prenantes.
 Assure un échange et un partage efficaces des informations entre les programmes, l'équipe de communication et le DME pour une gestion efficace des connaissances.
 IV. Prise en charge d'autres processus DME 
 Examine les bases de données de suivi et d'évaluation des grappes et les rapports trimestriels pour garantir la qualité, l'exhaustivité et la ponctualité, et partage le rapport de situation avec le superviseur et les gestionnaires de grappe pour suite à donner.
 Met à jour et gère la base de données du S&E du cluster, établit les tendances de performance et partage les rapports trimestriels avec le superviseur et les gestionnaires de cluster.
 Trace les principaux processus opérationnels de programmation dans le cluster et les programmes, et participe au processus de leur analyse et de leur amélioration.
 Fournit un soutien à l'équipe du cluster pendant le processus de conception, afin d'assurer un processus et des conseils de qualité.
 Participe aux rapports du CWBT en utilisant les informations pertinentes, telles que les données de suivi des résultats et des extrants, ainsi que les innovations et les enseignements tirés.
 Qualifications et compétences requises 
 Le titulaire de ce poste doit posséder la qualification suivante qui peut être acquise grâce à une combinaison de formation formelle ou autonome, d'expérience antérieure ou de formation en cours d'emploi.
   Minimum un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle en IT ou domaines similaires Avoir au minimum deux ans d’expérience professionnelle dans le poste similaire 
 Avoir une connaissance minimum des normes de qualité du système de gestion de parrainage est un atout 
 Très bonnes compétences informatiques, notamment MS office, Excel, Word, Internet et PowerPoint. 
 La connaissance des progiciels statistiques sera un avantage supplémentaire Bonnes capacités d'analyse et d’écriture ; 
 Compréhension de base de la conception, du suivi et de l'évaluation. 
 Bonnes capacités d'analyse des données et de reporting Connaissance des SIG, utilisation de la technologie mobile pour la collecte et l'analyse des données, la méthodologie LQAS et toute autre technologie pertinente 
 Connaissances de base sur le fonctionnement et l'utilisation efficace des appareils Mobiles 
 Une bonne maîtrise du français et de l’anglais est obligatoire pour ce poste Capacité de travailler sans supervision et sous pressions 
 Aptitude d’apprendre les nouvelles initiatives et auto-formation Habileté à travailler sur terrain Capacité démontrée à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel.

 Envoyer votre dossier de candidature (lettre de motivation portant mention du numéro de l’offre, CV avec 3 personnes de références des employeurs précédents dont une référence ecclésiastique, le casier judiciaire, une copie carte de demandeur d’emploi délivré par l’ONEM et des copies des autres documents nécessaires pouvant appuyer votre dossier adressé au Directeur des Ressources Humaines au plus tard le 26 novembre 2026 avec en objet la mention « Child Well-being Tracking Officer _ Kinshasa/Ngandu »

offres.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.
Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
 Employee Contract Type: 
Local - Fixed Term Employee (durée déterminée) 
 Job Description: 
 Responsabilités Majeure 
 1. Visiter les sites, les écoles, les centres et village des bénéficiaires du programme alimentaire pour s’assurer que les règlements de l’assistance de WV sont respectés, puis les assister dans la gestion de vivres et dans les distributions.
 2. Suivre les dispatches, les réceptions et les distributions des vivres et non vivres au niveau des sites, écoles et centres de santé en veillant au remplissage des formulaires exigés pour la distribution de ces vivres/non vivres.
 3. Produire des rapports mensuels après chaque distribution et soumettre aux FAIRO puis au Field Coordinator dans les délais pour vérification et approbation. (au plus tard le 3 du mois qui suit)
 4. Rédiger des rapports hebdomadaires, trimestriel des visites et supervisions de sites/Village, écoles ou centre de façon précise et fidèle et laisser un document écrit de la visite sur les observations et recommandations des actions à entreprendre.
 5. S’assurer que tous les documents de rapport produit sont classé et aux complets.
 6. En collaboration avec les partenaires sur terrain, s’assurer que les réceptions des vivres / non vivres sont régulièrement bien effectue par le respect des procédures.
 7. En collaboration avec Field Coordinator organiser les distributions en élaborant un le plan de distribution en respectant la ration prévue pour chaque bénéficiaire et qui respecte aussi le calendrier des activités du mois.
 9. Proposer des solutions aux problèmes et sont apportées à l’intention du superviseur direct.
 Consulter son superviseur pour tous les problèmes qui demandent une visite de suivi.
 Effectuer des visites de suivi sur demande du superviseur.
 10. Tenir des réunions périodiques pour expliquer le projet et les objectifs aux bénéficiaires et personnes intéressées et produire un compte rendu de la rencontre à son superviseur.
 Tenir au besoin des réunions de formation et d’informations avec les responsables des sites/villages, écoles et centres de santé.
 11. Participer au contrôle de déchargement des vivres dans le site avant ou pendant la distribution, dans les écoles et centre de santé.
 Informer les bénéficiaires de la provenance des vivres et de la ration qu’ils doivent recevoir.
 Transmettre en temps et clairement les informations demandées par son superviseur et a son hiérarchie.
 12. Aider tout bénéficiaire qui vient au site ou bureau pour demander de l’aide ou explications.
 13. Sensibiliser et impliquer la communauté à travers des comités (relais) dans l’appropriation du projet – ex : contributions dans la gestion du projet, le déchargement des vivres et non vivres dans les délais, participer dans la réhabilitation des infrastructures sanitaires.
 14. S’assurer que les procédures de gestion et rapportage des vivres PERDUS OU ENDOMMAGES sont bien rapportés avec le format approprié.
 15. Engager activement la communauté pour la promotion de l’hygiène, de la santé, de la sécurité alimentaire et la protection de l’enfance et de l’environnement.
 16. Assister à la planification et participer aux réunions hebdomadaires, mensuel ou de recyclage du Monitoring.
 Assister les superviseurs et le staff de DM&E dans la collecte des données sur les plaintes lors d’une distribution et faire le classement de tous les documents.
 17. Accompagner les Représentants de WVI et les bailleurs lors de leur visite des sites.
 Accompagner, orienter les agents aux cours de visites conjointes sur le terrain, pour les initier aux tâches de contrôle.
 18. Participer à l’inventaire physique des dépôts ou magasin des écoles.
 19. Remplir au besoin toute autre tâche relative à son niveau à l’intérieur de l’organisation sous la demande de la direction de WV pour le bénéfice de l’organisation.
 20. Prendre soin des biens de l’organisation que vous utilisez pour votre travail et signaler toute perte ou dommage de ce bien à la hiérarchie directement après et faire un rapport d’incident pour justifier le fait (la perte).
 Qualifications : Education/connaissances /compétences techniques et de l'expérience 
 Diplôme de graduation ou équivalent dans des domaines comme la gestion, les sciences sociales, le développement communautaire, la Nutrition,
 Expérience : Avoir au minimum deux ans de travail de terrain.
 Préférence : Expérience de travail dans le domaine humanitaire et précisément dans la distribution des vivres, Cash et non vivres.
 Autres Compétences (Attributs) : 
 Capacité de travailler en équipe ;
 Avoir un permis de conduire d'une motocyclette ;
 Avoir une expérience de travail dans un environnement stressant et exigent ;
 Expérience de travail avec des ONGs et en particulier World Vision constitue un avantage ;
 Aptitudes d’écrire et de parler le Français.
 Connaissance de l’anglais et de l’utilisation de l’outil informatique constitue un plus.
 Être capable de travailler sous pression avec un minimum de supervision ;
 Avoir d’excellentes aptitudes interpersonnelles et de bonne moralité ;
 Comment postuler 
 Tout candidat souhaitant postuler doit soumettre sa candidature sur le site de World Vision International : www.wvi.org , en utilisant une adresse e-mail valide. Toutes les communications relatives au processus de recrutement se feront via la plateforme en ligne.
 Veuillez utiliser votre adresse e-mail comme nom d'utilisateur (Username) lors de la création de votre compte et choisir un mot de passe que vous devrez conserver pendant toute la durée du processus de recrutement.
 Pour postuler à ce poste, veuillez cliquer sur le lien de candidature et joindre les documents suivants : Un curriculum vitae (CV) à jour ;
 Une copie de votre carte nationale d'identité ;
 Les copies de vos diplômes ;
 Les certificats de travail ou attestations d'emploi pertinents.
 NB : Assurez-vous que tous les documents soumis sont lisibles et à jour afin de faciliter le traitement de votre candidature.
 Applicant Types Accepted: 
Local Applicants Only

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.
 Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Purpose of the position 
 The Risk and Compliance Manager will be responsible for World Vision International Central African Republic’s overall risk and compliance management and works cross-functionally and collaboratively to achieve the objectives of WV CAR’s Response Strategy. The Risk and Compliance Manager will be expected to understand and evaluate WV CAR’s unique organizational and operating environment, and apply a deep understanding of technical risk and compliance principles to develop an effective compliance function and culture. 
 The responsibilities of the Risk and Compliance Manager include the identification, analysis and management of risks that impact the delivery of mandates and strategic objectives. He/She will advise on and ensure the implementation of risk mitigation measures to minimize WVI Central African Republic’s risk. The incumbent will also ensure compliance with policies, procedures and standards and facilitate the alignment of risk management with internal control measures.
 This post will plan and design appropriate tools to strategically review World Vision’s operations and Support Services periodically to determine risk levels, propose strategies and systems to minimize risks and effectively track progress in the implementation of recommendations that will reduce or eliminate risks.
 The incumbent will be based in the CAR capital city, Bangui, and will report the Response Country Director 
 Major Responsibilities: 
 Development and Management of Enterprise Risk Management Framework 
 Define World Vision’s enterprise risk management framework and establish guidelines for the development and implementation of relevant partnership policies and procedures.
 Champion the design, implementation and review of WVI Central African Republic’s risk policy and framework.
 Carry out compliance checks & risk assessments.
 Support the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) in the implementation, review, monitoring and approval of the enterprise risk framework which includes the organization’s risk culture, risk appetite and risk limits.
 Implementation of Risk Management Processes and Practice 20% 
 Incorporate risk considerations into strategic decision-making and ensure alignment between Response Office strategy and WVI Central African Republic’s risk policy.
 Manage the implementation of all aspects of the risk function, including implementation of processes, tools and systems (such as Riskonnect and ICMT) to identify, assess, measure, manage, monitor and report risks.
 Manage corporate risk and control processes.
 Communicate risk management policies, risk appetite and risk limits across all levels of WVI Central African Republic.
 Review and provide feedback on the adequacy of WVI Central African Republic risk management and controls.
 Build a Culture of Risk Awareness in Program and Project Management 
 Work with the Response Director (RD) and SLT to ensure all programs and projects incorporate risk management in design.
 Conduct organization-wide training and awareness sessions on internal controls, policies and risk management plans; and establish and maintain risk awareness culture within WVI Central African Republic, and provide appropriate opportunities for organizational learning, including lessons learned from previous problems, ongoing communication, training and development
 Verify and report the organization’s ability to consistently comply with standards, policies and procedures especially in Grants and PNS; and innovate to increase the efficiency of Grant management.
 Evaluate risk management in WVI Central African Republic annually and recommend appropriate actions to manage risks.
 Work with unit leads to popularize internal and external policies that are relevant to WVI Central African Republic’s operations and strategy realization.
 Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Reporting 
 Lead monitoring and reporting of significant deficiencies and weaknesses in internal control and ensure that appropriate remedial action is taken to reduce or eliminate the risks.
 Undertake bi-annual risk evaluations, which involves comparing estimated risks with criteria established by the organization such as costs, legal requirements and environmental factors, and evaluate the organization’s previous handling of risks.
  Develop a dashboard for tracking risk compliance and implementation of the organizational effectiveness and audit recommendations for Projects and the Response Office.
 Conduct special reviews & investigations as may be directed by the SLT and ensure that internal controls are developed and implemented by various departments, Grants, PNS, Zonal Offices and Response Office.
 Audit Support 
 Verify on a quarterly basis that the Global and Internal Audit recommendations are being implemented within the agreed timelines and report on progress to WVI Central African Republic’s management.
 Ensure that work practices follow the Institute of Internal Auditors Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing (SPPIA), the US Government Generally Accepted Auditing Standards (GAGAS) for US Government Funding and World Vision’s Financial Manual Internal Audit policies and procedures.
 Participate and serve as the Secretary in the Audit Committee meetings to enhance World Vision risk management.
 Incident and Investigation Management 
 Evaluate and analyse new whistle-blower reports when received in accordance with WVI recommended criteria; conduct and advise on whistle-blower investigations; coordinate and lead evaluation; ensure ultimate accountability on conclusions and follow through by line management.
 Ensure investigations are conducted by qualified personnel and in alignment with policies.
 Requirements: 
 Master' s Degree in Business Administration, Management, Risk Management, Finance, Accounting, Political Science, Law, or any related field.
 Professional Certifications: e.g. CPA, CA, CIA, CISA, or equivalent
 A minimum of seven (7) years of progressive responsibility in relief and development programs
 Experience in Auditing, Public Administration, Organizational Development, operations management, research, and or equivalent.
 Experience in working for INGOs in a fragile context
 Experience in designing Risk Frameworks and proposing Risk Treatment Plans
 Applicant Types Accepted: 
Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted
 World Vision is a Christian humanitarian organisation with a mission centred on following Jesus Christ in service to the world´s most vulnerable children. Therefore, in all locations to the fullest extent legally permissible, the successful applicant will affirm our core documents, observe conduct compatible with Christian principles, serve at a high level of professional ethics and strive to act in accordance with cultural sensitivities. Furthermore, regular attendance with team and office devotions, chapel and prayer gatherings are expected in line with policies in the World Vision host location and its departments.
