 Key Responsibilities: 
 The Monitoring, Evaluation Accountability & Learning will lead monitoring and evaluation of program results at all levels (impact, outcome, output, process and input) are measured to provide basis for accountability and informed decision making at both program and policy level. This includes performance framework, a legal document through which World Vision and Global Fund commonly agree on the indicators to be used and the targets to be achieved to demonstrate performance and consequently ensure continued funding. The M&E system should allow for data to be collected, processed, and transformed into strategic information to allow for informed decision-making at all levels; local, country, and global level. 
 The Monitoring and Evaluation Team Leader will bring significant experience and fresh ideas to MEAL system implementation, review and evaluations, MEAL budgeting, and recruitment. The Team Leader will ensure that all World Vision International CAR and Sub Recipients are supported to ensure the quality, effectiveness, and appropriateness of various Global Fund interventions. The Team Leader will promote a learning culture in the Global Fund Program and communicate this information to the Global Fund, relevant Ministry of Health disease programs (Malaria, HIV and Tuberculosis) and other audiences to improve ongoing and future programming.
 Key Job Responsibilities: 
 (a) Establish and operationalize a robust Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning system 
 Develop and update a costed M&E work plan using an appropriate template. The work plan should cover at least one or two years. This should include the cost of the impact/outcome measurement framework, including costs for each activity regardless of frequency (one-time or routine).
 Work with GF and MOH staff to finalize indicator definitions and measurements by ensuring that the M&E plan includes a table presenting all indicators for which data are collected by the national disease program or by the Principal Recipient, depending on the performance framework approved by the Global Fund.
 Put in place a system/plan to collect data for measuring impact/outcome indicators and programmatic indicators.
 Design and roll out a data management system that promotes interoperability and/or triangulation of programmatic data to facilitate monitoring across disease programs
 Ensure that data management (data collection, storage, processing, and analysis) is appropriately done in order to generate the reports at national and district level
 Develop and operationalize an information dissemination strategy that ensures exchange of feedback and information to the community and facility level as well as national and international stakeholders
 Ensure that data is collected, analysed and used to inform decision-making and increase efficiency and effectiveness of the program through a periodic report according to the Global Fund requirements.
 Lead the roll out of the CommCare application to support routine data collection
 Ensure that the M&E plan demonstrates coordinated governance arrangements, data flow and data sharing and harmonized supervision.
 Establish and roll out programme accountability mechanisms that promote provision of information, consultation and participation of participants including KPs and collection and acting on complaints and feedback.
 Engage MOH DPPI unit, disease programs and sub national units to ensure that data sharing and learning practices are harmonized
 Network with external and internal partners to promote a culture of learning and achieve M&E excellence
 Support the Sub Grantees to conduct routine learning forums
 (b) Data Quality Assurance 
 Develop data quality assessment protocols
 Develop and operationalize data quality assurance mechanisms that ensure quality of data during data collection, transfer, compilation, analysis and storage. This mechanism should include how late, missing, and incomplete data is accounted for.
 Carry out routine data quality assurance to mitigate risks of data manipulation, misreporting, and other data-integrity issues.” in relation to program targets and service delivery. This may include organizing internal data quality audits.
 Develop improvement plans for data quality, reporting completeness and/or timeliness (people, systems, processes, tools to review and suggest improvements)
 Put in place mechanisms to ensure data security, including cybersecurity, storage, transmission, and use. This includes, but is not limited to, data protection, confidentiality, access controls, and secure data management, in coordination with the IT/security function
 (c) Capacity Building 
 Assess M&E capacity of grant, Sub Recipient and implementing staff and develop capacity building plan so as to improve the M&E human resource capacity over the plan’s life span
 Plan and roll out training for Global Fund grants staff, Sub Recipients and implementing partners to strengthen MEAL capacity.
 Provide appropriate mentoring, coaching, and supervision in order to equip, motivate, and empower grant M&E staff, sub-recipients, and implementing partners.
 Guide staff and sub-grantees to identify and resolve issues and challenges in monitoring systems, using an ongoing mentorship and coaching approach
 (d) Program Review, Evaluation, and Surveys 
 Supervise the program’s overall performance, cost-effectiveness, and impact by doing program reviews, evaluations, and surveys according to the norms and requirements of the Global Fund and provide data for decision-making
 Coordinate the PR’s support to the planning and execution of national HIV, TB, and malaria surveys and studies according to internationally agreed guidelines/standard protocols (Stigma Index Surveys, Drug Resistance Studies, TB prevalence surveys and Malaria Indicator Survey)
 Consolidate national and sub-national population size estimates to be used to inform programming (obtain reliable coverage estimates, identify population in need of routine services or targeted programs for key populations)
 Support execution of regular national analyses of sub-national, disaggregated data as well as regular analyses at the provincial and district levels to inform planning and/or programmatic decisions
 Conduct or contribute to relevant analyses to inform resource mapping, stratification, optimization, intervention targeting and efficient deployment of resources
 Ensure ethical collection and protection of data, including privacy, confidentiality, access to health information, and data protection.
 (e) Reporting 
 Compile periodic reports for each Global Fund component (Malaria, HIV, TB, RSSH), facilitate review and submission to GF
 Review reports from sub-recipients and implementing partners and provide feedback
 Build capacity of the PR2 staff, sub-recipients, and implementing staff on quality reporting
 Prepare MMRs and submit to Chief of Party
 Lead integration of HMIS data systems used by World Vision (CommCare) and MOH (disease-specific HMIS, community data systems, private health sector data) to facilitate seamless reporting
 Ensures that all reports are accurate, complete, consistent, and timely
 Systematic monitoring of SR indicator performance, reporting timeliness, data quality, and implementation of corrective actions.
 Required Professional Experience, Knowledge, and Qualifications for the role: 
 Must have 5 -7 years of progressive relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation in the public health sector, epidemiological literacy, and surveillance.

 Job Description: 
 Position Purpose: 
 The coordinator – MEAL, based in Cox’s Bazar and reporting to the National Office PQA function, leads quality monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning and information management across the Bangladesh Rohingya Crisis Response. Working closely with the Deputy Response Director, sector teams and partners, the role strengthens MEAL systems, data quality, community feedback, assessments and donor reporting; supports evidence-based decisions; and ensures response approaches align with organizational and humanitarian accountability standards. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 MEAL systems, project design, data management, quality assurance and performance reporting: 
 Support sector teams and partners to develop and review proposals, theories of change, logframes, results frameworks, indicators, MEAL plans and budgets in line with donor requirements and World Vision standards. 
 Coordinate the development and consistent application of BRCR MEAL strategies, protocols, tools, data flows and reporting procedures with technical guidance from National Office PQA/DMEAL. 
 Coordinate use of approved digital systems, including DMIS, Horizon, iMPAQ and WV Relief, as applicable to each project, for data entry, validation, consolidation, indicator monitoring and reporting. 
 Ensure secure and ethical management of response data, including appropriate access, confidentiality, protection of personal information and responsible handling of sensitive refugee-related records. 
 Establish data quality assurance plans; conduct routine validation, field verification, data quality assessments and audits; document discrepancies and follow up corrective action. 
 Coordinate baseline and endline assessments, PDM, evaluations, needs assessments and operational studies with technically sound methods, appropriate disaggregation and safeguards. 
 Analyse quantitative and qualitative monitoring data against agreed targets; develop accessible dashboards, indicator trackers and management briefs identifying trends, gaps and risks. 
 Consolidate and quality-check periodic, donor-required and National Office MEAL reports, ensuring timely sharing with BRCR sector leads, the Deputy Response Director and National Office PQA. 
 Facilitate performance review and after-action learning with sector teams and partners; document findings, success and failure stories, lessons and recommendations for adaptive programming. 
 Maintain regular technical coordination with National Office PQA/DMEAL on standards, system issues, monitoring quality, reporting obligations and improvement priorities. 
 MEAL capacity building, technical support and organisational learning: 
 Conduct MEAL competency and capacity gap assessments jointly with BRCR sector teams, partners and National Office PQA, and develop targeted support plans. 
 Organise practical training, blended learning, field mentoring and coaching on project logic, indicator tracking, sampling, monitoring, evaluation, accountability, reporting and data quality. 
 Coach staff and partners on data collection, verification, analysis, outcome measurement and interpretation for evidence-based programme management. 
 Strengthen skills in the approved use of DMIS, Horizon, iMPAQ and WV Relief, as applicable, together with relevant digital data collection and analysis tools. 
 Clarify MEAL roles, reporting responsibilities and data quality expectations for project personnel, enumerators and implementing partners. 
 Promote common tools, harmonised methods, peer learning and sharing of lessons across BRCR sectors and partners in line with National Office standards. 
 Update relevant stakeholders on new MEAL processes, technical guidance, data protection responsibilities and system developments. 
 Community-led monitoring, participation and accountability 
 Strengthen participatory, accessible and context-sensitive community-led monitoring across Rohingya refugee and host-community programmes. 
 Collect, analyse and share community monitoring findings to improve the relevance, quality and responsiveness of current and future projects. 
 Communicate relevant project designs, monitoring findings and MEAL plans with communities, sectoral working groups and partners in appropriate languages and formats. 
 Monitor applicable Humanitarian Accountability Framework (HAF), participation, transparency and feedback indicators as part of routine project tracking. 
 Coordinate with accountability staff to maintain simple, secure records of community monitoring issues, referrals and follow-up actions. 
 Analyse disaggregated feedback trends and participation barriers, including issues affecting women, children, persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups. 
 Engage with relevant inter-agency accountability and community engagement coordination mechanisms within delegated responsibilities. 
 Present community-led monitoring findings and recommendations to sector teams and BRCR management, tracking agreed management responses. 
 Programme accountability, operational coordination and quality assurance 
 Coordinate closely with the Deputy Response Director – BRCR on response planning, management reviews, programme-quality issues, implementation priorities and agreed MEAL follow-up actions. 
 Act as the technical coordination link between National Office PQA/DMEAL and BRCR management, facilitating clear reporting, communication, joint problem-solving and escalation. 
 Work with sector leads, project managers, partners and support functions to integrate MEAL evidence into operational decisions and address cross-sector monitoring constraints. 
 Coordinate development and implementation of project accountability and distribution monitoring plans based on approved logframes, response arrangements and applicable humanitarian commitments. 
 Support safe, accessible and confidential channels for information sharing, community feedback and complaints; ensure cases are handled or referred by authorised functions following established procedures. 
 Ensure communities understand their right to information, participation, feedback and complaints, including available referral mechanisms and how concerns will be addressed. 
 Monitor feedback systems and distribution accountability findings; analyse trends, service gaps and risks, and report significant issues through appropriate internal channels. 
 Present MEAL findings and programme-quality risks in BRCR management and sectoral coordination meetings, recommending feasible corrective actions. 
 Maintain a documented tracker of management recommendations, responsible functions, deadlines and closure status arising from reviews, evaluations, audits and feedback trends. 
 Escalate critical data-quality, accountability, safeguarding or compliance concerns to the designated National Office line manager and appropriate authorised functions, while coordinating operational follow-up with BRCR management. 
 Coordinate technical information sharing with relevant humanitarian actors, government counterparts and partners, within organisational mandates and data-sharing protocols. 
 Personal and professional development, organisational values and compliance 
 Demonstrate World Vision core values, professional integrity, respectful collaboration and accountability in the humanitarian response environment. 
 Keep current with humanitarian MEAL guidance, organisational data management developments, safeguarding expectations and relevant technical standards.

 Job Description: 
 Job Purpose : The AP Sponsorship Specialist provides specialised support for the implementation of Child Sponsorship Operations within the AP. The AP Sponsorship Specialist works closely with AP team and community volunteers to ensure processes to ensure well-being of sponsored and non sponsored children are in place and the organizational requirements related to sponsorship are met according to sponsorship standards and policies.
 Major Responsibilities :
 Sponsorship Management and Coordination :
 Child Sponsorship essentials : Manage Child Sponsorship as a transformative relationship of children and sponsors, fulfilling donor promise. Ensure participation of registered children, ensuring Child Sponsorship contributes to child well-being through two essentials of Community-Led Care & Protection and Children’s Participation and Voice within the community.
 Child, family and community’s experience of Sponsorship : Manage the operations of Child Sponsorship within the Area Programme to ensure community, family, and children’s experience of every aspect of sponsorship is enjoyable, transformative and that children’s views are actively considered through feedback processes. Ensure every sponsorship activity with children contributes directly to the child’s life alongside any organizational output that is gathered. Utilize sponsorship to build child leadership, skills and voice.
 Sponsorship operations implementation : Provide specialised support for the implementation of Sponsorship Operations within the Area Programme. Ensure Child Sponsorship processes are managed efficiently and with quality according toglobal and national standards. Facilitate efficient and timely implementation of planned activities within time, scope and budget. Review Sponsorship Standards to ensure they are consistently met and achieved. Identify issues and concerns on sponsorship service operations to ensure effective functioning of Sponsorship Operations within the AP.
 Integration and planning : Support the AP Manager to ensure Sponsorship is included within AP plans to maximise integration with programme activities and to support development of Community-Led Care & Protection and Children’s Participation and Voice within the community.
 Sponsorship reporting : Facilitate Child Sponsorship reporting to ensure well-being of Registered Children and manage quality of Child Sponsorship, such as periodical CMS and SOI Exception reports (SSUI) for review, analysis, tracking and follow-up at AP level (analyse, reconcile AP Performance status, identify emerging issues and engage stakeholders).
 RC Portfolio : Engage AP Manager to manage sponsorship key business process of RC Management to ensure RC supply for Support Offices is always within standard and meets budget, including creating new child records and reactivation of holds.
 Sponsorship in Programming :
 · Sponsorship Integration : Provide Sponsorship in Programming subject matter expertise and technical support to ensure Child Sponsorship integrated within AP Annual Plans and TP and CESP activities. Ensure Sponsorship Risk Management is reviewed and applied. Review quality of Sponsorship in Programming annually using SiP Reflection tool. Ensure community, families, and children’s understanding of child sponsorship for transformation.
 RC and MVC inclusion and participation : Ensure all RC are aware of major planned activities in the AP that they could participate in and benefit from. Ensure all RC are included (participating and benefitting) in age-appropriate program activities (TP / CESP), as per Standards, contributing to their overall development. Ensure inclusion of MVC in sponsorship whenever appropriate. Ensure child participation data is captured, updated in SSUI, and analysed to inform AP Manager and team of the status of RC as proxy.
 Community engagement : Participate in sponsorship education processes and provide technical input on sponsorship messaging and sponsorship aspects of community engagement, and ongoing community sponsorship education and messaging processes. Actively engage RC parents and community on new sponsorship initiatives to strengthen participation of parents and communities in sponsorship activities.
 Manage Child Sponsorship to contribute to Community-led Care & Protection : Work with AP team to ensure Child Sponsorship contribution to local care and child protection efforts. Establish child selection and monitoring through local Child Well-Being Committee linked to child protection. This includes -
 Child selection : the development of child community selection criteria into sponsorship programme, community participation in selection processes and mandated documentation is complete.
 CMS : Support child monitoring processes to ensure children are monitored according to Child Monitoring Standards.
 Case management and follow-up : Ensure SSUI Child Wellbeing data (Case Management) is regularly reviewed and updated. Ensure reporting and follow-up adherence to child death, sickness and accident/protection protocols.
 Programme links : Provide analysis, interpretation of CMS, Child-Wellbeing and child participation data with AP team for appropriate case management follow-through and action.
 Sponsor and Child Engagement :
 Nurture sponsor and child connections : Facilitate quality and timely communication between sponsors and Registered Children.
 Manage sponsorship activities to contribute to Child Participation, Life Skills and Voice : Ensure sponsor engagement feature opportunities (IL, SL, CR, CGV, CPA, CC, APR, DPR, etc.) contribute to developing life skills and promoting child participation and voice. Support implementation of sponsor communication through programme activities as per activity designs.
 Eficient management & delivery of sponsor engagement features : Facilitate practices and appropriate tools to ensure management of sponsor child communications (IL, SL, GN, EL, APR, CEW, CC, Queries, FL, BB, Sponsorship 2.0 content and sponsor queries), within sponsorship standards.
 Quality review : Quality review of Sponsorship 2.0 products and translations.
 Facilitate translation : Facilitate translation of correspondence to ensure accuracy and emotional nuance is communicated to children and sponsors.
 Production and delivery of materials : Support coordination of design, development of communication materials, quality assurance and administration.
 Sponsor visits : Plan and facilitate sponsor visits, and ensure the visiting sponsors are well attended on and get wide exposure and positive impression from visit, with adherence of required protocols
 Capture transformational stories : Ensure Quality Communication that captures Transformational Stories to communicate with sponsors. Support the capture, document and share lessons, good practices, innovations, impact stories, photos and videos for other stakeholders.
 Quality Assurance and Risk Management :
 Child protection standards : Facilitate to ensure sponsorship data management, quality and practices are aligned to sponsorship and child protection policies, standards and procedures. Maintain updated child information in the system and ensure data protection as per WV Guidelines.
 Awareness : Facilitate awareness of community, sponsors, registered children and ADP staff on sponsorship protocols and standards.

 The position provides overall leadership, coordination and management of the respective programs and grant projects in the assigned Area Program (AP) that supports World Vision Kenya efforts to promote Child well Being outcomes in line with the World Vision Kenya Strategy, Policies and Standards. 
 In order to successfully do so, the AP Manager must be able to effectively communicate World Vision’s Christian ethos and demonstrate a quality of spiritual life that serves as an example to others.
 Please Note: World Vision is a Christian humanitarian organization with a mission centred on following Jesus Christ in service to the world´s most vulnerable children. Therefore, in all locations to the fullest extent legally permissible, the successful applicant will affirm our core documents, observe conduct compatible with Christian principles, serve at a high level of professional ethics, and strive to act in accordance with cultural sensitivities. Furthermore, regular attendance with team and office devotions, chapel, and prayer gatherings are expected in line with policies in the World Vision host location and its departments. 
 Expected results 
  Well-coordinated programs at the Area Program level
 Acceptable implementation rates
 Area Program Risk registers in place and updated regularly and risk mitigated in a timely manner
 Well-coordinated and managed projects and programs operations with clear mandates at AP.
 Cohesive and effective team at Area Program level
 ADP Leadership and Management 
 Provide strong and positive leadership to the Area Program teams ensuring competent and motivated staff
 Ensure over 95% implementation of Annual Plans and budget by close of financial year, ensuring adherence to Detailed Implementation Plans, 4-Dimensional matrices and -5% budget variance parameters; Supervise and monitor the implementation of the program plans of action
 Ensure all operations, planning and budgeting processes are aligned with the WVK requirements and standards
 Provide   leadership to the   three-track   ministry (One   operation, one organization) principle
 Lead in the development and implementation of a risk register and uploading of the same in Riskonnect, prescribing controls and treatments and regularly monitoring effectiveness of the same
 Contribute to the development of strategy, directions for the program in line with World Vision Ministry focus
 Provide management oversight on all operational risks including the core security requirements
 Provides oversight for sponsorship integration as part of Area Programs planning processes, ensuring that sponsorship programming and sponsorship service operations objectives are met.
 Compile a multi-year plan for all activities across the Area Programmes, and produce an indicative multi-year budget.
 Manage all programming within the Area Programmes, across multiple technical projects, giving a holistic view of the Area Programmes.
 Ensure that Child Protection and adult safeguarding Policy is understood and adhered to in all programs implementation and any issues arising in the programs area are reported in accordance with the WV Policies and guidelines and dealt with through established structures and working with other likeminded partners to uphold their wellbeing.
 Accountability and Quality Assurance 
 Oversight and overall financial Management at the Area Program level ensuring efficiency and effectiveness and compliance with WV Polices and standards.
 Ensure that the Program accountability frameworks (PAF) are in place in all APs for accountability and as a feedback mechanism for program quality improvement.
 Manage the Development Program Approach (DPA) community engagement process in all communities to identify appropriate technical projects for implementation with partners, and to adapt them for the context
 Ensure that WVK Operations at AP level are within the organization’s policies, procedures and business processes
 Ensure 100% implementation of audit recommendations and presence of risk management plan/document to guide operations
 Ensure security of assets is sustained
 Ensure green indicators for sponsorship year round Service Operation Indicators (SOIs/KPIs) and accountable sponsorship management practice
 Ensure a functional and effective accountability (complaints and feedback) mechanism
 Ensure quality workmanship of projects being implemented in the AP in line with WVK organizational policies and strategies (Ministry policies, Advocacy,
 Child Sponsorship, and Disaster Preparedness Plan, cross cutting themes, LEAP, WV Development Program Approach; among others)
 Ensure implementation of the necessary recommendations for effective ministry.
 Manage monitoring across the Area Programs to identify progress made and make necessary adjustments to plans; this will be including the annual review and planning meetings in all communities, and at the Area Programs level
 Facilitate development and monitoring of the AP procurement plans and SC processes
 Provide oversight to contract management - ensure contractors and consultants deliver within stipulated timelines and adhere to the stipulated contract terms
 Designs

 Job Description: 
 CONTEXT 
 World Vision is a Christian relief, development and advocacy organization working to improve the quality of life of people, especially children, who are marginalized and living in poverty.  World Vision helps all who are in need regardless of their religion, race, ethnicity or gender. 
 World Vision International in Viet Nam (WVIV) is supported by multiple countries and funded through a combination of sponsorship programs (majority) and Private Non-Sponsorship (PNS)/grants. WVIV operates across multiple provinces and implements Area Development Programs (ADPs) that focus on communities with high levels of poverty, often including ethnic minority populations. In addition to ADPs, WVIV implements various Special and Grant Projects to address the specific needs of vulnerable children in both ADP and non-ADP areas. 
 WVIV is headquartered in Hanoi, while majority of staff are based locally in Area Development Programs and project sites across the country which enables them to work closely with government partners and communities on a daily basis.
 JOB PURPOSE 
 The Digital Services Assistant supports WVIV's digital transformation and technology service delivery efforts by assisting in the development, configuration, testing, deployment and support of digital solutions and technology services. This role contributes to improving business processes, enhancing user adoption and ensuring reliable digital service delivery through effective user support, service administration and continuous improvement activities.
 MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Digital Solutions Support & Configuration (35%) 
 •         Configure approved forms, workflows, low-code applications and automation solutions based on documented business requirements, ensuring compliance with security, data quality, version control and release procedures.
 •         Participate in developing, troubleshooting, enhancing and upgrading assigned digital solutions within approved designs, standards and work plans, under the technical guidance of the supervisor.
 •         Prepare prototypes and support solution deployment, testing coordination and release activities.
 •         Maintain technical documentation, configuration records and solution-related knowledge assets in accordance with established standards.
 Solution Testing & User Support (25%) 
 •         Prepare test plans, test cases, test data and test evidence for solution validation activities.
 •         Conduct functional testing, regression testing and support user acceptance testing (UAT), documenting defects and user feedback.
 •         Log, track, prioritize and follow up on defects, issues and corrective actions through to closure, escalating material risks when required.
 •         Provide first-line support for digital solutions, responding to user inquiries and resolving routine issues.
 •         Support user onboarding, knowledge transfer and basic training for newly deployed digital solutions.
 IT Operations & Workplace Technology Support (20%) 
 •         Provide first-level support for hardware, software, collaboration platforms and workplace technology, including ticket logging, service tracking and case closure documentation.
 •         Support user account administration, software installation, access requests and related user support activities.
 •         Maintain IT asset inventory records and support asset lifecycle administration.
 •         Provide support for meeting room technology, virtual meetings and hybrid collaboration tools.
 Service Administration & Knowledge Management (15%) 
 •         Maintain service tickets, operational records and knowledge base content, ensuring data accuracy, completeness and audit readiness.
 •         Develop and update user guides, technical notes and release documentation to support service delivery and user adoption.
 •         Monitor service trends, identify recurring issues and support implementation of service improvement actions.
 •         Prepare service reports, performance metrics and operational insights to support decision-making and continuous improvement.
 Others (5%) 
 •         Perform other duties as assigned.
 JOB REQUIREMENTS 
 -          At least 2 years of relevant experience in IT support, digital solutions, systems administration, service desk operations, or related fields.
 -          Experience working with Microsoft 365 applications and collaboration tools.
 -          Experience supporting business applications, digital platforms, or workflow automation solutions is an advantage.
 -          Experience in an NGO/INGO environment is desirable.
 -         Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Information Systems, or related disciplines.
 -         Strong customer service and user support orientation.
 -         Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
 -         Strong attention to detail and documentation skills.
 -         Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities effectively.
 -         Good verbal and written communication skills in English and Vietnamese.
 -         Ability to work collaboratively with staff at all levels of the organization.
 -         Willingness to learn new technologies and continuously develop technical capabilities.

 F. Autres responsabilités et amélioration continue

 Promouvoir l'utilisation des outils numériques et de l'intelligence artificielle pour améliorer l'efficacité administrative, dans le respect des politiques et procédures de World Vision.

Une connaissance avérée de la gestion des bureaux exécutifs, de la gouvernance organisationnelle, de la planification stratégique ainsi que des politiques et systèmes de World Vision est également appréciée.

 Aptitude à travailler de manière autonome, à proposer des solutions innovantes et à contribuer à la dynamique d'équipe.

 4. Qualités personnelles et comportementales

 Se rassurer de la qualité de l’eau de boisson au niveau communautaire et des écoles

 S’assurer de la Supervisions des contractants et leur fournir tout appui technique et matériel nécessaires dans la construction des ouvrages d’eau et d’assainissement dans les écoles ainsi que dans les communautés
 Associer notamment le ONHR, La chefferie, Les Zones de santé, le Sous Proved, COPA dans le choix des sites, à l’implantation et à la réalisation des ouvrages.
 Elaborer le design, et les lignes de conduite dans la mise en œuvre des interventions WASH dans leur zone de sante

 Job Description: 
 World Vision is the Principal Recipient of the Global Fund grant to Solomon Islands for TB, Malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH). This grant is also supported by World Vision Korea. The Grant cycle 7 for Solomon Islands has strategic shifts in technical approaches, implementation arrangement and requires increased rigor in grant monitoring and evaluation function. The National Strategic plans for TB and National Malaria plans which contribute to National Health Strategic plans of Solomon Islands (2022-2031) are in place and indicate significant focus on prevention, care and treatment and advocacy, with major cross cutting themes such as addressing gender/ human rights barriers, community systems strengthening as part of health systems strengthening.  The grant cycle 7 will conclude on 31 Dec 2026 and World Vision will continue to work closely with Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) for grant cycle 8, starting January 2027.
 There are national level data management support functions to address the chronic gaps of data quality for TB and malaria, while implementation of interventions is done jointly by National and provincial Govt health services and PR staff.  There is an increased intentional involvement of provincial health services which are responsible for health service delivery in 9 provinces and Honiara City Council. WHO is the main partner which also addresses disease surveillance, data management, and DHIS2 functionality.
 There was a late start to the grant in 2024, and the Malaria interventions form a major part of the budget allocation for the grant including bednet (LLIN -Long lasting Insecticidal nets). In order to demonstrate results within short implementation cycles, the Global Fund invests in critical human resources to support the implementation and grant management so that the country’s targets are realized. The disease burden of TB and Malaria in Solomon Islands are of major concern without good quality data to know the true burden of disease. There are recently launched strategic plans such as Revised TB strategic plan and also the Malaria Elimination Road map which set out clear objectives and deliverables for both programs to achieve disease burden reduction.
 The role of M&E Manager is a national role to support PR and National programs to carry out program monitoring and contribute to addressing major gaps in data quality, reporting and data usage across the country. The key responsibilities will include
 Strategic technical support to all provinces through direct and indirect reports for data quality (timeliness, accuracy), donor and CCM reporting.
 Technical and operational support for TB and Malaria data reporting.
 Specifics for the role include:
 Create M&E plan for the grant 
 Develop/ adapt M&E implementation guidelines with necessary tools. 
 Information flow mapping for TB and Malaria and map out data management ecosystems
 Engage with DHIS2 community of practice, GF interest group 
 Review and list out all the relevant GF guidelines for M&E that are applicable for Solomon Islands 
 Preparation of reports for GF, SO at required intervals 
 Strategic engagement with donors 
 Facilitate program data conversations with programs for better data use and explore formation of working group for M&E in Solomon Islands 
 Capacity development of team 
 Data quality 
 Conduct data validation on National TB and Vector Borne indicators before submission to GF 
 Review and prepare Malaria LLIN distribution data (Coverage and usage), key indicators for malaria
 Review and prepare key indicators for TB including Treatment outcomes.
 Support National and Provincial M&E officers for TB and Malaria – data management and data analysis 
 Design and participate in Supervisory Visit alongside national TB and Malaria program 
 Provide Monitoring tools for LLIN distribution. Carry out Spot checks and team leader check list 
 Data analysis on Monthly and quarterly reports from TB and Malaria 
 Assist LFA visits
 Work with WV International for data for any impact reporting, abstracts etc 
 World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children as well as adults living where World Vision operates. We have zero tolerance for incidents of violence or abuse against children or adults, including sexual exploitation or abuse, committed either by employees or others affiliated with our work. Therefore, World Vision does not hire staff whose background is not suitable for working with children or vulnerable adults, even if their role does not interact directly with them. Each potential team member needs to understand the importance of these issues and be open to further training and guidance on our safeguarding policies and responsibilities

 Job Description: 
 Planification des risques et registre des risques 
 Préparez le plan annuel de gestion des risques et d'examen de conformité pour la subvention GC8, pour approbation par le responsable des risques et de la conformité.
 Faciliter l'identification, l'évaluation et le suivi des risques au sein des PR et des sous-bénéficiaires, en utilisant les catégories de risques du Fonds mondial et le cadre de gestion des risques d'entreprise de WV.
 Tenir le registre des risques GC8 et le registre des problèmes ; faire un suivi des détenteurs de risques concernant les actions d'atténuation et les échéances.
 Tenez-vous informé des évolutions des politiques du Fonds mondial, des politiques de WV et des réglementations CAR, et signalez leurs implications pour la subvention.
 Examens de conformité et suivi 
 Effectuer des examens de conformité et des contrôles ponctuels sur les finances, les achats, les actifs, la paie et la mise en œuvre des programmes au sein des PR et des sous-bénéficiaires, conformément au plan approuvé.
 Vérifiez le respect de l'Accord de subvention, des Lignes directrices du Fonds mondial pour la budgétisation des subventions, du Code de conduite des bénéficiaires et des politiques de WV, y compris l'éligibilité des dépenses et des documents justificatifs.
 Soutenir l'examen des rapports PU/PUDR et financiers pour la conformité avant leur soumission à la LFA.
 Documentez les lacunes et faiblesses matérielles du contrôle interne et proposez des améliorations.
 Vérifications de conformité des politiques des donateurs et de la Republique Centrafricaine 
 Vérifiez la conformité au dépistage des parties bloquées (BPS) effectué avant la date pour les fournisseurs, partenaires et personnel, y compris les sous-bénéficiaires.
 Vérifier la conformité aux exigences en matière de rapports de répartition de la main-d'œuvre (LDR) et de feuilles de temps selon la politique WV et les règles du Fonds mondial.
 Vérifier que les coûts partagés et indirects facturés à la subvention respectent les lignes directrices du Fonds mondial pour la budgétisation des subventions ainsi que la politique d'allocation des coûts de la WVI CAR.
 Examiner la ponctualité des paiements des fournisseurs, les rapprochements de comptes et l'ancienneté des éléments du bilan pour la subvention GC8, et signaler les exceptions pour les Finances et le Gestionnaire des risques et de la conformité.
 Suivi de l'audit et enregistrement des incidents 
 Soutenir la préparation aux examens LFA, audits externes, audits OIG et audits internes WV, y compris la collecte de documents.
 Maintenir le suivi des recommandations d'audit et assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre des recommandations d'audit, de LFA et de suivi par partenaires.
 Analyser les résultats récurrents des audits et proposer des améliorations du contrôle interne.
 Consignez tous les incidents signalés de fraude, corruption, protection de la protection / SEAH ou autres inconduites et adressez-les rapidement au responsable des risques et de la conformité pour qu'ils soient signalés et enquêtes par des enquêteurs qualifiés.
 Formation et renforcement des capacités des partenaires 
 Organiser des sessions de formation et de sensibilisation à l'échelle des subventions sur le contrôle interne, la gestion des risques, la lutte contre la fraude et les canaux de signalement.
 Coordonner les évaluations de capacité et de risque de tous les sous-bénéficiaires (SR) et fournisseurs de services (SP) GC8.
 Coordonner le renforcement des capacités des SR sur la base des résultats d'évaluation et de suivi.
 Transition et clôture des subventions 
 Soutenir la clôture conforme de la subvention GC7 et la transition vers GC8, y compris l'examen des rapports finaux PU/PUDR.
 Finaliser la vérification et le rapprochement des équipements et des actifs non monétaires et produire une liste complète des actifs.
 Coordonner la disposition des liquidités, équipements et actifs non monétaires conformément aux exigences de clôture du Fonds mondial.
 Connaissance et qualifications 
 Minimum de trois (3) années d'expérience progressivement responsable en gestion des risques, contrôle interne, conformité, audit, finance ou gestion de subventions au sein d'une ONG internationale, d'un programme financé par des donateurs ou d'une organisation de développement.
 Une expérience des exigences de conformité des donateurs ; l'expérience sur les subventions du Fonds mondial (en tant que PR, SR ou LFA) est fortement privilégiée.
 Expérience dans la réalisation d'examens de conformité, de contrôles ponctuels et de suivi des recommandations d'audit.
 L'expérience d'évaluer ou de suivre les partenaires ou sous-bénéficiaires de la mise en œuvre est un atout.
 Licence en comptabilité, finance, gestion des risques, audit, administration des affaires, économie, administration publique ou domaine connexe.
 La progression vers une certification professionnelle (par exemple ACCA, CPA, CIA, CFE) est un avantage.
 Connaissance des exigences du Fonds mondial : règlements sur les subventions, lignes directrices pour la budgétisation des subventions, code de conduite des bénéficiaires et rôles de la LFA et de l'OIG.
 Compréhension des indicateurs de contrôle interne, d'évaluation des risques et de risque de fraude.
 MS Excel avancé ; bonne maîtrise de Word et PowerPoint.
 Solides compétences analytiques et de rédaction de rapports.
 Connaissances en budgétisation et en reporting financier.
 Intégrité, discrétion et objectivité dans le traitement des informations confidentielles.

offres.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

 Employee Contract Type: 
Local - Fixed Term Employee (durée déterminée) 
 Job Description: 
 Assurer le leadership stratégique, la coordination et le suivi des interventions d’engagement communautaire et de promotion de la santé dans le cadre de la subvention intégrée GC8, afin de renforcer la participation effective des communautés, d'accroître l'utilisation des services de prévention, de dépistage et de traitement du VIH, de la tuberculose et du paludisme, de promouvoir durablement les comportements favorables à la santé, et de garantir un accès équitable aux services pour les populations vulnérables et marginalisées, conformément aux exigences du Fonds mondial en matière de Communautés, Droits et Genre (CRG), de suivi mené par la communauté (Community-Led Monitoring) et de renforcement des systèmes communautaires
 undefined Concevoir, piloter et rendre compte de la stratégie d’engagement communautaire et de promotion de la santé (communication pour le changement social et de comportement — SBC) de la subvention intégrée GC8 : mobilisation sociale, génération de la demande de services VIH/TB/paludisme/SRPS, systèmes communautaires (ASC/OSC/PNC), suivi mené par la communauté (community-led monitoring) et promotion des comportements santé, en garantissant l’accès équitable, l’intégration des trois maladies et la conformité aux exigences Fonds mondial (CRG), pour une appropriation durable des interventions par les communautés.
 Responsabilités principales 1. Stratégie d’engagement communautaire et SBC •
 Élaborer et déployer le plan national d’engagement communautaire et de promotion de la santé (SBC) intégré VIH–TB–paludisme–SRPS : analyse des comportements et des barrières (BCA 
 — Barrier and Behavior Analysis), segmentation des audiences, stratégies de communication interpersonnelle et de masse 
 Développer les outils et messages SBC harmonisés (radio, spots, théâtres communautaires, matériel IEC) en français et langues locales (sango, arabe peul, zande), avec validation communautaire et du Genre Coordinator ;
 Assurer la synergie avec les campagnes de masse (MILDA, PID, campagnes vaccinales) : co-distribution des messages et des plateformes.
 2. Systèmes communautaires et populations spéciales
 •Coordonner et renforcer les capacités des OSC partenaires, ASC: formation initiale et recyclage, mentorat, suivi de la motivation et de la performance, gestion des contrats et des plans de travail communautaires ;
 •Garantir l’accès équitable des populations spéciales : campements peuls et sites miniers (relais Ardos/pistoeurs), îlots fluviaux (piroguiers-relais), populations Aka (guides), déplacés internes, populations clés et personnes handicapées ;
 •Superviser l’intégration des interventions communautaires aux quatre composantes (VIH, TB, paludisme, SRPS) : dépistage communautaire, accompagnement des patients (observance TARV/anti-TB, recherches des perdus de vue), promotion de la prévention (MILDA, eau-assainissement-hygiène).
 3. Suivi mené par la communauté (CLM) et redevabilité
 •Mettre en œuvre et superviser le community-led monitoring : recrutement et formation des moniteurs communautaires, collecte mensuelle des retours d’usagers, mécanismes de feedback et de plaintes, boucle de remédiation documentée (en lien avec le Genre Coordinator pour les plaintes VBG) ;
 •Analyser les indicateurs communautaires (personnes touchées, enfants zéro dose référés puis vaccinés, demande de services, qualité des données des OSC) : tableaux de bord mensuels, notes d’analyse,
•Assurer la conformité du volet communautaire/CRG du Performance Framework ; contribuer aux PUDR semestriels et préparer les revues LFA ; documenter les bonnes pratiques et leçons apprises.tableaux de bord mensuels, notes d’analyse, triangulation avec les données FOSA/DHIS2 ;
 Accompagnement des SR/OSC et coordination 
 • Accompagner les SR (IMC, CRS, CRF) et les équipes CRS-UGPD/UGPD sur les volets communautaires : supervisions trimestrielles, évaluation des capacités (ECAP) des OSC, plans d’action correctifs suivis jusqu’à clôture ;
 •Coordonner avec le volet PC/OSC des sous-accords SR et la DPV pour l’institutionnalisation des dispositifs communautaires (intégration aux micro-plans de district, plans de pérennisation) ;
 •Animer les forums de coordination communautaire (OSC, leaders, moniteurs CLM) et représenter l’UGPPS dans les instances communautaires (clusters, coordination engagement communautaire ). 
 Minimum de sept (7) années d’expérience professionnelle dans les domaines de l’engagement communautaire, de la promotion de la santé, de la communication pour le changement social et de comportement (SBC) ou du développement communautaire.
 Au moins trois (3) années d’expérience démontrée dans la coordination et la supervision d’Organisations de la Société Civile (OSC), d’Agents de Santé Communautaire (ASC) ou d’équipes communautaires à grande échelle.
 Expérience avérée dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi de stratégies de mobilisation sociale, de changement de comportement et de renforcement des systèmes communautaires.
 Expérience dans l’utilisation des approches communautaires pour améliorer l’accès aux services de santé, notamment dans les domaines du VIH, de la tuberculose, du paludisme, de la vaccination ou de la santé communautaire intégrée.
 Expérience des approches Zéro Dose, IRMMA (Integrated Routine Immunization and Maternal, Newborn and Child Health Services), Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) ou des mécanismes de redevabilité communautaire fortement souhaitée.
 Expérience de collaboration avec les autorités sanitaires, les partenaires techniques et financiers, les leaders communautaires et les organisations locales.
 Une expérience dans la gestion de projets financés par le Fonds mondial, notamment dans les domaines CRG (Communities, Rights and Gender) et PUDR, constitue un atout important.
 Expérience de travail en République Centrafricaine ou dans un contexte fragile, humanitaire ou post-conflit fortement souhaitée.
 · Diplôme universitaire de niveau Master (Bac+5) en Santé Publique, Sciences Sociales, Développement Communautaire, Communication pour le Changement Social et de Comportement (SBC), Promotion de la Santé ou discipline connexe.
 · Formation complémentaire en mobilisation communautaire, communication pour le changement de comportement, santé communautaire, suivi-évaluation ou gestion de projets souhaitée.
 · Certification ou formation spécialisée en engagement communautaire, participation citoyenne, redevabilité sociale ou développement des systèmes communautaires constitue un avantage.
 · Formation sur les approches liées aux droits humains, au genre, à l’équité et à l’inclusion (GEDSI/CRG) souhaitée.
 · Excellente maîtrise du français écrit et oral.
 · Bonne connaissance de l’anglais professionnel, notamment pour la rédaction de rapports techniques et les échanges avec les partenaires internationaux
  · Excellente connaissance des approches de Communication pour le Changement Social et de Comportement (SBC) , de mobilisation sociale et de promotion de la santé.
 · Bonne maîtrise des mécanismes de renforcement des systèmes communautaires, du Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) et de la participation communautaire.
 · Expérience avérée dans la conception et l’animation de dialogues communautaires, forums participatifs et campagnes de sensibilisation à grande échelle.
 · Solides compétences en gestion, supervision, coaching et renforcement des capacités des OSC, ASC et autres acteurs communautaires.
 · Bonne connaissance des principes de Genre, Équité, Diversité, Inclusion, Communautés, Droits

 Leadership technique : Suivi et évaluation

 Fournir un appui en suivi et évaluation (M&E) aux projets financés par des subventions et aux projets de réponse d'urgence.

 Superviser les Chargés du suivi du bien-être de l'enfant (CWB Tracking Officers). 
 Superviser les spécialistes techniques de projets. 
 Coacher le personnel.

 Renforcer les capacités du personnel de terrain en matière de suivi et d'évaluation.

This includes conducting initial analysis of funding opportunities (eligibility, strategic fit, competitiveness, partnership requirements and WV Chad’s capacity to deliver) to inform go/no-go decisions with the RAM Director, managing the end-to-end proposal development process for assigned opportunities and ensuring strategic donor engagement. Foster innovation and adaptation in program design and implementation to respond to emerging needs in Chad’s changing contexts. Ensure programs are aligned with the global Fragile Context Initiative and grant acquisition strategic priorities.

This includes overseeing reporting standards and ensuring alignment with donor and World Vision policies. Identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with grant implementation, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and World Vision policies.
 3.      Donor and Partner Engagement : Manage day-to-day engagement with assigned donors, World Vision Support Offices and partners, in coordination with the RAM Director. This includes positioning WV Chad effectively to secure and manage grants, fostering strong relationships with donors, partners, and institutions, and systematically tracking engagement to inform pre-positioning.
 4.      Capacity Building and Knowledge Management : Build the capacity of WV Chad’s team in grant acquisition and management, including technical specialists taking on GAM responsibilities, ensuring staff are equipped to handle complex grants in fragile contexts. Contribute to knowledge management and the systematisation of GAM processes by systematically archiving grant and proposal documentation in WV Chad’s designated systems, and by maintaining ImpaQ, WV Chad’s impact measurement system, to ensure data is complete, accurate and up to date. Contribute to the systematisation of GAM processes and promote a culture of collaboration, learning, and knowledge sharing within WV Chad and with external partners, including local partners, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of programs.

 Employee Contract Type: 
Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term) 
 Job Description: 
 1. Stratégie, politiques et analyse genre 
 ·       Élaborer et mettre en œuvre le plan genre et inclusion de la subvention (annuel et pluriannuel), aligné sur le cadre CRG du Fonds mondial et les politiques nationales de genre ;
 ·       Conduire l'analyse genre des interventions (participation, accès, contrôle des ressources, bénéfices) et l'analyse des barrières liées au genre et aux droits humains, en lien avec le Responsable Engagement Communautaire ;
 ·       Développer et diffuser les politiques et outils UGPPS : politique de non-discrimination, protocole de prévention et de prise en charge des VBG, code de conduite et de sauvegarde, directives d'inclusion des personnes handicapées et des populations clés ;
 ·       S'assurer que tous les documents du programme (PAT, budgets, TDR, sous-accords SR) intègrent explicitement les dimensions genre et inclusion avec budgets dédiés traçables.
 2-Intégration du genre dans les interventions techniques (VIH, TB, paludisme, SRPS) 
 •Appuyer les référents techniques pour l'intégration du genre dans les cascades de soins : analyse désagrégée par sexe et âge de la cascade 95-95-95 VIH, du traitement TB et de la prise en charge paludisme, avec analyse des écarts et mesures correctives ;
 •Renforcer les services sensibles au genre : consultations adaptées (horaires, personnel féminin disponible, confidentialité), contraception et planning familial intégrés aux soins VIH/TB/palu, prise en charge de la santé reproductive et maternelle ;
 •Appuyer l'accès des populations clés et vulnérables : protocoles de dépistage et de soins non stigmatisants, réduction des barrières juridiques et sociales, partenariat avec les réseaux communautaires ;
 •Superviser l'intégration de l'approche GEDSI dans les campagnes de masse et le community-led monitoring (moniteurs hommes/femmes, outils sensibles au genre).
 3. Prévention et prise en charge des VBG et sauvegarde 
 •Mettre en œuvre le volet VBG du programme : formation des prestataires à la première ligne (reconnaissance, écoute, consentement éclairé, PEP sous 72 h, référencement), disponibilité des kits post-viol, cartographie et mise à jour des circuits de référencement VBG dans chaque district ;
 •Coordonner la réponse aux survivantes avec le ministère en charge du Genre, les services sociaux et les OSC spécialisées ; garantir la confidentialité et la sécurité des survivantes ;
 •Superviser la politique de sauvegarde (safeguarding) : code de conduite signé par tout le personnel, enquêtes et mesures disciplinaires, mécanisme de signalement confidentiel fonctionnel.
 4. Renforcement des capacités, coordination et redevabilité Fonds mondial 
 •Former et coacher les équipes UGPPS, SR, OSC et districtales au genre, à l'inclusion et à la prise en charge des VBG (plan de formation annuel, suivi post-formation à 3–6 mois) ;
 •Coordonner les mécanismes de participation communautaire : forums de femmes, comités de suivi avec représentation équitable (≥ 40 % de femmes), intégration des retours du community-led monitoring dans la prise de décision ;
 •Assurer la conformité des indicateurs CRG/genre du Performance Framework : consolidation des données désagrégées, contribution aux PUDR semestriels, préparation des revues LFA ;
 •Documenter et capitaliser : bonnes pratiques, études de cas, leçons apprises ; représenter l'UGPPS dans les instances genre (clusters, groupes techniques, partenaires).
 CONNAISSANCE ET QUALIFICATIONS POUR LE ROLE 
 Required Professional Experience
 Minimum 7 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans le domaine du genre, de l’inclusion sociale et/ou de la santé publique au sein d’organisations nationales ou internationales.
 Au moins 3 ans d’expérience avérée en coordination des approches Genre, Équité, Diversité, Inclusion et Sauvegarde (GEDSI) dans des programmes de développement ou humanitaires.
 Expérience significative dans la prévention et la prise en charge des violences basées sur le genre (VBG) , y compris l’accompagnement des survivantes et l’orientation vers les services appropriés. Expérience dans la mise en œuvre et le suivi de projets financés par des bailleurs internationaux, notamment le Fonds mondial , est fortement souhaitée.
 Expérience en analyse de genre, collecte et utilisation de données désagrégées, suivi-évaluation et production de rapports techniques.
 Une expérience de travail dans un contexte fragile ou affecté par des crises, notamment en République Centrafricaine , constitue un atout majeur.
 Diplôme de niveau Master (Bac+5) en études de genre, droit des femmes, santé publique, sciences sociales, développement international ou toute discipline connexe.
 QUALIFICATIONS 
 Formation spécialisée en Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG) , protection, sauvegarde (Safeguarding) ou accompagnement des survivantes.
 ·  Formation certifiée en Genre, Équité, Diversité et Inclusion (GEDSI) ou dans un domaine similaire souhaitée.
 ·  Certification ou formation complémentaire en gestion de projets, suivi-évaluation ou santé communautaire constituant un avantage.
 ·  Excellente maîtrise du français écrit et parlé ; bonne connaissance de l’anglais professionnel souhaitée.
 AUTRES COMPETENCES 
 Excellente connaissance des concepts, cadres et outils d’analyse de genre.
 Bonne maîtrise des politiques, stratégies et directives du Fonds mondial , particulièrement celles relatives aux droits humains, au genre et à l’engagement communautaire (CRG).
 Solides compétences en conception et animation de formations destinées à des publics variés.
 Capacité à élaborer et mettre en œuvre des plans d’action en matière de genre, diversité, inclusion et sauvegarde.
 Expérience en plaidoyer, mobilisation communautaire et facilitation de concertations multi-acteurs.
 Capacité à analyser, interpréter et présenter des données désagrégées par sexe, âge et vulnérabilité.
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication, rédaction de rapports techniques et formulation de recommandations stratégiques.
 Sens élevé de l’éthique, de la confidentialité et de la protection des personnes vulnérables.
 Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants (Microsoft Office 365, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams) et des plateformes de collecte de données.

 Synergie d'action et redevabilité Fonds mondial
 Faciliter la synergie entre Programme (UGPPSS), SR et OSC : forums de coordination, matrice d'alignement des activités, résolution des chevauchements et partage des apprentissages ;
